title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
author: Mark Twain
intro_en: A boy in a sleepy Mississippi River town paints a fence, hunts for treasure, runs off to be a pirate, and stumbles into real danger. Mark Twain’s 1876 classic of mischief, friendship, and growing up.
intro_zh: 密西西比河边一个昏昏欲睡的小镇上,一个男孩刷篱笆、寻宝藏、离家去当“海盗”,还意外卷进真正的险境。马克·吐温 1876 年的经典,写顽皮、友情与长大。
copyright_note: 公有领域 · Mark Twain, 1876 · 文本来源 Project Gutenberg (#74)

paragraphs.en: “Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: No answer.
paragraphs.cn: 没人应声。

paragraphs.en: “TOM!”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: No answer.
paragraphs.cn: 没人应声。

paragraphs.en: “What’s gone with that boy, I wonder?
paragraphs.cn: “那孩子跑哪去了？汤姆，你快出来！”

paragraphs.en: You TOM!”
paragraphs.cn: 你，汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: No answer.
paragraphs.cn: 没人应声。

paragraphs.en: The old lady pulled her spectacles down and looked over them about the room; then she put them up and looked out under them.
paragraphs.cn: 老奶奶把眼镜拉下来，从上面看屋子里。然后她又把眼镜推上去，从下面往外看。

paragraphs.en: She seldom or never looked _through_ them for so small a thing as a boy; they were her state pair, the pride of her heart, and were built for “style,” not service—she could have seen through a pair of stove-lids just as well.
paragraphs.cn: 她从来不用这副眼镜看东西，尤其是找小男孩。因为这眼镜只是好看的，不是用来真看的。

paragraphs.en: She looked perplexed for a moment, and then said, not fiercely, but still loud enough for the furniture to hear:
paragraphs.cn: 她愣了一下，有点儿没明白。然后她大声说，声音大得屋子里的家具都听得见：

paragraphs.en: “Well, I lay if I get hold of you I’ll—”
paragraphs.cn: “哼，要是被我抓住，看我怎么收拾你——”

paragraphs.en: She did not finish, for by this time she was bending down and punching under the bed with the broom, and so she needed breath to punctuate the punches with.
paragraphs.cn: 她话没说完，因为她弯腰用扫帚往床底下捅，捅一下就要喘口气。

paragraphs.en: She resurrected nothing but the cat.
paragraphs.cn: 她什么也没捅出来，只有一只猫。

paragraphs.en: “I never did see the beat of that boy!”
paragraphs.cn: “我从没见过这么调皮的孩子！”

paragraphs.en: She went to the open door and stood in it and looked out among the tomato vines and “jimpson” weeds that constituted the garden.
paragraphs.cn: 她走到开着的门口，站在那儿往外看。外面是花园，有西红柿和一些杂草。

paragraphs.en: No Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 没看到汤姆。

paragraphs.en: So she lifted up her voice at an angle calculated for distance and shouted:
paragraphs.cn: 于是她大声喊起来，声音传得很远：

paragraphs.en: “Y-o-u-u TOM!”
There was a slight noise behind her and she turned just in time to seize a small boy by the slack of his roundabout and arrest his flight.
paragraphs.cn: 她身后传来一点声音，她一转身，正好抓住一个小男孩的衣服，没让他跑掉。

paragraphs.en: “There!
paragraphs.cn: “抓到你了！

paragraphs.en: I might ’a’ thought of that closet.
paragraphs.cn: 我早该想到那个柜子了。

paragraphs.en: What you been doing in there?”
paragraphs.cn: 你在里面干什么呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Nothing.”
paragraphs.cn: “什么也没干。”

paragraphs.en: “Nothing!
paragraphs.cn: “什么也没干？！看看你的手，再看看你的嘴。这到底是什么呀？”

paragraphs.en: Look at your hands.
paragraphs.cn: 看看你的手。

paragraphs.en: And look at your mouth.
paragraphs.cn: 再看看你的嘴巴。

paragraphs.en: What _is_ that truck?”
paragraphs.cn: 那是什么卡车呀？

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know, aunt.”
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道，阿姨。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I know.
paragraphs.cn: “哼，我知道。

paragraphs.en: It’s jam—that’s what it is.
paragraphs.cn: 是果酱——就是它！”

paragraphs.en: Forty times I’ve said if you didn’t let that jam alone I’d skin you.
paragraphs.cn: 我跟你说了好多次，不许动果酱，不然我就要惩罚你！

paragraphs.en: Hand me that switch.”
paragraphs.cn: 把那根小棍子给我。

paragraphs.en: The switch hovered in the air—the peril was desperate—
paragraphs.cn: 小棍子举在空中，情况非常危险。

paragraphs.en: “My!
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀！

paragraphs.en: Look behind you, aunt!”
paragraphs.cn: 姨妈，快看你身后！

paragraphs.en: The old lady whirled round, and snatched her skirts out of danger.
paragraphs.cn: 老太太猛地转过身，赶紧把裙子拉开。

paragraphs.en: The lad fled on the instant, scrambled up the high board-fence, and disappeared over it.
paragraphs.cn: 小男孩立刻就跑了，他爬上高高的木板围墙，一下子就翻了过去，不见了。

paragraphs.en: His aunt Polly stood surprised a moment, and then broke into a gentle laugh.
paragraphs.cn: 他的姨妈波莉姨妈愣了一下，然后轻轻地笑了出来。

paragraphs.en: “Hang the boy, can’t I never learn anything?
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀这孩子，我怎么就学不乖呢？

paragraphs.en: Ain’t he played me tricks enough like that for me to be looking out for him by this time?
paragraphs.cn: 他不是已经这样骗了我很多次了吗？我早该提防他了才对呀！

paragraphs.en: But old fools is the biggest fools there is.
paragraphs.cn: 可是年纪大的人，有时就是最笨的。

paragraphs.en: Can’t learn an old dog new tricks, as the saying is.
paragraphs.cn: 俗话说，老狗学不会新把戏。

paragraphs.en: But my goodness, he never plays them alike, two days, and how is a body to know what’s coming?
paragraphs.cn: 可是天哪，他每天的鬼点子都不一样，我怎么知道他又要搞什么鬼呢？

paragraphs.en: He ’pears to know just how long he can torment me before I get my dander up, and he knows if he can make out to put me off for a minute or make me laugh, it’s all down again and I can’t hit him a lick.
paragraphs.cn: 他好像知道他能把我气多久，也知道只要他能拖延我一分钟，或者把我逗笑，我就又下不了手打他了。

paragraphs.en: I ain’t doing my duty by that boy, and that’s the Lord’s truth, goodness knows.
paragraphs.cn: 我没有好好管教这个孩子，天知道这是真的。

paragraphs.en: Spare the rod and spile the child, as the Good Book says.
paragraphs.cn: 俗话说，不打不成器。

paragraphs.en: I’m a laying up sin and suffering for us both, I know.
paragraphs.cn: 我知道我这样做，是在给我们俩都埋下祸根啊。

paragraphs.en: He’s full of the Old Scratch, but laws-a-me! he’s my own dead sister’s boy, poor thing, and I ain’t got the heart to lash him, somehow.
paragraphs.cn: 他简直就是个小恶魔，可是哎呀！他是我的亲姐姐留下的孩子，真可怜，我怎么也舍不得打他呀。

paragraphs.en: Every time I let him off, my conscience does hurt me so, and every time I hit him my old heart most breaks.
paragraphs.cn: 每次我放过他，我的良心就觉得不安；每次我打他，我的心都快碎了。

paragraphs.en: Well-a-well, man that is born of woman is of few days and full of trouble, as the Scripture says, and I reckon it’s so.
paragraphs.cn: 唉，算了，人生在世，烦恼可真多啊，书上也是这么说的，我想确实是这样。

paragraphs.en: He’ll play hookey this evening,[*] and I’ll just be obleeged to make him work, tomorrow, to punish him.
paragraphs.cn: 他今天下午肯定又会逃学了，所以我明天只好让他干活，来惩罚他。

paragraphs.en: It’s mighty hard to make him work Saturdays, when all the boys is having holiday, but he hates work more than he hates anything else, and I’ve _got_ to do some of my duty by him, or I’ll be the ruination of the child.”
paragraphs.cn: 星期六让他干活可真难，因为所有的小朋友都在放假，但他最讨厌的就是干活。我必须好好管教他，不然我就毁了这个孩子了。

paragraphs.en: [*] Southwestern for “afternoon”
paragraphs.cn: （这里的意思是“下午”）

paragraphs.en: Tom did play hookey, and he had a very good time.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆确实逃学了，而且玩得很开心。

paragraphs.en: He got back home barely in season to help Jim, the small colored boy, saw next-day’s wood and split the kindlings before supper—at least he was there in time to tell his adventures to Jim while Jim did three-fourths of the work.
paragraphs.cn: 他刚赶回家，正好能帮小黑人男孩吉姆锯第二天的柴火，劈好引火柴，赶在晚饭前做完。至少他赶上了，可以把自己的冒险故事讲给吉姆听，而吉姆呢，则干了四分之三的活儿。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s younger brother (or rather half-brother) Sid was already through with his part of the work (picking up chips), for he was a quiet boy, and had no adventurous, trouble-some ways.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆的弟弟（或者说是同父异母的弟弟）希德已经把他的那份活儿（捡木屑）干完了，因为他是个安静的孩子，从不喜欢冒险，也不惹麻烦。

paragraphs.en: While Tom was eating his supper, and stealing sugar as opportunity offered, Aunt Polly asked him questions that were full of guile, and very deep—for she wanted to trap him into damaging revealments.
paragraphs.cn: 当汤姆吃晚饭的时候，他一有机会就偷吃糖。这时，波莉姨妈问他一些很有心机、很深奥的问题，因为她想让他说漏嘴，说出那些对他不利的秘密。

paragraphs.en: Like many other simple-hearted souls, it was her pet vanity to believe she was endowed with a talent for dark and mysterious diplomacy, and she loved to contemplate her most transparent devices as marvels of low cunning.
paragraphs.cn: 像许多心思单纯的人一样，她最喜欢觉得自己很有计谋，很会玩心眼，甚至觉得她那些一眼就能看穿的小把戏，都是很了不起的聪明才智。

paragraphs.en: Said she:
paragraphs.cn: 她说道：

paragraphs.en: “Tom, it was middling warm in school, warn’t it?”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，学校里是不是有点热呀？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes’m.”
paragraphs.cn: “是的。”

paragraphs.en: “Powerful warm, warn’t it?”
paragraphs.cn: “天气很热，是吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes’m.”
paragraphs.cn: “是的。”

paragraphs.en: “Didn’t you want to go in a-swimming, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: “你不想去游泳吗，汤姆？”

paragraphs.en: A bit of a scare shot through Tom—a touch of uncomfortable suspicion.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆心里有点害怕，感觉有点不对劲。

paragraphs.en: He searched Aunt Polly’s face, but it told him nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 他看着波莉姨妈的脸，但什么也没看出来。

paragraphs.en: So he said:
paragraphs.cn: 他就说：

paragraphs.en: “No’m—well, not very much.”
paragraphs.cn: “不是的——嗯，不太想。”

paragraphs.en: The old lady reached out her hand and felt Tom’s shirt, and said:
paragraphs.cn: 老奶奶伸手摸了摸汤姆的衬衫，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “But you ain’t too warm now, though.”
paragraphs.cn: “不过你现在倒是不热了。”

paragraphs.en: And it flattered her to reflect that she had discovered that the shirt was dry without anybody knowing that that was what she had in her mind.
paragraphs.cn: 她心里很高兴，因为她发现衬衫是干的，而且没人知道她为什么摸衬衫。

paragraphs.en: But in spite of her, Tom knew where the wind lay, now.
paragraphs.cn: 但是，汤姆还是明白了她的意思。

paragraphs.en: So he forestalled what might be the next move:
paragraphs.cn: 于是他抢先一步说：

paragraphs.en: “Some of us pumped on our heads—mine’s damp yet.
paragraphs.cn: “我们有的人用水浇了头，我的头现在还湿着呢。

paragraphs.en: See?”
paragraphs.cn: 你瞧？”

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly was vexed to think she had overlooked that bit of circumstantial evidence, and missed a trick.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈有点不高兴，因为她没想到这一点，也错过了一个机会。

paragraphs.en: Then she had a new inspiration:
paragraphs.cn: 接着她又想到了一个好主意：

paragraphs.en: “Tom, you didn’t have to undo your shirt collar where I sewed it, to pump on your head, did you?
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，你往头上浇水的时候，不用解开我缝好的衣领吧？

paragraphs.en: Unbutton your jacket!”
paragraphs.cn: 解开你的外套！”

paragraphs.en: The trouble vanished out of Tom’s face.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆脸上的担心不见了。

paragraphs.en: He opened his jacket.
paragraphs.cn: 他打开了外套。

paragraphs.en: His shirt collar was securely sewed.
paragraphs.cn: 他的衬衫衣领缝得好好的。

paragraphs.en: “Bother!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀！

paragraphs.en: Well, go ’long with you.
paragraphs.cn: 去吧。

paragraphs.en: I’d made sure you’d played hookey and been a-swimming.
paragraphs.cn: 我还以为你肯定逃学去游泳了呢。

paragraphs.en: But I forgive ye, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 但这次我原谅你，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: I reckon you’re a kind of a singed cat, as the saying is—better’n you look.
paragraphs.cn: 我觉得你呀，就像俗话说的，是个“外表不怎么样，其实很棒”的孩子。

paragraphs.en: _This_ time.”
paragraphs.cn: 就这一次哦。”

paragraphs.en: She was half sorry her sagacity had miscarried, and half glad that Tom had stumbled into obedient conduct for once.
paragraphs.cn: 她有点遗憾自己没猜对，又有点高兴汤姆这次竟然乖乖听话了。

paragraphs.en: But Sidney said:
paragraphs.cn: 但是西德尼说：

paragraphs.en: “Well, now, if I didn’t think you sewed his collar with white thread, but it’s black.”
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，我明明记得你用的是白线，怎么衣领现在是黑的呢？

paragraphs.en: “Why, I did sew it with white!
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，我确实是用白线缝的！

paragraphs.en: Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆！

paragraphs.en: But Tom did not wait for the rest.
paragraphs.cn: 但汤姆没有等他说完。

paragraphs.en: As he went out at the door he said:
paragraphs.cn: 他出门的时候说：

paragraphs.en: “Siddy, I’ll lick you for that.”
paragraphs.cn: “西迪，我会好好教训你的！”

paragraphs.en: In a safe place Tom examined two large needles which were thrust into the lapels of his jacket, and had thread bound about them—one needle carried white thread and the other black.
paragraphs.cn: 在一个没人看见的地方，汤姆看了看他外套领子上的两根大针。针上缠着线，一根是白线，一根是黑线。

paragraphs.en: He said:
paragraphs.cn: 他说：

paragraphs.en: “She’d never noticed if it hadn’t been for Sid.
paragraphs.cn: “要不是希德，她根本不会发现。

paragraphs.en: Confound it! sometimes she sews it with white, and sometimes she sews it with black.
paragraphs.cn: 真是的！她有时用白线缝，有时用黑线缝。

paragraphs.en: I wish to gee-miny she’d stick to one or t’other—I can’t keep the run of ’em.
paragraphs.cn: 我真希望她能一直用一种颜色——我都搞不清了。

paragraphs.en: But I bet you I’ll lam Sid for that.
paragraphs.cn: 但我敢打赌，我会好好揍希德一顿。

paragraphs.en: I’ll learn him!”
paragraphs.cn: 我会教训他的！”

paragraphs.en: He was not the Model Boy of the village.
paragraphs.cn: 他不是村子里的模范男孩。

paragraphs.en: He knew the model boy very well though—and loathed him.
paragraphs.cn: 他虽然认识那个模范男孩——但很讨厌他。

paragraphs.en: Within two minutes, or even less, he had forgotten all his troubles.
paragraphs.cn: 不到两分钟，甚至更短的时间，他就把所有烦恼都忘了。

paragraphs.en: Not because his troubles were one whit less heavy and bitter to him than a man’s are to a man, but because a new and powerful interest bore them down and drove them out of his mind for the time—just as men’s misfortunes are forgotten in the excitement of new enterprises.
paragraphs.cn: 不是因为他的烦恼变小了，而是因为他有了一个新的、很有意思的事情。这事让他一下子把烦恼都忘了。就像大人有了新工作，也会忘了不开心的事情一样。

paragraphs.en: This new interest was a valued novelty in whistling, which he had just acquired from a negro, and he was suffering to practise it undisturbed.
paragraphs.cn: 这个新兴趣是学一种很特别的口哨。他刚从一个人那里学会，现在特别想安静地练习。

paragraphs.en: It consisted in a peculiar bird-like turn, a sort of liquid warble, produced by touching the tongue to the roof of the mouth at short intervals in the midst of the music—the reader probably remembers how to do it, if he has ever been a boy.
paragraphs.cn: 这种口哨特别，听起来像小鸟唱歌。吹的时候，舌头要一直轻轻碰上牙膛。如果你也当过小男孩，可能也知道怎么吹吧。

paragraphs.en: Diligence and attention soon gave him the knack of it, and he strode down the street with his mouth full of harmony and his soul full of gratitude.
paragraphs.cn: 他很认真地练习，很快就学会了。他嘴里吹着好听的曲子，心里美滋滋地走在街上。

paragraphs.en: He felt much as an astronomer feels who has discovered a new planet—no doubt, as far as strong, deep, unalloyed pleasure is concerned, the advantage was with the boy, not the astronomer.
paragraphs.cn: 他开心极了，就像天文学家发现了一颗新星球一样。不过，要说最纯粹、最开心的快乐，这个小男孩肯定比天文学家还高兴。

paragraphs.en: The summer evenings were long.
paragraphs.cn: 夏天的晚上很长。

paragraphs.en: It was not dark, yet.
paragraphs.cn: 天还没黑呢。

paragraphs.en: Presently Tom checked his whistle.
paragraphs.cn: 忽然，汤姆停下了口哨。

paragraphs.en: A stranger was before him—a boy a shade larger than himself.
paragraphs.cn: 他面前站着一个陌生人——一个比他稍微高一点的男孩。

paragraphs.en: A new-comer of any age or either sex was an impressive curiosity in the poor little shabby village of St. Petersburg.
paragraphs.cn: 在圣彼得斯堡这个又小又旧的村子里，不管是大人还是小孩，只要是新来的，大家都会觉得很好奇。

paragraphs.en: This boy was well dressed, too—well dressed on a week-day.
paragraphs.cn: 这个男孩穿得很好，而且还是在平时穿这么好。

paragraphs.en: This was simply astounding.
paragraphs.cn: 这简直太让人惊讶了。

paragraphs.en: His cap was a dainty thing, his close-buttoned blue cloth roundabout was new and natty, and so were his pantaloons.
paragraphs.cn: 他的帽子很精致，紧扣的蓝色短上衣又新又漂亮，裤子也是一样。

paragraphs.en: He had shoes on—and it was only Friday.
paragraphs.cn: 他穿着鞋——而且这天才星期五呢。

paragraphs.en: He even wore a necktie, a bright bit of ribbon.
paragraphs.cn: 他甚至还戴了一条领带，一条亮亮的彩带。

paragraphs.en: He had a citified air about him that ate into Tom’s vitals.
paragraphs.cn: 他一看就像是从城里来的，这让汤姆心里很不舒服。

paragraphs.en: The more Tom stared at the splendid marvel, the higher he turned up his nose at his finery and the shabbier and shabbier his own outfit seemed to him to grow.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆越看这个厉害的小孩，就越觉得他的衣服很漂亮，而自己的衣服却越来越旧。

paragraphs.en: Neither boy spoke.
paragraphs.cn: 两个小孩都没说话。

paragraphs.en: If one moved, the other moved—but only sidewise, in a circle; they kept face to face and eye to eye all the time.
paragraphs.cn: 一个动，另一个也跟着动——只是侧着身子，绕着圈子走；他们一直面对面，眼睛对着眼睛。

paragraphs.en: Finally Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 最后，汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “I can lick you!”
paragraphs.cn: “我能打败你！”

paragraphs.en: “I’d like to see you try it.”
paragraphs.cn: “我倒想看看你怎么打。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I can do it.”
paragraphs.cn: “哼，我就是能！”

paragraphs.en: “No you can’t, either.”
paragraphs.cn: “不，你不能。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes I can.”
paragraphs.cn: “我能！”

paragraphs.en: “No you can’t.”
paragraphs.cn: “你不能！”

paragraphs.en: “I can.”
paragraphs.cn: “我能！”

paragraphs.en: “You can’t.”
paragraphs.cn: “你不能！”

paragraphs.en: “Can!”
“Can’t!”
paragraphs.cn: “不能！”

paragraphs.en: An uncomfortable pause.
paragraphs.cn: 气氛有点僵。

paragraphs.en: Then Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 然后，汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “What’s your name?”
paragraphs.cn: “你叫什么名字？”

paragraphs.en: “’Tisn’t any of your business, maybe.”
paragraphs.cn: “这可能不关你的事。”

paragraphs.en: “Well I ’low I’ll _make_ it my business.”
paragraphs.cn: “哼，我偏要管！”

paragraphs.en: “Well why don’t you?”
paragraphs.cn: “那你怎么还不动手？”

paragraphs.en: “If you say much, I will.”
paragraphs.cn: “你要是再说，我就真动手了。”

paragraphs.en: “Much—much—_much_.
There now.”
paragraphs.cn: 怎么样？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, you think you’re mighty smart, _don’t_ you?
paragraphs.cn: “噢，你觉得自己很聪明，是不是？我一只手绑在后面都能打败你，只要我愿意。”

paragraphs.en: I could lick you with one hand tied behind me, if I wanted to.”
paragraphs.cn: 我就算一只手绑在后面，也能赢你，只要我愿意。

paragraphs.en: “Well why don’t you _do_ it?
paragraphs.cn: “那你怎么还不‘做’呢？你‘说’你能做。”

paragraphs.en: You _say_ you can do it.”
paragraphs.cn: 你说你能做到。

paragraphs.en: “Well I _will_, if you fool with me.”
paragraphs.cn: “哼，你要是再跟我捣乱，我就真‘做’了。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh yes—I’ve seen whole families in the same fix.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，是啊，我见过好多家都遇到过这种事。”

paragraphs.en: “Smarty!
paragraphs.cn: “小聪明鬼！

paragraphs.en: You think you’re _some_, now, _don’t_ you?
paragraphs.cn: 你现在觉得自己很厉害，对不对？

paragraphs.en: Oh, what a hat!”
paragraphs.cn: 哦，这帽子真难看！”

paragraphs.en: “You can lump that hat if you don’t like it.
paragraphs.cn: “你要是不喜欢那帽子，管它呢。

paragraphs.en: I dare you to knock it off—and anybody that’ll take a dare will suck eggs.”
paragraphs.cn: 你敢把它打掉吗？谁要是敢，就是笨蛋！”

paragraphs.en: “You’re a liar!”
paragraphs.cn: “你是个骗子！”

paragraphs.en: “You’re another.”
paragraphs.cn: “你才是！”

paragraphs.en: “You’re a fighting liar and dasn’t take it up.”
paragraphs.cn: “你这个爱打架的骗子，你不敢！”

paragraphs.en: “Aw—take a walk!”
paragraphs.cn: “哎——走开啦！”

paragraphs.en: “Say—if you give me much more of your sass I’ll take and bounce a rock off’n your head.”
paragraphs.cn: “喂，你要是再多嘴，我就拿石头砸你脑袋！”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, of _course_ you will.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，你当然会啦。”

paragraphs.en: “Well I _will_.”
paragraphs.cn: “我就是会。”

paragraphs.en: “Well why don’t you _do_ it then?
paragraphs.cn: “那你为什么不做呢？

paragraphs.en: What do you keep _saying_ you will for?
paragraphs.cn: 你为什么老是说你会做？

paragraphs.en: Why don’t you _do_ it?
paragraphs.cn: 你为什么不做？

paragraphs.en: It’s because you’re afraid.”
paragraphs.cn: 那是因为你害怕！”

paragraphs.en: “I _ain’t_ afraid.”
paragraphs.cn: “我才不怕！”

paragraphs.en: “You are.”
paragraphs.cn: “你就是怕。”

paragraphs.en: “I ain’t.”
paragraphs.cn: “我才不。”

paragraphs.en: “You are.”
paragraphs.cn: “你就是。”

paragraphs.en: Another pause, and more eying and sidling around each other.
paragraphs.cn: 又停了一会儿，他们继续你看看我，我看看你，还互相绕着走。

paragraphs.en: Presently they were shoulder to shoulder.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，他们就肩并肩站着了。

paragraphs.en: Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “Get away from here!”
paragraphs.cn: “走开！”

paragraphs.en: “Go away yourself!”
paragraphs.cn: “你才走开呢！”

paragraphs.en: “I won’t.”
paragraphs.cn: “我偏不。”

paragraphs.en: “I won’t either.”
paragraphs.cn: “我也不。”

paragraphs.en: So they stood, each with a foot placed at an angle as a brace, and both shoving with might and main, and glowering at each other with hate.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们就那样站着，一只脚斜斜地撑着地，使劲地推着对方，互相瞪着眼睛，满是讨厌。

paragraphs.en: But neither could get an advantage.
paragraphs.cn: 但是谁也赢不了谁。

paragraphs.en: After struggling till both were hot and flushed, each relaxed his strain with watchful caution, and Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 两人打得很用力，脸都红了。他们小心地松开，汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “You’re a coward and a pup.
paragraphs.cn: “你这个胆小鬼，小不点儿。

paragraphs.en: I’ll tell my big brother on you, and he can thrash you with his little finger, and I’ll make him do it, too.”
paragraphs.cn: 我会告诉我哥哥，他用小手指头就能把你打趴下，我还要他真这么做！”

paragraphs.en: “What do I care for your big brother?
paragraphs.cn: “我才不怕你哥哥呢！

paragraphs.en: I’ve got a brother that’s bigger than he is—and what’s more, he can throw him over that fence, too.”
paragraphs.cn: 我也有个哥哥，比你哥哥还厉害——他能把你哥哥扔过那边的篱笆呢！”

paragraphs.en: [Both brothers were imaginary.]
paragraphs.cn: （其实两个哥哥都是他们编出来的。）

paragraphs.en: “That’s a lie.”
paragraphs.cn: “你骗人！”

paragraphs.en: “_Your_ saying so don’t make it so.”
paragraphs.cn: “你说不算数！”

paragraphs.en: Tom drew a line in the dust with his big toe, and said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆用大脚趾在土里画了一条线，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “I dare you to step over that, and I’ll lick you till you can’t stand up.
paragraphs.cn: “你敢不敢跨过这条线？我打得你站不起来！

paragraphs.en: Anybody that’ll take a dare will steal sheep.”
paragraphs.cn: 敢这么做的人，都是坏孩子！”

paragraphs.en: The new boy stepped over promptly, and said:
paragraphs.cn: 新来的男孩立刻就跨了过去，他说：

paragraphs.en: “Now you said you’d do it, now let’s see you do it.”
paragraphs.cn: “你刚才说要打我，快来啊，我等着呢！”

paragraphs.en: “Don’t you crowd me now; you better look out.”
paragraphs.cn: “你别逼我！你最好小心点！”

paragraphs.en: “Well, you _said_ you’d do it—why don’t you do it?”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，你不是说要打我吗？怎么不打呀？”

paragraphs.en: “By jingo! for two cents I _will_ do it.”
paragraphs.cn: “哼！只要两分钱，我就打！”

paragraphs.en: The new boy took two broad coppers out of his pocket and held them out with derision.
paragraphs.cn: 新来的男孩从口袋里拿出两枚大铜币，笑着伸了出来。

paragraphs.en: Tom struck them to the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆把钱打到了地上。

paragraphs.en: In an instant both boys were rolling and tumbling in the dirt, gripped together like cats; and for the space of a minute they tugged and tore at each other’s hair and clothes, punched and scratched each other’s nose, and covered themselves with dust and glory.
paragraphs.cn: 瞬间，两个男孩就在泥土里滚来滚去，像小猫一样扭打在一起。他们互相抓头发、扯衣服，还互相打鼻子、挠脸，身上沾满了灰尘。

paragraphs.en: Presently the confusion took form, and through the fog of battle Tom appeared, seated astride the new boy, and pounding him with his fists.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，这场打斗就分出了胜负。从一片尘土中，汤姆出现了，他骑在新来的男孩身上，用拳头打他。

paragraphs.en: “Holler ’nuff!” said he.
paragraphs.cn: “快喊‘我认输’！”他说。

paragraphs.en: The boy only struggled to free himself.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩只是拼命挣扎，想把自己救出来。

paragraphs.en: He was crying—mainly from rage.
paragraphs.cn: 他哭了——主要是气得。

paragraphs.en: “Holler ’nuff!”
paragraphs.cn: “快喊‘我认输’！”

paragraphs.en: —and the pounding went on.
paragraphs.cn: ——拳头还在继续打。

paragraphs.en: At last the stranger got out a smothered “’Nuff!” and Tom let him up and said:
paragraphs.cn: 最后，那个陌生男孩终于小声地喊了句：“我认输了！”汤姆这才让他站起来，说：

paragraphs.en: “Now that’ll learn you.
paragraphs.cn: “这下你该懂了吧。

paragraphs.en: Better look out who you’re fooling with next time.”
paragraphs.cn: 下次再惹我，你可要小心了。”

paragraphs.en: The new boy went off brushing the dust from his clothes, sobbing, snuffling, and occasionally looking back and shaking his head and threatening what he would do to Tom the “next time he caught him out.”
paragraphs.cn: 新来的男孩拍打着身上的灰尘走了，他还在抽泣着，吸着鼻子。他时不时回头，摇着头，威胁说下次再碰到汤姆，一定要好好教训他。

paragraphs.en: To which Tom responded with jeers, and started off in high feather, and as soon as his back was turned the new boy snatched up a stone, threw it and hit him between the shoulders and then turned tail and ran like an antelope.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆嘲笑了他几句，然后得意洋洋地走了。汤姆刚一转身，新来的男孩就抓起一块石头，扔过去打中了汤姆的后背。然后他立马掉头，像羚羊一样跑走了。

paragraphs.en: Tom chased the traitor home, and thus found out where he lived.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆追着那个“坏蛋”回了家，知道了他的住处。

paragraphs.en: He then held a position at the gate for some time, daring the enemy to come outside, but the enemy only made faces at him through the window and declined.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他在门口站了一会儿，挑衅那个“敌人”出来，但“敌人”只在窗户里朝他做鬼脸，不肯出来。

paragraphs.en: At last the enemy’s mother appeared, and called Tom a bad, vicious, vulgar child, and ordered him away.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，“敌人”的妈妈出现了，说汤姆是个坏孩子、没礼貌的孩子，让他走开。

paragraphs.en: So he went away; but he said he “’lowed” to “lay” for that boy.
paragraphs.cn: 所以他走了；但他心里想，他会“盯”上那个男孩的。

paragraphs.en: He got home pretty late that night, and when he climbed cautiously in at the window, he uncovered an ambuscade, in the person of his aunt; and when she saw the state his clothes were in her resolution to turn his Saturday holiday into captivity at hard labor became adamantine in its firmness.
paragraphs.cn: 他那天晚上回家很晚，当他小心翼翼地从窗户爬进去时，发现他阿姨正守在那儿等着他；阿姨看到他衣服很脏，就决定让他周六干苦活，不让他玩了。

paragraphs.en: Saturday morning was come, and all the summer world was bright and fresh, and brimming with life.
paragraphs.cn: 周六早上到了，整个夏天都阳光明媚，充满生机。

paragraphs.en: There was a song in every heart; and if the heart was young the music issued at the lips.
paragraphs.cn: 每个人的心里都有歌声；如果是年轻的心，歌声就会从嘴里唱出来。

paragraphs.en: There was cheer in every face and a spring in every step.
paragraphs.cn: 每个人的脸上都带着笑容，每一步都充满活力。

paragraphs.en: The locust-trees were in bloom and the fragrance of the blossoms filled the air.
paragraphs.cn: 刺槐树开花了，花儿的香味弥漫在空气中。

paragraphs.en: Cardiff Hill, beyond the village and above it, was green with vegetation and it lay just far enough away to seem a Delectable Land, dreamy, reposeful, and inviting.
paragraphs.cn: 卡迪夫山在村子外面，高高的地方，绿草如茵，离得刚刚好，看起来像一个美丽的地方，安静又诱人。

paragraphs.en: Tom appeared on the sidewalk with a bucket of whitewash and a long-handled brush.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆带着一桶石灰水和一把长柄刷子出现在人行道上。

paragraphs.en: He surveyed the fence, and all gladness left him and a deep melancholy settled down upon his spirit.
paragraphs.cn: 他看着那道篱笆墙，所有的快乐都消失了，心里充满了深深的忧伤。

paragraphs.en: Thirty yards of board fence nine feet high.
paragraphs.cn: 三十码长，九英尺高的木板篱笆。

paragraphs.en: Life to him seemed hollow, and existence but a burden.
paragraphs.cn: 对他来说，生活是空虚的，活着就是一种负担。

paragraphs.en: Sighing, he dipped his brush and passed it along the topmost plank; repeated the operation; did it again; compared the insignificant whitewashed streak with the far-reaching continent of unwhitewashed fence, and sat down on a tree-box discouraged.
paragraphs.cn: 他叹了口气，把刷子蘸了一下，刷过最上面那块木板；又刷了一次；再刷了一次；他把那一点点刷白的地方，和远处一大片没刷的篱笆对比了一下，然后沮丧地坐在树箱上。

paragraphs.en: Jim came skipping out at the gate with a tin pail, and singing Buffalo Gals.
paragraphs.cn: 吉姆蹦蹦跳跳地从大门出来，手里提着一个锡桶，嘴里唱着《布法罗姑娘》。

paragraphs.en: Bringing water from the town pump had always been hateful work in Tom’s eyes, before, but now it did not strike him so.
paragraphs.cn: 以前，在汤姆看来，从镇上的水泵打水总是很讨厌的活儿，但现在他却不这么觉得了。

paragraphs.en: He remembered that there was company at the pump.
paragraphs.cn: 他想起来，水泵那里有人。

paragraphs.en: White, mulatto, and negro boys and girls were always there waiting their turns, resting, trading playthings, quarrelling, fighting, skylarking.
paragraphs.cn: 白人、混血儿和黑人男孩女孩总是在那里等着轮流打水，休息，交换玩具，吵架，打架，玩闹。

paragraphs.en: And he remembered that although the pump was only a hundred and fifty yards off, Jim never got back with a bucket of water under an hour—and even then somebody generally had to go after him.
paragraphs.cn: 他还记得，虽然水泵只有一百五十码远，但吉姆打一桶水回来总要一个多小时——而且就算那样，通常也得有人去叫他回来。

paragraphs.en: Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “Say, Jim, I’ll fetch the water if you’ll whitewash some.”
paragraphs.cn: “喂，吉姆，如果你帮我刷墙，我就帮你打水。”

paragraphs.en: Jim shook his head and said:
paragraphs.cn: 吉姆摇了摇头说：

paragraphs.en: “Can’t, Mars Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “不行啊，汤姆少爷。

paragraphs.en: Ole missis, she tole me I got to go an’ git dis water an’ not stop foolin’ roun’ wid anybody.
paragraphs.cn: 老夫人让我去打水，不能跟任何人玩。

paragraphs.en: She say she spec’ Mars Tom gwine to ax me to whitewash, an’ so she tole me go ’long an’ ’tend to my own business—she ’lowed _she’d_ ’tend to de whitewashin’.”
paragraphs.cn: 她说她知道汤姆少爷你会让我刷墙，所以她让我去干自己的事——她说_她_会来刷墙的。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, never you mind what she said, Jim.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，别管她说什么了，吉姆。

paragraphs.en: That’s the way she always talks.
paragraphs.cn: 她总是那么说。

paragraphs.en: Gimme the bucket—I won’t be gone only a a minute.
paragraphs.cn: 把桶给我——我只去一会儿就回来。

paragraphs.en: _She_ won’t ever know.”
paragraphs.cn: _她_永远不会知道的。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I dasn’t, Mars Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，我不敢，汤姆少爷。

paragraphs.en: Ole missis she’d take an’ tar de head off’n me.
paragraphs.cn: 老太太会把我的头拧下来的。

paragraphs.en: ’Deed she would.”
paragraphs.cn: 她真的会的。”

paragraphs.en: “_She_!
paragraphs.cn: “她才不会呢！

paragraphs.en: She never licks anybody—whacks ’em over the head with her thimble—and who cares for that, I’d like to know.
paragraphs.cn: 她从来不打人，就是用顶针敲敲头。那算什么呀，谁会在乎呢？

paragraphs.en: She talks awful, but talk don’t hurt—anyways it don’t if she don’t cry.
paragraphs.cn: 她说话是有点凶，但说话又不会伤人——反正她不哭就没事。

paragraphs.en: Jim, I’ll give you a marvel.
paragraphs.cn: 吉姆，我给你一个弹珠。

paragraphs.en: I’ll give you a white alley!”
paragraphs.cn: 我给你一个白色的玻璃弹珠！”

paragraphs.en: Jim began to waver.
paragraphs.cn: 吉姆开始犹豫了。

paragraphs.en: “White alley, Jim!
paragraphs.cn: “白色的玻璃弹珠啊，吉姆！

paragraphs.en: And it’s a bully taw.”
paragraphs.cn: 这可是一个很棒的弹珠哦。”

paragraphs.en: “My!
Dat’s a mighty gay marvel, I tell you!
paragraphs.cn: 那是一个非常漂亮的弹珠，我跟你说！

paragraphs.en: But Mars Tom I’s powerful ’fraid ole missis—”
paragraphs.cn: 可是汤姆少爷，我真的很怕那个老太太——”

paragraphs.en: “And besides, if you will I’ll show you my sore toe.”
paragraphs.cn: “而且，如果你愿意，我给你看我受伤的脚趾头。”

paragraphs.en: Jim was only human—this attraction was too much for him.
paragraphs.cn: 吉姆也是个普通人——这个诱惑对他来说太大了。

paragraphs.en: He put down his pail, took the white alley, and bent over the toe with absorbing interest while the bandage was being unwound.
paragraphs.cn: 他放下桶，拿起白色的玻璃弹珠，好奇地弯下腰看脚趾头，绷带正在慢慢解开。

paragraphs.en: In another moment he was flying down the street with his pail and a tingling rear, Tom was whitewashing with vigor, and Aunt Polly was retiring from the field with a slipper in her hand and triumph in her eye.
paragraphs.cn: 不一会儿，他就提着桶，屁股刺痛地跑下街了。汤姆正在起劲地刷墙，波莉姨妈手里拿着拖鞋，眼睛里带着胜利的表情，离开了。

paragraphs.en: But Tom’s energy did not last.
paragraphs.cn: 可是汤姆的力气没有持续很久。

paragraphs.en: He began to think of the fun he had planned for this day, and his sorrows multiplied.
paragraphs.cn: 他开始想起今天本来要玩的那些好玩的事，他的烦恼越来越多。

paragraphs.en: Soon the free boys would come tripping along on all sorts of delicious expeditions, and they would make a world of fun of him for having to work—the very thought of it burnt him like fire.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，那些不用干活的小伙伴就会开心地跑过来，去玩各种各样的有趣冒险。他们会嘲笑他还在干活——一想到这，他就气得像火烧一样。

paragraphs.en: He got out his worldly wealth and examined it—bits of toys, marbles, and trash; enough to buy an exchange of _work_, maybe, but not half enough to buy so much as half an hour of pure freedom.
paragraphs.cn: 他拿出他所有的“宝贝”，看了看——一些小玩具、弹珠和垃圾；也许够买来一次“替工”的机会，但连半小时的自由都买不到。

paragraphs.en: So he returned his straitened means to his pocket, and gave up the idea of trying to buy the boys.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他把这些不多的东西放回口袋，放弃了想用钱请小伙伴替他干活的念头。

paragraphs.en: At this dark and hopeless moment an inspiration burst upon him!
paragraphs.cn: 就在这个又黑又没希望的时候，他突然有了一个好主意！

paragraphs.en: Nothing less than a great, magnificent inspiration.
paragraphs.cn: 这可不是一般的好主意，而是一个非常棒的、了不起的主意！

paragraphs.en: He took up his brush and went tranquilly to work.
paragraphs.cn: 他拿起刷子，平静地开始干活了。

paragraphs.en: Ben Rogers hove in sight presently—the very boy, of all boys, whose ridicule he had been dreading.
paragraphs.cn: 本·罗杰斯很快就出现了——这正是他最害怕会嘲笑他的那个孩子。

paragraphs.en: Ben’s gait was the hop-skip-and-jump—proof enough that his heart was light and his anticipations high.
paragraphs.cn: 本边走边跳，开心得不得了，看起来心情很好，对今天充满期待。

paragraphs.en: He was eating an apple, and giving a long, melodious whoop, at intervals, followed by a deep-toned ding-dong-dong, ding-dong-dong, for he was personating a steamboat.
paragraphs.cn: 他一边吃着苹果，一边不时地发出长长的、好听的汽笛声，接着又是“叮咚咚，叮咚咚”的低沉响声，因为他正在假装自己是一艘蒸汽船。

paragraphs.en: As he drew near, he slackened speed, took the middle of the street, leaned far over to starboard and rounded to ponderously and with laborious pomp and circumstance—for he was personating the Big Missouri, and considered himself to be drawing nine feet of water.
paragraphs.cn: 当他走近时，他放慢了速度，走到街中央，身体大大地向右边倾斜，笨重又费力地转了个弯，摆出一副很气派的样子——因为他正在扮演“大密苏里号”蒸汽船，觉得自己像船一样吃水很深。

paragraphs.en: He was boat and captain and engine-bells combined, so he had to imagine himself standing on his own hurricane-deck giving the orders and executing them:
paragraphs.cn: 他既是船，又是船长，还是汽笛声，所以他得想象自己站在船顶上，自己发号施令，自己执行。

paragraphs.en: “Stop her, sir!
paragraphs.cn: “停船，先生！”

paragraphs.en: Ting-a-ling-ling!”
paragraphs.cn: “叮铃铃！”

paragraphs.en: The headway ran almost out, and he drew up slowly toward the sidewalk.
paragraphs.cn: 船慢慢停了下来，他缓缓地靠向了岸边。

paragraphs.en: “Ship up to back!
paragraphs.cn: “倒船！”

paragraphs.en: Ting-a-ling-ling!”
paragraphs.cn: “叮铃铃！”

paragraphs.en: His arms straightened and stiffened down his sides.
paragraphs.cn: 他的胳膊伸得直直的，贴在身体两边，一动不动。

paragraphs.en: “Set her back on the stabboard!
paragraphs.cn: “向右倒船！”

paragraphs.en: Ting-a-ling-ling!
paragraphs.cn: “叮铃铃！”

paragraphs.en: Chow! ch-chow-wow!
paragraphs.cn: “嘟！嘟-嘟-呜！”

paragraphs.en: Chow!”
His right hand, mean-time, describing stately circles—for it was representing a forty-foot wheel.
paragraphs.cn: 同时，他的右手画着大大的圈，那是在模仿一个四十英尺的大轮子。

paragraphs.en: “Let her go back on the labboard!
paragraphs.cn: “向左倒船！”

paragraphs.en: Ting-a-ling-ling!
paragraphs.cn: “叮铃铃！”

paragraphs.en: Chow-ch-chow-chow!”
paragraphs.cn: “嘟-嘟-嘟-嘟！”

paragraphs.en: The left hand began to describe circles.
paragraphs.cn: 他的左手也开始画圈了。

paragraphs.en: “Stop the stabboard!
paragraphs.cn: “右舷停！”

paragraphs.en: Ting-a-ling-ling!
paragraphs.cn: “叮铃铃！”

paragraphs.en: Stop the labboard!
paragraphs.cn: “左舷停！”

paragraphs.en: Come ahead on the stabboard!
paragraphs.cn: “右舷前进！”

paragraphs.en: Stop her!
paragraphs.cn: “停船！”

paragraphs.en: Let your outside turn over slow!
paragraphs.cn: “让船慢慢转过去！”

paragraphs.en: Ting-a-ling-ling!
paragraphs.cn: “叮铃铃！”

paragraphs.en: Chow-ow-ow!
Get out that head-line!
paragraphs.cn: “把船头缆绳拉出来！”

paragraphs.en: _lively_ now!
paragraphs.cn: “快点！”

paragraphs.en: Come—out with your spring-line—what’re you about there!
paragraphs.cn: “快把你的缆绳也放出去！你在干什么呢！”

paragraphs.en: Take a turn round that stump with the bight of it!
paragraphs.cn: “用绳子在那个木桩上绕一圈！”

paragraphs.en: Stand by that stage, now—let her go!
paragraphs.cn: “准备好那个踏板，现在——放开！”

paragraphs.en: Done with the engines, sir!
paragraphs.cn: “引擎操作好了，先生！”

paragraphs.en: Ting-a-ling-ling!
paragraphs.cn: 叮铃铃！

paragraphs.en: SH’T!
S’H’T!
SH’T!”
(trying the gauge-cocks).
paragraphs.cn: (试着去扳那些小把手)。

paragraphs.en: Tom went on whitewashing—paid no attention to the steamboat.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆继续刷白墙，没理那艘蒸汽船。

paragraphs.en: Ben stared a moment and then said: “_Hi-Yi!
paragraphs.cn: 本盯着看了一会儿，然后说：“喂——！

paragraphs.en: You’re_ up a stump, ain’t you!”
paragraphs.cn: 你可真被难住了，是吧！”

paragraphs.en: No answer.
paragraphs.cn: 没有回答。

paragraphs.en: Tom surveyed his last touch with the eye of an artist, then he gave his brush another gentle sweep and surveyed the result, as before.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆像艺术家一样看看自己刚刷的地方，然后又轻轻刷了一下，再像之前那样看看效果。

paragraphs.en: Ben ranged up alongside of him.
paragraphs.cn: 本走到他身边。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s mouth watered for the apple, but he stuck to his work.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆看到苹果口水都要流出来了，但他还是坚持工作。

paragraphs.en: Ben said:
paragraphs.cn: 本说：

paragraphs.en: “Hello, old chap, you got to work, hey?”
paragraphs.cn: “嘿，老朋友，你得干活儿了，是吗？”

paragraphs.en: Tom wheeled suddenly and said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆突然转过身，说：

paragraphs.en: “Why, it’s you, Ben!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，是本啊！

paragraphs.en: I warn’t noticing.”
paragraphs.cn: 我都没注意到你。”

paragraphs.en: “Say—I’m going in a-swimming, I am.
paragraphs.cn: “听着——我要去游泳了，我真要去。

paragraphs.en: Don’t you wish you could?
paragraphs.cn: 你是不是也想去？

paragraphs.en: But of course you’d druther _work_—wouldn’t you?
paragraphs.cn: 不过你当然更喜欢_干活儿_——不是吗？

paragraphs.en: Course you would!”
paragraphs.cn: 你当然会！”

paragraphs.en: Tom contemplated the boy a bit, and said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆看了看那个男孩，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “What do you call work?”
paragraphs.cn: “你管这叫干活儿吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, ain’t _that_ work?”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，_这_不是工作吗？”

paragraphs.en: Tom resumed his whitewashing, and answered carelessly:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆继续刷白墙，随便地回答说：

paragraphs.en: “Well, maybe it is, and maybe it ain’t.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，也许是吧，也许不是。

paragraphs.en: All I know, is, it suits Tom Sawyer.”
paragraphs.cn: 我只知道，它很适合汤姆·索亚。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh come, now, you don’t mean to let on that you _like_ it?”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，得了吧，你不会是想说你_喜欢_它吧？”

paragraphs.en: The brush continued to move.
paragraphs.cn: 刷子继续动着。

paragraphs.en: “Like it?
paragraphs.cn: “喜欢它？

paragraphs.en: Well, I don’t see why I oughtn’t to like it.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，我觉得挺好的呀。

paragraphs.en: Does a boy get a chance to whitewash a fence every day?”
paragraphs.cn: 不是每天都能刷墙的，对不对？

paragraphs.en: That put the thing in a new light.
paragraphs.cn: 这下本明白过来了。

paragraphs.en: Ben stopped nibbling his apple.
paragraphs.cn: 本不啃苹果了。

paragraphs.en: Tom swept his brush daintily back and forth—stepped back to note the effect—added a touch here and there—criticised the effect again—Ben watching every move and getting more and more interested, more and more absorbed.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆轻轻地来回刷着，然后退后看看效果，这里补一点，那里加一笔，又看看。本盯着他，看得越来越入迷，越来越想试试。

paragraphs.en: Presently he said:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，他说：

paragraphs.en: “Say, Tom, let _me_ whitewash a little.”
paragraphs.cn: “喂，汤姆，让我刷一会儿好不好？”

paragraphs.en: Tom considered, was about to consent; but he altered his mind:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆想了想，本来想答应，但又改主意了：

paragraphs.en: “No—no—I reckon it wouldn’t hardly do, Ben.
paragraphs.cn: “不行，不行，本，我觉得这不太好。

paragraphs.en: You see, Aunt Polly’s awful particular about this fence—right here on the street, you know—but if it was the back fence I wouldn’t mind and _she_ wouldn’t.
paragraphs.cn: 你看，波莉姨妈对这面墙很讲究的，你知道，就在街边上。要是后面的墙，我就不介意，她也不会。

paragraphs.en: Yes, she’s awful particular about this fence; it’s got to be done very careful; I reckon there ain’t one boy in a thousand, maybe two thousand, that can do it the way it’s got to be done.”
paragraphs.cn: 是啊，她对这面墙特别认真。得刷得很仔细才行。我想啊，一千个小孩里，可能两千个小孩里，都找不出一个能刷得像样子的。”

paragraphs.en: “No—is that so?
paragraphs.cn: “啊？真的吗？

paragraphs.en: Oh come, now—lemme just try.
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，让我试试嘛。

paragraphs.en: Only just a little—I’d let _you_, if you was me, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: 就刷一点点。要是我是你，汤姆，我肯定让你刷的。”

paragraphs.en: “Ben, I’d like to, honest injun; but Aunt Polly—well, Jim wanted to do it, but she wouldn’t let him; Sid wanted to do it, and she wouldn’t let Sid.
paragraphs.cn: “本，我真想让你刷。但是波莉姨妈——你看，吉姆想刷，她不让他刷；希德也想刷，她也不让希德刷。

paragraphs.en: Now don’t you see how I’m fixed?
paragraphs.cn: 你看看我现在多难办啊？

paragraphs.en: If you was to tackle this fence and anything was to happen to it—”
paragraphs.cn: 要是你刷这面墙，万一弄坏了—”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, shucks, I’ll be just as careful.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，我肯定会很小心的！

paragraphs.en: Now lemme try.
paragraphs.cn: 让我试试嘛。

paragraphs.en: Say—I’ll give you the core of my apple.”
paragraphs.cn: 这样吧——我的苹果核给你！”

paragraphs.en: “Well, here—No, Ben, now don’t.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，这个嘛——不行，本，别这样。

paragraphs.en: I’m afeard—”
paragraphs.cn: 我怕——”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll give you _all_ of it!”
paragraphs.cn: “我把整个苹果都给你！”

paragraphs.en: Tom gave up the brush with reluctance in his face, but alacrity in his heart.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆脸上虽然不情愿，心里却很开心，把刷子给了本。

paragraphs.en: And while the late steamer Big Missouri worked and sweated in the sun, the retired artist sat on a barrel in the shade close by, dangled his legs, munched his apple, and planned the slaughter of more innocents.
paragraphs.cn: 就在大密苏里号“努力工作”晒太阳的时候，这位“退休画家”坐在旁边阴凉处的桶上，晃着腿，吃着苹果，盘算着怎么让更多的小孩来刷墙。

paragraphs.en: There was no lack of material; boys happened along every little while; they came to jeer, but remained to whitewash.
paragraphs.cn: 他一点也不缺“材料”；不一会儿就有小孩经过。他们本来是来看笑话的，结果都留下来刷墙了。

paragraphs.en: By the time Ben was fagged out, Tom had traded the next chance to Billy Fisher for a kite, in good repair; and when he played out, Johnny Miller bought in for a dead rat and a string to swing it with—and so on, and so on, hour after hour.
paragraphs.cn: 等本累得不行了，汤姆又把下一个刷墙的机会，用一个完好的风筝换给了比利·费舍尔。比利刷累了，约翰尼·米勒又用一只死老鼠和一根绳子换到了刷墙的机会——就这样，一个小时又一个小时地过去了。

paragraphs.en: And when the middle of the afternoon came, from being a poor poverty-stricken boy in the morning, Tom was literally rolling in wealth.
paragraphs.cn: 到了下午，早上还是个穷小子，汤姆这会儿已经“财源滚滚”了！

paragraphs.en: He had besides the things before mentioned, twelve marbles, part of a jews-harp, a piece of blue bottle-glass to look through, a spool cannon, a key that wouldn’t unlock anything, a fragment of chalk, a glass stopper of a decanter, a tin soldier, a couple of tadpoles, six fire-crackers, a kitten with only one eye, a brass door-knob, a dog-collar—but no dog—the handle of a knife, four pieces of orange-peel, and a dilapidated old window sash.
paragraphs.cn: 除了刚才说的那些东西，他还得了十二颗弹珠，口琴的一部分，一块蓝色的玻璃片（可以透过它看东西），一个线轴大炮，一把打不开任何东西的钥匙，一小块粉笔，一个玻璃瓶塞，一个锡兵，两只小蝌蚪，六个鞭炮，一只独眼小猫，一个黄铜门把手，一个狗项圈（可没有狗），一个刀把，四片橘子皮，还有一个破旧的窗框。

paragraphs.en: He had had a nice, good, idle time all the while—plenty of company—and the fence had three coats of whitewash on it!
paragraphs.cn: 他一直过得很开心，很悠闲，还有很多小伙伴陪着——而且墙上已经刷了三层白漆了！

paragraphs.en: If he hadn’t run out of whitewash he would have bankrupted every boy in the village.
paragraphs.cn: 如果他的白石灰没用完，他就会让村里所有的小朋友都把自己的东西给他。

paragraphs.en: Tom said to himself that it was not such a hollow world, after all.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆心想，原来这个世界并没有那么糟嘛。

paragraphs.en: He had discovered a great law of human action, without knowing it—namely, that in order to make a man or a boy covet a thing, it is only necessary to make the thing difficult to attain.
paragraphs.cn: 他发现了一个大秘密：要想让一个人或一个小朋友想要一件东西，只要让这东西不好得到就行了。

paragraphs.en: If he had been a great and wise philosopher, like the writer of this book, he would now have comprehended that Work consists of whatever a body is _obliged_ to do, and that Play consists of whatever a body is not obliged to do.
paragraphs.cn: 如果他很聪明，像写这本书的人一样，他就会明白：_必须_做的事叫工作，_不用_做的事叫玩耍。

paragraphs.en: And this would help him to understand why constructing artificial flowers or performing on a tread-mill is work, while rolling ten-pins or climbing Mont Blanc is only amusement.
paragraphs.cn: 这样他就能明白，为什么做假花或在跑步机上跑是工作，而打保龄球或爬勃朗峰却是玩。

paragraphs.en: There are wealthy gentlemen in England who drive four-horse passenger-coaches twenty or thirty miles on a daily line, in the summer, because the privilege costs them considerable money; but if they were offered wages for the service, that would turn it into work and then they would resign.
paragraphs.cn: 在英国，有些有钱的先生夏天喜欢开四马马车，每天跑很远。因为这要花很多钱，所以他们觉得好玩。但如果别人给他们钱让他们做这个，这就会变成工作，他们就不干了。

paragraphs.en: The boy mused awhile over the substantial change which had taken place in his worldly circumstances, and then wended toward headquarters to report.
paragraphs.cn: 小朋友想了想自己现在变厉害了，然后就往家走去报告。

paragraphs.en: Tom presented himself before Aunt Polly, who was sitting by an open window in a pleasant rearward apartment, which was bedroom, breakfast-room, dining-room, and library, combined.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆走到波莉姨妈面前。波莉姨妈正坐在一扇开着的窗户旁边，房间很舒服，在屋子后面。这个房间是卧室、早餐室、餐厅和书房的组合。

paragraphs.en: The balmy summer air, the restful quiet, the odor of the flowers, and the drowsing murmur of the bees had had their effect, and she was nodding over her knitting—for she had no company but the cat, and it was asleep in her lap.
paragraphs.cn: 夏天暖暖的风吹着，周围很安静。花儿香香的，小蜜蜂嗡嗡叫。她织着毛衣，头一点一点的，快睡着了。只有猫咪陪着她，猫咪也在她腿上睡着了。

paragraphs.en: Her spectacles were propped up on her gray head for safety.
paragraphs.cn: 她的眼镜安全地架在她的白头发上。

paragraphs.en: She had thought that of course Tom had deserted long ago, and she wondered at seeing him place himself in her power again in this intrepid way.
paragraphs.cn: 她以为汤姆早就跑掉了，没想到他又这么大胆地自己回来了，让她很惊讶。

paragraphs.en: He said: “Mayn’t I go and play now, aunt?”
paragraphs.cn: 他说：“我现在可以去玩了吗，姨妈？”

paragraphs.en: “What, a’ready?
paragraphs.cn: “什么？这么快？”

paragraphs.en: How much have you done?”
paragraphs.cn: “你刷了多少呀？”

paragraphs.en: “It’s all done, aunt.”
paragraphs.cn: “都刷完了，姨妈。”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, don’t lie to me—I can’t bear it.”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，不要骗我——我可受不了。”

paragraphs.en: “I ain’t, aunt; it _is_ all done.”
paragraphs.cn: “我没骗您，姨妈；真的都刷完了。”

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly placed small trust in such evidence.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈不太相信这些话。

paragraphs.en: She went out to see for herself; and she would have been content to find twenty per cent. of Tom’s statement true.
paragraphs.cn: 她自己出去看了一下；她本来以为，就算汤姆说的话有百分之二十是真的，她都会很高兴了。

paragraphs.en: When she found the entire fence white-washed, and not only whitewashed but elaborately coated and recoated, and even a streak added to the ground, her astonishment was almost unspeakable.
paragraphs.cn: 当她发现整面围墙都刷白了，而且不只刷了一层，还刷得又厚又仔细，甚至连地上都有一道白漆，她的惊讶简直无法形容。

paragraphs.en: She said:
paragraphs.cn: 她说：

paragraphs.en: “Well, I never!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，真没想到！”

paragraphs.en: There’s no getting round it, you can work when you’re a mind to, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “没法不承认，汤姆，你真想做的时候，还是能干活的。”

paragraphs.en: And then she diluted the compliment by adding, “But it’s powerful seldom you’re a mind to, I’m bound to say.
paragraphs.cn: 然后她接着又说：“不过你很少这么想做，我得说实话。”

paragraphs.en: Well, go ’long and play; but mind you get back some time in a week, or I’ll tan you.”
paragraphs.cn: “好了，去玩吧；不过记住，一个星期内一定要回来，不然我就要打你的屁股了。”

paragraphs.en: She was so overcome by the splendor of his achievement that she took him into the closet and selected a choice apple and delivered it to him, along with an improving lecture upon the added value and flavor a treat took to itself when it came without sin through virtuous effort.
paragraphs.cn: 她看他做得那么好，特别开心。她带他到柜子旁，挑了一个又大又甜的苹果给他。她还告诉他，不犯错，自己努力得到的奖励，吃起来才更甜更好吃。

paragraphs.en: And while she closed with a happy Scriptural flourish, he “hooked” a doughnut.
paragraphs.cn: 就在她开心地引用《圣经》讲完话的时候，他悄悄地“偷”了一个甜甜圈。

paragraphs.en: Then he skipped out, and saw Sid just starting up the outside stairway that led to the back rooms on the second floor.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他蹦蹦跳跳地跑了出去，看到希德正要走上通往二楼后屋的室外楼梯。

paragraphs.en: Clods were handy and the air was full of them in a twinkling.
paragraphs.cn: 地上的土块正好在手边，眨眼间，空中就到处都是土块了。

paragraphs.en: They raged around Sid like a hail-storm; and before Aunt Polly could collect her surprised faculties and sally to the rescue, six or seven clods had taken personal effect, and Tom was over the fence and gone.
paragraphs.cn: 土块像冰雹一样打在希德的周围；还没等波莉姨妈反应过来要去帮忙，六七块土块就已经打到了他，然后汤姆就翻过围墙跑走了。

paragraphs.en: There was a gate, but as a general thing he was too crowded for time to make use of it.
paragraphs.cn: 有扇门，但他平时太忙了，没时间用它。

paragraphs.en: His soul was at peace, now that he had settled with Sid for calling attention to his black thread and getting him into trouble.
paragraphs.cn: 他心里踏实了，因为他已经和希德说好了，之前希德提到了他的黑线，让他惹了麻烦。

paragraphs.en: Tom skirted the block, and came round into a muddy alley that led by the back of his aunt’s cow-stable.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆绕过街区，来到一条泥泞的小巷，这条小巷在他姨妈的牛棚后面。

paragraphs.en: He presently got safely beyond the reach of capture and punishment, and hastened toward the public square of the village, where two “military” companies of boys had met for conflict, according to previous appointment.
paragraphs.cn: 他很快就安全了，没有人能抓住他或惩罚他。他赶紧去了村里的广场，那里有两队“小兵”男孩，他们之前约好了要打仗。

paragraphs.en: Tom was General of one of these armies, Joe Harper (a bosom friend) General of the other.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆是其中一队小兵的将军，乔·哈珀（他的好朋友）是另一队的将军。

paragraphs.en: These two great commanders did not condescend to fight in person—that being better suited to the still smaller fry—but sat together on an eminence and conducted the field operations by orders delivered through aides-de-camp.
paragraphs.cn: 这两位大将军不自己上阵打仗——那是小小孩做的事。他们坐在一起，在高处指挥战斗，通过传令兵下达命令。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s army won a great victory, after a long and hard-fought battle.
paragraphs.cn: 经过一场又长又难的战斗，汤姆的小兵们赢了大胜仗。

paragraphs.en: Then the dead were counted, prisoners exchanged, the terms of the next disagreement agreed upon, and the day for the necessary battle appointed; after which the armies fell into line and marched away, and Tom turned homeward alone.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，他们数了“阵亡”的人，交换了“俘虏”，还约定了下次打仗的规矩和时间。然后，小兵们排好队走开了，汤姆一个人回家了。

paragraphs.en: As he was passing by the house where Jeff Thatcher lived, he saw a new girl in the garden—a lovely little blue-eyed creature with yellow hair plaited into two long-tails, white summer frock and embroidered pantalettes.
paragraphs.cn: 他经过杰夫·撒切尔家的时候，看到花园里有个新来的小女孩。她有一双蓝眼睛，黄色的头发编成两条长辫子，穿着白色夏装和绣花裤子，非常可爱。

paragraphs.en: The fresh-crowned hero fell without firing a shot.
paragraphs.cn: 那个刚当上英雄的小男孩，还没“开枪”呢，就“倒”了。

paragraphs.en: A certain Amy Lawrence vanished out of his heart and left not even a memory of herself behind.
paragraphs.cn: 某个艾米·劳伦斯从他心里消失了，连一点回忆都没留下。

paragraphs.en: He had thought he loved her to distraction; he had regarded his passion as adoration; and behold it was only a poor little evanescent partiality.
paragraphs.cn: 他以为自己爱她爱得很疯狂；他以为那份爱是崇拜。可没想到，那只是一点点很快就消失的小喜欢。

paragraphs.en: He had been months winning her; she had confessed hardly a week ago; he had been the happiest and the proudest boy in the world only seven short days, and here in one instant of time she had gone out of his heart like a casual stranger whose visit is done.
paragraphs.cn: 他花了几个月才让她喜欢上自己；她才刚答应他不到一周。他才当了七天全世界最开心最骄傲的男孩，可就在这一瞬间，她就从他心里离开了，就像一个客人走了一样。

paragraphs.en: He worshipped this new angel with furtive eye, till he saw that she had discovered him; then he pretended he did not know she was present, and began to “show off” in all sorts of absurd boyish ways, in order to win her admiration.
paragraphs.cn: 他偷偷地看着这位新来的“小天使”，直到发现她也看到了他。然后，他假装不知道她在，开始用各种好笑的男孩方式“炫耀”，想让她喜欢他。

paragraphs.en: He kept up this grotesque foolishness for some time; but by-and-by, while he was in the midst of some dangerous gymnastic performances, he glanced aside and saw that the little girl was wending her way toward the house.
paragraphs.cn: 他这样傻傻地“炫耀”了一会儿。过了一阵子，当他正在做一些危险的“体操表演”时，他瞟了一眼，发现小女孩正往房子那边走去。

paragraphs.en: Tom came up to the fence and leaned on it, grieving, and hoping she would tarry yet awhile longer.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆走到篱笆边，靠在上面，心里很难过，希望她能再多呆一会儿。

paragraphs.en: She halted a moment on the steps and then moved toward the door.
paragraphs.cn: 她在台阶上停了一会儿，然后走向门。

paragraphs.en: Tom heaved a great sigh as she put her foot on the threshold.
paragraphs.cn: 当她把脚踏上门槛时，汤姆深深地叹了口气。

paragraphs.en: But his face lit up, right away, for she tossed a pansy over the fence a moment before she disappeared.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，他的脸马上亮了起来！因为在她消失之前，她朝篱笆外面扔了一朵三色堇。

paragraphs.en: The boy ran around and stopped within a foot or two of the flower, and then shaded his eyes with his hand and began to look down street as if he had discovered something of interest going on in that direction.
paragraphs.cn: 小男孩跑过去，在离花朵一两英尺的地方停下。然后他用手遮住眼睛，开始沿着街往下看，好像他发现那个方向有什么有趣的事情正在发生。

paragraphs.en: Presently he picked up a straw and began trying to balance it on his nose, with his head tilted far back; and as he moved from side to side, in his efforts, he edged nearer and nearer toward the pansy; finally his bare foot rested upon it, his pliant toes closed upon it, and he hopped away with the treasure and disappeared round the corner.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，他捡起一根草，头往后仰，试着把它平衡在鼻子上。他一边左右晃动，一边努力地靠近三色堇；最后，他的光脚踩到了它，柔软的脚趾夹住了它，然后他带着这个“宝贝”跳着跑开了，在拐角处消失了。

paragraphs.en: But only for a minute—only while he could button the flower inside his jacket, next his heart—or next his stomach, possibly, for he was not much posted in anatomy, and not hypercritical, anyway.
paragraphs.cn: 但只是一会儿——只是他把花扣在夹克里，靠近他的心——或者靠近他的肚子，也可能是这样，因为他对人体结构不太懂，反正他也不太讲究。

paragraphs.en: He returned, now, and hung about the fence till nightfall, “showing off,” as before; but the girl never exhibited herself again, though Tom comforted himself a little with the hope that she had been near some window, meantime, and been aware of his attentions.
paragraphs.cn: 他现在又回来了，在篱笆边晃到天黑，像之前一样“炫耀”。但那个女孩再也没出现过，不过汤姆安慰自己说，她可能一直在某个窗户边，看到了他的举动。

paragraphs.en: Finally he strode home reluctantly, with his poor head full of visions.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，他很不情愿地大步走回家，脑子里装满了各种幻想。

paragraphs.en: All through supper his spirits were so high that his aunt wondered “what had got into the child.”
paragraphs.cn: 整个晚饭时间，他都特别高兴，他姨妈很奇怪“这孩子怎么了”。

paragraphs.en: He took a good scolding about clodding Sid, and did not seem to mind it in the least.
paragraphs.cn: 他因为用土块砸希德被好好骂了一顿，但他一点都不介意。

paragraphs.en: He tried to steal sugar under his aunt’s very nose, and got his knuckles rapped for it.
paragraphs.cn: 他当着姨妈的面，想偷糖吃，结果手背被打了。

paragraphs.en: He said:
paragraphs.cn: 他说：

paragraphs.en: “Aunt, you don’t whack Sid when he takes it.”
paragraphs.cn: “姨妈，希德拿糖的时候，你可没打他。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, Sid don’t torment a body the way you do.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，希德可不像你这样折腾人。”

paragraphs.en: You’d be always into that sugar if I warn’t watching you.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果我不看着你，你肯定会一直偷吃糖。”

paragraphs.en: Presently she stepped into the kitchen, and Sid, happy in his immunity, reached for the sugar-bowl—a sort of glorying over Tom which was wellnigh unbearable.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，她走进了厨房。希德 觉得自己没事了，高兴地去拿糖罐——他有点得意地看了一眼 汤姆，让 汤姆 几乎气坏了。

paragraphs.en: But Sid’s fingers slipped and the bowl dropped and broke.
paragraphs.cn: 可是 希德 的手滑了一下，糖罐掉下去摔碎了。

paragraphs.en: Tom was in ecstasies.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 高兴坏了。

paragraphs.en: In such ecstasies that he even controlled his tongue and was silent.
paragraphs.cn: 他高兴得连话都不说了，一声不吭。

paragraphs.en: He said to himself that he would not speak a word, even when his aunt came in, but would sit perfectly still till she asked who did the mischief; and then he would tell, and there would be nothing so good in the world as to see that pet model “catch it.”
paragraphs.cn: 他心里想，阿姨进来他也不说话。他会一动不动地坐着，直到阿姨问是谁弄坏的。然后他就会告诉阿姨，看到那个被宠坏的家伙被骂，那会是世界上最开心的事情。

paragraphs.en: He was so brimful of exultation that he could hardly hold himself when the old lady came back and stood above the wreck discharging lightnings of wrath from over her spectacles.
paragraphs.cn: 他高兴得快要忍不住了。奶奶回来了，她站在摔碎的糖罐旁边，透过眼镜，气呼呼地瞪着。

paragraphs.en: He said to himself, “Now it’s coming!”
paragraphs.cn: 他心想：“这下要来了！”

paragraphs.en: And the next instant he was sprawling on the floor!
paragraphs.cn: 就在下一秒，他一下子摔倒在地！

paragraphs.en: The potent palm was uplifted to strike again when Tom cried out:
paragraphs.cn: 那只厉害的手又要打下来了，这时 汤姆 大声喊道：

paragraphs.en: “Hold on, now, what ’er you belting _me_ for?
paragraphs.cn: “等等！你为什么要打我？”

paragraphs.en: —Sid broke it!”
paragraphs.cn: “——是 希德 弄坏的！”

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly paused, perplexed, and Tom looked for healing pity.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈 停住了，有点懵。汤姆 等着别人来安慰她。

paragraphs.en: But when she got her tongue again, she only said:
paragraphs.cn: 但当她又能说话时，她只说了一句：

paragraphs.en: “Umf!
Well, you didn’t get a lick amiss, I reckon.
paragraphs.cn: 我想你挨打一点都没错。

paragraphs.en: You been into some other audacious mischief when I wasn’t around, like enough.”
paragraphs.cn: 你肯定在我不在的时候，还做了其他淘气的事情，大概就是这样！”

paragraphs.en: Then her conscience reproached her, and she yearned to say something kind and loving; but she judged that this would be construed into a confession that she had been in the wrong, and discipline forbade that.
paragraphs.cn: 她的心里有点不舒服，很想说些温柔的话。但她又觉得，那样就好像承认自己错了，所以她不能说。

paragraphs.en: So she kept silence, and went about her affairs with a troubled heart.
paragraphs.cn: 于是她什么也没说，心里带着一丝不安去忙自己的事了。

paragraphs.en: Tom sulked in a corner and exalted his woes.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 独自在角落里生闷气，还觉得自己特别可怜。

paragraphs.en: He knew that in her heart his aunt was on her knees to him, and he was morosely gratified by the consciousness of it.
paragraphs.cn: 他知道姑妈心里肯定觉得对不起他，他嘴上不说，心里却有点得意。

paragraphs.en: He would hang out no signals, he would take notice of none.
paragraphs.cn: 他什么表示都没有，也假装没看到任何表示。

paragraphs.en: He knew that a yearning glance fell upon him, now and then, through a film of tears, but he refused recognition of it.
paragraphs.cn: 他知道姑妈有时会带着泪水，用想和好的眼神看他，但他假装没看见。

paragraphs.en: He pictured himself lying sick unto death and his aunt bending over him beseeching one little forgiving word, but he would turn his face to the wall, and die with that word unsaid.
paragraphs.cn: 他想象自己病得很重，快要死了。姑妈弯着腰求他，希望他说一句原谅的话，但他会把脸转向墙壁，一句话也不说就死了。

paragraphs.en: Ah, how would she feel then?
paragraphs.cn: 唉，那时她会怎么样呢？

paragraphs.en: And he pictured himself brought home from the river, dead, with his curls all wet, and his sore heart at rest.
paragraphs.cn: 他还想象自己从河里被抬回家，已经死了，卷发都湿透了，他那颗难过的心也终于平静下来了。

paragraphs.en: How she would throw herself upon him, and how her tears would fall like rain, and her lips pray God to give her back her boy and she would never, never abuse him any more!
paragraphs.cn: 她会扑到他身上，眼泪像下雨一样，嘴里会求上帝把她的孩子还给她，说再也不会，再也不会欺负他了！

paragraphs.en: But he would lie there cold and white and make no sign—a poor little sufferer, whose griefs were at an end.
paragraphs.cn: 但他会冰冰冷冷、白白的躺在那里，什么反应都没有——一个可怜的小家伙，所有的难过都结束了。

paragraphs.en: He so worked upon his feelings with the pathos of these dreams, that he had to keep swallowing, he was so like to choke; and his eyes swam in a blur of water, which overflowed when he winked, and ran down and trickled from the end of his nose.
paragraphs.cn: 他被这些想象出来的难过故事感动得不行，一个劲儿地吞口水，感觉都要哭出来了；他的眼睛里模糊一片，都是泪水，他一眨眼，泪水就流出来，从鼻尖滴了下来。

paragraphs.en: And such a luxury to him was this petting of his sorrows, that he could not bear to have any worldly cheeriness or any grating delight intrude upon it; it was too sacred for such contact; and so, presently, when his cousin Mary danced in, all alive with the joy of seeing home again after an age-long visit of one week to the country, he got up and moved in clouds and darkness out at one door as she brought song and sunshine in at the other.
paragraphs.cn: 他很喜欢沉浸在自己的悲伤里，不希望任何开心的事来打扰他；因为这对他来说太重要了。所以，当他的表妹 玛丽 蹦蹦跳跳地跑进来时，她因为在乡下玩了一周回家而高兴得不得了，他却闷闷不乐地从另一扇门走出去，而她把歌声和阳光带进了屋里。

paragraphs.en: He wandered far from the accustomed haunts of boys, and sought desolate places that were in harmony with his spirit.
paragraphs.cn: 他没有去小朋友们常去玩的地方，而是跑到很远很安静的地方，感觉那里很适合他。

paragraphs.en: A log raft in the river invited him, and he seated himself on its outer edge and contemplated the dreary vastness of the stream, wishing, the while, that he could only be drowned, all at once and unconsciously, without undergoing the uncomfortable routine devised by nature.
paragraphs.cn: 河里有个木筏，他坐到木筏边上，看着又大又冷的河水。他心里想，要是能一下子沉下去，什么都不知道就好了。

paragraphs.en: Then he thought of his flower.
paragraphs.cn: 然后，他想起了他的那朵花。

paragraphs.en: He got it out, rumpled and wilted, and it mightily increased his dismal felicity.
paragraphs.cn: 他把花拿出来，花已经皱巴巴的，也枯萎了。这让他心里更难过了。

paragraphs.en: He wondered if she would pity him if she knew?
paragraphs.cn: 他想，如果她知道了，会可怜他吗？

paragraphs.en: Would she cry, and wish that she had a right to put her arms around his neck and comfort him?
paragraphs.cn: 她会哭吗？会想抱抱他，安慰他吗？

paragraphs.en: Or would she turn coldly away like all the hollow world?
paragraphs.cn: 还是会像其他人一样，冷冷地走开呢？

paragraphs.en: This picture brought such an agony of pleasurable suffering that he worked it over and over again in his mind and set it up in new and varied lights, till he wore it threadbare.
paragraphs.cn: 想到这些，他又难过又有点开心。他一直在心里反复地想这个画面，想了又想，直到他想累了。

paragraphs.en: At last he rose up sighing and departed in the darkness.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，他叹了口气，站起来，在夜色中离开了。

paragraphs.en: About half-past nine or ten o’clock he came along the deserted street to where the Adored Unknown lived; he paused a moment; no sound fell upon his listening ear; a candle was casting a dull glow upon the curtain of a second-story window.
paragraphs.cn: 大概九点半或十点的时候，他走在空荡荡的街上，来到了他喜欢那个女孩的家。他停了一下，什么声音也没听到。二楼的窗帘后面，有一支蜡烛发着微弱的光。

paragraphs.en: Was the sacred presence there?
paragraphs.cn: 她在里面吗？

paragraphs.en: He climbed the fence, threaded his stealthy way through the plants, till he stood under that window; he looked up at it long, and with emotion; then he laid him down on the ground under it, disposing himself upon his back, with his hands clasped upon his breast and holding his poor wilted flower.
paragraphs.cn: 他爬过篱笆，悄悄地穿过植物，来到那扇窗户下面。他抬头看了很久，心里很难过。然后他躺在窗下的地上，双手抱在胸前，手里还握着那朵枯萎的花。

paragraphs.en: And thus he would die—out in the cold world, with no shelter over his homeless head, no friendly hand to wipe the death-damps from his brow, no loving face to bend pityingly over him when the great agony came.
paragraphs.cn: 他就这样死了——在这个冰冷的世界里，没有家，没有可以遮风避雨的地方，也没有人来擦去他额头上的汗水，更没有人会在他最痛苦的时候，怜爱地看着他。

paragraphs.en: And thus _she_ would see him when she looked out upon the glad morning, and oh! would she drop one little tear upon his poor, lifeless form, would she heave one little sigh to see a bright young life so rudely blighted, so untimely cut down?
paragraphs.cn: 当她早上开心地往外看的时候，就会看到他。哦！她会为他冰冷的身体流下一滴眼泪吗？会为他这么年轻就死去了，难过地叹一口气吗？

paragraphs.en: The window went up, a maid-servant’s discordant voice profaned the holy calm, and a deluge of water drenched the prone martyr’s remains!
paragraphs.cn: 窗户开了，一个女仆刺耳的声音打破了安静。一大盆水泼了下来，把躺在地上的他淋了个透！

paragraphs.en: The strangling hero sprang up with a relieving snort.
paragraphs.cn: 他喘着粗气，一下子跳了起来。

paragraphs.en: There was a whiz as of a missile in the air, mingled with the murmur of a curse, a sound as of shivering glass followed, and a small, vague form went over the fence and shot away in the gloom.
paragraphs.cn: 只听见“嗖”的一声，好像有什么东西飞过来了，还夹杂着几句骂人的话，接着是玻璃碎裂的声音。一个模糊的小身影翻过篱笆，跑进了黑暗里。

paragraphs.en: Not long after, as Tom, all undressed for bed, was surveying his drenched garments by the light of a tallow dip, Sid woke up; but if he had any dim idea of making any “references to allusions,” he thought better of it and held his peace, for there was danger in Tom’s eye.
paragraphs.cn: 不久之后，当汤姆脱了衣服准备睡觉，正借着蜡烛光看他湿透的衣服时，希德醒了。不过，希德就算心里隐约想说些什么，也还是没说，因为他觉得汤姆的眼神很吓人。

paragraphs.en: Tom turned in without the added vexation of prayers, and Sid made mental note of the omission.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆没有祷告就去睡觉了，希德在心里偷偷记下了他没祷告这件事。

paragraphs.en: The sun rose upon a tranquil world, and beamed down upon the peaceful village like a benediction.
paragraphs.cn: 太阳升起来了，照亮了一个平静的世界，阳光像祝福一样洒满了宁静的村庄。

paragraphs.en: Breakfast over, Aunt Polly had family worship: it began with a prayer built from the ground up of solid courses of Scriptural quotations, welded together with a thin mortar of originality; and from the summit of this she delivered a grim chapter of the Mosaic Law, as from Sinai.
paragraphs.cn: 吃完早饭，波莉姨妈带着全家人做礼拜。她先是做了一个很长的祷告，里面有很多圣经里的话。祷告完了，她又像从西奈山上传来一样，严肃地读了一章《摩西律法》。

paragraphs.en: Then Tom girded up his loins, so to speak, and went to work to “get his verses.”
paragraphs.cn: 接着，汤姆就准备好，开始“背他的经文”了。

paragraphs.en: Sid had learned his lesson days before.
paragraphs.cn: 希德几天前就学过这课了。

paragraphs.en: Tom bent all his energies to the memorizing of five verses, and he chose part of the Sermon on the Mount, because he could find no verses that were shorter.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆尽力去背那五节经文。他选了《山上宝训》的一部分，因为他找不到更短的经文了。

paragraphs.en: At the end of half an hour Tom had a vague general idea of his lesson, but no more, for his mind was traversing the whole field of human thought, and his hands were busy with distracting recreations.
paragraphs.cn: 半小时后，汤姆对他的课文只有一点点模糊的印象。因为他的心思早就飞到别的地方去了，手也忙着玩各种分散注意力的东西。

paragraphs.en: Mary took his book to hear him recite, and he tried to find his way through the fog:
paragraphs.cn: 玛丽拿着书听他背诵，他努力地想从这团迷雾中找到头绪：

paragraphs.en: “Blessed are the—a—a—”
paragraphs.cn: “有福的是——啊——啊——”

paragraphs.en: “Poor”—
paragraphs.cn: “贫穷的——”

paragraphs.en: “Yes—poor; blessed are the poor—a—a—”
paragraphs.cn: “对——贫穷的；有福的是贫穷的——啊——啊——”

paragraphs.en: “In spirit—”
paragraphs.cn: “在灵里——”

paragraphs.en: “In spirit; blessed are the poor in spirit, for they—they—”
paragraphs.cn: “心里贫穷的人有福了，因为他们—他们—”

paragraphs.en: “_Theirs_—”
“For _theirs_.
paragraphs.cn: “因为_他们_。

paragraphs.en: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
paragraphs.cn: 心里贫穷的人有福了，因为天国是他们的。

paragraphs.en: Blessed are they that mourn, for they—they—”
paragraphs.cn: 哀恸的人有福了，因为他们—他们—”

paragraphs.en: “Sh—”
“For they—a—”
paragraphs.cn: “因为他们—啊—”

paragraphs.en: “For they S, H—Oh, I don’t know what it is!”
paragraphs.cn: “因为他们S，H—哦，我不知道是什么了！”

paragraphs.en: “_Shall_!”
“Oh, _shall_! for they shall—for they shall—a—a—shall mourn—a—a—blessed are they that shall—they that—a—they that shall mourn, for they shall—a—shall _what_?
paragraphs.cn: “哦，_必_！因为他们必—因为他们必—啊—啊—必哀恸—啊—啊—有福的是那些必—那些—啊—那些必哀恸的，因为他们必—啊—必_什么_？

paragraphs.en: Why don’t you tell me, Mary?
paragraphs.cn: 你为什么不告诉我呢，玛丽？

paragraphs.en: —what do you want to be so mean for?”
paragraphs.cn: —你为什么要这么刻薄？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Tom, you poor thick-headed thing, I’m not teasing you.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，汤姆，你这个可怜的笨脑袋，我不是在逗你玩。

paragraphs.en: I wouldn’t do that.
paragraphs.cn: 我不会那样做的。

paragraphs.en: You must go and learn it again.
paragraphs.cn: 你得再去学一遍。

paragraphs.en: Don’t you be discouraged, Tom, you’ll manage it—and if you do, I’ll give you something ever so nice.
paragraphs.cn: 别灰心，汤姆，你会成功的—如果你做到了，我会给你一个非常好的东西。

paragraphs.en: There, now, that’s a good boy.”
paragraphs.cn: 好了，你真是个好孩子。”

paragraphs.en: “All right!
paragraphs.cn: “好的！

paragraphs.en: What is it, Mary, tell me what it is.”
paragraphs.cn: 那是什么呢，玛丽，快告诉我那是什么。”

paragraphs.en: “Never you mind, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “别担心啦，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: You know if I say it’s nice, it is nice.”
paragraphs.cn: 你知道我说它好，它就是好的。”

paragraphs.en: “You bet you that’s so, Mary.
paragraphs.cn: “你说的肯定对，玛丽。

paragraphs.en: All right, I’ll tackle it again.”
paragraphs.cn: 好的，我再去试试。”

paragraphs.en: And he did “tackle it again”—and under the double pressure of curiosity and prospective gain he did it with such spirit that he accomplished a shining success.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他真的“再去试试”—在好奇心和期待获得奖励的双重作用下，他满怀热情地做这件事，最终获得了巨大的成功。

paragraphs.en: Mary gave him a brand-new “Barlow” knife worth twelve and a half cents; and the convulsion of delight that swept his system shook him to his foundations.
paragraphs.cn: 玛丽给了他一把全新的“巴洛”小刀，值十二点五美分；他兴奋得全身颤抖，开心极了。

paragraphs.en: True, the knife would not cut anything, but it was a “sure-enough” Barlow, and there was inconceivable grandeur in that—though where the Western boys ever got the idea that such a weapon could possibly be counterfeited to its injury is an imposing mystery and will always remain so, perhaps.
paragraphs.cn: 确实，这把刀什么都切不动，但它是一把“货真价实”的巴洛刀，这让它显得无比了不起—不过，西部孩子们是从哪里认为这种武器可能会被仿冒到损坏的地步，这真是一个巨大的谜团，也许永远都是个谜。

paragraphs.en: Tom contrived to scarify the cupboard with it, and was arranging to begin on the bureau, when he was called off to dress for Sunday-school.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆用它在碗柜上刻了几道，正准备开始刻梳妆台，这时他被叫去为主日学校打扮。

paragraphs.en: Mary gave him a tin basin of water and a piece of soap, and he went outside the door and set the basin on a little bench there; then he dipped the soap in the water and laid it down; turned up his sleeves; poured out the water on the ground, gently, and then entered the kitchen and began to wipe his face diligently on the towel behind the door.
paragraphs.cn: 玛丽给了他一个锡盆，里面有水和一块肥皂，他走到门外，把盆放在一个小板凳上；然后他把肥皂蘸了水，又放下；卷起袖子；轻轻地把水倒在地上，然后走进厨房，开始认真地用门后面的毛巾擦脸。

paragraphs.en: But Mary removed the towel and said:
paragraphs.cn: 但是玛丽拿走了毛巾，说：

paragraphs.en: “Now ain’t you ashamed, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “你难道不觉得不好意思吗，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: You mustn’t be so bad.
paragraphs.cn: 你不能这么淘气了。

paragraphs.en: Water won’t hurt you.”
paragraphs.cn: 水不会弄疼你的。”

paragraphs.en: Tom was a trifle disconcerted.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆有点慌乱。

paragraphs.en: The basin was refilled, and this time he stood over it a little while, gathering resolution; took in a big breath and began.
paragraphs.cn: 盆里又装满了水。他站在旁边，鼓足了勇气；深吸一口气，然后就开始洗了。

paragraphs.en: When he entered the kitchen presently, with both eyes shut and groping for the towel with his hands, an honorable testimony of suds and water was dripping from his face.
paragraphs.cn: 他走进厨房时，闭着眼睛，摸索着找毛巾。脸上还滴着肥皂泡和水。

paragraphs.en: But when he emerged from the towel, he was not yet satisfactory, for the clean territory stopped short at his chin and his jaws, like a mask; below and beyond this line there was a dark expanse of unirrigated soil that spread downward in front and backward around his neck.
paragraphs.cn: 但是当他擦完脸时，还是不让人满意。干净的地方只到下巴和脸颊，就像戴着面具一样；这条线下面和外面，脖子前面和后面都还是脏的。

paragraphs.en: Mary took him in hand, and when she was done with him he was a man and a brother, without distinction of color, and his saturated hair was neatly brushed, and its short curls wrought into a dainty and symmetrical general effect.
paragraphs.cn: 玛丽亲自来帮他弄。等她弄完，他变得干干净净的。湿漉漉的头发梳得整齐，短短的卷发看起来也很漂亮。

paragraphs.en: [He privately smoothed out the curls, with labor and difficulty, and plastered his hair close down to his head; for he held curls to be effeminate, and his own filled his life with bitterness.]
paragraphs.cn: 他偷偷地、费力地把卷发弄直，紧紧地贴在头皮上。因为他觉得卷发不好看，自己的卷发让他很不开心。

paragraphs.en: Then Mary got out a suit of his clothing that had been used only on Sundays during two years—they were simply called his “other clothes”—and so by that we know the size of his wardrobe.
paragraphs.cn: 然后玛丽拿出了一套他的衣服，这衣服两年里只在星期天穿。大家就叫它们“另外一套衣服”。这样我们就知道他有多少衣服了。

paragraphs.en: The girl “put him to rights” after he had dressed himself; she buttoned his neat roundabout up to his chin, turned his vast shirt collar down over his shoulders, brushed him off and crowned him with his speckled straw hat.
paragraphs.cn: 他穿好衣服后，女孩又帮他整理了一下。她把他的小夹克扣到下巴，把宽大的衬衫领子翻到肩膀上，给他掸了掸灰，还给他戴上花斑的草帽。

paragraphs.en: He now looked exceedingly improved and uncomfortable.
paragraphs.cn: 他现在看起来好多了，但也很不舒服。

paragraphs.en: He was fully as uncomfortable as he looked; for there was a restraint about whole clothes and cleanliness that galled him.
paragraphs.cn: 他真的和看起来一样不舒服。因为穿整齐的衣服和干干净净让他觉得很不自在。

paragraphs.en: He hoped that Mary would forget his shoes, but the hope was blighted; she coated them thoroughly with tallow, as was the custom, and brought them out.
paragraphs.cn: 他希望玛丽能忘记他的鞋子，但这个希望落空了。她按照习惯，把鞋子仔细涂上牛油，然后拿了出来。

paragraphs.en: He lost his temper and said he was always being made to do everything he didn’t want to do.
paragraphs.cn: 他发脾气说，他总是被逼着做所有他不想做的事情。

paragraphs.en: But Mary said, persuasively:
paragraphs.cn: 但玛丽温柔地说：

paragraphs.en: “Please, Tom—that’s a good boy.”
paragraphs.cn: “乖，汤姆——做个好孩子。”

paragraphs.en: So he got into the shoes snarling.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他很不情愿地穿上了鞋子。

paragraphs.en: Mary was soon ready, and the three children set out for Sunday-school—a place that Tom hated with his whole heart; but Sid and Mary were fond of it.
paragraphs.cn: 玛丽也很快准备好了，三个孩子出发去主日学校。那是汤姆非常讨厌的地方，但希德和玛丽都很喜欢那里。

paragraphs.en: Sabbath-school hours were from nine to half-past ten; and then church service.
paragraphs.cn: 主日学校从九点上到十点半，然后是教堂礼拜。

paragraphs.en: Two of the children always remained for the sermon voluntarily, and the other always remained too—for stronger reasons.
paragraphs.cn: 其中两个孩子总是自愿留下听布道，另一个孩子也总是留下——因为有其他原因。

paragraphs.en: The church’s high-backed, uncushioned pews would seat about three hundred persons; the edifice was but a small, plain affair, with a sort of pine board tree-box on top of it for a steeple.
paragraphs.cn: 教堂里高高的、没有垫子的长椅可以坐大约三百人。这座教堂很小，也很普通，上面有个用松木板做的像烟囱一样的尖顶。

paragraphs.en: At the door Tom dropped back a step and accosted a Sunday-dressed comrade:
paragraphs.cn: 在门口，汤姆慢了一步，叫住了他一个穿着礼拜日衣服的朋友。

paragraphs.en: “Say, Billy, got a yaller ticket?”
paragraphs.cn: “嘿，比利，你有黄票吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes.”
“What’ll you take for her?”
paragraphs.cn: “你拿什么换它？”

paragraphs.en: “What’ll you give?”
paragraphs.cn: “你给我什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Piece of lickrish and a fish-hook.”
paragraphs.cn: “一块甘草糖和一个鱼钩。”

paragraphs.en: “Less see ’em.”
paragraphs.cn: “给我看看。”

paragraphs.en: Tom exhibited.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆把东西拿了出来。

paragraphs.en: They were satisfactory, and the property changed hands.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都很满意，东西也换了主人。

paragraphs.en: Then Tom traded a couple of white alleys for three red tickets, and some small trifle or other for a couple of blue ones.
paragraphs.cn: 然后，汤姆 用几颗白色弹珠换了三张红色票，又用其他一些小东西换了两张蓝色票。

paragraphs.en: He waylaid other boys as they came, and went on buying tickets of various colors ten or fifteen minutes longer.
paragraphs.cn: 他拦住其他来的小男生，又继续买了十到十五分钟的各种颜色的票。

paragraphs.en: He entered the church, now, with a swarm of clean and noisy boys and girls, proceeded to his seat and started a quarrel with the first boy that came handy.
paragraphs.cn: 他现在走进教堂，那里有一大群干净又吵闹的小男生小女生。他走到自己的座位，就开始和第一个碰到的男生吵架。

paragraphs.en: The teacher, a grave, elderly man, interfered; then turned his back a moment and Tom pulled a boy’s hair in the next bench, and was absorbed in his book when the boy turned around; stuck a pin in another boy, presently, in order to hear him say “Ouch!” and got a new reprimand from his teacher.
paragraphs.cn: 老师是个严肃的老爷爷，他过来制止了。然后他一转身，汤姆 就拔了旁边座位一个男生的头发。那个男生转过头来的时候，汤姆 又装作在认真看书。过了一会儿，他又用大头针扎另一个男生，就为了听他叫一声“哎哟！” 结果又被老师骂了。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s whole class were of a pattern—restless, noisy, and troublesome.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 班上的同学都一个样——坐不住，很吵，还爱捣乱。

paragraphs.en: When they came to recite their lessons, not one of them knew his verses perfectly, but had to be prompted all along.
paragraphs.cn: 轮到他们背课文时，没有一个人能背得很熟，每次都要别人提醒才行。

paragraphs.en: However, they worried through, and each got his reward—in small blue tickets, each with a passage of Scripture on it; each blue ticket was pay for two verses of the recitation.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，他们总算挺过去了，每个人都得到了奖励——小小的蓝色票，每张票上都有一段圣经经文；每张蓝色票可以换背诵两句经文的奖励。

paragraphs.en: Ten blue tickets equalled a red one, and could be exchanged for it; ten red tickets equalled a yellow one; for ten yellow tickets the superintendent gave a very plainly bound Bible (worth forty cents in those easy times) to the pupil.
paragraphs.cn: 十张蓝色票可以换一张红色票；十张红色票可以换一张黄色票；集齐十张黄色票，校长就会送给那个小朋友一本包装很普通的圣经（在那个时候只值四十美分）。

paragraphs.en: How many of my readers would have the industry and application to memorize two thousand verses, even for a Doré Bible?
paragraphs.cn: 我的读者里，有多少人能这么努力用功，记住两千句经文，哪怕是为了得到一本精美的多雷圣经呢？

paragraphs.en: And yet Mary had acquired two Bibles in this way—it was the patient work of two years—and a boy of German parentage had won four or five.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，玛丽 却用这个办法得到了两本圣经——这可是他两年努力的结果。一个德国血统的小男生甚至得到了四五本呢。

paragraphs.en: He once recited three thousand verses without stopping; but the strain upon his mental faculties was too great, and he was little better than an idiot from that day forth—a grievous misfortune for the school, for on great occasions, before company, the superintendent (as Tom expressed it) had always made this boy come out and “spread himself.”
paragraphs.cn: 他曾经一口气背了三千句经文，但那对他来说太累了，从那天起他就像个傻子一样——这对学校来说真是个大麻烦，因为在重要的场合，有客人来的时候，校长（用汤姆的话说）总是让这个男生出来“好好表现一番”。

paragraphs.en: Only the older pupils managed to keep their tickets and stick to their tedious work long enough to get a Bible, and so the delivery of one of these prizes was a rare and noteworthy circumstance; the successful pupil was so great and conspicuous for that day that on the spot every scholar’s heart was fired with a fresh ambition that often lasted a couple of weeks.
paragraphs.cn: 只有那些年纪大一点的学生才能一直把票留着，坚持做这些无聊的事情，直到换到一本圣经。所以，能得到这种奖品是件稀奇又特别的事；那个得奖的学生在那天会显得非常了不起，非常引人注目，一下子就让每个小朋友的心里都燃起了新的决心，这种决心通常能持续几个星期。

paragraphs.en: It is possible that Tom’s mental stomach had never really hungered for one of those prizes, but unquestionably his entire being had for many a day longed for the glory and the eclat that came with it.
paragraphs.cn: 也许汤姆的心里从来没有真正渴望过这些奖品，但毫无疑问，他很久以前就一直盼望着得到奖品带来的荣耀和风光。

paragraphs.en: In due course the superintendent stood up in front of the pulpit, with a closed hymn-book in his hand and his forefinger inserted between its leaves, and commanded attention.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，校长站在讲台前，手里拿着一本合上的赞美诗集，食指夹在书页中间，他让大家安静。

paragraphs.en: When a Sunday-school superintendent makes his customary little speech, a hymn-book in the hand is as necessary as is the inevitable sheet of music in the hand of a singer who stands forward on the platform and sings a solo at a concert—though why, is a mystery: for neither the hymn-book nor the sheet of music is ever referred to by the sufferer.
paragraphs.cn: 当一位主日学校校长发表他习惯的小演讲时，手里拿着一本赞美诗集就像歌唱家站在舞台上独唱时手里那张必然的乐谱一样重要——虽然为什么会这样，是个谜：因为无论是赞美诗集还是乐谱，表演者都从来不会看一眼。

paragraphs.en: This superintendent was a slim creature of thirty-five, with a sandy goatee and short sandy hair; he wore a stiff standing-collar whose upper edge almost reached his ears and whose sharp points curved forward abreast the corners of his mouth—a fence that compelled a straight lookout ahead, and a turning of the whole body when a side view was required; his chin was propped on a spreading cravat which was as broad and as long as a bank-note, and had fringed ends; his boot toes were turned sharply up, in the fashion of the day, like sleigh-runners—an effect patiently and laboriously produced by the young men by sitting with their toes pressed against a wall for hours together.
paragraphs.cn: 这位校长是个三十五岁，瘦瘦高高的人，留着山羊胡子，头发也是沙色的，短短的。他穿着硬挺的立领衬衫，领子边儿几乎碰到他的耳朵，尖尖的领角向前弯到嘴边——这就像一道围栏，让他只能直直地往前看，如果想看旁边就得整个身子都转过去；他的下巴靠在一块又宽又长的领带上，领带就像钞票一样大，还有流苏边；他的靴子尖也像那时流行的一样，向上翘得很高，就像雪橇的滑板——这是年轻男生们为了赶时髦，花了好几个小时把脚趾抵在墙上，辛苦弄出来的效果。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Walters was very earnest of mien, and very sincere and honest at heart; and he held sacred things and places in such reverence, and so separated them from worldly matters, that unconsciously to himself his Sunday-school voice had acquired a peculiar intonation which was wholly absent on week-days.
paragraphs.cn: 沃尔特斯先生的样子很认真，心里也很真诚老实；他非常尊敬神圣的事物和地方，把它们和世俗的事情分得很开，以至于他自己都没有发现，他的主日学校声音变得很特别，那种腔调在平时是完全没有的。

paragraphs.en: He began after this fashion:
paragraphs.cn: 他是这样开始说的：

paragraphs.en: “Now, children, I want you all to sit up just as straight and pretty as you can and give me all your attention for a minute or two.
paragraphs.cn: “孩子们，现在请大家坐得直直的、漂亮亮的，把耳朵竖起来听我说一两分钟。

paragraphs.en: There—that is it.
paragraphs.cn: 好——就是这样。

paragraphs.en: That is the way good little boys and girls should do.
paragraphs.cn: 乖巧的小男生小女生就应该这样做。

paragraphs.en: I see one little girl who is looking out of the window—I am afraid she thinks I am out there somewhere—perhaps up in one of the trees making a speech to the little birds.
paragraphs.cn: 我看到一个小女生正在看窗外——我猜她可能以为我跑出去了，也许是爬到树上给小鸟们演讲呢。

paragraphs.en: [Applausive titter.]
paragraphs.cn: （掌声伴着窃笑声。）

paragraphs.en: I want to tell you how good it makes me feel to see so many bright, clean little faces assembled in a place like this, learning to do right and be good.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想告诉大家，看到这么多聪明又干净的小脸蛋聚在这里，学习做对的事，做好孩子，我心里感到多高兴啊！

paragraphs.en: And so forth and so on.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样，一直说着。

paragraphs.en: It is not necessary to set down the rest of the oration.
paragraphs.cn: 没有必要把后面所有的演讲内容都写下来了。

paragraphs.en: It was of a pattern which does not vary, and so it is familiar to us all.
paragraphs.cn: 这演讲的套路总是这样，一点儿也没变，所以我们大家都知道是怎么回事。

paragraphs.en: The latter third of the speech was marred by the resumption of fights and other recreations among certain of the bad boys, and by fidgetings and whisperings that extended far and wide, washing even to the bases of isolated and incorruptible rocks like Sid and Mary.
paragraphs.cn: 演讲最后三分之一的时候，一些调皮的男生又开始打架和玩闹了，还有一些小动作和窃窃私语也传得很远很广，甚至影响到了像希德和玛丽这样平时很乖的小朋友。

paragraphs.en: But now every sound ceased suddenly, with the subsidence of Mr. Walters’ voice, and the conclusion of the speech was received with a burst of silent gratitude.
paragraphs.cn: 但是，当沃尔特斯先生的声音渐渐变小，演讲结束的时候，所有的声音都突然停了下来，大家默默地，心里很感激。

paragraphs.en: A good part of the whispering had been occasioned by an event which was more or less rare—the entrance of visitors: lawyer Thatcher, accompanied by a very feeble and aged man; a fine, portly, middle-aged gentleman with iron-gray hair; and a dignified lady who was doubtless the latter’s wife.
paragraphs.cn: 大家小声说话，是因为有客人来了。律师撒切尔来了，还有一位很老的爷爷、一位头发灰白的叔叔，和一位阿姨。阿姨应该是叔叔的妻子。

paragraphs.en: The lady was leading a child.
paragraphs.cn: 阿姨牵着一个小朋友。

paragraphs.en: Tom had been restless and full of chafings and repinings; conscience-smitten, too—he could not meet Amy Lawrence’s eye, he could not brook her loving gaze.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆心里坐立不安，还有点内疚。他不敢看艾米·劳伦斯的眼睛，也受不了她那么温柔的眼神。

paragraphs.en: But when he saw this small newcomer his soul was all ablaze with bliss in a moment.
paragraphs.cn: 但当他看到这个新来的小朋友时，他的心里立刻充满了快乐。

paragraphs.en: The next moment he was “showing off” with all his might—cuffing boys, pulling hair, making faces—in a word, using every art that seemed likely to fascinate a girl and win her applause.
paragraphs.cn: 接下来，他使劲地“炫耀”自己——打男生、拉头发、做鬼脸。总之，他用尽了各种办法来吸引那个小女孩，想让她喜欢他。
