paragraphs.en: His exaltation had but one alloy—the memory of his humiliation in this angel’s garden—and that record in sand was fast washing out, under the waves of happiness that were sweeping over it now.
paragraphs.cn: 他虽然很高兴，但心里还有一点点不开心——他想起在那个“天使花园”里，他被羞辱的事。不过，现在快乐的浪潮涌过来，那不开心的事就像沙子上的字一样，很快就被冲走了。

paragraphs.en: The visitors were given the highest seat of honor, and as soon as Mr. Walters’ speech was finished, he introduced them to the school.
paragraphs.cn: 客人们被安排坐在最好的位置。沃尔特先生一讲完话，就把他们介绍给大家。

paragraphs.en: The middle-aged man turned out to be a prodigious personage—no less a one than the county judge—altogether the most august creation these children had ever looked upon—and they wondered what kind of material he was made of—and they half wanted to hear him roar, and were half afraid he might, too.
paragraphs.cn: 这位叔叔原来是个大人物——他竟然是县里的法官！这些小朋友们从来没见过这么威风的人。他们好奇他是什么做的，一半想听他大吼一声，一半又有点害怕他真的会吼出来。

paragraphs.en: He was from Constantinople, twelve miles away—so he had travelled, and seen the world—these very eyes had looked upon the county court-house—which was said to have a tin roof.
paragraphs.cn: 他从十二英里外的君士坦丁堡来，去过很多地方，见过大世面。他的眼睛亲眼看过县法院，听说那里还是铁皮屋顶呢！

paragraphs.en: The awe which these reflections inspired was attested by the impressive silence and the ranks of staring eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 大家被这些事吓到了，都安静下来，一排排的眼睛都盯着他看。

paragraphs.en: This was the great Judge Thatcher, brother of their own lawyer.
paragraphs.cn: 这就是厉害的撒切尔法官，是他们自己律师的哥哥。

paragraphs.en: Jeff Thatcher immediately went forward, to be familiar with the great man and be envied by the school.
paragraphs.cn: 杰夫撒切尔立刻走上前去认识这位大人物，好让学校里的人都羡慕他。

paragraphs.en: It would have been music to his soul to hear the whisperings:
paragraphs.cn: 如果能听到这些悄悄话，他心里一定很高兴：

paragraphs.en: “Look at him, Jim!
paragraphs.cn: “快看他，吉姆！

paragraphs.en: He’s a going up there.
paragraphs.cn: 他要走过去了。

paragraphs.en: Say—look! he’s a going to shake hands with him—he _is_ shaking hands with him!
paragraphs.cn: 快看啊！他要去跟他握手了——他真的在握手了！

paragraphs.en: By jings, don’t you wish you was Jeff?”
paragraphs.cn: 天哪，你是不是也想当杰夫啊？”

paragraphs.en: Mr. Walters fell to “showing off,” with all sorts of official bustlings and activities, giving orders, delivering judgments, discharging directions here, there, everywhere that he could find a target.
paragraphs.cn: 沃尔特先生也开始“炫耀”自己了。他忙着做各种重要的事，在能找到目标的地方，到处发号施令。

paragraphs.en: The librarian “showed off”—running hither and thither with his arms full of books and making a deal of the splutter and fuss that insect authority delights in.
paragraphs.cn: 图书管理员也“炫耀”起来了，他抱着一堆书跑来跑去，像个小官僚一样，装作很忙很厉害的样子。

paragraphs.en: The young lady teachers “showed off”—bending sweetly over pupils that were lately being boxed, lifting pretty warning fingers at bad little boys and patting good ones lovingly.
paragraphs.cn: 年轻的女老师们也“炫耀”起来了——她们温柔地弯下腰，去关心那些刚才才被惩罚过的学生；对着调皮的小男生竖起手指轻轻警告，对乖巧的小男生则爱抚地拍拍头。

paragraphs.en: The young gentlemen teachers “showed off” with small scoldings and other little displays of authority and fine attention to discipline—and most of the teachers, of both sexes, found business up at the library, by the pulpit; and it was business that frequently had to be done over again two or three times (with much seeming vexation).
paragraphs.cn: 年轻的男老师们也“炫耀”起来了——他们轻轻地责骂几句，展示一下自己的权威，表示自己很注重纪律。大部分老师，不管男女，都在图书馆的讲台旁边找到事情做，而且这些事经常需要重复做两三次（还假装很烦恼的样子）。

paragraphs.en: The little girls “showed off” in various ways, and the little boys “showed off” with such diligence that the air was thick with paper wads and the murmur of scufflings.
paragraphs.cn: 小女孩们也用各种方式“炫耀”自己，小男孩们也努力地“炫耀”，结果空气中都是纸团，还有打闹的吵闹声。

paragraphs.en: And above it all the great man sat and beamed a majestic judicial smile upon all the house, and warmed himself in the sun of his own grandeur—for he was “showing off,” too.
paragraphs.cn: 在这一切之上，那个大人物坐在那里，威严地笑着，目光扫过整个屋子，陶醉在自己的威风里——因为他也在“炫耀”自己呢。

paragraphs.en: There was only one thing wanting to make Mr. Walters’ ecstasy complete, and that was a chance to deliver a Bible-prize and exhibit a prodigy.
paragraphs.cn: 沃尔特先生还差一件事就更开心了，那就是能颁发一本圣经奖品，然后展示一个天才学生。

paragraphs.en: Several pupils had a few yellow tickets, but none had enough—he had been around among the star pupils inquiring.
paragraphs.cn: 有几个学生有一些黄色的票，但都没有集齐足够的。他一直在优秀学生中打听。

paragraphs.en: He would have given worlds, now, to have that German lad back again with a sound mind.
paragraphs.cn: 他现在愿意付出一切，只希望能让那个德国小男孩能恢复正常，回到这里。

paragraphs.en: And now at this moment, when hope was dead, Tom Sawyer came forward with nine yellow tickets, nine red tickets, and ten blue ones, and demanded a Bible.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这时，当他已经不抱希望的时候，汤姆·索亚走了上前。他拿着九张黄票、九张红票和十张蓝票，要了一本圣经。

paragraphs.en: This was a thunderbolt out of a clear sky.
paragraphs.cn: 这真是意想不到的事！

paragraphs.en: Walters was not expecting an application from this source for the next ten years.
paragraphs.cn: 沃尔特先生根本没想到，这个人会在未来十年里来领圣经。

paragraphs.en: But there was no getting around it—here were the certified checks, and they were good for their face.
paragraphs.cn: 但也没办法，这些票是真的，而且数量也够了。

paragraphs.en: Tom was therefore elevated to a place with the Judge and the other elect, and the great news was announced from headquarters.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆被大家推举到了法官和那些被选中的人身边，这个大好消息也从总部传开了。

paragraphs.en: It was the most stunning surprise of the decade, and so profound was the sensation that it lifted the new hero up to the judicial one’s altitude, and the school had two marvels to gaze upon in place of one.
paragraphs.cn: 这是十年来最让人吃惊的事。这件事太轰动了，新来的小英雄一下子和那位法官一样高了。学校里也多了一个了不起的人，现在有两个了。

paragraphs.en: The boys were all eaten up with envy—but those that suffered the bitterest pangs were those who perceived too late that they themselves had contributed to this hated splendor by trading tickets to Tom for the wealth he had amassed in selling whitewashing privileges.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们都嫉妒死了。但那些最难过的人是后来才发现的，他们自己也帮了汤姆，让他这么风光。他们把奖票换给了汤姆，为了钱，让汤姆去卖粉刷的特权。

paragraphs.en: These despised themselves, as being the dupes of a wily fraud, a guileful snake in the grass.
paragraphs.cn: 他们很讨厌自己，觉得自己被一个狡猾的坏蛋给骗了。

paragraphs.en: The prize was delivered to Tom with as much effusion as the superintendent could pump up under the circumstances; but it lacked somewhat of the true gush, for the poor fellow’s instinct taught him that there was a mystery here that could not well bear the light, perhaps; it was simply preposterous that this boy had warehoused two thousand sheaves of Scriptural wisdom on his premises—a dozen would strain his capacity, without a doubt.
paragraphs.cn: 校长尽力热情地把奖品给了汤姆，但在那种情况下，他的热情有点假。校长心里觉得这件事有点奇怪，可能经不起推敲。这个小男孩怎么可能记住两千段圣经经文呢？记住十几段都很难了。

paragraphs.en: Amy Lawrence was proud and glad, and she tried to make Tom see it in her face—but he wouldn’t look.
paragraphs.cn: 艾米·劳伦斯又高兴又骄傲，她想让汤姆看到她脸上的笑容，但汤姆却不看她。

paragraphs.en: She wondered; then she was just a grain troubled; next a dim suspicion came and went—came again; she watched; a furtive glance told her worlds—and then her heart broke, and she was jealous, and angry, and the tears came and she hated everybody.
paragraphs.cn: 她想了想，有点不开心。接着，她开始有点怀疑。她一直看着。一个偷偷的眼神让她全明白了。她的心碎了，她很吃醋，很生气，眼泪也流了下来，她讨厌所有的人。

paragraphs.en: Tom most of all (she thought).
paragraphs.cn: (她想)她最恨汤姆了。

paragraphs.en: Tom was introduced to the Judge; but his tongue was tied, his breath would hardly come, his heart quaked—partly because of the awful greatness of the man, but mainly because he was her parent.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆被介绍给法官。他说不出话，几乎喘不过气，心里直打鼓。一部分是因为法官很了不起，主要是因为他是汤姆的爸爸。

paragraphs.en: He would have liked to fall down and worship him, if it were in the dark.
paragraphs.cn: 如果天黑的话，他真想跪下来拜他。

paragraphs.en: The Judge put his hand on Tom’s head and called him a fine little man, and asked him what his name was.
paragraphs.cn: 法官把手放在汤姆的头上，夸他是好孩子，还问他叫什么名字。

paragraphs.en: The boy stammered, gasped, and got it out:
paragraphs.cn: 男孩结结巴巴地喘着气，终于说出来了：

paragraphs.en: “Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, no, not Tom—it is—”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，不，不是汤姆——是——”

paragraphs.en: “Thomas.”
paragraphs.cn: “托马斯。”

paragraphs.en: “Ah, that’s it.
paragraphs.cn: “啊，对了。

paragraphs.en: I thought there was more to it, maybe.
paragraphs.cn: 我想，也许还有别的名字。

paragraphs.en: That’s very well.
paragraphs.cn: 非常好。

paragraphs.en: But you’ve another one I daresay, and you’ll tell it to me, won’t you?”
paragraphs.cn: 但我猜你还有另一个名字，你会告诉我，对吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Tell the gentleman your other name, Thomas,” said Walters, “and say sir.
paragraphs.cn: “托马斯，告诉这位先生你另一个名字，”沃尔特说，“还要说‘先生’。

paragraphs.en: You mustn’t forget your manners.”
paragraphs.cn: 你不能忘记礼貌。”

paragraphs.en: “Thomas Sawyer—sir.”
paragraphs.cn: “托马斯·索亚——先生。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s it!
paragraphs.cn: “对了！

paragraphs.en: That’s a good boy.
paragraphs.cn: 真是个好孩子。

paragraphs.en: Fine boy.
paragraphs.cn: 好孩子。

paragraphs.en: Fine, manly little fellow.
paragraphs.cn: 真棒，像个小男子汉。

paragraphs.en: Two thousand verses is a great many—very, very great many.
paragraphs.cn: 两千段经文很多很多。

paragraphs.en: And you never can be sorry for the trouble you took to learn them; for knowledge is worth more than anything there is in the world; it’s what makes great men and good men; you’ll be a great man and a good man yourself, some day, Thomas, and then you’ll look back and say, It’s all owing to the precious Sunday-school privileges of my boyhood—it’s all owing to my dear teachers that taught me to learn—it’s all owing to the good superintendent, who encouraged me, and watched over me, and gave me a beautiful Bible—a splendid elegant Bible—to keep and have it all for my own, always—it’s all owing to right bringing up!
paragraphs.cn: 你永远不会后悔花力气学习这些东西，因为知识比世界上任何东西都宝贵。它能让人变得很棒很好。总有一天，托马斯，你也会成为一个很棒很好的人。那时你会回头说：‘这都要感谢我小时候宝贵的主日学校特权！这都要感谢我亲爱的老师教我学习！这都要感谢好校长，他鼓励我，照顾我，还给了我一本漂亮的圣经，一本非常精美的圣经，让我永远拥有它！这都要感谢正确的教育！’

paragraphs.en: That is what you will say, Thomas—and you wouldn’t take any money for those two thousand verses—no indeed you wouldn’t.
paragraphs.cn: 托马斯，你就会这么说。你不会为了这两千段经文收钱的，你肯定不会。

paragraphs.en: And now you wouldn’t mind telling me and this lady some of the things you’ve learned—no, I know you wouldn’t—for we are proud of little boys that learn.
paragraphs.cn: 现在你不介意告诉我还有这位女士一些你学到的东西吧？不，我知道你不会介意的，因为我们为爱学习的小男孩感到骄傲。”

paragraphs.en: Now, no doubt you know the names of all the twelve disciples.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，你一定知道那十二个门徒的名字了吧。

paragraphs.en: Won’t you tell us the names of the first two that were appointed?”
paragraphs.cn: 你能告诉我们，最先被选的两个人叫什么名字吗？

paragraphs.en: Tom was tugging at a button-hole and looking sheepish.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆拉着衣扣，看起来有点不好意思。

paragraphs.en: He blushed, now, and his eyes fell.
paragraphs.cn: 他脸红了，眼睛也向下看。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Walters’ heart sank within him.
paragraphs.cn: 沃尔特斯先生心里很难过。

paragraphs.en: He said to himself, it is not possible that the boy can answer the simplest question—why _did_ the Judge ask him?
paragraphs.cn: 他心想，这个孩子肯定答不出最简单的问题——法官为什么要问他呢？

paragraphs.en: Yet he felt obliged to speak up and say:
paragraphs.cn: 可他还是觉得应该说点什么：

paragraphs.en: “Answer the gentleman, Thomas—don’t be afraid.”
paragraphs.cn: “托马斯，回答这位叔叔——别害怕。”

paragraphs.en: Tom still hung fire.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆还是没有说话。

paragraphs.en: “Now I know you’ll tell me,” said the lady.
paragraphs.cn: “我知道你现在会告诉我了，”那位阿姨说。

paragraphs.en: “The names of the first two disciples were—”
paragraphs.cn: “最先的两个门徒，他们的名字是——”

paragraphs.en: “_David and Goliah!
paragraphs.cn: “大卫和歌利亚！

paragraphs.en: Let us draw the curtain of charity over the rest of the scene.
paragraphs.cn: 剩下的事情，我们就不多说了。

paragraphs.en: About half-past ten the cracked bell of the small church began to ring, and presently the people began to gather for the morning sermon.
paragraphs.cn: 大约十点半，小教堂的旧钟响了。很快，人们就来听早上的讲道了。

paragraphs.en: The Sunday-school children distributed themselves about the house and occupied pews with their parents, so as to be under supervision.
paragraphs.cn: 主日学校家的孩子们分散在教堂里，和爸爸妈妈坐在一起，这样才有人看着他们。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly came, and Tom and Sid and Mary sat with her—Tom being placed next the aisle, in order that he might be as far away from the open window and the seductive outside summer scenes as possible.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈来了，汤姆、希德和玛丽和她坐在一起——汤姆坐在靠过道的地方，这样他就离打开的窗户和外面好玩的夏天景色远一些。

paragraphs.en: The crowd filed up the aisles: the aged and needy postmaster, who had seen better days; the mayor and his wife—for they had a mayor there, among other unnecessaries; the justice of the peace; the widow Douglas, fair, smart, and forty, a generous, good-hearted soul and well-to-do, her hill mansion the only palace in the town, and the most hospitable and much the most lavish in the matter of festivities that St. Petersburg could boast; the bent and venerable Major and Mrs. Ward; lawyer Riverson, the new notable from a distance; next the belle of the village, followed by a troop of lawn-clad and ribbon-decked young heart-breakers; then all the young clerks in town in a body—for they had stood in the vestibule sucking their cane-heads, a circling wall of oiled and simpering admirers, till the last girl had run their gantlet; and last of all came the Model Boy, Willie Mufferson, taking as heedful care of his mother as if she were cut glass.
paragraphs.cn: 人们排队走过过道：有老邮递员，他以前很风光；有市长和他的妻子；有法官；有道格拉斯寡妇，她四十岁，又漂亮又聪明，人很好，也很有钱。她家山上的大房子是镇上最好的，也是圣彼得斯堡最爱去玩、最热闹的地方。还有驼背的沃德少校夫妇；新来的里弗森律师；接着是村里最漂亮的女孩，后面跟着一群穿着漂亮衣服的年轻小伙子；然后是镇上所有年轻的店员们，他们之前一直在门口等女孩子。最后来的是模范男孩威利·马弗森，他非常小心地照顾他的妈妈，好像妈妈是玻璃做的。

paragraphs.en: He always brought his mother to church, and was the pride of all the matrons.
paragraphs.cn: 他总是带妈妈去教堂，是所有阿姨妈妈们都夸奖的好孩子。

paragraphs.en: The boys all hated him, he was so good.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩子们都讨厌他，因为他太好了。

paragraphs.en: And besides, he had been “thrown up to them” so much.
paragraphs.cn: 而且，大家总是拿他来跟别的孩子比。

paragraphs.en: His white handkerchief was hanging out of his pocket behind, as usual on Sundays—accidentally.
paragraphs.cn: 他的白色手帕，像每个星期天一样，“不小心”地从他后面的口袋里露出来。

paragraphs.en: Tom had no handkerchief, and he looked upon boys who had as snobs.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆没有手帕，他觉得有手帕的男孩都是爱炫耀的人。

paragraphs.en: The congregation being fully assembled, now, the bell rang once more, to warn laggards and stragglers, and then a solemn hush fell upon the church which was only broken by the tittering and whispering of the choir in the gallery.
paragraphs.cn: 大家到齐后，钟又响了一声，提醒迟到的人。接着教堂里就安静下来了，只有楼上的唱诗班还在小声说话、笑。

paragraphs.en: The choir always tittered and whispered all through service.
paragraphs.cn: 唱诗班在讲道的时候总是小声说话、笑。

paragraphs.en: There was once a church choir that was not ill-bred, but I have forgotten where it was, now.
paragraphs.cn: 以前有一个唱诗班，他们很有礼貌，但我现在忘了是哪里的了。

paragraphs.en: It was a great many years ago, and I can scarcely remember anything about it, but I think it was in some foreign country.
paragraphs.cn: 那是很久很久以前的事了，我几乎都不记得了，但我想是在一个很远的国家。

paragraphs.en: The minister gave out the hymn, and read it through with a relish, in a peculiar style which was much admired in that part of the country.
paragraphs.cn: 牧师宣布了要唱的歌，他用一种特别的方式大声念出来，大家都觉得很好听。

paragraphs.en: His voice began on a medium key and climbed steadily up till it reached a certain point, where it bore with strong emphasis upon the topmost word and then plunged down as if from a spring-board:
paragraphs.cn: 他的声音从不高不低开始，慢慢地升高，到一个地方会特别大声地念最上面的字，然后又像跳水一样，一下就降下去了：

paragraphs.en: Shall I be car-ri-ed toe the skies, on flow’ry _beds_ of ease,
paragraphs.cn: 我能被带到天空，躺在舒服的花床上吗？

paragraphs.en: Whilst others fight to win the prize, and sail thro’ _blood_ -y seas?
paragraphs.cn: 当别人争着要赢奖品，在血海里航行时，他又会怎样呢？

paragraphs.en: He was regarded as a wonderful reader.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都觉得他书读得很好。

paragraphs.en: At church “sociables” he was always called upon to read poetry; and when he was through, the ladies would lift up their hands and let them fall helplessly in their laps, and “wall” their eyes, and shake their heads, as much as to say, “Words cannot express it; it is too beautiful, TOO beautiful for this mortal earth.”
paragraphs.cn: 在教堂聚会时，大家总请他念诗。他念完后，女士们会把手抬起又放下，眼睛睁得大大的，还不停地摇头，好像在说：“哇，太美了！美得说不出来！这个世界根本配不上这么好的声音！”

paragraphs.en: After the hymn had been sung, the Rev.
paragraphs.cn: 赞美诗唱完后，那位牧师。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Sprague turned himself into a bulletin-board, and read off “notices” of meetings and societies and things till it seemed that the list would stretch out to the crack of doom—a queer custom which is still kept up in America, even in cities, away here in this age of abundant newspapers.
paragraphs.cn: 斯普拉格牧师就像一个布告栏，念着各种会议、社团的“通知”，念得没完没了，好像要念到世界末日一样。这真是一个奇怪的规矩，即使在现在报纸很多的美国城市里，也还是这样。

paragraphs.en: Often, the less there is to justify a traditional custom, the harder it is to get rid of it.
paragraphs.cn: 很多时候，一个老规矩越是没道理，就越难改掉。

paragraphs.en: And now the minister prayed.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，牧师开始祈祷了。

paragraphs.en: A good, generous prayer it was, and went into details: it pleaded for the church, and the little children of the church; for the other churches of the village; for the village itself; for the county; for the State; for the State officers; for the United States; for the churches of the United States; for Congress; for the President; for the officers of the Government; for poor sailors, tossed by stormy seas; for the oppressed millions groaning under the heel of European monarchies and Oriental despotisms; for such as have the light and the good tidings, and yet have not eyes to see nor ears to hear withal; for the heathen in the far islands of the sea; and closed with a supplication that the words he was about to speak might find grace and favor, and be as seed sown in fertile ground, yielding in time a grateful harvest of good.
paragraphs.cn: 牧师做了个很棒的祈祷，说得特别详细：他为教堂和教堂里的小朋友们祈祷；为村里其他的教堂和村子祈祷；为县里、州里和州的官员们祈祷；为美国、美国的教堂、国会、总统和政府的官员们祈祷；他为那些在大海里遇到暴风雨的可怜水手祈祷；为那些被欧洲国王和东方暴君欺负的很多人祈祷；为那些知道好消息却看不见也听不见的人祈祷；为远方海岛上那些不信神的人祈祷；最后，他请求上帝，希望他接下来要说的话能像种子一样，种在肥沃的土地里，将来长出好多好的东西来。

paragraphs.en: Amen.
paragraphs.cn: 阿门。

paragraphs.en: There was a rustling of dresses, and the standing congregation sat down.
paragraphs.cn: 裙子发出沙沙的声音，站着的人们都坐了下来。

paragraphs.en: The boy whose history this book relates did not enjoy the prayer, he only endured it—if he even did that much.
paragraphs.cn: 这个故事里的小男孩不喜欢祈祷，他只是在忍着，都不知道他有没有真的忍住。

paragraphs.en: He was restive all through it; he kept tally of the details of the prayer, unconsciously—for he was not listening, but he knew the ground of old, and the clergyman’s regular route over it—and when a little trifle of new matter was interlarded, his ear detected it and his whole nature resented it; he considered additions unfair, and scoundrelly.
paragraphs.cn: 他整个祈祷过程都坐不住。他没有在听，却把祈祷的细节默默记下来，因为他对牧师那些老套的祈祷内容和顺序太熟悉了。每当牧师偷偷加进一点点新内容时，他耳朵一听就知道了，心里特别生气。他觉得这些多加的东西太不公平了，简直是坏透了。

paragraphs.en: In the midst of the prayer a fly had lit on the back of the pew in front of him and tortured his spirit by calmly rubbing its hands together, embracing its head with its arms, and polishing it so vigorously that it seemed to almost part company with the body, and the slender thread of a neck was exposed to view; scraping its wings with its hind legs and smoothing them to its body as if they had been coat-tails; going through its whole toilet as tranquilly as if it knew it was perfectly safe.
paragraphs.cn: 祈祷的时候，一只苍蝇停在他前面长椅的椅背上。它不慌不忙地搓着前腿，抱着头，用力地擦呀擦，好像头都要跟身子分开了，细细的脖子都露出来了。它又用后腿刮刮翅膀，把翅膀理顺贴在身上，就像穿了件燕尾服。苍蝇慢悠悠地打扮着自己，好像知道这里很安全，一点也不害怕。小男孩看着它，心里烦透了。

paragraphs.en: As indeed it was; for as sorely as Tom’s hands itched to grab for it they did not dare—he believed his soul would be instantly destroyed if he did such a thing while the prayer was going on.
paragraphs.cn: 苍蝇确实很安全。小男孩的手痒痒地想去抓它，却不敢动。他觉得如果在祈祷的时候去抓苍蝇，自己的灵魂会立刻完蛋的。

paragraphs.en: But with the closing sentence his hand began to curve and steal forward; and the instant the “Amen” was out the fly was a prisoner of war.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，当牧师念完最后一句，他的手就开始弯曲着，悄悄地伸了出去。牧师刚一说“阿门”，苍蝇就被他抓住了。

paragraphs.en: His aunt detected the act and made him let it go.
paragraphs.cn: 他阿姨看到了，让他把苍蝇放了。

paragraphs.en: The minister gave out his text and droned along monotonously through an argument that was so prosy that many a head by and by began to nod—and yet it was an argument that dealt in limitless fire and brimstone and thinned the predestined elect down to a company so small as to be hardly worth the saving.
paragraphs.cn: 牧师讲起了他的道理，声音又单调又枯燥，很多人听着听着都打起了瞌睡。他讲的是关于地狱的熊熊烈火和硫磺，还说能得救的人太少了，少到几乎不值得去救了。

paragraphs.en: Tom counted the pages of the sermon; after church he always knew how many pages there had been, but he seldom knew anything else about the discourse.
paragraphs.cn: 小男孩数着讲道稿的页数；每次礼拜结束后，他总是知道有几页，但其他内容他什么都不知道。

paragraphs.en: However, this time he was really interested for a little while.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，这一次他真的有一小会儿很感兴趣。

paragraphs.en: The minister made a grand and moving picture of the assembling together of the world’s hosts at the millennium when the lion and the lamb should lie down together and a little child should lead them.
paragraphs.cn: 牧师描绘了一幅又宏大又动人的画面：等到大家说的那个和平时代来临，狮子和羊会和平地躺在一起，一个小孩子来带领它们。

paragraphs.en: But the pathos, the lesson, the moral of the great spectacle were lost upon the boy; he only thought of the conspicuousness of the principal character before the on-looking nations; his face lit with the thought, and he said to himself that he wished he could be that child, if it was a tame lion.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，小男孩没有理解这个大场面的悲伤、道理和意义。他只想着那个小孩子在所有国家面前是多么引人注目。他想到这里，脸上亮了起来，心想：如果那只狮子是温顺的，他真希望能是那个小孩子。

paragraphs.en: Now he lapsed into suffering again, as the dry argument was resumed.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，随着枯燥的道理又开始讲起来，他又觉得难受了。

paragraphs.en: Presently he bethought him of a treasure he had and got it out.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，他想起自己有个宝贝，就把它拿了出来。

paragraphs.en: It was a large black beetle with formidable jaws—a “pinchbug,” he called it.
paragraphs.cn: 那是一只大大的黑甲虫，嘴巴很厉害，他管它叫“夹子虫”。

paragraphs.en: It was in a percussion-cap box.
paragraphs.cn: 它装在一个火帽盒子里。

paragraphs.en: The first thing the beetle did was to take him by the finger.
paragraphs.cn: 甲虫做的第一件事就是咬他的手指头。

paragraphs.en: A natural fillip followed, the beetle went floundering into the aisle and lit on its back, and the hurt finger went into the boy’s mouth.
paragraphs.cn: 小男孩条件反射地一弹，甲虫就跌跌撞撞地掉到过道里，肚子朝上。他的手指头被咬疼了，就赶紧放进嘴里。

paragraphs.en: The beetle lay there working its helpless legs, unable to turn over.
paragraphs.cn: 甲虫躺在那里，无助地挥舞着腿，翻不过身来。

paragraphs.en: Tom eyed it, and longed for it; but it was safe out of his reach.
paragraphs.cn: 小男孩盯着它，很想要它；可是它已经远了，他抓不到了。

paragraphs.en: Other people uninterested in the sermon found relief in the beetle, and they eyed it too.
paragraphs.cn: 其他对讲道不感兴趣的人也因为这只甲虫找到了乐趣，他们也盯着它看。

paragraphs.en: Presently a vagrant poodle dog came idling along, sad at heart, lazy with the summer softness and the quiet, weary of captivity, sighing for change.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，一只流浪的贵宾犬溜达过来了。它心里有点难过，夏天懒洋洋的，它也不想被关起来，就想换个地方玩。

paragraphs.en: He spied the beetle; the drooping tail lifted and wagged.
paragraphs.cn: 它看到了那只甲虫。耷拉着的尾巴一下子就竖起来，摇了摇。

paragraphs.en: He surveyed the prize; walked around it; smelt at it from a safe distance; walked around it again; grew bolder, and took a closer smell; then lifted his lip and made a gingerly snatch at it, just missing it; made another, and another; began to enjoy the diversion; subsided to his stomach with the beetle between his paws, and continued his experiments; grew weary at last, and then indifferent and absent-minded.
paragraphs.cn: 它看看这个“奖品”。它绕着甲虫走了一圈，远远地闻了闻。又绕了一圈，胆子变大了，凑近闻了闻。然后，它抬起嘴唇，小心地去抓，没抓到。它又抓了一次，又抓了一次。它开始觉得很好玩。它趴下来，把甲虫放在爪子中间，继续玩。最后它玩累了，就变得不理它了，心里想着别的事。

paragraphs.en: His head nodded, and little by little his chin descended and touched the enemy, who seized it.
paragraphs.cn: 它的头一点一点地往下点，下巴慢慢地碰到了“敌人”。甲虫一下子就咬住了它的下巴。

paragraphs.en: There was a sharp yelp, a flirt of the poodle’s head, and the beetle fell a couple of yards away, and lit on its back once more.
paragraphs.cn: 贵宾犬“嗷”地大叫一声，猛地甩了甩头，甲虫就掉到好几米外，又四脚朝天地躺着了。

paragraphs.en: The neighboring spectators shook with a gentle inward joy, several faces went behind fans and hand-kerchiefs, and Tom was entirely happy.
paragraphs.cn: 旁边看的人都偷偷地笑，好几个人用扇子或手帕挡住脸。汤姆 可真是太高兴了。

paragraphs.en: The dog looked foolish, and probably felt so; but there was resentment in his heart, too, and a craving for revenge.
paragraphs.cn: 这只狗看起来傻乎乎的，可能它自己也觉得挺丢脸。但是它心里也挺不服气，想去报仇。

paragraphs.en: So he went to the beetle and began a wary attack on it again; jumping at it from every point of a circle, lighting with his fore-paws within an inch of the creature, making even closer snatches at it with his teeth, and jerking his head till his ears flapped again.
paragraphs.cn: 于是它又走到甲虫那里，小心地又去攻击它。它从各个方向跳过去，前爪落在离甲虫很近的地方，用牙齿更近地去咬它。它还甩着头，耳朵又扇动起来了。

paragraphs.en: But he grew tired once more, after a while; tried to amuse himself with a fly but found no relief; followed an ant around, with his nose close to the floor, and quickly wearied of that; yawned, sighed, forgot the beetle entirely, and sat down on it.
paragraphs.cn: 但过了一会儿，它又累了。它想和苍蝇玩，觉得没意思。它鼻子贴着地，跟着一只蚂蚁转，很快又玩腻了。它打了个哈欠，叹了口气，把甲虫忘得一干二净，然后一屁股坐了上去。

paragraphs.en: Then there was a wild yelp of agony and the poodle went sailing up the aisle; the yelps continued, and so did the dog; he crossed the house in front of the altar; he flew down the other aisle; he crossed before the doors; he clamored up the home-stretch; his anguish grew with his progress, till presently he was but a woolly comet moving in its orbit with the gleam and the speed of light.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，贵宾犬痛苦地大叫一声，一下子就冲向过道。它一直叫着，也一直跑着。它跑过祭坛前面，穿过教堂；又飞快地跑下另一条过道；它跑过门前；它冲向终点。它跑得越快，就越痛苦。最后，它就像一颗毛茸茸的彗星，飞快地跑着，像一道光一样。

paragraphs.en: At last the frantic sufferer sheered from its course, and sprang into its master’s lap; he flung it out of the window, and the voice of distress quickly thinned away and died in the distance.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，这只疼得乱跑的狗改了方向，一下子跳到主人的腿上。主人把它扔出了窗外，它难过的叫声很快就越来越小，然后听不见了。

paragraphs.en: By this time the whole church was red-faced and suffocating with suppressed laughter, and the sermon had come to a dead standstill.
paragraphs.cn: 这时候，整个教堂里的人都憋着笑，脸涨得通红。布道也完全停了下来。

paragraphs.en: The discourse was resumed presently, but it went lame and halting, all possibility of impressiveness being at an end; for even the gravest sentiments were constantly being received with a smothered burst of unholy mirth, under cover of some remote pew-back, as if the poor parson had said a rarely facetious thing.
paragraphs.cn: 讲道很快又开始了，但讲得很不顺，也一点都不严肃了。因为牧师说的再严肃的话，也会被后面座位上的人偷偷笑声打断，好像那个可怜的牧师说了很好笑的话一样。

paragraphs.en: It was a genuine relief to the whole congregation when the ordeal was over and the benediction pronounced.
paragraphs.cn: 当这场“不容易”的事情终于结束，牧师说了祝福的话后，教堂里的人都真正松了一口气。

paragraphs.en: Tom Sawyer went home quite cheerful, thinking to himself that there was some satisfaction about divine service when there was a bit of variety in it.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆·索亚 高高兴兴地回家了，他心里想，礼拜仪式如果有点好玩的事，那还是挺不错的。

paragraphs.en: He had but one marring thought; he was willing that the dog should play with his pinchbug, but he did not think it was upright in him to carry it off.
paragraphs.cn: 他就只有一个不太好的想法：他愿意让狗玩他的甲虫，但觉得狗把它叼走就不太好。

paragraphs.en: Monday morning found Tom Sawyer miserable.
paragraphs.cn: 星期一早上，汤姆·索亚 觉得很难受。

paragraphs.en: Monday morning always found him so—because it began another week’s slow suffering in school.
paragraphs.cn: 星期一早上他总是这样——因为又要开始在学校里慢慢“受苦”一周了。

paragraphs.en: He generally began that day with wishing he had had no intervening holiday, it made the going into captivity and fetters again so much more odious.
paragraphs.cn: 他通常一到这天就希望没有假期，因为假期过后又要回学校（就像又被关起来一样），这让他觉得更讨厌。

paragraphs.en: Tom lay thinking.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 躺着想事。

paragraphs.en: Presently it occurred to him that he wished he was sick; then he could stay home from school.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，他想，要是自己生病了就好了；那样就可以不去上学了。

paragraphs.en: Here was a vague possibility.
paragraphs.cn: 也许可以这样。

paragraphs.en: He canvassed his system.
paragraphs.cn: 他检查了一下自己的身体有没有不舒服。

paragraphs.en: No ailment was found, and he investigated again.
paragraphs.cn: 没发现哪里不舒服，他又检查了一遍。

paragraphs.en: This time he thought he could detect colicky symptoms, and he began to encourage them with considerable hope.
paragraphs.cn: 这次他觉得好像有点肚子疼。他心里很高兴，就想着让肚子疼得更厉害一点。

paragraphs.en: But they soon grew feeble, and presently died wholly away.
paragraphs.cn: 但是这些肚子疼的感觉很快就变弱了，然后完全消失了。

paragraphs.en: He reflected further.
paragraphs.cn: 他又想了想。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly he discovered something.
paragraphs.cn: 突然，他发现了一件事。

paragraphs.en: One of his upper front teeth was loose.
paragraphs.cn: 他一颗上面的门牙松了。

paragraphs.en: This was lucky; he was about to begin to groan, as a “starter,” as he called it, when it occurred to him that if he came into court with that argument, his aunt would pull it out, and that would hurt.
paragraphs.cn: 这可真幸运。他正想先哼哼几声，算是“开场白”，突然他想到，如果他用这个理由请假，姑妈会把牙拔掉，那可就太疼了。

paragraphs.en: So he thought he would hold the tooth in reserve for the present, and seek further.
paragraphs.cn: 他想先把牙疼留着，再找找别的。

paragraphs.en: Nothing offered for some little time, and then he remembered hearing the doctor tell about a certain thing that laid up a patient for two or three weeks and threatened to make him lose a finger.
paragraphs.cn: 一会儿都没想出啥。他突然想起医生说过一种病，会让人躺两三周，还可能让手指掉下来。

paragraphs.en: So the boy eagerly drew his sore toe from under the sheet and held it up for inspection.
paragraphs.cn: 于是，他赶紧把疼的脚趾从被子里伸出来，举起来给大家看。

paragraphs.en: But now he did not know the necessary symptoms.
paragraphs.cn: 可他不知道这种病会有什么样子。

paragraphs.en: However, it seemed well worth while to chance it, so he fell to groaning with considerable spirit.
paragraphs.cn: 算了，试试吧！他就很有精神地开始哼哼起来。

paragraphs.en: But Sid slept on unconscious.
paragraphs.cn: 可是希德还在睡，没醒。

paragraphs.en: Tom groaned louder, and fancied that he began to feel pain in the toe.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆哼得更大声了，还觉得脚趾真的有点疼。

paragraphs.en: No result from Sid.
paragraphs.cn: 希德没有反应。

paragraphs.en: Tom was panting with his exertions by this time.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，汤姆已经累得直喘气了。

paragraphs.en: He took a rest and then swelled himself up and fetched a succession of admirable groans.
paragraphs.cn: 他休息了一下，然后鼓起肚子，又哼了几声好听的。

paragraphs.en: Sid snored on.
paragraphs.cn: 希德还在打呼噜。

paragraphs.en: Tom was aggravated.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆有点生气了。

paragraphs.en: He said, “Sid, Sid!” and shook him.
paragraphs.cn: 他说：“希德，希德！”然后摇了摇他。

paragraphs.en: This course worked well, and Tom began to groan again.
paragraphs.cn: 这招很管用，汤姆又开始哼哼了。

paragraphs.en: Sid yawned, stretched, then brought himself up on his elbow with a snort, and began to stare at Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 希德打了个哈欠，伸了伸懒腰，然后哼了一声，用手肘撑起身子，看着汤姆。

paragraphs.en: Tom went on groaning.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆还在哼哼。

paragraphs.en: Sid said:
paragraphs.cn: 希德说：

paragraphs.en: “Tom!
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆！

paragraphs.en: Say, Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: 喂，汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: [No response.]
paragraphs.cn: [没有回答。]

paragraphs.en: “Here, Tom!
paragraphs.cn: “喂，汤姆！

paragraphs.en: TOM!
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆！

paragraphs.en: What is the matter, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，你怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: And he shook him and looked in his face anxiously.
paragraphs.cn: 他摇了摇他，着急地看着他的脸。

paragraphs.en: Tom moaned out:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆哼哼着说：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, don’t, Sid.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，希德，别这样。

paragraphs.en: Don’t joggle me.”
paragraphs.cn: 别晃我。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, what’s the matter, Tom?
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，汤姆，你怎么了？

paragraphs.en: I must call auntie.”
paragraphs.cn: 我得去叫阿姨了。”

paragraphs.en: “No—never mind.
paragraphs.cn: “不—没关系。

paragraphs.en: It’ll be over by and by, maybe.
paragraphs.cn: 也许很快就会好了。

paragraphs.en: Don’t call anybody.”
paragraphs.cn: 不要叫任何人来。”

paragraphs.en: “But I must!
paragraphs.cn: “可是我一定要叫人来！

paragraphs.en: _Don’t_ groan so, Tom, it’s awful.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，别再哼哼了，太难受了。

paragraphs.en: How long you been this way?”
paragraphs.cn: 你这样多久了？”

paragraphs.en: “Hours.
paragraphs.cn: “好几个小时了。

paragraphs.en: Ouch!
paragraphs.cn: 哎哟！

paragraphs.en: Oh, don’t stir so, Sid, you’ll kill me.”
paragraphs.cn: 噢，希德，别动来动去了，你会把我弄死的。”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, why didn’t you wake me sooner?
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，你为什么不早点叫醒我？

paragraphs.en: Oh, Tom, _don’t!
paragraphs.cn: 噢，汤姆，不要这样！

paragraphs.en: _ It makes my flesh crawl to hear you.
paragraphs.cn: 听你这么哼哼，我全身都起鸡皮疙瘩了。

paragraphs.en: Tom, what is the matter?”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，你怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: “I forgive you everything, Sid.
paragraphs.cn: “希德，我原谅你所有的事情。

paragraphs.en: [Groan.]
paragraphs.cn: [哼哼声。]

paragraphs.en: Everything you’ve ever done to me.
paragraphs.cn: 你对我做过的所有事。

paragraphs.en: When I’m gone—”
paragraphs.cn: 等我走了以后——”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Tom, you ain’t dying, are you?
paragraphs.cn: “噢，汤姆，你不是快死了吧？

paragraphs.en: Don’t, Tom—oh, don’t.
paragraphs.cn: 别这样，汤姆——噢，别这样。

paragraphs.en: Maybe—”
paragraphs.cn: 也许——”

paragraphs.en: “I forgive everybody, Sid.
paragraphs.cn: “我原谅每一个人，希德。

paragraphs.en: [Groan.]
paragraphs.cn: [哼哼声。]

paragraphs.en: Tell ’em so, Sid.
paragraphs.cn: 希德，告诉他们。

paragraphs.en: And Sid, you give my window-sash and my cat with one eye to that new girl that’s come to town, and tell her—”
paragraphs.cn: 还有希德，你把我的窗框和我那只独眼猫送给刚来镇上的那个新女孩，告诉她——”

paragraphs.en: But Sid had snatched his clothes and gone.
paragraphs.cn: 可是希德已经抓起他的衣服跑了。

paragraphs.en: Tom was suffering in reality, now, so handsomely was his imagination working, and so his groans had gathered quite a genuine tone.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆现在真的在受苦了，因为他的想象力太丰富了，所以他的哼哼声也变得非常真实了。

paragraphs.en: Sid flew downstairs and said:
paragraphs.cn: 希德飞快地跑下楼，喊道：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Aunt Polly, come!
paragraphs.cn: “噢，波莉姨妈，快来！

paragraphs.en: Tom’s dying!”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆快死了！”

paragraphs.en: “Dying!”
paragraphs.cn: “快死了？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes’m.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，太太。”

paragraphs.en: Don’t wait—come quick!”
paragraphs.cn: “别等了—快来！”

paragraphs.en: “Rubbage!
paragraphs.cn: “胡说！

paragraphs.en: I don’t believe it!”
paragraphs.cn: 我不相信！”

paragraphs.en: But she fled upstairs, nevertheless, with Sid and Mary at her heels.
paragraphs.cn: 但她还是跑上楼了，希德 和 玛丽 紧跟着她。

paragraphs.en: And her face grew white, too, and her lip trembled.
paragraphs.cn: 她的脸也白了，嘴唇也在抖。

paragraphs.en: When she reached the bedside she gasped out:
paragraphs.cn: 她走到床边时，喘着气说：

paragraphs.en: “You, Tom!
paragraphs.cn: “你，汤姆！

paragraphs.en: Tom, what’s the matter with you?”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，你怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, auntie, I’m—”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，姨妈，我—”

paragraphs.en: “What’s the matter with you—what is the matter with you, child?”
paragraphs.cn: “你怎么了—孩子，你怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, auntie, my sore toe’s mortified!”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，姨妈，我的脚趾头疼死了！”

paragraphs.en: The old lady sank down into a chair and laughed a little, then cried a little, then did both together.
paragraphs.cn: 老太太一屁股坐到椅子上，先是笑了笑，又哭了一会儿，然后又哭又笑。

paragraphs.en: This restored her and she said:
paragraphs.cn: 这让她缓过来了，她说道：

paragraphs.en: “Tom, what a turn you did give me.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，你真是吓了我一大跳。

paragraphs.en: Now you shut up that nonsense and climb out of this.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在别胡闹了，快起来吧。”

paragraphs.en: The groans ceased and the pain vanished from the toe.
paragraphs.cn: 哼哼声停了，脚趾头的疼痛也消失了。

paragraphs.en: The boy felt a little foolish, and he said:
paragraphs.cn: 男孩觉得有点儿不好意思，他说：

paragraphs.en: “Aunt Polly, it _seemed_ mortified, and it hurt so I never minded my tooth at all.”
paragraphs.cn: “波莉姨妈，它好像疼死了，疼得我连牙齿都忘了。”

paragraphs.en: “Your tooth, indeed!
paragraphs.cn: “你的牙齿，真的吗！

paragraphs.en: What’s the matter with your tooth?”
paragraphs.cn: 你的牙齿怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: “One of them’s loose, and it aches perfectly awful.”
paragraphs.cn: “我有一颗牙松了，疼得厉害。”

paragraphs.en: “There, there, now, don’t begin that groaning again.
paragraphs.cn: “好了好了，别再哼哼了。

paragraphs.en: Open your mouth.
paragraphs.cn: 张开嘴巴。

paragraphs.en: Well—your tooth _is_ loose, but you’re not going to die about that.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯—你的牙齿是松了，但你不会因此死掉的。

paragraphs.en: Mary, get me a silk thread, and a chunk of fire out of the kitchen.”
paragraphs.cn: 玛丽，去给我拿一根丝线，再从厨房拿一块火炭来。”

paragraphs.en: Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 说：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, please, auntie, don’t pull it out.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，求求你，姨妈，别拔掉它。

paragraphs.en: It don’t hurt any more.
paragraphs.cn: 它不疼了。

paragraphs.en: I wish I may never stir if it does.
paragraphs.cn: 如果它还疼，我就再也不动了。

paragraphs.en: Please don’t, auntie.
paragraphs.cn: 求你，姨妈，别拔。

paragraphs.en: I don’t want to stay home from school.”
paragraphs.cn: 我不想在家待着，不去学校。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, you don’t, don’t you?
paragraphs.cn: “噢，你不想吗？

paragraphs.en: So all this row was because you thought you’d get to stay home from school and go a-fishing?
paragraphs.cn: 你闹腾了半天，就因为你以为能不去上学，好去钓鱼吗？

paragraphs.en: Tom, Tom, I love you so, and you seem to try every way you can to break my old heart with your outrageousness.”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，汤姆，我真爱你，可你总用调皮捣蛋让我伤透了心。”

paragraphs.en: By this time the dental instruments were ready.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，拔牙的工具都准备好了。

paragraphs.en: The old lady made one end of the silk thread fast to Tom’s tooth with a loop and tied the other to the bedpost.
paragraphs.cn: 老太太用线的一头把汤姆的牙齿套住，另一头系在床柱上。

paragraphs.en: Then she seized the chunk of fire and suddenly thrust it almost into the boy’s face.
paragraphs.cn: 然后她拿起一团火，突然把它伸到男孩的脸前。

paragraphs.en: The tooth hung dangling by the bedpost, now.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，那颗牙就挂在床柱边荡来荡去。

paragraphs.en: But all trials bring their compensations.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，受了苦，总会有好事发生。

paragraphs.en: As Tom wended to school after breakfast, he was the envy of every boy he met because the gap in his upper row of teeth enabled him to expectorate in a new and admirable way.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆吃完早饭去上学，他遇到的每个男孩都羡慕他，因为他上排牙齿有个洞，让他能用一种很酷的方式吐口水。

paragraphs.en: He gathered quite a following of lads interested in the exhibition; and one that had cut his finger and had been a centre of fascination and homage up to this time, now found himself suddenly without an adherent, and shorn of his glory.
paragraphs.cn: 他吸引了一群喜欢看他表演的男孩子；有个男孩以前手指头受伤，一直都是大家围着看的明星，现在突然没人理他了，他的风头也没了。

paragraphs.en: His heart was heavy, and he said with a disdain which he did not feel that it wasn’t anything to spit like Tom Sawyer; but another boy said, “Sour grapes!” and he wandered away a dismantled hero.
paragraphs.cn: 他心里很难受，嘴上却假装不屑地说，像汤姆·索亚那样吐口水，有什么了不起的；可另一个男孩说：“吃不到葡萄说葡萄酸！”他就这样，不再是英雄，伤心地走开了。

paragraphs.en: Shortly Tom came upon the juvenile pariah of the village, Huckleberry Finn, son of the town drunkard.
paragraphs.cn: 没多久，汤姆就遇到了村里那个大家不太喜欢的小孩哈克贝利·费恩，他是镇上爱喝酒叔叔的儿子。

paragraphs.en: Huckleberry was cordially hated and dreaded by all the mothers of the town, because he was idle and lawless and vulgar and bad—and because all their children admired him so, and delighted in his forbidden society, and wished they dared to be like him.
paragraphs.cn: 镇上所有的妈妈们都非常讨厌和害怕哈克贝利，因为他很懒，不听话，又粗鲁又调皮——更因为她们的孩子都特别喜欢他，喜欢跟他玩那些不让玩的游戏，还希望自己也敢像他一样。

paragraphs.en: Tom was like the rest of the respectable boys, in that he envied Huckleberry his gaudy outcast condition, and was under strict orders not to play with him.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆和其他那些规矩的男孩一样，他羡慕哈克贝利那种被排斥却很酷的生活，而且他被严格命令不能和哈克贝利玩。

paragraphs.en: So he played with him every time he got a chance.
paragraphs.cn: 所以，他一有机会就和他玩。

paragraphs.en: Huckleberry was always dressed in the cast-off clothes of full-grown men, and they were in perennial bloom and fluttering with rags.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克贝利总是穿着大人穿旧的衣服，那些衣服总是破破烂烂的，飘着布条。

paragraphs.en: His hat was a vast ruin with a wide crescent lopped out of its brim; his coat, when he wore one, hung nearly to his heels and had the rearward buttons far down the back; but one suspender supported his trousers; the seat of the trousers bagged low and contained nothing, the fringed legs dragged in the dirt when not rolled up.
paragraphs.cn: 他的帽子很大，破了一个大大的月牙形缺口；他穿的外套几乎拖到脚后跟，后面的扣子也都系得很低；只有一根背带吊着他的裤子；裤子屁股那儿松松垮垮的，里面空空的，裤腿边磨成了穗子，不卷起来就拖在地上。

paragraphs.en: Huckleberry came and went, at his own free will.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克贝利来去自由，想怎么样就怎么样。

paragraphs.en: He slept on doorsteps in fine weather and in empty hogsheads in wet; he did not have to go to school or to church, or call any being master or obey anybody; he could go fishing or swimming when and where he chose, and stay as long as it suited him; nobody forbade him to fight; he could sit up as late as he pleased; he was always the first boy that went barefoot in the spring and the last to resume leather in the fall; he never had to wash, nor put on clean clothes; he could swear wonderfully.
paragraphs.cn: 天气好的时候，哈克贝利睡在别人家门口；下雨的时候，就睡在空的酒桶里。他不用去上学，也不用去教堂。他不用听谁的命令，也不用服从任何人。他想去哪儿钓鱼或游泳，想待多久都行。没人不让他打架。他想熬夜到多晚都可以。他总是春天里第一个不穿鞋的男孩，也是秋天里最后一个穿鞋的男孩。他从来不用洗澡，也不用穿干净衣服。他骂人的话也说得可溜了。

paragraphs.en: In a word, everything that goes to make life precious that boy had.
paragraphs.cn: 总之，所有让生活变得快乐的事情，那个男孩都有。

paragraphs.en: So thought every harassed, hampered, respectable boy in St. Petersburg.
paragraphs.cn: 圣彼得斯堡镇上每个被管着、被约束的“好孩子”都这样想。

paragraphs.en: Tom hailed the romantic outcast:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆向这个自由自在的“野孩子”打招呼：

paragraphs.en: “Hello, Huckleberry!”
paragraphs.cn: “你好，哈克贝利！”

paragraphs.en: “Hello yourself, and see how you like it.”
paragraphs.cn: “你也好啊，你自己看看喜不喜欢。”

paragraphs.en: “What’s that you got?”
paragraphs.cn: “你拿的是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Dead cat.”
paragraphs.cn: “死猫。”

paragraphs.en: “Lemme see him, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “让我看看他，哈克。

paragraphs.en: My, he’s pretty stiff.
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，他真硬。

paragraphs.en: Where’d you get him?”
paragraphs.cn: 你在哪儿找到他的？”

paragraphs.en: “Bought him off’n a boy.”
paragraphs.cn: 从一个男孩那里买的。

paragraphs.en: “What did you give?”
paragraphs.cn: 你给了什么？

paragraphs.en: “I give a blue ticket and a bladder that I got at the slaughter-house.”
paragraphs.cn: 我给了一张蓝色的票，还有一个我在屠宰场拿到的气球。

paragraphs.en: “Where’d you get the blue ticket?”
paragraphs.cn: 你的蓝票是从哪里来的？

paragraphs.en: “Bought it off’n Ben Rogers two weeks ago for a hoop-stick.”
paragraphs.cn: 两周前，我用一个铁环棒，从 本·罗杰斯 那里买的。

paragraphs.en: “Say—what is dead cats good for, Huck?”
paragraphs.cn: 哎——死猫有什么用啊，哈克？

paragraphs.en: “Good for?
paragraphs.cn: 有什么用？

paragraphs.en: Cure warts with.”
paragraphs.cn: 可以治疣子。

paragraphs.en: “No!
paragraphs.cn: 不是吧！

paragraphs.en: Is that so?
paragraphs.cn: 真的吗？

paragraphs.en: I know something that’s better.”
paragraphs.cn: 我知道一个更好的办法。

paragraphs.en: “I bet you don’t.
paragraphs.cn: 我才不信呢。

paragraphs.en: What is it?”
paragraphs.cn: 是什么呀？

paragraphs.en: “Why, spunk-water.”
paragraphs.cn: 嘿，是树洞水。

paragraphs.en: “Spunk-water!
paragraphs.cn: 树洞水！

paragraphs.en: I wouldn’t give a dern for spunk-water.”
paragraphs.cn: 树洞水一点用都没有。

paragraphs.en: “You wouldn’t, wouldn’t you?
paragraphs.cn: 你不信？

paragraphs.en: D’you ever try it?”
paragraphs.cn: 你试过吗？

paragraphs.en: “No, I hain’t.
paragraphs.cn: 没有，我没试过。

paragraphs.en: But Bob Tanner did.”
paragraphs.cn: 但是鲍勃·坦纳试过。

paragraphs.en: “Who told you so!”
paragraphs.cn: 谁告诉你的！

paragraphs.en: “Why, he told Jeff Thatcher, and Jeff told Johnny Baker, and Johnny told Jim Hollis, and Jim told Ben Rogers, and Ben told a nigger, and the nigger told me.
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，他告诉了杰夫 撒切尔，杰夫告诉了约翰尼·贝克，约翰尼告诉了 吉姆 霍利斯，吉姆 告诉了 本·罗杰斯，本告诉了一个黑人，那个黑人又告诉了我。

paragraphs.en: There now!”
paragraphs.cn: 这下你知道了吧！

paragraphs.en: “Well, what of it?
paragraphs.cn: 那又怎么样？

paragraphs.en: They’ll all lie.
paragraphs.cn: 他们都会说谎。

paragraphs.en: Leastways all but the nigger.
paragraphs.cn: 至少除了那个黑人。

paragraphs.en: I don’t know _him_.
paragraphs.cn: 我不认识他。

paragraphs.en: But I never see a nigger that _wouldn’t_ lie.
paragraphs.cn: 但我从没见过一个黑人不会说谎。

paragraphs.en: Shucks!
paragraphs.cn: 呸！

paragraphs.en: Now you tell me how Bob Tanner done it, Huck.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在你告诉我，鲍勃·坦纳是怎么做到的，哈克。

paragraphs.en: “Why, he took and dipped his hand in a rotten stump where the rain-water was.”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，他把手伸进了一个有雨水的烂树桩里。”

paragraphs.en: “In the daytime?”
paragraphs.cn: “白天吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Certainly.”
paragraphs.cn: “当然啦！”

paragraphs.en: “With his face to the stump?”
paragraphs.cn: “脸对着树桩吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes.
paragraphs.cn: “是呀。

paragraphs.en: Least I reckon so.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想是吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Did he say anything?”
paragraphs.cn: “他说了什么吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t reckon he did.
paragraphs.cn: “我想他没有。

paragraphs.en: I don’t know.”
paragraphs.cn: 我不知道。”

paragraphs.en: “Aha!
paragraphs.cn: “啊哈！

paragraphs.en: Talk about trying to cure warts with spunk-water such a blame fool way as that!
paragraphs.cn: 这种笨办法根本治不好疣子！

paragraphs.en: Why, that ain’t a-going to do any good.
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，那根本没用。

paragraphs.en: You got to go all by yourself, to the middle of the woods, where you know there’s a spunk-water stump, and just as it’s midnight you back up against the stump and jam your hand in and say:
paragraphs.cn: 你得一个人走到森林深处，找到一个有雨水的烂树桩。等半夜的时候，你背对着树桩，把手伸进去，然后说：

paragraphs.en: ‘Barley-corn, barley-corn, injun-meal shorts, Spunk-water, spunk-water, swaller these warts,’
paragraphs.cn: ‘大麦粒，大麦粒，玉米粉渣，臭水，臭水，把这些疣子吞掉吧，’

paragraphs.en: and then walk away quick, eleven steps, with your eyes shut, and then turn around three times and walk home without speaking to anybody.
paragraphs.cn: 然后闭着眼睛快走开，走十一步。接着转三圈，然后不和任何人说话就回家。

paragraphs.en: Because if you speak the charm’s busted.”
paragraphs.cn: 因为如果你说话了，咒语就没用了。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, that sounds like a good way; but that ain’t the way Bob Tanner done.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，这个办法听起来不错；但这不是鲍勃·坦纳做的。”

paragraphs.en: “No, sir, you can bet he didn’t, becuz he’s the wartiest boy in this town; and he wouldn’t have a wart on him if he’d knowed how to work spunk-water.
paragraphs.cn: “不，他肯定没那么做，因为他是镇上疣子最多的男孩；如果他知道怎么用臭水，他身上就不会有疣子了。

paragraphs.en: I’ve took off thousands of warts off of my hands that way, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: 我用那种方法去掉了手上成千上万个疣子，哈克。

paragraphs.en: I play with frogs so much that I’ve always got considerable many warts.
paragraphs.cn: 我总是和青蛙玩，所以手上总是有很多疣子。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes I take ’em off with a bean.”
paragraphs.cn: 有时候我用豆子把它们去掉。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, bean’s good.
paragraphs.cn: “是呀，豆子很好用。

paragraphs.en: I’ve done that.”
paragraphs.cn: 我也那样做过。”

paragraphs.en: “Have you?
paragraphs.cn: “你做过吗？

paragraphs.en: What’s your way?”
paragraphs.cn: 你的办法是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “You take and split the bean, and cut the wart so as to get some blood, and then you put the blood on one piece of the bean and take and dig a hole and bury it ’bout midnight at the crossroads in the dark of the moon, and then you burn up the rest of the bean.
paragraphs.cn: “你把豆子掰开，把疣子弄破一点，让它流点血。然后把血滴在豆子的一半上，接着挖个洞，在半夜、在月亮看不见的时候，把它埋在十字路口。然后把剩下的豆子烧掉。

paragraphs.en: You see that piece that’s got the blood on it will keep drawing and drawing, trying to fetch the other piece to it, and so that helps the blood to draw the wart, and pretty soon off she comes.”
paragraphs.cn: 你看，沾了血的那一半豆子会一直吸，一直吸，想要把另一半拉过来。这样呢，血就能把疣子吸走，很快疣子就掉了。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, that’s it, Huck—that’s it; though when you’re burying it if you say ‘Down bean; off wart; come no more to bother me!’ it’s better.
paragraphs.cn: “是呀，就是这样，哈克——就是这样；不过，如果你在埋的时候说‘豆子下去；疣子掉下；别再来烦我！’那就更好了。

paragraphs.en: That’s the way Joe Harper does, and he’s been nearly to Coonville and most everywheres.
paragraphs.cn: 乔·哈珀就是这么做的，他去过浣熊镇，几乎所有地方都去过了。

paragraphs.en: But say—how do you cure ’em with dead cats?”
paragraphs.cn: 不过你说——怎么用死猫来治呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, you take your cat and go and get in the grave-yard ’long about midnight when somebody that was wicked has been buried; and when it’s midnight a devil will come, or maybe two or three, but you can’t see ’em, you can only hear something like the wind, or maybe hear ’em talk; and when they’re taking that feller away, you heave your cat after ’em and say, ‘Devil follow corpse, cat follow devil, warts follow cat, I’m done with ye!’
paragraphs.cn: “嘿，你带着猫，半夜去墓地。那里埋了一个坏人。到了半夜，魔鬼就会来。你看不见他们，只能听到风声，或者他们说话。当他们带走那个坏人的时候，你就把猫扔过去，然后说：‘魔鬼跟着死人跑，猫跟着魔鬼跑，瘊子跟着猫跑，我好了！’

paragraphs.en: That’ll fetch _any_ wart.”
paragraphs.cn: 这样就能把瘊子弄掉！”

paragraphs.en: “Sounds right.
paragraphs.cn: “听起来有道理。

paragraphs.en: D’you ever try it, Huck?”
paragraphs.cn: 你试过吗，哈克？”

paragraphs.en: “No, but old Mother Hopkins told me.”
paragraphs.cn: “没有，但是霍普金斯老奶奶告诉我的。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I reckon it’s so, then.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，那我想是真的了。

paragraphs.en: Becuz they say she’s a witch.”
paragraphs.cn: 因为他们都说她是个巫婆。”

paragraphs.en: “Say!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀！

paragraphs.en: Why, Tom, I _know_ she is.
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，汤姆，我就是知道她是。

paragraphs.en: She witched pap.
paragraphs.cn: 她把爸爸施了巫术。

paragraphs.en: Pap says so his own self.
paragraphs.cn: 爸爸自己说的。

paragraphs.en: He come along one day, and he see she was a-witching him, so he took up a rock, and if she hadn’t dodged, he’d a got her.
paragraphs.cn: 有一天他看到她在施魔法，就拿起一块石头。如果她没躲开，爸爸就打到她了。

paragraphs.en: Well, that very night he rolled off’n a shed wher’ he was a layin drunk, and broke his arm.”
paragraphs.cn: 那天晚上，爸爸喝醉了，从棚子上摔下来，把胳膊摔断了。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, that’s awful.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，这太可怕了。

paragraphs.en: How did he know she was a-witching him?”
paragraphs.cn: 他怎么知道她在对他施魔法呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Lord, pap can tell, easy.
paragraphs.cn: “天哪，爸爸很容易就能看出来。

paragraphs.en: Pap says when they keep looking at you right stiddy, they’re a-witching you.
paragraphs.cn: 爸爸说，如果他们一直盯着你看，就是在对你施魔法。

paragraphs.en: Specially if they mumble.
paragraphs.cn: 特别是如果他们嘴里念念有词的话。

paragraphs.en: Becuz when they mumble they’re saying the Lord’s Prayer backards.”
paragraphs.cn: 因为他们念念有词的时候，是在倒着念《主祷文》。”

paragraphs.en: “Say, Hucky, when you going to try the cat?”
paragraphs.cn: “哎，哈克，你什么时候去试那个猫啊？”

paragraphs.en: “To-night.
paragraphs.cn: “今晚。

paragraphs.en: I reckon they’ll come after old Hoss Williams to-night.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想他们今晚会来找老霍斯·威廉姆斯。”

paragraphs.en: “But they buried him Saturday.
paragraphs.cn: “可是他们周六就埋了他啊。

paragraphs.en: Didn’t they get him Saturday night?”
paragraphs.cn: 他们周六晚上没带走他吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, how you talk!
paragraphs.cn: “你说什么呢！

paragraphs.en: How could their charms work till midnight?
paragraphs.cn: 他们的咒语怎么可能等到半夜才有用呢？

paragraphs.en: —and _then_ it’s Sunday.
paragraphs.cn: ——而且那时就是星期天了。

paragraphs.en: Devils don’t slosh around much of a Sunday, I don’t reckon.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想，魔鬼星期天一般不会到处晃悠的。”

paragraphs.en: “I never thought of that.
paragraphs.cn: “我从没想过这个。

paragraphs.en: That’s so.
paragraphs.cn: 是这样啊。”

paragraphs.en: Lemme go with you?”
paragraphs.cn: 我能跟你一起去吗？

paragraphs.en: “Of course—if you ain’t afeard.”
paragraphs.cn: 当然啦，如果你不怕的话。

paragraphs.en: “Afeard!
paragraphs.cn: 害怕！

paragraphs.en: ’Tain’t likely.
paragraphs.cn: 才不会呢。

paragraphs.en: Will you meow?”
paragraphs.cn: 你会喵喵叫吗？

paragraphs.en: “Yes—and you meow back, if you get a chance.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，如果你有机会，你也喵喵叫。

paragraphs.en: Last time, you kep’ me a-meowing around till old Hays went to throwing rocks at me and says ‘Dern that cat!’ and so I hove a brick through his window—but don’t you tell.”
paragraphs.cn: 上次你一直让我喵喵叫，直到老海斯开始扔石头打我，还说‘真是只讨厌的猫！’，所以我朝他窗户扔了块砖头——但你可别说出去哦。

paragraphs.en: “I won’t.
paragraphs.cn: 我不会的。

paragraphs.en: I couldn’t meow that night, becuz auntie was watching me, but I’ll meow this time.
paragraphs.cn: 那天晚上我没法喵喵叫，因为阿姨在看着我，但这次我会喵喵叫的。

paragraphs.en: Say—what’s that?”
paragraphs.cn: 哎——那是什么？

paragraphs.en: “Nothing but a tick.”
paragraphs.cn: 只是一只蜱虫。

paragraphs.en: “Where’d you get him?”
paragraphs.cn: 你从哪儿弄来的？

paragraphs.en: “Out in the woods.”
paragraphs.cn: 在树林里。

paragraphs.en: “What’ll you take for him?”
paragraphs.cn: 你用它换什么？

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know.
paragraphs.cn: 我不知道。

paragraphs.en: I don’t want to sell him.”
paragraphs.cn: 我不想卖掉它。

paragraphs.en: “All right.
paragraphs.cn: 好吧。

paragraphs.en: It’s a mighty small tick, anyway.”
paragraphs.cn: 反正它只是一只很小的蜱虫。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, anybody can run a tick down that don’t belong to them.
paragraphs.cn: 哦，谁都能抓到不属于自己的蜱虫。

paragraphs.en: I’m satisfied with it.
paragraphs.cn: 我对它很满意。

paragraphs.en: It’s a good enough tick for me.”
paragraphs.cn: 对我来说，它已经够好了。

paragraphs.en: “Sho, there’s ticks a plenty.
paragraphs.cn: 哼，蜱虫多的是呢。

paragraphs.en: I could have a thousand of ’em if I wanted to.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想要的话，能有一千只呢。

paragraphs.en: “Well, why don’t you?
paragraphs.cn: 那你为什么不弄呢？

paragraphs.en: Becuz you know mighty well you can’t.
paragraphs.cn: 因为你很清楚你做不到。

paragraphs.en: This is a pretty early tick, I reckon.
paragraphs.cn: 我猜，这是一只很早出现的蜱虫。

paragraphs.en: It’s the first one I’ve seen this year.”
paragraphs.cn: 这是我今年看到的第一只呢。

paragraphs.en: “Say, Huck—I’ll give you my tooth for him.”
paragraphs.cn: 哎，哈克——我把我的牙齿给你，来换它。

paragraphs.en: “Less see it.”
paragraphs.cn: 让我看看。

paragraphs.en: Tom got out a bit of paper and carefully unrolled it.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆拿出一张小纸片，然后小心翼翼地打开了它。

paragraphs.en: Huckleberry viewed it wistfully.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克伯里看着它，心里很想要。

paragraphs.en: The temptation was very strong.
paragraphs.cn: 他很想很想要。

paragraphs.en: At last he said:
paragraphs.cn: 他终于说：

paragraphs.en: “Is it genuwyne?”
paragraphs.cn: “这是真的吗？”

paragraphs.en: Tom lifted his lip and showed the vacancy.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 抬起嘴唇，露出牙齿的空隙。

paragraphs.en: “Well, all right,” said Huckleberry, “it’s a trade.”
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，”哈克伯里说，“我们换！”

paragraphs.en: Tom enclosed the tick in the percussion-cap box that had lately been the pinchbug’s prison, and the boys separated, each feeling wealthier than before.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 把小虫子放进小盒子里，这个盒子之前关过甲虫。两个男孩分开了，都觉得比以前更开心了。

paragraphs.en: When Tom reached the little isolated frame school-house, he strode in briskly, with the manner of one who had come with all honest speed.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 跑到小木头学校时，他快步走进去，好像自己一点也没迟到。

paragraphs.en: He hung his hat on a peg and flung himself into his seat with business-like alacrity.
paragraphs.cn: 他把帽子挂好，一下子就坐下了。

paragraphs.en: The master, throned on high in his great splint-bottom arm-chair, was dozing, lulled by the drowsy hum of study.
paragraphs.cn: 老师坐在大椅子上打瞌睡，被同学们小声读书的声音催眠了。

paragraphs.en: The interruption roused him.
paragraphs.cn: 他被吵醒了。

paragraphs.en: “Thomas Sawyer!”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆·索亚！”

paragraphs.en: Tom knew that when his name was pronounced in full, it meant trouble.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 知道，老师叫他全名，就是有麻烦了。

paragraphs.en: “Sir!”
“Come up here.
paragraphs.cn: “你过来。

paragraphs.en: Now, sir, why are you late again, as usual?”
paragraphs.cn: 现在，你为什么又迟到了，老是这样？”

paragraphs.en: Tom was about to take refuge in a lie, when he saw two long tails of yellow hair hanging down a back that he recognized by the electric sympathy of love; and by that form was _the only vacant place_ on the girls’ side of the school-house.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 正想撒谎，却看到一个他喜欢的女孩的背影，她长长的金发垂下来。在女生那边，_只有_她的旁边是空位。

paragraphs.en: He instantly said:
paragraphs.cn: 他马上说：

paragraphs.en: “_I stopped to talk with Huckleberry Finn!
paragraphs.cn: “_我停下来和 哈克贝利·费恩 说话了！_

paragraphs.en: The master’s pulse stood still, and he stared helplessly.
paragraphs.cn: 老师的心跳好像停了，他呆呆地看着。

paragraphs.en: The buzz of study ceased.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都不读书了。

paragraphs.en: The pupils wondered if this foolhardy boy had lost his mind.
paragraphs.cn: 同学们想，这个男孩是不是疯了？

paragraphs.en: The master said:
paragraphs.cn: 老师说：

paragraphs.en: “You—you did what?”
paragraphs.cn: “你——你做了什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Stopped to talk with Huckleberry Finn.”
paragraphs.cn: “停下来和 哈克贝利·费恩 说话了。”

paragraphs.en: There was no mistaking the words.
paragraphs.cn: 老师听得很清楚。

paragraphs.en: “Thomas Sawyer, this is the most astounding confession I have ever listened to.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆·索亚，这是我听过最最让人吃惊的话！

paragraphs.en: No mere ferule will answer for this offence.
paragraphs.cn: 只是打手心，可不够惩罚你这次的错误。

paragraphs.en: Take off your jacket.”
paragraphs.cn: 把你外套脱掉！”

paragraphs.en: The master’s arm performed until it was tired and the stock of switches notably diminished.
paragraphs.cn: 老师的手都打累了，小树枝也用完了。

paragraphs.en: Then the order followed:
paragraphs.cn: 接着，老师说：

paragraphs.en: “Now, sir, go and sit with the girls!
paragraphs.cn: “好了，孩子，去跟女孩子们坐一起吧！

paragraphs.en: And let this be a warning to you.”
paragraphs.cn: 记住这次教训哦。”

paragraphs.en: The titter that rippled around the room appeared to abash the boy, but in reality that result was caused rather more by his worshipful awe of his unknown idol and the dread pleasure that lay in his high good fortune.
paragraphs.cn: 房间里有小声的笑声，男孩好像很不好意思。其实他脸红，是因为能跟那个他喜欢的女孩坐在一起，心里又高兴又有点害怕。

paragraphs.en: He sat down upon the end of the pine bench and the girl hitched herself away from him with a toss of her head.
paragraphs.cn: 他坐在长凳的尽头，那个女孩把头一甩，挪开了身子，离他远一点。

paragraphs.en: Nudges and winks and whispers traversed the room, but Tom sat still, with his arms upon the long, low desk before him, and seemed to study his book.
paragraphs.cn: 房间里有人互相推推，眨眨眼，小声说话。但是汤姆坐得很稳，他把胳膊放在身前的矮桌上，好像在认真看书。

paragraphs.en: By and by attention ceased from him, and the accustomed school murmur rose upon the dull air once more.
paragraphs.cn: 慢慢地，大家不再注意他了，教室里又回到了以前那种吵吵闹闹的声音。

paragraphs.en: Presently the boy began to steal furtive glances at the girl.
paragraphs.cn: 没多久，男孩开始偷偷看那个女孩。

paragraphs.en: She observed it, “made a mouth” at him and gave him the back of her head for the space of a minute.
paragraphs.cn: 她发现了，就朝他做了个鬼脸，然后转过头去，背对着他，有一分钟那么久。

paragraphs.en: When she cautiously faced around again, a peach lay before her.
paragraphs.cn: 等她小心翼翼地转过身来，发现面前放着一个桃子。

paragraphs.en: She thrust it away.
paragraphs.cn: 她把桃子推开了。

paragraphs.en: Tom gently put it back.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆又轻轻地把它放了回去。

paragraphs.en: She thrust it away again, but with less animosity.
paragraphs.cn: 她又推开了一次，但这次没那么生气了。

paragraphs.en: Tom patiently returned it to its place.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆耐心地把它放回原位。

paragraphs.en: Then she let it remain.
paragraphs.cn: 这次她没再动。

paragraphs.en: Tom scrawled on his slate, “Please take it—I got more.”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆在石板上写道：“请收下吧——我还有很多。”

paragraphs.en: The girl glanced at the words, but made no sign.
paragraphs.cn: 女孩看了一眼那些字，但没有表示什么。

paragraphs.en: Now the boy began to draw something on the slate, hiding his work with his left hand.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，男孩开始在石板上画画，他用左手把画盖住。

paragraphs.en: For a time the girl refused to notice; but her human curiosity presently began to manifest itself by hardly perceptible signs.
paragraphs.cn: 一开始女孩假装没看见，但过了一会儿，她还是忍不住好奇，偷偷地看了起来。

paragraphs.en: The boy worked on, apparently unconscious.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩继续画画，假装没发现她在看。

paragraphs.en: The girl made a sort of non-committal attempt to see, but the boy did not betray that he was aware of it.
paragraphs.cn: 女孩又小心地想看一眼，但男孩没有露出他知道的表情。

paragraphs.en: At last she gave in and hesitatingly whispered:
paragraphs.cn: 最后，她放弃了，犹豫地小声说：

paragraphs.en: “Let me see it.”
paragraphs.cn: “给我看看。”

paragraphs.en: Tom partly uncovered a dismal caricature of a house with two gable ends to it and a corkscrew of smoke issuing from the chimney.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆掀开了一点，露出了一幅画。画的是一栋奇怪的房子，房顶尖尖的，烟囱里冒着卷起来的烟。

paragraphs.en: Then the girl’s interest began to fasten itself upon the work and she forgot everything else.
paragraphs.cn: 女孩对这幅画越来越感兴趣，忘了其他所有事。

paragraphs.en: When it was finished, she gazed a moment, then whispered:
paragraphs.cn: 画画完了，她看了一会儿，然后小声说：

paragraphs.en: “It’s nice—make a man.”
paragraphs.cn: “画得真好，画个人吧。”

paragraphs.en: The artist erected a man in the front yard, that resembled a derrick.
paragraphs.cn: 画家（男孩）在房子前面画了一个人，那个人长得像个高高的吊车。

paragraphs.en: He could have stepped over the house; but the girl was not hypercritical; she was satisfied with the monster, and whispered:
paragraphs.cn: 那个人高得都能跨过房子了！但女孩没挑剔，她很满意这个“怪物”，小声说：

paragraphs.en: “It’s a beautiful man—now make me coming along.”
paragraphs.cn: “真是个帅哥——现在让我跟着你一起去吧。”

paragraphs.en: Tom drew an hour-glass with a full moon and straw limbs to it and armed the spreading fingers with a portentous fan.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 画了一个沙漏，上面有圆圆的月亮和稻草做的手脚。他还给张开的手指画了一把很特别的扇子。

paragraphs.en: The girl said:
paragraphs.cn: 女孩说：

paragraphs.en: “It’s ever so nice—I wish I could draw.”
paragraphs.cn: “画得真好啊！我真希望我也会画画。”

paragraphs.en: “It’s easy,” whispered Tom, “I’ll learn you.”
paragraphs.cn: “这很容易的，”汤姆 小声说，“我来教你。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, will you?
paragraphs.cn: “哦，真的吗？

paragraphs.en: When?”
paragraphs.cn: 什么时候？”

paragraphs.en: “At noon.
paragraphs.cn: “中午的时候。

paragraphs.en: Do you go home to dinner?”
paragraphs.cn: 你回家吃午饭吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll stay if you will.”
paragraphs.cn: “如果你留下，我就留下。”

paragraphs.en: “Good—that’s a whack.
paragraphs.cn: “好啊——就这样说定了。

paragraphs.en: What’s your name?”
paragraphs.cn: 你叫什么名字？”

paragraphs.en: “Becky Thatcher.
paragraphs.cn: “贝琪·撒切尔。

paragraphs.en: What’s yours?
paragraphs.cn: 你呢？

paragraphs.en: Oh, I know.
paragraphs.cn: 哦，我知道了。

paragraphs.en: It’s Thomas Sawyer.”
paragraphs.cn: 你是托马斯·索亚。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s the name they lick me by.
paragraphs.cn: “我挨打的时候他们会叫那个名字。

paragraphs.en: I’m Tom when I’m good.
paragraphs.cn: 我乖的时候，他们叫我 汤姆。

paragraphs.en: You call me Tom, will you?”
paragraphs.cn: 你叫我 汤姆，好吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes.”
paragraphs.cn: “好啊。”

paragraphs.en: Now Tom began to scrawl something on the slate, hiding the words from the girl.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，汤姆 开始在石板上乱写乱画，不让女孩看到他写了什么。

paragraphs.en: But she was not backward this time.
paragraphs.cn: 但这次她没有退缩。

paragraphs.en: She begged to see.
paragraphs.cn: 她央求着想看。

paragraphs.en: Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 说：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, it ain’t anything.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，没什么的。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes it is.”
paragraphs.cn: “就是有呀！”

paragraphs.en: “No it ain’t.
paragraphs.cn: “不，真的没什么。

paragraphs.en: You don’t want to see.”
paragraphs.cn: 你不想看的。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes I do, indeed I do.
paragraphs.cn: “我想看，我真的想看。

paragraphs.en: Please let me.”
paragraphs.cn: 求求你让我看吧！”

paragraphs.en: “You’ll tell.”
paragraphs.cn: “你会说的。”

paragraphs.en: “No I won’t—deed and deed and double deed won’t.”
paragraphs.cn: “不，我不会说的——真的，真的，绝对不会说的。”

paragraphs.en: “You won’t tell anybody at all?
paragraphs.cn: “你真的不会告诉任何人吗？

paragraphs.en: Ever, as long as you live?”
paragraphs.cn: 一辈子都不会说吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No, I won’t ever tell _any_body.
paragraphs.cn: “不，我绝对不会告诉任何人的。

paragraphs.en: Now let me.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在让我看看。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, _you_ don’t want to see!”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，你才不想看呢！”

paragraphs.en: “Now that you treat me so, I _will_ see.”
paragraphs.cn: “既然你这样对我，我偏要看！”

paragraphs.en: And she put her small hand upon his and a little scuffle ensued, Tom pretending to resist in earnest but letting his hand slip by degrees till these words were revealed: “_I love you_.”
paragraphs.cn: 她把小手放在他手上，两人轻轻推搡起来，汤姆假装很认真地抵抗，但慢慢地让他的手溜走，直到看到这些字：“我爱你。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, you bad thing!”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，你这个小坏蛋！”

paragraphs.en: And she hit his hand a smart rap, but reddened and looked pleased, nevertheless.
paragraphs.cn: 她轻轻拍了一下他的手，脸红了，但看起来还是很高兴。

paragraphs.en: Just at this juncture the boy felt a slow, fateful grip closing on his ear, and a steady lifting impulse.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这时，男孩感到一只手慢慢地、牢牢地捏住了他的耳朵，并把他稳稳地提了起来。

paragraphs.en: In that wise he was borne across the house and deposited in his own seat, under a peppering fire of giggles from the whole school.
paragraphs.cn: 他就这样被提着穿过教室，放回了自己的座位上，全班同学都咯咯地笑个不停。

paragraphs.en: Then the master stood over him during a few awful moments, and finally moved away to his throne without saying a word.
paragraphs.cn: 老师在他身边站了几分钟，气氛很严肃，最后没说什么就走回了他的座位。

paragraphs.en: But although Tom’s ear tingled, his heart was jubilant.
paragraphs.cn: 虽然汤姆的耳朵火辣辣的，但他的心里却很高兴。

paragraphs.en: As the school quieted down Tom made an honest effort to study, but the turmoil within him was too great.
paragraphs.cn: 学校安静下来后，汤姆努力想学习，但他心里太激动了，静不下来。

paragraphs.en: In turn he took his place in the reading class and made a botch of it; then in the geography class and turned lakes into mountains, mountains into rivers, and rivers into continents, till chaos was come again; then in the spelling class, and got “turned down,” by a succession of mere baby words, till he brought up at the foot and yielded up the pewter medal which he had worn with ostentation for months.
paragraphs.cn: 轮到他读课文时，他读得一塌糊涂；然后上地理课时，他把湖泊说成山，把山说成河，把河说成大洲，真是乱七八糟；接着是拼写课，连一些非常简单的词都拼错了，结果他站到了队尾，还交出了他戴了几个月、一直很炫耀的锡奖章。

paragraphs.en: The harder Tom tried to fasten his mind on his book, the more his ideas wandered.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆越努力想把心思放在书本上，他的想法就越是跑来跑去。

paragraphs.en: So at last, with a sigh and a yawn, he gave it up.
paragraphs.cn: 所以最后，他叹了口气，打了个哈欠，放弃了。

paragraphs.en: It seemed to him that the noon recess would never come.
paragraphs.cn: 他觉得中午的休息时间永远不会来。

paragraphs.en: The air was utterly dead.
paragraphs.cn: 空气一点都不流动。

paragraphs.en: There was not a breath stirring.
paragraphs.cn: 一点风都没有。

paragraphs.en: It was the sleepiest of sleepy days.
paragraphs.cn: 这是最让人犯困的一天。

paragraphs.en: The drowsing murmur of the five and twenty studying scholars soothed the soul like the spell that is in the murmur of bees.
paragraphs.cn: 二十五个学生们学习时发出的嗡嗡声，就像蜜蜂的声音一样，让人觉得很舒服，想睡觉。

paragraphs.en: Away off in the flaming sunshine, Cardiff Hill lifted its soft green sides through a shimmering veil of heat, tinted with the purple of distance; a few birds floated on lazy wing high in the air; no other living thing was visible but some cows, and they were asleep.
paragraphs.cn: 远处，在烈日下，卡迪夫山在热浪中，泛着远处的紫色，露出了它柔软的绿色山坡；几只鸟儿懒洋洋地在高空中飞翔；除了几头正在睡觉的牛，看不到其他活物。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s heart ached to be free, or else to have something of interest to do to pass the dreary time.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆心里很渴望自由，或者能做点有趣的事来打发这无聊的时间。

paragraphs.en: His hand wandered into his pocket and his face lit up with a glow of gratitude that was prayer, though he did not know it.
paragraphs.cn: 他的手伸进了口袋，脸上露出了一丝感激的笑容，那就像在祈祷一样，虽然他自己并不知道。

paragraphs.en: Then furtively the percussion-cap box came out.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，他偷偷地拿出了那个火帽盒。

paragraphs.en: He released the tick and put him on the long flat desk.
paragraphs.cn: 他放出了那只蜱虫，把它放在长长的平桌上。

paragraphs.en: The creature probably glowed with a gratitude that amounted to prayer, too, at this moment, but it was premature: for when he started thankfully to travel off, Tom turned him aside with a pin and made him take a new direction.
paragraphs.cn: 这只小虫子此时可能也充满了感激，就像在祈祷一样，但这高兴得太早了：因为它刚想感激地走开，汤姆就用一根针把它拨到一边，让它换个方向走。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s bosom friend sat next him, suffering just as Tom had been, and now he was deeply and gratefully interested in this entertainment in an instant.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 的好朋友坐在他旁边，刚才也和 汤姆 一样不舒服。但很快，他一下子就被这个有趣的游戏吸引住了。

paragraphs.en: This bosom friend was Joe Harper.
paragraphs.cn: 这个好朋友就是 乔·哈珀。

paragraphs.en: The two boys were sworn friends all the week, and embattled enemies on Saturdays.
paragraphs.cn: 这两个小男孩，平时是一周的好朋友，可一到星期六就成了爱打闹的小敌人。

paragraphs.en: Joe took a pin out of his lapel and began to assist in exercising the prisoner.
paragraphs.cn: 乔从衣服上取下一枚别针，开始帮着逗弄那只小虫子。

paragraphs.en: The sport grew in interest momently.
paragraphs.cn: 这个游戏一下子变得更有趣了。

paragraphs.en: Soon Tom said that they were interfering with each other, and neither getting the fullest benefit of the tick.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，汤姆 说他们这样互相挤着，都没法好好玩那只小虫子。

paragraphs.en: So he put Joe’s slate on the desk and drew a line down the middle of it from top to bottom.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他把乔的小板子放到桌上，在板子中间从上到下画了一条线。

paragraphs.en: “Now,” said he, “as long as he is on your side you can stir him up and I’ll let him alone; but if you let him get away and get on my side, you’re to leave him alone as long as I can keep him from crossing over.”
paragraphs.cn: “听好了，”他说，“只要它在你这边，你就可以逗它，我不碰它；但如果你让它跑了，跑到我这边来，那我就要管它不让它跑过去。在这段时间里，你就不能碰它了。”

paragraphs.en: “All right, go ahead; start him up.”
paragraphs.cn: “好的，开始吧；去逗逗它！”

paragraphs.en: The tick escaped from Tom, presently, and crossed the equator.
paragraphs.cn: 那只小虫子很快就从汤姆那儿跑掉了，跑过了那条线。

paragraphs.en: Joe harassed him awhile, and then he got away and crossed back again.
paragraphs.cn: 乔逗了它一会儿，然后它又跑掉了，跑回了对面。

paragraphs.en: This change of base occurred often.
paragraphs.cn: 它就这样老是跑来跑去。

paragraphs.en: While one boy was worrying the tick with absorbing interest, the other would look on with interest as strong, the two heads bowed together over the slate, and the two souls dead to all things else.
paragraphs.cn: 一个男孩特别认真地逗着小虫子，另一个也一样认真地看着。两个小脑袋凑在一起，看着小板子，什么都忘了。

paragraphs.en: At last luck seemed to settle and abide with Joe.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，乔的运气好像越来越好。

paragraphs.en: The tick tried this, that, and the other course, and got as excited and as anxious as the boys themselves, but time and again just as he would have victory in his very grasp, so to speak, and Tom’s fingers would be twitching to begin, Joe’s pin would deftly head him off, and keep possession.
paragraphs.cn: 小虫子这边跑跑，那边跑跑，也像小男孩们一样，又激动又着急。每次眼看就要跑赢了，汤姆 的手指头都痒痒地想去碰它，乔的别针就会一下子把它挡回去，不让它跑掉。

paragraphs.en: At last Tom could stand it no longer.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，汤姆 再也忍不住了。

paragraphs.en: The temptation was too strong.
paragraphs.cn: 他太想去碰那只小虫子了。

paragraphs.en: So he reached out and lent a hand with his pin.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他伸出手，用自己的别针去帮了一下忙。

paragraphs.en: Joe was angry in a moment.
paragraphs.cn: 乔一下子就生气了。

paragraphs.en: Said he:
paragraphs.cn: 他说：

paragraphs.en: “Tom, you let him alone.”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，你别碰它！”

paragraphs.en: “I only just want to stir him up a little, Joe.”
paragraphs.cn: “乔，我只是想逗逗它嘛。”

paragraphs.en: “No, sir, it ain’t fair; you just let him alone.”
paragraphs.cn: “不行，这不公平；你别碰它！”

paragraphs.en: “Blame it, I ain’t going to stir him much.”
paragraphs.cn: “真是的，我又不会多碰它一下。”

paragraphs.en: “Let him alone, I tell you.”
paragraphs.cn: “我跟你说，你别碰它！”

paragraphs.en: “I won’t!”
paragraphs.cn: “我偏不！”

paragraphs.en: “You shall—he’s on my side of the line.”
paragraphs.cn: “你得！它在我这边呢！”

paragraphs.en: “Look here, Joe Harper, whose is that tick?”
paragraphs.cn: “喂，乔·哈珀，那只小虫子是谁的？”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t care whose tick he is—he’s on my side of the line, and you sha’n’t touch him.”
paragraphs.cn: “我才不管它是谁的呢——它在我这边，你不能碰它！”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’ll just bet I will, though.
paragraphs.cn: “哼，我偏要碰。”

paragraphs.en: He’s my tick and I’ll do what I blame please with him, or die!”
paragraphs.cn: “他是我的人，我想怎么对待他都行，不然我就去死！”

paragraphs.en: A tremendous whack came down on Tom’s shoulders, and its duplicate on Joe’s; and for the space of two minutes the dust continued to fly from the two jackets and the whole school to enjoy it.
paragraphs.cn: “一个重重的巴掌打在汤姆的肩膀上，乔的肩膀上也挨了一下；接下来两分钟里，两件衣服上的灰尘一直往外飞，全校同学都看得可开心了。”

paragraphs.en: The boys had been too absorbed to notice the hush that had stolen upon the school awhile before when the master came tiptoeing down the room and stood over them.
paragraphs.cn: “孩子们太专心了，没注意到之前学校里突然安静下来，因为老师踮着脚走到他们身边。”

paragraphs.en: He had contemplated a good part of the performance before he contributed his bit of variety to it.
paragraphs.cn: “他先看了好一会儿，才加入了自己的‘表演’。”

paragraphs.en: When school broke up at noon, Tom flew to Becky Thatcher, and whispered in her ear:
paragraphs.cn: “中午放学的时候，汤姆跑到贝琪·撒切尔身边，在她耳边悄悄说：”

paragraphs.en: “Put on your bonnet and let on you’re going home; and when you get to the corner, give the rest of ’em the slip, and turn down through the lane and come back.
paragraphs.cn: “‘戴上你的小帽子，假装要回家；等你走到拐角时，甩开他们，然后穿过小路回来。’”

paragraphs.en: I’ll go the other way and come it over ’em the same way.”
paragraphs.cn: “‘我走另一条路，也用同样的方法甩开他们。’”

paragraphs.en: So the one went off with one group of scholars, and the other with another.
paragraphs.cn: “于是，一个和一群同学走了，另一个和另一群同学走了。”

paragraphs.en: In a little while the two met at the bottom of the lane, and when they reached the school they had it all to themselves.
paragraphs.cn: “不一会儿，他俩在小路的尽头碰面了；等他们回到学校的时候，学校里就只有他们两个人了。”

paragraphs.en: Then they sat together, with a slate before them, and Tom gave Becky the pencil and held her hand in his, guiding it, and so created another surprising house.
paragraphs.cn: “然后他们坐在一起，面前放着一块写字板，汤姆把铅笔递给贝琪，牵着她的手教她画，就这样画出了一个令人惊喜的房子。”

paragraphs.en: When the interest in art began to wane, the two fell to talking.
paragraphs.cn: “当画画的兴趣渐渐没了，他俩就开始聊天。”

paragraphs.en: Tom was swimming in bliss.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆觉得幸福极了。”

paragraphs.en: He said:
paragraphs.cn: “他说：”

paragraphs.en: “Do you love rats?”
paragraphs.cn: “‘你喜欢老鼠吗？’”

paragraphs.en: “No!
I hate them!”
paragraphs.cn: “‘我讨厌它们！’”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I do, too—_live_ ones.
paragraphs.cn: “‘嗯，我也讨厌——活的。’”

paragraphs.en: But I mean dead ones, to swing round your head with a string.”
paragraphs.cn: “‘但我说的是死老鼠，可以用绳子拴着，在你头顶上甩来甩去的那种。’”

paragraphs.en: “No, I don’t care for rats much, anyway.
paragraphs.cn: “‘不，反正我不太喜欢老鼠。’”

paragraphs.en: What I like is chewing-gum.”
paragraphs.cn: “‘我喜欢的是口香糖。’”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I should say so!
paragraphs.cn: “‘噢，我也喜欢！’”

paragraphs.en: I wish I had some now.”
paragraphs.cn: “‘我现在真想有块啊。’”

paragraphs.en: “Do you?
I’ve got some.
paragraphs.cn: “‘我有一些。’”

paragraphs.en: I’ll let you chew it awhile, but you must give it back to me.”
paragraphs.cn: “‘我可以让你嚼一会儿，但你嚼完必须还给我。’”

paragraphs.en: That was agreeable, so they chewed it turn about, and dangled their legs against the bench in excess of contentment.
paragraphs.cn: “他们觉得这样很好，就轮流嚼着口香糖，开心得把腿悬在长凳外晃来晃去。”

paragraphs.en: “Was you ever at a circus?” said Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆说：‘你去过马戏团吗？’”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, and my pa’s going to take me again some time, if I’m good.”
paragraphs.cn: “‘去过，而且如果我乖的话，我爸爸还会再带我去。’”

paragraphs.en: “I been to the circus three or four times—lots of times.
paragraphs.cn: “‘我去过三四次马戏团了——去过好多次了。’”

paragraphs.en: Church ain’t shucks to a circus.
paragraphs.cn: “‘教堂跟马戏团比起来简直太没意思了。’”

paragraphs.en: There’s things going on at a circus all the time.
paragraphs.cn: 马戏团里总是有好多好玩的事情。

paragraphs.en: I’m going to be a clown in a circus when I grow up.”
paragraphs.cn: 我长大了要当马戏团的小丑。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, are you!
paragraphs.cn: “哦，是吗！

paragraphs.en: That will be nice.
paragraphs.cn: 那会很好玩。

paragraphs.en: They’re so lovely, all spotted up.”
paragraphs.cn: 它们真可爱，身上都有斑点。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, that’s so.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，就是那样。

paragraphs.en: And they get slathers of money—most a dollar a day, Ben Rogers says.
paragraphs.cn: 他们能赚好多钱呢——本·罗杰斯说，一天差不多能赚一美元。

paragraphs.en: Say, Becky, was you ever engaged?”
paragraphs.cn: 喂，贝琪，你订过婚吗？”

paragraphs.en: “What’s that?”
paragraphs.cn: “那是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, engaged to be married.”
paragraphs.cn: “就是，要结婚了的意思。”

paragraphs.en: “No.”
paragraphs.cn: “没有。”

paragraphs.en: “Would you like to?”
paragraphs.cn: “你想吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I reckon so.
paragraphs.cn: “我猜想会的。

paragraphs.en: I don’t know.
paragraphs.cn: 我不知道。

paragraphs.en: What is it like?”
paragraphs.cn: 那是什么样的呀？”

paragraphs.en: “Like?
paragraphs.cn: “什么样？

paragraphs.en: Why it ain’t like anything.
paragraphs.cn: 嗨，它不像任何东西。

paragraphs.en: You only just tell a boy you won’t ever have anybody but him, ever ever ever, and then you kiss and that’s all.
paragraphs.cn: 你只要告诉一个男生，你永远永远永远只要他，然后亲一下，就那样。

paragraphs.en: Anybody can do it.”
paragraphs.cn: 谁都能做到。”

paragraphs.en: “Kiss?
paragraphs.cn: “亲亲？

paragraphs.en: What do you kiss for?”
paragraphs.cn: 为什么要亲亲呀？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, that, you know, is to—well, they always do that.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，那个嘛，你知道，就是——嗯，他们总是那样做。”

paragraphs.en: “Everybody?”
paragraphs.cn: “所有人都会吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, yes, everybody that’s in love with each other.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，是的，所有互相喜欢的人都会。

paragraphs.en: Do you remember what I wrote on the slate?”
paragraphs.cn: 你记得我写在石板上的是什么吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Ye—yes.”
“What was it?”
paragraphs.cn: “那是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “I sha’n’t tell you.”
paragraphs.cn: “我不会告诉你。”

paragraphs.en: “Shall I tell _you_?”
paragraphs.cn: “要我告诉你吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Ye—yes—but some other time.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯——嗯——但是下次再说吧。”

paragraphs.en: “No, now.”
paragraphs.cn: “不，就现在。”

paragraphs.en: “No, not now—to-morrow.”
paragraphs.cn: “不，不是现在——是明天。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, no, _now_.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，不，就现在。

paragraphs.en: Please, Becky—I’ll whisper it, I’ll whisper it ever so easy.”
paragraphs.cn: 求你了，贝琪——我小声说，我轻轻地小声说。”

paragraphs.en: Becky hesitating, Tom took silence for consent, and passed his arm about her waist and whispered the tale ever so softly, with his mouth close to her ear.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪有点犹豫，汤姆就当她同意了，他搂着她的腰，嘴巴凑到她的耳朵边，轻轻地讲着这个故事。

paragraphs.en: And then he added:
paragraphs.cn: 然后他又说：

paragraphs.en: “Now you whisper it to me—just the same.”
paragraphs.cn: “现在你悄悄地跟我说——也这样说。”

paragraphs.en: She resisted, for a while, and then said:
paragraphs.cn: 她反抗了一会儿，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “You turn your face away so you can’t see, and then I will.
paragraphs.cn: “你把脸转过去，不许看，那样我就说。

paragraphs.en: But you mustn’t ever tell anybody—_will_ you, Tom?
paragraphs.cn: 但是你绝不能告诉任何人——好不好啊，汤姆？

paragraphs.en: Now you won’t, _will_ you?”
paragraphs.cn: 你肯定不会说，对不对？”

paragraphs.en: “No, indeed, indeed I won’t.
paragraphs.cn: “不，真的，我真的不会说。

paragraphs.en: Now, Becky.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在，贝琪。”

paragraphs.en: He turned his face away.
paragraphs.cn: 他把脸转过去了。

paragraphs.en: She bent timidly around till her breath stirred his curls and whispered, “I—love—you!”
paragraphs.cn: 她害羞地凑过去，直到她的气息吹动了他的卷发，她小声说：“我——爱——你！”

paragraphs.en: Then she sprang away and ran around and around the desks and benches, with Tom after her, and took refuge in a corner at last, with her little white apron to her face.
paragraphs.cn: 然后她跑开了，围着课桌和长凳跑了一圈又一圈，汤姆追在她后面。最后她躲在一个角落里，用她的小白围裙捂住了脸。

paragraphs.en: Tom clasped her about her neck and pleaded:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆搂着她的脖子，请求道：

paragraphs.en: “Now, Becky, it’s all done—all over but the kiss.
paragraphs.cn: “现在，贝琪，都说完了——就差亲亲了。

paragraphs.en: Don’t you be afraid of that—it ain’t anything at all.
paragraphs.cn: 你别害怕——一点儿都不可怕。

paragraphs.en: Please, Becky.”
paragraphs.cn: 求你了，贝琪。”

paragraphs.en: And he tugged at her apron and the hands.
paragraphs.cn: 他拉了拉她的围裙和手。

paragraphs.en: By and by she gave up, and let her hands drop; her face, all glowing with the struggle, came up and submitted.
paragraphs.cn: 渐渐地她放弃了，把手放了下来；她的脸因为挣扎而红扑扑的，抬了起来，不再反抗了。

paragraphs.en: Tom kissed the red lips and said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆亲了亲那红红的嘴唇，说：

paragraphs.en: “Now it’s all done, Becky.
paragraphs.cn: “现在都做好了，贝琪。

paragraphs.en: And always after this, you know, you ain’t ever to love anybody but me, and you ain’t ever to marry anybody but me, ever never and forever.
paragraphs.cn: 从今以后，你要知道，你只能爱我一个人，也只能嫁给我一个人，永远永远都是这样。

paragraphs.en: Will you?”
paragraphs.cn: 好吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No, I’ll never love anybody but you, Tom, and I’ll never marry anybody but you—and you ain’t to ever marry anybody but me, either.”
paragraphs.cn: “不，我只会爱你一个人，汤姆，也只会嫁给你一个人——你也不能和除了我以外的任何人结婚。”

paragraphs.en: “Certainly.
paragraphs.cn: “当然。

paragraphs.en: Of course.
paragraphs.cn: 那当然。

paragraphs.en: That’s _part_ of it.
paragraphs.cn: 这是其中一部分。”

paragraphs.en: And always coming to school or when we’re going home, you’re to walk with me, when there ain’t anybody looking—and you choose me and I choose you at parties, because that’s the way you do when you’re engaged.”
paragraphs.cn: 每次来学校或者回家，你都要和我一起走，当没人看着的时候。在聚会上，你选我，我选你，因为订婚的人都这样。

paragraphs.en: “It’s so nice.
paragraphs.cn: “真好。

paragraphs.en: I never heard of it before.”
paragraphs.cn: 我以前没听说过这个。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, it’s ever so gay!
paragraphs.cn: “哦，那可太开心了！

paragraphs.en: Why, me and Amy Lawrence—”
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，我和艾米·劳伦斯——”

paragraphs.en: The big eyes told Tom his blunder and he stopped, confused.
paragraphs.cn: 大眼睛让汤姆知道他犯错了，他停了下来，有点懵。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Tom!
paragraphs.cn: “哦，汤姆！

paragraphs.en: Then I ain’t the first you’ve ever been engaged to!”
paragraphs.cn: 那我不是第一个跟你订婚的人了！”

paragraphs.en: The child began to cry.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子开始哭了。

paragraphs.en: Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, don’t cry, Becky, I don’t care for her any more.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，别哭，贝琪，我不再喜欢她了。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, you do, Tom—you know you do.”
paragraphs.cn: “才不是呢，汤姆——你知道你还喜欢她的。”

paragraphs.en: Tom tried to put his arm about her neck, but she pushed him away and turned her face to the wall, and went on crying.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆想抱她的脖子，但她推开他，脸对着墙，继续哭。

paragraphs.en: Tom tried again, with soothing words in his mouth, and was repulsed again.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆又试了一次，嘴里说着好听的话，但又被她推开了。

paragraphs.en: Then his pride was up, and he strode away and went outside.
paragraphs.cn: 他觉得有点生气了，就大步走开，出去了。

paragraphs.en: He stood about, restless and uneasy, for a while, glancing at the door, every now and then, hoping she would repent and come to find him.
paragraphs.cn: 他在外面站着，一会儿看看门，心里很不舒服，希望她能后悔出来找他。

paragraphs.en: But she did not.
paragraphs.cn: 但她没有。

paragraphs.en: Then he began to feel badly and fear that he was in the wrong.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他开始觉得难过，害怕自己做错了。
