paragraphs.en: It was a hard struggle with him to make new advances, now, but he nerved himself to it and entered.
paragraphs.cn: 他很挣扎，不知道该不该再过去，但他鼓起勇气，走了进去。

paragraphs.en: She was still standing back there in the corner, sobbing, with her face to the wall.
paragraphs.cn: 她还在角落里，脸对着墙，小声哭着。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s heart smote him.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆心里很难过。

paragraphs.en: He went to her and stood a moment, not knowing exactly how to proceed.
paragraphs.cn: 他走到她身边，站了一会儿，不知道该怎么办。

paragraphs.en: Then he said hesitatingly:
paragraphs.cn: 然后他有点犹豫地说：

paragraphs.en: “Becky, I—I don’t care for anybody but you.”
paragraphs.cn: “贝琪，我——我只喜欢你一个人。”

paragraphs.en: No reply—but sobs.
paragraphs.cn: 没有回答——只有抽泣声。

paragraphs.en: “Becky”—pleadingly.
paragraphs.cn: “贝琪”——他央求道。

paragraphs.en: “Becky, won’t you say something?”
paragraphs.cn: “贝琪，你能不能说句话？”

paragraphs.en: More sobs.
paragraphs.cn: 又是一阵抽泣声。

paragraphs.en: Tom got out his chiefest jewel, a brass knob from the top of an andiron, and passed it around her so that she could see it, and said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆拿出他最宝贝的东西，是一个壁炉架上的铜把手。他把它在她面前晃了晃，让她能看到，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “Please, Becky, won’t you take it?”
paragraphs.cn: “求你了，贝琪，你收下好不好？”

paragraphs.en: She struck it to the floor.
paragraphs.cn: 她把它摔到地上。

paragraphs.en: Then Tom marched out of the house and over the hills and far away, to return to school no more that day.
paragraphs.cn: 然后，汤姆 走出家门，翻过山，走得很远，那天再也不回学校了。

paragraphs.en: Presently Becky began to suspect.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，贝琪 开始觉得不对劲。

paragraphs.en: She ran to the door; he was not in sight; she flew around to the play-yard; he was not there.
paragraphs.cn: 她跑到门口，没看见他；她又跑去院子，他也不在那儿。

paragraphs.en: Then she called:
paragraphs.cn: 然后她喊道：

paragraphs.en: “Tom!
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆！

paragraphs.en: Come back, Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: 回来，汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: She listened intently, but there was no answer.
paragraphs.cn: 她仔细听着，但是没有回应。

paragraphs.en: She had no companions but silence and loneliness.
paragraphs.cn: 只有安静和孤单陪着她。

paragraphs.en: So she sat down to cry again and upbraid herself; and by this time the scholars began to gather again, and she had to hide her griefs and still her broken heart and take up the cross of a long, dreary, aching afternoon, with none among the strangers about her to exchange sorrows with.
paragraphs.cn: 她又坐下来哭了，还怪自己。这时，同学们又开始聚过来了，她只好藏起难过，假装不伤心。漫长又难过的下午，身边一个能分担的人都没有。

paragraphs.en: Tom dodged hither and thither through lanes until he was well out of the track of returning scholars, and then fell into a moody jog.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 在小路上东躲西藏，直到远离了回家的同学，然后闷闷不乐地小跑起来。

paragraphs.en: He crossed a small “branch” two or three times, because of a prevailing juvenile superstition that to cross water baffled pursuit.
paragraphs.cn: 他过了一条小溪两三次，因为小朋友们都觉得，只要过了水，别人就追不到了。

paragraphs.en: Half an hour later he was disappearing behind the Douglas mansion on the summit of Cardiff Hill, and the school-house was hardly distinguishable away off in the valley behind him.
paragraphs.cn: 半小时后，他消失在卡迪夫山山顶上的道格拉斯大房子后面。学校在他身后的山谷里，几乎都看不见了。

paragraphs.en: He entered a dense wood, picked his pathless way to the centre of it, and sat down on a mossy spot under a spreading oak.
paragraphs.cn: 他走进一片茂密的森林，在没有路的地方走到了森林中间，坐在一棵大橡树下长满苔藓的地方。

paragraphs.en: There was not even a zephyr stirring; the dead noonday heat had even stilled the songs of the birds; nature lay in a trance that was broken by no sound but the occasional far-off hammering of a wood-pecker, and this seemed to render the pervading silence and sense of loneliness the more profound.
paragraphs.cn: 一点风都没有。中午热得要命，连鸟都不唱歌了。整个大自然像睡着了一样，只有远处偶尔传来啄木鸟的声音。这让周围更安静，他感到更孤单了。

paragraphs.en: The boy’s soul was steeped in melancholy; his feelings were in happy accord with his surroundings.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩心里很忧伤，他的心情和周围的环境一样。

paragraphs.en: He sat long with his elbows on his knees and his chin in his hands, meditating.
paragraphs.cn: 他坐了很久，胳膊肘放在膝盖上，下巴托在手里，想着事情。

paragraphs.en: It seemed to him that life was but a trouble, at best, and he more than half envied Jimmy Hodges, so lately released; it must be very peaceful, he thought, to lie and slumber and dream forever and ever, with the wind whispering through the trees and caressing the grass and the flowers over the grave, and nothing to bother and grieve about, ever any more.
paragraphs.cn: 他觉得生活太麻烦了。他有点羡慕刚去世的吉米·霍奇斯。他想，永远躺着睡觉、做梦，一定很平静。风在树林里轻声吹过，轻轻抚摸着坟墓上的草和花，再也没有什么可烦恼和伤心的了。

paragraphs.en: If he only had a clean Sunday-school record he could be willing to go, and be done with it all.
paragraphs.cn: 要是他有一个清白的主日学校记录，他就能安心地走了，把这一切都结束掉。

paragraphs.en: Now as to this girl.
paragraphs.cn: 现在说说这个女孩。

paragraphs.en: What had he done?
paragraphs.cn: 他做了什么呢？

paragraphs.en: Nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 什么也没做。

paragraphs.en: He had meant the best in the world, and been treated like a dog—like a very dog.
paragraphs.cn: 他本来是好心好意，却像狗一样被对待。

paragraphs.en: She would be sorry some day—maybe when it was too late.
paragraphs.cn: 总有一天她会后悔的——也许到时候就太晚了。

paragraphs.en: Ah, if he could only die _temporarily_!
paragraphs.cn: 哎，要是他能暂时死掉就好了！

paragraphs.en: But the elastic heart of youth cannot be compressed into one constrained shape long at a time.
paragraphs.cn: 但是年轻人的心是很有弹性的，不会被一种情绪一直压着。

paragraphs.en: Tom presently began to drift insensibly back into the concerns of this life again.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，汤姆 又不知不觉地开始关心起生活里的事情了。

paragraphs.en: What if he turned his back, now, and disappeared mysteriously?
paragraphs.cn: 要是他现在转身，神秘地消失了呢？

paragraphs.en: What if he went away—ever so far away, into unknown countries beyond the seas—and never came back any more!
paragraphs.cn: 要是他走了——走得很远很远，去大海那边陌生的国家——再也不回来了呢！

paragraphs.en: How would she feel then!
paragraphs.cn: 那时她会怎么想呢！

paragraphs.en: The idea of being a clown recurred to him now, only to fill him with disgust.
paragraphs.cn: 他又想到当小丑，这让他觉得很恶心。

paragraphs.en: For frivolity and jokes and spotted tights were an offense, when they intruded themselves upon a spirit that was exalted into the vague august realm of the romantic.
paragraphs.cn: 因为那些好玩的事、笑话和带斑点的紧身衣，让他很不高兴，他心里正在想很厉害、很浪漫的事。

paragraphs.en: No, he would be a soldier, and return after long years, all war-worn and illustrious.
paragraphs.cn: 不，他要当个士兵，很多年后回来，又勇敢又有名。

paragraphs.en: No—better still, he would join the Indians, and hunt buffaloes and go on the warpath in the mountain ranges and the trackless great plains of the Far West, and away in the future come back a great chief, bristling with feathers, hideous with paint, and prance into Sunday-school, some drowsy summer morning, with a blood-curdling war-whoop, and sear the eyeballs of all his companions with unappeasable envy.
paragraphs.cn: 不——更好的是，他要加入印第安人，打野牛，在远西的山里和没路的大平原上打仗。以后他会变成一个戴着羽毛、脸上画着可怕图案的大酋长回来，在一个困困的夏日早晨，带着可怕的战吼，得意洋洋地走进主日学校，让所有小伙伴都羡慕得不得了。

paragraphs.en: But no, there was something gaudier even than this.
paragraphs.cn: 但不对，还有比这更酷的！

paragraphs.en: He would be a pirate!
paragraphs.cn: 他要当海盗！

paragraphs.en: That was it!
paragraphs.cn: 对，就是这样！

paragraphs.en: _now_ his future lay plain before him, and glowing with unimaginable splendor.
paragraphs.cn: 现在他的未来就在眼前，闪着特别亮的光。

paragraphs.en: How his name would fill the world, and make people shudder!
paragraphs.cn: 他的名字会响遍世界，让人们害怕！

paragraphs.en: How gloriously he would go plowing the dancing seas, in his long, low, black-hulled racer, the Spirit of the Storm, with his grisly flag flying at the fore!
paragraphs.cn: 他会驾驶又长又矮的黑船“暴风之灵”，前面飘着他可怕的旗子，在波涛汹涌的海上航行，多威风啊！

paragraphs.en: And at the zenith of his fame, how he would suddenly appear at the old village and stalk into church, brown and weather-beaten, in his black velvet doublet and trunks, his great jack-boots, his crimson sash, his belt bristling with horse-pistols, his crime-rusted cutlass at his side, his slouch hat with waving plumes, his black flag unfurled, with the skull and crossbones on it, and hear with swelling ecstasy the whisperings, “It’s Tom Sawyer the Pirate!
paragraphs.cn: 在他最有名的时候，他会突然回到老村子，大步走进教堂！他晒得黑黑的，穿着黑色的天鹅绒上衣和短裤，大靴子，红腰带，腰带上插满了手枪，腰间挂着生锈的刀，头上戴着插羽毛的宽边帽，还展开他的黑旗，上面有骷髅和交叉骨。他会非常开心听到大家小声说：“是汤姆·索亚海盗！

paragraphs.en: —the Black Avenger of the Spanish Main!”
paragraphs.cn: ——西班牙海域的黑色复仇者！”

paragraphs.en: Yes, it was settled; his career was determined.
paragraphs.cn: 对，他决定好了；他的未来就是这样了。

paragraphs.en: He would run away from home and enter upon it.
paragraphs.cn: 他要离家出走，开始这个计划。

paragraphs.en: He would start the very next morning.
paragraphs.cn: 他明天一早就开始。

paragraphs.en: Therefore he must now begin to get ready.
paragraphs.cn: 所以他现在必须开始准备。

paragraphs.en: He would collect his resources together.
paragraphs.cn: 他要把他的东西都找出来。

paragraphs.en: He went to a rotten log near at hand and began to dig under one end of it with his Barlow knife.
paragraphs.cn: 他走到旁边一根烂木头那儿，用他的巴洛刀开始挖木头的一头。

paragraphs.en: He soon struck wood that sounded hollow.
paragraphs.cn: 他很快就挖到一个听起来是空的木头。

paragraphs.en: He put his hand there and uttered this incantation impressively:
paragraphs.cn: 他把手伸进去，庄重地念起咒语：

paragraphs.en: “What hasn’t come here, come!
paragraphs.cn: “没来到这里的，快来！

paragraphs.en: What’s here, stay here!”
paragraphs.cn: 在这里的，留下！”

paragraphs.en: Then he scraped away the dirt, and exposed a pine shingle.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他把土刮掉，露出一块松木瓦片。

paragraphs.en: He took it up and disclosed a shapely little treasure-house whose bottom and sides were of shingles.
paragraphs.cn: 他拿起瓦片，露出了一个漂亮的小宝藏盒，盒子底和边都是用瓦片做的。

paragraphs.en: In it lay a marble.
paragraphs.cn: 里面躺着一颗弹珠。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s astonishment was boundless!
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆惊讶极了！

paragraphs.en: He scratched his head with a perplexed air, and said:
paragraphs.cn: 他很困惑地挠了挠头，说：

paragraphs.en: “Well, that beats anything!”
paragraphs.cn: “哇，这真是太奇怪了！”

paragraphs.en: Then he tossed the marble away pettishly, and stood cogitating.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他生气地把弹珠扔掉，站在那里想事情。

paragraphs.en: The truth was, that a superstition of his had failed, here, which he and all his comrades had always looked upon as infallible.
paragraphs.cn: 其实，他相信的一个迷信在这里没有灵验，他和他的小伙伴们一直都觉得这个迷信是从来不会错的。

paragraphs.en: If you buried a marble with certain necessary incantations, and left it alone a fortnight, and then opened the place with the incantation he had just used, you would find that all the marbles you had ever lost had gathered themselves together there, meantime, no matter how widely they had been separated.
paragraphs.cn: 如果你把一颗弹珠埋起来，念一些魔法咒语，然后放上两个星期。当你再念咒语打开时，你所有弄丢的弹珠都会跑到那里去，不管它们之前分得有多远。

paragraphs.en: But now, this thing had actually and unquestionably failed.
paragraphs.cn: 可是现在，这个办法真的不管用了。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s whole structure of faith was shaken to its foundations.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆一下子什么都不信了。

paragraphs.en: He had many a time heard of this thing succeeding but never of its failing before.
paragraphs.cn: 他听过很多次这个办法成功了，可从来没听说过它会失败。

paragraphs.en: It did not occur to him that he had tried it several times before, himself, but could never find the hiding-places afterward.
paragraphs.cn: 他没有想起来，自己以前也试过好几次，可后来怎么也找不到藏弹珠的地方了。

paragraphs.en: He puzzled over the matter some time, and finally decided that some witch had interfered and broken the charm.
paragraphs.cn: 他想了半天，最后觉得一定是有个巫婆来捣乱，把魔法弄坏了。

paragraphs.en: He thought he would satisfy himself on that point; so he searched around till he found a small sandy spot with a little funnel-shaped depression in it.
paragraphs.cn: 他想弄清楚是不是这样，于是四处寻找，直到找到一小块沙地，上面有一个小小的漏斗形坑洞。

paragraphs.en: He laid himself down and put his mouth close to this depression and called—
paragraphs.cn: 他趴下来，嘴巴凑到这个小坑旁边，大声喊——

paragraphs.en: “Doodle-bug, doodle-bug, tell me what I want to know!
paragraphs.cn: “嘟嘟虫，嘟嘟虫，快告诉我我想知道的事！

paragraphs.en: Doodle-bug, doodle-bug, tell me what I want to know!”
paragraphs.cn: 嘟嘟虫，嘟嘟虫，快告诉我我想知道的事！”

paragraphs.en: The sand began to work, and presently a small black bug appeared for a second and then darted under again in a fright.
paragraphs.cn: 沙子动了起来，不一会儿，一只小黑虫子露了个头，然后吓得赶紧又钻了回去。

paragraphs.en: “He dasn’t tell!
paragraphs.cn: “它不敢说！

paragraphs.en: So it _was_ a witch that done it.
paragraphs.cn: 果然是巫婆搞的鬼。

paragraphs.en: I just knowed it.”
paragraphs.cn: 我就知道！”

paragraphs.en: He well knew the futility of trying to contend against witches, so he gave up discouraged.
paragraphs.cn: 他知道跟巫婆作对是没用的，所以很泄气，放弃了。

paragraphs.en: But it occurred to him that he might as well have the marble he had just thrown away, and therefore he went and made a patient search for it.
paragraphs.cn: 可是他突然想到，不如把自己刚刚扔掉的那颗弹珠找回来。于是他过去，很有耐心地找了起来。

paragraphs.en: But he could not find it.
paragraphs.cn: 可是他没有找到。

paragraphs.en: Now he went back to his treasure-house and carefully placed himself just as he had been standing when he tossed the marble away; then he took another marble from his pocket and tossed it in the same way, saying:
paragraphs.cn: 于是他回到那个“藏宝地”，小心地站好，就像刚才扔弹珠的时候一样。然后他从口袋里掏出另一颗弹珠，也用同样的方法扔了出去，嘴里还念着：

paragraphs.en: “Brother, go find your brother!”
paragraphs.cn: “兄弟，快去找你的兄弟吧！”

paragraphs.en: He watched where it stopped, and went there and looked.
paragraphs.cn: 他看着弹珠停在哪里，然后走过去看。

paragraphs.en: But it must have fallen short or gone too far; so he tried twice more.
paragraphs.cn: 可是弹珠不是扔近了就是扔远了；于是他又试了两次。

paragraphs.en: The last repetition was successful.
paragraphs.cn: 最后一次，他成功了。

paragraphs.en: The two marbles lay within a foot of each other.
paragraphs.cn: 两颗弹珠躺在一起，离得很近。

paragraphs.en: Just here the blast of a toy tin trumpet came faintly down the green aisles of the forest.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这时，森林里绿色的林间小道上传来一阵微弱的玩具锡喇叭声。

paragraphs.en: Tom flung off his jacket and trousers, turned a suspender into a belt, raked away some brush behind the rotten log, disclosing a rude bow and arrow, a lath sword and a tin trumpet, and in a moment had seized these things and bounded away, barelegged, with fluttering shirt.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆脱掉夹克和裤子，把背带当腰带系上。他扒开烂木头后面的草丛，里面藏着一把粗糙的弓箭、一把木板剑和一个锡喇叭。他飞快地抓起这些东西，光着腿，衬衫随风飘舞，跑走了。

paragraphs.en: He presently halted under a great elm, blew an answering blast, and then began to tiptoe and look warily out, this way and that.
paragraphs.cn: 他很快在一棵大榆树下停了下来，也吹了一声喇叭来回应。接着他踮着脚，小心翼翼地向四周张望。

paragraphs.en: He said cautiously—to an imaginary company:
paragraphs.cn: 他小心地对想象中的同伴们说：

paragraphs.en: “Hold, my merry men!
paragraphs.cn: “停下，我的伙伴们！

paragraphs.en: Keep hid till I blow.”
paragraphs.cn: 藏好，等我吹号角。”

paragraphs.en: Now appeared Joe Harper, as airily clad and elaborately armed as Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，乔·哈珀也出现了，他穿得轻便，武器也准备得很齐全，就像汤姆一样。

paragraphs.en: Tom called:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 喊道：

paragraphs.en: “Hold!
paragraphs.cn: “站住！

paragraphs.en: Who comes here into Sherwood Forest without my pass?”
paragraphs.cn: 谁没我的通行证就跑到谢伍德森林来了？”

paragraphs.en: “Guy of Guisborne wants no man’s pass.
paragraphs.cn: “吉斯伯恩的盖伊才不需要谁的通行证呢。

paragraphs.en: Who art thou that—that—”
paragraphs.cn: 你是谁，竟敢——竟敢——”

paragraphs.en: “Dares to hold such language,” said Tom, prompting—for they talked “by the book,” from memory.
paragraphs.cn: “竟敢说这样的话，”汤姆 提示道——他们可是“照着书”背台词呢。

paragraphs.en: “Who art thou that dares to hold such language?”
paragraphs.cn: “你是谁，竟敢说这样的话？”

paragraphs.en: “I, indeed!
paragraphs.cn: “就是我！

paragraphs.en: I am Robin Hood, as thy caitiff carcase soon shall know.”
paragraphs.cn: 我就是罗宾汉，你这坏蛋很快就会知道的！”

paragraphs.en: “Then art thou indeed that famous outlaw?
paragraphs.cn: “那么你真是那个有名的强盗吗？

paragraphs.en: Right gladly will I dispute with thee the passes of the merry wood.
paragraphs.cn: 我非常乐意在这片快乐树林和你比试一番。

paragraphs.en: Have at thee!”
paragraphs.cn: 放马过来！”

paragraphs.en: They took their lath swords, dumped their other traps on the ground, struck a fencing attitude, foot to foot, and began a grave, careful combat, “two up and two down.”
paragraphs.cn: 他们拿起木剑，把其他东西扔到地上，摆出击剑的架势，脚对脚，开始了一场认真又小心的打斗，一招一式“两上两下”。

paragraphs.en: Presently Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，汤姆 说道：

paragraphs.en: “Now, if you’ve got the hang, go it lively!”
paragraphs.cn: “好了，如果你学会了，那就打得再活泼点！”

paragraphs.en: So they “went it lively,” panting and perspiring with the work.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们“活泼地打起来”，打得气喘吁吁，满头大汗。

paragraphs.en: By and by Tom shouted:
paragraphs.cn: 不一会儿，汤姆 喊道：

paragraphs.en: “Fall! fall!
paragraphs.cn: “倒下！倒下！

paragraphs.en: Why don’t you fall?”
paragraphs.cn: 你怎么不倒下呀？”

paragraphs.en: “I sha’n’t!
paragraphs.cn: “我才不！

paragraphs.en: Why don’t you fall yourself?
paragraphs.cn: 你自己怎么不倒下呀？

paragraphs.en: You’re getting the worst of it.”
paragraphs.cn: 你才是快要输了呢。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, that ain’t anything.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，那不算什么。

paragraphs.en: I can’t fall; that ain’t the way it is in the book.
paragraphs.cn: 我不能倒下；书上不是那样写的。

paragraphs.en: The book says, ‘Then with one back-handed stroke he slew poor Guy of Guisborne.’
paragraphs.cn: 书上说，‘然后他反手一击，杀死了可怜的吉斯伯恩的盖伊。’

paragraphs.en: You’re to turn around and let me hit you in the back.”
paragraphs.cn: 你要转过身去，让我在你背后打你一下。”

paragraphs.en: There was no getting around the authorities, so Joe turned, received the whack and fell.
paragraphs.cn: 没办法，乔只好转过身，挨了一下，然后倒下了。

paragraphs.en: “Now,” said Joe, getting up, “you got to let me kill _you_.
paragraphs.cn: “现在，”乔站起来说，“你得让我杀死你。

paragraphs.en: That’s fair.”
paragraphs.cn: 这很公平。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, I can’t do that, it ain’t in the book.”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，我不能那样做，书上没有那样写。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, it’s blamed mean—that’s all.”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，这太坏了——就是这样。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, say, Joe, you can be Friar Tuck or Much the miller’s son, and lam me with a quarter-staff; or I’ll be the Sheriff of Nottingham and you be Robin Hood a little while and kill me.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，乔，你可以演塔克修士或磨坊主的儿子马奇，然后用棍子打我；或者我当诺丁汉的郡长，你当罗宾汉一会儿，把我杀死。”

paragraphs.en: This was satisfactory, and so these adventures were carried out.
paragraphs.cn: 这让他们很满意，于是他们玩起了这些冒险游戏。

paragraphs.en: Then Tom became Robin Hood again, and was allowed by the treacherous nun to bleed his strength away through his neglected wound.
paragraphs.cn: 后来汤姆又当了罗宾汉。那个坏心的修女让他流血不止，伤口一直没包扎，力气都没了。

paragraphs.en: And at last Joe, representing a whole tribe of weeping outlaws, dragged him sadly forth, gave his bow into his feeble hands, and Tom said, “Where this arrow falls, there bury poor Robin Hood under the greenwood tree.”
paragraphs.cn: 最后，乔扮成一群哭泣的绿林好汉，他难过地把汤姆拖出来，把弓放在他没力气的手里。汤姆说：“这支箭落在哪里，就把可怜的罗宾汉埋在哪里，就在绿树林下面。”

paragraphs.en: Then he shot the arrow and fell back and would have died, but he lit on a nettle and sprang up too gaily for a corpse.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他射出箭，倒了下去，本来会死的。但他碰到了荨麻，又很开心地跳起来，一点也不像个死人。

paragraphs.en: The boys dressed themselves, hid their accoutrements, and went off grieving that there were no outlaws any more, and wondering what modern civilization could claim to have done to compensate for their loss.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们穿好衣服，藏好玩的道具，然后伤心地走了。他们难过，因为再也没有绿林好汉了。他们想，现代社会有什么能比得上绿林好汉的乐趣呢？

paragraphs.en: They said they would rather be outlaws a year in Sherwood Forest than President of the United States forever.
paragraphs.cn: 他们说，他们宁愿在舍伍德森林里当一年的绿林好汉，也不想永远当美国的总统。

paragraphs.en: At half-past nine, that night, Tom and Sid were sent to bed, as usual.
paragraphs.cn: 那天晚上九点半，汤姆和希德像平时一样被送上床睡觉。

paragraphs.en: They said their prayers, and Sid was soon asleep.
paragraphs.cn: 他们做了祷告，希德很快就睡着了。

paragraphs.en: Tom lay awake and waited, in restless impatience.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆醒着躺在床上，又急又不安地等着。

paragraphs.en: When it seemed to him that it must be nearly daylight, he heard the clock strike ten!
paragraphs.cn: 他觉得天都快亮了，却听到钟敲了十下！

paragraphs.en: This was despair.
paragraphs.cn: 这让他很绝望。

paragraphs.en: He would have tossed and fidgeted, as his nerves demanded, but he was afraid he might wake Sid.
paragraphs.cn: 他本来想翻来覆去，动来动去，因为他很紧张。但他怕吵醒希德。

paragraphs.en: So he lay still, and stared up into the dark.
paragraphs.cn: 所以他一动不动地躺着，看着黑黑的天花板。

paragraphs.en: Everything was dismally still.
paragraphs.cn: 周围安静得可怕。

paragraphs.en: By and by, out of the stillness, little, scarcely perceptible noises began to emphasize themselves.
paragraphs.cn: 慢慢地，在这安静里，一些很小很小的声音开始变得能听见了。

paragraphs.en: The ticking of the clock began to bring itself into notice.
paragraphs.cn: 钟表滴答滴答的声音，也开始能听见了。

paragraphs.en: Old beams began to crack mysteriously.
paragraphs.cn: 老旧的横梁开始发出奇怪的吱呀声。

paragraphs.en: The stairs creaked faintly.
paragraphs.cn: 楼梯也轻轻地吱呀响。

paragraphs.en: Evidently spirits were abroad.
paragraphs.cn: 肯定有小精灵在外面。

paragraphs.en: A measured, muffled snore issued from Aunt Polly’s chamber.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈的房间里传来均匀又闷闷的打鼾声。

paragraphs.en: And now the tiresome chirping of a cricket that no human ingenuity could locate, began.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，一只蟋蟀又开始烦人地叫了，没有人能找到它在哪里。

paragraphs.en: Next the ghastly ticking of a death-watch in the wall at the bed’s head made Tom shudder—it meant that somebody’s days were numbered.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，床头墙壁里传来一种“报死虫”可怕的滴答声，让汤姆吓得发抖——这意味着有人快要死了。

paragraphs.en: Then the howl of a far-off dog rose on the night air, and was answered by a fainter howl from a remoter distance.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，远处传来一声狗叫，更远的地方又传来一声更小的狗叫回应。

paragraphs.en: Tom was in an agony.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆非常痛苦。

paragraphs.en: At last he was satisfied that time had ceased and eternity begun; he began to doze, in spite of himself; the clock chimed eleven, but he did not hear it.
paragraphs.cn: 最后他觉得时间停了，好像永远不会过去了。他忍不住开始打瞌睡。钟敲了十一点，但他没听到。

paragraphs.en: And then there came, mingling with his half-formed dreams, a most melancholy caterwauling.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，在他的半梦半醒中，传来一阵非常难过的猫叫声。

paragraphs.en: The raising of a neighboring window disturbed him.
paragraphs.cn: 旁边一扇窗户被打开，把他吵醒了。

paragraphs.en: A cry of “Scat! you devil!” and the crash of an empty bottle against the back of his aunt’s woodshed brought him wide awake, and a single minute later he was dressed and out of the window and creeping along the roof of the “ell” on all fours.
paragraphs.cn: 一声“滚开！你这坏蛋！”的喊叫，和一个空瓶子砸到他姨妈家柴房后面的声音，把他彻底吵醒了。只过了一分钟，他就穿好衣服，从窗户爬了出去，四肢着地沿着“L形”屋顶爬。

paragraphs.en: He “meow’d” with caution once or twice, as he went; then jumped to the roof of the woodshed and thence to the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 他边走边小心地“喵”了几声，然后跳上柴房顶，再跳到地上。

paragraphs.en: Huckleberry Finn was there, with his dead cat.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克贝利·费恩 也在那里，他带着他的死猫。

paragraphs.en: The boys moved off and disappeared in the gloom.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们走开了，消失在黑暗中。

paragraphs.en: At the end of half an hour they were wading through the tall grass of the graveyard.
paragraphs.cn: 半小时后，他们走进了墓地，穿过高高的草丛。

paragraphs.en: It was a graveyard of the old-fashioned Western kind.
paragraphs.cn: 那是一个老式的西方墓地。

paragraphs.en: It was on a hill, about a mile and a half from the village.
paragraphs.cn: 它在一个小山上，离村子大约一英里半远。

paragraphs.en: It had a crazy board fence around it, which leaned inward in places, and outward the rest of the time, but stood upright nowhere.
paragraphs.cn: 墓地周围有一圈摇摇晃晃的木板围栏，有的地方往里歪，有的地方往外歪，没有一处是直立的。

paragraphs.en: Grass and weeds grew rank over the whole cemetery.
paragraphs.cn: 整个墓地都长满了杂草。

paragraphs.en: All the old graves were sunken in, there was not a tombstone on the place; round-topped, worm-eaten boards staggered over the graves, leaning for support and finding none.
paragraphs.cn: 所有旧坟都塌陷了，那里没有一块墓碑；只有些圆顶的、被虫蛀的木板歪斜地立在坟头，它们想找个支撑，却什么也找不到。

paragraphs.en: “Sacred to the memory of” So-and-So had been painted on them once, but it could no longer have been read, on the most of them, now, even if there had been light.
paragraphs.cn: 以前上面写着“纪念某某某”，但现在大部分都看不清了，就算有光也看不清。

paragraphs.en: A faint wind moaned through the trees, and Tom feared it might be the spirits of the dead, complaining at being disturbed.
paragraphs.cn: 一阵微风在树林里呜咽，汤姆 害怕那是死者的魂魄在抱怨他们被打扰了。

paragraphs.en: The boys talked little, and only under their breath, for the time and the place and the pervading solemnity and silence oppressed their spirits.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们很少说话，只是低声细语，因为时间和地点，还有周围庄严的寂静，都让他们觉得很压抑。

paragraphs.en: They found the sharp new heap they were seeking, and ensconced themselves within the protection of three great elms that grew in a bunch within a few feet of the grave.
paragraphs.cn: 他们找到了要找的新坟堆，然后躲进了离坟几英尺远的三棵大榆树的下面。

paragraphs.en: Then they waited in silence for what seemed a long time.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他们安静地等着，好像过了很久。

paragraphs.en: The hooting of a distant owl was all the sound that troubled the dead stillness.
paragraphs.cn: 只有远处猫头鹰的叫声，打破了这死一般的寂静。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s reflections grew oppressive.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 心里的想法让他觉得很难受。

paragraphs.en: He must force some talk.
paragraphs.cn: 他必须说点什么。

paragraphs.en: So he said in a whisper:
paragraphs.cn: 于是他小声说：

paragraphs.en: “Hucky, do you believe the dead people like it for us to be here?”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，你觉得死人喜欢我们来这里吗？”

paragraphs.en: Huckleberry whispered:
paragraphs.cn: 哈克贝利小声说：

paragraphs.en: “I wisht I knowed.
paragraphs.cn: “我希望我知道。

paragraphs.en: It’s awful solemn like, _ain’t_ it?”
paragraphs.cn: 感觉好严肃啊，是不是？”

paragraphs.en: “I bet it is.”
paragraphs.cn: “我打赌是的。”

paragraphs.en: There was a considerable pause, while the boys canvassed this matter inwardly.
paragraphs.cn: 他们沉默了一会儿，男孩们在心里琢磨这件事。

paragraphs.en: Then Tom whispered:
paragraphs.cn: 接着 汤姆 小声说：

paragraphs.en: “Say, Hucky—do you reckon Hoss Williams hears us talking?”
paragraphs.cn: “嘿，哈克——你觉得霍斯·威廉姆斯听得到我们说话吗？”

paragraphs.en: “O’ course he does.
paragraphs.cn: “他当然听得到。

paragraphs.en: Least his sperrit does.”
paragraphs.cn: 至少他的魂魄听得到。”

paragraphs.en: Tom, after a pause:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 停顿了一下，说：

paragraphs.en: “I wish I’d said Mister Williams.
paragraphs.cn: “我真希望我说了威廉姆斯先生。”

paragraphs.en: But I never meant any harm.
paragraphs.cn: 我可没想害人。

paragraphs.en: Everybody calls him Hoss.”
paragraphs.cn: 大家都叫他霍斯。”

paragraphs.en: “A body can’t be too partic’lar how they talk ’bout these-yer dead people, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “说这些死掉的人，可不能太不小心了，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: This was a damper, and conversation died again.
paragraphs.cn: 这事让人扫兴，大家又没话说了。

paragraphs.en: Presently Tom seized his comrade’s arm and said:
paragraphs.cn: 没多久，汤姆抓住他朋友的胳膊说：

paragraphs.en: “Sh!”
“What is it, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: “怎么了，汤姆？”

paragraphs.en: And the two clung together with beating hearts.
paragraphs.cn: 两人心怦怦跳着，紧紧靠在一起。

paragraphs.en: “Sh!
There ’tis again!
paragraphs.cn: 又来了！

paragraphs.en: Didn’t you hear it?”
paragraphs.cn: 你没听到吗？”

paragraphs.en: “There!
Now you hear it.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在你听到了吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Lord, Tom, they’re coming!
paragraphs.cn: “天哪，汤姆，他们来了！

paragraphs.en: They’re coming, sure.
paragraphs.cn: 他们真的来了。

paragraphs.en: What’ll we do?”
paragraphs.cn: 我们该怎么办？”

paragraphs.en: “I dono.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道。

paragraphs.en: Think they’ll see us?”
paragraphs.cn: 你觉得他们会看到我们吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Tom, they can see in the dark, same as cats.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，汤姆，他们能像猫一样在黑夜里看东西。

paragraphs.en: I wisht I hadn’t come.”
paragraphs.cn: 我真希望我没来。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, don’t be afeard.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，别害怕。

paragraphs.en: I don’t believe they’ll bother us.
paragraphs.cn: 我不相信他们会来烦我们。

paragraphs.en: We ain’t doing any harm.
paragraphs.cn: 我们没有做坏事。

paragraphs.en: If we keep perfectly still, maybe they won’t notice us at all.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果我们一动不动，他们也许根本不会发现我们。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll try to, Tom, but, Lord, I’m all of a shiver.”
paragraphs.cn: “我会尽量做到，汤姆，可是，天哪，我全身都在抖。”

paragraphs.en: “Listen!”
The boys bent their heads together and scarcely breathed.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们凑在一起，几乎屏住了呼吸。

paragraphs.en: A muffled sound of voices floated up from the far end of the graveyard.
paragraphs.cn: 模糊的声音从墓地的远处飘了过来。

paragraphs.en: “Look!
See there!” whispered Tom. “What is it?”
paragraphs.cn: “快看！” 汤姆 小声说。“那是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “It’s devil-fire.
paragraphs.cn: “那是鬼火。

paragraphs.en: Oh, Tom, this is awful.”
paragraphs.cn: 哦，汤姆，这太可怕了。”

paragraphs.en: Some vague figures approached through the gloom, swinging an old-fashioned tin lantern that freckled the ground with innumerable little spangles of light.
paragraphs.cn: 几个模糊的身影在黑暗中走过来，他们手里拿着一个旧灯笼，地上有好多小亮光。

paragraphs.en: Presently Huckleberry whispered with a shudder:
paragraphs.cn: 接着，哈克贝利哆嗦着小声说：

paragraphs.en: “It’s the devils sure enough.
paragraphs.cn: “真的是魔鬼。

paragraphs.en: Three of ’em!
paragraphs.cn: 有三个！

paragraphs.en: Lordy, Tom, we’re goners!
paragraphs.cn: 天哪，汤姆，我们死定了！

paragraphs.en: Can you pray?”
paragraphs.cn: 你会祈祷吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll try, but don’t you be afeard.
paragraphs.cn: “我试试看，但你别害怕。

paragraphs.en: They ain’t going to hurt us.
paragraphs.cn: 他们不会伤害我们的。

paragraphs.en: ‘Now I lay me down to sleep, I—’”
paragraphs.cn: “我现在要睡觉了，我——”

paragraphs.en: “Sh!”
“What is it, Huck?”
paragraphs.cn: “那是什么，哈克？”

paragraphs.en: “They’re _humans_!
paragraphs.cn: “他们是人！

paragraphs.en: One of ’em is, anyway.
paragraphs.cn: 至少有一个是。

paragraphs.en: One of ’em’s old Muff Potter’s voice.”
paragraphs.cn: 其中一个声音是老莫夫·波特的。”

paragraphs.en: “No—’tain’t so, is it?”
paragraphs.cn: “不——不是吧？”

paragraphs.en: “I bet I know it.
paragraphs.cn: “我敢打赌我知道。

paragraphs.en: Don’t you stir nor budge.
paragraphs.cn: 你别动，也别挪。

paragraphs.en: He ain’t sharp enough to notice us.
paragraphs.cn: 他不够机灵，不会发现我们。

paragraphs.en: Drunk, the same as usual, likely—blamed old rip!”
paragraphs.cn: 他可能又喝醉了，和以前一样——那个该死的老家伙！”

paragraphs.en: “All right, I’ll keep still.
paragraphs.cn: “好的，我安静待着。

paragraphs.en: Now they’re stuck.
paragraphs.cn: 现在他们不动了。

paragraphs.en: Can’t find it.
paragraphs.cn: 找不到。

paragraphs.en: Here they come again.
paragraphs.cn: 他们又来了。

paragraphs.en: Now they’re hot.
paragraphs.cn: 现在他们热了。

paragraphs.en: Cold again.
paragraphs.cn: 又冷了。

paragraphs.en: Hot again.
paragraphs.cn: 又热了。

paragraphs.en: Red hot!
paragraphs.cn: 烫手了！

paragraphs.en: They’re p’inted right, this time.
paragraphs.cn: 这次他们指对地方了。

paragraphs.en: Say, Huck, I know another o’ them voices; it’s Injun Joe.”
paragraphs.cn: 喂，哈克，我认出另一个声音了；是印第安·乔。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s so—that murderin’ half-breed!
paragraphs.cn: “是真的——那个杀人的混血儿！

paragraphs.en: I’d druther they was devils a dern sight.
paragraphs.cn: 我宁愿他们是魔鬼呢。

paragraphs.en: What kin they be up to?”
paragraphs.cn: 他们想干什么呢？”

paragraphs.en: The whisper died wholly out, now, for the three men had reached the grave and stood within a few feet of the boys’ hiding-place.
paragraphs.cn: 小声说话的声音完全消失了，因为那三个人已经走到坟墓边，离孩子们藏身的地方只有几步远了。

paragraphs.en: “Here it is,” said the third voice; and the owner of it held the lantern up and revealed the face of young Doctor Robinson.
paragraphs.cn: “在这儿呢，”第三个声音说；那个人把灯笼举起来，露出了年轻的罗宾逊医生。

paragraphs.en: Potter and Injun Joe were carrying a handbarrow with a rope and a couple of shovels on it.
paragraphs.cn: 波特和印第安·乔抬着一个手推车，上面有绳子和两把铁锹。

paragraphs.en: They cast down their load and began to open the grave.
paragraphs.cn: 他们放下东西，开始挖坟墓。

paragraphs.en: The doctor put the lantern at the head of the grave and came and sat down with his back against one of the elm trees.
paragraphs.cn: 医生把灯笼放在坟墓前面，然后走到一棵榆树旁，背靠着树坐了下来。

paragraphs.en: He was so close the boys could have touched him.
paragraphs.cn: 他离得那么近，孩子们都快能碰到他了。

paragraphs.en: “Hurry, men!” he said, in a low voice; “the moon might come out at any moment.”
paragraphs.cn: “快点，伙计们！”他小声说，“月亮随时都可能出来。”

paragraphs.en: They growled a response and went on digging.
paragraphs.cn: 他们哼了一声作为回应，继续挖土。

paragraphs.en: For some time there was no noise but the grating sound of the spades discharging their freight of mould and gravel.
paragraphs.cn: 有一阵子，除了铁锹刮着土石的声音，没有别的响动。

paragraphs.en: It was very monotonous.
paragraphs.cn: 真是太单调了。

paragraphs.en: Finally a spade struck upon the coffin with a dull woody accent, and within another minute or two the men had hoisted it out on the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 终于，一把铁锹砰地一声碰到了棺材，又过了一两分钟，人们就把棺材抬了出来，放在地上。

paragraphs.en: They pried off the lid with their shovels, got out the body and dumped it rudely on the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 他们用铁锹撬开棺材盖，把尸体抬出来，粗鲁地扔在地上。

paragraphs.en: The moon drifted from behind the clouds and exposed the pallid face.
paragraphs.cn: 月亮从云后面慢慢出来，照亮了那张苍白的脸。

paragraphs.en: The barrow was got ready and the corpse placed on it, covered with a blanket, and bound to its place with the rope.
paragraphs.cn: 手推车准备好了，尸体被放在上面，盖上毯子，然后用绳子绑好。

paragraphs.en: Potter took out a large spring-knife and cut off the dangling end of the rope and then said:
paragraphs.cn: 波特拿出一把大弹簧刀，割断了垂下来的绳子末端，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “Now the cussed thing’s ready, Sawbones, and you’ll just out with another five, or here she stays.”
paragraphs.cn: “现在这鬼东西准备好了，医生，你再拿出五块钱来，不然它就留在这儿了。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s the talk!” said Injun Joe.
paragraphs.cn: “说得好！”印第安·乔说。

paragraphs.en: “Look here, what does this mean?” said the doctor. “You required your pay in advance, and I’ve paid you.”
paragraphs.cn: “听着，这是什么意思？”医生说，“你要求提前付款，我已经付给你了。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, and you done more than that,” said Injun Joe, approaching the doctor, who was now standing.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，而且你做得更多，”印第安·乔说，他走近了医生，医生现在正站着。

paragraphs.en: “Five years ago you drove me away from your father’s kitchen one night, when I come to ask for something to eat, and you said I warn’t there for any good; and when I swore I’d get even with you if it took a hundred years, your father had me jailed for a vagrant.
paragraphs.cn: “五年前的一个晚上，我去找你父亲要吃的，你把我赶出了厨房，还说我没安好心；等我发誓说就算等一百年也要报复你的时候，你父亲就把我当作流浪汉抓去坐牢了。

paragraphs.en: Did you think I’d forget?
paragraphs.cn: 你以为我会忘记吗？

paragraphs.en: The Injun blood ain’t in me for nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 我可不是白白有印第安人的血统。

paragraphs.en: And now I’ve _got_ you, and you got to _settle_, you know!”
paragraphs.cn: “现在我抓住你了，你得给我个交代，你懂的！”

paragraphs.en: He was threatening the doctor, with his fist in his face, by this time.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，他把拳头伸到医生面前，威胁着他。

paragraphs.en: The doctor struck out suddenly and stretched the ruffian on the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 医生突然出手，一拳就把那个恶棍打倒在地。

paragraphs.en: Potter dropped his knife, and exclaimed:
paragraphs.cn: 波特的刀掉了，他大喊：

paragraphs.en: “Here, now, don’t you hit my pard!” and the next moment he had grappled with the doctor and the two were struggling with might and main, trampling the grass and tearing the ground with their heels.
paragraphs.cn: “喂，别打我的伙伴！” 接着，他一把抓住医生，两人就拼命打起来。他们踩坏了草地，脚后跟把泥土都踢了起来。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe sprang to his feet, his eyes flaming with passion, snatched up Potter’s knife, and went creeping, catlike and stooping, round and round about the combatants, seeking an opportunity.
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔跳起来，眼睛里冒着火。他拿起波特的刀，像猫一样弯着腰，悄悄地绕着打架的两个人转来转去，想找个机会。

paragraphs.en: All at once the doctor flung himself free, seized the heavy headboard of Williams’ grave and felled Potter to the earth with it—and in the same instant the half-breed saw his chance and drove the knife to the hilt in the young man’s breast.
paragraphs.cn: 突然，医生挣脱了，拿起威廉姆斯墓碑那块重重的石板，把波特打倒在地。就在那一刻，那个混血儿抓住了机会，把刀深深地刺进了那个年轻人的胸口。

paragraphs.en: He reeled and fell partly upon Potter, flooding him with his blood, and in the same moment the clouds blotted out the dreadful spectacle and the two frightened boys went speeding away in the dark.
paragraphs.cn: 他摇摇晃晃地倒下，一部分身子压在波特身上，血流了他一身。就在这时，乌云遮住了可怕的景象，两个吓坏了的男孩赶紧跑进了黑暗里。

paragraphs.en: Presently, when the moon emerged again, Injun Joe was standing over the two forms, contemplating them.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，月亮又出来了。印第安·乔站在那两具尸体旁边，看着它们。

paragraphs.en: The doctor murmured inarticulately, gave a long gasp or two and was still.
paragraphs.cn: 医生哼了几声，喘了几口气，就没动静了。

paragraphs.en: The half-breed muttered:
paragraphs.cn: 那个混血儿小声说：

paragraphs.en: “_That_ score is settled—damn you.”
paragraphs.cn: “这笔账算清了——去你的。”

paragraphs.en: Then he robbed the body.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他搜刮了那具尸体。

paragraphs.en: After which he put the fatal knife in Potter’s open right hand, and sat down on the dismantled coffin.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，他把那把要命的刀放在波特张开的右手里，然后坐在那个散架的棺材上。

paragraphs.en: Three—four—five minutes passed, and then Potter began to stir and moan.
paragraphs.cn: 三分钟、四分钟、五分钟过去了，然后波特开始动了动，还哼了几声。

paragraphs.en: His hand closed upon the knife; he raised it, glanced at it, and let it fall, with a shudder.
paragraphs.cn: 他的手抓住了刀；他把刀举起来，看了看，然后发抖着把刀扔了。

paragraphs.en: Then he sat up, pushing the body from him, and gazed at it, and then around him, confusedly.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他坐起来，把尸体推开，看着它，接着又迷迷糊糊地看了看周围。

paragraphs.en: His eyes met Joe’s.
paragraphs.cn: 他的眼睛碰到了乔的目光。

paragraphs.en: “Lord, how is this, Joe?” he said.
paragraphs.cn: “天哪，乔，这是怎么回事？”他问。

paragraphs.en: “It’s a dirty business,” said Joe, without moving.
paragraphs.cn: “这事儿太糟了，”乔没动，说。

paragraphs.en: “What did you do it for?”
paragraphs.cn: “你为什么要这么做？”

paragraphs.en: I never done it!”
paragraphs.cn: 我从来没做过！”

paragraphs.en: “Look here!
paragraphs.cn: “听着！

paragraphs.en: That kind of talk won’t wash.”
paragraphs.cn: 这种话可没人信。”

paragraphs.en: Potter trembled and grew white.
paragraphs.cn: 波特全身发抖，脸也白了。

paragraphs.en: “I thought I’d got sober.
paragraphs.cn: “我以为我清醒了。

paragraphs.en: I’d no business to drink to-night.
paragraphs.cn: 今晚我不该喝酒的。

paragraphs.en: But it’s in my head yet—worse’n when we started here.
paragraphs.cn: 但我的头还是晕晕的——比我们刚来的时候还糟。

paragraphs.en: I’m all in a muddle; can’t recollect anything of it, hardly.
paragraphs.cn: 我脑子里乱糟糟的；几乎什么也记不起来了。

paragraphs.en: Tell me, Joe—_honest_, now, old feller—did I do it?
paragraphs.cn: 乔，告诉我——说实话，老朋友——是我做的吗？

paragraphs.en: Joe, I never meant to—’pon my soul and honor, I never meant to, Joe.
paragraphs.cn: 乔，我不是故意的——我发誓，我真的不是故意的，乔。

paragraphs.en: Tell me how it was, Joe.
paragraphs.cn: 乔，告诉我到底是怎么回事。

paragraphs.en: Oh, it’s awful—and him so young and promising.”
paragraphs.cn: 哦，太惨了，他还那么年轻，多好的一个人啊。

paragraphs.en: “Why, you two was scuffling, and he fetched you one with the headboard and you fell flat; and then up you come, all reeling and staggering like, and snatched the knife and jammed it into him, just as he fetched you another awful clip—and here you’ve laid, as dead as a wedge til now.”
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，你们俩打架了。他用床头板打了你一下，你倒了。你又晃晃悠悠爬起来，拿起刀子捅了他。他正好又狠狠打了你一下。你就就像死了一样躺在这儿，到现在才醒。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I didn’t know what I was a-doing.
paragraphs.cn: 哦，我不知道我在做什么。

paragraphs.en: I wish I may die this minute if I did.
paragraphs.cn: 如果我知道，就让我现在死掉吧。

paragraphs.en: It was all on account of the whiskey and the excitement, I reckon.
paragraphs.cn: 我猜，都是因为喝了酒，太激动了。

paragraphs.en: I never used a weepon in my life before, Joe.
paragraphs.cn: 乔，我以前从来没用过武器。

paragraphs.en: I’ve fought, but never with weepons.
paragraphs.cn: 我打过架，但从没用过武器。

paragraphs.en: They’ll all say that.
paragraphs.cn: 他们都会那么说的。

paragraphs.en: Joe, don’t tell!
paragraphs.cn: 乔，别告诉别人！

paragraphs.en: Say you won’t tell, Joe—that’s a good feller.
paragraphs.cn: 乔，你说你不会说的，你是个好人。

paragraphs.en: I always liked you, Joe, and stood up for you, too.
paragraphs.cn: 乔，我一直都喜欢你，也一直帮着你。

paragraphs.en: Don’t you remember?
paragraphs.cn: 你不记得了吗？

paragraphs.en: You _won’t_ tell, _will_ you, Joe?”
paragraphs.cn: 乔，你不会说的，是吗？

paragraphs.en: And the poor creature dropped on his knees before the stolid murderer, and clasped his appealing hands.
paragraphs.cn: 这个可怜的人跪在那个冷酷的杀人犯面前，双手合十地恳求着。

paragraphs.en: “No, you’ve always been fair and square with me, Muff Potter, and I won’t go back on you.
paragraphs.cn: 不，你一直对我很好，莫夫·波特，我不会出卖你的。

paragraphs.en: There, now, that’s as fair as a man can say.”
paragraphs.cn: 好了，我能说的也就这些了。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Joe, you’re an angel.
paragraphs.cn: 哦，乔，你真是个天使。

paragraphs.en: I’ll bless you for this the longest day I live.”
paragraphs.cn: 我这辈子都会感谢你的。

paragraphs.en: And Potter began to cry.
paragraphs.cn: 然后波特开始哭了。

paragraphs.en: “Come, now, that’s enough of that.
paragraphs.cn: 好了，够了。

paragraphs.en: This ain’t any time for blubbering.
paragraphs.cn: 现在不是哭的时候。

paragraphs.en: You be off yonder way and I’ll go this.
paragraphs.cn: 你走那边，我走这边。

paragraphs.en: Move, now, and don’t leave any tracks behind you.”
paragraphs.cn: 快走吧，别留下脚印。

paragraphs.en: Potter started on a trot that quickly increased to a run.
paragraphs.cn: 波特开始小跑，接着就跑了起来。

paragraphs.en: The half-breed stood looking after him.
paragraphs.cn: 那个混血儿站在原地看着他。

paragraphs.en: He muttered:
paragraphs.cn: 他嘟囔着说：

paragraphs.en: “If he’s as much stunned with the lick and fuddled with the rum as he had the look of being, he won’t think of the knife till he’s gone so far he’ll be afraid to come back after it to such a place by himself—chicken-heart!”
paragraphs.cn: 要是他真像看着那样，被揍晕了，又喝醉了酒，就不会想到那把刀。等他跑远了，就不敢一个人回来拿刀了——真是个胆小鬼！

paragraphs.en: Two or three minutes later the murdered man, the blanketed corpse, the lidless coffin, and the open grave were under no inspection but the moon’s.
paragraphs.cn: 两三分钟后，那个死去的人，盖着毯子的尸体，没盖子的棺材，还有那个敞开的坟墓，就只有月亮看着了。

paragraphs.en: The stillness was complete again, too.
paragraphs.cn: 一切又变得完全安静了。

paragraphs.en: The two boys flew on and on, toward the village, speechless with horror.
paragraphs.cn: 两个男孩吓坏了，一句话也说不出来，一直朝着村子跑啊跑。

paragraphs.en: They glanced backward over their shoulders from time to time, apprehensively, as if they feared they might be followed.
paragraphs.cn: 他们时不时回头看，心里有点怕，好像有人跟着他们。

paragraphs.en: Every stump that started up in their path seemed a man and an enemy, and made them catch their breath; and as they sped by some outlying cottages that lay near the village, the barking of the aroused watch-dogs seemed to give wings to their feet.
paragraphs.cn: 路上每个树桩都像一个人、一个坏蛋，让他们吓得喘不过气。当他们跑过村子旁的小房子时，狗狗的叫声好像给他们插上了翅膀，跑得更快了。

paragraphs.en: “If we can only get to the old tannery before we break down!” whispered Tom, in short catches between breaths. “I can’t stand it much longer.”
paragraphs.cn: “要是我们能在撑不住之前，跑到那个旧皮革厂就好了！” 汤姆喘着气小声说，“我真的快撑不住了。”

paragraphs.en: Huckleberry’s hard pantings were his only reply, and the boys fixed their eyes on the goal of their hopes and bent to their work to win it.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克贝利只是拼命喘气，没有说话。孩子们盯着他们想去的地方，努力跑向那里。

paragraphs.en: They gained steadily on it, and at last, breast to breast, they burst through the open door and fell grateful and exhausted in the sheltering shadows beyond.
paragraphs.cn: 他们一点点靠近，最后，一起冲进敞开的门，又累又庆幸地倒在屋里的阴影里。

paragraphs.en: By and by their pulses slowed down, and Tom whispered:
paragraphs.cn: 慢慢地，他们的心跳慢了下来，汤姆小声说：

paragraphs.en: “Huckleberry, what do you reckon’ll come of this?”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克贝利，你觉得这件事会怎么样啊？”

paragraphs.en: “If Doctor Robinson dies, I reckon hanging’ll come of it.”
paragraphs.cn: “要是罗宾逊医生死了，我猜他们会把我们吊起来。”

paragraphs.en: “Do you though?”
paragraphs.cn: “真的吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, I _know_ it, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “当然是真的，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: Tom thought a while, then he said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆想了一会儿，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “Who’ll tell?
paragraphs.cn: “谁会去说呢？

paragraphs.en: We?”
paragraphs.cn: 我们吗？”

paragraphs.en: “What are you talking about?
paragraphs.cn: “你在说什么呀？

paragraphs.en: S’pose something happened and Injun Joe _didn’t_ hang?
paragraphs.cn: 要是万一 印第安·乔 没被吊死呢？

paragraphs.en: Why, he’d kill us some time or other, just as dead sure as we’re a laying here.”
paragraphs.cn: 那他迟早会杀了我们的，就像我们现在躺在这里一样确定。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s just what I was thinking to myself, Huck.”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，我刚才也是这么想的。”

paragraphs.en: “If anybody tells, let Muff Potter do it, if he’s fool enough.
paragraphs.cn: “要是有人要说，就让 莫夫·波特 去说吧，如果他那么傻的话。

paragraphs.en: He’s generally drunk enough.”
paragraphs.cn: 他一般都喝得醉醺醺的。”

paragraphs.en: Tom said nothing—went on thinking.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆没说话，继续想着。

paragraphs.en: Presently he whispered:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，他小声说：

paragraphs.en: “Huck, Muff Potter don’t know it.
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，莫夫·波特不知道这件事。

paragraphs.en: How can he tell?”
paragraphs.cn: 他怎么会说出去呢？”

paragraphs.en: “What’s the reason he don’t know it?”
paragraphs.cn: “他怎么会不知道呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Because he’d just got that whack when Injun Joe done it.
paragraphs.cn: “因为 印第安·乔 做这件事的时候，他刚被打了那一下。

paragraphs.en: D’you reckon he could see anything?
paragraphs.cn: 你觉得他能看到什么吗？

paragraphs.en: D’you reckon he knowed anything?”
paragraphs.cn: 你觉得他知道什么吗？”

paragraphs.en: “By hokey, that’s so, Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，是这样啊，汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: “And besides, look-a-here—maybe that whack done for _him_!”
paragraphs.cn: “而且你看——说不定那一打，把他给打死了呢！”

paragraphs.en: “No, ’taint likely, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “不，不可能的，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: He had liquor in him; I could see that; and besides, he always has.
paragraphs.cn: 他喝了酒，我看得出来。他一直都这样。

paragraphs.en: Well, when pap’s full, you might take and belt him over the head with a church and you couldn’t phase him.
paragraphs.cn: 爸爸喝醉了，你用教堂砸他头，他也不会有感觉。

paragraphs.en: He says so, his own self.
paragraphs.cn: 他自己就是这么说的。

paragraphs.en: So it’s the same with Muff Potter, of course.
paragraphs.cn: 那么对 莫夫·波特 来说，当然也是一样。

paragraphs.en: But if a man was dead sober, I reckon maybe that whack might fetch him; I dono.”
paragraphs.cn: 但如果一个人没喝酒，我猜那一打可能让他清醒过来。我不知道。”

paragraphs.en: After another reflective silence, Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 又安静了一会儿，汤姆 说：

paragraphs.en: “Hucky, you sure you can keep mum?”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，你确定能保守秘密吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, we _got_ to keep mum.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，我们_一定_要保守秘密。

paragraphs.en: You know that.
paragraphs.cn: 你知道的。

paragraphs.en: That Injun devil wouldn’t make any more of drownding us than a couple of cats, if we was to squeak ’bout this and they didn’t hang him.
paragraphs.cn: 如果我们把这事说出去，那个坏蛋没被抓，他就会像淹死两只猫一样，把我们淹死。

paragraphs.en: Now, look-a-here, Tom, less take and swear to one another—that’s what we got to do—swear to keep mum.”
paragraphs.cn: 喂，汤姆，我们互相发个誓吧。我们得这么做，发誓保守秘密。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m agreed.
paragraphs.cn: “我同意。

paragraphs.en: It’s the best thing.
paragraphs.cn: 这是最好的办法。

paragraphs.en: Would you just hold hands and swear that we—”
paragraphs.cn: 你能牵着手发誓说我们——”

paragraphs.en: “Oh no, that wouldn’t do for this.
paragraphs.cn: “哦不，这事不能这样。

paragraphs.en: That’s good enough for little rubbishy common things—specially with gals, cuz _they_ go back on you anyway, and blab if they get in a huff—but there orter be writing ’bout a big thing like this.
paragraphs.cn: 那只对小事有用，特别是对女孩子。她们总是说话不算数，一生气就说出去。但是像这样的大事，就得写下来。

paragraphs.en: And blood.”
paragraphs.cn: 还要有血。”

paragraphs.en: Tom’s whole being applauded this idea.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 特别喜欢这个主意。

paragraphs.en: It was deep, and dark, and awful; the hour, the circumstances, the surroundings, were in keeping with it.
paragraphs.cn: 这主意又深奥又吓人。当时的时间、事情、周围的一切都很符合。

paragraphs.en: He picked up a clean pine shingle that lay in the moon-light, took a little fragment of “red keel” out of his pocket, got the moon on his work, and painfully scrawled these lines, emphasizing each slow down-stroke by clamping his tongue between his teeth, and letting up the pressure on the up-strokes.
paragraphs.cn: 他捡起一块干净的松木板，它在月光下。他从口袋里拿出一小块“红石头笔”。借着月光，他很吃力地写下这些字。每写一个慢笔画，他就把舌头夹在牙齿间。向上提笔时，他就放松。

paragraphs.en: “Huck Finn and Tom Sawyer swears they will keep mum about This and They wish They may Drop down dead in Their Tracks if They ever Tell and Rot.”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克 芬恩和 汤姆·索亚 发誓会保守这个秘密。如果他们说出去，他们希望自己立刻死掉，身体腐烂。”

paragraphs.en: Huckleberry was filled with admiration of Tom’s facility in writing, and the sublimity of his language.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克伯利很佩服 汤姆 写字写得好，话也说得棒。

paragraphs.en: He at once took a pin from his lapel and was going to prick his flesh, but Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 他马上从衣服上拿下一根别针，想扎自己的肉。但 汤姆 说：

paragraphs.en: “Hold on!
paragraphs.cn: “等等！

paragraphs.en: Don’t do that.
paragraphs.cn: 别这样做。

paragraphs.en: A pin’s brass.
paragraphs.cn: 别针是黄铜做的。

paragraphs.en: It might have verdigrease on it.”
paragraphs.cn: 它上面可能有铜绿。”

paragraphs.en: “What’s verdigrease?”
paragraphs.cn: “铜绿是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “It’s p’ison.
paragraphs.cn: “那是毒药。

paragraphs.en: That’s what it is.
paragraphs.cn: 就是那个东西。

paragraphs.en: You just swaller some of it once—you’ll see.”
paragraphs.cn: 你尝一点点，就知道了。

paragraphs.en: So Tom unwound the thread from one of his needles, and each boy pricked the ball of his thumb and squeezed out a drop of blood.
paragraphs.cn: 于是汤姆把针上的线解开，两个男孩都用针扎了一下大拇指头，挤出了一滴血。

paragraphs.en: In time, after many squeezes, Tom managed to sign his initials, using the ball of his little finger for a pen.
paragraphs.cn: 过了好一会儿，挤了好几次后，汤姆终于用他的小指头当笔，写下了自己的名字缩写。

paragraphs.en: Then he showed Huckleberry how to make an H and an F, and the oath was complete.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他教哈克贝利写H和F，这个誓言就完成了。

paragraphs.en: They buried the shingle close to the wall, with some dismal ceremonies and incantations, and the fetters that bound their tongues were considered to be locked and the key thrown away.
paragraphs.cn: 他们把木板埋在墙边，举行了一些很神秘的仪式，念了一些咒语。他们觉得自己的秘密被锁住了，钥匙也被扔掉了，再也不能说出去了。

paragraphs.en: A figure crept stealthily through a break in the other end of the ruined building, now, but they did not notice it.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，一个人影悄悄地从破房子另一边的缺口爬了进来，但他们没有发现。

paragraphs.en: “Tom,” whispered Huckleberry, “does this keep us from _ever_ telling—_always_?”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，”哈克贝利小声说，“这能让我们永远不说出去吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Of course it does.
paragraphs.cn: “当然可以。”

paragraphs.en: It don’t make any difference _what_ happens, we got to keep mum.
paragraphs.cn: “不管发生什么事，我们都不能说出去。”

paragraphs.en: We’d drop down dead—don’t _you_ know that?”
paragraphs.cn: “我们会突然死掉的，难道你不知道吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, I reckon that’s so.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我想是这样。”

paragraphs.en: They continued to whisper for some little time.
paragraphs.cn: 他们又小声说了好一会儿话。

paragraphs.en: Presently a dog set up a long, lugubrious howl just outside—within ten feet of them.
paragraphs.cn: 突然，外面传来一阵长长的、悲伤的狗叫声，就在他们外面，离他们不到三米远的地方。

paragraphs.en: The boys clasped each other suddenly, in an agony of fright.
paragraphs.cn: 两个男孩吓得要命，一下子紧紧抱在一起。

paragraphs.en: “Which of us does he mean?” gasped Huckleberry.
paragraphs.cn: “它是在说我们中的谁？”哈克贝利喘着气问。

paragraphs.en: “I dono—peep through the crack.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道——从缝隙里往外看。

paragraphs.en: Quick!”
paragraphs.cn: 快点！”

paragraphs.en: “No, _you_, Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: “不，你去看，汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: “I can’t—I can’t _do_ it, Huck!”
paragraphs.cn: “我不能——我做不到，哈克！”

paragraphs.en: “Please, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “求你了，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: There ’tis again!”
paragraphs.cn: 又来了！”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, lordy, I’m thankful!” whispered Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，天啊，太好了！”汤姆小声说。

paragraphs.en: “I know his voice.
paragraphs.cn: “我认识这个声音。

paragraphs.en: It’s Bull Harbison.”
paragraphs.cn: 是布尔·哈比森。”

paragraphs.en: [* If Mr. Harbison owned a slave named Bull, Tom would have spoken of him as “Harbison’s Bull,” but a son or a dog of that name was “Bull Harbison.”
paragraphs.cn: [* 如果哈比森先生有个叫布尔的奴隶，汤姆会说他是“哈比森家的布尔”，但如果是他叫布尔的儿子或狗，就会说“布尔·哈比森”。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, that’s good—I tell you, Tom, I was most scared to death; I’d a bet anything it was a _stray_ dog.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，太好了——我跟你说，汤姆，我刚才快吓死了；我敢打赌那是一条流浪狗。”

paragraphs.en: The dog howled again.
paragraphs.cn: 狗又叫了一声。

paragraphs.en: The boys’ hearts sank once more.
paragraphs.cn: 两个男孩的心又沉了下去。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, my! that ain’t no Bull Harbison!” whispered Huckleberry. “_Do_, Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀！那不是布尔·哈比森！”哈克小声说。“快，汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: Tom, quaking with fear, yielded, and put his eye to the crack.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆吓得发抖，听话地把眼睛凑到缝隙上。

paragraphs.en: His whisper was hardly audible when he said:
paragraphs.cn: 他的声音很小，几乎听不见，他说：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Huck, _it’s a stray dog_!”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，哈克，那是一只流浪狗！”

paragraphs.en: “Quick, Tom, quick!
paragraphs.cn: “快，汤姆，快！

paragraphs.en: Who does he mean?”
paragraphs.cn: 他指的是谁？”

paragraphs.en: “Huck, he must mean us both—we’re right together.”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，他肯定是指我们俩——我们就在一起。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Tom, I reckon we’re goners.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，汤姆，我想我们完了。

paragraphs.en: I reckon there ain’t no mistake ’bout where _I’ll_ go to.
paragraphs.cn: 我想我肯定知道我将要去哪里了。

paragraphs.en: I been so wicked.”
paragraphs.cn: 我太坏了。”

paragraphs.en: “Dad fetch it!
paragraphs.cn: “真是的！

paragraphs.en: This comes of playing hookey and doing everything a feller’s told _not_ to do.
paragraphs.cn: 这都是因为逃学，还做了所有不让做的事。

paragraphs.en: I might a been good, like Sid, if I’d a tried—but no, I wouldn’t, of course.
paragraphs.cn: 我本来可以像希德一样乖的，如果我努力过——可是不，我当然不会那样做。

paragraphs.en: But if ever I get off this time, I lay I’ll just _waller_ in Sunday-schools!”
paragraphs.cn: 但如果这次我能逃过一劫，我发誓我一定会好好去上主日学的！”

paragraphs.en: And Tom began to snuffle a little.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆开始轻轻地抽泣起来。

paragraphs.en: “_You_ bad!” and Huckleberry began to snuffle too.
paragraphs.cn: “你坏！”哈克也开始抽泣了。

paragraphs.en: “Consound it, Tom Sawyer, you’re just old pie, ’long-side o’ what I am.
paragraphs.cn: “真是的，汤姆·索亚，你根本就不坏，比我好多了。

paragraphs.en: Oh, _lordy_, lordy, lordy, I wisht I only had half your chance.”
paragraphs.cn: 哦，天哪，天哪，天哪，我真希望我能像你一样好。”

paragraphs.en: Tom choked off and whispered:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆停住了抽泣，小声说：

paragraphs.en: “Look, Hucky, look!
paragraphs.cn: “看，哈克，看！

paragraphs.en: He’s got his _back_ to us!”
paragraphs.cn: 他背对着我们！”

paragraphs.en: Hucky looked, with joy in his heart.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克看了看，心里很高兴。

paragraphs.en: “Well, he has, by jingoes!
paragraphs.cn: “真的，他确实是这样！

paragraphs.en: Did he before?”
paragraphs.cn: 他之前也是吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, he did.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，他之前是。

paragraphs.en: But I, like a fool, never thought.
paragraphs.cn: 可我真傻，从来没想过。

paragraphs.en: Oh, this is bully, you know.
paragraphs.cn: 哦，这太棒了，你知道吗。

paragraphs.en: _Now_ who can he mean?”
paragraphs.cn: 那么现在，他能指的是谁呢？”

paragraphs.en: The howling stopped.
paragraphs.cn: 嚎叫声停了。

paragraphs.en: Tom pricked up his ears.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆竖起了耳朵。

paragraphs.en: “Sh!
What’s that?” he whispered.
paragraphs.cn: 那是什么声音？”他小声问。

paragraphs.en: “Sounds like—like hogs grunting.
paragraphs.cn: “听起来像——像猪在哼哼。

paragraphs.en: No—it’s somebody snoring, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: 不对——是有人在打呼噜，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: “That _is_ it!
paragraphs.cn: “就是这个声音！

paragraphs.en: Where ’bouts is it, Huck?”
paragraphs.cn: 声音在哪儿，哈克？”

paragraphs.en: “I bleeve it’s down at ’tother end.
paragraphs.cn: “我觉得声音在那边。

paragraphs.en: Sounds so, anyway.
paragraphs.cn: 反正听起来是那样。

paragraphs.en: Pap used to sleep there, sometimes, ’long with the hogs, but laws bless you, he just lifts things when _he_ snores.
paragraphs.cn: 爸爸以前有时和猪一起睡在那儿，但他打呼噜的时候，声音可大了，像把东西都震起来了一样。

paragraphs.en: Besides, I reckon he ain’t ever coming back to this town any more.”
paragraphs.cn: 再说，我想他再也不会回这个镇子了。”

paragraphs.en: The spirit of adventure rose in the boys’ souls once more.
paragraphs.cn: 两个小男孩心里又充满了冒险精神。

paragraphs.en: “Hucky, do you das’t to go if I lead?”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，我带头的话，你敢不敢去？”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t like to, much.
paragraphs.cn: “我不太想去。

paragraphs.en: Tom, s’pose it’s Injun Joe!”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，万一那是印第安·乔呢！”

paragraphs.en: Tom quailed.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆害怕了。

paragraphs.en: But presently the temptation rose up strong again and the boys agreed to try, with the understanding that they would take to their heels if the snoring stopped.
paragraphs.cn: 但很快，好奇心又变得很强，两个男孩决定去看看，他们说好了，要是打呼噜的声音停了，他们就赶紧跑。

paragraphs.en: So they went tiptoeing stealthily down, the one behind the other.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们一个跟着一个，踮着脚悄悄地走下去。

paragraphs.en: When they had got to within five steps of the snorer, Tom stepped on a stick, and it broke with a sharp snap.
paragraphs.cn: 当他们离打呼噜的人只有五步远的时候，汤姆踩到了一根小树枝，树枝“啪”的一声断了。

paragraphs.en: The man moaned, writhed a little, and his face came into the moonlight.
paragraphs.cn: 那个人哼了一声，扭动了一下，他的脸露在了月光下。

paragraphs.en: It was Muff Potter.
paragraphs.cn: 原来是莫夫·波特。

paragraphs.en: The boys’ hearts had stood still, and their hopes too, when the man moved, but their fears passed away now.
paragraphs.cn: 那个人动的时候，两个男孩的心都快要停止跳动了，他们的希望也快没了，但现在他们的害怕都消失了。

paragraphs.en: They tip-toed out, through the broken weather-boarding, and stopped at a little distance to exchange a parting word.
paragraphs.cn: 他们踮着脚从破烂的木板缝里走出去，在不远处停下来，小声说了几句告别的话。

paragraphs.en: That long, lugubrious howl rose on the night air again!
paragraphs.cn: 那又长又悲伤的狗叫声，再次在夜空中响起！

paragraphs.en: They turned and saw the strange dog standing within a few feet of where Potter was lying, and _facing_ Potter, with his nose pointing heavenward.
paragraphs.cn: 他们转过身，看到那只陌生的狗站在离波特躺着的地方几英尺远的地方，鼻子朝上，正对着波特。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, geeminy, it’s _him_!” exclaimed both boys, in a breath.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，天哪，是_他_！”两个男孩异口同声地喊道。

paragraphs.en: “Say, Tom—they say a stray dog come howling around Johnny Miller’s house, ’bout midnight, as much as two weeks ago; and a whippoorwill come in and lit on the banisters and sung, the very same evening; and there ain’t anybody dead there yet.”
paragraphs.cn: “喂，汤姆——他们说，大约两周前，有一只流浪狗半夜在约翰尼·米勒家附近嚎叫；同一天晚上，一只北美夜鹰飞进来，落在扶手上唱歌；但他们家到现在还没人死。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I know that.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我知道。

paragraphs.en: And suppose there ain’t.
paragraphs.cn: 就算没有呢？

paragraphs.en: Didn’t Gracie Miller fall in the kitchen fire and burn herself terrible the very next Saturday?”
paragraphs.cn: 下一个星期六，格蕾西·米勒不是掉进厨房的火里，烧伤得很厉害吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, but she ain’t _dead_.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，但她还没_死_。”

paragraphs.en: And what’s more, she’s getting better, too.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且啊，她现在也越来越好了。

paragraphs.en: “All right, you wait and see.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，你等着瞧吧。

paragraphs.en: She’s a goner, just as dead sure as Muff Potter’s a goner.
paragraphs.cn: 她肯定活不成了，就像莫夫·波特肯定活不成了一样。

paragraphs.en: That’s what the niggers say, and they know all about these kind of things, Huck.”
paragraphs.cn: 他们就是这么说的，而且他们对这些事情很了解，哈克。”

paragraphs.en: Then they separated, cogitating.
paragraphs.cn: 之后他们分开了，各自想着心事。

paragraphs.en: When Tom crept in at his bedroom window the night was almost spent.
paragraphs.cn: 当汤姆从他卧室的窗户爬进去的时候，天快亮了。

paragraphs.en: He undressed with excessive caution, and fell asleep congratulating himself that nobody knew of his escapade.
paragraphs.cn: 他非常小心地脱了衣服，然后睡着了，心里还庆幸着没人知道他偷偷溜出去的事。

paragraphs.en: He was not aware that the gently-snoring Sid was awake, and had been so for an hour.
paragraphs.cn: 他不知道，正在轻轻打鼾的希德其实醒着，而且已经醒了一个小时了。

paragraphs.en: When Tom awoke, Sid was dressed and gone.
paragraphs.cn: 当汤姆醒来时，希德已经穿好衣服走了。

paragraphs.en: There was a late look in the light, a late sense in the atmosphere.
paragraphs.cn: 光线看起来很迟钝，周围的气氛也很沉闷。

paragraphs.en: He was startled.
paragraphs.cn: 他吓了一跳。

paragraphs.en: Why had he not been called—persecuted till he was up, as usual?
paragraphs.cn: 为什么没人叫他起床呢？以前可总是催着他，直到他起来为止啊！

paragraphs.en: The thought filled him with bodings.
paragraphs.cn: 这个想法让他心里充满了不好的预感。

paragraphs.en: Within five minutes he was dressed and down-stairs, feeling sore and drowsy.
paragraphs.cn: 不到五分钟，他就穿好衣服下楼了，感觉浑身酸痛又犯困。

paragraphs.en: The family were still at table, but they had finished breakfast.
paragraphs.cn: 家里人还在桌边，不过他们已经吃完早饭了。

paragraphs.en: There was no voice of rebuke; but there were averted eyes; there was a silence and an air of solemnity that struck a chill to the culprit’s heart.
paragraphs.cn: 没有人责骂他；但大家都不看他，气氛很安静也很严肃，这让这个犯错的孩子心里凉凉的。

paragraphs.en: He sat down and tried to seem gay, but it was up-hill work; it roused no smile, no response, and he lapsed into silence and let his heart sink down to the depths.
paragraphs.cn: 他坐下来，想表现得很开心，但这太难了；没人对他笑，也没人回应他，于是他又沉默了，心里也越来越难过。

paragraphs.en: After breakfast his aunt took him aside, and Tom almost brightened in the hope that he was going to be flogged; but it was not so.
paragraphs.cn: 吃完早饭，阿姨把他拉到一边，汤姆心里甚至有点高兴，以为自己要挨打了；但结果并不是这样。

paragraphs.en: His aunt wept over him and asked him how he could go and break her old heart so; and finally told him to go on, and ruin himself and bring her gray hairs with sorrow to the grave, for it was no use for her to try any more.
paragraphs.cn: 阿姨哭着抱住他，问他怎么能这么伤她的心；最后告诉他，随便他去闯祸吧，把她的白头发都气得伤心带到坟墓里去，她再也不管了。

paragraphs.en: This was worse than a thousand whippings, and Tom’s heart was sorer now than his body.
paragraphs.cn: 这比打他一千次还难受，汤姆的心比身体更痛了。

paragraphs.en: He cried, he pleaded for forgiveness, promised to reform over and over again, and then received his dismissal, feeling that he had won but an imperfect forgiveness and established but a feeble confidence.
paragraphs.cn: 他哭了，不停地求大家原谅他，一遍又一遍地保证会改好，最后他被放走了，感觉自己得到的原谅不太完全，大家对他的信任也很少。

paragraphs.en: He left the presence too miserable to even feel revengeful toward Sid; and so the latter’s prompt retreat through the back gate was unnecessary.
paragraphs.cn: 他离开的时候太难过了，甚至都顾不上生希德的气了；所以希德赶紧从后门溜走其实是没必要的。

paragraphs.en: He moped to school gloomy and sad, and took his flogging, along with Joe Harper, for playing hookey the day before, with the air of one whose heart was busy with heavier woes and wholly dead to trifles.
paragraphs.cn: 他闷闷不乐、愁眉苦脸地去了学校，和乔·哈珀一起因为前一天逃学而挨了打，但他心里只想着更沉重的事情，对这些小事一点都不在乎。

paragraphs.en: Then he betook himself to his seat, rested his elbows on his desk and his jaws in his hands, and stared at the wall with the stony stare of suffering that has reached the limit and can no further go.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他回到座位上，把手肘放在桌上，两只手托着下巴，呆呆地看着墙，那种痛苦的眼神好像已经到了极限，再也承受不住了。

paragraphs.en: His elbow was pressing against some hard substance.
paragraphs.cn: 他的手肘碰到一个硬硬的东西。

paragraphs.en: After a long time he slowly and sadly changed his position, and took up this object with a sigh.
paragraphs.cn: 过了很久，他才慢慢地、伤心地换了个姿势，叹了口气，拿起那个东西。

paragraphs.en: It was in a paper.
paragraphs.cn: 它包在纸里。

paragraphs.en: He unrolled it.
paragraphs.cn: 他把它打开了。

paragraphs.en: A long, lingering, colossal sigh followed, and his heart broke.
paragraphs.cn: 接着他长长地、久久地、大大地叹了口气，然后他的心都碎了。

paragraphs.en: It was his brass andiron knob!
paragraphs.cn: 那是他的黄铜火炉架装饰球！

paragraphs.en: This final feather broke the camel’s back.
paragraphs.cn: 这最后一根羽毛，把骆驼压垮了。

paragraphs.en: Close upon the hour of noon the whole village was suddenly electrified with the ghastly news.
paragraphs.cn: 快到中午的时候，整个村子突然被一个可怕的消息吓到了。

paragraphs.en: No need of the as yet un-dreamed-of telegraph; the tale flew from man to man, from group to group, from house to house, with little less than telegraphic speed.
paragraphs.cn: 那时还没有电报，消息却传得飞快。一个人告诉另一个人，一家人告诉另一家人，比电报还快呢！

paragraphs.en: Of course the schoolmaster gave holiday for that afternoon; the town would have thought strangely of him if he had not.
paragraphs.cn: 当然，那天下午老师就给大家放假了。要是他不放假，村里人都会觉得他很奇怪呢。

paragraphs.en: A gory knife had been found close to the murdered man, and it had been recognized by somebody as belonging to Muff Potter—so the story ran.
paragraphs.cn: 被杀的人旁边，发现了一把沾血的刀。有人说，这把刀是莫夫·波特的——大家都这么传。

paragraphs.en: And it was said that a belated citizen had come upon Potter washing himself in the “branch” about one or two o’clock in the morning, and that Potter had at once sneaked off—suspicious circumstances, especially the washing which was not a habit with Potter.
paragraphs.cn: 还有人说，一个回家晚了的人，在凌晨一两点的时候，看见波特在小河里洗澡。然后，波特就马上偷偷溜走了——这事很可疑，特别是洗澡这件事，因为波特平时可不爱洗澡呢。

paragraphs.en: It was also said that the town had been ransacked for this “murderer” (the public are not slow in the matter of sifting evidence and arriving at a verdict), but that he could not be found.
paragraphs.cn: 大家还说，整个镇子都在找这个“杀人犯”，可是找不到他。

paragraphs.en: Horsemen had departed down all the roads in every direction, and the Sheriff “was confident” that he would be captured before night.
paragraphs.cn: 骑马的人已经往四面八方的路上出发了。警长说，他“很有信心”，一定能在天黑前抓住凶手。

paragraphs.en: All the town was drifting toward the graveyard.
paragraphs.cn: 整个镇子的人都慢慢走向墓地。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s heartbreak vanished and he joined the procession, not because he would not a thousand times rather go anywhere else, but because an awful, unaccountable fascination drew him on.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆不再那么伤心了，他也跟着人群走去。不是因为他更想去那里，而是因为一种可怕又说不清的吸引力把他拉了过去。

paragraphs.en: Arrived at the dreadful place, he wormed his small body through the crowd and saw the dismal spectacle.
paragraphs.cn: 到了那个可怕的地方，他挤过人群，看到了那悲惨的一幕。

paragraphs.en: It seemed to him an age since he was there before.
paragraphs.cn: 他觉得，上次来这里到现在，好像过了好久好久。

paragraphs.en: Somebody pinched his arm.
paragraphs.cn: 有人捏了一下他的胳膊。

paragraphs.en: He turned, and his eyes met Huckleberry’s.
paragraphs.cn: 他转过头，看到了哈克贝利。

paragraphs.en: Then both looked elsewhere at once, and wondered if anybody had noticed anything in their mutual glance.
paragraphs.cn: 然后，两人立刻看向别处，心想有没有人发现他们刚才互相看了一眼。

paragraphs.en: But everybody was talking, and intent upon the grisly spectacle before them.
paragraphs.cn: 但是大家都在说话，全神贯注地看着眼前那个可怕的景象。

paragraphs.en: “Poor fellow!”
paragraphs.cn: “可怜的家伙！”

paragraphs.en: “Poor young fellow!”
paragraphs.cn: “可怜的年轻人啊！”

paragraphs.en: “This ought to be a lesson to grave robbers!”
paragraphs.cn: “这下，盗墓贼可要得到教训了！”

paragraphs.en: “Muff Potter’ll hang for this if they catch him!”
paragraphs.cn: “如果他们抓住莫夫·波特，他就要被吊死了！”

paragraphs.en: This was the drift of remark; and the minister said, “It was a judgment; His hand is here.”
paragraphs.cn: 大家都是这么说的；牧师说：“这是老天爷的惩罚，老天爷在管这件事呢。”

paragraphs.en: Now Tom shivered from head to heel; for his eye fell upon the stolid face of Injun Joe.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，汤姆从头到脚都颤抖起来；因为他的目光落在了印第安·乔那没有表情的脸上。

paragraphs.en: At this moment the crowd began to sway and struggle, and voices shouted, “It’s him! it’s him! he’s coming himself!”
paragraphs.cn: 就在这时，人群开始晃动和推搡，有人喊起来：“是他！是他！他自己来了！”

paragraphs.en: “Who?
Who?” from twenty voices.
paragraphs.cn: 二十多个人都在问：“是谁？”

paragraphs.en: “Muff Potter!”
paragraphs.cn: “莫夫·波特！”

paragraphs.en: “Hallo, he’s stopped!
paragraphs.cn: “嘿，他停下来了！

paragraphs.en: —Look out, he’s turning!
paragraphs.cn: —快看，他在转身！

paragraphs.en: Don’t let him get away!”
paragraphs.cn: 别让他跑了！”

paragraphs.en: People in the branches of the trees over Tom’s head said he wasn’t trying to get away—he only looked doubtful and perplexed.
paragraphs.cn: 在汤姆头顶上方树枝上的人说，他没有想跑——他只是看起来有点犹豫，不知道该怎么办。

paragraphs.en: “Infernal impudence!” said a bystander; “wanted to come and take a quiet look at his work, I reckon—didn’t expect any company.”
paragraphs.cn: “真是太不像话了！”一个围观的人说，“他肯定是想偷偷来看看他做的事，没想到有人在这。”

paragraphs.en: The crowd fell apart, now, and the Sheriff came through, ostentatiously leading Potter by the arm.
paragraphs.cn: 人群散开了，警长走了过来，故意拉着波特的胳膊。

paragraphs.en: The poor fellow’s face was haggard, and his eyes showed the fear that was upon him.
paragraphs.cn: 这个可怜人脸色苍白，眼睛里全是害怕。

paragraphs.en: When he stood before the murdered man, he shook as with a palsy, and he put his face in his hands and burst into tears.
paragraphs.cn: 当他站在被杀的人面前时，他抖得厉害，他把脸埋在手里，大哭起来。

paragraphs.en: “I didn’t do it, friends,” he sobbed; “’pon my word and honor I never done it.”
paragraphs.cn: “朋友们，不是我干的！”他抽泣着说，“我发誓，真的不是我干的。”

paragraphs.en: “Who’s accused you?” shouted a voice.
paragraphs.cn: “谁说你干的？”一个声音喊道。

paragraphs.en: This shot seemed to carry home.
paragraphs.cn: 这句话好像让他听进去了。

paragraphs.en: Potter lifted his face and looked around him with a pathetic hopelessness in his eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 波特抬起脸，看了看四周，他的眼睛里带着绝望。

paragraphs.en: He saw Injun Joe, and exclaimed:
paragraphs.cn: 他看到了印第安·乔，大声说：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Injun Joe, you promised me you’d never—”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，印第安·乔，你答应过我你不会——”

paragraphs.en: “Is that your knife?” and it was thrust before him by the Sheriff.
paragraphs.cn: “这是你的刀吗？”警长把刀推到他面前。

paragraphs.en: Potter would have fallen if they had not caught him and eased him to the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 波特差点摔倒，幸好大家扶住了他，让他坐在地上。

paragraphs.en: Then he said:
paragraphs.cn: 然后他说：

paragraphs.en: “Something told me ’t if I didn’t come back and get—” He shuddered; then waved his nerveless hand with a vanquished gesture and said, “Tell ’em, Joe, tell ’em—it ain’t any use any more.”
paragraphs.cn: “我心里好像有个声音告诉我，如果我不回来拿——”他发抖了；然后他无力地挥了挥手，像认输一样说，“告诉他们吧，乔，告诉他们吧——现在说什么都没用了。”

paragraphs.en: Then Huckleberry and Tom stood dumb and staring, and heard the stony-hearted liar reel off his serene statement, they expecting every moment that the clear sky would deliver God’s lightnings upon his head, and wondering to see how long the stroke was delayed.
paragraphs.cn: 然后哈克贝利和汤姆呆呆地站在那儿，一动不动，听着那个狠心的骗子平静地说着谎话，他们每时每刻都以为老天爷会打雷劈他，想知道为什么雷还没劈下来。

paragraphs.en: And when he had finished and still stood alive and whole, their wavering impulse to break their oath and save the poor betrayed prisoner’s life faded and vanished away, for plainly this miscreant had sold himself to Satan and it would be fatal to meddle with the property of such a power as that.
paragraphs.cn: 等他说完，还好好地活着，他们想打破誓言，救那个可怜的被冤枉的人的念头就消失了，因为很明显，这个坏蛋把自己卖给了魔鬼，和魔鬼的东西作对，会很危险的。

paragraphs.en: “Why didn’t you leave?
paragraphs.cn: “你为什么不走？

paragraphs.en: What did you want to come here for?” somebody said.
paragraphs.cn: 你来这里干什么？”有人说。

paragraphs.en: “I couldn’t help it—I couldn’t help it,” Potter moaned.
paragraphs.cn: “我没办法——我没办法！”波特痛苦地呻吟着。

paragraphs.en: “I wanted to run away, but I couldn’t seem to come anywhere but here.”
paragraphs.cn: “我想跑掉，但我好像只能来这里。”

paragraphs.en: And he fell to sobbing again.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他又开始抽泣起来。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe repeated his statement, just as calmly, a few minutes afterward on the inquest, under oath; and the boys, seeing that the lightnings were still withheld, were confirmed in their belief that Joe had sold himself to the devil.
paragraphs.cn: 几分钟后，印第安·乔在法庭上发誓，还是那么平静地重复了他的话；男孩们看到雷电还是没有劈下来，就更相信乔把自己卖给了魔鬼。

paragraphs.en: He was now become, to them, the most balefully interesting object they had ever looked upon, and they could not take their fascinated eyes from his face.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，他成了他们见过最吓人、最有意思的人，他们被他的脸迷住了，眼睛都移不开。

paragraphs.en: They inwardly resolved to watch him nights, when opportunity should offer, in the hope of getting a glimpse of his dread master.
paragraphs.cn: 他们心里决定晚上要盯着他，等有机会的时候，希望能看到那个可怕的魔鬼主人。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe helped to raise the body of the murdered man and put it in a wagon for removal; and it was whispered through the shuddering crowd that the wound bled a little!
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔帮忙抬起了被杀的人的尸体，放进马车里运走；颤抖的人群中，有人小声说伤口竟然流了一点血！

paragraphs.en: The boys thought that this happy circumstance would turn suspicion in the right direction; but they were disappointed, for more than one villager remarked:
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们以为这个“好兆头”会让大家怀疑对的人；但他们失望了，因为不止一个村民说：

paragraphs.en: “It was within three feet of Muff Potter when it done it.”
paragraphs.cn: “这件事发生的时候，就在莫夫·波特身边三英尺的地方。”

paragraphs.en: Tom’s fearful secret and gnawing conscience disturbed his sleep for as much as a week after this; and at breakfast one morning Sid said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆的可怕秘密和内心不安让他一个多星期都睡不好觉；有一天早上吃早饭时，希德说：

paragraphs.en: “Tom, you pitch around and talk in your sleep so much that you keep me awake half the time.”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，你睡觉的时候老是翻来翻去，还说梦话，害得我一半时间都睡不着。”

paragraphs.en: Tom blanched and dropped his eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆脸色发白，低下了头。

paragraphs.en: “It’s a bad sign,” said Aunt Polly, gravely.
paragraphs.cn: “这是个不好的兆头，” 波莉姨妈认真地说。

paragraphs.en: “What you got on your mind, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: “你心里在想什么，汤姆？”

paragraphs.en: “Nothing.
paragraphs.cn: “没什么。

paragraphs.en: Nothing ’t I know of.”
paragraphs.cn: 我不知道有什么事。”

paragraphs.en: But the boy’s hand shook so that he spilled his coffee.
paragraphs.cn: 但是男孩的手抖得厉害，把咖啡都洒了。

paragraphs.en: “And you do talk such stuff,” Sid said.
paragraphs.cn: “你确实说了一些奇怪的话，” 希德说。

paragraphs.en: “Last night you said, ‘It’s blood, it’s blood, that’s what it is!’
paragraphs.cn: “昨晚你说，‘是血，是血，就是血！’

paragraphs.en: You said that over and over.
paragraphs.cn: 你一遍又一遍地说。

paragraphs.en: And you said, ‘Don’t torment me so—I’ll tell!’
paragraphs.cn: 你还说，‘别再折磨我了——我会说出来的！’

paragraphs.en: Tell _what_?
paragraphs.cn: 说什么呢？

paragraphs.en: What is it you’ll tell?”
paragraphs.cn: 你要说什么？”

paragraphs.en: Everything was swimming before Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆觉得眼前的东西都在转。

paragraphs.en: There is no telling what might have happened, now, but luckily the concern passed out of Aunt Polly’s face and she came to Tom’s relief without knowing it.
paragraphs.cn: 现在不知道会发生什么，但幸好，波莉姨妈脸上的担心不见了。她自己都没发现，就帮了汤姆的忙。

paragraphs.en: She said:
paragraphs.cn: 她说：

paragraphs.en: “Sho!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀！

paragraphs.en: It’s that dreadful murder.
paragraphs.cn: 是那件可怕的杀人案。

paragraphs.en: I dream about it most every night myself.
paragraphs.cn: 我自己几乎每晚都梦到它。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes I dream it’s me that done it.”
paragraphs.cn: 有时我梦到是我干的。”

paragraphs.en: Mary said she had been affected much the same way.
paragraphs.cn: 玛丽说她也和她一样，心里很难受。

paragraphs.en: Sid seemed satisfied.
paragraphs.cn: 希德看起来很满意。

paragraphs.en: Tom got out of the presence as quick as he plausibly could, and after that he complained of toothache for a week, and tied up his jaws every night.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆赶紧离开了。那以后，他抱怨牙疼了一周，每天晚上都把嘴巴包起来。

paragraphs.en: He never knew that Sid lay nightly watching, and frequently slipped the bandage free and then leaned on his elbow listening a good while at a time, and afterward slipped the bandage back to its place again.
paragraphs.cn: 他从不知道，希德每晚都会躺着悄悄看他。她常常把绷带解开，然后靠着胳膊，静静地听好久。听完后，又把绷带绑回去。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s distress of mind wore off gradually and the toothache grew irksome and was discarded.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆心里难受的感觉慢慢淡了，牙疼也变得很烦人，后来就不再管它了。

paragraphs.en: If Sid really managed to make anything out of Tom’s disjointed mutterings, he kept it to himself.
paragraphs.cn: 如果希德真的从汤姆说的话里听懂了什么，他也没告诉别人。

paragraphs.en: It seemed to Tom that his schoolmates never would get done holding inquests on dead cats, and thus keeping his trouble present to his mind.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆觉得他的同学们好像永远也查不完死猫的事，这让他的烦恼总在心里。

paragraphs.en: Sid noticed that Tom never was coroner at one of these inquiries, though it had been his habit to take the lead in all new enterprises; he noticed, too, that Tom never acted as a witness—and that was strange; and Sid did not overlook the fact that Tom even showed a marked aversion to these inquests, and always avoided them when he could.
paragraphs.cn: 希德发现，汤姆从来没有在这些调查中做过“验尸官”，虽然他以前总是喜欢带头做新事。他还发现，汤姆也从来没有做过证人——这很奇怪。希德也没有忽略一点，那就是汤姆好像特别不喜欢这些调查，能躲开就躲开。

paragraphs.en: Sid marvelled, but said nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 希德很惊讶，但什么也没说。

paragraphs.en: However, even inquests went out of vogue at last, and ceased to torture Tom’s conscience.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，这些调查最后也不流行了，汤姆的良心也不再受折磨了。

paragraphs.en: Every day or two, during this time of sorrow, Tom watched his opportunity and went to the little grated jail-window and smuggled such small comforts through to the “murderer” as he could get hold of.
paragraphs.cn: 在这段难过的日子里，每隔一两天，汤姆就会找机会去小小的监狱窗户那里，把能弄到的小零食什么的偷偷塞给那个“凶手”。

paragraphs.en: The jail was a trifling little brick den that stood in a marsh at the edge of the village, and no guards were afforded for it; indeed, it was seldom occupied.
paragraphs.cn: 那个监狱是个小小的砖房，孤零零地立在村子边上的沼泽地里。那里没有守卫看管，而且也很少有人住。

paragraphs.en: These offerings greatly helped to ease Tom’s conscience.
paragraphs.cn: 这些东西让汤姆心里好受了很多。

paragraphs.en: The villagers had a strong desire to tar-and-feather Injun Joe and ride him on a rail, for body-snatching, but so formidable was his character that nobody could be found who was willing to take the lead in the matter, so it was dropped.
paragraphs.cn: 村民们很想惩罚印第安·乔，因为他挖坟偷尸体。但是他太厉害了，没人敢带头，所以这件事就放下了。

paragraphs.en: He had been careful to begin both of his inquest-statements with the fight, without confessing the grave-robbery that preceded it; therefore it was deemed wisest not to try the case in the courts at present.
paragraphs.cn: 他很小心，两次说起这件事，都只从打架开始，没有说之前他偷尸体的事。所以，大家觉得现在不要去法庭上审理这个案子最聪明。

paragraphs.en: One of the reasons why Tom’s mind had drifted away from its secret troubles was, that it had found a new and weighty matter to interest itself about.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆不再为自己的秘密烦恼了，因为他发现了一件新的、更重要的事情，让他很感兴趣。

paragraphs.en: Becky Thatcher had stopped coming to school.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪·撒切尔不来学校了。

paragraphs.en: Tom had struggled with his pride a few days, and tried to “whistle her down the wind,” but failed.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆挣扎了好几天，想放下他的骄傲，假装不在乎她，但没有成功。

paragraphs.en: He began to find himself hanging around her father’s house, nights, and feeling very miserable.
paragraphs.cn: 他开始在晚上跑到她爸爸家附近转悠，心里很难过。

paragraphs.en: She was ill.
paragraphs.cn: 她生病了。

paragraphs.en: What if she should die!
paragraphs.cn: 万一她死了怎么办！

paragraphs.en: There was distraction in the thought.
paragraphs.cn: 这个想法让他很不安。

paragraphs.en: He no longer took an interest in war, nor even in piracy.
paragraphs.cn: 他不再对打仗感兴趣了，甚至连海盗游戏也不喜欢了。

paragraphs.en: The charm of life was gone; there was nothing but dreariness left.
paragraphs.cn: 生活的乐趣没有了；只剩下无聊。

paragraphs.en: He put his hoop away, and his bat; there was no joy in them any more.
paragraphs.cn: 他把呼啦圈和球棒收起来了；玩它们再也没有乐趣了。

paragraphs.en: His aunt was concerned.
paragraphs.cn: 他的姨妈很担心。

paragraphs.en: She began to try all manner of remedies on him.
paragraphs.cn: 她开始在他身上试各种各样的药方。

paragraphs.en: She was one of those people who are infatuated with patent medicines and all new-fangled methods of producing health or mending it.
paragraphs.cn: 她就是那种特别喜欢偏方和各种新奇保健方法的人。

paragraphs.en: She was an inveterate experimenter in these things.
paragraphs.cn: 她总是喜欢尝试这些东西。

paragraphs.en: When something fresh in this line came out she was in a fever, right away, to try it; not on herself, for she was never ailing, but on anybody else that came handy.
paragraphs.cn: 只要有新的东西出来，她就会立刻兴奋地想去试；不是在她自己身上试，因为她从不生病，而是找身边的人试。

paragraphs.en: She was a subscriber for all the “Health” periodicals and phrenological frauds; and the solemn ignorance they were inflated with was breath to her nostrils.
paragraphs.cn: 她订阅了所有“健康”杂志和那些假装看相识人的刊物；这些东西里那些一本正经的无知内容，她却深信不疑。

paragraphs.en: All the “rot” they contained about ventilation, and how to go to bed, and how to get up, and what to eat, and what to drink, and how much exercise to take, and what frame of mind to keep one’s self in, and what sort of clothing to wear, was all gospel to her, and she never observed that her health-journals of the current month customarily upset everything they had recommended the month before.
paragraphs.cn: 杂志里说的那些关于通风、睡觉、起床、吃什么、喝什么、做多少运动、保持什么心情、穿什么衣服的“废话”，在她看来都是真理。她从来没发现，这个月的健康杂志总是推翻上个月推荐的东西。

paragraphs.en: She was as simple-hearted and honest as the day was long, and so she was an easy victim.
paragraphs.cn: 她心很单纯，很诚实，所以很容易上当受骗。

paragraphs.en: She gathered together her quack periodicals and her quack medicines, and thus armed with death, went about on her pale horse, metaphorically speaking, with “hell following after.”
paragraphs.cn: 她把那些骗人的杂志和假药都收集起来。她就像一个带着“死亡”武器的人，到处乱跑，用这些不好的东西去“害人”。

paragraphs.en: But she never suspected that she was not an angel of healing and the balm of Gilead in disguise, to the suffering neighbors.
paragraphs.cn: 但她从没怀疑过自己不是一个治病救人的天使，没怀疑过自己不是给受苦的邻居带来安慰的良药。

paragraphs.en: The water treatment was new, now, and Tom’s low condition was a windfall to her.
paragraphs.cn: 水疗法现在很流行，汤姆生病了，这可让她逮着机会了。

paragraphs.en: She had him out at daylight every morning, stood him up in the wood-shed and drowned him with a deluge of cold water; then she scrubbed him down with a towel like a file, and so brought him to; then she rolled him up in a wet sheet and put him away under blankets till she sweated his soul clean and “the yellow stains of it came through his pores”—as Tom said.
paragraphs.cn: 她每天早上天一亮就把他叫起来，让他站在柴棚里，然后用一大盆一大盆的冷水往他身上泼。接着，她用粗糙的毛巾像搓衣服一样擦他，直到他清醒过来。然后，她把他裹在湿床单里，盖上毯子，让他一直出汗，直到他全身的“脏东西都从毛孔里流出来”——就像汤姆自己说的那样。

paragraphs.en: Yet notwithstanding all this, the boy grew more and more melancholy and pale and dejected.
paragraphs.cn: 但尽管这样，这个男孩还是越来越伤心、脸色苍白、无精打采。

paragraphs.en: She added hot baths, sitz baths, shower baths, and plunges.
paragraphs.cn: 她又给他加上了热水浴、坐浴、淋浴和浸泡浴。

paragraphs.en: The boy remained as dismal as a hearse.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩仍然闷闷不乐，一点都不开心。

paragraphs.en: She began to assist the water with a slim oatmeal diet and blister-plasters.
paragraphs.cn: 她开始在水疗法之外，给他吃很少的燕麦片，还给他贴上起泡膏药。

paragraphs.en: She calculated his capacity as she would a jug’s, and filled him up every day with quack cure-alls.
paragraphs.cn: 她像量杯子一样估算他的胃口，每天都给他灌满那些假药。

paragraphs.en: Tom had become indifferent to persecution by this time.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 这时候已经对受罚不当回事了。

paragraphs.en: This phase filled the old lady’s heart with consternation.
paragraphs.cn: 老奶奶看到这样，心里很着急。

paragraphs.en: This indifference must be broken up at any cost.
paragraphs.cn: 这种不当回事的态度，一定要改掉。

paragraphs.en: Now she heard of Pain-killer for the first time.
paragraphs.cn: 她现在第一次听说了“止痛药”。

paragraphs.en: She ordered a lot at once.
paragraphs.cn: 她立刻买了很多。

paragraphs.en: She tasted it and was filled with gratitude.
paragraphs.cn: 她尝了尝，非常感激。

paragraphs.en: It was simply fire in a liquid form.
paragraphs.cn: 这就像是液体的火。

paragraphs.en: She dropped the water treatment and everything else, and pinned her faith to Pain-killer.
paragraphs.cn: 她不再用水和其他方法了，只信止痛药。

paragraphs.en: She gave Tom a teaspoonful and watched with the deepest anxiety for the result.
paragraphs.cn: 她给汤姆喂了一小勺，非常担心地等着看效果。
