paragraphs.en: Her troubles were instantly at rest, her soul at peace again; for the “indifference” was broken up.
paragraphs.cn: 她的烦恼一下子就没了，心里又平静了。因为那种“不理不睬”没有了。

paragraphs.en: The boy could not have shown a wilder, heartier interest, if she had built a fire under him.
paragraphs.cn: 要是老奶奶在他屁股下点火，他也不会表现得更野、更来劲了。

paragraphs.en: Tom felt that it was time to wake up; this sort of life might be romantic enough, in his blighted condition, but it was getting to have too little sentiment and too much distracting variety about it.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 觉得是时候清醒了。他这样受罪的日子，也许有点意思，但少了感情，让人分心的事情却太多了。

paragraphs.en: So he thought over various plans for relief, and finally hit upon that of professing to be fond of Pain-killer.
paragraphs.cn: 所以他想了很多办法来解脱，最后想到了假装自己喜欢“止痛药”。

paragraphs.en: He asked for it so often that he became a nuisance, and his aunt ended by telling him to help himself and quit bothering her.
paragraphs.cn: 他老是缠着姑妈要止痛药，姑妈烦透了，就让他自己去拿，别再烦她了。

paragraphs.en: If it had been Sid, she would have had no misgivings to alloy her delight; but since it was Tom, she watched the bottle clandestinely.
paragraphs.cn: 要是希德拿药，她不会有什么不放心，会很高兴；但因为是汤姆，她就偷偷地看着药瓶。

paragraphs.en: She found that the medicine did really diminish, but it did not occur to her that the boy was mending the health of a crack in the sitting-room floor with it.
paragraphs.cn: 她发现药确实少了，但她没想到男孩在用它修补客厅地板的裂缝。

paragraphs.en: One day Tom was in the act of dosing the crack when his aunt’s yellow cat came along, purring, eyeing the teaspoon avariciously, and begging for a taste.
paragraphs.cn: 有一天，汤姆正在往裂缝里倒药，姑妈的黄猫走了过来。它一边发出咕噜咕噜的声音，一边贪婪地盯着小勺子，还想尝尝。

paragraphs.en: Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 说：

paragraphs.en: “Don’t ask for it unless you want it, Peter.”
paragraphs.cn: “彼得，你不想吃就别要。”

paragraphs.en: But Peter signified that he did want it.
paragraphs.cn: 但彼得表示他确实想吃。

paragraphs.en: “You better make sure.”
paragraphs.cn: “你最好确定一下。”

paragraphs.en: Peter was sure.
paragraphs.cn: 彼得很确定。

paragraphs.en: “Now you’ve asked for it, and I’ll give it to you, because there ain’t anything mean about me; but if you find you don’t like it, you mustn’t blame anybody but your own self.”
paragraphs.cn: “既然你都开口了，那我就给你，因为我可不小气；不过如果你发现不喜欢，可不能怪别人，只能怪你自己。”

paragraphs.en: Peter was agreeable.
paragraphs.cn: 彼得同意了。

paragraphs.en: So Tom pried his mouth open and poured down the Pain-killer.
paragraphs.cn: 于是汤姆撬开它的嘴巴，把止痛药倒了进去。

paragraphs.en: Peter sprang a couple of yards in the air, and then delivered a war-whoop and set off round and round the room, banging against furniture, upsetting flower-pots, and making general havoc.
paragraphs.cn: 彼得一下子跳到半空中几码高，然后大叫一声，在屋子里跑来跑去，撞到家具，打翻花盆，把房间弄得一团糟。

paragraphs.en: Next he rose on his hind feet and pranced around, in a frenzy of enjoyment, with his head over his shoulder and his voice proclaiming his unappeasable happiness.
paragraphs.cn: 接着它用后腿站起来，又跳又舞，开心得发疯，头扭过肩，大声叫着它止不住的快乐。

paragraphs.en: Then he went tearing around the house again spreading chaos and destruction in his path.
paragraphs.cn: 然后它又在屋子里到处跑，一路制造混乱和破坏。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly entered in time to see him throw a few double summersets, deliver a final mighty hurrah, and sail through the open window, carrying the rest of the flower-pots with him.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈 及时走了进来，看到它做了几个空中翻转，最后用力大喊一声，然后从开着的窗户飞了出去，还把剩下的花盆也带走了。

paragraphs.en: The old lady stood petrified with astonishment, peering over her glasses; Tom lay on the floor expiring with laughter.
paragraphs.cn: 老奶奶惊讶得呆住了，她透过眼镜看着；汤姆则躺在地板上笑得喘不过气来。

paragraphs.en: “Tom, what on earth ails that cat?”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，那猫到底怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know, aunt,” gasped the boy.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道，阿姨。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, I never see anything like it.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，我从没见过这样的事。

paragraphs.en: What did make him act so?”
paragraphs.cn: 它怎么会这样啊？”

paragraphs.en: “Deed I don’t know, Aunt Polly; cats always act so when they’re having a good time.”
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道，波莉姨妈；猫玩得开心的时候，总是这样。”

paragraphs.en: “They do, do they?”
paragraphs.cn: “它们是这样吗？”

paragraphs.en: There was something in the tone that made Tom apprehensive.
paragraphs.cn: 她的语气让汤姆有点害怕。

paragraphs.en: “Yes’m.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，阿姨。

paragraphs.en: That is, I believe they do.”
paragraphs.cn: 我是说，我觉得是这样。”

paragraphs.en: “You _do_?”
paragraphs.cn: “你真的觉得是这样吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes’m.”
paragraphs.cn: “是的，阿姨。”

paragraphs.en: The old lady was bending down, Tom watching, with interest emphasized by anxiety.
paragraphs.cn: 老妇人弯下腰，汤姆看着，又好奇又担心。

paragraphs.en: Too late he divined her “drift.”
paragraphs.cn: 太晚了，他才明白她的意思。

paragraphs.en: The handle of the telltale tea-spoon was visible under the bed-valance.
paragraphs.cn: 那把勺子的把手从床罩下面露出来了。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly took it, held it up.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈把它拿起来，举着。

paragraphs.en: Tom winced, and dropped his eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆吓得一哆嗦，并低下了头。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly raised him by the usual handle—his ear—and cracked his head soundly with her thimble.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈像平时一样揪住他的耳朵，用顶针狠狠敲了一下他的头。

paragraphs.en: “Now, sir, what did you want to treat that poor dumb beast so, for?”
paragraphs.cn: “喂，你啊，你为什么要这样对待那只可怜的小动物呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I done it out of pity for him—because he hadn’t any aunt.”
paragraphs.cn: “我可怜它才这么做的——因为它没有阿姨。”

paragraphs.en: “Hadn’t any aunt!
paragraphs.cn: “没有阿姨！

paragraphs.en: —you numskull.
paragraphs.cn: ——你这个笨蛋。

paragraphs.en: What has that got to do with it?”
paragraphs.cn: 这有什么关系？”

paragraphs.en: “Heaps.
paragraphs.cn: “关系可大了。

paragraphs.en: Because if he’d had one she’d a burnt him out herself!
paragraphs.cn: 因为如果它有阿姨，她会自己把它烧死的！

paragraphs.en: She’d a roasted his bowels out of him ’thout any more feeling than if he was a human!”
paragraphs.cn: 她会毫不留情地把它烤焦，一点都不会心疼，就好像它不是活物一样！”

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly felt a sudden pang of remorse.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈突然觉得很后悔。

paragraphs.en: This was putting the thing in a new light; what was cruelty to a cat _might_ be cruelty to a boy, too.
paragraphs.cn: 这件事让她有了新的想法；虐待猫咪，也许也算是虐待小男孩吧。

paragraphs.en: She began to soften; she felt sorry.
paragraphs.cn: 她开始心软了；她感到很抱歉。

paragraphs.en: Her eyes watered a little, and she put her hand on Tom’s head and said gently:
paragraphs.cn: 她的眼睛有点湿润了，她把手放在汤姆的头上，温柔地说：

paragraphs.en: “I was meaning for the best, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “我是为了你好，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: And, Tom, it _did_ do you good.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且，汤姆，那对你真的有好处。

paragraphs.en: Tom looked up in her face with just a perceptible twinkle peeping through his gravity.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆抬头看着她的脸。他虽然很认真，但眼睛里还是藏着一点点小顽皮。

paragraphs.en: “I know you was meaning for the best, aunty, and so was I with Peter.
paragraphs.cn: “阿姨，我知道你是为我好，我对彼得也是这样想的。

paragraphs.en: It done _him_ good, too.
paragraphs.cn: 那对他也有好处呢。

paragraphs.en: I never see him get around so since—”
paragraphs.cn: 我从没见过他这么开心，自从——”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, go ’long with you, Tom, before you aggravate me again.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，汤姆，快走开，别再惹我生气了。

paragraphs.en: And you try and see if you can’t be a good boy, for once, and you needn’t take any more medicine.”
paragraphs.cn: 你试着乖一次，这样就不用再吃药了。”

paragraphs.en: Tom reached school ahead of time.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆早早就到了学校。

paragraphs.en: It was noticed that this strange thing had been occurring every day latterly.
paragraphs.cn: 大家发现，最近他每天都这样，真奇怪。

paragraphs.en: And now, as usual of late, he hung about the gate of the schoolyard instead of playing with his comrades.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，和最近一样，他没跟小朋友们玩，而是站在学校门口。

paragraphs.en: He was sick, he said, and he looked it.
paragraphs.cn: 他说他生病了，看起来也真的不舒服。

paragraphs.en: He tried to seem to be looking everywhere but whither he really was looking—down the road.
paragraphs.cn: 他假装看别的地方，其实眼睛一直盯着路那边。

paragraphs.en: Presently Jeff Thatcher hove in sight, and Tom’s face lighted; he gazed a moment, and then turned sorrowfully away.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，杰夫撒切尔出现了，汤姆的脸一下子亮了；他看了一会儿，又伤心地转过头。

paragraphs.en: When Jeff arrived, Tom accosted him; and “led up” warily to opportunities for remark about Becky, but the giddy lad never could see the bait.
paragraphs.cn: 杰夫来了，汤姆走过去跟他说话。她想偷偷问问关于贝琪的事，可那个傻乎乎的男孩根本没明白。

paragraphs.en: Tom watched and watched, hoping whenever a frisking frock came in sight, and hating the owner of it as soon as he saw she was not the right one.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆一直看着，只要看到有小裙子出现，就希望能是她。但一发现不是，他就又不喜欢那个人了。

paragraphs.en: At last frocks ceased to appear, and he dropped hopelessly into the dumps; he entered the empty schoolhouse and sat down to suffer.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，再也没看到小裙子了。他很伤心，一点力气都没有了。他走进空空的教室，坐下来，感觉好难受。

paragraphs.en: Then one more frock passed in at the gate, and Tom’s heart gave a great bound.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这时，又一件小裙子从门口进来了，汤姆的心一下子跳得好快。

paragraphs.en: The next instant he was out, and “going on” like an Indian; yelling, laughing, chasing boys, jumping over the fence at risk of life and limb, throwing handsprings, standing on his head—doing all the heroic things he could conceive of, and keeping a furtive eye out, all the while, to see if Becky Thatcher was noticing.
paragraphs.cn: 下一秒，他就冲了出去，像个印第安人一样“疯”起来！他大喊大叫，哈哈大笑，追着小男孩跑，还冒着危险跳过围栏，又翻跟头，又倒立——做了所有他觉得很酷的事情。不过，他一直偷偷地看，看贝琪·撒切尔有没有注意到他。

paragraphs.en: But she seemed to be unconscious of it all; she never looked.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，她好像什么都不知道，一眼都没看他。

paragraphs.en: Could it be possible that she was not aware that he was there?
paragraphs.cn: 难道她不知道他在这里吗？

paragraphs.en: He carried his exploits to her immediate vicinity; came war-whooping around, snatched a boy’s cap, hurled it to the roof of the schoolhouse, broke through a group of boys, tumbling them in every direction, and fell sprawling, himself, under Becky’s nose, almost upsetting her—and she turned, with her nose in the air, and he heard her say: “Mf! some people think they’re mighty smart—always showing off!”
paragraphs.cn: 他把自己的“表演”弄到了她旁边；他大叫着跑过来，抢了一个小男孩的帽子，扔到学校屋顶上。他又冲进一群男孩里，把他们都撞倒了，自己也摔倒在贝琪的鼻子前面，差点撞到她。她转过身，抬着头，鼻子翘得高高的，他听到她说：“哼！有些人觉得自己可厉害了——老是喜欢表现！”

paragraphs.en: Tom’s cheeks burned.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆的脸一下子红了。

paragraphs.en: He gathered himself up and sneaked off, crushed and crestfallen.
paragraphs.cn: 他站起来，偷偷地走了，心里又难过又失望。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s mind was made up now.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆现在决定了。

paragraphs.en: He was gloomy and desperate.
paragraphs.cn: 他很沮丧，心里也很绝望。

paragraphs.en: He was a forsaken, friendless boy, he said; nobody loved him; when they found out what they had driven him to, perhaps they would be sorry; he had tried to do right and get along, but they would not let him; since nothing would do them but to be rid of him, let it be so; and let them blame _him_ for the consequences—why shouldn’t they?
paragraphs.cn: 他说他是个被大家抛弃、没有朋友的小男孩；没有人喜欢他。等他们知道把他逼成什么样了，也许会后悔吧。他努力想做好孩子，好好跟人相处，可他们不让他这样。既然他们只想赶走他，那就随他们吧。让他们怪他做错事好了——为什么不呢？

paragraphs.en: What right had the friendless to complain?
paragraphs.cn: 没有朋友的人，有什么好抱怨的呢？

paragraphs.en: Yes, they had forced him to it at last: he would lead a life of crime.
paragraphs.cn: 是啊，他们最后还是把他逼到了这一步：他要去做坏事了。

paragraphs.en: There was no choice.
paragraphs.cn: 没办法了。

paragraphs.en: By this time he was far down Meadow Lane, and the bell for school to “take up” tinkled faintly upon his ear.
paragraphs.cn: 这时候，他已经走到草地巷很远的地方了。上课的铃声，轻轻地传到他的耳朵里。

paragraphs.en: He sobbed, now, to think he should never, never hear that old familiar sound any more—it was very hard, but it was forced on him; since he was driven out into the cold world, he must submit—but he forgave them.
paragraphs.cn: 他哭着想，再也听不到那个熟悉的声音了。这太难了，但他没办法。他被赶了出来，只能认命。不过，他还是原谅了他们。

paragraphs.en: Then the sobs came thick and fast.
paragraphs.cn: 他哭得更厉害了，一声接一声。

paragraphs.en: Just at this point he met his soul’s sworn comrade, Joe Harper—hard-eyed, and with evidently a great and dismal purpose in his heart.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这时，他遇到了最好的朋友 乔·哈珀。乔·哈珀 眼神亮亮的，心里好像藏着一个大大的、有点伤心的计划。

paragraphs.en: Plainly here were “two souls with but a single thought.”
paragraphs.cn: 看来他们两个人的想法一样。

paragraphs.en: Tom, wiping his eyes with his sleeve, began to blubber out something about a resolution to escape from hard usage and lack of sympathy at home by roaming abroad into the great world never to return; and ended by hoping that Joe would not forget him.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 用袖子擦着眼睛，哭着说他决定要离家出走。因为家里对他不好，也没人关心他。他要去外面的大世界闯荡，再也不回来了。最后，他希望乔不要忘记他。

paragraphs.en: But it transpired that this was a request which Joe had just been going to make of Tom, and had come to hunt him up for that purpose.
paragraphs.cn: 但原来，乔也正想对 汤姆 说同样的话。他就是来找 汤姆 说这件事的。

paragraphs.en: His mother had whipped him for drinking some cream which he had never tasted and knew nothing about; it was plain that she was tired of him and wished him to go; if she felt that way, there was nothing for him to do but succumb; he hoped she would be happy, and never regret having driven her poor boy out into the unfeeling world to suffer and die.
paragraphs.cn: 他妈妈打了他，因为他喝了奶油。可他根本没喝过，也不知道这回事。看来妈妈是烦他了，想让他走。既然她这样想，他只能认命了。他希望妈妈会开心，永远不要后悔把她可怜的孩子赶出去受苦。

paragraphs.en: As the two boys walked sorrowing along, they made a new compact to stand by each other and be brothers and never separate till death relieved them of their troubles.
paragraphs.cn: 两个小男孩伤心地走着，他们定了一个新约定。他们要互相帮助，像亲兄弟一样，永远不分开，直到他们的烦恼都消失。

paragraphs.en: Then they began to lay their plans.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他们开始商量计划。

paragraphs.en: Joe was for being a hermit, and living on crusts in a remote cave, and dying, some time, of cold and want and grief; but after listening to Tom, he conceded that there were some conspicuous advantages about a life of crime, and so he consented to be a pirate.
paragraphs.cn: 乔想当一个隐士，住在很远的洞穴里，吃着硬面包，最后因为又冷又饿又伤心而死掉。但听了 汤姆 的话后，他觉得当坏蛋也有很多好处。所以他同意当一个海盗。

paragraphs.en: Three miles below St. Petersburg, at a point where the Mississippi River was a trifle over a mile wide, there was a long, narrow, wooded island, with a shallow bar at the head of it, and this offered well as a rendezvous.
paragraphs.cn: 离 圣彼得斯堡 三英里远，在 密西西比 河宽一点点超过一英里的地方，有一个又长又窄、长满了树的小岛。岛的一头有片很浅的沙滩。这个地方很适合作为他们的碰头地点。

paragraphs.en: It was not inhabited; it lay far over toward the further shore, abreast a dense and almost wholly unpeopled forest.
paragraphs.cn: 岛上没有人住。它靠近河的对岸，对岸是一片茂密、几乎没人住的森林。

paragraphs.en: So Jackson’s Island was chosen.
paragraphs.cn: 所以，他们就选了杰克逊岛。

paragraphs.en: Who were to be the subjects of their piracies was a matter that did not occur to them.
paragraphs.cn: 至于他们要去打劫谁，他们根本没想过这个问题。

paragraphs.en: Then they hunted up Huckleberry Finn, and he joined them promptly, for all careers were one to him; he was indifferent.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他们去找 哈克贝利·费恩，哈克贝利·费恩 立刻就加入了他们。因为对他来说，做什么都一样，他一点也不在乎。

paragraphs.en: They presently separated to meet at a lonely spot on the river-bank two miles above the village at the favorite hour—which was midnight.
paragraphs.cn: 他们分开了，约定在村子上面两英里远的一个河边小角落见面，在他们最喜欢的时间——半夜。

paragraphs.en: There was a small log raft there which they meant to capture.
paragraphs.cn: 那里有一个小小的木头筏子，他们想把它弄到手。

paragraphs.en: Each would bring hooks and lines, and such provision as he could steal in the most dark and mysterious way—as became outlaws.
paragraphs.cn: 每个人都要带上鱼钩和鱼线，还要用最神秘的方式，偷来一些吃的东西，就像那些亡命之徒一样。

paragraphs.en: And before the afternoon was done, they had all managed to enjoy the sweet glory of spreading the fact that pretty soon the town would “hear something.”
paragraphs.cn: 傍晚还没到，他们就开心地到处说，很快镇上就会“听到什么大消息了”。

paragraphs.en: All who got this vague hint were cautioned to “be mum and wait.”
paragraphs.cn: 那些听到一点点消息的人，都被提醒要“保密，等着看”。

paragraphs.en: About midnight Tom arrived with a boiled ham and a few trifles, and stopped in a dense undergrowth on a small bluff overlooking the meeting-place.
paragraphs.cn: 大概半夜的时候，汤姆 带着一个煮熟的火腿和一些小东西来了。他在一个小山坡上，一片茂密的灌木丛里停了下来，那里能看到他们约定的地方。

paragraphs.en: It was starlight, and very still.
paragraphs.cn: 天上都是星星，四周非常安静。

paragraphs.en: The mighty river lay like an ocean at rest.
paragraphs.cn: 宽阔的河水像睡着了的大海一样。

paragraphs.en: Tom listened a moment, but no sound disturbed the quiet.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 听了一会儿，没有声音打破这份安静。

paragraphs.en: Then he gave a low, distinct whistle.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他轻轻地、清楚地吹了一声口哨。

paragraphs.en: It was answered from under the bluff.
paragraphs.cn: 小山坡下面有人回应了他。

paragraphs.en: Tom whistled twice more; these signals were answered in the same way.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 又吹了两声口哨，对方也同样回应了他。

paragraphs.en: Then a guarded voice said:
paragraphs.cn: 然后，一个小心翼翼的声音说：

paragraphs.en: “Who goes there?”
paragraphs.cn: “谁在那里？”

paragraphs.en: “Tom Sawyer, the Black Avenger of the Spanish Main.
paragraphs.cn: “我是 汤姆·索亚，加勒比海的黑衣复仇者。”

paragraphs.en: Name your names.”
paragraphs.cn: 说出你们的名字。

paragraphs.en: “Huck Finn the Red-Handed, and Joe Harper the Terror of the Seas.”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克 红手芬恩，还有 乔·哈珀 海上大魔王。”

paragraphs.en: Tom had furnished these titles, from his favorite literature.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 从他最喜欢的故事书里，给他们起了这些名字。

paragraphs.en: “’Tis well.
paragraphs.cn: “好极了。

paragraphs.en: Give the countersign.”
paragraphs.cn: 说出暗号吧。”

paragraphs.en: Two hoarse whispers delivered the same awful word simultaneously to the brooding night:
paragraphs.cn: 两个沙哑的声音，同时在黑夜里悄悄说出了那个可怕的词：

paragraphs.en: “_Blood_!”
Then Tom tumbled his ham over the bluff and let himself down after it, tearing both skin and clothes to some extent in the effort.
paragraphs.cn: 然后 汤姆 把他的火腿推下悬崖，自己也跟着滑了下去，他把皮肤和衣服都蹭破了一些。

paragraphs.en: There was an easy, comfortable path along the shore under the bluff, but it lacked the advantages of difficulty and danger so valued by a pirate.
paragraphs.cn: 悬崖下面有条小路，走起来很方便，也很舒服。可是海盗们喜欢冒险，那条路一点也不难，也不危险。

paragraphs.en: The Terror of the Seas had brought a side of bacon, and had about worn himself out with getting it there.
paragraphs.cn: 海上大魔王带了一大块培根肉，为了把它弄过来，他都快累坏了。

paragraphs.en: Finn the Red-Handed had stolen a skillet and a quantity of half-cured leaf tobacco, and had also brought a few corn-cobs to make pipes with.
paragraphs.cn: 红手芬恩偷了一个平底锅和一些半干的烟叶，还带了几个玉米棒子做烟斗。

paragraphs.en: But none of the pirates smoked or “chewed” but himself.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，除了他自己，别的海盗都不抽烟，也不“嚼烟叶”。

paragraphs.en: The Black Avenger of the Spanish Main said it would never do to start without some fire.
paragraphs.cn: 加勒比海黑侠说，没有火可不行，没法开始。

paragraphs.en: That was a wise thought; matches were hardly known there in that day.
paragraphs.cn: 这个主意真聪明！那时候，火柴可不常见呢。

paragraphs.en: They saw a fire smouldering upon a great raft a hundred yards above, and they went stealthily thither and helped themselves to a chunk.
paragraphs.cn: 他们看到上面一百码远的大木筏上，有一堆火正在慢慢烧着。他们偷偷摸摸地走过去，拿了一块火炭。

paragraphs.en: They made an imposing adventure of it, saying, “Hist!” every now and then, and suddenly halting with finger on lip; moving with hands on imaginary dagger-hilts; and giving orders in dismal whispers that if “the foe” stirred, to “let him have it to the hilt,” because “dead men tell no tales.”
paragraphs.cn: 他们把这件事变成了一场很棒的冒险。他们时不时地“嘘！”一声，突然停下来，把手指放在嘴唇上；手放在想象中的匕首柄上；用低沉的耳语下命令说，如果“敌人”动了，就“捅他个透心凉”，因为“死人不会说话”。

paragraphs.en: They knew well enough that the raftsmen were all down at the village laying in stores or having a spree, but still that was no excuse for their conducting this thing in an unpiratical way.
paragraphs.cn: 他们很清楚，那些木筏工人都在村子里买东西或者玩乐呢。但是，这也不能成为他们不按海盗方式做事的理由。

paragraphs.en: They shoved off, presently, Tom in command, Huck at the after oar and Joe at the forward.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，他们把木筏推离岸边，汤姆 来指挥，哈克 在船尾划桨，乔在船头划桨。

paragraphs.en: Tom stood amidships, gloomy-browed, and with folded arms, and gave his orders in a low, stern whisper:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 站在船中间，皱着眉头，抱着手臂，用低沉、严肃的声音下命令：

paragraphs.en: “Luff, and bring her to the wind!”
paragraphs.cn: “迎风转向，把船头对着风！”

paragraphs.en: “Aye-aye, sir!”
paragraphs.cn: “遵命，长官！”

paragraphs.en: “Steady, steady-y-y-y!”
paragraphs.cn: “稳住，稳住-住-住-住！”

paragraphs.en: “Steady it is, sir!”
paragraphs.cn: “已经稳住了，长官！”

paragraphs.en: “Let her go off a point!”
paragraphs.cn: “让船偏离一点方向！”

paragraphs.en: “Point it is, sir!”
paragraphs.cn: “已经偏了，长官！”

paragraphs.en: As the boys steadily and monotonously drove the raft toward mid-stream it was no doubt understood that these orders were given only for “style,” and were not intended to mean anything in particular.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们稳定又单调地把木筏划向河中央。大家肯定都明白，这些命令只是为了“耍酷”，并没有特别的意思。

paragraphs.en: “What sail’s she carrying?”
paragraphs.cn: “船上挂着什么帆？”

paragraphs.en: “Courses, tops’ls, and flying-jib, sir.”
paragraphs.cn: “主帆、上桅帆和飞前帆，长官。”

paragraphs.en: “Send the r’yals up!
paragraphs.cn: “把顶桅帆升起来！

paragraphs.en: Lay out aloft, there, half a dozen of ye—foretopmaststuns’l!
paragraphs.cn: 上去几个人——挂前顶桅副帆！”

paragraphs.en: Lively, now!”
paragraphs.cn: 大家动起来！

paragraphs.en: “Aye-aye, sir!”
paragraphs.cn: “是，长官！”

paragraphs.en: “Shake out that maintogalans’l!
paragraphs.cn: “把主桅顶帆张开！

paragraphs.en: Sheets and braces!
paragraphs.cn: 拉好帆索！

paragraphs.en: _now_ my hearties!”
paragraphs.cn: 现在，伙计们！”

paragraphs.en: “Aye-aye, sir!”
paragraphs.cn: “是，长官！”

paragraphs.en: “Hellum-a-lee—hard a port!
paragraphs.cn: “船舵向左，打到底！

paragraphs.en: Stand by to meet her when she comes!
paragraphs.cn: 准备好，等船转过来！

paragraphs.en: Port, port!
paragraphs.cn: 左边，左边！

paragraphs.en: _Now_, men!
paragraphs.cn: 现在，伙计们！

paragraphs.en: With a will!
paragraphs.cn: 要快，要用力！

paragraphs.en: Stead-y-y-y!”
“Steady it is, sir!”
paragraphs.cn: “稳住了，长官！”

paragraphs.en: The raft drew beyond the middle of the river; the boys pointed her head right, and then lay on their oars.
paragraphs.cn: 木筏过了河中间；男孩们把筏头朝右边，然后就休息了，不划桨了。

paragraphs.en: The river was not high, so there was not more than a two or three mile current.
paragraphs.cn: 河水不深，所以水流不快，只有两三英里的速度。

paragraphs.en: Hardly a word was said during the next three-quarters of an hour.
paragraphs.cn: 接下来的四十五分钟里，他们几乎没说话。

paragraphs.en: Now the raft was passing before the distant town.
paragraphs.cn: 现在木筏正从远处的镇子前经过。

paragraphs.en: Two or three glimmering lights showed where it lay, peacefully sleeping, beyond the vague vast sweep of star-gemmed water, unconscious of the tremendous event that was happening.
paragraphs.cn: 只有两三点闪烁的灯光，表明那里是一个小镇，正在安静地睡觉。它不知道，在星光点点的广阔水面上，正发生着一件大事。

paragraphs.en: The Black Avenger stood still with folded arms, “looking his last” upon the scene of his former joys and his later sufferings, and wishing “she” could see him now, abroad on the wild sea, facing peril and death with dauntless heart, going to his doom with a grim smile on his lips.
paragraphs.cn: 黑侠客抱着胳膊，一动不动地站着，最后看了一眼他曾经开心和痛苦的地方。他多希望‘她’能看到他现在在大海上，勇敢面对危险和死亡，脸上带着坚定的笑容。

paragraphs.en: It was but a small strain on his imagination to remove Jackson’s Island beyond eye-shot of the village, and so he “looked his last” with a broken and satisfied heart.
paragraphs.cn: 他想象杰克逊岛已经离村子很远了，心里有点难过，又有点满意，这样就“最后看了一眼”。

paragraphs.en: The other pirates were looking their last, too; and they all looked so long that they came near letting the current drift them out of the range of the island.
paragraphs.cn: 其他的海盗也在最后看一眼。他们看了很久，差点就被水流带到离岛很远的地方去了。

paragraphs.en: But they discovered the danger in time, and made shift to avert it.
paragraphs.cn: 但他们很快发现了危险，并及时把它化解了。

paragraphs.en: About two o’clock in the morning the raft grounded on the bar two hundred yards above the head of the island, and they waded back and forth until they had landed their freight.
paragraphs.cn: 凌晨两点左右，木筏在小岛上游两百码处的一个沙滩上停住了。他们来回趟水，把所有的东西都搬到了岸上。

paragraphs.en: Part of the little raft’s belongings consisted of an old sail, and this they spread over a nook in the bushes for a tent to shelter their provisions; but they themselves would sleep in the open air in good weather, as became outlaws.
paragraphs.cn: 小木筏上有些东西，其中一块旧帆被他们铺在灌木丛里，搭成一个小帐篷，用来放食物。但他们自己，天气好的时候，就像野外的人一样，直接睡在外面。

paragraphs.en: They built a fire against the side of a great log twenty or thirty steps within the sombre depths of the forest, and then cooked some bacon in the frying-pan for supper, and used up half of the corn “pone” stock they had brought.
paragraphs.cn: 他们在森林深处，离一个大木头二三十步远的地方生了一堆火。然后用平底锅煎了些培根当晚餐，还吃掉了一半带来的玉米面包。

paragraphs.en: It seemed glorious sport to be feasting in that wild, free way in the virgin forest of an unexplored and uninhabited island, far from the haunts of men, and they said they never would return to civilization.
paragraphs.cn: 在这个没有人去过的岛上，原始森林里，离人群很远，这样自由自在地大吃一顿，真是太好玩了！他们说再也不回城市生活了。

paragraphs.en: The climbing fire lit up their faces and threw its ruddy glare upon the pillared tree-trunks of their forest temple, and upon the varnished foliage and festooning vines.
paragraphs.cn: 跳动的火光照亮了他们的脸。火光还把红色的光芒投向了森林里那些像柱子一样高大的树干上，也照亮了闪亮的树叶和垂下来的藤蔓。

paragraphs.en: When the last crisp slice of bacon was gone, and the last allowance of corn pone devoured, the boys stretched themselves out on the grass, filled with contentment.
paragraphs.cn: 最后一片脆培根和最后一块玉米饼都吃光后，男孩们心满意足地躺在草地上，伸了个懒腰。

paragraphs.en: They could have found a cooler place, but they would not deny themselves such a romantic feature as the roasting campfire.
paragraphs.cn: 他们本来可以找一个更凉快的地方，但他们不想错过围着篝火取暖这种浪漫的感觉。

paragraphs.en: “_Ain’t_ it gay?” said Joe.
paragraphs.cn: “是不是很棒？”乔说。

paragraphs.en: “It’s _nuts_!” said Tom. “What would the boys say if they could see us?”
paragraphs.cn: “这太棒了！”汤姆说。“要是男孩们看到我们，他们会说什么呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Say?
paragraphs.cn: “说什么？

paragraphs.en: Well, they’d just die to be here—hey, Hucky!”
paragraphs.cn: 他们肯定会特别想来这儿——嘿，哈克！”

paragraphs.en: “I reckon so,” said Huckleberry; “anyways, I’m suited.
paragraphs.cn: “我想也是。”哈克贝利说；“反正，我很满意。

paragraphs.en: I don’t want nothing better’n this.
paragraphs.cn: 我觉得现在这样最好了。

paragraphs.en: I don’t ever get enough to eat, gen’ally—and here they can’t come and pick at a feller and bullyrag him so.”
paragraphs.cn: 我平时总吃不饱——在这儿，没人能来挑剔我，欺负我了。”

paragraphs.en: “It’s just the life for me,” said Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “这正是我想要的生活，”汤姆说。

paragraphs.en: “You don’t have to get up, mornings, and you don’t have to go to school, and wash, and all that blame foolishness.
paragraphs.cn: “你不用早上起床，也不用去上学，不用洗漱，那些烦人的事儿都不用做。

paragraphs.en: You see a pirate don’t have to do _anything_, Joe, when he’s ashore, but a hermit _he_ has to be praying considerable, and then he don’t have any fun, anyway, all by himself that way.”
paragraphs.cn: 你看，乔，海盗上岸后什么都不用做，但是隐士呢，他得不停地祷告，而且一个人在那儿，一点儿也不好玩。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh yes, that’s so,” said Joe, “but I hadn’t thought much about it, you know.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，对，是这样。”乔说，“不过我之前没怎么想过这事儿，你知道的。

paragraphs.en: I’d a good deal rather be a pirate, now that I’ve tried it.”
paragraphs.cn: 既然我都试过了，我现在宁愿当个海盗。”

paragraphs.en: “You see,” said Tom, “people don’t go much on hermits, nowadays, like they used to in old times, but a pirate’s always respected.
paragraphs.cn: “你看，”汤姆说，“像以前那样，现在的人不怎么喜欢隐士了，但是海盗总是受人尊敬的。

paragraphs.en: And a hermit’s got to sleep on the hardest place he can find, and put sackcloth and ashes on his head, and stand out in the rain, and—”
paragraphs.cn: 而且隐士还得睡在能找到的最硬的地方，把粗麻布和灰尘放在头上，还要站在雨里，然后——”

paragraphs.en: “What does he put sackcloth and ashes on his head for?” inquired Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “他为什么要戴粗麻布和灰尘在头上？”哈克问。

paragraphs.en: “I dono.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道。

paragraphs.en: But they’ve _got_ to do it.
paragraphs.cn: 但他们就是必须这么做。

paragraphs.en: Hermits always do.
paragraphs.cn: 隐士总是这样。

paragraphs.en: You’d have to do that if you was a hermit.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果你是隐士，你也得这么做。”

paragraphs.en: “Dern’d if I would,” said Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “我才不呢！”哈克说。

paragraphs.en: “Well, what would you do?”
paragraphs.cn: “那，你会怎么做呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I dono.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道。

paragraphs.en: But I wouldn’t do that.”
paragraphs.cn: 但我不会那么做。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, Huck, you’d _have_ to.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，哈克，你必须这么做啊。

paragraphs.en: How’d you get around it?”
paragraphs.cn: 你怎么能躲开呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, I just wouldn’t stand it.
paragraphs.cn: “哼，我才不受那份罪呢。

paragraphs.en: I’d run away.”
paragraphs.cn: 我会跑掉的。”

paragraphs.en: “Run away!
paragraphs.cn: “跑掉！

paragraphs.en: Well, you _would_ be a nice old slouch of a hermit.
paragraphs.cn: 哼，那你可就不是个合格的隐士了。

paragraphs.en: You’d be a disgrace.”
paragraphs.cn: 你会让人瞧不起的。”

paragraphs.en: The Red-Handed made no response, being better employed.
paragraphs.cn: “红手”没有回答，他正忙着更重要的事。

paragraphs.en: He had finished gouging out a cob, and now he fitted a weed stem to it, loaded it with tobacco, and was pressing a coal to the charge and blowing a cloud of fragrant smoke—he was in the full bloom of luxurious contentment.
paragraphs.cn: 他做好了烟斗，装上烟草。他点着烟，喷出香喷喷的烟雾。他非常非常开心。

paragraphs.en: The other pirates envied him this majestic vice, and secretly resolved to acquire it shortly.
paragraphs.cn: 其他海盗好羡慕他这样。他们都偷偷决定，很快也要学会抽烟。

paragraphs.en: Presently Huck said:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，哈克说：

paragraphs.en: “What does pirates have to do?”
paragraphs.cn: “海盗都要做什么呀？”

paragraphs.en: Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, they have just a bully time—take ships and burn them, and get the money and bury it in awful places in their island where there’s ghosts and things to watch it, and kill everybody in the ships—make ’em walk a plank.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，他们可开心了！他们抢船，把船烧掉。他们拿走钱，埋在岛上可怕的地方。那里有鬼看着钱。他们还会杀死船上所有的人，让他们走跳板。”

paragraphs.en: “And they carry the women to the island,” said Joe; “they don’t kill the women.”
paragraphs.cn: “他们还会把女人带到岛上，”乔说，“他们不杀女人。”

paragraphs.en: “No,” assented Tom, “they don’t kill the women—they’re too noble.
paragraphs.cn: “对，”汤姆同意说，“他们不杀女人。他们太善良了。

paragraphs.en: And the women’s always beautiful, too.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且女人都特别漂亮。”

paragraphs.en: “And don’t they wear the bulliest clothes!
paragraphs.cn: “他们穿的衣服可真棒！

paragraphs.en: Oh no!
paragraphs.cn: 哦，不是！

paragraphs.en: All gold and silver and di’monds,” said Joe, with enthusiasm.
paragraphs.cn: 都是金子、银子和钻石！”乔很兴奋地说。

paragraphs.en: “Who?” said Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “谁？”哈克问。

paragraphs.en: “Why, the pirates.”
paragraphs.cn: “就是海盗啊。”

paragraphs.en: Huck scanned his own clothing forlornly.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克伤心地看了看自己的衣服。

paragraphs.en: “I reckon I ain’t dressed fitten for a pirate,” said he, with a regretful pathos in his voice; “but I ain’t got none but these.”
paragraphs.cn: “我想我这身衣服不像海盗穿的，”他有点难过地说，“可是我只有这些衣服了。”

paragraphs.en: But the other boys told him the fine clothes would come fast enough, after they should have begun their adventures.
paragraphs.cn: 但其他男孩告诉他，等他们开始冒险后，很快就会有好看的衣服了。

paragraphs.en: They made him understand that his poor rags would do to begin with, though it was customary for wealthy pirates to start with a proper wardrobe.
paragraphs.cn: 他们让他明白，虽然有钱的海盗一开始就有漂亮的衣服，但他这些破烂衣服也够用了。

paragraphs.en: Gradually their talk died out and drowsiness began to steal upon the eyelids of the little waifs.
paragraphs.cn: 他们的话渐渐少了，困意慢慢爬上了这些小流浪儿的眼皮。

paragraphs.en: The pipe dropped from the fingers of the Red-Handed, and he slept the sleep of the conscience-free and the weary.
paragraphs.cn: 烟斗从“红手”的手里滑落，他睡着了。他睡得又安心又累。

paragraphs.en: The Terror of the Seas and the Black Avenger of the Spanish Main had more difficulty in getting to sleep.
paragraphs.cn: “海上恶魔”和“西班牙海的黑色复仇者”更难入睡。

paragraphs.en: They said their prayers inwardly, and lying down, since there was nobody there with authority to make them kneel and recite aloud; in truth, they had a mind not to say them at all, but they were afraid to proceed to such lengths as that, lest they might call down a sudden and special thunderbolt from heaven.
paragraphs.cn: 他们躺着默默地祈祷。因为没人让他们跪着大声念。其实他们不想祈祷，但又怕不说的话，老天爷会突然打雷劈他们。

paragraphs.en: Then at once they reached and hovered upon the imminent verge of sleep—but an intruder came, now, that would not “down.”
paragraphs.cn: 他们快要睡着了，但一个东西突然出现了，怎么也赶不走。

paragraphs.en: It was conscience.
paragraphs.cn: 那是他们的良心。

paragraphs.en: They began to feel a vague fear that they had been doing wrong to run away; and next they thought of the stolen meat, and then the real torture came.
paragraphs.cn: 他们开始有点害怕，觉得跑出来是不对的。接着他们想起了偷来的肉，真正的痛苦就来了。

paragraphs.en: They tried to argue it away by reminding conscience that they had purloined sweetmeats and apples scores of times; but conscience was not to be appeased by such thin plausibilities; it seemed to them, in the end, that there was no getting around the stubborn fact that taking sweetmeats was only “hooking,” while taking bacon and hams and such valuables was plain simple stealing—and there was a command against that in the Bible.
paragraphs.cn: 他们想对良心说，他们以前偷过很多次糖果和苹果。但良心不听他们的话。他们觉得，偷糖果只是“拿”，而偷培根、火腿这些贵重东西就是“偷”。圣经里说了不能偷东西。

paragraphs.en: So they inwardly resolved that so long as they remained in the business, their piracies should not again be sullied with the crime of stealing.
paragraphs.cn: 所以他们心里决定，只要他们还做海盗，就再也不偷东西了。

paragraphs.en: Then conscience granted a truce, and these curiously inconsistent pirates fell peacefully to sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，良心终于放过了他们，这两个有点奇怪的海盗就安心地睡着了。

paragraphs.en: When Tom awoke in the morning, he wondered where he was.
paragraphs.cn: 早上汤姆醒来时，他想：这是哪里呀？

paragraphs.en: He sat up and rubbed his eyes and looked around.
paragraphs.cn: 他坐起来，揉揉眼睛，看了看四周。

paragraphs.en: Then he comprehended.
paragraphs.cn: 然后，他明白了。

paragraphs.en: It was the cool gray dawn, and there was a delicious sense of repose and peace in the deep pervading calm and silence of the woods.
paragraphs.cn: 天亮了，凉凉的，有点灰。森林里很安静，让他觉得很舒服、很平静。

paragraphs.en: Not a leaf stirred; not a sound obtruded upon great Nature’s meditation.
paragraphs.cn: 一片叶子都没动，没有一点声音打扰大自然。

paragraphs.en: Beaded dewdrops stood upon the leaves and grasses.
paragraphs.cn: 晶莹的露珠挂在叶子和草上。

paragraphs.en: A white layer of ashes covered the fire, and a thin blue breath of smoke rose straight into the air.
paragraphs.cn: 火上盖了一层白白的灰，一缕细细的蓝色烟雾笔直地飘向天空。

paragraphs.en: Joe and Huck still slept.
paragraphs.cn: 乔和 哈克 还在睡觉。

paragraphs.en: Now, far away in the woods a bird called; another answered; presently the hammering of a woodpecker was heard.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，森林深处一只鸟叫了一声，另一只回应了。很快，又听到了啄木鸟敲打树干的声音。

paragraphs.en: Gradually the cool dim gray of the morning whitened, and as gradually sounds multiplied and life manifested itself.
paragraphs.cn: 凉凉的灰色清晨慢慢变亮了，声音越来越多，万物都活了过来。

paragraphs.en: The marvel of Nature shaking off sleep and going to work unfolded itself to the musing boy.
paragraphs.cn: 大自然从睡梦中醒来，开始活动了，男孩看着，觉得很神奇。

paragraphs.en: A little green worm came crawling over a dewy leaf, lifting two-thirds of his body into the air from time to time and “sniffing around,” then proceeding again—for he was measuring, Tom said; and when the worm approached him, of its own accord, he sat as still as a stone, with his hopes rising and falling, by turns, as the creature still came toward him or seemed inclined to go elsewhere; and when at last it considered a painful moment with its curved body in the air and then came decisively down upon Tom’s leg and began a journey over him, his whole heart was glad—for that meant that he was going to have a new suit of clothes—without the shadow of a doubt a gaudy piratical uniform.
paragraphs.cn: 一条绿色的小虫子爬过一片带露水的叶子。它时不时抬起身体，好像在“闻来闻去”，然后又继续爬。汤姆说，它在量尺寸呢。当小虫子自己爬向他时，他像石头一样一动不动。小虫子有时朝他爬来，有时又好像要爬去别的地方，他的心情也一会儿高兴，一会儿紧张。最后，小虫子弯着身子在空中想了一会儿，然后坚定地爬到了 汤姆 的腿上，开始在他身上旅行。他心里可高兴了——因为这意味着他会有一套新衣服，肯定是一套很帅的海盗服！

paragraphs.en: Now a procession of ants appeared, from nowhere in particular, and went about their labors; one struggled manfully by with a dead spider five times as big as itself in its arms, and lugged it straight up a tree-trunk.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，一队蚂蚁不知道从哪里冒出来，开始干活了。有一只蚂蚁抱着一只比自己大五倍的死蜘蛛，很用力地把它拖上树干。

paragraphs.en: A brown spotted lady-bug climbed the dizzy height of a grass blade, and Tom bent down close to it and said, “Lady-bug, lady-bug, fly away home, your house is on fire, your children’s alone,” and she took wing and went off to see about it—which did not surprise the boy, for he knew of old that this insect was credulous about conflagrations, and he had practised upon its simplicity more than once.
paragraphs.cn: 一只棕色斑点的瓢虫爬到高高的草叶上。汤姆 弯下身子，凑近它说：“瓢虫瓢虫飞回家，你的房子着火了，你的孩子孤单了。” 瓢虫真的飞走了，去看个究竟。男孩一点也不惊讶，因为他早就知道这种小虫子很容易相信着火的事，他以前就用这招骗过它好几次了。

paragraphs.en: A tumblebug came next, heaving sturdily at its ball, and Tom touched the creature, to see it shut its legs against its body and pretend to be dead.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，一只屎壳郎来了，它很用力地推着它的粪球。汤姆 碰了碰它，它就把腿缩起来，假装死了。

paragraphs.en: The birds were fairly rioting by this time.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，鸟儿们已经叽叽喳喳地叫个不停了。

paragraphs.en: A catbird, the Northern mocker, lit in a tree over Tom’s head, and trilled out her imitations of her neighbors in a rapture of enjoyment; then a shrill jay swept down, a flash of blue flame, and stopped on a twig almost within the boy’s reach, cocked his head to one side and eyed the strangers with a consuming curiosity; a gray squirrel and a big fellow of the “fox” kind came skurrying along, sitting up at intervals to inspect and chatter at the boys, for the wild things had probably never seen a human being before and scarcely knew whether to be afraid or not.
paragraphs.cn: 一只反舌鸟（它会学别的鸟叫）飞到 汤姆 头顶的树上，高兴地学着邻居们的叫声，唱起歌来。接着，一只蓝色的松鸦像一道蓝光一样飞下来，停在男孩几乎能碰到的树枝上。它歪着头，好奇地看着这些陌生人。一只灰松鼠和一只像狐狸一样的大动物跑了过来，时不时停下来，看看男孩们，还吱吱喳喳地叫。这些小动物可能从来没见过人，都不知道该害怕还是不害怕呢。

paragraphs.en: All Nature was wide awake and stirring, now; long lances of sunlight pierced down through the dense foliage far and near, and a few butterflies came fluttering upon the scene.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，大自然的所有生物都醒了，都动起来了。远近的阳光像长矛一样，穿过茂密的树叶照下来。几只蝴蝶飞舞着出现了。

paragraphs.en: Tom stirred up the other pirates and they all clattered away with a shout, and in a minute or two were stripped and chasing after and tumbling over each other in the shallow limpid water of the white sandbar.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 叫醒了其他的小海盗们，他们大叫一声跑开了。一两分钟后，他们就脱光了衣服，在白色沙洲上清澈的浅水里互相追逐打闹。

paragraphs.en: They felt no longing for the little village sleeping in the distance beyond the majestic waste of water.
paragraphs.cn: 他们一点也不想念远处那片宽广水面后，正在睡觉的小村庄。

paragraphs.en: A vagrant current or a slight rise in the river had carried off their raft, but this only gratified them, since its going was something like burning the bridge between them and civilization.
paragraphs.cn: 不知道是河水变急了，还是水位升高了，把他们的木筏冲走了。但他们却很高兴，因为木筏冲走了，就像烧掉了他们和文明世界的桥梁一样。

paragraphs.en: They came back to camp wonderfully refreshed, glad-hearted, and ravenous; and they soon had the camp-fire blazing up again.
paragraphs.cn: 他们回到营地，感觉舒服极了，心里很高兴，肚子也饿扁了。很快，他们又让篝火熊熊燃烧起来。

paragraphs.en: Huck found a spring of clear cold water close by, and the boys made cups of broad oak or hickory leaves, and felt that water, sweetened with such a wildwood charm as that, would be a good enough substitute for coffee.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 在附近找到了一股清澈冰凉的山泉水。男孩们用宽大的橡树叶或山核桃叶做了杯子。他们觉得，有这样特别的野外风味，这水喝起来比咖啡还要好喝。

paragraphs.en: While Joe was slicing bacon for breakfast, Tom and Huck asked him to hold on a minute; they stepped to a promising nook in the river-bank and threw in their lines; almost immediately they had reward.
paragraphs.cn: 乔正在切培根准备早餐时，汤姆 和 哈克 叫他等一下。他们走到河岸边一个看起来不错的小角落，把鱼线抛了下去。几乎立刻就有了收获。

paragraphs.en: Joe had not had time to get impatient before they were back again with some handsome bass, a couple of sun-perch and a small catfish—provisions enough for quite a family.
paragraphs.cn: 乔还没来得及不耐烦，他们就带着几条漂亮的鲈鱼、两条太阳鱼和一条小鲶鱼回来了——这些鱼足够一家人吃了。

paragraphs.en: They fried the fish with the bacon, and were astonished; for no fish had ever seemed so delicious before.
paragraphs.cn: 他们把鱼和培根一起煎，吃惊极了，因为从来没有鱼这么好吃过。

paragraphs.en: They did not know that the quicker a fresh-water fish is on the fire after he is caught the better he is; and they reflected little upon what a sauce open-air sleeping, open-air exercise, bathing, and a large ingredient of hunger make, too.
paragraphs.cn: 他们不知道，淡水鱼抓上来后越快煮就越好吃。他们也没想到，在野外睡觉、玩耍、洗澡，再加上肚子很饿，这些都是最好的调味料呢。

paragraphs.en: They lay around in the shade, after breakfast, while Huck had a smoke, and then went off through the woods on an exploring expedition.
paragraphs.cn: 早餐后，他们躺在树荫下休息了一会儿，然后就穿过森林去探险了。

paragraphs.en: They tramped gayly along, over decaying logs, through tangled underbrush, among solemn monarchs of the forest, hung from their crowns to the ground with a drooping regalia of grape-vines.
paragraphs.cn: 他们高兴地走着，跨过腐烂的木头，穿过缠绕在一起的灌木丛，走在森林里高大的老树中间，那些树上挂满了像藤蔓一样垂下来的葡萄。

paragraphs.en: Now and then they came upon snug nooks carpeted with grass and jeweled with flowers.
paragraphs.cn: 他们不时会遇到一些舒服的小角落，那里铺着草地，点缀着花朵。

paragraphs.en: They found plenty of things to be delighted with, but nothing to be astonished at.
paragraphs.cn: 他们发现了许多让他们高兴的东西，但没有让他们特别吃惊的东西。

paragraphs.en: They discovered that the island was about three miles long and a quarter of a mile wide, and that the shore it lay closest to was only separated from it by a narrow channel hardly two hundred yards wide.
paragraphs.cn: 他们发现这个岛大约有三英里长，四分之一英里宽。离岛最近的岸边，中间只隔着一条不到两百码宽的狭窄水道。

paragraphs.en: They took a swim about every hour, so it was close upon the middle of the afternoon when they got back to camp.
paragraphs.cn: 他们差不多每个小时都去游一次泳，所以快到下午才回到营地。

paragraphs.en: They were too hungry to stop to fish, but they fared sumptuously upon cold ham, and then threw themselves down in the shade to talk.
paragraphs.cn: 他们太饿了，没去钓鱼，而是大口吃着冷火腿，然后就躺在树荫下聊天。

paragraphs.en: But the talk soon began to drag, and then died.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，他们很快就聊不下去了，变得很安静。

paragraphs.en: The stillness, the solemnity that brooded in the woods, and the sense of loneliness, began to tell upon the spirits of the boys.
paragraphs.cn: 树林里很安静，感觉很严肃，也很孤独，这些让小男孩们的心情变差了。

paragraphs.en: They fell to thinking.
paragraphs.cn: 他们开始想事情。

paragraphs.en: A sort of undefined longing crept upon them.
paragraphs.cn: 他们心里慢慢生出一种说不清的思念。

paragraphs.en: This took dim shape, presently—it was budding homesickness.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，这种感觉变得有点清楚了——原来是想家了。

paragraphs.en: Even Finn the Red-Handed was dreaming of his doorsteps and empty hogsheads.
paragraphs.cn: 连红手芬恩都开始想念他家的台阶和空木桶了。

paragraphs.en: But they were all ashamed of their weakness, and none was brave enough to speak his thought.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，他们都觉得想家是件很弱的事，没有人敢说出自己心里的想法。

paragraphs.en: For some time, now, the boys had been dully conscious of a peculiar sound in the distance, just as one sometimes is of the ticking of a clock which he takes no distinct note of.
paragraphs.cn: 有段时间了，小男孩们隐约觉得远处有奇怪的声音，就像平时听到时钟“嘀嗒”响，却没特别注意一样。

paragraphs.en: But now this mysterious sound became more pronounced, and forced a recognition.
paragraphs.cn: 但现在，这个奇怪的声音更响了，让他们不得不去听清楚。

paragraphs.en: The boys started, glanced at each other, and then each assumed a listening attitude.
paragraphs.cn: 小男孩们吓了一跳，互相看了看，然后都竖起耳朵仔细听。

paragraphs.en: There was a long silence, profound and unbroken; then a deep, sullen boom came floating down out of the distance.
paragraphs.cn: 接着是很长时间的安静，很深很沉。然后，远处传来一声低沉、闷闷的“轰”声。

paragraphs.en: “What is it!” exclaimed Joe, under his breath.
paragraphs.cn: “那是什么？”乔小声地喊道。

paragraphs.en: “I wonder,” said Tom in a whisper.
paragraphs.cn: “我想知道，”汤姆小声地说。

paragraphs.en: “’Tain’t thunder,” said Huckleberry, in an awed tone, “becuz thunder—”
paragraphs.cn: “这不是打雷，”哈克贝利敬畏地说，“因为打雷的话——”

paragraphs.en: “Hark!” said Tom. “Listen—don’t talk.”
paragraphs.cn: “听！”汤姆说，“仔细听——别说话。”

paragraphs.en: They waited a time that seemed an age, and then the same muffled boom troubled the solemn hush.
paragraphs.cn: 他们等了好久，感觉像等了一辈子。然后，那一声闷响又打破了安静。

paragraphs.en: “Let’s go and see.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们去看看吧。”

paragraphs.en: They sprang to their feet and hurried to the shore toward the town.
paragraphs.cn: 他们跳起来，快步跑到岸边，朝小镇那边走。

paragraphs.en: They parted the bushes on the bank and peered out over the water.
paragraphs.cn: 他们拨开岸边的树丛，朝水面上看。

paragraphs.en: The little steam ferry-boat was about a mile below the village, drifting with the current.
paragraphs.cn: 那艘小小的蒸汽渡船，在村子下面一英里左右的地方，正跟着水流漂。

paragraphs.en: Her broad deck seemed crowded with people.
paragraphs.cn: 船上宽宽的甲板上，好像挤满了人。

paragraphs.en: There were a great many skiffs rowing about or floating with the stream in the neighborhood of the ferryboat, but the boys could not determine what the men in them were doing.
paragraphs.cn: 渡船周围有很多小船，有的在划，有的跟着水漂。但小男孩们看不清船上的人在做什么。

paragraphs.en: Presently a great jet of white smoke burst from the ferryboat’s side, and as it expanded and rose in a lazy cloud, that same dull throb of sound was borne to the listeners again.
paragraphs.cn: 突然，渡船旁边冒出一大股白烟，它慢慢散开，变成一朵懒洋洋的云。接着，那闷闷的声音又传到了他们耳边。

paragraphs.en: “I know now!” exclaimed Tom; “somebody’s drownded!”
paragraphs.cn: “我现在知道了！”汤姆喊道，“有人掉到水里了！”

paragraphs.en: “That’s it!” said Huck; “they done that last summer, when Bill Turner got drownded; they shoot a cannon over the water, and that makes him come up to the top.
paragraphs.cn: “没错！”哈克说，“去年夏天比尔·特纳掉到水里时，他们就是这样做的。他们在水上开炮，那样他就会浮上来。

paragraphs.en: Yes, and they take loaves of bread and put quicksilver in ’em and set ’em afloat, and wherever there’s anybody that’s drownded, they’ll float right there and stop.”
paragraphs.cn: 是啊，他们还会拿面包，把水银放进去，再把面包放到水里。哪里有人掉到水里，面包就会漂到哪里停下来。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, I’ve heard about that,” said Joe.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我听说过这事。”乔说。

paragraphs.en: “I wonder what makes the bread do that.”
paragraphs.cn: “我想知道面包为什么会那样。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, it ain’t the bread, so much,” said Tom; “I reckon it’s mostly what they _say_ over it before they start it out.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，重要的不是面包本身，”汤姆说，“我觉得主要是他们在使用面包前，对着它说了些什么。”

paragraphs.en: “But they don’t say anything over it,” said Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “可是他们什么也没说呀，”哈克说。

paragraphs.en: “I’ve seen ’em and they don’t.”
paragraphs.cn: “我看到过，他们没说。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, that’s funny,” said Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，真奇怪，”汤姆说。

paragraphs.en: “But maybe they say it to themselves.
paragraphs.cn: “也许他们是对自己说的吧。

paragraphs.en: Of _course_ they do.
paragraphs.cn: 当然是啦。

paragraphs.en: Anybody might know that.”
paragraphs.cn: 谁都知道的呀。”

paragraphs.en: The other boys agreed that there was reason in what Tom said, because an ignorant lump of bread, uninstructed by an incantation, could not be expected to act very intelligently when set upon an errand of such gravity.
paragraphs.cn: 其他的男孩都同意汤姆的话，因为一块没念过咒语的“笨面包”，在办这么重要的事情时，肯定不会很聪明。

paragraphs.en: “By jings, I wish I was over there, now,” said Joe.
paragraphs.cn: “天哪，我真希望现在就在那儿，”乔说。

paragraphs.en: “I do too,” said Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “我也是，”哈克说。

paragraphs.en: “I’d give heaps to know who it is.”
paragraphs.cn: “我真想知道那是谁。”

paragraphs.en: The boys still listened and watched.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们继续听着，看着。

paragraphs.en: Presently a revealing thought flashed through Tom’s mind, and he exclaimed:
paragraphs.cn: 忽然，一个想法闪过汤姆的脑海，他大声喊道：

paragraphs.en: “Boys, I know who’s drownded—it’s us!”
paragraphs.cn: “伙计们，我知道谁淹死了——是我们！”

paragraphs.en: They felt like heroes in an instant.
paragraphs.cn: 他们立刻觉得自己像英雄一样。

paragraphs.en: Here was a gorgeous triumph; they were missed; they were mourned; hearts were breaking on their account; tears were being shed; accusing memories of unkindness to these poor lost lads were rising up, and unavailing regrets and remorse were being indulged; and best of all, the departed were the talk of the whole town, and the envy of all the boys, as far as this dazzling notoriety was concerned.
paragraphs.cn: 这真是一场了不起的胜利！大家都想念他们，为他们难过；好多人的心都碎了；眼泪哗哗地流；大家都在后悔对这些可怜的失踪男孩不够好；无尽的遗憾和悔恨也涌了上来；最棒的是，这些“死去”的男孩成了全镇的话题，所有男孩子都羡慕他们，因为他们太出名了。

paragraphs.en: This was fine.
paragraphs.cn: 这太棒了。

paragraphs.en: It was worth while to be a pirate, after all.
paragraphs.cn: 看来当海盗还是值得的。

paragraphs.en: As twilight drew on, the ferryboat went back to her accustomed business and the skiffs disappeared.
paragraphs.cn: 天色渐渐暗下来，渡船回到它平时工作的地方，小船也不见了。

paragraphs.en: The pirates returned to camp.
paragraphs.cn: 海盗们回到了营地。

paragraphs.en: They were jubilant with vanity over their new grandeur and the illustrious trouble they were making.
paragraphs.cn: 他们因为自己的“新身份”和制造的“大麻烦”而洋洋得意。

paragraphs.en: They caught fish, cooked supper and ate it, and then fell to guessing at what the village was thinking and saying about them; and the pictures they drew of the public distress on their account were gratifying to look upon—from their point of view.
paragraphs.cn: 他们抓了鱼，做了晚饭，吃完后就开始猜镇上的人会怎么说他们。他们想象着镇上的人为他们难过的样子，觉得真开心。

paragraphs.en: But when the shadows of night closed them in, they gradually ceased to talk, and sat gazing into the fire, with their minds evidently wandering elsewhere.
paragraphs.cn: 但是当夜幕降临，他们渐渐不说话了，坐着盯着火堆，心里显然在想别的事情。

paragraphs.en: The excitement was gone, now, and Tom and Joe could not keep back thoughts of certain persons at home who were not enjoying this fine frolic as much as they were.
paragraphs.cn: 兴奋劲儿不见了，汤姆和乔忍不住想起家里的一些人，他们可没有像自己这样享受这场“精彩的游戏”。

paragraphs.en: Misgivings came; they grew troubled and unhappy; a sigh or two escaped, unawares.
paragraphs.cn: 他们开始担心，变得心神不宁，不开心；不经意间叹了几口气。

paragraphs.en: By and by Joe timidly ventured upon a roundabout “feeler” as to how the others might look upon a return to civilization—not right now, but—
paragraphs.cn: 过了会儿，乔小心翼翼地，拐弯抹角地问大家，如果回到原来的生活，其他人会怎么看——不是现在回去，而是——

paragraphs.en: Tom withered him with derision!
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆嘲笑了他，让他没了精神！

paragraphs.en: Huck, being uncommitted as yet, joined in with Tom, and the waverer quickly “explained,” and was glad to get out of the scrape with as little taint of chicken-hearted home-sickness clinging to his garments as he could.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克还没有表态，也跟着汤姆一起嘲笑，那个犹豫不决的男孩赶紧“解释”起来，他很高兴能摆脱这个困境，身上没有沾染一点“胆小鬼想家”的痕迹。

paragraphs.en: Mutiny was effectually laid to rest for the moment.
paragraphs.cn: 叛逆的想法暂时被压制住了。

paragraphs.en: As the night deepened, Huck began to nod, and presently to snore.
paragraphs.cn: 夜深了，哈克开始打瞌睡，没一会儿就打起了呼噜。

paragraphs.en: Joe followed next.
paragraphs.cn: 乔也跟着过来了。

paragraphs.en: Tom lay upon his elbow motionless, for some time, watching the two intently.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 趴在胳膊上，一动不动地看了他俩好一会儿。

paragraphs.en: At last he got up cautiously, on his knees, and went searching among the grass and the flickering reflections flung by the campfire.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，他小心地跪起来，在草地和篝火的亮光里找东西。

paragraphs.en: He picked up and inspected several large semi-cylinders of the thin white bark of a sycamore, and finally chose two which seemed to suit him.
paragraphs.cn: 他捡起几块又大又圆的梧桐树皮，看了看，最后选了两块觉得合适的。

paragraphs.en: Then he knelt by the fire and painfully wrote something upon each of these with his “red keel”; one he rolled up and put in his jacket pocket, and the other he put in Joe’s hat and removed it to a little distance from the owner.
paragraphs.cn: 然后，他跪在火边，用他的“红铅笔”艰难地在每块树皮上写了点东西。一块他卷起来放进口袋，另一块放在乔的帽子里，再把帽子移到离乔远一点的地方。

paragraphs.en: And he also put into the hat certain schoolboy treasures of almost inestimable value—among them a lump of chalk, an India-rubber ball, three fishhooks, and one of that kind of marbles known as a “sure ’nough crystal.”
paragraphs.cn: 他还在帽子里放了一些小男孩非常宝贝的东西——比如一块粉笔、一个橡皮球、三根鱼钩，还有一颗叫“真水晶”的弹珠。

paragraphs.en: Then he tiptoed his way cautiously among the trees till he felt that he was out of hearing, and straightway broke into a keen run in the direction of the sandbar.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他小心翼翼地在树林里踮着脚走，直到听不到声音了，就立刻朝着沙洲的方向跑去。

paragraphs.en: A few minutes later Tom was in the shoal water of the bar, wading toward the Illinois shore.
paragraphs.cn: 几分钟后，汤姆 到了沙洲的浅水区，往伊利诺伊岸边走去。

paragraphs.en: Before the depth reached his middle he was halfway over; the current would permit no more wading, now, so he struck out confidently to swim the remaining hundred yards.
paragraphs.cn: 水还没到他腰部，他就已经走到一半了。现在水流太急，不能再走了，他就自信地游向剩下的百米路程。

paragraphs.en: He swam quartering upstream, but still was swept downward rather faster than he had expected.
paragraphs.cn: 他逆着水流斜着游，但还是被冲得比他想的快一些。

paragraphs.en: However, he reached the shore finally, and drifted along till he found a low place and drew himself out.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，他终于游到了岸边，沿着岸漂了一会儿，找到一个低洼的地方爬了上去。

paragraphs.en: He put his hand on his jacket pocket, found his piece of bark safe, and then struck through the woods, following the shore, with streaming garments.
paragraphs.cn: 他把手放进上衣口袋，发现那块树皮还在，然后就穿着湿衣服，沿着岸边穿过树林。

paragraphs.en: Shortly before ten o’clock he came out into an open place opposite the village, and saw the ferryboat lying in the shadow of the trees and the high bank.
paragraphs.cn: 快到十点的时候，他来到村子对面的一片空地，看到了停在树荫下和高岸边的大渡船。

paragraphs.en: Everything was quiet under the blinking stars.
paragraphs.cn: 眨眼的星星下，一切都很安静。

paragraphs.en: He crept down the bank, watching with all his eyes, slipped into the water, swam three or four strokes and climbed into the skiff that did “yawl” duty at the boat’s stern.
paragraphs.cn: 他小心地爬下岸边，瞪大眼睛看着，悄悄滑进水里，游了三四下，爬进了那艘停在大船船尾的小船。

paragraphs.en: He laid himself down under the thwarts and waited, panting.
paragraphs.cn: 他躺在船板下面，喘着气等待着。

paragraphs.en: Presently the cracked bell tapped and a voice gave the order to “cast off.”
paragraphs.cn: 很快，破铃铛响了一下，一个声音喊道：“开船！”

paragraphs.en: A minute or two later the skiff’s head was standing high up, against the boat’s swell, and the voyage was begun.
paragraphs.cn: 一两分钟后，小船的船头高高翘起，迎着大船的水波，航行开始了。

paragraphs.en: Tom felt happy in his success, for he knew it was the boat’s last trip for the night.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 为自己的成功感到高兴，因为他知道这是大船今晚最后一趟了。

paragraphs.en: At the end of a long twelve or fifteen minutes the wheels stopped, and Tom slipped overboard and swam ashore in the dusk, landing fifty yards downstream, out of danger of possible stragglers.
paragraphs.cn: 大概过了漫长的十二到十五分钟，轮子停了。汤姆 悄悄跳下船，在黄昏中游上岸，在下游五十码的地方上岸，这样就不会被可能路过的人发现。

paragraphs.en: He flew along unfrequented alleys, and shortly found himself at his aunt’s back fence.
paragraphs.cn: 他沿着没人的小巷飞快地跑着，很快就到了他姨妈家的后院围栏。

paragraphs.en: He climbed over, approached the “ell,” and looked in at the sitting-room window, for a light was burning there.
paragraphs.cn: 他翻过去，走到“L形”屋子旁边，朝客厅的窗户里看去，因为里面亮着灯。

paragraphs.en: There sat Aunt Polly, Sid, Mary, and Joe Harper’s mother, grouped together, talking.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈、希德、玛丽 和 乔·哈珀 的妈妈坐在一起，正在聊天。

paragraphs.en: They were by the bed, and the bed was between them and the door.
paragraphs.cn: 他们在床边，床在他们和门中间。

paragraphs.en: Tom went to the door and began to softly lift the latch; then he pressed gently and the door yielded a crack; he continued pushing cautiously, and quaking every time it creaked, till he judged he might squeeze through on his knees; so he put his head through and began, warily.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 走到门边，轻轻地抬起门闩；然后他轻轻一推，门就开了一道缝；他继续小心地推着，门每次嘎吱响，他都吓得发抖，直到他觉得可以跪着挤进去了；于是他把头探进去，小心翼翼地进去了。

paragraphs.en: “What makes the candle blow so?” said Aunt Polly.
paragraphs.cn: “蜡烛怎么吹得这么厉害？”波莉姨妈 说。

paragraphs.en: Tom hurried up.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 赶紧走上前。

paragraphs.en: “Why, that door’s open, I believe.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，我相信那扇门是开着的。”

paragraphs.en: Why, of course it is.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，当然是了。”

paragraphs.en: No end of strange things now.
paragraphs.cn: “现在真是奇怪事儿太多了。”

paragraphs.en: Go ’long and shut it, Sid.”
paragraphs.cn: “去把它关上，希德。”

paragraphs.en: Tom disappeared under the bed just in time.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 及时地钻到了床底下。

paragraphs.en: He lay and “breathed” himself for a time, and then crept to where he could almost touch his aunt’s foot.
paragraphs.cn: 他躺着，“喘”了一会儿气，然后悄悄地爬过去，离他阿姨的脚很近，几乎能碰到。

paragraphs.en: “But as I was saying,” said Aunt Polly, “he warn’t _bad_, so to say—only misch_ee_vous.
paragraphs.cn: “我刚才说啊，” 波莉姨妈 说，“他其实不坏，就是有点调皮。”

paragraphs.en: Only just giddy, and harum-scarum, you know.
paragraphs.cn: 他只是有点淘气，爱闹腾，你知道的。

paragraphs.en: He warn’t any more responsible than a colt.
paragraphs.cn: 他就像个小马驹，一点也不懂事。

paragraphs.en: _He_ never meant any harm, and he was the best-hearted boy that ever was”—and she began to cry.
paragraphs.cn: 他从来没想过要捣乱，他是个心地最好的孩子了！”——说着，她哭了起来。

paragraphs.en: “It was just so with my Joe—always full of his devilment, and up to every kind of mischief, but he was just as unselfish and kind as he could be—and laws bless me, to think I went and whipped him for taking that cream, never once recollecting that I throwed it out myself because it was sour, and I never to see him again in this world, never, never, never, poor abused boy!”
paragraphs.cn: “我的乔就是这样——总是那么淘气，喜欢搞各种恶作剧，但他心地善良，一点也不自私——天哪，我竟然因为他拿了奶油而打了他，我完全忘了那奶油是我自己倒掉的，因为它坏了。现在我再也见不到他了，永远，永远，永远都见不到了，我可怜的孩子啊！”

paragraphs.en: And Mrs. Harper sobbed as if her heart would break.
paragraphs.cn: 哈珀太太哭得非常伤心，好像心都要碎了。

paragraphs.en: “I hope Tom’s better off where he is,” said Sid, “but if he’d been better in some ways—”
paragraphs.cn: “我希望 汤姆 在那边过得更好，” 希德 说，“可他要是能更好一点就好了——”

paragraphs.en: “_Sid!
_” Tom felt the glare of the old lady’s eye, though he could not see it.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 感觉到了老奶奶锐利的目光，虽然他没看见。

paragraphs.en: “Not a word against my Tom, now that he’s gone!
paragraphs.cn: “我的 汤姆 都走了，谁也不许说他坏话！”

paragraphs.en: God’ll take care of _him_—never you trouble _your_self, sir!
paragraphs.cn: 上帝会照顾他的——你不用为自己担心，先生！

paragraphs.en: Oh, Mrs. Harper, I don’t know how to give him up!
paragraphs.cn: 哦，哈珀太太，我真的舍不得他！

paragraphs.en: I don’t know how to give him up!
paragraphs.cn: 我真的舍不得他！

paragraphs.en: He was such a comfort to me, although he tormented my old heart out of me, ’most.”
paragraphs.cn: 他给了我很多安慰，虽然他有时也让我这颗老心操碎了。”

paragraphs.en: “The Lord giveth and the Lord hath taken away—Blessed be the name of the Lord!
paragraphs.cn: “上帝赐予生命，上帝也带走生命——愿上帝的名字得到赞美！

paragraphs.en: But it’s so hard—Oh, it’s so hard!
paragraphs.cn: 可是，这真的太难了——哦，太难了！

paragraphs.en: Only last Saturday my Joe busted a firecracker right under my nose and I knocked him sprawling.
paragraphs.cn: 就在上周六，我的乔在我鼻子底下放了个鞭炮，我气得把他推倒在地。

paragraphs.en: Little did I know then, how soon—Oh, if it was to do over again I’d hug him and bless him for it.”
paragraphs.cn: 我那时哪知道，他会这么快就——哦，如果能再来一次，我一定会抱抱他，感谢他。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, yes, yes, I know just how you feel, Mrs. Harper, I know just exactly how you feel.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，是的，是的，哈珀太太，我非常明白你的感受，我完全明白你的感受。

paragraphs.en: No longer ago than yesterday noon, my Tom took and filled the cat full of Pain-killer, and I did think the cretur would tear the house down.
paragraphs.cn: 就在昨天中午，我的 汤姆 把止痛药灌给了猫，我当时真以为那小东西要把房子给拆了。

paragraphs.en: And God forgive me, I cracked Tom’s head with my thimble, poor boy, poor dead boy.
paragraphs.cn: 愿上帝原谅我，我用顶针敲了 汤姆 的头，可怜的孩子，可怜的去世的孩子。

paragraphs.en: But he’s out of all his troubles now.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，他现在已经没有烦恼了。

paragraphs.en: And the last words I ever heard him say was to reproach—”
paragraphs.cn: 我最后一次听到他说的话，是他在责怪——”

paragraphs.en: But this memory was too much for the old lady, and she broke entirely down.
paragraphs.cn: 但这段回忆让老太太受不了了，她彻底崩溃了。

paragraphs.en: Tom was snuffling, now, himself—and more in pity of himself than anybody else.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 自己也抽泣起来，他更可怜的是自己，而不是别人。

paragraphs.en: He could hear Mary crying, and putting in a kindly word for him from time to time.
paragraphs.cn: 他能听到 玛丽 在哭，还不时地替他说好话。

paragraphs.en: He began to have a nobler opinion of himself than ever before.
paragraphs.cn: 他开始觉得自己比以前更了不起了。

paragraphs.en: Still, he was sufficiently touched by his aunt’s grief to long to rush out from under the bed and overwhelm her with joy—and the theatrical gorgeousness of the thing appealed strongly to his nature, too, but he resisted and lay still.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，他还是被阿姨的伤心感动了，很想从床底下冲出去，给她一个大大的惊喜——这种像演戏一样的事情也特别吸引他，但他还是忍住了，一动不动地躺着。

paragraphs.en: He went on listening, and gathered by odds and ends that it was conjectured at first that the boys had got drowned while taking a swim; then the small raft had been missed; next, certain boys said the missing lads had promised that the village should “hear something” soon; the wise-heads had “put this and that together” and decided that the lads had gone off on that raft and would turn up at the next town below, presently; but toward noon the raft had been found, lodged against the Missouri shore some five or six miles below the village—and then hope perished; they must be drowned, else hunger would have driven them home by nightfall if not sooner.
paragraphs.cn: 他继续听着，零零散散地了解到：大家一开始猜，孩子们可能是在游泳时淹死的；接着，小木筏不见了；然后，有几个孩子说，失踪的孩子们说过要让村子里“听到点什么”；聪明的大人们把这些线索“串起来一想”，就觉得孩子们是坐木筏走了，很快会在下游的下一个小镇出现；可是，到了中午，木筏被找到了，它卡在村子下游五六英里处的密苏里河岸边——这时，所有希望都破灭了；他们一定是淹死了，不然，即使不早点回家，到晚上也会因为饿了而回家。

paragraphs.en: It was believed that the search for the bodies had been a fruitless effort merely because the drowning must have occurred in mid-channel, since the boys, being good swimmers, would otherwise have escaped to shore.
paragraphs.cn: 大家觉得，找他们身体的努力是白费力气，因为他们可能是在河中央淹死的，要是他们在岸边，那么会游泳的孩子们肯定能游到岸边。

paragraphs.en: This was Wednesday night.
paragraphs.cn: 这是星期三晚上。

paragraphs.en: If the bodies continued missing until Sunday, all hope would be given over, and the funerals would be preached on that morning.
paragraphs.cn: 如果他们的身体到星期天还没找到，大家就会放弃所有希望，然后那天早上就会举行葬礼。

paragraphs.en: Tom shuddered.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 shuddered.

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Harper gave a sobbing goodnight and turned to go.
paragraphs.cn: 哈珀太太哭着说了声晚安，然后转身准备离开。

paragraphs.en: Then with a mutual impulse the two bereaved women flung themselves into each other’s arms and had a good, consoling cry, and then parted.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，两个失去亲人的女人不约而同地抱在一起，好好地哭了一场，互相安慰，然后才分开。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly was tender far beyond her wont, in her goodnight to Sid and Mary.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈 破天荒地温柔，对 希德 和 玛丽 说了晚安。

paragraphs.en: Sid snuffled a bit and Mary went off crying with all her heart.
paragraphs.cn: 希德 抽泣了几声，玛丽 也伤心地哭着离开了。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly knelt down and prayed for Tom so touchingly, so appealingly, and with such measureless love in her words and her old trembling voice, that he was weltering in tears again, long before she was through.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈 跪下来为 汤姆 祈祷。她的祈祷是那么感人，那么恳切，话语里和她颤抖的嗓音里充满了无限的爱，以至于她还没说完，他又早已泪流满面了。

paragraphs.en: He had to keep still long after she went to bed, for she kept making broken-hearted ejaculations from time to time, tossing unrestfully, and turning over.
paragraphs.cn: 她睡着后很久，他都必须保持安静，因为她不时地发出伤心的声音，翻来覆去，睡不安稳。

paragraphs.en: But at last she was still, only moaning a little in her sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 不过最后她还是安静了，只是在睡梦中轻轻地哼了几声。

paragraphs.en: Now the boy stole out, rose gradually by the bedside, shaded the candle-light with his hand, and stood regarding her.
paragraphs.cn: 小男孩悄悄地走出来，慢慢走到床边，用手遮住烛光，站着看她。

paragraphs.en: His heart was full of pity for her.
paragraphs.cn: 他心里很同情她。

paragraphs.en: He took out his sycamore scroll and placed it by the candle.
paragraphs.cn: 他拿出他的梧桐树皮卷，把它放在蜡烛旁边。

paragraphs.en: But something occurred to him, and he lingered considering.
paragraphs.cn: 但他突然想到一件事，他停下来想了想。

paragraphs.en: His face lighted with a happy solution of his thought; he put the bark hastily in his pocket.
paragraphs.cn: 他想到了一个好办法，脸上亮了起来；他赶紧把树皮放进口袋。

paragraphs.en: Then he bent over and kissed the faded lips, and straightway made his stealthy exit, latching the door behind him.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他弯下腰，亲了亲她苍白的嘴唇，悄悄地走了出去，关上了身后的门。

paragraphs.en: He threaded his way back to the ferry landing, found nobody at large there, and walked boldly on board the boat, for he knew she was tenantless except that there was a watchman, who always turned in and slept like a graven image.
paragraphs.cn: 他摸索着回到渡船码头，没看到什么人，就大胆地走上了船。他知道船上没人，只有一个看守，看守总是睡得很香，像个木头人。

paragraphs.en: He untied the skiff at the stern, slipped into it, and was soon rowing cautiously upstream.
paragraphs.cn: 他解开船尾的小船，滑进去，很快就小心地向上游划去。

paragraphs.en: When he had pulled a mile above the village, he started quartering across and bent himself stoutly to his work.
paragraphs.cn: 当他划到村庄上方一英里时，他开始横着划过去，用力地划着。

paragraphs.en: He hit the landing on the other side neatly, for this was a familiar bit of work to him.
paragraphs.cn: 他稳稳地靠上了对岸的码头，因为他很熟悉这个活。

paragraphs.en: He was moved to capture the skiff, arguing that it might be considered a ship and therefore legitimate prey for a pirate, but he knew a thorough search would be made for it and that might end in revelations.
paragraphs.cn: 他想把小船带走，心想这可以算是一艘船，海盗可以抢它。但他知道大家会仔细找船，那样他的秘密就会被发现。

paragraphs.en: So he stepped ashore and entered the woods.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他上了岸，走进了树林。

paragraphs.en: He sat down and took a long rest, torturing himself meanwhile to keep awake, and then started warily down the home-stretch.
paragraphs.cn: 他坐下来好好休息，努力不让自己睡着，然后小心翼翼地往回走。

paragraphs.en: The night was far spent.
paragraphs.cn: 夜已经很深了。

paragraphs.en: It was broad daylight before he found himself fairly abreast the island bar.
paragraphs.cn: 天大亮时，他才走到岛边的沙洲旁边。

paragraphs.en: He rested again until the sun was well up and gilding the great river with its splendor, and then he plunged into the stream.
paragraphs.cn: 他又休息了一会儿，直到太阳高高升起，把大河照得金光闪闪，然后他跳进了河里。

paragraphs.en: A little later he paused, dripping, upon the threshold of the camp, and heard Joe say:
paragraphs.cn: 不久后，他浑身湿淋淋地停在营地门口，听到乔说：

paragraphs.en: “No, Tom’s true-blue, Huck, and he’ll come back.
paragraphs.cn: “不，汤姆 是个忠实的朋友，哈克，他会回来的。”

paragraphs.en: He won’t desert.
paragraphs.cn: 他不会抛弃我们的。

paragraphs.en: He knows that would be a disgrace to a pirate, and Tom’s too proud for that sort of thing.
paragraphs.cn: 他知道那对海盗来说是丢脸的事，而 汤姆 太骄傲了，不会做那种事。

paragraphs.en: He’s up to something or other.
paragraphs.cn: 他肯定在搞什么名堂。

paragraphs.en: Now I wonder what?”
paragraphs.cn: “现在我想知道是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Well, the things is ours, anyway, ain’t they?”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，反正这些东西是我们的，对吧？”

paragraphs.en: “Pretty near, but not yet, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “差不多了，但还没到，哈克。”

paragraphs.en: The writing says they are if he ain’t back here to breakfast.”
paragraphs.cn: 纸上写着，如果他早餐没回来，这些东西就是我们的了。”

paragraphs.en: “Which he is!” exclaimed Tom, with fine dramatic effect, stepping grandly into camp.
paragraphs.cn: “他就是！” 汤姆 大声喊道，带着很有趣的表演效果，大摇大摆地走进了营地。

paragraphs.en: A sumptuous breakfast of bacon and fish was shortly provided, and as the boys set to work upon it, Tom recounted (and adorned) his adventures.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，一份丰盛的培根鱼肉早餐就准备好了。孩子们开始吃的时候，汤姆 讲起了（还添油加醋地美化了）他的冒险故事。

paragraphs.en: They were a vain and boastful company of heroes when the tale was done.
paragraphs.cn: 故事讲完后，他们都成了爱炫耀的英雄。

paragraphs.en: Then Tom hid himself away in a shady nook to sleep till noon, and the other pirates got ready to fish and explore.
paragraphs.cn: 于是 汤姆 躲到一个阴凉的角落里睡到中午，其他海盗则准备去钓鱼和探险。

paragraphs.en: After dinner all the gang turned out to hunt for turtle eggs on the bar.
paragraphs.cn: 晚饭后，所有人都出去在沙洲上找海龟蛋。

paragraphs.en: They went about poking sticks into the sand, and when they found a soft place they went down on their knees and dug with their hands.
paragraphs.cn: 他们拿着棍子在沙子里戳，当他们找到一个软的地方时，就跪下来用手挖。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes they would take fifty or sixty eggs out of one hole.
paragraphs.cn: 有时候他们能从一个洞里挖出五六十个蛋。

paragraphs.en: They were perfectly round white things a trifle smaller than an English walnut.
paragraphs.cn: 它们是圆圆的白色小东西，比核桃稍微小一点。

paragraphs.en: They had a famous fried-egg feast that night, and another on Friday morning.
paragraphs.cn: 那天晚上，他们吃了一顿丰盛的煎蛋大餐，星期五早上又吃了一顿。

paragraphs.en: After breakfast they went whooping and prancing out on the bar, and chased each other round and round, shedding clothes as they went, until they were naked, and then continued the frolic far away up the shoal water of the bar, against the stiff current, which latter tripped their legs from under them from time to time and greatly increased the fun.
paragraphs.cn: 早餐后，他们欢呼雀跃地跑到沙洲上，互相追逐打闹，跑着跑着就把衣服脱光了。然后继续在沙洲的浅水区玩耍，逆着水流。水流有时会把他们的腿绊倒，这让游戏更加有趣。

paragraphs.en: And now and then they stooped in a group and splashed water in each other’s faces with their palms, gradually approaching each other, with averted faces to avoid the strangling sprays, and finally gripping and struggling till the best man ducked his neighbor, and then they all went under in a tangle of white legs and arms and came up blowing, sputtering, laughing, and gasping for breath at one and the same time.
paragraphs.cn: 他们有时会蹲下来，用手掌互相泼水到脸上，慢慢靠近对方。他们脸扭向一边，避开呛人的水花。最后扭打起来，直到最厉害的人把旁边的人按到水里。接着，他们白花花的胳膊和腿缠在一起，全都沉入了水下，然后浮上来，呼气、吐水、大笑，同时大口喘气。

paragraphs.en: When they were well exhausted, they would run out and sprawl on the dry, hot sand, and lie there and cover themselves up with it, and by and by break for the water again and go through the original performance once more.
paragraphs.cn: 他们玩累了，就跑到沙滩上。沙滩又干又热，他们躺下，用沙子盖住自己。过一会儿，又跑去玩水，再玩一遍。

paragraphs.en: Finally it occurred to them that their naked skin represented flesh-colored “tights” very fairly; so they drew a ring in the sand and had a circus—with three clowns in it, for none would yield this proudest post to his neighbor.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，他们觉得光着身子就像穿了肉色的“紧身衣”。于是他们在沙滩上画了个圈，玩起了马戏。里面有三个小丑，谁也不想把这个最厉害的角色让给别人。

paragraphs.en: Next they got their marbles and played “knucks” and “ringtaw” and “keeps” till that amusement grew stale.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，他们拿出弹珠，玩了好几种弹珠游戏，直到玩腻了。

paragraphs.en: Then Joe and Huck had another swim, but Tom would not venture, because he found that in kicking off his trousers he had kicked his string of rattlesnake rattles off his ankle, and he wondered how he had escaped cramp so long without the protection of this mysterious charm.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，乔和 哈克 又游了一次。但 汤姆 不敢下水，因为他发现自己脱裤子的时候，把系在脚踝上的响尾蛇响环给踢掉了。他很奇怪，没有这个神秘护身符的保护，他怎么这么久都没抽筋。

paragraphs.en: He did not venture again until he had found it, and by that time the other boys were tired and ready to rest.
paragraphs.cn: 他没找到就不敢再玩。等他找到时，别的小伙伴都累了，想休息了。

paragraphs.en: They gradually wandered apart, dropped into the “dumps,” and fell to gazing longingly across the wide river to where the village lay drowsing in the sun.
paragraphs.cn: 他们慢慢地分开了，心情不太好，开始看着宽阔的河对面。那里的小村庄正在阳光下睡懒觉。

paragraphs.en: Tom found himself writing “BECKY” in the sand with his big toe; he scratched it out, and was angry with himself for his weakness.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 发现自己用大脚趾在沙子上写“BECKY”；他赶紧抹掉了，气自己怎么这么没用。

paragraphs.en: But he wrote it again, nevertheless; he could not help it.
paragraphs.cn: 但是他还是又写了一遍，他忍不住啊。

paragraphs.en: He erased it once more and then took himself out of temptation by driving the other boys together and joining them.
paragraphs.cn: 他又擦了一次。然后他叫上其他男孩一起玩，不让自己再想那个了。

paragraphs.en: But Joe’s spirits had gone down almost beyond resurrection.
paragraphs.cn: 但是乔的心情已经很糟很糟了，好像好不起来了。

paragraphs.en: He was so homesick that he could hardly endure the misery of it.
paragraphs.cn: 他太想家了，难受得受不了了。

paragraphs.en: The tears lay very near the surface.
paragraphs.cn: 眼泪都快要流出来了。

paragraphs.en: Huck was melancholy, too.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 也很难过。

paragraphs.en: Tom was downhearted, but tried hard not to show it.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 心情很不好，但他努力不表现出来。

paragraphs.en: He had a secret which he was not ready to tell, yet, but if this mutinous depression was not broken up soon, he would have to bring it out.
paragraphs.cn: 他有个秘密还没准备好说，但如果他再不开心，他就得说出来了。

paragraphs.en: He said, with a great show of cheerfulness:
paragraphs.cn: 他装作很开心地说：

paragraphs.en: “I bet there’s been pirates on this island before, boys.
paragraphs.cn: “我打赌，这岛上以前肯定有海盗，孩子们。

paragraphs.en: We’ll explore it again.
paragraphs.cn: 我们再来找找看。

paragraphs.en: They’ve hid treasures here somewhere.
paragraphs.cn: 他们肯定把宝贝藏在这儿了。

paragraphs.en: How’d you feel to light on a rotten chest full of gold and silver—hey?”
paragraphs.cn: 找到一个装满金子和银子的旧箱子，你们高不高兴啊？”

paragraphs.en: But it roused only faint enthusiasm, which faded out, with no reply.
paragraphs.cn: 但大家没什么兴趣，也没人回答。

paragraphs.en: Tom tried one or two other seductions; but they failed, too.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 又试着说了别的好玩的事，可也没用。

paragraphs.en: It was discouraging work.
paragraphs.cn: 这让他有点泄气。

paragraphs.en: Joe sat poking up the sand with a stick and looking very gloomy.
paragraphs.cn: 乔用小棍子戳着沙子，看起来很不开心。

paragraphs.en: Finally he said:
paragraphs.cn: 最后他说：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, boys, let’s give it up.
paragraphs.cn: “哎，孩子们，我们别玩了。

paragraphs.en: I want to go home.
paragraphs.cn: 我想回家。

paragraphs.en: It’s so lonesome.”
paragraphs.cn: 这儿太孤单了。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh no, Joe, you’ll feel better by and by,” said Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，乔，等会儿你就会好起来的，” 汤姆 说。

paragraphs.en: “Just think of the fishing that’s here.”
paragraphs.cn: “想想这儿可以钓鱼啊。”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t care for fishing.
paragraphs.cn: “我不想钓鱼。

paragraphs.en: I want to go home.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想回家。”

paragraphs.en: “But, Joe, there ain’t such another swimming-place anywhere.”
paragraphs.cn: “可是，乔，没有比这儿更好的游泳地方了。”

paragraphs.en: “Swimming’s no good.
paragraphs.cn: “游泳一点也不好玩。

paragraphs.en: I don’t seem to care for it, somehow, when there ain’t anybody to say I sha’n’t go in.
paragraphs.cn: 没人管我，我就不想游了。

paragraphs.en: I mean to go home.”
paragraphs.cn: 我就是要回家。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, shucks!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀！

paragraphs.en: Baby!
paragraphs.cn: 你真是个小孩子！

paragraphs.en: You want to see your mother, I reckon.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想，你是想妈妈了吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, I _do_ want to see my mother—and you would, too, if you had one.
paragraphs.cn: “对，我就是想妈妈了——你要是有妈妈，你也会想的。

paragraphs.en: I ain’t any more baby than you are.”
paragraphs.cn: 我才不像你说的那样是小孩子呢！”

paragraphs.en: And Joe snuffled a little.
paragraphs.cn: 乔轻轻地抽了抽鼻子。

paragraphs.en: “Well, we’ll let the crybaby go home to his mother, won’t we, Huck?
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，我们让那个爱哭鬼回家找妈妈，好不好啊，哈克？”

paragraphs.en: Poor thing—does it want to see its mother?
paragraphs.cn: 可怜的，你想妈妈了吗？

paragraphs.en: And so it shall.
paragraphs.cn: 那就可以去啊。

paragraphs.en: You like it here, don’t you, Huck?
paragraphs.cn: 你喜欢这里，对吧，哈克？

paragraphs.en: We’ll stay, won’t we?”
paragraphs.cn: 我们会留下，对吗？

paragraphs.en: Huck said, “Y-e-s”—without any heart in it.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 没精打采地说：“是——的。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll never speak to you again as long as I live,” said Joe, rising.
paragraphs.cn: “我一辈子都不会再跟你说话了！”乔站起来说。

paragraphs.en: “There now!”
And he moved moodily away and began to dress himself.
paragraphs.cn: 他不高兴地走开，开始穿衣服。

paragraphs.en: “Who cares!” said Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “Who cares!” said 汤姆.

paragraphs.en: “Nobody wants you to.
paragraphs.cn: “没人想你留下。

paragraphs.en: Go ’long home and get laughed at.
paragraphs.cn: 回家去吧，让别人笑话你。

paragraphs.en: Oh, you’re a nice pirate.
paragraphs.cn: 你可真是个‘好’海盗啊。

paragraphs.en: Huck and me ain’t crybabies.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 和我才不是爱哭鬼。

paragraphs.en: We’ll stay, won’t we, Huck?
paragraphs.cn: 我们会留下来，对不对，哈克？

paragraphs.en: Let him go if he wants to.
paragraphs.cn: 他想走就让他走吧。

paragraphs.en: I reckon we can get along without him, per’aps.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想，我们没有他也能玩得好，也许吧。”

paragraphs.en: But Tom was uneasy, nevertheless, and was alarmed to see Joe go sullenly on with his dressing.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，汤姆 心里还是不安，他看到乔不高兴地继续穿衣服，吓了一跳。

paragraphs.en: And then it was discomforting to see Huck eying Joe’s preparations so wistfully, and keeping up such an ominous silence.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，他看到 哈克 那么渴望地看着乔准备，还一直保持着不祥的沉默，这让他感到很不舒服。

paragraphs.en: Presently, without a parting word, Joe began to wade off toward the Illinois shore.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，乔什么也没说，就开始趟水走向伊利诺伊州的岸边。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s heart began to sink.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 的心开始往下沉。

paragraphs.en: He glanced at Huck.
paragraphs.cn: 他看了一眼 哈克。

paragraphs.en: Huck could not bear the look, and dropped his eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 不敢看，就低下了头。

paragraphs.en: Then he said:
paragraphs.cn: 然后他说：

paragraphs.en: “I want to go, too, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “我也想去，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: It was getting so lonesome anyway, and now it’ll be worse.
paragraphs.cn: 反正已经很孤单了，现在会更糟。

paragraphs.en: Let’s us go, too, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们也一起去吧，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: “I won’t!
paragraphs.cn: “我才不呢！

paragraphs.en: You can all go, if you want to.
paragraphs.cn: 你们想走就都走吧。

paragraphs.en: I mean to stay.”
paragraphs.cn: 我要留下来。”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, I better go.”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆, I better go.”

paragraphs.en: “Well, go ’long—who’s hendering you.”
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，走吧——谁拦着你了呀。”

paragraphs.en: Huck began to pick up his scattered clothes.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 开始捡他散落的衣服。

paragraphs.en: He said:
paragraphs.cn: 他说：

paragraphs.en: “Tom, I wisht you’d come, too.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆, I wisht you’d come, too.

paragraphs.en: Now you think it over.
paragraphs.cn: 现在你好好想想吧。

paragraphs.en: We’ll wait for you when we get to shore.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们到了岸边就等你。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, you’ll wait a blame long time, that’s all.”
paragraphs.cn: “哼，那你们可得等好久好久，就这样。”

paragraphs.en: Huck started sorrowfully away, and Tom stood looking after him, with a strong desire tugging at his heart to yield his pride and go along too.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 难过地走了。汤姆 看着他走远，心里好想也放下脸面，跟着一起去。

paragraphs.en: He hoped the boys would stop, but they still waded slowly on.
paragraphs.cn: 他希望大家停下来，但他们还是慢慢地往前走。

paragraphs.en: It suddenly dawned on Tom that it was become very lonely and still.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 突然觉得，这里变得很安静，也很孤单。

paragraphs.en: He made one final struggle with his pride, and then darted after his comrades, yelling:
paragraphs.cn: 他最后跟自己挣扎了一下，然后就冲向伙伴们，大声喊：

paragraphs.en: “Wait!
paragraphs.cn: “等等！

paragraphs.en: Wait!
paragraphs.cn: 等等！

paragraphs.en: I want to tell you something!”
paragraphs.cn: 我想告诉你们一件事！”

paragraphs.en: They presently stopped and turned around.
paragraphs.cn: 他们立刻停了下来，转过身。

paragraphs.en: When he got to where they were, he began unfolding his secret, and they listened moodily till at last they saw the “point” he was driving at, and then they set up a warwhoop of applause and said it was “splendid!” and said if he had told them at first, they wouldn’t have started away.
paragraphs.cn: 他走到他们身边，就开始说出他的秘密。大家一开始不开心，但是后来终于明白了他说的是什么“重点”，然后就大声欢呼起来，说“太棒了！” 还说，要是他早点告诉他们，他们就不会走了。

paragraphs.en: He made a plausible excuse; but his real reason had been the fear that not even the secret would keep them with him any very great length of time, and so he had meant to hold it in reserve as a last seduction.
paragraphs.cn: 他找了个好听的借口；但真正的原因是他担心，就算说了秘密，他们也留不了多久，所以他想把秘密留着，等到最后才说，好让他们不走。

paragraphs.en: The lads came gayly back and went at their sports again with a will, chattering all the time about Tom’s stupendous plan and admiring the genius of it.
paragraphs.cn: 小伙子们开心地回来了，又开始尽情玩耍，他们一直聊着汤姆的那个很棒的计划，都觉得他很聪明。

paragraphs.en: After a dainty egg and fish dinner, Tom said he wanted to learn to smoke, now.
paragraphs.cn: 吃了一顿美味的鸡蛋鱼肉晚餐后，汤姆 说他现在想学抽烟。

paragraphs.en: Joe caught at the idea and said he would like to try, too.
paragraphs.cn: 乔一听到这个主意，就说他也想试试看。

paragraphs.en: So Huck made pipes and filled them.
paragraphs.cn: 于是哈克做了烟斗，还把烟草装了进去。

paragraphs.en: These novices had never smoked anything before but cigars made of grapevine, and they “bit” the tongue, and were not considered manly anyway.
paragraphs.cn: 这些新手以前从来没抽过烟，只抽过葡萄藤做的“雪茄”，那种东西会“咬”舌头，而且一点也不觉得很男子汉。

paragraphs.en: Now they stretched themselves out on their elbows and began to puff, charily, and with slender confidence.
paragraphs.cn: 现在他们趴着用胳膊肘撑着，小心翼翼地，有点没信心地开始抽烟。

paragraphs.en: The smoke had an unpleasant taste, and they gagged a little, but Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 烟的味道不好闻，他们有点想吐，但汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “Why, it’s just as easy!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，这太容易了！

paragraphs.en: If I’d a knowed this was all, I’d a learnt long ago.”
paragraphs.cn: 要是早知道这么简单，我早就学会了。”

paragraphs.en: “So would I,” said Joe.
paragraphs.cn: “我也是！”乔说。

paragraphs.en: “It’s just nothing.”
paragraphs.cn: “一点都不难。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, many a time I’ve looked at people smoking, and thought well I wish I could do that; but I never thought I could,” said Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，我看了好多人抽烟，心想我也能抽就好了；但我从没想过我真的能做到。”汤姆说。

paragraphs.en: “That’s just the way with me, hain’t it, Huck?
paragraphs.cn: “我也是这样想的，不是吗，哈克？

paragraphs.en: You’ve heard me talk just that way—haven’t you, Huck?
paragraphs.cn: 你听我这么说过吧，哈克？

paragraphs.en: I’ll leave it to Huck if I haven’t.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果我没说过，就让哈克来说。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes—heaps of times,” said Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “是的——好多好多次了。”哈克说。

paragraphs.en: “Well, I have too,” said Tom; “oh, hundreds of times.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我也说过。”汤姆说，“哦，几百次了。

paragraphs.en: Once down by the slaughter-house.
paragraphs.cn: 有一次在屠宰场旁边。

paragraphs.en: Don’t you remember, Huck?
paragraphs.cn: Don’t you remember, 哈克?

paragraphs.en: Bob Tanner was there, and Johnny Miller, and Jeff Thatcher, when I said it.
paragraphs.cn: 我说的时候，鲍勃·坦纳、约翰尼·米勒和杰夫·撒切尔都在场。

paragraphs.en: Don’t you remember, Huck, ’bout me saying that?”
paragraphs.cn: 你不记得了吗，哈克，我说了那些话？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, that’s so,” said Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “Yes, that’s so,” said 哈克.

paragraphs.en: “That was the day after I lost a white alley.
paragraphs.cn: “那是我弄丢了一个白色弹珠的第二天。

paragraphs.en: No, ’twas the day before.”
paragraphs.cn: 不对，是前一天。”

paragraphs.en: “There—I told you so,” said Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “看吧——我早就告诉你了。”汤姆说。

paragraphs.en: “Huck recollects it.”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克 recollects it.”

paragraphs.en: “I bleeve I could smoke this pipe all day,” said Joe.
paragraphs.cn: “我觉得我能抽这个烟斗一整天，”乔说。
