paragraphs.en: “I don’t feel sick.”
paragraphs.cn: “我一点也不觉得恶心。”

paragraphs.en: “Neither do I,” said Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “Neither do I,” said 汤姆.

paragraphs.en: “I could smoke it all day.
paragraphs.cn: “我能抽一整天。

paragraphs.en: But I bet you Jeff Thatcher couldn’t.”
paragraphs.cn: “但我敢打赌，杰夫·撒切尔肯定不行。”

paragraphs.en: “Jeff Thatcher!
paragraphs.cn: “Jeff 撒切尔!

paragraphs.en: Why, he’d keel over just with two draws.
paragraphs.cn: 哼，他只要抽两口就会倒下。

paragraphs.en: Just let him try it once.
paragraphs.cn: 让他试试看就知道了。

paragraphs.en: _He’d_ see!”
paragraphs.cn: 他会看到的！”

paragraphs.en: “I bet he would.
paragraphs.cn: “我敢打赌他会的。

paragraphs.en: And Johnny Miller—I wish could see Johnny Miller tackle it once.”
paragraphs.cn: 还有约翰尼·米勒——我真希望约翰尼·米勒能来试一次。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, don’t I!” said Joe.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，可不是嘛！”乔说。

paragraphs.en: “Why, I bet you Johnny Miller couldn’t any more do this than nothing.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，我敢说约翰尼·米勒根本做不到这个。

paragraphs.en: Just one little snifter would fetch _him_.”
paragraphs.cn: 只要喝一小口，就能把他叫来。

paragraphs.en: “’Deed it would, Joe.
paragraphs.cn: 是啊，乔，他肯定会来的。

paragraphs.en: Say—I wish the boys could see us now.”
paragraphs.cn: 哎——真希望那些小伙伴能看到我们现在这样！

paragraphs.en: “So do I.”
paragraphs.cn: 我也是。

paragraphs.en: “Say—boys, don’t say anything about it, and some time when they’re around, I’ll come up to you and say, ‘Joe, got a pipe?
paragraphs.cn: 哎——伙计们，这事咱们谁也别说出去。等他们都在的时候，我就走过去对你说，‘乔，你有烟斗吗？

paragraphs.en: I want a smoke.’
paragraphs.cn: 我想抽一口。’

paragraphs.en: And you’ll say, kind of careless like, as if it warn’t anything, you’ll say, ‘Yes, I got my _old_ pipe, and another one, but my tobacker ain’t very good.’
paragraphs.cn: 然后你就会装作不在乎的样子，好像这没什么大不了的，你会说，‘有啊，我有我的老烟斗，还有一个备用的，不过我的烟叶不怎么样。’

paragraphs.en: And I’ll say, ‘Oh, that’s all right, if it’s _strong_ enough.’
paragraphs.cn: 我就会说，‘哦，没关系，只要味道够浓就行。’

paragraphs.en: And then you’ll out with the pipes, and we’ll light up just as ca’m, and then just see ’em look!”
paragraphs.cn: 然后你就会拿出烟斗，我们俩就安安静静地点上烟，然后就看他们惊讶的样子！

paragraphs.en: “By jings, that’ll be gay, Tom!
paragraphs.cn: “天哪，那一定会很好玩，汤姆！

paragraphs.en: I wish it was _now_!”
paragraphs.cn: 真希望是现在！

paragraphs.en: “So do I!
paragraphs.cn: 我也是！

paragraphs.en: And when we tell ’em we learned when we was off pirating, won’t they wish they’d been along?”
paragraphs.cn: 等我们告诉他们，这是我们当海盗的时候学会的，他们会不会后悔没跟我们一起来？

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I reckon not!
paragraphs.cn: 哦，我觉得不会！

paragraphs.en: I’ll just _bet_ they will!”
paragraphs.cn: 我敢打赌他们会的！

paragraphs.en: So the talk ran on.
paragraphs.cn: 他们就一直这样聊啊聊。

paragraphs.en: But presently it began to flag a trifle, and grow disjointed.
paragraphs.cn: 但是没过多久，他们的话题就有点说不动了，变得断断续续的。

paragraphs.en: The silences widened; the expectoration marvellously increased.
paragraphs.cn: 他们安静的时间越来越长；吐口水的次数也变多了。

paragraphs.en: Every pore inside the boys’ cheeks became a spouting fountain; they could scarcely bail out the cellars under their tongues fast enough to prevent an inundation; little overflowings down their throats occurred in spite of all they could do, and sudden retchings followed every time.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们的嘴巴里不停地冒着口水，怎么也咽不完，即使努力忍着，口水还是会流到喉咙里，每次都让他们想吐。

paragraphs.en: Both boys were looking very pale and miserable, now.
paragraphs.cn: 两个男孩现在脸色都很难看，非常不舒服。

paragraphs.en: Joe’s pipe dropped from his nerveless fingers.
paragraphs.cn: 乔的烟斗从他没力气的手指缝里掉了下来。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s followed.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆’s followed.

paragraphs.en: Both fountains were going furiously and both pumps bailing with might and main.
paragraphs.cn: 他们两个都吐得厉害，嘴巴里也拼命地往外冒水。

paragraphs.en: Joe said feebly:
paragraphs.cn: 乔有气无力地说：

paragraphs.en: “I’ve lost my knife.
paragraphs.cn: “我的小刀不见了。

paragraphs.en: I reckon I better go and find it.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想我最好去把它找回来。”

paragraphs.en: Tom said, with quivering lips and halting utterance:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆嘴唇颤抖着，说话结结巴巴地说：

paragraphs.en: “I’ll help you.
paragraphs.cn: “我帮你。

paragraphs.en: You go over that way and I’ll hunt around by the spring.
paragraphs.cn: 你往那边走，我到泉水边上去找找看。

paragraphs.en: No, you needn’t come, Huck—we can find it.”
paragraphs.cn: “不，你不用来了，哈克——我们能找到的。”

paragraphs.en: So Huck sat down again, and waited an hour.
paragraphs.cn: 于是哈克又坐了下来，等了一个小时。

paragraphs.en: Then he found it lonesome, and went to find his comrades.
paragraphs.cn: 后来他觉得一个人很孤单，就去R找他的小伙伴了。

paragraphs.en: They were wide apart in the woods, both very pale, both fast asleep.
paragraphs.cn: 他们两个在树林里离得很远，脸色都很白，都睡着了。

paragraphs.en: But something informed him that if they had had any trouble they had got rid of it.
paragraphs.cn: 但是他心里明白，如果他们之前有什么不舒服，现在也都好了。

paragraphs.en: They were not talkative at supper that night.
paragraphs.cn: 那天晚上吃晚饭的时候，他们都不怎么说话了。

paragraphs.en: They had a humble look, and when Huck prepared his pipe after the meal and was going to prepare theirs, they said no, they were not feeling very well—something they ate at dinner had disagreed with them.
paragraphs.cn: 他们看起来很没精神。哈克吃完饭后准备好自己的烟斗，正要帮他们准备时，他们却说不，他们感觉不太舒服——晚餐吃的东西让他们不舒服。

paragraphs.en: About midnight Joe awoke, and called the boys.
paragraphs.cn: 大约半夜，乔醒了，叫醒了孩子们。

paragraphs.en: There was a brooding oppressiveness in the air that seemed to bode something.
paragraphs.cn: 空气里有种闷闷的感觉，好像要发生什么事。

paragraphs.en: The boys huddled themselves together and sought the friendly companionship of the fire, though the dull dead heat of the breathless atmosphere was stifling.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们挤在一起，想靠近火堆取暖，虽然空气又闷又热，让人喘不过气。

paragraphs.en: They sat still, intent and waiting.
paragraphs.cn: 他们安静地坐着，认真地等待。

paragraphs.en: The solemn hush continued.
paragraphs.cn: 周围还是静悄悄的。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the light of the fire everything was swallowed up in the blackness of darkness.
paragraphs.cn: 火光外面一片漆黑，什么都看不见。

paragraphs.en: Presently there came a quivering glow that vaguely revealed the foliage for a moment and then vanished.
paragraphs.cn: 突然，一道微弱的光亮闪了一下，树叶模模糊糊地出现，又很快不见了。

paragraphs.en: By and by another came, a little stronger.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，又来了一道，亮了一些。

paragraphs.en: Then another.
paragraphs.cn: 然后又一道。

paragraphs.en: Then a faint moan came sighing through the branches of the forest and the boys felt a fleeting breath upon their cheeks, and shuddered with the fancy that the Spirit of the Night had gone by.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，一阵微风穿过树林，发出轻轻的叹息声。孩子们脸上感到一丝凉意，他们抖了一下，心想是不是黑夜精灵路过了。

paragraphs.en: There was a pause.
paragraphs.cn: 停了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: Now a weird flash turned night into day and showed every little grassblade, separate and distinct, that grew about their feet.
paragraphs.cn: 突然一道奇怪的闪电，把黑夜照得像白天一样亮，连他们脚边每一根小草都看得清清楚楚。

paragraphs.en: And it showed three white, startled faces, too.
paragraphs.cn: 它还照亮了三张发白、受惊的脸。

paragraphs.en: A deep peal of thunder went rolling and tumbling down the heavens and lost itself in sullen rumblings in the distance.
paragraphs.cn: 一声很响的雷声，轰隆隆地从天上滚下来，最后在远处变成了沉闷的低吼。

paragraphs.en: A sweep of chilly air passed by, rustling all the leaves and snowing the flaky ashes broadcast about the fire.
paragraphs.cn: 一阵冷风吹过，树叶沙沙作响，火堆里的灰烬像雪花一样四处飞散。

paragraphs.en: Another fierce glare lit up the forest and an instant crash followed that seemed to rend the treetops right over the boys’ heads.
paragraphs.cn: 又一道耀眼的闪电照亮了森林，紧接着一声巨响，好像要把孩子们头顶上的树梢都劈开一样。

paragraphs.en: They clung together in terror, in the thick gloom that followed.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，四周变得一片漆黑，他们害怕地紧紧抱在一起。

paragraphs.en: A few big raindrops fell pattering upon the leaves.
paragraphs.cn: 几滴大雨点噼里啪啦地落在树叶上。

paragraphs.en: “Quick! boys, go for the tent!” exclaimed Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “快！孩子们，去拿帐篷！”汤姆大声喊道。

paragraphs.en: They sprang away, stumbling over roots and among vines in the dark, no two plunging in the same direction.
paragraphs.cn: 他们跳起来就跑，在黑暗中被树根和藤蔓绊倒，每个人跑的方向都不一样。

paragraphs.en: A furious blast roared through the trees, making everything sing as it went.
paragraphs.cn: 一阵狂风怒吼着穿过树林，把所有东西都吹得呼呼作响。

paragraphs.en: One blinding flash after another came, and peal on peal of deafening thunder.
paragraphs.cn: 一道又一道刺眼的闪电接连出现，震耳欲聋的雷声一声连着一声。

paragraphs.en: And now a drenching rain poured down and the rising hurricane drove it in sheets along the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，倾盆大雨哗哗地下，越来越大的暴风把它像水帘一样扫向地面。

paragraphs.en: The boys cried out to each other, but the roaring wind and the booming thunderblasts drowned their voices utterly.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们互相大喊，可狂风呼啸，雷声轰鸣，完全盖住了他们的声音。

paragraphs.en: However, one by one they straggled in at last and took shelter under the tent, cold, scared, and streaming with water; but to have company in misery seemed something to be grateful for.
paragraphs.cn: 终于，他们一个接一个地跑回帐篷，又冷又怕，全身湿透；但能有伙伴在一起，就算再糟糕也觉得好一些。

paragraphs.en: They could not talk, the old sail flapped so furiously, even if the other noises would have allowed them.
paragraphs.cn: 他们没法说话，因为旧帐篷布被风吹得噼啪作响，即使没有其他噪音也听不清。

paragraphs.en: The tempest rose higher and higher, and presently the sail tore loose from its fastenings and went winging away on the blast.
paragraphs.cn: 暴风越来越大，不一会儿，帐篷布就被刮得脱离了固定绳，随风飞走了。

paragraphs.en: The boys seized each others’ hands and fled, with many tumblings and bruises, to the shelter of a great oak that stood upon the riverbank.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们拉着手跑了，跌跌撞撞，身上青一块紫一块，跑到河边一棵大橡树下躲起来。

paragraphs.en: Now the battle was at its highest.
paragraphs.cn: 这时候，暴风雨达到了最猛烈的时候。

paragraphs.en: Under the ceaseless conflagration of lightning that flamed in the skies, everything below stood out in cleancut and shadowless distinctness: the bending trees, the billowy river, white with foam, the driving spray of spumeflakes, the dim outlines of the high bluffs on the other side, glimpsed through the drifting cloudrack and the slanting veil of rain.
paragraphs.cn: 闪电不停地在天上亮着，把下面的东西都照得清清楚楚，没有影子：弯曲的树，翻滚着白色浪花的河水，飞溅的水沫，还有远处高高的悬崖，在飘动的乌云和斜下的雨帘中隐约可见。

paragraphs.en: Every little while some giant tree yielded the fight and fell crashing through the younger growth; and the unflagging thunderpeals came now in ear-splitting explosive bursts, keen and sharp, and unspeakably appalling.
paragraphs.cn: 不一会儿，就有大树被风吹倒，轰隆一声砸向小树林；雷声也变得又尖又响，震耳欲聋，让人感到非常非常可怕。

paragraphs.en: The storm culminated in one matchless effort that seemed likely to tear the island to pieces, burn it up, drown it to the treetops, blow it away, and deafen every creature in it, all at one and the same moment.
paragraphs.cn: 暴风雨变得很大很大，好像要把小岛撕碎，烧掉，淹到树顶，吹跑，还要震聋小动物们，这些都好像同时发生。

paragraphs.en: It was a wild night for homeless young heads to be out in.
paragraphs.cn: 对那些没家的小脑袋瓜来说，那个晚上很可怕。

paragraphs.en: But at last the battle was done, and the forces retired with weaker and weaker threatenings and grumblings, and peace resumed her sway.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，大风雨终于停了，声音越来越小，世界又安静下来了。

paragraphs.en: The boys went back to camp, a good deal awed; but they found there was still something to be thankful for, because the great sycamore, the shelter of their beds, was a ruin, now, blasted by the lightnings, and they were not under it when the catastrophe happened.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们回到营地，心里很害怕，但又觉得很幸运。因为那棵大大的梧桐树，平时他们睡在下面，现在被闪电劈坏了。还好，出事的时候他们没在树下。

paragraphs.en: Everything in camp was drenched, the campfire as well; for they were but heedless lads, like their generation, and had made no provision against rain.
paragraphs.cn: 营地里什么都湿透了，篝火也灭了。因为他们是粗心的小男孩，根本没准备怎么防雨。

paragraphs.en: Here was matter for dismay, for they were soaked through and chilled.
paragraphs.cn: 这下他们可惨了，全身湿冷湿冷的。

paragraphs.en: They were eloquent in their distress; but they presently discovered that the fire had eaten so far up under the great log it had been built against (where it curved upward and separated itself from the ground), that a handbreadth or so of it had escaped wetting; so they patiently wrought until, with shreds and bark gathered from the under sides of sheltered logs, they coaxed the fire to burn again.
paragraphs.cn: 他们很难过地抱怨着。不过，他们发现大木头底下有一点点没湿。于是，他们耐心找来一些干树皮和木屑，终于又把火点着了。

paragraphs.en: Then they piled on great dead boughs till they had a roaring furnace, and were gladhearted once more.
paragraphs.cn: 他们往火里加了很多大干树枝，火就烧得旺旺的，他们又高兴起来了。

paragraphs.en: They dried their boiled ham and had a feast, and after that they sat by the fire and expanded and glorified their midnight adventure until morning, for there was not a dry spot to sleep on, anywhere around.
paragraphs.cn: 他们烤干了煮好的火腿，饱饱地吃了一顿。然后，他们坐在火边，把夜里的冒险故事讲得好精彩，一直讲到天亮。因为周围根本没有一块干地方能睡觉。

paragraphs.en: As the sun began to steal in upon the boys, drowsiness came over them, and they went out on the sandbar and lay down to sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 太阳出来了，照在男孩们身上，他们就困了。他们走到沙滩上躺下睡着了。

paragraphs.en: They got scorched out by and by, and drearily set about getting breakfast.
paragraphs.cn: 没多久，他们就被晒热了，只好没精打采地起来做早饭。

paragraphs.en: After the meal they felt rusty, and stiff-jointed, and a little homesick once more.
paragraphs.cn: 吃完饭，他们觉得全身不舒服，关节也硬硬的，又有点想家了。

paragraphs.en: Tom saw the signs, and fell to cheering up the pirates as well as he could.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆看到了这些迹象，就开始尽力安慰那些海盗们。

paragraphs.en: But they cared nothing for marbles, or circus, or swimming, or anything.
paragraphs.cn: 但他们对玩弹珠、看马戏、游泳什么的，都没兴趣了。

paragraphs.en: He reminded them of the imposing secret, and raised a ray of cheer.
paragraphs.cn: 他提起了那个很重要的秘密，让大家开心了一点。

paragraphs.en: While it lasted, he got them interested in a new device.
paragraphs.cn: 趁着大家心情好，他又让他们对一个新玩法有了兴趣。

paragraphs.en: This was to knock off being pirates, for a while, and be Indians for a change.
paragraphs.cn: 这个新玩法就是，暂时不当海盗了，改成玩印第安人。

paragraphs.en: They were attracted by this idea; so it was not long before they were stripped, and striped from head to heel with black mud, like so many zebras—all of them chiefs, of course—and then they went tearing through the woods to attack an English settlement.
paragraphs.cn: 他们觉得这个主意很好玩！很快，他们就脱了衣服，从头到脚涂满了黑泥，像一只只斑马——当然，他们都是大首领！然后，他们就冲进树林，去“攻击”一个英国村子。

paragraphs.en: By and by they separated into three hostile tribes, and darted upon each other from ambush with dreadful warwhoops, and killed and scalped each other by thousands.
paragraphs.cn: 后来，他们分成了三个“敌人部落”，从藏身的地方冲出来，大声喊着“战斗口号”，互相“杀死”对方，还“割下”了好多头皮。

paragraphs.en: It was a gory day.
paragraphs.cn: 那真是“血淋淋”的一天。

paragraphs.en: Consequently it was an extremely satisfactory one.
paragraphs.cn: 所以，他们玩得非常开心。

paragraphs.en: They assembled in camp toward suppertime, hungry and happy; but now a difficulty arose—hostile Indians could not break the bread of hospitality together without first making peace, and this was a simple impossibility without smoking a pipe of peace.
paragraphs.cn: 吃晚饭的时候，他们又饿又开心地回到营地。可是，一个难题来了——“敌人部落”的印第安人，不先“和好”，就不能一起吃饭。而要“和好”，就得一起抽“和平烟斗”。

paragraphs.en: There was no other process that ever they had heard of.
paragraphs.cn: 他们只知道这一个办法。

paragraphs.en: Two of the savages almost wished they had remained pirates.
paragraphs.cn: 其中两个“小野人”差点希望自己还是当海盗算了。

paragraphs.en: However, there was no other way; so with such show of cheerfulness as they could muster they called for the pipe and took their whiff as it passed, in due form.
paragraphs.cn: 没办法，没有别的办法了。于是，他们假装开心地要来了烟斗，按照规矩，一人抽了一口。

paragraphs.en: And behold, they were glad they had gone into savagery, for they had gained something; they found that they could now smoke a little without having to go and hunt for a lost knife; they did not get sick enough to be seriously uncomfortable.
paragraphs.cn: 瞧，他们很高兴自己成了“野人”，因为他们学会了一件事：现在他们可以抽一点烟，而不用担心会不舒服。他们一点也没觉得难受。

paragraphs.en: They were not likely to fool away this high promise for lack of effort.
paragraphs.cn: 他们可不会轻易放过这个好机会。

paragraphs.en: No, they practised cautiously, after supper, with right fair success, and so they spent a jubilant evening.
paragraphs.cn: 才不呢！晚饭后，他们小心地练习抽烟，还挺成功的。所以他们度过了一个非常开心的夜晚。

paragraphs.en: They were prouder and happier in their new acquirement than they would have been in the scalping and skinning of the Six Nations.
paragraphs.cn: 他们为自己学会的新本领感到非常骄傲和开心，比“剥掉六个民族的头皮”还要高兴。

paragraphs.en: We will leave them to smoke and chatter and brag, since we have no further use for them at present.
paragraphs.cn: 我们就让他们去抽烟、聊天、吹牛吧，我们现在不需要他们了。

paragraphs.en: But there was no hilarity in the little town that same tranquil Saturday afternoon.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，在那个安静的星期六下午，小镇里可一点也不热闹。

paragraphs.en: The Harpers, and Aunt Polly’s family, were being put into mourning, with great grief and many tears.
paragraphs.cn: 哈珀家和波莉姨妈的家人都在为他们哀悼，非常伤心，流了很多眼泪。

paragraphs.en: An unusual quiet possessed the village, although it was ordinarily quiet enough, in all conscience.
paragraphs.cn: 整个村子都非常安静，比平时还要安静。

paragraphs.en: The villagers conducted their concerns with an absent air, and talked little; but they sighed often.
paragraphs.cn: 村里的人们心不在焉，很少说话，却总是叹气。

paragraphs.en: The Saturday holiday seemed a burden to the children.
paragraphs.cn: 星期六的假期，孩子们觉得一点也不开心。

paragraphs.en: They had no heart in their sports, and gradually gave them up.
paragraphs.cn: 他们玩游戏都提不起精神，慢慢地就不玩了。

paragraphs.en: In the afternoon Becky Thatcher found herself moping about the deserted schoolhouse yard, and feeling very melancholy.
paragraphs.cn: 下午，贝琪·撒切尔发现自己独自在空荡荡的学校操场上闲逛，感觉非常难过。

paragraphs.en: But she found nothing there to comfort her.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，她什么也没找到来安慰自己。

paragraphs.en: She soliloquized:
paragraphs.cn: 她自言自语地说：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, if I only had a brass andiron-knob again!
paragraphs.cn: “唉，要是我还能找到一个黄铜火钳把手就好了！”

paragraphs.en: But I haven’t got anything now to remember him by.”
paragraphs.cn: “可是我现在什么都没有，没法想起他了。”

paragraphs.en: And she choked back a little sob.
paragraphs.cn: 她努力忍住，没有哭出来。

paragraphs.en: Presently she stopped, and said to herself:
paragraphs.cn: 很快，她停下来，对自己说：

paragraphs.en: “It was right here.
paragraphs.cn: “就是在这里。

paragraphs.en: Oh, if it was to do over again, I wouldn’t say that—I wouldn’t say it for the whole world.
paragraphs.cn: 唉，如果能重新来过，我绝不会说那样的话——给我全世界我也不说。”

paragraphs.en: But he’s gone now; I’ll never, never, never see him any more.”
paragraphs.cn: “可是他现在走了；我再也，再也，再也见不到他了。”

paragraphs.en: This thought broke her down, and she wandered away, with tears rolling down her cheeks.
paragraphs.cn: 想到这里，她伤心地哭起来，眼泪流下脸颊，然后就走开了。

paragraphs.en: Then quite a group of boys and girls—playmates of Tom’s and Joe’s—came by, and stood looking over the paling fence and talking in reverent tones of how Tom did so-and-so the last time they saw him, and how Joe said this and that small trifle (pregnant with awful prophecy, as they could easily see now!)
paragraphs.cn: 接着，一群男孩女孩——汤姆和乔的朋友们——走了过来。他们站在木栅栏边，用很尊敬的语气说着：上次见到汤姆时，汤姆做了什么事；乔又说了哪些小事（他们现在才明白，这些小事里藏着可怕的预言啊！）。

paragraphs.en: —and each speaker pointed out the exact spot where the lost lads stood at the time, and then added something like “and I was a-standing just so—just as I am now, and as if you was him—I was as close as that—and he smiled, just this way—and then something seemed to go all over me, like—awful, you know—and I never thought what it meant, of course, but I can see now!”
paragraphs.cn: ——每个人都指着孩子们当时站的地方说：“我就站在这里，离他那么近。他就这样笑了一下，然后我全身都感觉怪怪的，很可怕。我那时不明白，但现在我懂了！”

paragraphs.en: Then there was a dispute about who saw the dead boys last in life, and many claimed that dismal distinction, and offered evidences, more or less tampered with by the witness; and when it was ultimately decided who _did_ see the departed last, and exchanged the last words with them, the lucky parties took upon themselves a sort of sacred importance, and were gaped at and envied by all the rest.
paragraphs.cn: 大家开始争论，谁是最后一个见到那些去世孩子的。很多人都说自己是，还拿出证据。最后大家决定了是谁，那些“幸运”的人就觉得自己很特别，大家都羡慕他们。

paragraphs.en: One poor chap, who had no other grandeur to offer, said with tolerably manifest pride in the remembrance:
paragraphs.cn: 有个可怜的小伙子，没什么可炫耀的，但他很自豪地回忆说：

paragraphs.en: “Well, Tom Sawyer he licked me once.”
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，汤姆·索亚他打过我一次。

paragraphs.en: But that bid for glory was a failure.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，他想得到这种荣耀的愿望失败了。

paragraphs.en: Most of the boys could say that, and so that cheapened the distinction too much.
paragraphs.cn: 因为很多孩子都能说出同样的话，所以这个“特别”就不那么特别了。

paragraphs.en: The group loitered away, still recalling memories of the lost heroes, in awed voices.
paragraphs.cn: 人们慢慢地散开了，他们还在小声地、很敬佩地回忆着那些离开的孩子们。

paragraphs.en: When the Sunday-school hour was finished, the next morning, the bell began to toll, instead of ringing in the usual way.
paragraphs.cn: 当主日学校小时过去了，第二天早上，钟敲响了，不是平时那种响法。

paragraphs.en: It was a very still Sabbath, and the mournful sound seemed in keeping with the musing hush that lay upon nature.
paragraphs.cn: 那天是安息日，很安静。这种悲伤的声音，就像大自然一样，让人安静地思考。

paragraphs.en: The villagers began to gather, loitering a moment in the vestibule to converse in whispers about the sad event.
paragraphs.cn: 村民们开始聚拢过来，他们在教堂入口处停了一会儿，小声地谈论着这件伤心事。

paragraphs.en: But there was no whispering in the house; only the funereal rustling of dresses as the women gathered to their seats disturbed the silence there.
paragraphs.cn: 但教堂里没有人说话；只有女人们坐下时，衣服发出的沙沙声打破了那里的安静。

paragraphs.en: None could remember when the little church had been so full before.
paragraphs.cn: 没有人记得这座小教堂以前什么时候坐过这么多人。

paragraphs.en: There was finally a waiting pause, an expectant dumbness, and then Aunt Polly entered, followed by Sid and Mary, and they by the Harper family, all in deep black, and the whole congregation, the old minister as well, rose reverently and stood until the mourners were seated in the front pew.
paragraphs.cn: 大家静静等了一会儿，没人说话。然后，波莉姨妈进来了，跟着是希德和玛丽，再是哈珀一家，他们都穿黑衣服。所有的人，连老牧师都恭敬地站着，直到那些伤心的人在第一排坐好。

paragraphs.en: There was another communing silence, broken at intervals by muffled sobs, and then the minister spread his hands abroad and prayed.
paragraphs.cn: 大家又安静下来，时不时传来低低的哭泣声。然后牧师伸开双手，开始祈祷。

paragraphs.en: A moving hymn was sung, and the text followed: “I am the Resurrection and the Life.”
paragraphs.cn: 接着，大家唱了一首感人的赞美诗，然后牧师念道：“我就是复活，我就是生命。”

paragraphs.en: As the service proceeded, the clergyman drew such pictures of the graces, the winning ways, and the rare promise of the lost lads that every soul there, thinking he recognized these pictures, felt a pang in remembering that he had persistently blinded himself to them always before, and had as persistently seen only faults and flaws in the poor boys.
paragraphs.cn: 仪式上，牧师讲起那些去世的孩子们有多好、多可爱、多有本事。在场的人都觉得自己认识这样的孩子，心里很痛，因为他们以前老是只看到这些孩子的缺点，没看到他们的好。

paragraphs.en: The minister related many a touching incident in the lives of the departed, too, which illustrated their sweet, generous natures, and the people could easily see, now, how noble and beautiful those episodes were, and remembered with grief that at the time they occurred they had seemed rank rascalities, well deserving of the cowhide.
paragraphs.cn: 牧师还讲了很多去世孩子感人的小故事，这些故事都说明他们很善良，很大方。现在大家才明白，这些事原来很美好，但伤心的是，他们当时却觉得这些都是坏事，觉得要狠狠地打一顿才行。

paragraphs.en: The congregation became more and more moved, as the pathetic tale went on, till at last the whole company broke down and joined the weeping mourners in a chorus of anguished sobs, the preacher himself giving way to his feelings, and crying in the pulpit.
paragraphs.cn: 随着这些感人故事的讲述，教徒们越来越感动，最后所有人都忍不住了，和哭泣的人们一起放声大哭起来。连牧师也控制不住自己的感情，在讲台上哭了起来。

paragraphs.en: There was a rustle in the gallery, which nobody noticed; a moment later the church door creaked; the minister raised his streaming eyes above his handkerchief, and stood transfixed!
paragraphs.cn: 阁楼上传来一阵沙沙声，没有人注意到；过了一会儿，教堂的门“吱呀”一声开了；牧师从手帕上方抬起他流着泪的眼睛，惊讶地呆住了！

paragraphs.en: First one and then another pair of eyes followed the minister’s, and then almost with one impulse the congregation rose and stared while the three dead boys came marching up the aisle, Tom in the lead, Joe next, and Huck, a ruin of drooping rags, sneaking sheepishly in the rear!
paragraphs.cn: 大家先是一个人，然后是另一个人，跟着牧师的目光看。然后，所有人都一起站起来，惊讶地盯着看。只见三个“死掉”的男孩大步走过走道，汤姆走在最前面，乔在中间，而哈克衣服破破烂烂地，不好意思地跟在最后面！

paragraphs.en: They had been hid in the unused gallery listening to their own funeral sermon!
paragraphs.cn: 他们一直躲在没人的楼上看台，听着大家给他们办的葬礼！

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly, Mary, and the Harpers threw themselves upon their restored ones, smothered them with kisses and poured out thanksgivings, while poor Huck stood abashed and uncomfortable, not knowing exactly what to do or where to hide from so many unwelcoming eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈、玛丽和哈珀一家冲向了他们找回来的亲人，抱着他们亲个不停，说了很多感谢的话。可怜的哈克却很不好意思，站在那里很不舒服。他不知道该做什么，也不知道怎么躲开那些不欢迎他的目光。

paragraphs.en: He wavered, and started to slink away, but Tom seized him and said:
paragraphs.cn: 他犹豫了一下，想溜走，但是汤姆抓住了他，说：

paragraphs.en: “Aunt Polly, it ain’t fair.
paragraphs.cn: “波莉姨妈, it ain’t fair.

paragraphs.en: Somebody’s got to be glad to see Huck.”
paragraphs.cn: 总得有人高兴见到哈克吧。

paragraphs.en: “And so they shall.
paragraphs.cn: 他们会的。

paragraphs.en: I’m glad to see him, poor motherless thing!”
paragraphs.cn: 我真高兴见到他，这个没妈妈的孩子真可怜！

paragraphs.en: And the loving attentions Aunt Polly lavished upon him were the one thing capable of making him more uncomfortable than he was before.
paragraphs.cn: 而波莉姨妈对他那么多的爱和关心，反而让他比以前更不舒服了。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly the minister shouted at the top of his voice: “Praise God from whom all blessings flow—_sing_!
paragraphs.cn: 牧师突然大声喊：“感谢上帝，他给了我们所有的好东西——快唱啊！

paragraphs.en: —and put your hearts in it!”
paragraphs.cn: ——要用心唱哦！”

paragraphs.en: And they did.
paragraphs.cn: 他们真的唱了。

paragraphs.en: Old Hundred swelled up with a triumphant burst, and while it shook the rafters Tom Sawyer the Pirate looked around upon the envying juveniles about him and confessed in his heart that this was the proudest moment of his life.
paragraphs.cn: 《古老百岁歌》雄壮地响起来，震得屋顶都抖了。海盗汤姆·索亚看着身边那些羡慕他的孩子们，心里觉得这是他一生中最骄傲的时刻。

paragraphs.en: As the “sold” congregation trooped out they said they would almost be willing to be made ridiculous again to hear Old Hundred sung like that once more.
paragraphs.cn: 大家被“骗”了，走出教堂时都说，就算再被笑一次，也想再听一次那样的歌。

paragraphs.en: Tom got more cuffs and kisses that day—according to Aunt Polly’s varying moods—than he had earned before in a year; and he hardly knew which expressed the most gratefulness to God and affection for himself.
paragraphs.cn: 那天，汤姆挨的打和得到的吻，随着波莉姨妈的心情变化，比他过去一年里得到的都多。他都不知道哪种方式表达了更多对上帝的感谢和对他的爱。

paragraphs.en: That was Tom’s great secret—the scheme to return home with his brother pirates and attend their own funerals.
paragraphs.cn: 那是汤姆的大秘密——他计划和他的海盗兄弟们一起回家，去参加他们自己的葬礼。

paragraphs.en: They had paddled over to the Missouri shore on a log, at dusk on Saturday, landing five or six miles below the village; they had slept in the woods at the edge of the town till nearly daylight, and had then crept through back lanes and alleys and finished their sleep in the gallery of the church among a chaos of invalided benches.
paragraphs.cn: 他们周六晚上，划着木头过河到密苏里岸边，在离村子很远的地方上了岸。他们在镇子边上的小树林里睡了一觉，天快亮才醒。然后，他们偷偷地穿过小路，到教堂楼上，在一堆坏椅子中间，继续睡觉。

paragraphs.en: At breakfast, Monday morning, Aunt Polly and Mary were very loving to Tom, and very attentive to his wants.
paragraphs.cn: 周一早上吃早饭的时候，波莉姨妈和玛丽对汤姆特别好，也很关心他想要什么。

paragraphs.en: There was an unusual amount of talk.
paragraphs.cn: 大家说了很多话。

paragraphs.en: In the course of it Aunt Polly said:
paragraphs.cn: 说着说着，波莉姨妈说：

paragraphs.en: “Well, I don’t say it wasn’t a fine joke, Tom, to keep everybody suffering ’most a week so you boys had a good time, but it is a pity you could be so hard-hearted as to let me suffer so.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，汤姆，我不是说这不是个好玩儿的玩笑。但你们为了玩，让大家难过了快一个星期，还那么狠心让我这么伤心，真是不应该。

paragraphs.en: If you could come over on a log to go to your funeral, you could have come over and give me a hint some way that you warn’t dead, but only run off.”
paragraphs.cn: 既然你能划着木头来看自己的葬礼，那你就应该过来告诉我，你没死，只是跑掉了！

paragraphs.en: “Yes, you could have done that, Tom,” said Mary; “and I believe you would if you had thought of it.”
paragraphs.cn: “是啊,你本可以那么做的,汤姆,”玛丽说,“我相信,只要你想到了,你就会那么做的。”

paragraphs.en: “Would you, Tom?” said Aunt Polly, her face lighting wistfully. “Say, now, would you, if you’d thought of it?”
paragraphs.cn: “你真会吗,汤姆?”波莉姨妈说,脸上露出渴望的神色,“说呀,要是你当时想到了,你真会那么做吗?”

paragraphs.en: “I—well, I don’t know.
paragraphs.cn: 我——嗯，我不知道。

paragraphs.en: ’Twould ’a’ spoiled everything.”
paragraphs.cn: 那样会把所有事都弄糟的。

paragraphs.en: “Tom, I hoped you loved me that much,” said Aunt Polly, with a grieved tone that discomforted the boy.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆,我原本盼着你有那么爱我呢,”波莉姨妈说,语气里的伤心让这孩子很不好受。

paragraphs.en: “It would have been something if you’d cared enough to _think_ of it, even if you didn’t _do_ it.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果你能多想想，就算没做，那也算你关心啊。

paragraphs.en: “Now, auntie, that ain’t any harm,” pleaded Mary; “it’s only Tom’s giddy way—he is always in such a rush that he never thinks of anything.”
paragraphs.cn: “姑妈,这没什么不好啦,”玛丽劝道,“这只是汤姆冒冒失失的性子——他总是急急忙忙,什么都想不到。”

paragraphs.en: “More’s the pity.
paragraphs.cn: 真可惜啊。

paragraphs.en: Sid would have thought.
paragraphs.cn: 希德会想到的。

paragraphs.en: And Sid would have come and _done_ it, too.
paragraphs.cn: 而且希德也会来做这件事的。

paragraphs.en: Tom, you’ll look back, some day, when it’s too late, and wish you’d cared a little more for me when it would have cost you so little.”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，总有一天你会后悔的，等太晚了，你会希望当时能多关心我一点点，那时候做起来多容易啊。”

paragraphs.en: “Now, auntie, you know I do care for you,” said Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “姑妈,你知道我是关心你的呀,”汤姆说。

paragraphs.en: “I’d know it better if you acted more like it.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果你表现得更好一点，我就知道了。

paragraphs.en: “I wish now I’d thought,” said Tom, with a repentant tone; “but I dreamt about you, anyway.
paragraphs.cn: “我现在真希望我当时想到了,”汤姆懊悔地说,“不过,我到底还是梦见你了呀。

paragraphs.en: That’s something, ain’t it?”
paragraphs.cn: 那也算做了点事，对吧？

paragraphs.en: “It ain’t much—a cat does that much—but it’s better than nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 那不算多——猫都能做到——但总比没有好。

paragraphs.en: What did you dream?”
paragraphs.cn: 你梦到什么了？

paragraphs.en: “Why, Wednesday night I dreamt that you was sitting over there by the bed, and Sid was sitting by the woodbox, and Mary next to him.”
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，星期三晚上我梦到你坐在床边，希德坐在柴火箱旁边，玛丽坐在他旁边。

paragraphs.en: “Well, so we did.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，我们确实梦到了。

paragraphs.en: So we always do.
paragraphs.cn: 我们总是这样。

paragraphs.en: I’m glad your dreams could take even that much trouble about us.”
paragraphs.cn: 真高兴你的梦还能想着我们。

paragraphs.en: “And I dreamt that Joe Harper’s mother was here.”
paragraphs.cn: 我还梦到乔·哈珀的妈妈在这里。

paragraphs.en: “Why, she was here!
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，她在这儿呢！

paragraphs.en: Did you dream any more?”
paragraphs.cn: 你还梦到别的了吗？

paragraphs.en: “Oh, lots.
paragraphs.cn: 哦，很多。

paragraphs.en: But it’s so dim, now.”
paragraphs.cn: 但是现在都记不清了。

paragraphs.en: “Well, try to recollect—can’t you?”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，你再想想看，好不好？”

paragraphs.en: “Somehow it seems to me that the wind—the wind blowed the—the—”
paragraphs.cn: “好像是风——风吹灭了——那个——”

paragraphs.en: “Try harder, Tom!
paragraphs.cn: “再努力想想，汤姆!

paragraphs.en: The wind did blow something.
paragraphs.cn: 风确实吹动了什么东西。

paragraphs.en: Come!”
paragraphs.cn: 快说！”

paragraphs.en: Tom pressed his fingers on his forehead an anxious minute, and then said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆紧张地用手指按着额头想了一会儿，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “I’ve got it now!
paragraphs.cn: “我想起来了！

paragraphs.en: I’ve got it now!
paragraphs.cn: 我想起来了！

paragraphs.en: It blowed the candle!”
paragraphs.cn: 是风把蜡烛吹灭了！”

paragraphs.en: “Mercy on us!
paragraphs.cn: “天哪！

paragraphs.en: Go on, Tom—go on!”
paragraphs.cn: 继续说，汤姆——继续说！”

paragraphs.en: “And it seems to me that you said, ‘Why, I believe that that door—’”
paragraphs.cn: “好像你说过，‘哎呀，我相信那扇门——’”

paragraphs.en: “Go _on_, Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: “继续说，汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: “Just let me study a moment—just a moment.
paragraphs.cn: “让我再想想——就一小会儿。

paragraphs.en: Oh, yes—you said you believed the door was open.”
paragraphs.cn: 哦，对了——你说你相信门是开着的。”

paragraphs.en: “As I’m sitting here, I did!
paragraphs.cn: “我坐在这里，我确实说过了！

paragraphs.en: Didn’t I, Mary!
paragraphs.cn: 是不是，玛丽！

paragraphs.en: Go on!”
paragraphs.cn: 继续说！”

paragraphs.en: “And then—and then—well I won’t be certain, but it seems like as if you made Sid go and—and—”
paragraphs.cn: “然后——然后——我不是很确定，但好像你让希德去——去——”

paragraphs.en: “Well?
Well?
paragraphs.cn: 嗯？

paragraphs.en: What did I make him do, Tom?
paragraphs.cn: 我让他做了什么，汤姆？

paragraphs.en: What did I make him do?”
paragraphs.cn: 我让他做了什么？”

paragraphs.en: “You made him—you—Oh, you made him shut it.”
paragraphs.cn: “你让他——你——哦，你让他把它关上。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, for the land’s sake!
paragraphs.cn: “天哪！

paragraphs.en: I never heard the beat of that in all my days!
paragraphs.cn: 我这辈子都没听过这么稀奇的事！

paragraphs.en: Don’t tell _me_ there ain’t anything in dreams, any more.
paragraphs.cn: 别再跟我说梦都是假的了。

paragraphs.en: Sereny Harper shall know of this before I’m an hour older.
paragraphs.cn: 我要马上去告诉塞伦尼·哈珀这件事。

paragraphs.en: I’d like to see her get around _this_ with her rubbage ’bout superstition.
paragraphs.cn: 我倒要看看她怎么用她那些迷信的说法来解释这个。

paragraphs.en: Go on, Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: 继续说，汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, it’s all getting just as bright as day, now.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，现在天都亮了。

paragraphs.en: Next you said I warn’t _bad_, only mischeevous and harum-scarum, and not any more responsible than—than—I think it was a colt, or something.”
paragraphs.cn: 接着你说我不是坏孩子，只是淘气，还很野，跟小马驹一样不让人省心。”

paragraphs.en: “And so it was!
paragraphs.cn: “是啊，就是这样！

paragraphs.en: Well, goodness gracious!
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，天哪！

paragraphs.en: Go on, Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: 快说啊，汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: “And then you began to cry.”
paragraphs.cn: “然后你就哭了。”

paragraphs.en: “So I did.
paragraphs.cn: “是啊，我哭了。

paragraphs.en: So I did.
paragraphs.cn: 是啊，我哭了。

paragraphs.en: Not the first time, neither.
paragraphs.cn: 也不是第一次了。

paragraphs.en: And then—”
paragraphs.cn: 然后—”

paragraphs.en: “Then Mrs. Harper she began to cry, and said Joe was just the same, and she wished she hadn’t whipped him for taking cream when she’d throwed it out her own self—”
paragraphs.cn: “然后哈珀太太也哭了，她说乔也是这样，还说她不该因为乔偷吃奶油就打他，因为她自己把奶油倒掉了—”

paragraphs.en: “Tom!
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆！

paragraphs.en: The sperrit was upon you!
paragraphs.cn: 你像被神灵附体一样！

paragraphs.en: You was a prophesying—that’s what you was doing!
paragraphs.cn: 你简直就是在预言—你就是在预言！

paragraphs.en: Land alive, go on, Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: 天哪，快说啊，汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: “Then Sid he said—he said—”
paragraphs.cn: “然后希德他说—他说—”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t think I said anything,” said Sid.
paragraphs.cn: “我想我什么也没说。”希德说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes you did, Sid,” said Mary.
paragraphs.cn: “不，你说了，希德。”玛丽说。

paragraphs.en: “Shut your heads and let Tom go on!
paragraphs.cn: “都闭嘴，让汤姆继续说！

paragraphs.en: What did he say, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: 他说什么了，汤姆？”

paragraphs.en: “He said—I _think_ he said he hoped I was better off where I was gone to, but if I’d been better sometimes—”
paragraphs.cn: “他说—我想他说他希望我去了那个地方会过得更好，但如果我平时能表现得好一点—”

paragraphs.en: “_There_, d’you hear that!
paragraphs.cn: “听，你们听到了吗！

paragraphs.en: It was his very words!”
paragraphs.cn: 他就是这么说的！”

paragraphs.en: “And you shut him up sharp.”
paragraphs.cn: “然后你立刻让他闭嘴了。”

paragraphs.en: “I lay I did!
paragraphs.cn: “我肯定做了！

paragraphs.en: There must ’a’ been an angel there.
paragraphs.cn: 那里一定有天使。

paragraphs.en: There _was_ an angel there, somewheres!”
paragraphs.cn: 那里真的有天使，就在某个地方！”

paragraphs.en: “And Mrs. Harper told about Joe scaring her with a firecracker, and you told about Peter and the Pain-killer—”
paragraphs.cn: “然后哈珀太太说乔用鞭炮吓唬她的事，你说了彼得和止痛药的事—”

paragraphs.en: “Just as true as I live!”
paragraphs.cn: “千真万确！”

paragraphs.en: “And then there was a whole lot of talk ’bout dragging the river for us, and ’bout having the funeral Sunday, and then you and old Miss Harper hugged and cried, and she went.”
paragraphs.cn: “然后大家说了很多，说要去河里打捞我们，说周日要为我们举行葬礼，然后你和老哈珀太太抱在一起哭了，她就走了。”

paragraphs.en: “It happened just so!
paragraphs.cn: “就是这样！

paragraphs.en: It happened just so, as sure as I’m a-sitting in these very tracks.
paragraphs.cn: 就是这样，我坐在这儿，是真的！

paragraphs.en: Tom, you couldn’t told it more like if you’d ’a’ seen it!
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，你说的真像，就像你亲眼看到了！

paragraphs.en: And then what?
paragraphs.cn: 然后呢？

paragraphs.en: Go on, Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: 继续说，汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: “Then I thought you prayed for me—and I could see you and hear every word you said.
paragraphs.cn: “然后我想，你为我祷告了——我能看见你，听到你说的每一句话。

paragraphs.en: And you went to bed, and I was so sorry that I took and wrote on a piece of sycamore bark, ‘We ain’t dead—we are only off being pirates,’ and put it on the table by the candle; and then you looked so good, laying there asleep, that I thought I went and leaned over and kissed you on the lips.”
paragraphs.cn: 你睡觉了，我很难过。我就在一块树皮上写：‘我们没死，只是去当海盗了。’把它放在蜡烛旁的桌上。你睡着了，看起来真好，我好像走过去，弯下腰亲了亲你的嘴。”

paragraphs.en: “Did you, Tom, _did_ you!
paragraphs.cn: “你亲了，汤姆，你真的亲了！

paragraphs.en: I just forgive you everything for that!”
paragraphs.cn: 就冲这个，我什么都原谅你了！”

paragraphs.en: And she seized the boy in a crushing embrace that made him feel like the guiltiest of villains.
paragraphs.cn: 她紧紧抱住男孩，让他觉得自己是世界上最坏的坏蛋。

paragraphs.en: “It was very kind, even though it was only a—dream,” Sid soliloquized just audibly.
paragraphs.cn: “这很善良，即使只是一个——梦，”希德轻轻地自言自语。

paragraphs.en: “Shut up, Sid!
paragraphs.cn: “闭嘴，希德！

paragraphs.en: A body does just the same in a dream as he’d do if he was awake.
paragraphs.cn: 人在梦里做的事，和醒着做的事是一样的。

paragraphs.en: Here’s a big Milum apple I’ve been saving for you, Tom, if you was ever found again—now go ’long to school.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，这是我一直为你留着的大米勒姆苹果，如果你能再被找到的话——现在去学校吧。

paragraphs.en: I’m thankful to the good God and Father of us all I’ve got you back, that’s long-suffering and merciful to them that believe on Him and keep His word, though goodness knows I’m unworthy of it, but if only the worthy ones got His blessings and had His hand to help them over the rough places, there’s few enough would smile here or ever enter into His rest when the long night comes.
paragraphs.cn: 我感谢好上帝，把我找回来了。他对相信他的人一直很耐心，很仁慈。虽然我知道自己不配，但是如果只有很好的人才能得到他的帮助，那很少人能在这里开心笑了。

paragraphs.en: Go ’long Sid, Mary, Tom—take yourselves off—you’ve hendered me long enough.”
paragraphs.cn: 去吧，希德，玛丽，汤姆——你们走吧——你们耽误我够久了。”

paragraphs.en: The children left for school, and the old lady to call on Mrs. Harper and vanquish her realism with Tom’s marvellous dream.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们去上学了，老太太去拜访哈珀太太，想用汤姆的奇妙梦想让她相信。

paragraphs.en: Sid had better judgment than to utter the thought that was in his mind as he left the house.
paragraphs.cn: 希德很聪明，他没有把离开家时心里的想法说出来。

paragraphs.en: It was this: “Pretty thin—as long a dream as that, without any mistakes in it!”
paragraphs.cn: 他的想法是：“太假了——那么长的梦，竟然一点错都没有！”

paragraphs.en: What a hero Tom was become, now!
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆现在真是个大英雄啊！

paragraphs.en: He did not go skipping and prancing, but moved with a dignified swagger as became a pirate who felt that the public eye was on him.
paragraphs.cn: 他没有蹦蹦跳跳，而是迈着神气的步子，就像一个觉得自己被大家盯着的海盗。

paragraphs.en: And indeed it was; he tried not to seem to see the looks or hear the remarks as he passed along, but they were food and drink to him.
paragraphs.cn: 确实如此；他假装没看到那些眼神，也没听到那些议论，但这些都让他很高兴。

paragraphs.en: Smaller boys than himself flocked at his heels, as proud to be seen with him, and tolerated by him, as if he had been the drummer at the head of a procession or the elephant leading a menagerie into town.
paragraphs.cn: 比他小的男孩们都跟在他后面，能和他一起出现，被他“允许”，他们都觉得很骄傲，就像他是游行队伍的鼓手，或者带领马戏团大象进城的人。

paragraphs.en: Boys of his own size pretended not to know he had been away at all; but they were consuming with envy, nevertheless.
paragraphs.cn: 和他一样大的男孩假装根本不知道他之前离开了；但他们心里仍然嫉妒得不得了。

paragraphs.en: They would have given anything to have that swarthy sun-tanned skin of his, and his glittering notoriety; and Tom would not have parted with either for a circus.
paragraphs.cn: 他们愿意付出任何代价，只为了拥有他那晒黑的皮肤，和他的英雄名声；而汤姆呢，就算用一个马戏团来换，他也不会放弃这些。

paragraphs.en: At school the children made so much of him and of Joe, and delivered such eloquent admiration from their eyes, that the two heroes were not long in becoming insufferably “stuck-up.”
paragraphs.cn: 在学校，孩子们非常看重他和乔，用眼睛表达了那么多的赞美，结果没多久，这两个英雄就变得非常“骄傲自大”了。

paragraphs.en: They began to tell their adventures to hungry listeners—but they only began; it was not a thing likely to have an end, with imaginations like theirs to furnish material.
paragraphs.cn: 他们开始把自己的冒险故事讲给那些很想听的孩子们——但他们才刚开始；这故事根本不可能讲完，因为他们的想象力太丰富了，总有新的内容。

paragraphs.en: And finally, when they got out their pipes and went serenely puffing around, the very summit of glory was reached.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，当他们拿出烟斗，悠闲地吸着烟四处走动时，他们的荣耀达到了最高点。

paragraphs.en: Tom decided that he could be independent of Becky Thatcher now.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆觉得他现在可以不用靠贝琪·撒切尔了。

paragraphs.en: Glory was sufficient.
paragraphs.cn: 荣耀就足够了。

paragraphs.en: He would live for glory.
paragraphs.cn: 他想变得很了不起。

paragraphs.en: Now that he was distinguished, maybe she would be wanting to “make up.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在他变得很厉害了，也许她会想跟他和好。

paragraphs.en: Well, let her—she should see that he could be as indifferent as some other people.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，让她来吧——她应该知道，他也能像别人一样，装作不在乎。

paragraphs.en: Presently she arrived.
paragraphs.cn: 她很快就来了。

paragraphs.en: Tom pretended not to see her.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆假装没看到她。

paragraphs.en: He moved away and joined a group of boys and girls and began to talk.
paragraphs.cn: 他走开了，走到一群小朋友中间，开始和他们说话。

paragraphs.en: Soon he observed that she was tripping gayly back and forth with flushed face and dancing eyes, pretending to be busy chasing schoolmates, and screaming with laughter when she made a capture; but he noticed that she always made her captures in his vicinity, and that she seemed to cast a conscious eye in his direction at such times, too.
paragraphs.cn: 很快他就看到她开心地跑来跑去，脸红扑扑的，眼睛亮亮的。她假装在追着同学玩，抓到人就大声笑。但他发现她总是在他旁边抓人，而且每次抓到人，好像都会偷偷看他一眼。

paragraphs.en: It gratified all the vicious vanity that was in him; and so, instead of winning him, it only “set him up” the more and made him the more diligent to avoid betraying that he knew she was about.
paragraphs.cn: 这让他心里暗暗得意。这不但没有让她打动他，反而让他更骄傲，更努力地假装不知道她在身边。

paragraphs.en: Presently she gave over skylarking, and moved irresolutely about, sighing once or twice and glancing furtively and wistfully toward Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 不一会儿，她不玩了，没精打采地走来走去，叹了两口气，偷偷地、很希望地看向汤姆。

paragraphs.en: Then she observed that now Tom was talking more particularly to Amy Lawrence than to any one else.
paragraphs.cn: 然后她看到，现在汤姆只跟艾米·劳伦斯说话，不跟别人说。

paragraphs.en: She felt a sharp pang and grew disturbed and uneasy at once.
paragraphs.cn: 她心里很难受，马上就觉得不开心、不舒服。

paragraphs.en: She tried to go away, but her feet were treacherous, and carried her to the group instead.
paragraphs.cn: 她想走开，可是脚不听话，反而把她带到了那个小组旁边。

paragraphs.en: She said to a girl almost at Tom’s elbow—with sham vivacity:
paragraphs.cn: 她对一个就在汤姆旁边的女孩子说，假装自己很有精神：

paragraphs.en: “Why, Mary Austin! you bad girl, why didn’t you come to Sunday-school?”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，玛丽奥斯汀！你这个小坏蛋，怎么没来找主日学校呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I did come—didn’t you see me?”
paragraphs.cn: “我来了呀——你没看到我吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, no!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，没有啊！

paragraphs.en: Did you?
paragraphs.cn: 你来了吗？

paragraphs.en: Where did you sit?”
paragraphs.cn: 你坐在哪里呀？”

paragraphs.en: “I was in Miss Peters’ class, where I always go.
paragraphs.cn: “我在彼得斯老师的班上，我总是在那里上课的呀。

paragraphs.en: I saw _you_.”
paragraphs.cn: 我看到了你！”

paragraphs.en: “Did you?
paragraphs.cn: “是吗？

paragraphs.en: Why, it’s funny I didn’t see you.
paragraphs.cn: 真奇怪我没看到你。

paragraphs.en: I wanted to tell you about the picnic.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想跟你说野餐的事儿。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, that’s jolly.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，那太好了！

paragraphs.en: Who’s going to give it?”
paragraphs.cn: 谁来办呢？”

paragraphs.en: “My ma’s going to let me have one.”
paragraphs.cn: “我妈妈要给我办一个野餐。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, goody; I hope she’ll let _me_ come.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，太好了！我希望她能让我去。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, she will.
paragraphs.cn: “她会让你来的。

paragraphs.en: The picnic’s for me.
paragraphs.cn: 这个野餐是为我办的。

paragraphs.en: She’ll let anybody come that I want, and I want you.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想要谁来，她就让谁来，我希望你来。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s ever so nice.
paragraphs.cn: “那可真好。

paragraphs.en: When is it going to be?”
paragraphs.cn: 什么时候去呢？”

paragraphs.en: “By and by.
paragraphs.cn: “过一阵子吧。

paragraphs.en: Maybe about vacation.”
paragraphs.cn: 也许是放假的时候。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, won’t it be fun!
paragraphs.cn: “噢，那一定很好玩！

paragraphs.en: You going to have all the girls and boys?”
paragraphs.cn: 你要把所有的男孩和女孩都叫上吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, every one that’s friends to me—or wants to be”; and she glanced ever so furtively at Tom, but he talked right along to Amy Lawrence about the terrible storm on the island, and how the lightning tore the great sycamore tree “all to flinders” while he was “standing within three feet of it.”
paragraphs.cn: “是的，所有是我的朋友，或者想成为我朋友的人都来。”她偷偷地看了汤姆一眼，但他还是不停地和艾米·劳伦斯说岛上可怕的暴风雨，说闪电怎么把那棵大梧桐树劈得粉碎，当时他离树只有三英尺远。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, may I come?” said Grace Miller.
paragraphs.cn: “噢，我能来吗？”格蕾丝·米勒说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes.”
“And me?” said Sally Rogers.
paragraphs.cn: “还有我呢？”莎莉·罗杰斯说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes.”
“And me, too?” said Susy Harper. “And Joe?”
paragraphs.cn: “还有我吗？”苏西·哈珀说。“乔呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes.”
And so on, with clapping of joyful hands till all the group had begged for invitations but Tom and Amy.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样，大家开心地拍着手，除了汤姆和艾米，所有人都求着要来参加。

paragraphs.en: Then Tom turned coolly away, still talking, and took Amy with him.
paragraphs.cn: 然后汤姆冷冷地转过身，还在说着话，带着艾米走了。

paragraphs.en: Becky’s lips trembled and the tears came to her eyes; she hid these signs with a forced gayety and went on chattering, but the life had gone out of the picnic, now, and out of everything else; she got away as soon as she could and hid herself and had what her sex call “a good cry.”
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪的嘴唇颤抖了，眼泪涌了出来；她强装开心，继续说笑，来掩饰这些。但野餐的乐趣，还有其他所有的乐趣，一下子都没有了。她赶紧跑开，找个地方躲起来，好好地哭了一场。

paragraphs.en: Then she sat moody, with wounded pride, till the bell rang.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，她心里很受伤，闷闷不乐地坐着，直到铃声响起。

paragraphs.en: She roused up, now, with a vindictive cast in her eye, and gave her plaited tails a shake and said she knew what _she’d_ do.
paragraphs.cn: 她一下子振作起来，眼里闪着不服气的光芒，甩了甩她的辫子，说她知道自己要怎么做了。

paragraphs.en: At recess Tom continued his flirtation with Amy with jubilant self-satisfaction.
paragraphs.cn: 课间休息时，汤姆继续和艾米亲近，心里得意洋洋。

paragraphs.en: And he kept drifting about to find Becky and lacerate her with the performance.
paragraphs.cn: 他一直在附近转悠，想找到贝琪，用这样的举动去伤害她。

paragraphs.en: At last he spied her, but there was a sudden falling of his mercury.
paragraphs.cn: 他终于看见了她，但他突然不高兴了。

paragraphs.en: She was sitting cosily on a little bench behind the schoolhouse looking at a picture-book with Alfred Temple—and so absorbed were they, and their heads so close together over the book, that they did not seem to be conscious of anything in the world besides.
paragraphs.cn: 她舒服地坐在学校后面的一张小板凳上，正和阿尔弗雷德·坦普尔一起看一本图画书。他们看得那么入迷，头靠得那么近，好像世界上除了他们，什么都没有了。

paragraphs.en: Jealousy ran red-hot through Tom’s veins.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆心里嫉妒得厉害。

paragraphs.en: He began to hate himself for throwing away the chance Becky had offered for a reconciliation.
paragraphs.cn: 他开始讨厌自己，因为他错过了贝琪本来给了他和好的机会。

paragraphs.en: He called himself a fool, and all the hard names he could think of.
paragraphs.cn: 他骂自己是个笨蛋，还想出了所有能想到的坏词骂自己。

paragraphs.en: He wanted to cry with vexation.
paragraphs.cn: 他气得想哭。

paragraphs.en: Amy chatted happily along, as they walked, for her heart was singing, but Tom’s tongue had lost its function.
paragraphs.cn: 艾米开心地一路走一路聊着天，因为她心里很高兴，但汤姆却一句话也说不出来了。

paragraphs.en: He did not hear what Amy was saying, and whenever she paused expectantly he could only stammer an awkward assent, which was as often misplaced as otherwise.
paragraphs.cn: 他根本没听艾米在说什么，每当艾米停下来等着他回答的时候，他只会结结巴巴地胡乱答应一声，而且常常答非所问。

paragraphs.en: He kept drifting to the rear of the schoolhouse, again and again, to sear his eyeballs with the hateful spectacle there.
paragraphs.cn: 他一次又一次地往学校后面走去，去看看那里让他生气的一幕。

paragraphs.en: He could not help it.
paragraphs.cn: 他忍不住。

paragraphs.en: And it maddened him to see, as he thought he saw, that Becky Thatcher never once suspected that he was even in the land of the living.
paragraphs.cn: 他气坏了，因为他觉得贝琪·撒切尔根本没发现他还活着呢。

paragraphs.en: But she did see, nevertheless; and she knew she was winning her fight, too, and was glad to see him suffer as she had suffered.
paragraphs.cn: 但她其实看见了。她知道自己要赢了，看到他也像她一样难受，她心里很高兴。

paragraphs.en: Amy’s happy prattle became intolerable.
paragraphs.cn: 艾米开心地说个不停，让他觉得实在受不了了。

paragraphs.en: Tom hinted at things he had to attend to; things that must be done; and time was fleeting.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆暗示自己有好多事要忙，时间过得真快。

paragraphs.en: But in vain—the girl chirped on.
paragraphs.cn: 可是没用——那个女孩还是叽叽喳喳地说着。

paragraphs.en: Tom thought, “Oh, hang her, ain’t I ever going to get rid of her?”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆心想：“哎呀，真烦她！我什么时候才能摆脱她啊？”

paragraphs.en: At last he must be attending to those things—and she said artlessly that she would be “around” when school let out.
paragraphs.cn: 最后他只好说他真的有事要忙了——她却天真地说，放学时还会回来找他呢。

paragraphs.en: And he hastened away, hating her for it.
paragraphs.cn: 他赶紧跑走了，心里很讨厌她。

paragraphs.en: “Any other boy!”
paragraphs.cn: “换成别的男孩都行！”

paragraphs.en: Tom thought, grating his teeth.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆咬着牙想。

paragraphs.en: “Any boy in the whole town but that Saint Louis smarty that thinks he dresses so fine and is aristocracy!
paragraphs.cn: “整个镇上谁都行，就是不能是那个圣路易斯来的小聪明蛋！他觉得自己穿得那么好看，是了不起的人！

paragraphs.en: Oh, all right, I licked you the first day you ever saw this town, mister, and I’ll lick you again!
paragraphs.cn: 哼，好吧，你第一天到这镇上的时候，我就打赢过你了，小子，我还会再打赢你一次！

paragraphs.en: You just wait till I catch you out!
paragraphs.cn: 你等着瞧吧，等我抓到你！

paragraphs.en: I’ll just take and—”
paragraphs.cn: 我一定会好好教训你——”

paragraphs.en: And he went through the motions of thrashing an imaginary boy—pummelling the air, and kicking and gouging.
paragraphs.cn: 他假装在揍一个不存在的男孩——对着空气拳打脚踢。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, you do, do you?
paragraphs.cn: “哦，你真的要这样吗？

paragraphs.en: You holler ’nough, do you?
paragraphs.cn: 你喊‘够了’，是吗？

paragraphs.en: Now, then, let that learn you!”
paragraphs.cn: 现在，好了，让你学个乖！”

paragraphs.en: And so the imaginary flogging was finished to his satisfaction.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样，这场假装的痛打让他觉得很满意地结束了。

paragraphs.en: Tom fled home at noon.
paragraphs.cn: 中午，汤姆跑回家了。

paragraphs.en: His conscience could not endure any more of Amy’s grateful happiness, and his jealousy could bear no more of the other distress.
paragraphs.cn: 他心里受不了艾米那种开心的样子了，也受不了别人再难过了。

paragraphs.en: Becky resumed her picture inspections with Alfred, but as the minutes dragged along and no Tom came to suffer, her triumph began to cloud and she lost interest; gravity and absentmindedness followed, and then melancholy; two or three times she pricked up her ear at a footstep, but it was a false hope; no Tom came.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪又和阿尔弗雷德一起看画了。但时间一分一秒过去，汤姆还是没有来难过。她的得意劲儿就没了，也失去了兴趣。接着她变得严肃，心不在焉，然后又很伤心。她两三次听到脚步声都竖起耳朵，但都是白高兴一场；汤姆没有来。

paragraphs.en: At last she grew entirely miserable and wished she hadn’t carried it so far.
paragraphs.cn: 最后她变得非常难过，希望自己没有做得太过分。

paragraphs.en: When poor Alfred, seeing that he was losing her, he did not know how, kept exclaiming: “Oh, here’s a jolly one! look at this!” she lost patience at last, and said, “Oh, don’t bother me!
paragraphs.cn: 可怜的阿尔弗雷德发现自己快要失去她了，却不知道为什么，他不停地叫着：“哦，这个真好玩！快看这个！”她终于没了耐心，说：“哦，别烦我了！

paragraphs.en: I don’t care for them!” and burst into tears, and got up and walked away.
paragraphs.cn: 我才不喜欢这些呢！”说着就大哭起来，然后站起来走开了。

paragraphs.en: Alfred dropped alongside and was going to try to comfort her, but she said:
paragraphs.cn: 阿尔弗雷德走到她身边，想安慰她，但她说：

paragraphs.en: “Go away and leave me alone, can’t you!
paragraphs.cn: “你走开，别管我，好不好啊！

paragraphs.en: I hate you!”
paragraphs.cn: 我讨厌你！”

paragraphs.en: So the boy halted, wondering what he could have done—for she had said she would look at pictures all through the nooning—and she walked on, crying.
paragraphs.cn: 于是男孩停住了，他不知道自己做错了什么——因为她之前还说整个中午都要看画呢——她却继续走着，哭个不停。

paragraphs.en: Then Alfred went musing into the deserted schoolhouse.
paragraphs.cn: 然后阿尔弗雷德心事重重地走进了空荡荡的校舍。

paragraphs.en: He was humiliated and angry.
paragraphs.cn: 他感到又羞又气。

paragraphs.en: He easily guessed his way to the truth—the girl had simply made a convenience of him to vent her spite upon Tom Sawyer.
paragraphs.cn: 他很快就猜到真相了——那个女孩只是利用他，把气撒在 汤姆·索亚 身上。

paragraphs.en: He was far from hating Tom the less when this thought occurred to him.
paragraphs.cn: 当他想到这个时，对 汤姆 的恨一点也没少。

paragraphs.en: He wished there was some way to get that boy into trouble without much risk to himself.
paragraphs.cn: 他希望有个办法能让那个男孩惹麻烦，又不会给自己带来太多风险。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s spelling-book fell under his eye.
paragraphs.cn: 他看到了 汤姆 的拼写书。

paragraphs.en: Here was his opportunity.
paragraphs.cn: 机会来了。

paragraphs.en: He gratefully opened to the lesson for the afternoon and poured ink upon the page.
paragraphs.cn: 他很高兴地翻到下午的课文，然后把墨水倒在书页上。

paragraphs.en: Becky, glancing in at a window behind him at the moment, saw the act, and moved on, without discovering herself.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪 当时正好从他身后的窗户往里看，看到了这一切，然后就走开了，没有让他发现。

paragraphs.en: She started homeward, now, intending to find Tom and tell him; Tom would be thankful and their troubles would be healed.
paragraphs.cn: 她现在开始回家，想去找 汤姆 告诉他这件事； 汤姆 会很感激，他们的麻烦也会解决。

paragraphs.en: Before she was half way home, however, she had changed her mind.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，她还没走到一半，就改变主意了。

paragraphs.en: The thought of Tom’s treatment of her when she was talking about her picnic came scorching back and filled her with shame.
paragraphs.cn: 想到 汤姆 之前在她讲野餐时对她的态度，她又感到羞耻。

paragraphs.en: She resolved to let him get whipped on the damaged spelling-book’s account, and to hate him forever, into the bargain.
paragraphs.cn: 她决定让他因为那本弄坏的拼写书挨打，而且永远恨他。

paragraphs.en: Tom arrived at home in a dreary mood, and the first thing his aunt said to him showed him that he had brought his sorrows to an unpromising market:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 心情很不好地回到家，他阿姨说的第一句话就让他知道，他的烦恼在这里不会有好结果：

paragraphs.en: “Tom, I’ve a notion to skin you alive!”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，我真想好好教训你！”

paragraphs.en: “Auntie, what have I done?”
paragraphs.cn: “阿姨，我做了什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Well, you’ve done enough.
paragraphs.cn: “你做的事情够多了。

paragraphs.en: Here I go over to Sereny Harper, like an old softy, expecting I’m going to make her believe all that rubbage about that dream, when lo and behold you she’d found out from Joe that you was over here and heard all the talk we had that night.
paragraphs.cn: 我像个老好人一样跑到 塞伦尼·哈珀 那里去，以为能让她相信所有关于那个梦的废话，结果她已经从乔那里知道你在这里，而且听到了我们那天晚上所有的谈话。

paragraphs.en: Tom, I don’t know what is to become of a boy that will act like that.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，我真不知道像你这样的孩子以后会怎么样。

paragraphs.en: It makes me feel so bad to think you could let me go to Sereny Harper and make such a fool of myself and never say a word.”
paragraphs.cn: 想到你让我去 塞伦尼·哈珀 那里出丑，却一句话也不说，我心里就很难过。”

paragraphs.en: This was a new aspect of the thing.
paragraphs.cn: 事情有了新的变化。

paragraphs.en: His smartness of the morning had seemed to Tom a good joke before, and very ingenious.
paragraphs.cn: 他早上耍的小聪明，之前他还觉得是个很棒的玩笑，也很巧妙。

paragraphs.en: It merely looked mean and shabby now.
paragraphs.cn: 现在看来，这事就显得又卑鄙又丢人。

paragraphs.en: He hung his head and could not think of anything to say for a moment.
paragraphs.cn: 他低着头，一时想不出说什么。

paragraphs.en: Then he said:
paragraphs.cn: 然后他说：

paragraphs.en: “Auntie, I wish I hadn’t done it—but I didn’t think.”
paragraphs.cn: “阿姨，我真希望我没做那件事——可是我没想那么多。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, child, you never think.
paragraphs.cn: “哎，孩子，你从来都不想事儿。

paragraphs.en: You never think of anything but your own selfishness.
paragraphs.cn: 你心里只想着你自己。

paragraphs.en: You could think to come all the way over here from Jackson’s Island in the night to laugh at our troubles, and you could think to fool me with a lie about a dream; but you couldn’t ever think to pity us and save us from sorrow.”
paragraphs.cn: 你能想到晚上从杰克逊岛跑过来嘲笑我们的烦恼，你也能想到用一个关于梦的谎话来骗我；但你却从来没想过可怜我们，救我们摆脱痛苦。”

paragraphs.en: “Auntie, I know now it was mean, but I didn’t mean to be mean.
paragraphs.cn: “阿姨，我现在知道那样做很坏，但我不是故意要那么坏的。

paragraphs.en: I didn’t, honest.
paragraphs.cn: 我真的没有。

paragraphs.en: And besides, I didn’t come over here to laugh at you that night.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且，那天晚上我来也不是为了笑你。”

paragraphs.en: “What did you come for, then?”
paragraphs.cn: “那你来干什么呢？”

paragraphs.en: “It was to tell you not to be uneasy about us, because we hadn’t got drownded.”
paragraphs.cn: “我是来告诉你，别为我们担心，因为我们没有淹死。”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, Tom, I would be the thankfullest soul in this world if I could believe you ever had as good a thought as that, but you know you never did—and I know it, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆, 汤姆，如果你真的有过这样的好想法，我就是世界上最感激的人了。可是你知道你从来没有过——我知道的，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: “Indeed and ’deed I did, auntie—I wish I may never stir if I didn’t.”
paragraphs.cn: “我真的有啊，姨妈——要是我没有，我就不活了。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Tom, don’t lie—don’t do it.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，汤姆，别撒谎——不要这样。

paragraphs.en: It only makes things a hundred times worse.”
paragraphs.cn: 那样只会让事情变得糟一百倍。”

paragraphs.en: “It ain’t a lie, auntie; it’s the truth.
paragraphs.cn: “这不是谎话，姨妈；这是真的。

paragraphs.en: I wanted to keep you from grieving—that was all that made me come.”
paragraphs.cn: 我只是想让你不要难过——我来就是为了这个。”

paragraphs.en: “I’d give the whole world to believe that—it would cover up a power of sins, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “我真想相信那是真的——那样就能抵消好多不好的事了，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: I’d ’most be glad you’d run off and acted so bad.
paragraphs.cn: 我几乎都会为你跑掉还做了坏事而高兴了。

paragraphs.en: But it ain’t reasonable; because, why didn’t you tell me, child?”
paragraphs.cn: 可是这不合情理；因为，你为什么不告诉我呢，孩子？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, you see, when you got to talking about the funeral, I just got all full of the idea of our coming and hiding in the church, and I couldn’t somehow bear to spoil it.
paragraphs.cn: “你看，当你开始说葬礼的时候，我就满脑子想着我们来教堂躲起来，我真舍不得把它毁掉。

paragraphs.en: So I just put the bark back in my pocket and kept mum.”
paragraphs.cn: 所以我把那块树皮又放回口袋里，没有说话。”

paragraphs.en: “What bark?”
paragraphs.cn: “什么树皮？”

paragraphs.en: “The bark I had wrote on to tell you we’d gone pirating.
paragraphs.cn: “就是我写字告诉你我们去当海盗的那块树皮。

paragraphs.en: I wish, now, you’d waked up when I kissed you—I do, honest.”
paragraphs.cn: 我现在真希望你当时被我亲醒了——真的，我发誓。”

paragraphs.en: The hard lines in his aunt’s face relaxed and a sudden tenderness dawned in her eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 他姨妈脸上的严肃表情变柔和了，眼睛里也突然充满了温柔。”

paragraphs.en: “_Did_ you kiss me, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: “你真的亲了我吗，汤姆？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, yes, I did.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，是啊，我亲了。”

paragraphs.en: “Are you sure you did, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: “你确定你亲了吗，汤姆？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, yes, I did, auntie—certain sure.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，是的，姨妈——千真万确。”

paragraphs.en: “What did you kiss me for, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: “你为什么要亲我呢，汤姆？”

paragraphs.en: “Because I loved you so, and you laid there moaning and I was so sorry.”
paragraphs.cn: “因为我太爱你了，你躺在那里哼哼着，我很心疼。”

paragraphs.en: The words sounded like truth.
paragraphs.cn: 那些话听起来是真的。”

paragraphs.en: The old lady could not hide a tremor in her voice when she said:
paragraphs.cn: 老太太说话的时候，声音都有点颤抖，藏不住了：

paragraphs.en: “Kiss me again, Tom!
paragraphs.cn: “再亲我一下，汤姆！

paragraphs.en: —and be off with you to school, now, and don’t bother me any more.”
paragraphs.cn: ——现在快去上学，别再烦我了。”

paragraphs.en: The moment he was gone, she ran to a closet and got out the ruin of a jacket which Tom had gone pirating in.
paragraphs.cn: 他一走，她就跑到柜子前，拿出汤姆穿去当海盗的旧夹克。

paragraphs.en: Then she stopped, with it in her hand, and said to herself:
paragraphs.cn: 她拿着夹克停了下来，自言自语道：”

paragraphs.en: “No, I don’t dare.
paragraphs.cn: “不，我不敢。

paragraphs.en: Poor boy, I reckon he’s lied about it—but it’s a blessed, blessed lie, there’s such a comfort come from it.
paragraphs.cn: 可怜的孩子，我想他说了谎——但这个谎太棒了，太棒了，让人心里很舒服。

paragraphs.en: I hope the Lord—I _know_ the Lord will forgive him, because it was such good-heartedness in him to tell it.
paragraphs.cn: 我希望上帝——我知道上帝会原谅他，因为他心地善良，才说了这个谎。

paragraphs.en: But I don’t want to find out it’s a lie.
paragraphs.cn: 但我不想知道这是个谎言。

paragraphs.en: I won’t look.”
paragraphs.cn: 我不看了。”

paragraphs.en: She put the jacket away, and stood by musing a minute.
paragraphs.cn: 她把外套收起来，站着想了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: Twice she put out her hand to take the garment again, and twice she refrained.
paragraphs.cn: 她两次伸手想再拿那件衣服，两次都停住了。

paragraphs.en: Once more she ventured, and this time she fortified herself with the thought: “It’s a good lie—it’s a good lie—I won’t let it grieve me.”
paragraphs.cn: 她又试了一次，这次她告诉自己：“这是个好谎言——是个好谎言——我不会因此难过。”

paragraphs.en: So she sought the jacket pocket.
paragraphs.cn: 于是她找外套的口袋。

paragraphs.en: A moment later she was reading Tom’s piece of bark through flowing tears and saying: “I could forgive the boy, now, if he’d committed a million sins!”
paragraphs.cn: 不一会儿，她流着泪读着汤姆的那块树皮，说：“就算他犯了一百万个错，我现在也能原谅他！”

paragraphs.en: There was something about Aunt Polly’s manner, when she kissed Tom, that swept away his low spirits and made him lighthearted and happy again.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈亲吻汤姆时，她的样子让他的坏心情一扫而空，他又变得轻松快乐了。

paragraphs.en: He started to school and had the luck of coming upon Becky Thatcher at the head of Meadow Lane.
paragraphs.cn: 他去上学，正好在草地小巷的尽头遇到了贝琪·撒切尔。

paragraphs.en: His mood always determined his manner.
paragraphs.cn: 他的心情总是决定他的举止。

paragraphs.en: Without a moment’s hesitation he ran to her and said:
paragraphs.cn: 他毫不犹豫地跑到她身边说：

paragraphs.en: “I acted mighty mean today, Becky, and I’m so sorry.
paragraphs.cn: “我今天表现得很坏，贝琪，我真抱歉。

paragraphs.en: I won’t ever, ever do that way again, as long as ever I live—please make up, won’t you?”
paragraphs.cn: 我再也不会那样做了，永远不会了——请你原谅我，好吗？”

paragraphs.en: The girl stopped and looked him scornfully in the face:
paragraphs.cn: 女孩停下来，轻蔑地看了他一眼：

paragraphs.en: “I’ll thank you to keep yourself _to_ yourself, Mr. Thomas Sawyer.
paragraphs.cn: “谢谢你管好你自己，托马斯·索亚先生。

paragraphs.en: I’ll never speak to you again.”
paragraphs.cn: 我再也不会跟你说话了。”

paragraphs.en: She tossed her head and passed on.
paragraphs.cn: 她一甩头，走开了。

paragraphs.en: Tom was so stunned that he had not even presence of mind enough to say “Who cares, Miss Smarty?” until the right time to say it had gone by.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆惊呆了，甚至没想到说“谁在乎啊，小聪明小姐？”，直到说这句话的好时机过去了。

paragraphs.en: So he said nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 所以他什么也没说。

paragraphs.en: But he was in a fine rage, nevertheless.
paragraphs.cn: 但他还是很生气。

paragraphs.en: He moped into the schoolyard wishing she were a boy, and imagining how he would trounce her if she were.
paragraphs.cn: 他闷闷不乐地走进校园，希望她是个男孩，想着如果她是个男孩，他会怎么揍她。

paragraphs.en: He presently encountered her and delivered a stinging remark as he passed.
paragraphs.cn: 他很快又遇到了她，经过时说了一句很刺耳的话。

paragraphs.en: She hurled one in return, and the angry breach was complete.
paragraphs.cn: 她也回敬了一句，两人彻底吵翻了。

paragraphs.en: It seemed to Becky, in her hot resentment, that she could hardly wait for school to “take in,” she was so impatient to see Tom flogged for the injured spelling-book.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪心里很气，她觉得她简直等不及学校开课了，她太想看到汤姆因为弄坏了拼写书而被打屁股了。

paragraphs.en: If she had had any lingering notion of exposing Alfred Temple, Tom’s offensive fling had driven it entirely away.
paragraphs.cn: 如果她还有一点点想揭穿阿尔弗雷德·坦普尔的念头，汤姆那句伤人的话也把它完全打消了。

paragraphs.en: Poor girl, she did not know how fast she was nearing trouble herself.
paragraphs.cn: 可怜的女孩，她不知道自己很快也要惹麻烦了。

paragraphs.en: The master, Mr. Dobbins, had reached middle age with an unsatisfied ambition.
paragraphs.cn: 老师多宾斯先生已经到了中年，但他有一个没有实现的愿望。

paragraphs.en: The darling of his desires was, to be a doctor, but poverty had decreed that he should be nothing higher than a village schoolmaster.
paragraphs.cn: 他好想当医生，可是家里穷，就只能当村里的小学老师。

paragraphs.en: Every day he took a mysterious book out of his desk and absorbed himself in it at times when no classes were reciting.
paragraphs.cn: 每天，他都会从抽屉里拿出一本很神秘的书，没上课的时候就看。

paragraphs.en: He kept that book under lock and key.
paragraphs.cn: 他把那本书锁得紧紧的。

paragraphs.en: There was not an urchin in school but was perishing to have a glimpse of it, but the chance never came.
paragraphs.cn: 学校里的小朋友都特别想看一眼那本书，可就是没机会。

paragraphs.en: Every boy and girl had a theory about the nature of that book; but no two theories were alike, and there was no way of getting at the facts in the case.
paragraphs.cn: 每个小朋友都猜那本书里写了什么，可大家猜的都不一样，也没人知道到底是什么。

paragraphs.en: Now, as Becky was passing by the desk, which stood near the door, she noticed that the key was in the lock!
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪 经过桌子旁边时，桌子就在门边，她发现钥匙还在锁里！

paragraphs.en: It was a precious moment.
paragraphs.cn: 这是一个很棒的机会。

paragraphs.en: She glanced around; found herself alone, and the next instant she had the book in her hands.
paragraphs.cn: 她四处看了看，发现没人，下一秒书就在她手上了。

paragraphs.en: The titlepage—Professor Somebody’s _Anatomy_—carried no information to her mind; so she began to turn the leaves.
paragraphs.cn: 封面写着“某某教授的《人体解剖学》”，她看不懂，就一页一页地翻起来。

paragraphs.en: She came at once upon a handsomely engraved and colored frontispiece—a human figure, stark naked.
paragraphs.cn: 她一下子就看到了一张印得很漂亮、涂了颜色的画——画着一个光着身子的人。

paragraphs.en: At that moment a shadow fell on the page and Tom Sawyer stepped in at the door and caught a glimpse of the picture.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这时，一个影子遮住了书页，汤姆·索亚 从门口走了进来，也看到了那幅画。

paragraphs.en: Becky snatched at the book to close it, and had the hard luck to tear the pictured page half down the middle.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪 赶紧抓起书想把它合上，却不小心把那张画撕成了两半。

paragraphs.en: She thrust the volume into the desk, turned the key, and burst out crying with shame and vexation.
paragraphs.cn: 她把书塞进抽屉里，转了转钥匙，然后又羞又气地大哭起来。

paragraphs.en: “Tom Sawyer, you are just as mean as you can be, to sneak up on a person and look at what they’re looking at.”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆·索亚，你真是太坏了，竟然偷偷摸摸地过来，看人家在看什么。”

paragraphs.en: “How could I know you was looking at anything?”
paragraphs.cn: “我怎么知道你在看东西呀？”

paragraphs.en: “You ought to be ashamed of yourself, Tom Sawyer; you know you’re going to tell on me, and oh, what shall I do, what shall I do!
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆·索亚，你真应该感到不好意思！你知道你会去告状的，哎呀，我该怎么办，我该怎么办！

paragraphs.en: I’ll be whipped, and I never was whipped in school.”
paragraphs.cn: 我会被打屁股的，我在学校从来没被打过呀！”

paragraphs.en: Then she stamped her little foot and said:
paragraphs.cn: 然后她跺了跺小脚，说：

paragraphs.en: “_Be_ so mean if you want to!
paragraphs.cn: “你想多坏就多坏吧！

paragraphs.en: I know something that’s going to happen.
paragraphs.cn: 我知道会有什么事发生！

paragraphs.en: You just wait and you’ll see!
paragraphs.cn: 你等着瞧吧！

paragraphs.en: Hateful, hateful, hateful!”
paragraphs.cn: 讨厌，讨厌，讨厌！”

paragraphs.en: —and she flung out of the house with a new explosion of crying.
paragraphs.cn: ——她又大哭起来，冲出了屋子。

paragraphs.en: Tom stood still, rather flustered by this onslaught.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 呆呆地站着，被她这样一说，有点慌张。

paragraphs.en: Presently he said to himself:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，他自言自语地说：

paragraphs.en: “What a curious kind of a fool a girl is!
paragraphs.cn: “女孩真是奇怪的傻瓜！

paragraphs.en: Never been licked in school!
paragraphs.cn: 没在学校被打过屁股！

paragraphs.en: Shucks!
paragraphs.cn: 哼！

paragraphs.en: What’s a licking!
paragraphs.cn: 打屁股算什么呀！

paragraphs.en: That’s just like a girl—they’re so thin-skinned and chicken-hearted.
paragraphs.cn: 这就是女孩的样子——她们太娇气，太胆小了。

paragraphs.en: Well, of course I ain’t going to tell old Dobbins on this little fool, because there’s other ways of getting even on her, that ain’t so mean; but what of it?
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，我当然不会把这小笨蛋的事告诉老 多宾斯。因为有别的方法可以跟她扯平，没那么坏。但这又怎样呢？

paragraphs.en: Old Dobbins will ask who it was tore his book.
paragraphs.cn: 老 多宾斯 会问是谁撕了他的书。

paragraphs.en: Nobody’ll answer.
paragraphs.cn: 没人会回答。

paragraphs.en: Then he’ll do just the way he always does—ask first one and then t’other, and when he comes to the right girl he’ll know it, without any telling.
paragraphs.cn: 然后他就会像往常一样，先问一个，再问另一个。当他问到那个女孩时，他不用问也会知道。

paragraphs.en: Girls’ faces always tell on them.
paragraphs.cn: 女孩的脸上总会露出秘密。

paragraphs.en: They ain’t got any backbone.
paragraphs.cn: 她们没有勇气。

paragraphs.en: She’ll get licked.
paragraphs.cn: 她会被打的。

paragraphs.en: Well, it’s a kind of a tight place for Becky Thatcher, because there ain’t any way out of it.”
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，这对 贝琪·撒切尔 来说是个麻烦，因为没法脱身。

paragraphs.en: Tom conned the thing a moment longer, and then added: “All right, though; she’d like to see me in just such a fix—let her sweat it out!”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 又想了一会儿，然后说：“好吧，她也想看到我这样为难——让她自己尝尝滋味吧！”

paragraphs.en: Tom joined the mob of skylarking scholars outside.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 加入了外面一群爱玩闹的同学。

paragraphs.en: In a few moments the master arrived and school “took in.”
paragraphs.cn: 没多久，老师来了，上课了。

paragraphs.en: Tom did not feel a strong interest in his studies.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 对学习不太感兴趣。

paragraphs.en: Every time he stole a glance at the girls’ side of the room Becky’s face troubled him.
paragraphs.cn: 每次他偷偷看教室里女孩那边，贝琪 的脸都让他有点担心。

paragraphs.en: Considering all things, he did not want to pity her, and yet it was all he could do to help it.
paragraphs.cn: 想来想去，他不想可怜她，但又忍不住。

paragraphs.en: He could get up no exultation that was really worthy the name.
paragraphs.cn: 他一点也高兴不起来。

paragraphs.en: Presently the spelling-book discovery was made, and Tom’s mind was entirely full of his own matters for a while after that.
paragraphs.cn: 不久，拼写书被发现了。之后 汤姆 的心思就全放在自己的事情上了。

paragraphs.en: Becky roused up from her lethargy of distress and showed good interest in the proceedings.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪 从难过中清醒过来，对发生的事情很感兴趣。

paragraphs.en: She did not expect that Tom could get out of his trouble by denying that he spilt the ink on the book himself; and she was right.
paragraphs.cn: 她不觉得 汤姆 否认是自己把墨水洒在书上就能摆脱麻烦，她猜对了。

paragraphs.en: The denial only seemed to make the thing worse for Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 否认只会让 汤姆 的情况变得更糟。

paragraphs.en: Becky supposed she would be glad of that, and she tried to believe she was glad of it, but she found she was not certain.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪 觉得她应该会为此感到高兴，她也试着相信自己是高兴的，但她发现自己其实不确定。

paragraphs.en: When the worst came to the worst, she had an impulse to get up and tell on Alfred Temple, but she made an effort and forced herself to keep still—because, said she to herself, “he’ll tell about me tearing the picture sure.
paragraphs.cn: 到了最糟糕的时候，她想站起来告发 阿尔弗雷德·坦普尔，但她努力控制自己，保持安静。她心想：“他一定会说我撕了画。

paragraphs.en: I wouldn’t say a word, not to save his life!”
paragraphs.cn: 我一个字都不会说，就算救他的命也不说！”

paragraphs.en: Tom took his whipping and went back to his seat not at all broken-hearted, for he thought it was possible that he had unknowingly upset the ink on the spelling-book himself, in some skylarking bout—he had denied it for form’s sake and because it was custom, and had stuck to the denial from principle.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 挨了打，回到座位上，一点也没伤心。因为他觉得可能是自己玩闹时不小心把墨水洒到拼写书上的。他否认只是因为面子和习惯，而且他觉得那样做是对的，所以一直不承认。

paragraphs.en: A whole hour drifted by, the master sat nodding in his throne, the air was drowsy with the hum of study.
paragraphs.cn: 一个小时过去了，老师在座位上打瞌睡。教室里是读书的嗡嗡声，让人想睡觉。

paragraphs.en: By and by, Mr. Dobbins straightened himself up, yawned, then unlocked his desk, and reached for his book, but seemed undecided whether to take it out or leave it.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，多宾斯先生 坐直了身子，打了个哈欠。然后打开抽屉，伸手去拿书，但他好像在犹豫是拿出来还是不拿。

paragraphs.en: Most of the pupils glanced up languidly, but there were two among them that watched his movements with intent eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 大多数同学都懒洋洋地抬起头看了一眼，但其中有两个人，眼睛一眨不眨地盯着他。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Dobbins fingered his book absently for a while, then took it out and settled himself in his chair to read!
paragraphs.cn: 多宾斯先生 漫不经心地摸了摸书一会儿，然后拿出来，在椅子上坐好，开始读起来！

paragraphs.en: Tom shot a glance at Becky.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 朝 贝琪 看了一眼。

paragraphs.en: He had seen a hunted and helpless rabbit look as she did, with a gun levelled at its head.
paragraphs.cn: 他看到过一只被追赶的、无助的兔子，眼神跟她一样，枪正对着它的头。

paragraphs.en: Instantly he forgot his quarrel with her.
paragraphs.cn: 他立刻就忘了和她的争吵。

paragraphs.en: Quick—something must be done! done in a flash, too!
paragraphs.cn: 快！得赶紧做点事！得马上做完！

paragraphs.en: But the very imminence of the emergency paralyzed his invention.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，事情太急了，他一时想不出好办法。

paragraphs.en: Good!
paragraphs.cn: 好！

paragraphs.en: —he had an inspiration!
paragraphs.cn: —他突然想到了一个好主意！

paragraphs.en: He would run and snatch the book, spring through the door and fly.
paragraphs.cn: 他要跑过去抢走书，然后冲出门，快点跑掉。

paragraphs.en: But his resolution shook for one little instant, and the chance was lost—the master opened the volume.
paragraphs.cn: 可是他只犹豫了一小下，机会就没了——老师已经把书打开了。

paragraphs.en: If Tom only had the wasted opportunity back again!
paragraphs.cn: 要是 汤姆 能让错过的机会再回来就好了！

paragraphs.en: Too late.
paragraphs.cn: 太晚了。

paragraphs.en: There was no help for Becky now, he said.
paragraphs.cn: 他说，现在 贝琪 已经没办法了。

paragraphs.en: The next moment the master faced the school.
paragraphs.cn: 下一刻，老师面向了全校同学。

paragraphs.en: Every eye sank under his gaze.
paragraphs.cn: 所有人都被他的目光看得低下了头。

paragraphs.en: There was that in it which smote even the innocent with fear.
paragraphs.cn: 老师的目光里带着一种东西，让没做错事的人也感到害怕。

paragraphs.en: There was silence while one might count ten—the master was gathering his wrath.
paragraphs.cn: 安静得能数到十——老师正在憋着火气。

paragraphs.en: Then he spoke: “Who tore this book?”
paragraphs.cn: 然后他开口说：“是谁撕了这本书？”

paragraphs.en: There was not a sound.
paragraphs.cn: 一点声音都没有。

paragraphs.en: One could have heard a pin drop.
paragraphs.cn: 连一根针掉到地上都能听见。

paragraphs.en: The stillness continued; the master searched face after face for signs of guilt.
paragraphs.cn: 教室里还是静悄悄的；老师一个一个地看大家的脸，想找出是谁做的。

paragraphs.en: “Benjamin Rogers, did you tear this book?”
paragraphs.cn: “本杰明·罗杰斯，是你撕的这本书吗？”

paragraphs.en: A denial.
paragraphs.cn: 他否认了。

paragraphs.en: Another pause.
paragraphs.cn: 又停了一下。

paragraphs.en: “Joseph Harper, did you?”
paragraphs.cn: “约瑟夫·哈珀，是你吗？”

paragraphs.en: Another denial.
paragraphs.cn: 他也否认了。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s uneasiness grew more and more intense under the slow torture of these proceedings.
paragraphs.cn: 在这样慢慢的追问下，汤姆 越来越不安了。

paragraphs.en: The master scanned the ranks of boys—considered a while, then turned to the girls:
paragraphs.cn: 老师扫视了一排排男生——想了一会儿，然后转向女生们说：

paragraphs.en: “Amy Lawrence?”
paragraphs.cn: “艾米·劳伦斯？”

paragraphs.en: A shake of the head.
paragraphs.cn: 她摇了摇头。

paragraphs.en: “Gracie Miller?”
paragraphs.cn: “格蕾丝·米勒？”

paragraphs.en: The same sign.
paragraphs.cn: 也是一样的动作。

paragraphs.en: “Susan Harper, did you do this?”
paragraphs.cn: “苏珊·哈珀，是你做的吗？”

paragraphs.en: Another negative.
paragraphs.cn: 她也说不是。

paragraphs.en: The next girl was Becky Thatcher.
paragraphs.cn: 下一个女孩是贝琪·撒切尔。

paragraphs.en: Tom was trembling from head to foot with excitement and a sense of the hopelessness of the situation.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆兴奋又绝望，全身都在发抖。

paragraphs.en: “Rebecca Thatcher” [Tom glanced at her face—it was white with terror]—“did you tear—no, look me in the face” [her hands rose in appeal]—“did you tear this book?”
paragraphs.cn: “丽贝卡撒切尔，” [汤姆看了看她的脸——吓得惨白] “是你撕的吗——不，看着我的脸” [她举起手，好像在求] “是你撕坏了这本书吗？”

paragraphs.en: A thought shot like lightning through Tom’s brain.
paragraphs.cn: 一个念头像闪电一样，飞快地划过汤姆的脑海。

paragraphs.en: He sprang to his feet and shouted—“I done it!”
paragraphs.cn: 他一下站起来，大喊：“是我做的！”

paragraphs.en: The school stared in perplexity at this incredible folly.
paragraphs.cn: 学校里的人都很困惑，盯着这个不可思议的傻事。

paragraphs.en: Tom stood a moment, to gather his dismembered faculties; and when he stepped forward to go to his punishment the surprise, the gratitude, the adoration that shone upon him out of poor Becky’s eyes seemed pay enough for a hundred floggings.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆站了一会儿，努力让自己清醒过来；当他走上前去领罚时，可怜的贝琪眼里闪烁着惊讶、感激和崇拜，这似乎比挨一百次打都值得。

paragraphs.en: Inspired by the splendor of his own act, he took without an outcry the most merciless flaying that even Mr. Dobbins had ever administered; and also received with indifference the added cruelty of a command to remain two hours after school should be dismissed—for he knew who would wait for him outside till his captivity was done, and not count the tedious time as loss, either.
paragraphs.cn: 他被自己行为的光辉感染了，默默地承受了最狠的鞭打，连多宾斯先生都从未挨过这样的打；他还毫不在意地接受了额外的惩罚：放学后多留两小时——因为他知道谁会在外面等他，直到他被关禁闭结束，并且不觉得那无聊的等待是浪费时间。

paragraphs.en: Tom went to bed that night planning vengeance against Alfred Temple; for with shame and repentance Becky had told him all, not forgetting her own treachery; but even the longing for vengeance had to give way, soon, to pleasanter musings, and he fell asleep at last with Becky’s latest words lingering dreamily in his ear—
paragraphs.cn: 那天晚上，汤姆上床睡觉时，心里还在想着要报复阿尔弗雷德·坦普尔；因为贝琪又羞又悔地把一切都告诉了他，也没忘了自己的背叛；但很快，报复的念头就让位给了更开心的想法，他最后伴着贝琪最近说的话在耳边回荡，迷迷糊糊地睡着了——

paragraphs.en: “Tom, how _could_ you be so noble!”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，你怎么能这么高尚呢！”

paragraphs.en: Vacation was approaching.
paragraphs.cn: 假期快到了。

paragraphs.en: The schoolmaster, always severe, grew severer and more exacting than ever, for he wanted the school to make a good showing on “Examination” day.
paragraphs.cn: 校长一直都很严厉，现在变得比以前更凶、要求更多了，因为他希望学校在“考试”那天表现得好。

paragraphs.en: His rod and his ferule were seldom idle now—at least among the smaller pupils.
paragraphs.cn: 他的教鞭和戒尺现在很少闲着——至少对那些小一点的学生来说是这样。

paragraphs.en: Only the biggest boys, and young ladies of eighteen and twenty, escaped lashing.
paragraphs.cn: 只有最大的男生，还有十八九岁的年轻女孩，才没有挨鞭打。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Dobbins’ lashings were very vigorous ones, too; for although he carried, under his wig, a perfectly bald and shiny head, he had only reached middle age, and there was no sign of feebleness in his muscle.
paragraphs.cn: 多宾斯先生打人也非常有力；虽然他戴着假发，假发下面是个光秃秃亮堂堂的脑袋，但他才中年，肌肉一点也不松弛。

paragraphs.en: As the great day approached, all the tyranny that was in him came to the surface; he seemed to take a vindictive pleasure in punishing the least shortcomings.
paragraphs.cn: 随着那个重要日子的临近，他所有的暴虐都显露了出来；他似乎很喜欢惩罚学生一点点的小错误，好像在报复一样。

paragraphs.en: The consequence was, that the smaller boys spent their days in terror and suffering and their nights in plotting revenge.
paragraphs.cn: 结果就是，小男生们白天都在恐惧和痛苦中度过，晚上则在琢磨着怎么报仇。

paragraphs.en: They threw away no opportunity to do the master a mischief.
paragraphs.cn: 他们不错过任何一个能恶作剧校长的机会。

paragraphs.en: But he kept ahead all the time.
paragraphs.cn: 但他总是能抢先一步。

paragraphs.en: The retribution that followed every vengeful success was so sweeping and majestic that the boys always retired from the field badly worsted.
paragraphs.cn: 每次他们成功报复后，接着而来的惩罚都那么厉害，那么有气势，结果男生们总是输得很惨，只好收手。

paragraphs.en: At last they conspired together and hit upon a plan that promised a dazzling victory.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，他们一起商量，想出了一个主意，这个主意看起来能让他们大获全胜。

paragraphs.en: They swore in the signpainter’s boy, told him the scheme, and asked his help.
paragraphs.cn: 他们找来了画招牌的男孩，告诉他这个计划，请他帮忙。

paragraphs.en: He had his own reasons for being delighted, for the master boarded in his father’s family and had given the boy ample cause to hate him.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩有自己的理由很高兴，因为校长住在他父亲家里，校长给了这男孩很多恨他的理由。

paragraphs.en: The master’s wife would go on a visit to the country in a few days, and there would be nothing to interfere with the plan; the master always prepared himself for great occasions by getting pretty well fuddled, and the signpainter’s boy said that when the dominie had reached the proper condition on Examination Evening he would “manage the thing” while he napped in his chair; then he would have him awakened at the right time and hurried away to school.
paragraphs.cn: 校长的妻子几天后会去乡下探亲，这样就不会有人干扰他们的计划了；校长总是在重要场合前喝得醉醺醺的，画招牌的男孩说，在考试之夜，等校长在椅子上睡着，喝到适当程度时，他会“处理好这件事”；然后他会在合适的时候叫醒校长，并催他赶紧去学校。

paragraphs.en: In the fulness of time the interesting occasion arrived.
paragraphs.cn: 终于，那个有趣的日子到来了。

paragraphs.en: At eight in the evening the schoolhouse was brilliantly lighted, and adorned with wreaths and festoons of foliage and flowers.
paragraphs.cn: 晚上八点，学校里灯火通明，还装饰着树叶和花朵做的花环和彩带。

paragraphs.en: The master sat throned in his great chair upon a raised platform, with his blackboard behind him.
paragraphs.cn: 校长坐在高高的讲台上，大椅子就像个宝座，黑板在他身后。

paragraphs.en: He was looking tolerably mellow.
paragraphs.cn: 他看起来心情还不错，有点和蔼。

paragraphs.en: Three rows of benches on each side and six rows in front of him were occupied by the dignitaries of the town and by the parents of the pupils.
paragraphs.cn: 校长两边各三排，前面六排的座位，都坐满了镇上的大人物和学生们的爸爸妈妈。
