paragraphs.en: To his left, back of the rows of citizens, was a spacious temporary platform upon which were seated the scholars who were to take part in the exercises of the evening; rows of small boys, washed and dressed to an intolerable state of discomfort; rows of gawky big boys; snowbanks of girls and young ladies clad in lawn and muslin and conspicuously conscious of their bare arms, their grandmothers’ ancient trinkets, their bits of pink and blue ribbon and the flowers in their hair.
paragraphs.cn: 在校长的左边，公民席后面，搭了一个很大的临时台子，上面坐着今晚要表演的学生们；一排排的小男生，洗得干干净净，穿得却很不舒服；一排排笨拙的大男生；还有一大群女孩和年轻女士，她们穿着薄纱和细棉布的衣服，很在意自己露出的胳膊、奶奶给的旧首饰、粉色和蓝色的小丝带，以及头上的花。

paragraphs.en: All the rest of the house was filled with non-participating scholars.
paragraphs.cn: 房子里其他的地方都坐满了没有参加表演的同学。

paragraphs.en: The exercises began.
paragraphs.cn: 表演开始了。

paragraphs.en: A very little boy stood up and sheepishly recited, “You’d scarce expect one of my age to speak in public on the stage,” etc.—accompanying himself with the painfully exact and spasmodic gestures which a machine might have used—supposing the machine to be a trifle out of order.
paragraphs.cn: 一个很小的小男孩站起来，有点害羞地背诵道：“你们大概不会想到，我这么小的孩子也会在台上讲话吧。”等等。他一边背诵，一边做着非常僵硬又奇怪的动作，就像一个坏掉的机器人在动一样。

paragraphs.en: But he got through safely, though cruelly scared, and got a fine round of applause when he made his manufactured bow and retired.
paragraphs.cn: 不过他还是顺利地演完了，虽然他很紧张。他鞠了个躬，就下台了，大家为他热烈鼓掌。

paragraphs.en: A little shamefaced girl lisped, “Mary had a little lamb,” etc., performed a compassion-inspiring curtsy, got her meed of applause, and sat down flushed and happy.
paragraphs.cn: 一个小女孩害羞地低声念道：“玛丽有只小羊羔。”等等。她还做了个可爱的屈膝礼，大家也为她鼓掌。她脸红红的，开心地坐下了。

paragraphs.en: Tom Sawyer stepped forward with conceited confidence and soared into the unquenchable and indestructible “Give me liberty or give me death” speech, with fine fury and frantic gesticulation, and broke down in the middle of it.
paragraphs.cn: 另一个孩子汤姆·索亚很自信地走上前，开始激动地演讲：“不自由，毋宁死！”他声音很大，手舞足蹈，可讲到一半就停下来了。

paragraphs.en: A ghastly stage-fright seized him, his legs quaked under him and he was like to choke.
paragraphs.cn: 他突然很害怕，腿都抖了起来，感觉要喘不过气了。

paragraphs.en: True, he had the manifest sympathy of the house but he had the house’s silence, too, which was even worse than its sympathy.
paragraphs.cn: 虽然大家都很同情他，但全场鸦雀无声，这比同情更让他难受。

paragraphs.en: The master frowned, and this completed the disaster.
paragraphs.cn: 老师也皱起了眉头，这下更糟糕了。

paragraphs.en: Tom struggled awhile and then retired, utterly defeated.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆努力了一下，但还是放弃了，非常沮丧地走下台。

paragraphs.en: There was a weak attempt at applause, but it died early.
paragraphs.cn: 大家稍微鼓了鼓掌，但很快就停了。

paragraphs.en: “The Boy Stood on the Burning Deck” followed; also “The Assyrian Came Down,” and other declamatory gems.
paragraphs.cn: 接着是《男孩站在燃烧的甲板上》和《亚述人来了》等诗歌朗诵。

paragraphs.en: Then there were reading exercises, and a spelling fight.
paragraphs.cn: 然后是朗读练习和拼写比赛。

paragraphs.en: The meagre Latin class recited with honor.
paragraphs.cn: 拉丁语班的学生人数很少，但他们表演得很棒。

paragraphs.en: The prime feature of the evening was in order, now—original “compositions” by the young ladies.
paragraphs.cn: 晚上最重要的环节来了——是小女生们自己写的“作文”。

paragraphs.en: Each in her turn stepped forward to the edge of the platform, cleared her throat, held up her manuscript (tied with dainty ribbon), and proceeded to read, with labored attention to “expression” and punctuation.
paragraphs.cn: 每个小女生都轮流走到台前，清了清嗓子，拿起她用漂亮丝带绑好的稿子，开始大声地读起来。她们读得很用心，还注意了语气和标点符号。

paragraphs.en: The themes were the same that had been illuminated upon similar occasions by their mothers before them, their grandmothers, and doubtless all their ancestors in the female line clear back to the Crusades.
paragraphs.cn: 她们作文的主题都一样，都是以前妈妈们、奶奶们，甚至更早的祖先们讲过的老故事。

paragraphs.en: “Friendship” was one; “Memories of Other Days”; “Religion in History”; “Dream Land”; “The Advantages of Culture”; “Forms of Political Government Compared and Contrasted”; “Melancholy”; “Filial Love”; “Heart Longings,” etc., etc.
paragraphs.cn: 比如有《友情》、《旧日回忆》、《历史中的宗教》、《梦幻之地》、《文化的好处》、《各种政府的比较》、《忧郁》、《孝顺的爱》、《心中的渴望》等等。

paragraphs.en: A prevalent feature in these compositions was a nursed and petted melancholy; another was a wasteful and opulent gush of “fine language”; another was a tendency to lug in by the ears particularly prized words and phrases until they were worn entirely out; and a peculiarity that conspicuously marked and marred them was the inveterate and intolerable sermon that wagged its crippled tail at the end of each and every one of them.
paragraphs.cn: 这些作文里，常常有一些矫情的忧伤；还有很多华丽却没用的大词；她们也喜欢把一些时髦的词语和句子用很多次，用到都听腻了；最特别的是，每篇作文的结尾，都会有一个长长的、让人觉得不舒服的“说教”。

paragraphs.en: No matter what the subject might be, a brainracking effort was made to squirm it into some aspect or other that the moral and religious mind could contemplate with edification.
paragraphs.cn: 不管主题是什么，她们总是想方设法把它扯到道德和宗教上去，让大家觉得受到了教育。

paragraphs.en: The glaring insincerity of these sermons was not sufficient to compass the banishment of the fashion from the schools, and it is not sufficient today; it never will be sufficient while the world stands, perhaps.
paragraphs.cn: 这些说教虽然很不真诚，但大家还是照样写，学校里也没有禁止。可能永远都不会禁止吧。

paragraphs.en: There is no school in all our land where the young ladies do not feel obliged to close their compositions with a sermon; and you will find that the sermon of the most frivolous and the least religious girl in the school is always the longest and the most relentlessly pious.
paragraphs.cn: 在我们这里，每个学校的小女生都觉得写作文一定要加说教。而且，你会发现，那些最爱玩、最不信教的女生的说教，反而是最长、最虔诚的。

paragraphs.en: But enough of this.
paragraphs.cn: 好了，这些就说到这里。

paragraphs.en: Homely truth is unpalatable.
paragraphs.cn: 有时候，实话听起来不太好听。

paragraphs.en: Let us return to the “Examination.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们还是回到“考试”上吧。

paragraphs.en: The first composition that was read was one entitled “Is this, then, Life?”
paragraphs.cn: 第一个读的作文题目是《这就是人生吗？》

paragraphs.en: Perhaps the reader can endure an extract from it:
paragraphs.cn: 也许你可以听听其中的一小段：

paragraphs.en: “In the common walks of life, with what delightful emotions does the youthful mind look forward to some anticipated scene of festivity!
paragraphs.cn: “在普通的生活中，年轻人的心是多么愉快地期待着未来的节日场景啊！

paragraphs.en: Imagination is busy sketching rose-tinted pictures of joy.
paragraphs.cn: 想象力正在忙着描绘粉红色的欢乐画面。

paragraphs.en: In fancy, the voluptuous votary of fashion sees herself amid the festive throng, ‘the observed of all observers.’
paragraphs.cn: 在幻想中，那个追求时尚的漂亮女生看到自己置身于热闹的人群中，‘吸引了所有人的目光’。

paragraphs.en: Her graceful form, arrayed in snowy robes, is whirling through the mazes of the joyous dance; her eye is brightest, her step is lightest in the gay assembly.
paragraphs.cn: 她穿着雪白的衣服，跳着舞，转来转去。她的眼睛亮亮的，脚步也最轻快。

paragraphs.en: “In such delicious fancies time quickly glides by, and the welcome hour arrives for her entrance into the Elysian world, of which she has had such bright dreams.
paragraphs.cn: 她想着这些美好的事，时间过得飞快。很快就到了她要去那个梦中世界的时候了。

paragraphs.en: How fairy-like does everything appear to her enchanted vision!
paragraphs.cn: 在她眼里，一切都像童话一样美妙！

paragraphs.en: Each new scene is more charming than the last.
paragraphs.cn: 每个地方都比上一个更好看。

paragraphs.en: But after a while she finds that beneath this goodly exterior, all is vanity, the flattery which once charmed her soul, now grates harshly upon her ear; the ballroom has lost its charms; and with wasted health and imbittered heart, she turns away with the conviction that earthly pleasures cannot satisfy the longings of the soul!”
paragraphs.cn: 但过了一会儿，她发现，外面看着好，其实都是空的。以前爱听的好话，现在听着很烦；舞厅也没意思了。她身体不好，心里也苦，就离开了。她知道，这些玩乐并不能让她真正高兴！

paragraphs.en: And so forth and so on.
paragraphs.cn: 就这样，一直说着。

paragraphs.en: There was a buzz of gratification from time to time during the reading, accompanied by whispered ejaculations of “How sweet!”
paragraphs.cn: 大家听着听着，有时会很高兴地小声说：“真好听啊！”

paragraphs.en: “How eloquent!”
paragraphs.cn: “说得真好！”

paragraphs.en: “So true!” etc., and after the thing had closed with a peculiarly afflicting sermon the applause was enthusiastic.
paragraphs.cn: “说得太对了！”等等。等到读完一个伤心的故事后，大家开心地鼓掌。

paragraphs.en: Then arose a slim, melancholy girl, whose face had the “interesting” paleness that comes of pills and indigestion, and read a “poem.”
paragraphs.cn: 接着，一个又瘦又有点不开心的女孩站起来。她的脸因为吃药和消化不好，显得有点白。她开始读一首“诗”。

paragraphs.en: Two stanzas of it will do:
paragraphs.cn: 读两小段就行了：

paragraphs.en: “A MISSOURI MAIDEN’S FAREWELL TO ALABAMA
paragraphs.cn: 密苏里少女告别阿拉巴马

paragraphs.en: “Alabama, goodbye!
paragraphs.cn: 阿拉巴马，再见！

paragraphs.en: I love thee well!
paragraphs.cn: 我非常爱你！

paragraphs.en: But yet for a while do I leave thee now!
paragraphs.cn: 但我现在要暂时离开你了！

paragraphs.en: Sad, yes, sad thoughts of thee my heart doth swell, And burning recollections throng my brow!
paragraphs.cn: 想到你，我心里就很难过，很多回忆涌上来。

paragraphs.en: For I have wandered through thy flowery woods; Have roamed and read near Tallapoosa’s stream; Have listened to Tallassee’s warring floods, And wooed on Coosa’s side Aurora’s beam.
paragraphs.cn: 我在你开满花的树林里走过；在塔拉普萨河边散步、看书；听过塔拉西河水的轰鸣；在库萨河边看过清晨的阳光。

paragraphs.en: “Yet shame I not to bear an o’erfull heart, Nor blush to turn behind my tearful eyes; ’Tis from no stranger land I now must part, ’Tis to no strangers left I yield these sighs.
paragraphs.cn: 我心里满满的，就算流泪也不觉得害羞。我不是离开陌生的地方，也不是把我的难过留给陌生人。

paragraphs.en: Welcome and home were mine within this State, Whose vales I leave—whose spires fade fast from me And cold must be mine eyes, and heart, and tête, When, dear Alabama! they turn cold on thee!”
paragraphs.cn: 在这个州，我感到很受欢迎，就像在家一样。现在我要离开这里的山谷，那些高高的尖顶也很快在我眼前消失了。亲爱的阿拉巴马！如果我的眼睛、我的心、我的头都对你变得冷冷的，那它们一定很冷很冷了！

paragraphs.en: There were very few there who knew what “_tête_” meant, but the poem was very satisfactory, nevertheless.
paragraphs.cn: 在场的人很少有知道“_tête_”是什么意思的，但这首诗大家还是很喜欢。

paragraphs.en: Next appeared a dark-complexioned, black-eyed, black-haired young lady, who paused an impressive moment, assumed a tragic expression, and began to read in a measured, solemn tone:
paragraphs.cn: 接着，走上来一位皮肤有点黑，眼睛和头发都是黑色的年轻女孩。她停了一会儿，做出很伤心的样子，然后用慢悠悠、很认真的声音开始读起来：

paragraphs.en: A VISION
paragraphs.cn: 一个景象

paragraphs.en: Dark and tempestuous was night.
paragraphs.cn: 夜晚又黑又狂风暴雨。

paragraphs.en: Around the throne on high not a single star quivered; but the deep intonations of the heavy thunder constantly vibrated upon the ear; whilst the terrific lightning revelled in angry mood through the cloudy chambers of heaven, seeming to scorn the power exerted over its terror by the illustrious Franklin!
paragraphs.cn: 天上没有一颗星星在闪。只有很响的雷声不停地轰隆隆响着。可怕的闪电在乌云里亮来亮去，好像在嘲笑富兰克林控制闪电的本事！

paragraphs.en: Even the boisterous winds unanimously came forth from their mystic homes, and blustered about as if to enhance by their aid the wildness of the scene.
paragraphs.cn: 连狂风也一起从它们藏身的地方冲出来，呼呼地吹着，好像要让这个夜晚变得更可怕。

paragraphs.en: At such a time, so dark, so dreary, for human sympathy my very spirit sighed; but instead thereof,
paragraphs.cn: 在这样又黑又闷的晚上，我的心里很想得到别人的关心；可是没有，

paragraphs.en: ‘My dearest friend, my counsellor, my comforter and guide— My joy in grief, my second bliss in joy,’ came to my side.
paragraphs.cn: “我最好的朋友，我的好帮手，在我伤心时安慰我，在我开心时让我更开心的人，”来到了我身边。

paragraphs.en: She moved like one of those bright beings pictured in the sunny walks of fancy’s Eden by the romantic and young, a queen of beauty unadorned save by her own transcendent loveliness.
paragraphs.cn: 她走起路来，就像那些年轻人在美丽图画里看到的小仙子。她不用打扮就很美，像个皇后一样。

paragraphs.en: So soft was her step, it failed to make even a sound, and but for the magical thrill imparted by her genial touch, as other unobtrusive beauties, she would have glided away unperceived—unsought.
paragraphs.cn: 她的脚步轻轻的，一点声音也没有。要不是她轻轻碰了我一下，让我感觉很奇妙，她就会像其他不被人注意的美女一样，悄悄地走开，谁也发现不了她。

paragraphs.en: A strange sadness rested upon her features, like icy tears upon the robe of December, as she pointed to the contending elements without, and bade me contemplate the two beings presented.
paragraphs.cn: 她脸上带着一点奇怪的伤心，就像十二月的冰冷雨滴。她指着外面刮风下雨的天气，让我仔细看看她给我看的两个人。

paragraphs.en: This nightmare occupied some ten pages of manuscript and wound up with a sermon so destructive of all hope to non-Presbyterians that it took the first prize.
paragraphs.cn: 这个故事像一场可怕的梦，写了好多页。它讲得太吓人了，结果得了第一名。

paragraphs.en: This composition was considered to be the very finest effort of the evening.
paragraphs.cn: 大家觉得这是那天晚上最棒的作品。

paragraphs.en: The mayor of the village, in delivering the prize to the author of it, made a warm speech in which he said that it was by far the most “eloquent” thing he had ever listened to, and that Daniel Webster himself might well be proud of it.
paragraphs.cn: 村长把奖品给写故事的人时，说了好多夸奖的话。他说这是他听过的最“动听”的故事，连丹尼尔·韦伯斯特都会为它骄傲。

paragraphs.en: It may be remarked, in passing, that the number of compositions in which the word “beauteous” was over-fondled, and human experience referred to as “life’s page,” was up to the usual average.
paragraphs.cn: 顺便说一句，很多作文里都太喜欢用“美丽极了”这个词，还把生活叫做“人生的书页”，这跟平时一样多。

paragraphs.en: Now the master, mellow almost to the verge of geniality, put his chair aside, turned his back to the audience, and began to draw a map of America on the blackboard, to exercise the geography class upon.
paragraphs.cn: 老师现在心情很好，他把椅子推开，背对着大家，开始在黑板上画美国地图，要给地理课用。

paragraphs.en: But he made a sad business of it with his unsteady hand, and a smothered titter rippled over the house.
paragraphs.cn: 可是他手不稳，画得不好看，大家就偷偷地笑了。

paragraphs.en: He knew what the matter was, and set himself to right it.
paragraphs.cn: 他知道大家为什么笑，就想把它改好。

paragraphs.en: He sponged out lines and remade them; but he only distorted them more than ever, and the tittering was more pronounced.
paragraphs.cn: 他擦掉线重新画，可画得更不像了，大家的笑声也更大了。

paragraphs.en: He threw his entire attention upon his work, now, as if determined not to be put down by the mirth.
paragraphs.cn: 他现在特别认真地画，好像下决心不让大家的笑声影响他。

paragraphs.en: He felt that all eyes were fastened upon him; he imagined he was succeeding, and yet the tittering continued; it even manifestly increased.
paragraphs.cn: 他觉得所有人都盯着他看，他以为自己画得不错了，可大家的笑声还在，而且更响了。

paragraphs.en: And well it might.
paragraphs.cn: 这笑声是有原因的。

paragraphs.en: There was a garret above, pierced with a scuttle over his head; and down through this scuttle came a cat, suspended around the haunches by a string; she had a rag tied about her head and jaws to keep her from mewing; as she slowly descended she curved upward and clawed at the string, she swung downward and clawed at the intangible air.
paragraphs.cn: 老师头顶上面有个阁楼，阁楼上有个小洞。一只猫被绳子绑着屁股，从那个洞里慢慢下来。它的头和嘴上还系着一块布，不让它叫。猫咪一边下来，一边弓着身子抓绳子，又荡下来抓空气。

paragraphs.en: The tittering rose higher and higher—the cat was within six inches of the absorbed teacher’s head—down, down, a little lower, and she grabbed his wig with her desperate claws, clung to it, and was snatched up into the garret in an instant with her trophy still in her possession!
paragraphs.cn: 大家笑得越来越大声——猫离专心画画的老师的头只有一点点远了——再往下，再往下一点点，它就用爪子抓住了老师的假发！猫紧紧地抓住假发，一下子就被拉回了阁楼，假发还在它手里呢！

paragraphs.en: And how the light did blaze abroad from the master’s bald pate—for the signpainter’s boy had _gilded_ it!
paragraphs.cn: 老师的光头亮闪闪的——原来是招牌店的男孩把它“涂成了金色”！

paragraphs.en: That broke up the meeting.
paragraphs.cn: 这样一来，聚会就散了。

paragraphs.en: The boys were avenged.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们总算报了仇。

paragraphs.en: Vacation had come.
paragraphs.cn: 假期到了。

paragraphs.en: [*] NOTE:—The pretended “compositions” quoted in this chapter are taken without alteration from a volume entitled “Prose and Poetry, by a Western Lady”—but they are exactly and precisely after the schoolgirl pattern, and hence are much happier than any mere imitations could be.
paragraphs.cn: [*] 注意：这一章里引用的“作文”都是真的，直接从一本叫做《一位西方女士的散文与诗歌》的书里拿来的。它们完全是女学生写作文的样子，比随便模仿的要好得多。

paragraphs.en: Tom joined the new order of Cadets of Temperance, being attracted by the showy character of their “regalia.”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆加入了新成立的“戒酒少年团”，因为他喜欢他们那些“漂亮制服”。

paragraphs.en: He promised to abstain from smoking, chewing, and profanity as long as he remained a member.
paragraphs.cn: 他答应只要是这个团里的人，就不抽烟、不嚼东西、不说脏话。

paragraphs.en: Now he found out a new thing—namely, that to promise not to do a thing is the surest way in the world to make a body want to go and do that very thing.
paragraphs.cn: 现在他发现了一件事——原来，答应不做某件事，反而会让你特别想去做那件事。

paragraphs.en: Tom soon found himself tormented with a desire to drink and swear; the desire grew to be so intense that nothing but the hope of a chance to display himself in his red sash kept him from withdrawing from the order.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆很快就特别想喝酒、想骂人；这种想法越来越强烈，只有想着有机会能穿上他的红腰带炫耀一下，才没让他退出这个团。

paragraphs.en: Fourth of July was coming; but he soon gave that up—gave it up before he had worn his shackles over forty-eight hours—and fixed his hopes upon old Judge Frazer, justice of the peace, who was apparently on his deathbed and would have a big public funeral, since he was so high an official.
paragraphs.cn: 独立日快到了；但他很快就放弃了——还没坚持两天呢就放弃了——然后把希望寄托在老法官弗雷泽身上。这个老法官好像快要死了，因为他是个大人物，所以肯定会有一个盛大的公开葬礼。

paragraphs.en: During three days Tom was deeply concerned about the Judge’s condition and hungry for news of it.
paragraphs.cn: 整整三天，汤姆都非常关心法官的身体状况，一直想知道他的消息。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes his hopes ran high—so high that he would venture to get out his regalia and practise before the looking-glass.
paragraphs.cn: 有时候，他抱的希望特别大——大到他会拿出制服，在镜子前练习。

paragraphs.en: But the Judge had a most discouraging way of fluctuating.
paragraphs.cn: 可是法官的病情总是不停地变好变坏，真是让人灰心。

paragraphs.en: At last he was pronounced upon the mend—and then convalescent.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，大家说他病情好转了——然后又说他康复了。

paragraphs.en: Tom was disgusted; and felt a sense of injury, too.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆觉得很生气；他还觉得受到了伤害。

paragraphs.en: He handed in his resignation at once—and that night the Judge suffered a relapse and died.
paragraphs.cn: 他马上递交了辞职信——那天晚上，法官却病情复发，去世了。

paragraphs.en: Tom resolved that he would never trust a man like that again.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆下定决心，以后再也不相信那样的人了。

paragraphs.en: The funeral was a fine thing.
paragraphs.cn: 这场葬礼很不错。

paragraphs.en: The Cadets paraded in a style calculated to kill the late member with envy.
paragraphs.cn: 少年兵们游行得特别棒，去世的人看了都会羡慕。

paragraphs.en: Tom was a free boy again, however—there was something in that.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆又变回自由的男孩了，这感觉真不错。

paragraphs.en: He could drink and swear, now—but found to his surprise that he did not want to.
paragraphs.cn: 他现在能喝酒骂人了，可他发现自己并不想那样。

paragraphs.en: The simple fact that he could, took the desire away, and the charm of it.
paragraphs.cn: 只要他能做，那种想做的心情和乐趣就没了。

paragraphs.en: Tom presently wondered to find that his coveted vacation was beginning to hang a little heavily on his hands.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆现在发现，他盼望已久的假期开始有点无聊了。

paragraphs.en: He attempted a diary—but nothing happened during three days, and so he abandoned it.
paragraphs.cn: 他想写日记，可三天都没事发生，于是他就放弃了。

paragraphs.en: The first of all the negro minstrel shows came to town, and made a sensation.
paragraphs.cn: 镇上来了第一个歌舞表演团，引起了轰动。

paragraphs.en: Tom and Joe Harper got up a band of performers and were happy for two days.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆和乔·哈珀组织了一个表演队，开心了足足两天。

paragraphs.en: Even the Glorious Fourth was in some sense a failure, for it rained hard, there was no procession in consequence, and the greatest man in the world (as Tom supposed), Mr. Benton, an actual United States Senator, proved an overwhelming disappointment—for he was not twenty-five feet high, nor even anywhere in the neighborhood of it.
paragraphs.cn: 甚至连光荣的七月四日都有些不顺心。那天下大雨，所以没有游行。汤姆以为世界上最了不起的人是本顿先生（他可是美国参议员呢），可他来了却让汤姆非常失望，因为本顿先生根本就没有二十五英尺那么高！

paragraphs.en: A circus came.
paragraphs.cn: 一个马戏团来了。

paragraphs.en: The boys played circus for three days afterward in tents made of rag carpeting—admission, three pins for boys, two for girls—and then circusing was abandoned.
paragraphs.cn: 之后三天，男孩子们用碎布地毯搭帐篷玩马戏。门票是：男孩三根大头针，女孩两根。然后，他们就不再玩马戏了。

paragraphs.en: A phrenologist and a mesmerizer came—and went again and left the village duller and drearier than ever.
paragraphs.cn: 一个测骨相的和会催眠的人来了又走了，村子比以前更无聊、更冷清了。

paragraphs.en: There were some boys-and-girls’ parties, but they were so few and so delightful that they only made the aching voids between ache the harder.
paragraphs.cn: 有些男女孩子一起的派对，可太少了，又太好玩了，让大家过后更觉空虚。

paragraphs.en: Becky Thatcher was gone to her Constantinople home to stay with her parents during vacation—so there was no bright side to life anywhere.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪·撒切尔去她君士坦丁堡的家和爸爸妈妈过暑假了，所以生活里到处都没有亮光了。

paragraphs.en: The dreadful secret of the murder was a chronic misery.
paragraphs.cn: 那个可怕的谋杀秘密，一直让他很痛苦。

paragraphs.en: It was a very cancer for permanency and pain.
paragraphs.cn: 这个秘密就像一个永远都好不了的痛。

paragraphs.en: Then came the measles.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，他得了麻疹。

paragraphs.en: During two long weeks Tom lay a prisoner, dead to the world and its happenings.
paragraphs.cn: 整整两周，汤姆躺在那里，对外面的世界什么都不知道。

paragraphs.en: He was very ill, he was interested in nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 他病得很重，对什么都不感兴趣。

paragraphs.en: When he got upon his feet at last and moved feebly downtown, a melancholy change had come over everything and every creature.
paragraphs.cn: 当他终于能站起来，虚弱地走到镇中心时，发现一切都变了，变得让人有点难过。

paragraphs.en: There had been a “revival,” and everybody had “got religion,” not only the adults, but even the boys and girls.
paragraphs.cn: 镇上举行了一场“布道会”，每个人都“信教”了，不只是大人，连男孩和女孩们也是。

paragraphs.en: Tom went about, hoping against hope for the sight of one blessed sinful face, but disappointment crossed him everywhere.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆到处转悠，多希望能看到一张没信教的脸，可去哪儿都让他失望。

paragraphs.en: He found Joe Harper studying a Testament, and turned sadly away from the depressing spectacle.
paragraphs.cn: 他发现乔·哈珀正在读《圣经》，就伤心地走开了，因为这景象太让他难过了。

paragraphs.en: He sought Ben Rogers, and found him visiting the poor with a basket of tracts.
paragraphs.cn: 他去找本·罗杰斯，发现本·罗杰斯正提着一篮子传教小册子去探望穷人。

paragraphs.en: He hunted up Jim Hollis, who called his attention to the precious blessing of his late measles as a warning.
paragraphs.cn: 他找到了吉姆·霍利斯，霍利斯提醒他，他最近得了麻疹，这是个重要的警告。

paragraphs.en: Every boy he encountered added another ton to his depression; and when, in desperation, he flew for refuge at last to the bosom of Huckleberry Finn and was received with a Scriptural quotation, his heart broke and he crept home and to bed realizing that he alone of all the town was lost, forever and forever.
paragraphs.cn: 他遇到的每个男孩都让他更沮丧；绝望中，他终于跑到哈克贝利·费恩身边寻求安慰，没想到哈克贝利·费恩却用了一句《圣经》里的话来对他。他心都碎了，悄悄地爬回了家，躺到床上，他觉得整个镇上只有自己是迷失的，永远地迷失了。

paragraphs.en: And that night there came on a terrific storm, with driving rain, awful claps of thunder and blinding sheets of lightning.
paragraphs.cn: 那天晚上，外面下起了可怕的暴风雨，瓢泼大雨，雷声阵阵，闪电耀眼。

paragraphs.en: He covered his head with the bedclothes and waited in a horror of suspense for his doom; for he had not the shadow of a doubt that all this hubbub was about him.
paragraphs.cn: 他用被子蒙住头，非常害怕地等待着，觉得惩罚要来了。因为他一点儿也不怀疑，外面所有的吵闹都是因为他。

paragraphs.en: He believed he had taxed the forbearance of the powers above to the extremity of endurance and that this was the result.
paragraphs.cn: 他觉得他惹恼了上天，上天已经忍无可忍了，而这暴风雨就是上天给他的惩罚。

paragraphs.en: It might have seemed to him a waste of pomp and ammunition to kill a bug with a battery of artillery, but there seemed nothing incongruous about the getting up such an expensive thunderstorm as this to knock the turf from under an insect like himself.
paragraphs.cn: 他觉得用大炮打一只小虫子有点浪费。可是，如果一场大雷雨把他这样的小虫子冲走，他倒觉得一点也不奇怪。

paragraphs.en: By and by the tempest spent itself and died without accomplishing its object.
paragraphs.cn: 慢慢地，大风大雨自己停了。它想做的事情，一件也没做成。

paragraphs.en: The boy’s first impulse was to be grateful, and reform.
paragraphs.cn: 小男孩最先想的是：要谢谢老天，以后要变好。

paragraphs.en: His second was to wait—for there might not be any more storms.
paragraphs.cn: 他第二个想法是等等看——也许不会再有大风大雨了。

paragraphs.en: The next day the doctors were back; Tom had relapsed.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天，医生们又来了。汤姆的病又犯了。

paragraphs.en: The three weeks he spent on his back this time seemed an entire age.
paragraphs.cn: 这次他躺在床上三星期，感觉就像过了一个世纪那么久。

paragraphs.en: When he got abroad at last he was hardly grateful that he had been spared, remembering how lonely was his estate, how companionless and forlorn he was.
paragraphs.cn: 当他终于能出门时，他一点也不开心自己还活着。他想到自己是多么孤单，一个朋友也没有。

paragraphs.en: He drifted listlessly down the street and found Jim Hollis acting as judge in a juvenile court that was trying a cat for murder, in the presence of her victim, a bird.
paragraphs.cn: 他没精打采地走在街上，看到吉姆霍利斯正在“小朋友的法庭”里当法官。他们在审一只猫，因为那只猫杀了一只小鸟，小鸟就在旁边。

paragraphs.en: He found Joe Harper and Huck Finn up an alley eating a stolen melon.
paragraphs.cn: 他看到乔·哈珀和哈克芬在小巷子里，吃着偷来的甜瓜。

paragraphs.en: Poor lads! they—like Tom—had suffered a relapse.
paragraphs.cn: 可怜的孩子们！他们——也像汤姆一样——又犯病了。

paragraphs.en: At last the sleepy atmosphere was stirred—and vigorously: the murder trial came on in the court.
paragraphs.cn: 终于，这里安静的气氛被打破了——而且是很热闹地打破了：法庭要审理那件杀人案了。

paragraphs.en: It became the absorbing topic of village talk immediately.
paragraphs.cn: 这事马上就成了村子里大家都在说的话题。

paragraphs.en: Tom could not get away from it.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆根本就躲不开这事。

paragraphs.en: Every reference to the murder sent a shudder to his heart, for his troubled conscience and fears almost persuaded him that these remarks were put forth in his hearing as “feelers”; he did not see how he could be suspected of knowing anything about the murder, but still he could not be comfortable in the midst of this gossip.
paragraphs.cn: 每次听到大家说杀人案，他心里就发抖。他做了亏心事，心里害怕，总觉得大家是故意说给他听，想试探他。他不知道大家怎么会怀疑他知道杀人案的事，可他听到这些话，就是不舒服。

paragraphs.en: It kept him in a cold shiver all the time.
paragraphs.cn: 这让他一直不停地发抖。

paragraphs.en: He took Huck to a lonely place to have a talk with him.
paragraphs.cn: 他把哈克带到一个没人的地方，想和他说说话。

paragraphs.en: It would be some relief to unseal his tongue for a little while; to divide his burden of distress with another sufferer.
paragraphs.cn: 说出来会让他心里好受一点；把心里难受的事情，分给另一个一样难受的朋友一点。

paragraphs.en: Moreover, he wanted to assure himself that Huck had remained discreet.
paragraphs.cn: 而且，他还想确定哈克一直都保守着秘密，没跟别人说。

paragraphs.en: “Huck, have you ever told anybody about—that?”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，你有没有跟别人说过——那件事？”

paragraphs.en: “’Bout what?”
paragraphs.cn: “说什么啊？”

paragraphs.en: “You know what.”
paragraphs.cn: “你知道是什么事。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh—’course I haven’t.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦——我当然没有说啊。”

paragraphs.en: “Never a word?”
paragraphs.cn: “一个字都没说吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Never a solitary word, so help me.
paragraphs.cn: “一个字都没说，我发誓。

paragraphs.en: What makes you ask?”
paragraphs.cn: 你为什么问这个呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I was afeard.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我有点害怕。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, Tom Sawyer, we wouldn’t be alive two days if that got found out.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，汤姆·索亚，要是那件事被发现了，我们两天都活不了的。

paragraphs.en: _You_ know that.”
paragraphs.cn: 你_知道_的。”

paragraphs.en: Tom felt more comfortable.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆心里舒服多了。

paragraphs.en: After a pause:
paragraphs.cn: 停顿了一下：

paragraphs.en: “Huck, they couldn’t anybody get you to tell, could they?”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，他们没法让你说出来，是吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Get me to tell?
paragraphs.cn: “让我说出来？

paragraphs.en: Why, if I wanted that halfbreed devil to drownd me they could get me to tell.
paragraphs.cn: 要是我想让那个坏蛋把我淹死，他们就能让我说出来。

paragraphs.en: They ain’t no different way.”
paragraphs.cn: 没有别的办法了。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, that’s all right, then.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，那好吧。

paragraphs.en: I reckon we’re safe as long as we keep mum.
paragraphs.cn: 我想只要我们不说，我们就安全了。

paragraphs.en: But let’s swear again, anyway.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我们还是再发一次誓吧。

paragraphs.en: It’s more surer.”
paragraphs.cn: 这样更保险一些。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m agreed.”
paragraphs.cn: “我同意。”

paragraphs.en: So they swore again with dread solemnities.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们又严肃地发了一次誓。

paragraphs.en: “What is the talk around, Huck?
paragraphs.cn: “外面都在说什么，哈克？

paragraphs.en: I’ve heard a power of it.”
paragraphs.cn: 我听到了很多。”

paragraphs.en: “Talk?
paragraphs.cn: “说什么？

paragraphs.en: Well, it’s just Muff Potter, Muff Potter, Muff Potter all the time.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，就是一直在说莫夫·波特、莫夫·波特、莫夫·波特。

paragraphs.en: It keeps me in a sweat, constant, so’s I want to hide som’ers.”
paragraphs.cn: 我一直很紧张，想找个地方躲起来。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s just the same way they go on round me.
paragraphs.cn: “他们在我身边也是那样说。

paragraphs.en: I reckon he’s a goner.
paragraphs.cn: 我想他这次肯定完了。

paragraphs.en: Don’t you feel sorry for him, sometimes?”
paragraphs.cn: 你有时不替他难过吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Most always—most always.
paragraphs.cn: “差不多总是这样——差不多总是这样。

paragraphs.en: He ain’t no account; but then he hain’t ever done anything to hurt anybody.
paragraphs.cn: 他没什么用；但他从没做过什么坏事伤害别人。

paragraphs.en: Just fishes a little, to get money to get drunk on—and loafs around considerable; but lord, we all do that—leastways most of us—preachers and such like.
paragraphs.cn: 他只是钓鱼赚点钱去喝酒——然后到处闲逛；但是天哪，我们大家——至少我们大多数人——牧师什么的，都那样做。

paragraphs.en: But he’s kind of good—he give me half a fish, once, when there warn’t enough for two; and lots of times he’s kind of stood by me when I was out of luck.”
paragraphs.cn: 但他还挺好的——有一次鱼不够两个人吃，他给了我一半；还有好多次，我倒霉的时候他都帮我。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, he’s mended kites for me, Huck, and knitted hooks on to my line.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，他给我修过风筝，哈克，还在我的鱼线上系过鱼钩。

paragraphs.en: I wish we could get him out of there.”
paragraphs.cn: 我真希望我们能把他救出来。”

paragraphs.en: “My! we couldn’t get him out, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀！我们救不了他，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: And besides, ’twouldn’t do any good; they’d ketch him again.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且，就算救出来也没用；他们还会再把他抓回去的。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes—so they would.
paragraphs.cn: “是啊——他们会的。

paragraphs.en: But I hate to hear ’em abuse him so like the dickens when he never done—that.”
paragraphs.cn: 但我讨厌听到他们那样骂他，他从没做过——那样的事。”

paragraphs.en: “I do too, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “我也是，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: Lord, I hear ’em say he’s the bloodiest looking villain in this country, and they wonder he wasn’t ever hung before.”
paragraphs.cn: 天哪，我听到他们说他是这个国家最坏的坏蛋，他们还奇怪他怎么没被吊死过。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, they talk like that, all the time.
paragraphs.cn: “对，他们总是这样说。

paragraphs.en: I’ve heard ’em say that if he was to get free they’d lynch him.”
paragraphs.cn: 我听他们说，如果他跑了，他们就会把他吊起来。”

paragraphs.en: “And they’d do it, too.”
paragraphs.cn: “他们真的会这么做。”

paragraphs.en: The boys had a long talk, but it brought them little comfort.
paragraphs.cn: 两个男孩聊了很久，但心里还是很难过。

paragraphs.en: As the twilight drew on, they found themselves hanging about the neighborhood of the little isolated jail, perhaps with an undefined hope that something would happen that might clear away their difficulties.
paragraphs.cn: 傍晚时分，他们来到那座小监狱附近，心里隐隐希望有什么事情发生，能解决他们的难题。

paragraphs.en: But nothing happened; there seemed to be no angels or fairies interested in this luckless captive.
paragraphs.cn: 可是什么也没发生；好像没有天使或小仙女来帮助这个可怜的人。

paragraphs.en: The boys did as they had often done before—went to the cell grating and gave Potter some tobacco and matches.
paragraphs.cn: 两个男孩像以前一样，来到牢房的铁栏杆那里，给了 波特 一些烟草和火柴。

paragraphs.en: He was on the ground floor and there were no guards.
paragraphs.cn: 他在底楼，旁边没有看守。

paragraphs.en: His gratitude for their gifts had always smote their consciences before—it cut deeper than ever, this time.
paragraphs.cn: 以前，他感谢他们的礼物时，他们心里就有点过意不去——这次，他们更觉得难受了。

paragraphs.en: They felt cowardly and treacherous to the last degree when Potter said:
paragraphs.cn: 当 波特 说这些话时，他们觉得自己非常胆小和背叛。

paragraphs.en: “You’ve been mighty good to me, boys—better’n anybody else in this town.
paragraphs.cn: “你们对我真好，孩子们——比城里任何人都好。

paragraphs.en: And I don’t forget it, I don’t.
paragraphs.cn: 我不会忘记的，真的不会。

paragraphs.en: Often I says to myself, says I, ‘I used to mend all the boys’ kites and things, and show ’em where the good fishin’ places was, and befriend ’em what I could, and now they’ve all forgot old Muff when he’s in trouble; but Tom don’t, and Huck don’t—_they_ don’t forget him,’ says I, ‘and I don’t forget them.’
paragraphs.cn: 我常常对自己说，‘我以前帮所有的孩子们修风筝，告诉他们哪里有好的钓鱼地方，尽力帮助他们。可现在，当老穆夫有麻烦时，他们都忘了。但 汤姆 没有忘， 哈克 也没有忘——他们没有忘记他，’我说，‘我也不会忘记他们。’

paragraphs.en: Well, boys, I done an awful thing—drunk and crazy at the time—that’s the only way I account for it—and now I got to swing for it, and it’s right.
paragraphs.cn: 哎，孩子们，我做了一件很糟糕的事——当时喝醉了，也疯了——我只能这样解释——现在我得为此付出代价了，这是对的。

paragraphs.en: Right, and _best_, too, I reckon—hope so, anyway.
paragraphs.cn: 对，而且也许是最好的，我猜——反正我是这么希望的。

paragraphs.en: Well, we won’t talk about that.
paragraphs.cn: 好了，我们别说这个了。

paragraphs.en: I don’t want to make _you_ feel bad; you’ve befriended me.
paragraphs.cn: 我不想让你们难过；你们一直对我很好。

paragraphs.en: But what I want to say, is, don’t _you_ ever get drunk—then you won’t ever get here.
paragraphs.cn: 但我想说的是，你们千万不要喝醉——这样就不会来到这里。

paragraphs.en: Stand a litter furder west—so—that’s it; it’s a prime comfort to see faces that’s friendly when a body’s in such a muck of trouble, and there don’t none come here but yourn.
paragraphs.cn: 站远一点，往西边一点——对——就是这样；一个人遇到这么多麻烦时，能看到友善的脸，真是很大的安慰，除了你们，没人来看我。

paragraphs.en: Good friendly faces—good friendly faces.
paragraphs.cn: 友善的脸——友善的脸。

paragraphs.en: Git up on one another’s backs and let me touch ’em.
paragraphs.cn: 你们爬到对方背上，让我摸摸你们。

paragraphs.en: That’s it.
paragraphs.cn: 就是这样。

paragraphs.en: Shake hands—yourn’ll come through the bars, but mine’s too big.
paragraphs.cn: 握握手——你们的手能伸过铁栏，但我的手太大了。

paragraphs.en: Little hands, and weak—but they’ve helped Muff Potter a power, and they’d help him more if they could.”
paragraphs.cn: 小小的手，弱弱的——但它们帮了 莫夫·波特 大忙，如果可以，它们还会帮他更多。”

paragraphs.en: Tom went home miserable, and his dreams that night were full of horrors.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 难过地回家了，那天晚上他做的梦都是可怕的。

paragraphs.en: The next day and the day after, he hung about the courtroom, drawn by an almost irresistible impulse to go in, but forcing himself to stay out.
paragraphs.cn: 接下来的一天又一天，他一直在法庭外面徘徊，心里非常想进去，但又强迫自己留在外面。

paragraphs.en: Huck was having the same experience.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 也有着同样的感受。

paragraphs.en: They studiously avoided each other.
paragraphs.cn: 他们很小心地避开对方。

paragraphs.en: Each wandered away, from time to time, but the same dismal fascination always brought them back presently.
paragraphs.cn: 两人时常会走开，但那种悲伤的吸引力总是很快又把他们带回来。

paragraphs.en: Tom kept his ears open when idlers sauntered out of the courtroom, but invariably heard distressing news—the toils were closing more and more relentlessly around poor Potter.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 仔细听着那些从法庭里闲逛出来的人说话，但总是听到不好的消息——困境正一步步地紧逼着可怜的 波特。

paragraphs.en: At the end of the second day the village talk was to the effect that Injun Joe’s evidence stood firm and unshaken, and that there was not the slightest question as to what the jury’s verdict would be.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天快结束时，村里人都在说印第安·乔的证据很牢固。大家觉得，陪审团会怎么判，已经很清楚了。

paragraphs.en: Tom was out late, that night, and came to bed through the window.
paragraphs.cn: 那个晚上，汤姆很晚才回来。他是从窗户爬进屋的，然后去睡觉了。

paragraphs.en: He was in a tremendous state of excitement.
paragraphs.cn: 他非常非常兴奋。

paragraphs.en: It was hours before he got to sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 过了好几个小时他才睡着。

paragraphs.en: All the village flocked to the courthouse the next morning, for this was to be the great day.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天早上，全村人都跑去法院了。因为这一天会发生大事。

paragraphs.en: Both sexes were about equally represented in the packed audience.
paragraphs.cn: 挤满了人的旁听席上，男人女人差不多一样多。

paragraphs.en: After a long wait the jury filed in and took their places; shortly afterward, Potter, pale and haggard, timid and hopeless, was brought in, with chains upon him, and seated where all the curious eyes could stare at him; no less conspicuous was Injun Joe, stolid as ever.
paragraphs.cn: 等了很久，陪审团的人才走进来坐好。没多久，波特被带了进来。他脸色苍白，瘦瘦的，很害怕，也没了希望。他身上带着链子，被安排坐在那里，所有人都盯着他看。印第安·乔也一样显眼，他还是那么平静。

paragraphs.en: There was another pause, and then the judge arrived and the sheriff proclaimed the opening of the court.
paragraphs.cn: 又安静了一会儿，法官来了。警长宣布，现在开庭！

paragraphs.en: The usual whisperings among the lawyers and gathering together of papers followed.
paragraphs.cn: 律师们像平时一样小声地交谈，整理着文件。

paragraphs.en: These details and accompanying delays worked up an atmosphere of preparation that was as impressive as it was fascinating.
paragraphs.cn: 这些小细节和等待的时间，让气氛变得很庄重，也很吸引人。

paragraphs.en: Now a witness was called who testified that he found Muff Potter washing in the brook, at an early hour of the morning that the murder was discovered, and that he immediately sneaked away.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，有人被叫来作证。他说，在发现凶案的那天早上很早的时候，他看到莫夫·波特在小溪边洗东西。莫夫·波特一看到他，就赶紧溜走了。

paragraphs.en: After some further questioning, counsel for the prosecution said:
paragraphs.cn: 又问了几句，控方律师说：

paragraphs.en: “Take the witness.”
paragraphs.cn: “请问证人吧。”

paragraphs.en: The prisoner raised his eyes for a moment, but dropped them again when his own counsel said:
paragraphs.cn: 犯人抬了一下头，但听到自己的律师说话，又把头低了下去。

paragraphs.en: “I have no questions to ask him.”
paragraphs.cn: “我没什么要问他的。”

paragraphs.en: The next witness proved the finding of the knife near the corpse.
paragraphs.cn: 下一个证人证明，那把刀是在尸体旁边找到的。

paragraphs.en: Counsel for the prosecution said:
paragraphs.cn: 控方律师说：

paragraphs.en: “Take the witness.”
paragraphs.cn: “请问证人吧。”

paragraphs.en: “I have no questions to ask him,” Potter’s lawyer replied.
paragraphs.cn: “我没什么要问他的，”波特的律师说。

paragraphs.en: A third witness swore he had often seen the knife in Potter’s possession.
paragraphs.cn: 第三个证人发誓说，他经常看到波特带着那把刀。

paragraphs.en: “Take the witness.”
paragraphs.cn: “请问证人吧。”

paragraphs.en: Counsel for Potter declined to question him.
paragraphs.cn: 波特的律师还是没有问他问题。

paragraphs.en: The faces of the audience began to betray annoyance.
paragraphs.cn: 旁听的人脸上开始露出不高兴的样子。

paragraphs.en: Did this attorney mean to throw away his client’s life without an effort?
paragraphs.cn: 这个律师难道要不努力就让当事人白白送命吗？

paragraphs.en: Several witnesses deposed concerning Potter’s guilty behavior when brought to the scene of the murder.
paragraphs.cn: 好几个证人都说，当波特被带到案发现场时，他表现得就像是个罪犯。

paragraphs.en: They were allowed to leave the stand without being cross-questioned.
paragraphs.cn: 他们可以离开了，没有人反过来问他们问题。

paragraphs.en: Every detail of the damaging circumstances that occurred in the graveyard upon that morning which all present remembered so well was brought out by credible witnesses, but none of them were cross-examined by Potter’s lawyer.
paragraphs.cn: 那天早上，墓地里发生了很多对波特不利的事。在场的人都记得很清楚。可靠的证人把每个细节都说了出来，但波特的律师一个也没反问。

paragraphs.en: The perplexity and dissatisfaction of the house expressed itself in murmurs and provoked a reproof from the bench.
paragraphs.cn: 旁听的人又困惑又不满，大家都小声议论起来，法官只好批评了他们。

paragraphs.en: Counsel for the prosecution now said:
paragraphs.cn: 控方律师现在说：

paragraphs.en: “By the oaths of citizens whose simple word is above suspicion, we have fastened this awful crime, beyond all possibility of question, upon the unhappy prisoner at the bar.
paragraphs.cn: “那些公民都发誓了，他们说的话谁都相信。我们已经把这件可怕的罪行，毫无疑问地，认定就是这个不幸的犯人做的。”

paragraphs.en: We rest our case here.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们的案子讲完了。

paragraphs.en: A groan escaped from poor Potter, and he put his face in his hands and rocked his body softly to and fro, while a painful silence reigned in the courtroom.
paragraphs.cn: 可怜的波特哼了一声，他把脸埋在手里，轻轻地摇晃身体。法庭里非常安静，让人觉得心里很难过。

paragraphs.en: Many men were moved, and many women’s compassion testified itself in tears.
paragraphs.cn: 很多叔叔伯伯都很难过，很多阿姨奶奶都哭了，眼泪哗哗地流下来。

paragraphs.en: Counsel for the defence rose and said:
paragraphs.cn: 律师叔叔站起来说：

paragraphs.en: “Your honor, in our remarks at the opening of this trial, we foreshadowed our purpose to prove that our client did this fearful deed while under the influence of a blind and irresponsible delirium produced by drink.
paragraphs.cn: “法官爷爷，我们最开始说，要证明他做这件可怕的事，是因为喝醉了，喝得迷迷糊糊，什么都不知道了。

paragraphs.en: We have changed our mind.
paragraphs.cn: 我们现在改变想法了。

paragraphs.en: We shall not offer that plea.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们不打算那么说了。”

paragraphs.en: [Then to the clerk:] “Call Thomas Sawyer!”
paragraphs.cn: [然后对旁边的人说：]“叫托马斯·索亚来！”

paragraphs.en: A puzzled amazement awoke in every face in the house, not even excepting Potter’s.
paragraphs.cn: 屋子里所有人的脸上都露出了吃惊又疑惑的表情，连波特也是一样。

paragraphs.en: Every eye fastened itself with wondering interest upon Tom as he rose and took his place upon the stand.
paragraphs.cn: 大家好奇的眼睛都盯着汤姆。他站起来，走到前面站着。

paragraphs.en: The boy looked wild enough, for he was badly scared.
paragraphs.cn: 这个小男孩看起来很害怕，他吓得不轻。

paragraphs.en: The oath was administered.
paragraphs.cn: 他进行了宣誓。

paragraphs.en: “Thomas Sawyer, where were you on the seventeenth of June, about the hour of midnight?”
paragraphs.cn: “托马斯·索亚，六月十七号半夜的时候，你在哪里呀？”

paragraphs.en: Tom glanced at Injun Joe’s iron face and his tongue failed him.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆看了一眼印第安·乔那张没有表情的脸，吓得说不出话来了。

paragraphs.en: The audience listened breathless, but the words refused to come.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都在屏住呼吸听着，可是他就是说不出话。

paragraphs.en: After a few moments, however, the boy got a little of his strength back, and managed to put enough of it into his voice to make part of the house hear:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，小男孩才稍微有了点力气，他努力让自己的声音大一点，好让屋子里的一些人能听到：

paragraphs.en: “In the graveyard!”
paragraphs.cn: “在墓地里！”

paragraphs.en: “A little bit louder, please.
paragraphs.cn: “请再大声一点。

paragraphs.en: Don’t be afraid.
paragraphs.cn: 别害怕哦。

paragraphs.en: You were—”
paragraphs.cn: 你当时在——”

paragraphs.en: “In the graveyard.”
paragraphs.cn: “在墓地里。”

paragraphs.en: A contemptuous smile flitted across Injun Joe’s face.
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔的脸上闪过一丝不屑的笑。

paragraphs.en: “Were you anywhere near Horse Williams’ grave?”
paragraphs.cn: “你当时在马·威廉姆斯的坟墓旁边吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, sir.”
paragraphs.cn: “是的，先生。”

paragraphs.en: “Speak up—just a trifle louder.
paragraphs.cn: “大声点——再大声一点点。

paragraphs.en: How near were you?”
paragraphs.cn: 你离得有多近？”

paragraphs.en: “Near as I am to you.”
paragraphs.cn: “就像我现在离你这么近。”

paragraphs.en: “Were you hidden, or not?”
paragraphs.cn: “你是藏起来了，还是没有？”

paragraphs.en: “I was hid.”
paragraphs.cn: “我藏起来了。”

paragraphs.en: “Where?”
paragraphs.cn: “藏在哪里？”

paragraphs.en: “Behind the elms that’s on the edge of the grave.”
paragraphs.cn: 在墓地边上的榆树后面。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe gave a barely perceptible start.
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔 轻轻地抖了一下。

paragraphs.en: “Any one with you?”
paragraphs.cn: 有谁和你一起吗？

paragraphs.en: “Yes, sir.
paragraphs.cn: 是的，先生。

paragraphs.en: I went there with—”
paragraphs.cn: 我跟—

paragraphs.en: “Wait—wait a moment.
paragraphs.cn: 等等—等等一下。

paragraphs.en: Never mind mentioning your companion’s name.
paragraphs.cn: 不用说你朋友的名字。

paragraphs.en: We will produce him at the proper time.
paragraphs.cn: 我们会在合适的时候让他出现。

paragraphs.en: Did you carry anything there with you.”
paragraphs.cn: 你有没有带什么东西去那里？

paragraphs.en: Tom hesitated and looked confused.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 犹豫了一下，看起来很困惑。

paragraphs.en: “Speak out, my boy—don’t be diffident.
paragraphs.cn: 大胆地说出来，孩子—不要害羞。

paragraphs.en: The truth is always respectable.
paragraphs.cn: 说实话总是好的。

paragraphs.en: What did you take there?”
paragraphs.cn: 你带了什么去那里？

paragraphs.en: “Only a—a—dead cat.”
paragraphs.cn: 只是一只—一只—死猫。

paragraphs.en: There was a ripple of mirth, which the court checked.
paragraphs.cn: 大家有点想笑，但法庭制止了。

paragraphs.en: “We will produce the skeleton of that cat.
paragraphs.cn: 我们会找到那只猫的骨头。

paragraphs.en: Now, my boy, tell us everything that occurred—tell it in your own way—don’t skip anything, and don’t be afraid.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在，孩子，把发生的一切都告诉我们—用你自己的方式说—不要跳过任何事，也不要害怕。

paragraphs.en: Tom began—hesitatingly at first, but as he warmed to his subject his words flowed more and more easily; in a little while every sound ceased but his own voice; every eye fixed itself upon him; with parted lips and bated breath the audience hung upon his words, taking no note of time, rapt in the ghastly fascinations of the tale.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 开始说了—一开始有些犹豫，但当他越说越起劲，话也越来越顺畅；不一会儿，除了他自己的声音，周围一片安静；所有人的眼睛都盯着他；大家张着嘴巴，屏住呼吸，紧紧地听着他的话，完全忘了时间，被这个可怕故事的魅力深深吸引住了。

paragraphs.en: The strain upon pent emotion reached its climax when the boy said:
paragraphs.cn: 当孩子说到这里时，大家紧张的心情达到了顶点：

paragraphs.en: “—and as the doctor fetched the board around and Muff Potter fell, Injun Joe jumped with the knife and—”
paragraphs.cn: —当医生把木板拿过来，莫夫·波特 倒下时，印第安·乔 拿着刀跳了过去，然后—

paragraphs.en: Crash!
paragraphs.cn: 砰！

paragraphs.en: Quick as lightning the halfbreed sprang for a window, tore his way through all opposers, and was gone!
paragraphs.cn: 那个混血儿像闪电一样冲向窗户，推开所有挡路的人，逃走了！

paragraphs.en: Tom was a glittering hero once more—the pet of the old, the envy of the young.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 又一次成了闪亮的英雄—老人们喜欢他，年轻人都羡慕他。

paragraphs.en: His name even went into immortal print, for the village paper magnified him.
paragraphs.cn: 他的名字甚至登上了报纸，因为村里的报纸把他夸大了。

paragraphs.en: There were some that believed he would be President, yet, if he escaped hanging.
paragraphs.cn: 有些人甚至觉得他将来会当总统，只要他能躲过绞刑。

paragraphs.en: As usual, the fickle, unreasoning world took Muff Potter to its bosom and fondled him as lavishly as it had abused him before.
paragraphs.cn: 和往常一样，这个喜怒无常、不讲道理的世界，现在又把 莫夫·波特 捧在手心里疼爱，就像以前狠狠骂他一样。

paragraphs.en: But that sort of conduct is to the world’s credit; therefore it is not well to find fault with it.
paragraphs.cn: 但这种做法是对世界有好处的；所以不应该去挑剔它。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s days were days of splendor and exultation to him, but his nights were seasons of horror.
paragraphs.cn: 对 汤姆 来说，白天是光彩夺目、充满喜悦的，但夜晚却是可怕的。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe infested all his dreams, and always with doom in his eye.
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔 出现在他所有的梦里，眼睛里总是带着不祥的预兆。

paragraphs.en: Hardly any temptation could persuade the boy to stir abroad after nightfall.
paragraphs.cn: 几乎没有任何诱惑能让这个孩子在天黑后出门。

paragraphs.en: Poor Huck was in the same state of wretchedness and terror, for Tom had told the whole story to the lawyer the night before the great day of the trial, and Huck was sore afraid that his share in the business might leak out, yet, notwithstanding Injun Joe’s flight had saved him the suffering of testifying in court.
paragraphs.cn: 可怜的 哈克 也吓坏了，很难过。因为 汤姆 在开庭前一晚，把所有的事情都告诉了律师。哈克 很担心自己的秘密也会被别人知道。幸好 印第安·乔 逃走了，他才不用去法庭说那些事。

paragraphs.en: The poor fellow had got the attorney to promise secrecy, but what of that?
paragraphs.cn: 那个可怜的人，让律师答应会保密，可是这有用吗？

paragraphs.en: Since Tom’s harassed conscience had managed to drive him to the lawyer’s house by night and wring a dread tale from lips that had been sealed with the dismalest and most formidable of oaths, Huck’s confidence in the human race was wellnigh obliterated.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 心里很难受，半夜跑到律师家，把秘密都说了出来。那些秘密原本是被最可怕的誓言藏着的。这让 哈克 觉得，他再也不能相信人类了。

paragraphs.en: Daily Muff Potter’s gratitude made Tom glad he had spoken; but nightly he wished he had sealed up his tongue.
paragraphs.cn: 白天的时候，莫夫·波特 很感谢 汤姆 说了实话，这让 汤姆 很高兴。可到了晚上，他又希望自己没说那些话。

paragraphs.en: Half the time Tom was afraid Injun Joe would never be captured; the other half he was afraid he would be.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 有时候担心 印第安·乔 永远也抓不到；有时候又担心 印第安·乔 会被抓到。

paragraphs.en: He felt sure he never could draw a safe breath again until that man was dead and he had seen the corpse.
paragraphs.cn: 他觉得，除非那个人死了，他亲眼看到那具尸体，不然他永远都不能安心地呼吸。

paragraphs.en: Rewards had been offered, the country had been scoured, but no Injun Joe was found.
paragraphs.cn: 大家悬赏找人，把全国都搜了一遍，可还是没有找到 印第安·乔。

paragraphs.en: One of those omniscient and awe-inspiring marvels, a detective, came up from St. Louis, moused around, shook his head, looked wise, and made that sort of astounding success which members of that craft usually achieve.
paragraphs.cn: 有一位很厉害的侦探，他是从圣路易斯来的。他什么都知道，很让人佩服。他四处转转，摇摇头，看起来很聪明，然后就和别的侦探一样，有了一个了不起的发现。

paragraphs.en: That is to say, he “found a clew.”
paragraphs.cn: 也就是说，他“找到了一个线索”。

paragraphs.en: But you can’t hang a “clew” for murder, and so after that detective had got through and gone home, Tom felt just as insecure as he was before.
paragraphs.cn: 可是，你不能把一个“线索”给吊死啊！所以，等那个侦探忙完了回家以后，汤姆 还是觉得一点也不安全，和以前一样。

paragraphs.en: The slow days drifted on, and each left behind it a slightly lightened weight of apprehension.
paragraphs.cn: 那些日子过得很慢，可每天过去，人们的担心就少了一点点。

paragraphs.en: There comes a time in every rightly-constructed boy’s life when he has a raging desire to go somewhere and dig for hidden treasure.
paragraphs.cn: 每个小男孩，总会有一段时间，非常非常想去一个地方挖宝藏。

paragraphs.en: This desire suddenly came upon Tom one day.
paragraphs.cn: 有一天，汤姆 突然也想去挖宝藏了。

paragraphs.en: He sallied out to find Joe Harper, but failed of success.
paragraphs.cn: 他出去找 乔·哈珀，可是没找到。

paragraphs.en: Next he sought Ben Rogers; he had gone fishing.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，他又去找 本·罗杰斯；结果 本·罗杰斯 去钓鱼了。

paragraphs.en: Presently he stumbled upon Huck Finn the Red-Handed.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，他碰到了“红手” 哈克 芬恩。

paragraphs.en: Huck would answer.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 会答应的。

paragraphs.en: Tom took him to a private place and opened the matter to him confidentially.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 带他到一个没人的地方，悄悄地把事情告诉了他。

paragraphs.en: Huck was willing.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 也很愿意。

paragraphs.en: Huck was always willing to take a hand in any enterprise that offered entertainment and required no capital, for he had a troublesome superabundance of that sort of time which is not money.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 总是很乐意参加那些好玩又不用花钱的事。因为他有好多好多时间，这些时间又不能当钱用，让他有点烦恼。

paragraphs.en: “Where’ll we dig?” said Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “我们去哪里挖呢？”哈克 说。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, most anywhere.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，差不多哪里都可以。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, is it hid all around?”
paragraphs.cn: “为什么，到处都藏着宝藏吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No, indeed it ain’t.
paragraphs.cn: “不，不是这样的。

paragraphs.en: It’s hid in mighty particular places, Huck—sometimes on islands, sometimes in rotten chests under the end of a limb of an old dead tree, just where the shadow falls at midnight; but mostly under the floor in ha’nted houses.”
paragraphs.cn: 宝藏藏在很特别的地方，哈克。有时候在小岛上，有时候在老树枝下面腐烂的箱子里，就是半夜影子落下来的地方。不过，大部分宝藏都藏在有鬼的房子的地板下面。”

paragraphs.en: “Who hides it?”
paragraphs.cn: “是谁把宝藏藏起来的呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, robbers, of course—who’d you reckon?
paragraphs.cn: “当然是坏蛋强盗啦——你觉得还会是谁？

paragraphs.en: Sunday-school sup’rintendents?”
paragraphs.cn: 主日学校 局长吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道。

paragraphs.en: If ’twas mine I wouldn’t hide it; I’d spend it and have a good time.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果是我的，我就不会藏起来。我会把它花掉，然后好好玩一玩。”

paragraphs.en: “So would I.
paragraphs.cn: “我也是。

paragraphs.en: But robbers don’t do that way.
paragraphs.cn: 但强盗不会那样做。

paragraphs.en: They always hide it and leave it there.”
paragraphs.cn: 他们总是把它藏起来，放在那里。”

paragraphs.en: “Don’t they come after it any more?”
paragraphs.cn: “他们不会再来拿了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No, they think they will, but they generally forget the marks, or else they die.
paragraphs.cn: “不会，他们以为会回来，但常常会忘记记号，或者死掉了。

paragraphs.en: Anyway, it lays there a long time and gets rusty; and by and by somebody finds an old yellow paper that tells how to find the marks—a paper that’s got to be ciphered over about a week because it’s mostly signs and hy’roglyphics.”
paragraphs.cn: 反正，它就在那儿放很久，都生锈了。然后，会有人找到一张旧旧的黄纸，上面写着怎么找那些记号——那张纸要花一个星期才能看懂，因为它上面有很多符号和奇怪的画。”

paragraphs.en: “Hyro—which?”
“Hy’roglyphics—pictures and things, you know, that don’t seem to mean anything.”
paragraphs.cn: “就是那种奇怪的画，还有一些图案，你懂吗？看起来没什么意思。”

paragraphs.en: “Have you got one of them papers, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: “你有没有那种纸啊，汤姆？”

paragraphs.en: “No.”
paragraphs.cn: “没有。”

paragraphs.en: “Well then, how you going to find the marks?”
paragraphs.cn: “那你要怎么找到那些记号呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t want any marks.
paragraphs.cn: “我才不要什么记号呢。

paragraphs.en: They always bury it under a ha’nted house or on an island, or under a dead tree that’s got one limb sticking out.
paragraphs.cn: 他们总是把它埋在鬼屋下面，或是在岛上，或是埋在一棵枯树下面，那棵树有一根树枝伸出来。

paragraphs.en: Well, we’ve tried Jackson’s Island a little, and we can try it again some time; and there’s the old ha’nted house up the Still-House branch, and there’s lots of dead-limb trees—dead loads of ’em.”
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，我们已经在杰克逊岛找了一点，以后还可以再去。还有酿酒厂那边有座老鬼屋，还有好多好多枯树呢。”

paragraphs.en: “Is it under all of them?”
paragraphs.cn: “在所有这些地方下面吗？”

paragraphs.en: “How you talk!
paragraphs.cn: “你胡说什么呢！

paragraphs.en: No!”
paragraphs.cn: 才不是！”

paragraphs.en: “Then how you going to know which one to go for?”
paragraphs.cn: “那你怎么知道要去哪个地方找呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Go for all of ’em!”
paragraphs.cn: “都去！”

paragraphs.en: “Why, Tom, it’ll take all summer.”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，汤姆，那会花掉我们整个夏天的时间呢！”

paragraphs.en: “Well, what of that?
paragraphs.cn: “那又怎么样嘛？

paragraphs.en: Suppose you find a brass pot with a hundred dollars in it, all rusty and gray, or rotten chest full of di’monds.
paragraphs.cn: 要是你找到一个生锈又旧的黄铜罐子，里面有一百块钱，或者一个烂烂的箱子，里面装满了钻石呢？

paragraphs.en: How’s that?”
paragraphs.cn: 怎么样？”

paragraphs.en: Huck’s eyes glowed.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克的眼睛发光了。

paragraphs.en: “That’s bully.
paragraphs.cn: “那真棒。

paragraphs.en: Plenty bully enough for me.
paragraphs.cn: 对我来说已经够好了。

paragraphs.en: Just you gimme the hundred dollars and I don’t want no di’monds.”
paragraphs.cn: 你只要给我一百块钱就行，我才不要什么钻石呢。”

paragraphs.en: “All right.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧。

paragraphs.en: But I bet you I ain’t going to throw off on di’monds.
paragraphs.cn: 但我跟你打赌，我可不会放过钻石的。

paragraphs.en: Some of ’em’s worth twenty dollars apiece—there ain’t any, hardly, but’s worth six bits or a dollar.”
paragraphs.cn: 有些钻石一颗就值二十块钱——几乎没有一颗是不值点钱的，最少也要几块钱呢。”

paragraphs.en: “No!
Is that so?”
paragraphs.cn: 是这样吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Cert’nly—anybody’ll tell you so.
paragraphs.cn: “当然啦——谁都会告诉你。

paragraphs.en: Hain’t you ever seen one, Huck?”
paragraphs.cn: 你没见过吗，哈克？”

paragraphs.en: “Not as I remember.”
paragraphs.cn: “我不记得了。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, kings have slathers of them.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，国王有很多很多。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I don’ know no kings, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我一个国王也不认识，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: “I reckon you don’t.
paragraphs.cn: “我想你是没见过。

paragraphs.en: But if you was to go to Europe you’d see a raft of ’em hopping around.”
paragraphs.cn: 但你要是去欧洲，就能看到一大堆在跳来跳去。”

paragraphs.en: “Do they hop?”
paragraphs.cn: “他们会跳吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Hop?
—your granny!
paragraphs.cn: ——才不会呢！

paragraphs.en: No!”
“Well, what did you say they did, for?”
paragraphs.cn: “那你刚才说他们会干嘛？”

paragraphs.en: “Shucks, I only meant you’d _see_ ’em—not hopping, of course—what do they want to hop for?
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，我只是说你会_看见_他们——当然不是跳来跳去啦——他们为什么要跳呢？

paragraphs.en: —but I mean you’d just see ’em—scattered around, you know, in a kind of a general way.
paragraphs.cn: ——我只是说你会看到他们——到处都是，你知道，就是那种到处都能看到的样子。

paragraphs.en: Like that old humpbacked Richard.”
paragraphs.cn: 就像那个驼背的老理查。”

paragraphs.en: “Richard?
paragraphs.cn: “理查？

paragraphs.en: What’s his other name?”
paragraphs.cn: 他还有别的名字吗？”

paragraphs.en: “He didn’t have any other name.
paragraphs.cn: “他没有别的名字了。

paragraphs.en: Kings don’t have any but a given name.”
paragraphs.cn: 国王都只有一个名字。”

paragraphs.en: “No?”
paragraphs.cn: “没有吗？”

paragraphs.en: “But they don’t.”
paragraphs.cn: “就是没有啊。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, if they like it, Tom, all right; but I don’t want to be a king and have only just a given name, like a nigger.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，要是他们喜欢那样，汤姆，那好吧；但我不想当国王，只有一个名字，像个黑人。

paragraphs.en: But say—where you going to dig first?”
paragraphs.cn: 不过，你说——我们先去哪里挖呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I don’t know.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我不知道。

paragraphs.en: S’pose we tackle that old dead-limb tree on the hill t’other side of Still-House branch?”
paragraphs.cn: 要不我们去小溪对面的山上，那棵枯树旁边看看？”

paragraphs.en: “I’m agreed.”
paragraphs.cn: “我同意。”

paragraphs.en: So they got a crippled pick and a shovel, and set out on their three-mile tramp.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们拿了一把坏了的镐和一把铁锹，就开始了三英里的徒步旅行。

paragraphs.en: They arrived hot and panting, and threw themselves down in the shade of a neighboring elm to rest and have a smoke.
paragraphs.cn: 他们又热又喘地到了，一头栽进旁边榆树的树荫下休息，还抽了根烟。

paragraphs.en: “I like this,” said Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “我喜欢这个，”汤姆 说。

paragraphs.en: “So do I.”
paragraphs.cn: “我也喜欢。”

paragraphs.en: “Say, Huck, if we find a treasure here, what you going to do with your share?”
paragraphs.cn: “哎，哈克，要是我们在这儿找到宝藏，你的那份要怎么用啊？”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’ll have pie and a glass of soda every day, and I’ll go to every circus that comes along.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我要每天都吃派，喝一杯汽水，还要去看所有的马戏表演。

paragraphs.en: I bet I’ll have a gay time.”
paragraphs.cn: 我敢说我会玩得很开心。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, ain’t you going to save any of it?”
paragraphs.cn: “哎，你就不打算存一点吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Save it?
paragraphs.cn: “存起来？

paragraphs.en: What for?”
paragraphs.cn: 为什么呀？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, so as to have something to live on, by and by.”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，以后好有钱用啊。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, that ain’t any use.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，那没用。

paragraphs.en: Pap would come back to thish-yer town some day and get his claws on it if I didn’t hurry up, and I tell you he’d clean it out pretty quick.
paragraphs.cn: 我爸爸哪天会回来这镇上，要是我不快点花掉，他会把钱都拿走的，我跟你说，他会很快花光的。

paragraphs.en: What you going to do with yourn, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，你的那份打算怎么用啊？”

paragraphs.en: “I’m going to buy a new drum, and a sure’nough sword, and a red necktie and a bull pup, and get married.”
paragraphs.cn: “我要买个新鼓，一把真剑，一条红领带，一只小牛头犬，还要结婚。”

paragraphs.en: “Married!”
“That’s it.”
paragraphs.cn: “就是这样。”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, you—why, you ain’t in your right mind.”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，你——哎呀，你脑子不清楚了吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Wait—you’ll see.”
paragraphs.cn: “等等——你会看到的。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, that’s the foolishest thing you could do.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，那可是你做的最傻的事了。

paragraphs.en: Look at pap and my mother.
paragraphs.cn: 看看我爸爸和我妈妈。

paragraphs.en: Fight!
paragraphs.cn: 他们吵架！

paragraphs.en: Why, they used to fight all the time.
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，他们以前总是吵架。

paragraphs.en: I remember, mighty well.”
paragraphs.cn: 我记得可清楚了。”

paragraphs.en: “That ain’t anything.
paragraphs.cn: “那不算什么。

paragraphs.en: The girl I’m going to marry won’t fight.”
paragraphs.cn: 我要娶的女孩才不会吵架呢。”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, I reckon they’re all alike.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，我看她们都一样。

paragraphs.en: They’ll all comb a body.
paragraphs.cn: 她们都会管着别人的。

paragraphs.en: Now you better think ’bout this awhile.
paragraphs.cn: 你最好好好想想这事儿。

paragraphs.en: I tell you you better.
paragraphs.cn: 我跟你说，你真的该好好想想。

paragraphs.en: What’s the name of the gal?”
paragraphs.cn: 那个姑娘叫什么名字啊？”

paragraphs.en: “It ain’t a gal at all—it’s a girl.”
paragraphs.cn: “不是什么姑娘——是个女孩。”

paragraphs.en: “It’s all the same, I reckon; some says gal, some says girl—both’s right, like enough.
paragraphs.cn: “都一样啦，我觉得；有人说“gal”，有人说“girl”——可能都对吧。

paragraphs.en: Anyway, what’s her name, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: 话说回来，她叫什么名字啊，汤姆？”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll tell you some time—not now.”
paragraphs.cn: “我以后再告诉你——现在不行。”

paragraphs.en: “All right—that’ll do.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧——那也行。

paragraphs.en: Only if you get married I’ll be more lonesomer than ever.”
paragraphs.cn: 只是如果你结婚了，我就会比现在更孤单了。”

paragraphs.en: “No you won’t.
paragraphs.cn: “不会啦。

paragraphs.en: You’ll come and live with me.
paragraphs.cn: 你会来和我一起住的。

paragraphs.en: Now stir out of this and we’ll go to digging.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在快点起来，我们去挖东西吧。”

paragraphs.en: They worked and sweated for half an hour.
paragraphs.cn: 他们又挖又出汗，干了半小时。

paragraphs.en: No result.
paragraphs.cn: 什么也没挖到。

paragraphs.en: They toiled another halfhour.
paragraphs.cn: 他们又辛苦了半小时。

paragraphs.en: Still no result.
paragraphs.cn: 还是什么都没挖到。

paragraphs.en: Huck said:
paragraphs.cn: 哈克说：

paragraphs.en: “Do they always bury it as deep as this?”
paragraphs.cn: “他们总是埋这么深吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Sometimes—not always.
paragraphs.cn: “有时候是——不总是。

paragraphs.en: Not generally.
paragraphs.cn: 通常不会。

paragraphs.en: I reckon we haven’t got the right place.”
paragraphs.cn: 我觉得我们没找到对的地方。”

paragraphs.en: So they chose a new spot and began again.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们选了个新地方，又开始挖。

paragraphs.en: The labor dragged a little, but still they made progress.
paragraphs.cn: 挖起来有点慢，但他们还在努力。

paragraphs.en: They pegged away in silence for some time.
paragraphs.cn: 他们默默地挖了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: Finally Huck leaned on his shovel, swabbed the beaded drops from his brow with his sleeve, and said:
paragraphs.cn: 最后，哈克靠在铲子上，用袖子擦掉额头上的汗珠，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “Where you going to dig next, after we get this one?”
paragraphs.cn: “我们挖完这里，接下来要去哪儿挖啊？”

paragraphs.en: “I reckon maybe we’ll tackle the old tree that’s over yonder on Cardiff Hill back of the widow’s.”
paragraphs.cn: “我觉得我们也许会去挖那个老树，就在那边寡妇家后面卡迪夫山。”

paragraphs.en: “I reckon that’ll be a good one.
paragraphs.cn: “我觉得那会是个好地方。

paragraphs.en: But won’t the widow take it away from us, Tom?
paragraphs.cn: 但是那个寡妇不会把它从我们手里拿走吗，汤姆？

paragraphs.en: It’s on her land.”
paragraphs.cn: 那是她的地啊。”

paragraphs.en: “_She_ take it away!
paragraphs.cn: “她把它拿走？

paragraphs.en: Maybe she’d like to try it once.
paragraphs.cn: 也许她想试试看吧。

paragraphs.en: Whoever finds one of these hid treasures, it belongs to him.
paragraphs.cn: 谁找到这些藏起来的宝贝，谁就能拥有它。

paragraphs.en: It don’t make any difference whose land it’s on.”
paragraphs.cn: 这和它在哪块地上没关系。”

paragraphs.en: That was satisfactory.
paragraphs.cn: 那还不错。

paragraphs.en: The work went on.
paragraphs.cn: 活儿继续干。

paragraphs.en: By and by Huck said:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，哈克说：

paragraphs.en: “Blame it, we must be in the wrong place again.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，我们肯定又找错地方了。

paragraphs.en: What do you think?”
paragraphs.cn: 你觉得呢？”

paragraphs.en: “It is mighty curious, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “这真奇怪，哈克。

paragraphs.en: I don’t understand it.
paragraphs.cn: 我不明白。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes witches interfere.
paragraphs.cn: 有时候是巫婆捣乱。

paragraphs.en: I reckon maybe that’s what’s the trouble now.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想，可能现在就是这样。”

paragraphs.en: “Shucks!
Witches ain’t got no power in the daytime.”
paragraphs.cn: 巫婆白天可没法力。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, that’s so.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，没错。

paragraphs.en: I didn’t think of that.
paragraphs.cn: 我没想到那个。

paragraphs.en: Oh, I know what the matter is!
paragraphs.cn: 哦，我知道问题出在哪儿了！

paragraphs.en: What a blamed lot of fools we are!
paragraphs.cn: 我们真是太笨了！

paragraphs.en: You got to find out where the shadow of the limb falls at midnight, and that’s where you dig!”
paragraphs.cn: 你得找到半夜时树枝的影子落在哪里，就在那里挖！”

paragraphs.en: “Then consound it, we’ve fooled away all this work for nothing.
paragraphs.cn: “那可恶，我们白费力气了。

paragraphs.en: Now hang it all, we got to come back in the night.
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，我们晚上还得回来。

paragraphs.en: It’s an awful long way.
paragraphs.cn: 路好远啊。

paragraphs.en: Can you get out?”
paragraphs.cn: 你能出来吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I bet I will.
paragraphs.cn: “我肯定能。

paragraphs.en: We’ve got to do it tonight, too, because if somebody sees these holes they’ll know in a minute what’s here and they’ll go for it.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们今晚就得去，要是别人看到这些洞，一下子就懂了，会把东西拿走的。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’ll come around and maow tonight.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我晚上会过来喵喵叫的。”

paragraphs.en: “All right.
paragraphs.cn: “好的。

paragraphs.en: Let’s hide the tools in the bushes.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们把工具藏到灌木丛里吧。”

paragraphs.en: The boys were there that night, about the appointed time.
paragraphs.cn: 那天晚上，孩子们在约好的时间去了那里。

paragraphs.en: They sat in the shadow waiting.
paragraphs.cn: 他们躲在影子里等着。

paragraphs.en: It was a lonely place, and an hour made solemn by old traditions.
paragraphs.cn: 那地方很安静，老故事让这个时间变得有点吓人。

paragraphs.en: Spirits whispered in the rustling leaves, ghosts lurked in the murky nooks, the deep baying of a hound floated up out of the distance, an owl answered with his sepulchral note.
paragraphs.cn: 树叶沙沙响，好像有小鬼在说话。黑漆漆的角落藏着幽灵。远处传来狗的叫声，猫头鹰也叫得很吓人。

paragraphs.en: The boys were subdued by these solemnities, and talked little.
paragraphs.cn: 这些事让孩子们很安静，他们几乎没说话。

paragraphs.en: By and by they judged that twelve had come; they marked where the shadow fell, and began to dig.
paragraphs.cn: 过了会儿，他们觉得十二点到了。他们记下影子的位置，就开始挖。

paragraphs.en: Their hopes commenced to rise.
paragraphs.cn: 他们的希望开始变大。

paragraphs.en: Their interest grew stronger, and their industry kept pace with it.
paragraphs.cn: 他们更感兴趣了，也挖得更起劲了。

paragraphs.en: The hole deepened and still deepened, but every time their hearts jumped to hear the pick strike upon something, they only suffered a new disappointment.
paragraphs.cn: 洞挖得越来越深。每次听到锄头碰到东西，他们心里就一跳，可每次都是失望。

paragraphs.en: It was only a stone or a chunk.
paragraphs.cn: 都只是一块石头或土块。

paragraphs.en: At last Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 最后 汤姆 说：

paragraphs.en: “It ain’t any use, Huck, we’re wrong again.”
paragraphs.cn: “没用了，哈克，我们又错了。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, but we _can’t_ be wrong.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，可我们不_会_错啊。”

paragraphs.en: We spotted the shadder to a dot.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们把影子看得清清楚楚。”

paragraphs.en: “I know it, but then there’s another thing.”
paragraphs.cn: “我知道，但还有一件事。”

paragraphs.en: “What’s that?”
paragraphs.cn: “什么事？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, we only guessed at the time.
paragraphs.cn: “我们只是猜的时间呀。

paragraphs.en: Like enough it was too late or too early.”
paragraphs.cn: 说不定太晚了，或者太早了。”

paragraphs.en: Huck dropped his shovel.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 放下了铲子。

paragraphs.en: “That’s it,” said he.
paragraphs.cn: “就是这样，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “That’s the very trouble.
paragraphs.cn: “问题就在这儿。

paragraphs.en: We got to give this one up.
paragraphs.cn: 我们得放弃了。

paragraphs.en: We can’t ever tell the right time, and besides this kind of thing’s too awful, here this time of night with witches and ghosts a-fluttering around so.
paragraphs.cn: 我们永远不知道确切时间。而且这事太吓人了，晚上有女巫和鬼魂在身边飞来飞去。

paragraphs.en: I feel as if something’s behind me all the time; and I’m afeard to turn around, becuz maybe there’s others in front a-waiting for a chance.
paragraphs.cn: 我老觉得背后有东西，不敢转身，因为前面可能还有别的东西等着。

paragraphs.en: I been creeping all over, ever since I got here.”
paragraphs.cn: 我来了之后就一直小心翼翼的。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’ve been pretty much so, too, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我也差不多，哈克。

paragraphs.en: They most always put in a dead man when they bury a treasure under a tree, to look out for it.”
paragraphs.cn: 他们在树下埋宝藏时，通常会放一个死人来看守它。”

paragraphs.en: “Lordy!”
paragraphs.cn: “天哪！”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, they do.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，他们会。

paragraphs.en: I’ve always heard that.”
paragraphs.cn: 我一直都听说是这样。”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, I don’t like to fool around much where there’s dead people.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，我不喜欢在有死人的地方玩。

paragraphs.en: A body’s bound to get into trouble with ’em, sure.”
paragraphs.cn: 肯定会跟他们惹麻烦的。”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t like to stir ’em up, either.
paragraphs.cn: “我也不喜欢去吵醒他们。

paragraphs.en: S’pose this one here was to stick his skull out and say something!”
paragraphs.cn: 万一这个死人把头伸出来，还说句话呢！”

paragraphs.en: “Don’t Tom!
paragraphs.cn: “别 汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: It’s awful.”
paragraphs.cn: 太可怕了。

paragraphs.en: “Well, it just is.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，就是这样。

paragraphs.en: Huck, I don’t feel comfortable a bit.”
paragraphs.cn: 哈克，我一点都不舒服。

paragraphs.en: “Say, Tom, let’s give this place up, and try somewheres else.”
paragraphs.cn: 喂，汤姆，我们放弃这里吧，去别的地方试试。

paragraphs.en: “All right, I reckon we better.”
paragraphs.cn: 好吧，我想我们最好还是那样。

paragraphs.en: “What’ll it be?”
paragraphs.cn: 那会是什么？

paragraphs.en: Tom considered awhile; and then said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆想了一会儿，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “The ha’nted house.
paragraphs.cn: 鬼屋。

paragraphs.en: That’s it!”
paragraphs.cn: 就是那里！

paragraphs.en: “Blame it, I don’t like ha’nted houses, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，我不喜欢鬼屋，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: Why, they’re a dern sight worse’n dead people.
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，它们比死人可怕多了。

paragraphs.en: Dead people might talk, maybe, but they don’t come sliding around in a shroud, when you ain’t noticing, and peep over your shoulder all of a sudden and grit their teeth, the way a ghost does.
paragraphs.cn: 死人也许会说话，但它们不会在你没注意时，穿着白布滑来滑去，突然从你肩后偷看，还像鬼一样咬牙切齿。

paragraphs.en: I couldn’t stand such a thing as that, Tom—nobody could.”
paragraphs.cn: 我受不了那样的事，汤姆——没人能受得了。

paragraphs.en: “Yes, but, Huck, ghosts don’t travel around only at night.
paragraphs.cn: 是的，但是，哈克，鬼只在晚上出来。

paragraphs.en: They won’t hender us from digging there in the daytime.”
paragraphs.cn: 它们白天不会妨碍我们挖东西。

paragraphs.en: “Well, that’s so.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，是这样。

paragraphs.en: But you know mighty well people don’t go about that ha’nted house in the day nor the night.”
paragraphs.cn: 但是你很清楚，白天晚上都没人去那个鬼屋。

paragraphs.en: “Well, that’s mostly because they don’t like to go where a man’s been murdered, anyway—but nothing’s ever been seen around that house except in the night—just some blue lights slipping by the windows—no regular ghosts.”
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，那大多是因为人们不喜欢去有人被杀的地方——不过那房子周围除了晚上，就没见过别的什么了——只有一些蓝光从窗户边飘过——没有真正的鬼。

paragraphs.en: “Well, where you see one of them blue lights flickering around, Tom, you can bet there’s a ghost mighty close behind it.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，汤姆，只要你看到那些蓝光在闪烁，你就可以肯定，附近一定有鬼。

paragraphs.en: It stands to reason.
paragraphs.cn: 这是很自然的。

paragraphs.en: Becuz you know that they don’t anybody but ghosts use ’em.”
paragraphs.cn: 因为你知道，除了鬼，没人会用它们。

paragraphs.en: “Yes, that’s so.
paragraphs.cn: 是的，是这样。

paragraphs.en: But anyway they don’t come around in the daytime, so what’s the use of our being afeard?”
paragraphs.cn: 但反正它们白天不出来，我们有什么好怕的呢？

paragraphs.en: “Well, all right.
paragraphs.cn: 好吧。

paragraphs.en: We’ll tackle the ha’nted house if you say so—but I reckon it’s taking chances.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果你坚持，我们就去鬼屋——但我认为这很冒险。

paragraphs.en: They had started down the hill by this time.
paragraphs.cn: 这时候，他们已经开始下山了。

paragraphs.en: There in the middle of the moonlit valley below them stood the “ha’nted” house, utterly isolated, its fences gone long ago, rank weeds smothering the very doorsteps, the chimney crumbled to ruin, the window-sashes vacant, a corner of the roof caved in.
paragraphs.cn: 在他们下面月光照耀的山谷中央，矗立着那座“鬼”屋。它完全孤立，围栏早就没了，杂草把门前台阶都盖住了，烟囱也塌了，窗框空空荡荡，屋顶一角也塌陷了。

paragraphs.en: The boys gazed awhile, half expecting to see a blue light flit past a window; then talking in a low tone, as befitted the time and the circumstances, they struck far off to the right, to give the haunted house a wide berth, and took their way homeward through the woods that adorned the rearward side of Cardiff Hill.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们看了一会儿，心里有点期待能看到蓝光从窗户飘过；然后他们小声说话，因为那时那景就该这样。他们远远地绕到右边，避开鬼屋，穿过卡迪夫山后面的树林回家了。

paragraphs.en: About noon the next day the boys arrived at the dead tree; they had come for their tools.
paragraphs.cn: 第二天中午左右，男孩们来到那棵枯树旁；他们是来拿工具的。

paragraphs.en: Tom was impatient to go to the haunted house; Huck was measurably so, also—but suddenly said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆很想去鬼屋；哈克也差不多——但他突然说：

paragraphs.en: “Lookyhere, Tom, do you know what day it is?”
paragraphs.cn: “你看，汤姆，你知道今天星期几吗？”

paragraphs.en: Tom mentally ran over the days of the week, and then quickly lifted his eyes with a startled look in them—
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 在心里想了想是星期几，然后吓了一跳，赶紧抬起头——

paragraphs.en: “My!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀！

paragraphs.en: I never once thought of it, Huck!”
paragraphs.cn: 我一点儿也没想到，哈克！”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I didn’t neither, but all at once it popped onto me that it was Friday.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我也没想起来。不过我突然想起来今天是星期五。”

paragraphs.en: “Blame it, a body can’t be too careful, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，哈克，我们可要小心点儿。

paragraphs.en: We might ’a’ got into an awful scrape, tackling such a thing on a Friday.”
paragraphs.cn: 要是星期五做这种事，可能会有大麻烦。”

paragraphs.en: “_Might_!
paragraphs.cn: “可能！

paragraphs.en: Better say we _would_!
paragraphs.cn: 不如说我们一定会的！

paragraphs.en: There’s some lucky days, maybe, but Friday ain’t.”
paragraphs.cn: 也许有些日子会走运，但星期五可不是。”

paragraphs.en: “Any fool knows that.
paragraphs.cn: “傻瓜都知道。

paragraphs.en: I don’t reckon _you_ was the first that found it out, Huck.”
paragraphs.cn: 我可不觉得你是第一个发现的，哈克。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I never said I was, did I?
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我没说过我是，对吧？

paragraphs.en: And Friday ain’t all, neither.
paragraphs.cn: 而且也不只是星期五。

paragraphs.en: I had a rotten bad dream last night—dreampt about rats.”
paragraphs.cn: 我昨晚做了个特别糟糕的梦——梦见老鼠了。”

paragraphs.en: “No!
Sure sign of trouble.
paragraphs.cn: 这肯定是麻烦的预兆。

paragraphs.en: Did they fight?”
paragraphs.cn: 它们打架了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No.”
paragraphs.cn: “没有。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, that’s good, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，那太好了，哈克。

paragraphs.en: When they don’t fight it’s only a sign that there’s trouble around, you know.
paragraphs.cn: 你知道，它们不打架就只是说明附近有麻烦。

paragraphs.en: All we got to do is to look mighty sharp and keep out of it.
paragraphs.cn: 我们只要非常小心，躲开就行了。

paragraphs.en: We’ll drop this thing for today, and play.
paragraphs.cn: 我们今天不弄这个了，去玩吧。

paragraphs.en: Do you know Robin Hood, Huck?”
paragraphs.cn: 你认识罗宾汉吗，哈克？”

paragraphs.en: “No. Who’s Robin Hood?”
paragraphs.cn: “不认识。罗宾汉是谁呀？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, he was one of the greatest men that was ever in England—and the best.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，他是英国最厉害的人之一，也是最好的人。

paragraphs.en: He was a robber.”
paragraphs.cn: 他是个强盗。”

paragraphs.en: “Cracky, I wisht I was.
paragraphs.cn: “哇，我真希望我是。

paragraphs.en: Who did he rob?”
paragraphs.cn: 他抢劫谁呀？”

paragraphs.en: “Only sheriffs and bishops and rich people and kings, and such like.
paragraphs.cn: “只抢治安官、主教、有钱人和国王，还有类似的人。

paragraphs.en: But he never bothered the poor.
paragraphs.cn: 但他从不欺负穷人。

paragraphs.en: He loved ’em.
paragraphs.cn: 他爱他们。

paragraphs.en: He always divided up with ’em perfectly square.”
paragraphs.cn: 他总是公平地把东西分给他们。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, he must ’a’ been a brick.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，他一定是个好人。”

paragraphs.en: “I bet you he was, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “我敢打赌他就是，哈克。

paragraphs.en: Oh, he was the noblest man that ever was.
paragraphs.cn: 哦，他是有史以来最好的人。

paragraphs.en: They ain’t any such men now, I can tell you.
paragraphs.cn: 我跟你说，现在可没有那样的人了。

paragraphs.en: He could lick any man in England, with one hand tied behind him; and he could take his yew bow and plug a ten-cent piece every time, a mile and a half.”
paragraphs.cn: 他能把英格兰的任何一个人打倒，就算他一只手被绑在身后；他还能用他的紫杉弓，每次都能射中一英里半远的一枚十美分硬币。”

paragraphs.en: “What’s a _yew_ bow?”
paragraphs.cn: “什么是紫杉弓？”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道。

paragraphs.en: It’s some kind of a bow, of course.
paragraphs.cn: 当然，那是一种弓。

paragraphs.en: And if he hit that dime only on the edge he would set down and cry—and curse.
paragraphs.cn: 如果他只射中那枚硬币的边边，他就会坐下来哭——还会骂人。

paragraphs.en: But we’ll play Robin Hood—it’s nobby fun.
paragraphs.cn: 但我们来玩罗宾汉吧——那很有趣。

paragraphs.en: I’ll learn you.”
paragraphs.cn: 我来教你。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m agreed.”
paragraphs.cn: “我同意。”

paragraphs.en: So they played Robin Hood all the afternoon, now and then casting a yearning eye down upon the haunted house and passing a remark about the morrow’s prospects and possibilities there.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们整个下午都在玩罗宾汉，不时地把渴望的目光投向那座鬼屋，还讨论着明天在那里可能有什么发现。

paragraphs.en: As the sun began to sink into the west they took their way homeward athwart the long shadows of the trees and soon were buried from sight in the forests of Cardiff Hill.
paragraphs.cn: 太阳开始西沉的时候，他们沿着树木长长的影子回家，很快就在卡迪夫山的森林里消失不见了。

paragraphs.en: On Saturday, shortly after noon, the boys were at the dead tree again.
paragraphs.cn: 星期六，刚过中午，男孩子们又来到了那棵枯树旁。

paragraphs.en: They had a smoke and a chat in the shade, and then dug a little in their last hole, not with great hope, but merely because Tom said there were so many cases where people had given up a treasure after getting down within six inches of it, and then somebody else had come along and turned it up with a single thrust of a shovel.
paragraphs.cn: 他们在树荫下抽了会儿烟，聊了会儿天，然后又在他们上次挖的那个洞里挖了挖，虽然没抱太大希望，只是因为汤姆说过，有好多人挖到离宝藏只有六英寸远的时候就放弃了，然后别人一来，一铲子就把宝藏挖出来了。

paragraphs.en: The thing failed this time, however, so the boys shouldered their tools and went away feeling that they had not trifled with fortune, but had fulfilled all the requirements that belong to the business of treasure-hunting.
paragraphs.cn: 不过这次还是没找到，所以男孩子们扛起工具走了，他们觉得他们没有辜负运气，已经把寻宝该做的事都做完了。

paragraphs.en: When they reached the haunted house there was something so weird and grisly about the dead silence that reigned there under the baking sun, and something so depressing about the loneliness and desolation of the place, that they were afraid, for a moment, to venture in.
paragraphs.cn: 他们走到鬼屋时，在烈日下，那里的死寂让人觉得很奇怪又有点吓人，这个地方又很孤单很荒凉，让人心里难过，所以他们有一会儿都不敢进去。

paragraphs.en: Then they crept to the door and took a trembling peep.
paragraphs.cn: 接着他们悄悄地走到门口，抖着身子往里看了一眼。

paragraphs.en: They saw a weedgrown, floorless room, unplastered, an ancient fireplace, vacant windows, a ruinous staircase; and here, there, and everywhere hung ragged and abandoned cobwebs.
paragraphs.cn: 他们看到一个长满野草、没有地板的房间，墙壁也没刷，还有一个老旧的壁炉，空空的窗户，摇摇欲坠的楼梯；到处都挂着破烂的、没人管的蜘蛛网。

paragraphs.en: They presently entered, softly, with quickened pulses, talking in whispers, ears alert to catch the slightest sound, and muscles tense and ready for instant retreat.
paragraphs.cn: 他们小心地走了进去，心跳得很快，小声说话，耳朵竖起来听着一点点声音，肌肉也绷紧了，随时准备马上跑出去。

paragraphs.en: In a little while familiarity modified their fears and they gave the place a critical and interested examination, rather admiring their own boldness, and wondering at it, too.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，他们熟悉了这里，害怕的心情就没那么重了，他们开始仔细又好奇地检查这个地方，还挺佩服自己的胆量，也觉得有点奇怪。

paragraphs.en: Next they wanted to look upstairs.
paragraphs.cn: 接着他们想去楼上看看。

paragraphs.en: This was something like cutting off retreat, but they got to daring each other, and of course there could be but one result—they threw their tools into a corner and made the ascent.
paragraphs.cn: 上楼就像是切断了后路，但他们互相壮胆，结果当然只有一个——他们把工具扔到角落里，就上去了。

paragraphs.en: Up there were the same signs of decay.
paragraphs.cn: 楼上也是一样，到处都是破旧的样子。

paragraphs.en: In one corner they found a closet that promised mystery, but the promise was a fraud—there was nothing in it.
paragraphs.cn: 在一个角落里，他们发现一个壁橱，看起来好像藏着什么秘密，但根本不是，里面什么都没有。

paragraphs.en: Their courage was up now and well in hand.
paragraphs.cn: 这时候，他们的胆量更大了，也更能控制自己了。

paragraphs.en: They were about to go down and begin work when—
paragraphs.cn: 他们正要下去干活，突然——

paragraphs.en: “Sh!” said Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “嘘！”汤姆说。

paragraphs.en: “What is it?” whispered Huck, blanching with fright.
paragraphs.cn: “怎么了？”哈克吓得脸都白了，小声问。

paragraphs.en: There!...
paragraphs.cn: 在那里！...

paragraphs.en: Hear it?”
paragraphs.cn: 听到了吗？”

paragraphs.en: Oh, my!
paragraphs.cn: 天哪！

paragraphs.en: Let’s run!”
paragraphs.cn: 快跑吧！”

paragraphs.en: “Keep still!
paragraphs.cn: “别动！

paragraphs.en: Don’t you budge!
paragraphs.cn: 一点都别动！

paragraphs.en: They’re coming right toward the door.”
paragraphs.cn: 他们正往门这边来。”

paragraphs.en: The boys stretched themselves upon the floor with their eyes to knotholes in the planking, and lay waiting, in a misery of fear.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们趴在地上，眼睛对着木板上的小洞看，心里很害怕地等着。

paragraphs.en: “They’ve stopped....
paragraphs.cn: “他们停下来了....

paragraphs.en: No—coming....
paragraphs.cn: 不——又过来了....

paragraphs.en: Here they are.
paragraphs.cn: 他们来了。

paragraphs.en: Don’t whisper another word, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: 别再小声说话了，哈克。

paragraphs.en: My goodness, I wish I was out of this!”
paragraphs.cn: 天哪，我真希望能离开这里！”

paragraphs.en: Two men entered.
paragraphs.cn: 两个人走了进来。

paragraphs.en: Each boy said to himself: “There’s the old deaf and dumb Spaniard that’s been about town once or twice lately—never saw t’other man before.”
paragraphs.cn: 每个孩子心里都想：“那是镇上最近出现过几次的，又聋又哑的老西班牙人——另一个人，我以前没见过。”

paragraphs.en: “T’other” was a ragged, unkempt creature, with nothing very pleasant in his face.
paragraphs.cn: “另一个人”穿着破旧的衣服，头发乱糟糟的，脸上也没什么好看的表情。

paragraphs.en: The Spaniard was wrapped in a serape; he had bushy white whiskers; long white hair flowed from under his sombrero, and he wore green goggles.
paragraphs.cn: 那个西班牙人身上裹着一条毯子；他有浓密的白胡子；长长的白头发从他的大帽子下面露出来，他还戴着绿色的眼镜。

paragraphs.en: When they came in, “t’other” was talking in a low voice; they sat down on the ground, facing the door, with their backs to the wall, and the speaker continued his remarks.
paragraphs.cn: 他们进来时，“另一个人”正小声说着话；他们坐在地上，面对着门，背靠着墙，那个说话的人继续说。

paragraphs.en: His manner became less guarded and his words more distinct as he proceeded:
paragraphs.cn: 他说话越来越不小心，声音也越来越清楚：

paragraphs.en: “No,” said he, “I’ve thought it all over, and I don’t like it.
paragraphs.cn: “不，”他说，“我想过了，我不喜欢这样。

paragraphs.en: It’s dangerous.”
paragraphs.cn: 这很危险。”

paragraphs.en: “Dangerous!” grunted the “deaf and dumb” Spaniard—to the vast surprise of the boys. “Milksop!”
paragraphs.cn: “危险！”“又聋又哑”的西班牙人哼了一声——孩子们都吓了一跳。“胆小鬼！”

paragraphs.en: This voice made the boys gasp and quake.
paragraphs.cn: 这个声音让孩子们吓得喘不过气，浑身发抖。

paragraphs.en: It was Injun Joe’s!
paragraphs.cn: 是印第安·乔的声音！

paragraphs.en: There was silence for some time.
paragraphs.cn: 一下子安静了下来。

paragraphs.en: Then Joe said:
paragraphs.cn: 接着乔说：

paragraphs.en: “What’s any more dangerous than that job up yonder—but nothing’s come of it.”
paragraphs.cn: “有什么比那里的活儿更危险的吗？——可是什么也没发生啊。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s different.
paragraphs.cn: “那可不一样。

paragraphs.en: Away up the river so, and not another house about.
