paragraphs.cn: 在河边那么远的地方，旁边连一栋房子都没有。

paragraphs.en: ’Twon’t ever be known that we tried, anyway, long as we didn’t succeed.”
paragraphs.cn: 反正只要我们没成功，就不会有人知道我们试过了。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, what’s more dangerous than coming here in the daytime!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，白天来这儿有什么更危险的吗！

paragraphs.en: —anybody would suspicion us that saw us.”
paragraphs.cn: 任何看到我们的人都会怀疑我们。”

paragraphs.en: “I know that.
paragraphs.cn: “我知道。

paragraphs.en: But there warn’t any other place as handy after that fool of a job.
paragraphs.cn: 可是那件傻事以后，就没有别的地方这么方便了。

paragraphs.en: I want to quit this shanty.
paragraphs.cn: 我想离开这个破棚子。

paragraphs.en: I wanted to yesterday, only it warn’t any use trying to stir out of here, with those infernal boys playing over there on the hill right in full view.”
paragraphs.cn: 我昨天就想走了，可是那些烦人的男孩就在山上玩，能看到这儿，所以根本没法儿动。”

paragraphs.en: “Those infernal boys” quaked again under the inspiration of this remark, and thought how lucky it was that they had remembered it was Friday and concluded to wait a day.
paragraphs.cn: “那些烦人的男孩”听到这话又吓得发抖，心想幸亏他们记住了今天是星期五，决定再等一天。

paragraphs.en: They wished in their hearts they had waited a year.
paragraphs.cn: 他们心里恨不得等上一年呢。

paragraphs.en: The two men got out some food and made a luncheon.
paragraphs.cn: 两个人拿出一些吃的，做了顿午饭。

paragraphs.en: After a long and thoughtful silence, Injun Joe said:
paragraphs.cn: 经过一段长时间的安静思考后，印第安·乔说：

paragraphs.en: “Look here, lad—you go back up the river where you belong.
paragraphs.cn: “听着，小子——你回到河上你的地方去。

paragraphs.en: Wait there till you hear from me.
paragraphs.cn: 在那儿等我的消息。

paragraphs.en: I’ll take the chances on dropping into this town just once more, for a look.
paragraphs.cn: 我会冒这个险，再进城一次看看。

paragraphs.en: We’ll do that ‘dangerous’ job after I’ve spied around a little and think things look well for it.
paragraphs.cn: 等我侦察一下，觉得情况不错了，我们再去干那件‘危险’的活儿。

paragraphs.en: Then for Texas!
paragraphs.cn: 然后去得克萨斯！

paragraphs.en: We’ll leg it together!”
paragraphs.cn: 我们一起跑路！”

paragraphs.en: This was satisfactory.
paragraphs.cn: 这样就行了。

paragraphs.en: Both men presently fell to yawning, and Injun Joe said:
paragraphs.cn: 两个人很快都打起了哈欠，然后印第安·乔说：

paragraphs.en: “I’m dead for sleep!
paragraphs.cn: “我困死了！

paragraphs.en: It’s your turn to watch.”
paragraphs.cn: 该你放哨了。”

paragraphs.en: He curled down in the weeds and soon began to snore.
paragraphs.cn: 他蜷缩在草丛里，很快就打起了呼噜。

paragraphs.en: His comrade stirred him once or twice and he became quiet.
paragraphs.cn: 他的同伴捅了他一两下，他就安静下来了。

paragraphs.en: Presently the watcher began to nod; his head drooped lower and lower, both men began to snore now.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，放哨的人也开始打瞌睡了；他的头越垂越低，两个人现在都打起了呼噜。

paragraphs.en: The boys drew a long, grateful breath.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们长长地松了口气，心里很感激。

paragraphs.en: Tom whispered:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆小声说：

paragraphs.en: “Now’s our chance—come!”
paragraphs.cn: “现在是我们的机会，快来！”

paragraphs.en: Huck said:
paragraphs.cn: 哈克说：

paragraphs.en: “I can’t—I’d die if they was to wake.”
paragraphs.cn: “我不能去，要是他们醒了，我会没命的。”

paragraphs.en: Tom urged—Huck held back.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆催他，但哈克还是没动。

paragraphs.en: At last Tom rose slowly and softly, and started alone.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，汤姆慢慢地、轻轻地站起来，一个人走了。

paragraphs.en: But the first step he made wrung such a hideous creak from the crazy floor that he sank down almost dead with fright.
paragraphs.cn: 可他才走第一步，那破地板就发出可怕的吱呀声，吓得他差点倒下。

paragraphs.en: He never made a second attempt.
paragraphs.cn: 他再也不敢尝试第二次了。

paragraphs.en: The boys lay there counting the dragging moments till it seemed to them that time must be done and eternity growing gray; and then they were grateful to note that at last the sun was setting.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们躺在那里，一分一秒地数着时间，感觉时间过得好慢，天都要老了；直到太阳终于落山，他们才松了口气。

paragraphs.en: Now one snore ceased.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，一声鼾声停了。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe sat up, stared around—smiled grimly upon his comrade, whose head was drooping upon his knees—stirred him up with his foot and said:
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔坐起来，看了看四周，对着他把头靠在膝盖上的同伴，冷冷地笑了笑，然后用脚踢了踢他，说：

paragraphs.en: “Here!
_You’re_ a watchman, ain’t you!
paragraphs.cn: 你是个看守，对不对！

paragraphs.en: All right, though—nothing’s happened.”
paragraphs.cn: 不过没关系，什么也没发生。”

paragraphs.en: “My! have I been asleep?”
paragraphs.cn: “啊！我睡着了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, partly, partly.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，睡了一会儿，一点点。

paragraphs.en: Nearly time for us to be moving, pard.
paragraphs.cn: 搭档，我们差不多该走了。

paragraphs.en: What’ll we do with what little swag we’ve got left?”
paragraphs.cn: 我们剩下这点东西怎么办呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know—leave it here as we’ve always done, I reckon.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道，我想还是像以前一样，放这儿吧。

paragraphs.en: No use to take it away till we start south.
paragraphs.cn: 等我们往南走的时候再带走也不迟。

paragraphs.en: Six hundred and fifty in silver’s something to carry.”
paragraphs.cn: 六百五十块银子可不好拿。”

paragraphs.en: “Well—all right—it won’t matter to come here once more.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，好吧，再来一次也没关系。”

paragraphs.en: “No—but I’d say come in the night as we used to do—it’s better.”
paragraphs.cn: “不，我觉得还是像以前一样晚上来，那样更好。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes: but look here; it may be a good while before I get the right chance at that job; accidents might happen; ’tain’t in such a very good place; we’ll just regularly bury it—and bury it deep.”
paragraphs.cn: “是啊，可是听我说；我可能很久才能有机会去办那件事；可能会出意外；这地方也不是很好；我们还是把它好好埋起来吧，埋得深一点。”

paragraphs.en: “Good idea,” said the comrade, who walked across the room, knelt down, raised one of the rearward hearth-stones and took out a bag that jingled pleasantly.
paragraphs.cn: “好主意，”那个同伴说。他走到屋子那边，跪下来，掀开一块后面的炉石，拿出一个叮当作响的袋子。

paragraphs.en: He subtracted from it twenty or thirty dollars for himself and as much for Injun Joe, and passed the bag to the latter, who was on his knees in the corner, now, digging with his bowie-knife.
paragraphs.cn: 他从袋子里拿出二三十块钱给自己，又给印第安·乔同样多的钱，然后把袋子递给印第安·乔。印第安·乔正跪在角落里，用他的博伊刀挖着。

paragraphs.en: The boys forgot all their fears, all their miseries in an instant.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们一下子忘了所有的害怕和不开心。

paragraphs.en: With gloating eyes they watched every movement.
paragraphs.cn: 他们眼睛发亮地看着每一个动作。

paragraphs.en: Luck!
paragraphs.cn: 太走运了！

paragraphs.en: —the splendor of it was beyond all imagination!
paragraphs.cn: 这太棒了，简直无法想象！

paragraphs.en: Six hundred dollars was money enough to make half a dozen boys rich!
paragraphs.cn: 六百块钱，足够让六个孩子都变富有了！

paragraphs.en: Here was treasure-hunting under the happiest auspices—there would not be any bothersome uncertainty as to where to dig.
paragraphs.cn: 这是一个非常棒的寻宝！不用担心去哪里挖。

paragraphs.en: They nudged each other every moment—eloquent nudges and easily understood, for they simply meant—“Oh, but ain’t you glad _now_ we’re here!”
paragraphs.cn: 他们不停地互相推搡，好像在说：“哦，我们真高兴现在在这里啊！”

paragraphs.en: Joe’s knife struck upon something.
paragraphs.cn: 乔的刀碰到了什么东西。

paragraphs.en: “Hello!” said he.
paragraphs.cn: “哈喽！”他说。

paragraphs.en: “What is it?” said his comrade.
paragraphs.cn: “那是什么？”他的伙伴问。

paragraphs.en: “Half-rotten plank—no, it’s a box, I believe.
paragraphs.cn: “一块烂木板——不，我觉得它是个盒子。

paragraphs.en: Here—bear a hand and we’ll see what it’s here for.
paragraphs.cn: 来——搭把手，我们看看这是干嘛的。

paragraphs.en: Never mind, I’ve broke a hole.”
paragraphs.cn: 没关系，我已经弄了个洞。”

paragraphs.en: He reached his hand in and drew it out—
paragraphs.cn: 他把手伸进去，然后拿了出来——

paragraphs.en: “Man, it’s money!”
paragraphs.cn: “天哪，是钱！”

paragraphs.en: The two men examined the handful of coins.
paragraphs.cn: 两个人仔细看了看手里的硬币。

paragraphs.en: They were gold.
paragraphs.cn: 它们是金子。

paragraphs.en: The boys above were as excited as themselves, and as delighted.
paragraphs.cn: 上面的孩子们也和他们一样兴奋，一样开心。

paragraphs.en: Joe’s comrade said:
paragraphs.cn: 乔的伙伴说：

paragraphs.en: “We’ll make quick work of this.
paragraphs.cn: “我们快点把它弄出来。

paragraphs.en: There’s an old rusty pick over amongst the weeds in the corner the other side of the fireplace—I saw it a minute ago.”
paragraphs.cn: 壁炉另一边的角落里，杂草中有个旧生锈的镐子——我刚才看到了。”

paragraphs.en: He ran and brought the boys’ pick and shovel.
paragraphs.cn: 他跑过去拿来了孩子们的镐子和铲子。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe took the pick, looked it over critically, shook his head, muttered something to himself, and then began to use it.
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔拿起镐子，仔细看了看，摇了摇头，小声说了些什么，然后就开始用了。

paragraphs.en: The box was soon unearthed.
paragraphs.cn: 那个盒子很快就被挖出来了。

paragraphs.en: It was not very large; it was iron bound and had been very strong before the slow years had injured it.
paragraphs.cn: 它不大；外面有铁箍，在被岁月损坏之前，它非常结实。

paragraphs.en: The men contemplated the treasure awhile in blissful silence.
paragraphs.cn: 两个人开心地默默看着那些宝藏。

paragraphs.en: “Pard, there’s thousands of dollars here,” said Injun Joe.
paragraphs.cn: “伙计，这里有好多钱啊，”印第安·乔说。

paragraphs.en: “’Twas always said that Murrel’s gang used to be around here one summer,” the stranger observed.
paragraphs.cn: “人们总说，有个叫默雷尔的坏蛋团伙，有一年夏天就在这附近，”那个陌生人说。

paragraphs.en: “I know it,” said Injun Joe; “and this looks like it, I should say.”
paragraphs.cn: “我知道，”印第安·乔说；“我觉得这很像他们做的。”

paragraphs.en: “Now you won’t need to do that job.”
paragraphs.cn: “现在你不用做那件事了。”

paragraphs.en: The halfbreed frowned.
paragraphs.cn: 那个混血儿皱起了眉头。

paragraphs.en: Said he:
paragraphs.cn: 他说：

paragraphs.en: “You don’t know me.
paragraphs.cn: “你不了解我。

paragraphs.en: Least you don’t know all about that thing.
paragraphs.cn: 至少你不知道那件事的全部。

paragraphs.en: ’Tain’t robbery altogether—it’s _revenge_!” and a wicked light flamed in his eyes.
paragraphs.cn: 这不全是抢劫——这是_报仇_！”他的眼睛里闪烁着邪恶的光芒。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll need your help in it.
paragraphs.cn: “我需要你的帮忙。

paragraphs.en: When it’s finished—then Texas.
paragraphs.cn: 事情做完后，就去得克萨斯。

paragraphs.en: Go home to your Nance and your kids, and stand by till you hear from me.”
paragraphs.cn: 回家陪南茜和孩子们吧，等我通知你。”

paragraphs.en: “Well—if you say so; what’ll we do with this—bury it again?”
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，你说了算；那这个怎么办？再埋起来吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes.
[Ravishing delight overhead.]
paragraphs.cn: 头顶传来惊喜的声音。

paragraphs.en: _No_! by the great Sachem, no!
paragraphs.cn: 不！绝不！

paragraphs.en: [Profound distress overhead.]
paragraphs.cn: 头顶传来非常痛苦的声音。

paragraphs.en: I’d nearly forgot.
paragraphs.cn: 我差点忘了。

paragraphs.en: That pick had fresh earth on it!
paragraphs.cn: 那个镐头上面有新土！

paragraphs.en: [The boys were sick with terror in a moment.]
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们立刻吓坏了。

paragraphs.en: What business has a pick and a shovel here?
paragraphs.cn: 镐头和铲子怎么会在这里？

paragraphs.en: What business with fresh earth on them?
paragraphs.cn: 上面怎么会有新土呢？

paragraphs.en: Who brought them here—and where are they gone?
paragraphs.cn: 谁把它们带来这里的——他们又去了哪里？

paragraphs.en: Have you heard anybody?
paragraphs.cn: 你听到有人来了吗？

paragraphs.en: —seen anybody?
paragraphs.cn: —看到有人了吗？

paragraphs.en: What! bury it again and leave them to come and see the ground disturbed?
paragraphs.cn: 什么！再埋起来，让他们过来看到地被动过了吗？

paragraphs.en: Not exactly—not exactly.
paragraphs.cn: 不完全是——不完全是。

paragraphs.en: We’ll take it to my den.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们把它带到我的藏身处去。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, of course!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，当然了！

paragraphs.en: Might have thought of that before.
paragraphs.cn: 我们早该想到。

paragraphs.en: You mean Number One?”
paragraphs.cn: 你是说第一个吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No—Number Two—under the cross.
paragraphs.cn: “不——是第二个——在十字架下面。

paragraphs.en: The other place is bad—too common.”
paragraphs.cn: 另一个地方不好——太普通了。”

paragraphs.en: “All right.
paragraphs.cn: “好的。

paragraphs.en: It’s nearly dark enough to start.”
paragraphs.cn: 天快黑了，可以开始动身了。”

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe got up and went about from window to window cautiously peeping out.
paragraphs.cn: 他起身，悄悄地走到每个窗户边，往外看。

paragraphs.en: Presently he said:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，他说：

paragraphs.en: “Who could have brought those tools here?
paragraphs.cn: “谁把这些工具带到这里来的？

paragraphs.en: Do you reckon they can be upstairs?”
paragraphs.cn: 你觉得它们会在楼上吗？”

paragraphs.en: The boys’ breath forsook them.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们吓得屏住了呼吸。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe put his hand on his knife, halted a moment, undecided, and then turned toward the stairway.
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔 把手放在刀上，犹豫了一下，然后转身走向楼梯。

paragraphs.en: The boys thought of the closet, but their strength was gone.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们想到了柜子，可他们已经没力气了。

paragraphs.en: The steps came creaking up the stairs—the intolerable distress of the situation woke the stricken resolution of the lads—they were about to spring for the closet, when there was a crash of rotten timbers and Injun Joe landed on the ground amid the debris of the ruined stairway.
paragraphs.cn: 脚步声咯吱咯吱地从楼梯上传来，孩子们吓坏了。他们正想冲向柜子，突然烂木头哗啦一声塌了，印第安·乔 摔到地上，被毁坏的楼梯碎片围住。

paragraphs.en: He gathered himself up cursing, and his comrade said:
paragraphs.cn: 他骂骂咧咧地爬起来，他的同伴说：

paragraphs.en: “Now what’s the use of all that?
paragraphs.cn: “现在这样有什么用呢？

paragraphs.en: If it’s anybody, and they’re up there, let them _stay_ there—who cares?
paragraphs.cn: 如果楼上有人，就让他们待在那儿好了——谁管他们呢？

paragraphs.en: If they want to jump down, now, and get into trouble, who objects?
paragraphs.cn: 如果他们想跳下来惹麻烦，谁会反对呢？

paragraphs.en: It will be dark in fifteen minutes—and then let them follow us if they want to.
paragraphs.cn: 十五分钟后天就黑了——到时候他们想跟着我们就跟着吧。

paragraphs.en: I’m willing.
paragraphs.cn: 我没意见。

paragraphs.en: In my opinion, whoever hove those things in here caught a sight of us and took us for ghosts or devils or something.
paragraphs.cn: 我觉得，往这里扔东西的人肯定看到了我们，把我们当成鬼或魔鬼什么的了。

paragraphs.en: I’ll bet they’re running yet.”
paragraphs.cn: 我敢打赌他们还在跑呢。”

paragraphs.en: Joe grumbled awhile; then he agreed with his friend that what daylight was left ought to be economized in getting things ready for leaving.
paragraphs.cn: 乔抱怨了一会儿，然后同意朋友的看法：剩下的这点亮光应该用来准备离开。

paragraphs.en: Shortly afterward they slipped out of the house in the deepening twilight, and moved toward the river with their precious box.
paragraphs.cn: 没过多久，天色越来越暗，他们带着珍贵的箱子悄悄溜出房子，走向河边。

paragraphs.en: Tom and Huck rose up, weak but vastly relieved, and stared after them through the chinks between the logs of the house.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 和 哈克 站起来，虽然有点虚弱，但心里轻松多了。他们透过房子的木头缝隙，盯着他们离开。

paragraphs.en: Follow?
paragraphs.cn: 跟着去？

paragraphs.en: Not they.
paragraphs.cn: 他们才不呢。

paragraphs.en: They were content to reach ground again without broken necks, and take the townward track over the hill.
paragraphs.cn: 他们能安全落地就已经很开心了，然后就沿着通往小镇的小路翻过山。

paragraphs.en: They did not talk much.
paragraphs.cn: 他们没怎么说话。

paragraphs.en: They were too much absorbed in hating themselves—hating the ill luck that made them take the spade and the pick there.
paragraphs.cn: 他们心里很讨厌自己——讨厌他们倒霉，偏偏要把铲子和镐带到那里。

paragraphs.en: But for that, Injun Joe never would have suspected.
paragraphs.cn: 要不是这样，印第安·乔 根本不会怀疑。

paragraphs.en: He would have hidden the silver with the gold to wait there till his “revenge” was satisfied, and then he would have had the misfortune to find that money turn up missing.
paragraphs.cn: 他会把银子和金子藏起来，等到他“报复”完。那时候他就会发现钱不见了，那可就倒霉了。

paragraphs.en: Bitter, bitter luck that the tools were ever brought there!
paragraphs.cn: 真是倒霉透了，竟然把工具带到了那里！

paragraphs.en: They resolved to keep a lookout for that Spaniard when he should come to town spying out for chances to do his revengeful job, and follow him to “Number Two,” wherever that might be.
paragraphs.cn: 他们决定留意那个西班牙人，等他到镇上来找机会报仇时，就跟着他去“二号地点”，不管那是在哪里。

paragraphs.en: Then a ghastly thought occurred to Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 突然，一个可怕的想法在 汤姆 的脑子里出现了。

paragraphs.en: “Revenge?
paragraphs.cn: “报复？

paragraphs.en: What if he means _us_, Huck!”
paragraphs.cn: 万一他指的是我们呢，哈克！”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, don’t!” said Huck, nearly fainting.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，别说了！”哈克 说，他差点晕过去了。

paragraphs.en: They talked it all over, and as they entered town they agreed to believe that he might possibly mean somebody else—at least that he might at least mean nobody but Tom, since only Tom had testified.
paragraphs.cn: 他们把这事儿聊了一遍。进城时，他们觉得他可能说的是别人——至少可能只说的是 汤姆，因为只有 汤姆 作证了。

paragraphs.en: Very, very small comfort it was to Tom to be alone in danger!
paragraphs.cn: 这对 汤姆 来说，独自面对危险，一点安慰都没有！

paragraphs.en: Company would be a palpable improvement, he thought.
paragraphs.cn: 他想，有个人陪着会好很多。

paragraphs.en: The adventure of the day mightily tormented Tom’s dreams that night.
paragraphs.cn: 那天发生的事，让汤姆晚上做了很多噩梦。

paragraphs.en: Four times he had his hands on that rich treasure and four times it wasted to nothingness in his fingers as sleep forsook him and wakefulness brought back the hard reality of his misfortune.
paragraphs.cn: 他梦到自己四次摸到了宝藏，可每次都从他手里溜走了。他一醒来，伤心的事就又回到他脑海里。

paragraphs.en: As he lay in the early morning recalling the incidents of his great adventure, he noticed that they seemed curiously subdued and far away—somewhat as if they had happened in another world, or in a time long gone by.
paragraphs.cn: 他清早躺在床上，回想着昨天的冒险。他觉得那些事好像变得很模糊，离他很远，就像发生在另一个世界，或者很久很久以前一样。

paragraphs.en: Then it occurred to him that the great adventure itself must be a dream!
paragraphs.cn: 接着他想到，昨天的冒险也许只是一个梦！

paragraphs.en: There was one very strong argument in favor of this idea—namely, that the quantity of coin he had seen was too vast to be real.
paragraphs.cn: 有一个很重要的理由让他觉得是梦，那就是他看到的钱实在太多了，不可能是真的。

paragraphs.en: He had never seen as much as fifty dollars in one mass before, and he was like all boys of his age and station in life, in that he imagined that all references to “hundreds” and “thousands” were mere fanciful forms of speech, and that no such sums really existed in the world.
paragraphs.cn: 他从没见过这么多钱，连五十块钱都没见过。他跟其他同龄的孩子一样，觉得“几百块”或“几千块”都是随便说说而已，世界上根本没有那么多钱。

paragraphs.en: He never had supposed for a moment that so large a sum as a hundred dollars was to be found in actual money in any one’s possession.
paragraphs.cn: 他从没想过，谁能真的有一百块钱那么多。

paragraphs.en: If his notions of hidden treasure had been analyzed, they would have been found to consist of a handful of real dimes and a bushel of vague, splendid, ungraspable dollars.
paragraphs.cn: 如果去看看他心里想的宝藏是什么样的，那里面可能只有一把真的小硬币，还有一大堆说不清道不明、很漂亮却抓不住的钱。

paragraphs.en: But the incidents of his adventure grew sensibly sharper and clearer under the attrition of thinking them over, and so he presently found himself leaning to the impression that the thing might not have been a dream, after all.
paragraphs.cn: 但他越想，昨天的冒险就越清楚真实。于是他觉得，也许那并不是一个梦。

paragraphs.en: This uncertainty must be swept away.
paragraphs.cn: 他得弄清楚，不能再这样不确定了。

paragraphs.en: He would snatch a hurried breakfast and go and find Huck.
paragraphs.cn: 他决定赶紧吃完早饭，去找哈克。

paragraphs.en: Huck was sitting on the gunwale of a flatboat, listlessly dangling his feet in the water and looking very melancholy.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克正坐在平底船的边上，他懒洋洋地把脚放在水里晃荡，看起来很伤心。

paragraphs.en: Tom concluded to let Huck lead up to the subject.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆决定让哈克先开口说这件事。

paragraphs.en: If he did not do it, then the adventure would be proved to have been only a dream.
paragraphs.cn: 如果他没做，那这次冒险就只是一个梦。

paragraphs.en: “Hello, Huck!”
paragraphs.cn: “你好，哈克！”

paragraphs.en: “Hello, yourself.”
paragraphs.cn: “你也好啊。”

paragraphs.en: Silence, for a minute.
paragraphs.cn: 一分钟里，他们都没有说话。

paragraphs.en: “Tom, if we’d ’a’ left the blame tools at the dead tree, we’d ’a’ got the money.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，要是我们把那些该死的工具留在枯树那里，我们就能拿到钱了。哎呀，太糟糕了！”

paragraphs.en: Oh, ain’t it awful!”
paragraphs.cn: 哦，真糟糕呀！

paragraphs.en: “’Tain’t a dream, then, ’tain’t a dream!
paragraphs.cn: “那不是梦，不是梦！

paragraphs.en: Somehow I most wish it was.
paragraphs.cn: 我真希望那是个梦。

paragraphs.en: Dog’d if I don’t, Huck.”
paragraphs.cn: 我真是这么希望的，哈克。”

paragraphs.en: “What ain’t a dream?”
paragraphs.cn: “什么不是梦？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, that thing yesterday.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，就是昨天的事。

paragraphs.en: I been half thinking it was.”
paragraphs.cn: 我一直以为那是个梦呢。”

paragraphs.en: “Dream!
If them stairs hadn’t broke down you’d ’a’ seen how much dream it was!
paragraphs.cn: 要是那些楼梯没坏，你就能看到那是不是梦了！

paragraphs.en: I’ve had dreams enough all night—with that patch-eyed Spanish devil going for me all through ’em—rot him!”
paragraphs.cn: 我一整晚都在做梦——梦里那个戴眼罩的西班牙坏蛋一直追着我——气死我了！”

paragraphs.en: “No, not rot him.
paragraphs.cn: “不，别气他。”

paragraphs.en: _Find_ him!
paragraphs.cn: 找到他！

paragraphs.en: Track the money!”
paragraphs.cn: 跟着钱走！”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, we’ll never find him.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，我们永远也找不到他了。

paragraphs.en: A feller don’t have only one chance for such a pile—and that one’s lost.
paragraphs.cn: 这么大一笔钱，一个人只有一次机会。现在机会没了。

paragraphs.en: I’d feel mighty shaky if I was to see him, anyway.”
paragraphs.cn: 要是真见到他，我肯定会吓坏的。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, so’d I; but I’d like to see him, anyway—and track him out—to his Number Two.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我也是。但我还是想见到他—跟着他找到他的‘二号’。”

paragraphs.en: “Number Two—yes, that’s it.
paragraphs.cn: “二号—对，就是它。

paragraphs.en: I been thinking ’bout that.
paragraphs.cn: 我一直在想这个事。

paragraphs.en: But I can’t make nothing out of it.
paragraphs.cn: 但我搞不懂那是什么。

paragraphs.en: What do you reckon it is?”
paragraphs.cn: 你觉得它是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “I dono.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道。

paragraphs.en: It’s too deep.
paragraphs.cn: 这个太难了。

paragraphs.en: Say, Huck—maybe it’s the number of a house!”
paragraphs.cn: 喂，哈克—也许是房子的号码！”

paragraphs.en: “Goody!...
No, Tom, that ain’t it.
paragraphs.cn: 不，汤姆，不是那个。

paragraphs.en: If it is, it ain’t in this one-horse town.
paragraphs.cn: 如果真是，那也不是在这个小镇上。

paragraphs.en: They ain’t no numbers here.”
paragraphs.cn: 这里可没有门牌号。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, that’s so.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，是这样。

paragraphs.en: Lemme think a minute.
paragraphs.cn: 让我好好想想。

paragraphs.en: Here—it’s the number of a room—in a tavern, you know!”
paragraphs.cn: 有了—它是一间屋子的号码—是酒馆里的房间，你懂的！”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, that’s the trick!
paragraphs.cn: “哦，原来是这样！

paragraphs.en: They ain’t only two taverns.
paragraphs.cn: 这里只有两家酒馆。

paragraphs.en: We can find out quick.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们很快就能查出来。”

paragraphs.en: “You stay here, Huck, till I come.”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，你留在这儿，等我回来。”

paragraphs.en: Tom was off at once.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆立刻就走了。

paragraphs.en: He did not care to have Huck’s company in public places.
paragraphs.cn: 他不想在外面公共场合和哈克待在一起。

paragraphs.en: He was gone half an hour.
paragraphs.cn: 他走了半个小时。

paragraphs.en: He found that in the best tavern, No. 2 had long been occupied by a young lawyer, and was still so occupied.
paragraphs.cn: 他发现，最好的酒馆里，2号房间早就住了一个年轻律师，现在也还在住。

paragraphs.en: In the less ostentatious house, No. 2 was a mystery.
paragraphs.cn: 在另一家没那么豪华的酒馆，2号房间却很神秘。

paragraphs.en: The tavern-keeper’s young son said it was kept locked all the time, and he never saw anybody go into it or come out of it except at night; he did not know any particular reason for this state of things; had had some little curiosity, but it was rather feeble; had made the most of the mystery by entertaining himself with the idea that that room was “ha’nted”; had noticed that there was a light in there the night before.
paragraphs.cn: 酒馆老板的小儿子说，那个房间一直锁着。他从没见过有人进去或出来，只有晚上例外。他也不知道为什么会这样。他有点好奇，但也没太在意。他喜欢自己编个故事，说这房间是‘鬼屋’，觉得这样很有趣。他还发现，前一天晚上房间里亮着灯。

paragraphs.en: “That’s what I’ve found out, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “这是我发现的，哈克。

paragraphs.en: I reckon that’s the very No. 2 we’re after.”
paragraphs.cn: 我觉得那就是我们要找的二号。”

paragraphs.en: “I reckon it is, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “我觉得是，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: Now what you going to do?”
paragraphs.cn: 你现在打算怎么做？”

paragraphs.en: “Lemme think.”
paragraphs.cn: “让我想想。”

paragraphs.en: Tom thought a long time.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆想了很久。

paragraphs.en: Then he said:
paragraphs.cn: 然后他说：

paragraphs.en: “I’ll tell you.
paragraphs.cn: “我告诉你。

paragraphs.en: The back door of that No. 2 is the door that comes out into that little close alley between the tavern and the old rattle trap of a brick store.
paragraphs.cn: 那个二号的后门，就通向酒馆和那个破旧砖头店之间的小巷子。

paragraphs.en: Now you get hold of all the doorkeys you can find, and I’ll nip all of auntie’s, and the first dark night we’ll go there and try ’em.
paragraphs.cn: 你去把能找到的门钥匙都拿来，我去偷阿姨的钥匙，等第一个很黑的晚上，我们就去那里试试。

paragraphs.en: And mind you, keep a lookout for Injun Joe, because he said he was going to drop into town and spy around once more for a chance to get his revenge.
paragraphs.cn: 记住，你要留意印第安·乔，因为他说他要回城里再偷偷看看，找机会报仇。

paragraphs.en: If you see him, you just follow him; and if he don’t go to that No. 2, that ain’t the place.”
paragraphs.cn: 如果你看到他，就跟着他；要是他没去那个二号，那地方就不是。”

paragraphs.en: “Lordy, I don’t want to foller him by myself!”
paragraphs.cn: “天哪，我不想一个人跟着他！”

paragraphs.en: “Why, it’ll be night, sure.
paragraphs.cn: “哎，肯定是在晚上。

paragraphs.en: He mightn’t ever see you—and if he did, maybe he’d never think anything.”
paragraphs.cn: 他可能根本看不到你——就算看到了，他也许也不会多想什么。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, if it’s pretty dark I reckon I’ll track him.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，要是天很黑，我觉得我会跟着他。

paragraphs.en: I dono—I dono.
paragraphs.cn: 我不知道——我不知道。

paragraphs.en: I’ll try.”
paragraphs.cn: 我会试试的。”

paragraphs.en: “You bet I’ll follow him, if it’s dark, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “你放心，要是天黑，我肯定会跟着他，哈克。

paragraphs.en: Why, he might ’a’ found out he couldn’t get his revenge, and be going right after that money.”
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，他可能已经发现他报不了仇了，然后就直接去拿钱了呢。”

paragraphs.en: “It’s so, Tom, it’s so.
paragraphs.cn: “是啊，汤姆，是啊。

paragraphs.en: I’ll foller him; I will, by jingoes!”
paragraphs.cn: 我会跟着他；我一定会跟着的，真的！”

paragraphs.en: “Now you’re _talking_!
paragraphs.cn: “这才对嘛！

paragraphs.en: Don’t you ever weaken, Huck, and I won’t.”
paragraphs.cn: 你可别泄气啊，哈克，我也不会的。”

paragraphs.en: That night Tom and Huck were ready for their adventure.
paragraphs.cn: 那天晚上，汤姆和哈克准备好去冒险了。

paragraphs.en: They hung about the neighborhood of the tavern until after nine, one watching the alley at a distance and the other the tavern door.
paragraphs.cn: 他们待在酒馆附近，一直到九点以后，一个人远远地看着小巷，另一个人看着酒馆的门。

paragraphs.en: Nobody entered the alley or left it; nobody resembling the Spaniard entered or left the tavern door.
paragraphs.cn: 没有人进出小巷；也没有像那个西班牙人的人进出酒馆的门。

paragraphs.en: The night promised to be a fair one; so Tom went home with the understanding that if a considerable degree of darkness came on, Huck was to come and “maow,” whereupon he would slip out and try the keys.
paragraphs.cn: 那个晚上看起来不会很黑；所以汤姆回家了，他们说好要是天变得很黑，哈克就来“喵”一声，然后他就会溜出来试钥匙。

paragraphs.en: But the night remained clear, and Huck closed his watch and retired to bed in an empty sugar hogshead about twelve.
paragraphs.cn: 但是那个晚上一直很亮，哈克就结束了守候，大约十二点的时候，他睡在一个空的糖桶里了。

paragraphs.en: Tuesday the boys had the same ill luck.
paragraphs.cn: 星期二，这些孩子们还是运气不好。

paragraphs.en: Also Wednesday.
paragraphs.cn: 也是周三。

paragraphs.en: But Thursday night promised better.
paragraphs.cn: 可是周四晚上，情况会好转。

paragraphs.en: Tom slipped out in good season with his aunt’s old tin lantern, and a large towel to blindfold it with.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆悄悄溜出来了，带着姑妈的旧灯笼，还有条大毛巾，用来把灯笼蒙住。

paragraphs.en: He hid the lantern in Huck’s sugar hogshead and the watch began.
paragraphs.cn: 他把灯笼藏在哈克的糖桶里，就开始守着。

paragraphs.en: An hour before midnight the tavern closed up and its lights (the only ones thereabouts) were put out.
paragraphs.cn: 午夜前一小时，酒馆关门了，灯也灭了（那是附近唯一的亮光）。

paragraphs.en: No Spaniard had been seen.
paragraphs.cn: 没看到西班牙人。

paragraphs.en: Nobody had entered or left the alley.
paragraphs.cn: 没人进出小巷。

paragraphs.en: Everything was auspicious.
paragraphs.cn: 一切都很顺利。

paragraphs.en: The blackness of darkness reigned, the perfect stillness was interrupted only by occasional mutterings of distant thunder.
paragraphs.cn: 周围一片漆黑，非常安静，只有远处偶尔传来几声雷鸣。

paragraphs.en: Tom got his lantern, lit it in the hogshead, wrapped it closely in the towel, and the two adventurers crept in the gloom toward the tavern.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆拿出灯笼，在桶里点亮，用毛巾紧紧包好。两个小朋友就悄悄地，在黑漆漆中走向酒馆。

paragraphs.en: Huck stood sentry and Tom felt his way into the alley.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克负责放哨，汤姆摸黑走进了小巷。

paragraphs.en: Then there was a season of waiting anxiety that weighed upon Huck’s spirits like a mountain.
paragraphs.cn: 接着是一阵焦急的等待，像一座大山一样，压得哈克心里喘不过气来。

paragraphs.en: He began to wish he could see a flash from the lantern—it would frighten him, but it would at least tell him that Tom was alive yet.
paragraphs.cn: 他开始希望看到灯笼闪一下——那会吓到他，但至少会告诉他，汤姆还活着呢。

paragraphs.en: It seemed hours since Tom had disappeared.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆消失了，感觉好像好几个小时过去了。

paragraphs.en: Surely he must have fainted; maybe he was dead; maybe his heart had burst under terror and excitement.
paragraphs.cn: 他肯定晕倒了；也许死了；也许是吓得、兴奋得，心都快跳出来了。

paragraphs.en: In his uneasiness Huck found himself drawing closer and closer to the alley; fearing all sorts of dreadful things, and momentarily expecting some catastrophe to happen that would take away his breath.
paragraphs.cn: 他心里很不安，发现自己离小巷越来越近。他害怕各种可怕的事，随时觉得会有什么灾难发生，吓得他不敢呼吸。

paragraphs.en: There was not much to take away, for he seemed only able to inhale it by thimblefuls, and his heart would soon wear itself out, the way it was beating.
paragraphs.cn: 他本来就没多少气可以吓掉，好像只能一点点地吸气。他的心跳得那么快，再这样下去，很快就会累坏的。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly there was a flash of light and Tom came tearing by him: “Run!” said he; “run, for your life!”
paragraphs.cn: 突然，一道亮光闪过，汤姆飞快地从他身边跑过：“快跑！”他说；“快跑，快逃命呀！”

paragraphs.en: He needn’t have repeated it; once was enough; Huck was making thirty or forty miles an hour before the repetition was uttered.
paragraphs.cn: 他不用重复第二遍，一遍就够了。哈克在他重复之前，就已经跑得飞快了。

paragraphs.en: The boys never stopped till they reached the shed of a deserted slaughter-house at the lower end of the village.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们一直没停，跑到村子尽头一个废弃的屠宰场棚子才停下。

paragraphs.en: Just as they got within its shelter the storm burst and the rain poured down.
paragraphs.cn: 他们刚躲进棚子里，暴风雨就来了，大雨哗哗地往下倒。

paragraphs.en: As soon as Tom got his breath he said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆刚喘过气来，就说：

paragraphs.en: “Huck, it was awful!
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，太吓人了！

paragraphs.en: I tried two of the keys, just as soft as I could; but they seemed to make such a power of racket that I couldn’t hardly get my breath I was so scared.
paragraphs.cn: 我试了两把钥匙，动作已经很轻很轻了；可是它们弄出的声音太大了，我吓得都快喘不过气了。

paragraphs.en: They wouldn’t turn in the lock, either.
paragraphs.cn: 钥匙也拧不动锁。

paragraphs.en: Well, without noticing what I was doing, I took hold of the knob, and open comes the door!
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，我没注意到自己在做什么，就去握门把手，结果门一下就开了！

paragraphs.en: It warn’t locked!
paragraphs.cn: 门根本没锁！

paragraphs.en: I hopped in, and shook off the towel, and, _Great Caesar’s Ghost!
paragraphs.cn: 我跳了进去，抖掉了毛巾，然后，_天哪！_

paragraphs.en: “What!
paragraphs.cn: “什么呀！”

paragraphs.en: —what’d you see, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: ——你看到了什么，汤姆？”

paragraphs.en: “Huck, I most stepped onto Injun Joe’s hand!”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，我差点踩到印第安·乔的手了！”

paragraphs.en: “No!”
“Yes!
paragraphs.cn: “是啊！

paragraphs.en: He was lying there, sound asleep on the floor, with his old patch on his eye and his arms spread out.”
paragraphs.cn: 他躺在那里，在地板上睡得可熟了，眼睛上还蒙着旧眼罩，胳膊也张开了。”

paragraphs.en: “Lordy, what did you do?
paragraphs.cn: “天哪，你做了什么？

paragraphs.en: Did he wake up?”
paragraphs.cn: 他醒了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No, never budged.
paragraphs.cn: “没有，他一动也没动。

paragraphs.en: Drunk, I reckon.
paragraphs.cn: 我看他是喝醉了。

paragraphs.en: I just grabbed that towel and started!”
paragraphs.cn: 我就拿起那条毛巾，开始动手了！”

paragraphs.en: “I’d never ’a’ thought of the towel, I bet!”
paragraphs.cn: “我可从来没想过用毛巾，真的！”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I would.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我就会。

paragraphs.en: My aunt would make me mighty sick if I lost it.”
paragraphs.cn: 要是我弄丢了它，我阿姨会气得要命。”

paragraphs.en: “Say, Tom, did you see that box?”
paragraphs.cn: “喂，汤姆，你看到那个盒子了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Huck, I didn’t wait to look around.
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，我没来得及四处看。

paragraphs.en: I didn’t see the box, I didn’t see the cross.
paragraphs.cn: 我没看到盒子，也没看到十字架。

paragraphs.en: I didn’t see anything but a bottle and a tin cup on the floor by Injun Joe; yes, I saw two barrels and lots more bottles in the room.
paragraphs.cn: 我什么都没看到，除了印第安·乔旁边地板上的一个瓶子和一个锡杯；是啊，我还看到屋里有两个桶和很多瓶子。

paragraphs.en: Don’t you see, now, what’s the matter with that ha’nted room?”
paragraphs.cn: 你现在还不明白吗，那个闹鬼的房间是怎么回事？”

paragraphs.en: “How?”
paragraphs.cn: “怎么会？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, it’s ha’nted with whiskey!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，那里面全是威士忌在‘闹鬼’呢！

paragraphs.en: Maybe _all_ the Temperance Taverns have got a ha’nted room, hey, Huck?”
paragraphs.cn: 也许所有的禁酒小酒馆都有个‘闹鬼’的房间，你说呢，哈克？”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I reckon maybe that’s so.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我猜也许真是这样。

paragraphs.en: Who’d ’a’ thought such a thing?
paragraphs.cn: 谁会想到这种事呢？

paragraphs.en: But say, Tom, now’s a mighty good time to get that box, if Injun Joe’s drunk.”
paragraphs.cn: 不过喂，汤姆，要是印第安·乔喝醉了，现在可是拿那个盒子的好时候。”

paragraphs.en: “It is, that!
paragraphs.cn: “没错，就是这样！

paragraphs.en: You try it!”
paragraphs.cn: 你去试试看！”

paragraphs.en: Huck shuddered.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克打了个寒颤。

paragraphs.en: “Well, no—I reckon not.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，不行——我看还是算了。”

paragraphs.en: “And I reckon not, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “我看也不行，哈克。

paragraphs.en: Only one bottle alongside of Injun Joe ain’t enough.
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔旁边只有一瓶酒，这可不够。”

paragraphs.en: If there’d been three, he’d be drunk enough and I’d do it.”
paragraphs.cn: 要是喝了三杯，他肯定醉了，我就可以去做了。

paragraphs.en: There was a long pause for reflection, and then Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 他们想了很久，然后汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “Lookyhere, Huck, less not try that thing any more till we know Injun Joe’s not in there.
paragraphs.cn: “听着，哈克，我们别再试那个了，直到我们知道印第安·乔不在里面。

paragraphs.en: It’s too scary.
paragraphs.cn: 那太吓人了。

paragraphs.en: Now, if we watch every night, we’ll be dead sure to see him go out, some time or other, and then we’ll snatch that box quicker’n lightning.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在，如果我们每天晚上都看着，就一定能看到他出去，到时候，我们就能像闪电一样快地把盒子拿走！”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’m agreed.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，我同意。

paragraphs.en: I’ll watch the whole night long, and I’ll do it every night, too, if you’ll do the other part of the job.”
paragraphs.cn: 我会看一整晚，每天晚上都看，如果你能做另一部分的话。”

paragraphs.en: “All right, I will.
paragraphs.cn: “好，我做。

paragraphs.en: All you got to do is to trot up Hooper Street a block and maow—and if I’m asleep, you throw some gravel at the window and that’ll fetch me.”
paragraphs.cn: 你只要走到胡珀街一个街区远的地方，喵喵叫几声就行——要是我睡着了，你就往窗户上扔些小石子，我就会醒的。”

paragraphs.en: “Agreed, and good as wheat!”
paragraphs.cn: “同意，一言为定！”

paragraphs.en: “Now, Huck, the storm’s over, and I’ll go home.
paragraphs.cn: “好了，哈克，暴风雨停了，我要回家了。

paragraphs.en: It’ll begin to be daylight in a couple of hours.
paragraphs.cn: 再过一两个小时天就亮了。

paragraphs.en: You go back and watch that long, will you?”
paragraphs.cn: 你回去再看一会儿，好吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I said I would, Tom, and I will.
paragraphs.cn: “我说我会的，汤姆，我一定会的。

paragraphs.en: I’ll ha’nt that tavern every night for a year!
paragraphs.cn: 我会每天晚上都在那个小酒馆附近守着，守一年！

paragraphs.en: I’ll sleep all day and I’ll stand watch all night.”
paragraphs.cn: 我白天睡觉，晚上守着。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s all right.
paragraphs.cn: “那好吧。

paragraphs.en: Now, where you going to sleep?”
paragraphs.cn: 你打算睡哪儿呢？”

paragraphs.en: “In Ben Rogers’ hayloft.
paragraphs.cn: “在本·罗杰斯家的干草棚里。

paragraphs.en: He lets me, and so does his pap’s nigger man, Uncle Jake.
paragraphs.cn: 他让我睡，他爸爸那儿的杰克叔叔也让我睡。

paragraphs.en: I tote water for Uncle Jake whenever he wants me to, and any time I ask him he gives me a little something to eat if he can spare it.
paragraphs.cn: 杰克叔叔要我帮忙挑水时我就去，我什么时候问他要吃的，他有的话就会给我一点。

paragraphs.en: That’s a mighty good nigger, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 他真是个好人，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: He likes me, becuz I don’t ever act as if I was above him.
paragraphs.cn: 他喜欢我，因为我从来不觉得自己比他厉害。

paragraphs.en: Sometime I’ve set right down and eat _with_ him.
paragraphs.cn: 有时候我还和他一起坐下来吃饭呢。

paragraphs.en: But you needn’t tell that.
paragraphs.cn: 不过你不用告诉别人。

paragraphs.en: A body’s got to do things when he’s awful hungry he wouldn’t want to do as a steady thing.”
paragraphs.cn: 一个人饿得不行的时候，会做一些平时不想做的事情。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, if I don’t want you in the daytime, I’ll let you sleep.
paragraphs.cn: “好，如果我白天不需要你帮忙，就让你睡觉。

paragraphs.en: I won’t come bothering around.
paragraphs.cn: 我不会去打扰你的。

paragraphs.en: Any time you see something’s up, in the night, just skip right around and maow.”
paragraphs.cn: 晚上你什么时候看到有什么情况，就马上跑过来喵喵叫。”

paragraphs.en: The first thing Tom heard on Friday morning was a glad piece of news—Judge Thatcher’s family had come back to town the night before.
paragraphs.cn: 星期五早上，汤姆听到的第一个好消息是——撒切尔法官一家人在前一天晚上回城了。

paragraphs.en: Both Injun Joe and the treasure sunk into secondary importance for a moment, and Becky took the chief place in the boy’s interest.
paragraphs.cn: 暂时，印第安·乔和宝藏都不那么重要了。小男孩最感兴趣的是贝琪。

paragraphs.en: He saw her and they had an exhausting good time playing “hispy” and “gully-keeper” with a crowd of their schoolmates.
paragraphs.cn: 他看到了她，然后他们和一群同学玩“hispy”和“gully-keeper”，玩得筋疲力尽，但很开心。

paragraphs.en: The day was completed and crowned in a peculiarly satisfactory way: Becky teased her mother to appoint the next day for the long-promised and long-delayed picnic, and she consented.
paragraphs.cn: 这天过得特别让人满意：贝琪缠着妈妈，让她把早就答应好的野餐定在第二天，妈妈同意了。

paragraphs.en: The child’s delight was boundless; and Tom’s not more moderate.
paragraphs.cn: 小孩们开心极了；汤姆也一样高兴。

paragraphs.en: The invitations were sent out before sunset, and straightway the young folks of the village were thrown into a fever of preparation and pleasurable anticipation.
paragraphs.cn: 太阳下山前，请帖就发出去了。村里的小伙伴们立刻兴奋起来，开始准备，满心期待。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s excitement enabled him to keep awake until a pretty late hour, and he had good hopes of hearing Huck’s “maow,” and of having his treasure to astonish Becky and the picnickers with, next day; but he was disappointed.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆太兴奋了，一直醒到很晚。他很希望能听到哈克的“喵呜”声，还想着第二天可以用他的宝贝吓唬吓唬贝琪和去野餐的人；但他失望了。

paragraphs.en: No signal came that night.
paragraphs.cn: 那晚，没有信号传来。

paragraphs.en: Morning came, eventually, and by ten or eleven o’clock a giddy and rollicking company were gathered at Judge Thatcher’s, and everything was ready for a start.
paragraphs.cn: 终于到了早上，十点或十一点的时候，一群又开心又闹腾的小伙伴们都聚集在撒切尔法官家，一切都准备好出发了。

paragraphs.en: It was not the custom for elderly people to mar the picnics with their presence.
paragraphs.cn: 老年人一般不会来野餐，免得扫了大家的兴。

paragraphs.en: The children were considered safe enough under the wings of a few young ladies of eighteen and a few young gentlemen of twenty-three or thereabouts.
paragraphs.cn: 有几个十八岁的年轻阿姨和二十三岁左右的年轻叔叔们看着，孩子们就被认为足够安全了。

paragraphs.en: The old steam ferry-boat was chartered for the occasion; presently the gay throng filed up the main street laden with provision-baskets.
paragraphs.cn: 那艘旧蒸汽渡船被租下来了；很快，开心的队伍就带着装满食物的篮子，排着队走上了主街。

paragraphs.en: Sid was sick and had to miss the fun; Mary remained at home to entertain him.
paragraphs.cn: 希德生病了，不能去玩；玛丽留在家里陪他。

paragraphs.en: The last thing Mrs. Thatcher said to Becky, was:
paragraphs.cn: 撒切尔太太对贝琪说的最后一句话是：

paragraphs.en: “You’ll not get back till late.
paragraphs.cn: “你会玩到很晚才回来。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps you’d better stay all night with some of the girls that live near the ferry-landing, child.”
paragraphs.cn: 孩子，也许你最好跟住在渡口附近的几个女孩子住一晚吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Then I’ll stay with Susy Harper, mamma.”
paragraphs.cn: “那我跟苏西·哈珀住，妈妈。”

paragraphs.en: “Very well.
paragraphs.cn: “好的。

paragraphs.en: And mind and behave yourself and don’t be any trouble.”
paragraphs.cn: 记得要听话，别惹麻烦哦。”

paragraphs.en: Presently, as they tripped along, Tom said to Becky:
paragraphs.cn: 走着走着，汤姆对贝琪说：

paragraphs.en: “Say—I’ll tell you what we’ll do.
paragraphs.cn: “听着——我告诉你我们怎么做。

paragraphs.en: ’Stead of going to Joe Harper’s we’ll climb right up the hill and stop at the Widow Douglas’.
paragraphs.cn: 我们不去乔·哈珀家了，我们直接爬上山，去道格拉斯寡妇家。

paragraphs.en: She’ll have ice-cream!
paragraphs.cn: 她家会有冰淇淋！

paragraphs.en: She has it most every day—dead loads of it.
paragraphs.cn: 她几乎每天都有冰淇淋——超级多。

paragraphs.en: And she’ll be awful glad to have us.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且她会非常高兴我们去。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, that will be fun!”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，那太好玩了！”

paragraphs.en: Then Becky reflected a moment and said:
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪想了想，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “But what will mamma say?”
paragraphs.cn: “可是妈妈会怎么说呢？”

paragraphs.en: “How’ll she ever know?”
paragraphs.cn: “她怎么会知道呢？”

paragraphs.en: The girl turned the idea over in her mind, and said reluctantly:
paragraphs.cn: 女孩在心里琢磨了一下，不情愿地说：

paragraphs.en: “I reckon it’s wrong—but—”
paragraphs.cn: “我觉得这不对——可是——”

paragraphs.en: “But shucks!
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀！

paragraphs.en: Your mother won’t know, and so what’s the harm?
paragraphs.cn: 你妈妈不会知道的，有什么关系呢？

paragraphs.en: All she wants is that you’ll be safe; and I bet you she’d ’a’ said go there if she’d ’a’ thought of it.
paragraphs.cn: 她只希望你平安。我敢说，如果她想到这个地方，她肯定会让你去的。

paragraphs.en: I know she would!”
paragraphs.cn: 我知道她会的！

paragraphs.en: The Widow Douglas’ splendid hospitality was a tempting bait.
paragraphs.cn: 道格拉斯寡妇家里真好玩，太吸引人了。

paragraphs.en: It and Tom’s persuasions presently carried the day.
paragraphs.cn: 他被汤姆的好玩和劝说打动了。

paragraphs.en: So it was decided to say nothing to anybody about the night’s programme.
paragraphs.cn: 所以他们决定不告诉任何人今晚要做什么。

paragraphs.en: Presently it occurred to Tom that maybe Huck might come this very night and give the signal.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，汤姆想到，也许哈克今晚就会来发信号。

paragraphs.en: The thought took a deal of the spirit out of his anticipations.
paragraphs.cn: 这个想法让他没那么开心了。

paragraphs.en: Still he could not bear to give up the fun at Widow Douglas’.
paragraphs.cn: 但他还是舍不得放弃去道格拉斯寡妇家玩。

paragraphs.en: And why should he give it up, he reasoned—the signal did not come the night before, so why should it be any more likely to come tonight?
paragraphs.cn: 他想，为什么要放弃呢？昨晚暗号没来，今晚也不一定来啊？

paragraphs.en: The sure fun of the evening outweighed the uncertain treasure; and, boy-like, he determined to yield to the stronger inclination and not allow himself to think of the box of money another time that day.
paragraphs.cn: 晚上肯定能玩得很开心，这比不确定的宝藏更吸引人。他像个孩子一样，决定跟着自己的心走，那天再也不去想那箱钱了。

paragraphs.en: Three miles below town the ferryboat stopped at the mouth of a woody hollow and tied up.
paragraphs.cn: 在离小镇三英里远的地方，渡船在一个长满树木的山谷口停了下来。

paragraphs.en: The crowd swarmed ashore and soon the forest distances and craggy heights echoed far and near with shoutings and laughter.
paragraphs.cn: 大家涌上岸，很快，远处森林和高高的山崖，到处都回荡着叫喊声和笑声。

paragraphs.en: All the different ways of getting hot and tired were gone through with, and by-and-by the rovers straggled back to camp fortified with responsible appetites, and then the destruction of the good things began.
paragraphs.cn: 大家玩得又热又累。过了一会儿，这群孩子们才三三两两地回到营地。他们肚子饿得咕咕叫，然后就开始大吃特吃美味的食物了。

paragraphs.en: After the feast there was a refreshing season of rest and chat in the shade of spreading oaks.
paragraphs.cn: 吃完大餐，大家在枝繁叶茂的橡树荫下休息聊天，感觉很舒服。

paragraphs.en: By-and-by somebody shouted:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，有人喊道：

paragraphs.en: “Who’s ready for the cave?”
paragraphs.cn: “谁准备好去山洞了？”

paragraphs.en: Everybody was.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都准备好了。

paragraphs.en: Bundles of candles were procured, and straightway there was a general scamper up the hill.
paragraphs.cn: 大家拿来很多蜡烛，然后立刻冲上山坡。

paragraphs.en: The mouth of the cave was up the hillside—an opening shaped like a letter A.
paragraphs.cn: 山洞口在山坡上，形状像字母A。

paragraphs.en: Its massive oaken door stood unbarred.
paragraphs.cn: 它厚重的橡木门开着。

paragraphs.en: Within was a small chamber, chilly as an icehouse, and walled by Nature with solid limestone that was dewy with a cold sweat.
paragraphs.cn: 里面是个小房间，像冰窖一样冷。墙壁是天然的坚硬石灰岩，上面湿漉漉的，像出了冷汗。

paragraphs.en: It was romantic and mysterious to stand here in the deep gloom and look out upon the green valley shining in the sun.
paragraphs.cn: 站在这里黑漆漆的山洞里，看着外面阳光下绿色的山谷，感觉既浪漫又神秘。

paragraphs.en: But the impressiveness of the situation quickly wore off, and the romping began again.
paragraphs.cn: 但这种特别的感觉很快就没了，大家又开始打闹起来。

paragraphs.en: The moment a candle was lighted there was a general rush upon the owner of it; a struggle and a gallant defence followed, but the candle was soon knocked down or blown out, and then there was a glad clamor of laughter and a new chase.
paragraphs.cn: 蜡烛一点亮，大家就冲上去抢拿蜡烛的人。虽然蜡烛主人努力保护，但很快蜡烛就被打翻或吹灭了。然后又是一阵开心的笑声，大家又开始了新的追逐。

paragraphs.en: But all things have an end.
paragraphs.cn: 但所有事情都会结束。

paragraphs.en: By-and-by the procession went filing down the steep descent of the main avenue, the flickering rank of lights dimly revealing the lofty walls of rock almost to their point of junction sixty feet overhead.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，队伍沿着主通道陡峭的下坡排队往前走。摇曳的烛光模模糊糊地照亮了高高的石壁，几乎能看到上方六十英尺高，石壁交接的地方。

paragraphs.en: This main avenue was not more than eight or ten feet wide.
paragraphs.cn: 这条主通道只有八到十英尺宽。

paragraphs.en: Every few steps other lofty and still narrower crevices branched from it on either hand—for McDougal’s cave was but a vast labyrinth of crooked aisles that ran into each other and out again and led nowhere.
paragraphs.cn: 每走几步，两边就会有其他更高更窄的裂缝分岔出来。因为麦克杜格尔的山洞就像一个大迷宫，里面弯弯曲曲的小路互相连着，又通向没有尽头的地方。

paragraphs.en: It was said that one might wander days and nights together through its intricate tangle of rifts and chasms, and never find the end of the cave; and that he might go down, and down, and still down, into the earth, and it was just the same—labyrinth under labyrinth, and no end to any of them.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都说，这个山洞很大很大。你走啊走，白天走到晚上都走不完。它下面还有好多好多的路，就像迷宫一样，根本没有尽头。

paragraphs.en: No man “knew” the cave.
paragraphs.cn: 没有人能完全知道这个山洞。

paragraphs.en: That was an impossible thing.
paragraphs.cn: 这根本做不到。

paragraphs.en: Most of the young men knew a portion of it, and it was not customary to venture much beyond this known portion.
paragraphs.cn: 大部分年轻人只知道山洞的一部分，他们一般不会走太远。

paragraphs.en: Tom Sawyer knew as much of the cave as any one.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆·索亚 对山洞的了解和别人一样多。

paragraphs.en: The procession moved along the main avenue some three-quarters of a mile, and then groups and couples began to slip aside into branch avenues, fly along the dismal corridors, and take each other by surprise at points where the corridors joined again.
paragraphs.cn: 大家沿着主路走了很远。接着，一些人就拐进旁边的小路，在黑黑的通道里跑来跑去，在路口互相吓一跳。

paragraphs.en: Parties were able to elude each other for the space of half an hour without going beyond the “known” ground.
paragraphs.cn: 他们可以在“认识”的地方玩半个小时捉迷藏，而且不会走出太远。

paragraphs.en: By-and-by, one group after another came straggling back to the mouth of the cave, panting, hilarious, smeared from head to foot with tallow drippings, daubed with clay, and entirely delighted with the success of the day.
paragraphs.cn: 后来，一队队的人陆陆续续回到山洞口。他们喘着气，开开心心的，身上沾满了蜡油和泥巴，对今天玩得开心极了。

paragraphs.en: Then they were astonished to find that they had been taking no note of time and that night was about at hand.
paragraphs.cn: 他们惊讶地发现，自己竟然没注意到时间，天快黑了。

paragraphs.en: The clanging bell had been calling for half an hour.
paragraphs.cn: 大钟已经叮当响了半个小时。

paragraphs.en: However, this sort of close to the day’s adventures was romantic and therefore satisfactory.
paragraphs.cn: 但是，用这种方式结束一天的探险，感觉又刺激又好玩。

paragraphs.en: When the ferryboat with her wild freight pushed into the stream, nobody cared sixpence for the wasted time but the captain of the craft.
paragraphs.cn: 当渡船载着吵吵闹闹的人开走时，除了船长，没人觉得时间浪费了。

paragraphs.en: Huck was already upon his watch when the ferryboat’s lights went glinting past the wharf.
paragraphs.cn: 当渡船的灯光闪过码头时，哈克 已经在值班了。

paragraphs.en: He heard no noise on board, for the young people were as subdued and still as people usually are who are nearly tired to death.
paragraphs.cn: 船上一点声音也没有，因为那些年轻人累坏了，都变得很安静。

paragraphs.en: He wondered what boat it was, and why she did not stop at the wharf—and then he dropped her out of his mind and put his attention upon his business.
paragraphs.cn: 他想这是什么船？它为什么不停靠码头呢？不过他很快就不想了，开始专心工作。

paragraphs.en: The night was growing cloudy and dark.
paragraphs.cn: 晚上天色越来越阴暗了。

paragraphs.en: Ten o’clock came, and the noise of vehicles ceased, scattered lights began to wink out, all straggling foot-passengers disappeared, the village betook itself to its slumbers and left the small watcher alone with the silence and the ghosts.
paragraphs.cn: 十点到了，车子声音没有了，零星的灯光也一个个熄灭。路上的人都走光了。整个村子都睡着了，只剩下小小的守夜人，周围很安静，感觉空荡荡的。

paragraphs.en: Eleven o’clock came, and the tavern lights were put out; darkness everywhere, now.
paragraphs.cn: 十一点到了，酒馆的灯也灭了；现在到处都是一片漆黑。

paragraphs.en: Huck waited what seemed a weary long time, but nothing happened.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 等了好久好久，可什么事也没发生。

paragraphs.en: His faith was weakening.
paragraphs.cn: 他开始有点没信心了。

paragraphs.en: Was there any use?
paragraphs.cn: 还有用吗？

paragraphs.en: Was there really any use?
paragraphs.cn: 真的还有用吗？

paragraphs.en: Why not give it up and turn in?
paragraphs.cn: 为什么不放弃，去睡觉算了？

paragraphs.en: A noise fell upon his ear.
paragraphs.cn: 他听到了一点声音。

paragraphs.en: He was all attention in an instant.
paragraphs.cn: 他一下子就竖起耳朵仔细听。

paragraphs.en: The alley door closed softly.
paragraphs.cn: 小巷的门轻轻地关上了。

paragraphs.en: He sprang to the corner of the brick store.
paragraphs.cn: 他嗖地一下躲到砖头商店的墙角。

paragraphs.en: The next moment two men brushed by him, and one seemed to have something under his arm.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，两个男人从他身边走过，其中一个人胳膊下面好像夹着什么东西。

paragraphs.en: It must be that box!
paragraphs.cn: 一定是那个箱子！

paragraphs.en: So they were going to remove the treasure.
paragraphs.cn: 那么他们是要把宝藏搬走。

paragraphs.en: Why call Tom now?
paragraphs.cn: 现在为什么要叫汤姆呢？

paragraphs.en: It would be absurd—the men would get away with the box and never be found again.
paragraphs.cn: 那样太傻了。那些人会带着箱子跑掉，就再也找不到了。

paragraphs.en: No, he would stick to their wake and follow them; he would trust to the darkness for security from discovery.
paragraphs.cn: 不，他要悄悄跟着他们。他相信黑夜能帮他藏好，不被发现。

paragraphs.en: So communing with himself, Huck stepped out and glided along behind the men, cat-like, with bare feet, allowing them to keep just far enough ahead not to be invisible.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克心里这么想着，就走了出来。他光着脚，像猫一样，悄悄跟在那些人后面。他让那些人走在前面，但不能离得太远，不然就看不见了。

paragraphs.en: They moved up the river street three blocks, then turned to the left up a crossstreet.
paragraphs.cn: 他们沿着河边的路走了三个街区，然后左转，拐进一条小街。

paragraphs.en: They went straight ahead, then, until they came to the path that led up Cardiff Hill; this they took.
paragraphs.cn: 他们一直往前走，直到看到一条通往卡迪夫山的小路。他们就走上了那条路。

paragraphs.en: They passed by the old Welshman’s house, halfway up the hill, without hesitating, and still climbed upward.
paragraphs.cn: 他们经过了半山腰上老威尔士人的房子，没有停，还在往上爬。

paragraphs.en: Good, thought Huck, they will bury it in the old quarry.
paragraphs.cn: “太好了，”哈克想，“他们会把它埋在那个老采石场。”

paragraphs.en: But they never stopped at the quarry.
paragraphs.cn: 但是他们没有在采石场停下来。

paragraphs.en: They passed on, up the summit.
paragraphs.cn: 他们继续往前走，一直走到山顶。

paragraphs.en: They plunged into the narrow path between the tall sumach bushes, and were at once hidden in the gloom.
paragraphs.cn: 他们钻进了高高的盐肤木丛之间的小路，一下子就消失在黑暗中了。

paragraphs.en: Huck closed up and shortened his distance, now, for they would never be able to see him.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克现在走近了一些，因为那些人再也看不见他了。

paragraphs.en: He trotted along awhile; then slackened his pace, fearing he was gaining too fast; moved on a piece, then stopped altogether; listened; no sound; none, save that he seemed to hear the beating of his own heart.
paragraphs.cn: 他走了一会儿，然后放慢了脚步，怕自己走得太快了。他又走了一小段，就完全停住了。他听了听，没有声音，什么声音都没有，只有他自己的心跳声。

paragraphs.en: The hooting of an owl came over the hill—ominous sound!
paragraphs.cn: 猫头鹰的叫声从山上飘过来——这声音真不吉利！

paragraphs.en: But no footsteps.
paragraphs.cn: 但是没有脚步声。

paragraphs.en: Heavens, was everything lost!
paragraphs.cn: 天哪，一切都完了吗！

paragraphs.en: He was about to spring with winged feet, when a man cleared his throat not four feet from him!
paragraphs.cn: 他正要飞奔起来，突然，一个男人在他身边清了清嗓子，离他不到四英尺远！

paragraphs.en: Huck’s heart shot into his throat, but he swallowed it again; and then he stood there shaking as if a dozen agues had taken charge of him at once, and so weak that he thought he must surely fall to the ground.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克的心都跳到嗓子眼了，但他又把它咽了回去。他站在那里发抖，好像突然生了好几场大病，虚弱得觉得自己一定会倒在地上。

paragraphs.en: He knew where he was.
paragraphs.cn: 他知道自己在哪儿。

paragraphs.en: He knew he was within five steps of the stile leading into Widow Douglas’ grounds.
paragraphs.cn: 他知道自己离进入道格拉斯寡妇家院子的台阶，只有五步远了。

paragraphs.en: Very well, he thought, let them bury it there; it won’t be hard to find.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，”他想，“让他们把它埋在那里吧，这样就不难找到了。”

paragraphs.en: Now there was a voice—a very low voice—Injun Joe’s:
paragraphs.cn: 这时，传来了一个声音——很低很低的声音——是印第安·乔的声音：

paragraphs.en: “Damn her, maybe she’s got company—there’s lights, late as it is.”
paragraphs.cn: “哼，这个女人，也许她家里有人——都这么晚了，还有灯光亮着。”

paragraphs.en: “I can’t see any.”
paragraphs.cn: “我没看到灯光。”

paragraphs.en: This was that stranger’s voice—the stranger of the haunted house.
paragraphs.cn: 这是那个陌生人的声音——就是那个闹鬼房子里的陌生人。

paragraphs.en: A deadly chill went to Huck’s heart—this, then, was the “revenge” job!
paragraphs.cn: 哈克的心里一阵冰凉——原来，这就是他们说的“报仇”的事！

paragraphs.en: His thought was, to fly.
paragraphs.cn: 他心里想，快跑！

paragraphs.en: Then he remembered that the Widow Douglas had been kind to him more than once, and maybe these men were going to murder her.
paragraphs.cn: 他又想起，道格拉斯寡妇对他很好，不止一次帮助过他。也许这些人是要去杀她呢。

paragraphs.en: He wished he dared venture to warn her; but he knew he didn’t dare—they might come and catch him.
paragraphs.cn: 他真希望自己敢去告诉她，让她小心；但他知道自己不敢——那些人可能会过来抓他。

paragraphs.en: He thought all this and more in the moment that elapsed between the stranger’s remark and Injun Joe’s next—which was—
paragraphs.cn: 在那个陌生人说完话和印第安·乔说下一句话之间，他想了这么多，甚至更多——接着，印第安·乔又说——

paragraphs.en: “Because the bush is in your way.
paragraphs.cn: “因为那片灌木挡住了你的路。

paragraphs.en: Now—this way—now you see, don’t you?”
paragraphs.cn: 现在——这边——你看到了，对不对？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes.
paragraphs.cn: “是的。

paragraphs.en: Well, there _is_ company there, I reckon.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，我觉得那里有人。

paragraphs.en: Better give it up.”
paragraphs.cn: 还是放弃吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Give it up, and I just leaving this country forever!
paragraphs.cn: “放弃？那我永远离开这个地方了！

paragraphs.en: Give it up and maybe never have another chance.
paragraphs.cn: 放弃了，也许就再也没机会了。

paragraphs.en: I tell you again, as I’ve told you before, I don’t care for her swag—you may have it.
paragraphs.cn: 我再说一遍，我以前也说过，我不在乎她的财物——你可以拿走。

paragraphs.en: But her husband was rough on me—many times he was rough on me—and mainly he was the justice of the peace that jugged me for a vagrant.
paragraphs.cn: 但她丈夫对我不好——他对我很多次都很粗暴——而且他就是那个把我当成流浪汉关起来的太平绅士。

paragraphs.en: And that ain’t all.
paragraphs.cn: 这还不算完。

paragraphs.en: It ain’t a millionth part of it!
paragraphs.cn: 这只是很少很少的一部分！

paragraphs.en: He had me _horsewhipped_!
paragraphs.cn: 他让人用马鞭抽我！

paragraphs.en: —horsewhipped in front of the jail, like a nigger!
paragraphs.cn: ——在监狱前面，像对待下贱人一样被马鞭抽打！

paragraphs.en: —with all the town looking on!
paragraphs.cn: ——全镇的人都看着！

paragraphs.en: _Horsewhipped_!
paragraphs.cn: 被马鞭抽打！

paragraphs.en: —do you understand?
paragraphs.cn: ——你明白吗？

paragraphs.en: He took advantage of me and died.
paragraphs.cn: 他欺负了我，然后死了。

paragraphs.en: But I’ll take it out of _her_.”
paragraphs.cn: 但我要在她身上报仇。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, don’t kill her!
paragraphs.cn: “哦，别杀她！

paragraphs.en: Don’t do that!”
paragraphs.cn: 别那样做！”

paragraphs.en: “Kill?
paragraphs.cn: “杀人？

paragraphs.en: Who said anything about killing?
paragraphs.cn: 谁说过要杀人？

paragraphs.en: I would kill _him_ if he was here; but not her.
paragraphs.cn: 如果他在这里，我会杀了他；但不是她。

paragraphs.en: When you want to get revenge on a woman you don’t kill her—bosh! you go for her looks.
paragraphs.cn: 如果你想报复一个女人，你不会杀了她——胡说！你要毁掉她的容貌。

paragraphs.en: You slit her nostrils—you notch her ears like a sow!”
paragraphs.cn: 你割开她的鼻孔——你像给母猪做记号一样剪她的耳朵！”

paragraphs.en: “By God, that’s—”
paragraphs.cn: “天啊，那真是——”

paragraphs.en: “Keep your opinion to yourself!
paragraphs.cn: “把你的想法藏起来！

paragraphs.en: It will be safest for you.
paragraphs.cn: 这样你最安全。

paragraphs.en: I’ll tie her to the bed.
paragraphs.cn: 我会把她绑在床上。

paragraphs.en: If she bleeds to death, is that my fault?
paragraphs.cn: 如果她流血死了，那是我的错吗？”

paragraphs.en: I’ll not cry, if she does.
paragraphs.cn: 她哭了，我也不会哭。

paragraphs.en: My friend, you’ll help me in this thing—for _my_ sake—that’s why you’re here—I mightn’t be able alone.
paragraphs.cn: 朋友，你要帮我这件事——为了我——你在这儿就是为了帮我——我一个人可能不行。

paragraphs.en: If you flinch, I’ll kill you.
paragraphs.cn: 你要是退缩，我就杀了你。

paragraphs.en: Do you understand that?
paragraphs.cn: 你明白了吗？

paragraphs.en: And if I have to kill you, I’ll kill her—and then I reckon nobody’ll ever know much about who done this business.”
paragraphs.cn: 要是我必须杀了你，我也会杀了她——然后，我想没人会知道是谁做的这件事。

paragraphs.en: “Well, if it’s got to be done, let’s get at it.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，要是非做不可，那就动手吧。

paragraphs.en: The quicker the better—I’m all in a shiver.”
paragraphs.cn: 越快越好——我全身都在发抖。”

paragraphs.en: “Do it _now_?
paragraphs.cn: “现在就做吗？

paragraphs.en: And company there?
paragraphs.cn: 那里还有人吗？

paragraphs.en: Look here—I’ll get suspicious of you, first thing you know.
paragraphs.cn: 听着——你要是不听话，我就会开始怀疑你。

paragraphs.en: No—we’ll wait till the lights are out—there’s no hurry.”
paragraphs.cn: 不——我们等灯都灭了再说——不着急。”

paragraphs.en: Huck felt that a silence was going to ensue—a thing still more awful than any amount of murderous talk; so he held his breath and stepped gingerly back; planted his foot carefully and firmly, after balancing, one-legged, in a precarious way and almost toppling over, first on one side and then on the other.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 觉得要安静下来了——这比那些杀人的话更可怕。于是他屏住呼吸，小心地往后退。他先单腿站着，摇摇晃晃，差点摔倒，一会儿往这边倒，一会儿往那边倒，然后才小心地、稳稳地把脚放好。

paragraphs.en: He took another step back, with the same elaboration and the same risks; then another and another, and—a twig snapped under his foot!
paragraphs.cn: 他又小心地往后退了一步，同样那么费劲，同样有危险；然后又一步，又一步——突然，一根小树枝在他脚下“啪”地断了！

paragraphs.en: His breath stopped and he listened.
paragraphs.cn: 他屏住了呼吸，仔细听着。

paragraphs.en: There was no sound—the stillness was perfect.
paragraphs.cn: 什么声音也没有——一片寂静。

paragraphs.en: His gratitude was measureless.
paragraphs.cn: 他心里非常感激。

paragraphs.en: Now he turned in his tracks, between the walls of sumach bushes—turned himself as carefully as if he were a ship—and then stepped quickly but cautiously along.
paragraphs.cn: 他现在原地转身，在野漆树丛的墙壁之间——他转得很小心，就像一艘大船一样——然后他快步但又很谨慎地往前走。

paragraphs.en: When he emerged at the quarry he felt secure, and so he picked up his nimble heels and flew.
paragraphs.cn: 当他走到采石场时，他觉得安全了，于是他赶紧跑起来，飞快地走了。

paragraphs.en: Down, down he sped, till he reached the Welshman’s.
paragraphs.cn: 他跑啊跑，一直跑到威尔士人那里。

paragraphs.en: He banged at the door, and presently the heads of the old man and his two stalwart sons were thrust from windows.
paragraphs.cn: 他使劲敲门，很快，那个老人和他两个强壮的儿子的头从窗户伸了出来。

paragraphs.en: “What’s the row there?
paragraphs.cn: “那里怎么回事？

paragraphs.en: Who’s banging?
paragraphs.cn: 谁在敲门？

paragraphs.en: What do you want?”
paragraphs.cn: 你想干什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Let me in—quick!
paragraphs.cn: “快让我进去！

paragraphs.en: I’ll tell everything.”
paragraphs.cn: 我会把所有的事情都告诉你们的。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, who are you?”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，你是谁啊？”

paragraphs.en: “Huckleberry Finn—quick, let me in!”
paragraphs.cn: “我是 哈克贝利·费恩——快，让我进去！”

paragraphs.en: “Huckleberry Finn, indeed!
paragraphs.cn: “原来是 哈克贝利·费恩 啊！

paragraphs.en: It ain’t a name to open many doors, I judge!
paragraphs.cn: 这个名字可开不了多少扇门，我想！

paragraphs.en: But let him in, lads, and let’s see what’s the trouble.”
paragraphs.cn: 不过，孩子们，让他进来吧，看看出了什么事。”

paragraphs.en: “Please don’t ever tell I told you,” were Huck’s first words when he got in.
paragraphs.cn: “请你千万别说是我告诉你的，”哈克一进来就这么说。

paragraphs.en: “Please don’t—I’d be killed, sure—but the widow’s been good friends to me sometimes, and I want to tell—I _will_ tell if you’ll promise you won’t ever say it was me.”
paragraphs.cn: “求求你别说出去——我肯定会被杀死的——不过那个寡妇有时候对我很好，我想告诉你——如果你答应不说是我说的，我_就_告诉你。”

paragraphs.en: “By George, he _has_ got something to tell, or he wouldn’t act so!” exclaimed the old man; “out with it and nobody here’ll ever tell, lad.”
paragraphs.cn: “天啊，他_真_有事情要说，不然他不会是这个样子！”老人叫道，“快说吧，这里没人会说出去的，孩子。”

paragraphs.en: Three minutes later the old man and his sons, well armed, were up the hill, and just entering the sumach path on tiptoe, their weapons in their hands.
paragraphs.cn: 三分钟后，老人和他的儿子们拿着武器，上了山。他们小心翼翼地走进漆树小路。

paragraphs.en: Huck accompanied them no further.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克没再跟着他们了。

paragraphs.en: He hid behind a great bowlder and fell to listening.
paragraphs.cn: 他躲在一块大石头后面，竖起耳朵听着。

paragraphs.en: There was a lagging, anxious silence, and then all of a sudden there was an explosion of firearms and a cry.
paragraphs.cn: 先是一阵很长的安静，让人有点紧张，然后突然传来枪声和叫喊声。

paragraphs.en: Huck waited for no particulars.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克没等他们讲清发生了什么。

paragraphs.en: He sprang away and sped down the hill as fast as his legs could carry him.
paragraphs.cn: 他跳起来，用最快的速度跑下山。

paragraphs.en: As the earliest suspicion of dawn appeared on Sunday morning, Huck came groping up the hill and rapped gently at the old Welshman’s door.
paragraphs.cn: 星期天早上，天刚蒙蒙亮，哈克摸黑爬上山，轻轻敲了敲老威尔士人的门。

paragraphs.en: The inmates were asleep, but it was a sleep that was set on a hair-trigger, on account of the exciting episode of the night.
paragraphs.cn: 里面的人都睡着了，但是因为昨晚太刺激了，他们睡得很警醒，一点声音就能把他们吵醒。

paragraphs.en: A call came from a window:
paragraphs.cn: 窗户里传来一个声音：

paragraphs.en: “Who’s there!”
paragraphs.cn: “谁在外面？”

paragraphs.en: Huck’s scared voice answered in a low tone:
paragraphs.cn: 哈克有点害怕，小声回答：

paragraphs.en: “Please let me in!
paragraphs.cn: “请让我进去！

paragraphs.en: It’s only Huck Finn!”
paragraphs.cn: 我是哈克芬！”

paragraphs.en: “It’s a name that can open this door night or day, lad!
paragraphs.cn: “孩子，这个名字能让这扇门无论白天黑夜都为你打开！

paragraphs.en: —and welcome!”
paragraphs.cn: ——欢迎你！”

paragraphs.en: These were strange words to the vagabond boy’s ears, and the pleasantest he had ever heard.
paragraphs.cn: 这些话对这个流浪男孩来说很特别，也是他听过最开心的话。

paragraphs.en: He could not recollect that the closing word had ever been applied in his case before.
paragraphs.cn: 他想不起来以前有人对他说过“欢迎”这个词。

paragraphs.en: The door was quickly unlocked, and he entered.
paragraphs.cn: 门很快就开了，他走了进去。

paragraphs.en: Huck was given a seat and the old man and his brace of tall sons speedily dressed themselves.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克坐了下来，老人和他的两个高个子儿子很快穿好了衣服。

paragraphs.en: “Now, my boy, I hope you’re good and hungry, because breakfast will be ready as soon as the sun’s up, and we’ll have a piping hot one, too—make yourself easy about that!
paragraphs.cn: “好了，孩子，我希望你很饿，因为太阳一出来早餐就做好了，而且会是热腾腾的——别担心！

paragraphs.en: I and the boys hoped you’d turn up and stop here last night.”
paragraphs.cn: 我和孩子们昨晚还希望你能来这里过夜呢。”

paragraphs.en: “I was awful scared,” said Huck, “and I run.
paragraphs.cn: “我吓坏了，”哈克说，“我就跑了。

paragraphs.en: I took out when the pistols went off, and I didn’t stop for three mile.
paragraphs.cn: 手枪一响，我就跑了，跑了三英里都没停。

paragraphs.en: I’ve come now becuz I wanted to know about it, you know; and I come before daylight becuz I didn’t want to run across them devils, even if they was dead.”
paragraphs.cn: 我现在来是因为我想知道发生了什么，你知道的；我天亮前就来了，因为我不想碰上那些坏人，就算他们已经死了。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, poor chap, you do look as if you’d had a hard night of it—but there’s a bed here for you when you’ve had your breakfast.
paragraphs.cn: “哎，可怜的孩子，你看起来昨晚过得很辛苦——不过你吃完早饭，这里有床给你睡。

paragraphs.en: No, they ain’t dead, lad—we are sorry enough for that.
paragraphs.cn: 不，他们没死，孩子——我们为此感到很遗憾。

paragraphs.en: You see we knew right where to put our hands on them, by your description; so we crept along on tiptoe till we got within fifteen feet of them—dark as a cellar that sumach path was—and just then I found I was going to sneeze.
paragraphs.cn: 你看，根据你说的，我们知道在哪里能找到他们；所以我们踮着脚尖悄悄走过去，直到离他们只有十五英尺远——那条漆树小路黑得像地窖一样——就在那时，我发现自己要打喷嚏了。

paragraphs.en: It was the meanest kind of luck!
paragraphs.cn: 真是太倒霉了！

paragraphs.en: I tried to keep it back, but no use—’twas bound to come, and it did come!
paragraphs.cn: 我想忍住，可是没用，它还是出来了！

paragraphs.en: I was in the lead with my pistol raised, and when the sneeze started those scoundrels a-rustling to get out of the path, I sung out, ‘Fire boys!’ and blazed away at the place where the rustling was.
paragraphs.cn: 我举着手枪走在最前面。当我打喷嚏的时候，那些坏蛋就想偷偷溜走。我大喊一声“开火，孩子们！”然后就对着他们动静的地方开枪了。

paragraphs.en: So did the boys.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们也跟着开枪了。

paragraphs.en: But they were off in a jiffy, those villains, and we after them, down through the woods.
paragraphs.cn: 可是那些坏蛋跑得可快了，我们跟着他们，穿过树林一直追。

paragraphs.en: I judge we never touched them.
paragraphs.cn: 我想我们根本没打中他们。

paragraphs.en: They fired a shot apiece as they started, but their bullets whizzed by and didn’t do us any harm.
paragraphs.cn: 他们跑的时候也开了几枪，但是子弹从我们身边飞过，一点也没伤到我们。

paragraphs.en: As soon as we lost the sound of their feet we quit chasing, and went down and stirred up the constables.
paragraphs.cn: 听不到他们的脚步声后，我们就没再追了。我们去叫来了警察。

paragraphs.en: They got a posse together, and went off to guard the river bank, and as soon as it is light the sheriff and a gang are going to beat up the woods.
paragraphs.cn: 他们召集了一帮人，去守住河边。天一亮，警长和他的手下就会去搜查树林。

paragraphs.en: My boys will be with them presently.
paragraphs.cn: 我的孩子们很快也会跟他们一起去。

paragraphs.en: I wish we had some sort of description of those rascals—’twould help a good deal.
paragraphs.cn: 要是我们知道那些坏蛋长什么样就好了——那样会帮大忙的。

paragraphs.en: But you couldn’t see what they were like, in the dark, lad, I suppose?”
paragraphs.cn: 但是在黑夜里，孩子，你肯定也看不清他们长什么样吧？

paragraphs.en: “Oh yes; I saw them downtown and follered them.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，看清了！我在城里见过他们，还跟着他们呢。”

paragraphs.en: “Splendid!
paragraphs.cn: “太棒了！

paragraphs.en: Describe them—describe them, my boy!”
paragraphs.cn: 快说说他们长什么样——快说，孩子！”

paragraphs.en: “One’s the old deaf and dumb Spaniard that’s ben around here once or twice, and t’other’s a mean-looking, ragged—”
paragraphs.cn: “一个是那个又聋又哑的老西班牙人，他以前在这里出现过一两次，另一个看起来很凶，衣服破破烂烂的——”

paragraphs.en: “That’s enough, lad, we know the men!
paragraphs.cn: “够了，孩子，我们知道是哪些人了！

paragraphs.en: Happened on them in the woods back of the widow’s one day, and they slunk away.
paragraphs.cn: 有一天我们在寡妇家后面的树林里碰见过他们，他们就偷偷溜走了。

paragraphs.en: Off with you, boys, and tell the sheriff—get your breakfast tomorrow morning!”
paragraphs.cn: 你们快去吧，孩子们，把这事告诉警长——明天早上再吃早饭！”

paragraphs.en: The Welshman’s sons departed at once.
paragraphs.cn: 威尔士人的儿子们立刻就走了。

paragraphs.en: As they were leaving the room Huck sprang up and exclaimed:
paragraphs.cn: 他们刚走出房间，哈克就跳起来大喊：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, please don’t tell _any_body it was me that blowed on them!
paragraphs.cn: “哦，求求你们，千万不要告诉任何人是我告发了他们！

paragraphs.en: Oh, please!”
paragraphs.cn: 哦，求求你们了！”

paragraphs.en: “All right if you say it, Huck, but you ought to have the credit of what you did.”
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，如果你这么说，哈克。但你做了好事，应该得到表扬的。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh no, no!
paragraphs.cn: “哦不，不！

paragraphs.en: Please don’t tell!”
paragraphs.cn: 求求你们不要说！”

paragraphs.en: When the young men were gone, the old Welshman said:
paragraphs.cn: 等那几个年轻人走了以后，老威尔士人说：

paragraphs.en: “They won’t tell—and I won’t.
paragraphs.cn: “他们不会说的——我也不会说。

paragraphs.en: But why don’t you want it known?”
paragraphs.cn: 可是你为什么不想让人知道呢？”

paragraphs.en: Huck would not explain, further than to say that he already knew too much about one of those men and would not have the man know that he knew anything against him for the whole world—he would be killed for knowing it, sure.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克没有多说，只是说他已经对其中一个坏蛋知道得太多了。他绝不能让那个坏蛋知道他知道那些秘密，不然他肯定会被杀死的。

paragraphs.en: The old man promised secrecy once more, and said:
paragraphs.cn: 老人又答应保密，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “How did you come to follow these fellows, lad?
paragraphs.cn: “你为什么跟着这些人呢，孩子？

paragraphs.en: Were they looking suspicious?”
paragraphs.cn: 他们看起来很可疑吗？”

paragraphs.en: Huck was silent while he framed a duly cautious reply.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 安静地想着该怎么小心回答。

paragraphs.en: Then he said:
paragraphs.cn: 然后他说：

paragraphs.en: “Well, you see, I’m a kind of a hard lot,—least everybody says so, and I don’t see nothing agin it—and sometimes I can’t sleep much, on account of thinking about it and sort of trying to strike out a new way of doing.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，你看，我这个人有点皮，——反正大家都这么说，我也不觉得有什么不好——有时候，我睡不着，因为总在想事情，想找个新办法来做。

paragraphs.en: That was the way of it last night.
paragraphs.cn: 昨晚就是这样。

paragraphs.en: I couldn’t sleep, and so I come along upstreet ’bout midnight, a-turning it all over, and when I got to that old shackly brick store by the Temperance Tavern, I backed up agin the wall to have another think.
paragraphs.cn: 我睡不着，所以半夜我就走到街上，一直想着事儿。到了禁酒旅馆旁边那个摇摇晃晃的旧砖房商店时，我靠着墙又想了会儿。

paragraphs.en: Well, just then along comes these two chaps slipping along close by me, with something under their arm, and I reckoned they’d stole it.
paragraphs.cn: 就在这时，那两个人从我身边偷偷溜过，胳膊下好像藏着东西，我猜他们是偷来的。

paragraphs.en: One was a-smoking, and t’other one wanted a light; so they stopped right before me and the cigars lit up their faces and I see that the big one was the deaf and dumb Spaniard, by his white whiskers and the patch on his eye, and t’other one was a rusty, ragged-looking devil.”
paragraphs.cn: 一个人在抽烟，另一个人想借火。他们就在我面前停了下来，雪茄的火光照亮了他们的脸。我看到高个子的是那个又聋又哑的西班牙人，因为他有白胡子和一只眼睛上蒙着眼罩。另一个人看起来又脏又破。”

paragraphs.en: “Could you see the rags by the light of the cigars?”
paragraphs.cn: “你能看到雪茄的亮光照出了那些破衣服吗？”

paragraphs.en: This staggered Huck for a moment.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 听了这话愣了一下。

paragraphs.en: Then he said:
paragraphs.cn: 然后他说：

paragraphs.en: “Well, I don’t know—but somehow it seems as if I did.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我不知道——但不知怎么的，好像是看到了。”

paragraphs.en: “Then they went on, and you—”
paragraphs.cn: “然后他们走了，你呢—”

paragraphs.en: “Follered ’em—yes.
paragraphs.cn: “跟着他们—对。

paragraphs.en: That was it.
paragraphs.cn: 就是这样。

paragraphs.en: I wanted to see what was up—they sneaked along so.
paragraphs.cn: 我想看看他们想做什么——他们走得那么鬼鬼祟祟。

paragraphs.en: I dogged ’em to the widder’s stile, and stood in the dark and heard the ragged one beg for the widder, and the Spaniard swear he’d spile her looks just as I told you and your two—”
paragraphs.cn: 我一路跟着他们到了寡妇家的栅栏那里，站在黑暗中，听到那个穿破烂衣服的人求寡妇，西班牙人发誓说要毁了她的容貌，就像我告诉你的，还有你的两个—”

paragraphs.en: “What!
paragraphs.cn: “什么！

paragraphs.en: The _deaf and dumb_ man said all that!”
paragraphs.cn: 那个又聋又哑的人说了所有这些话！”

paragraphs.en: Huck had made another terrible mistake!
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 又犯了个大错！

paragraphs.en: He was trying his best to keep the old man from getting the faintest hint of who the Spaniard might be, and yet his tongue seemed determined to get him into trouble in spite of all he could do.
paragraphs.cn: 他已经尽力不让老人知道西班牙人是谁，可是他的嘴巴好像偏要给他惹麻烦。

paragraphs.en: He made several efforts to creep out of his scrape, but the old man’s eye was upon him and he made blunder after blunder.
paragraphs.cn: 他试了好几次想把事情圆回来，但老人一直盯着他，他反而错上加错。

paragraphs.en: Presently the Welshman said:
paragraphs.cn: 接着，那个威尔士人说：

paragraphs.en: “My boy, don’t be afraid of me.
paragraphs.cn: “孩子，别怕我。

paragraphs.en: I wouldn’t hurt a hair of your head for all the world.
paragraphs.cn: 我绝对不会伤害你一根头发的。

paragraphs.en: No—I’d protect you—I’d protect you.
paragraphs.cn: 不—我会保护你—我会保护你。

paragraphs.en: This Spaniard is not deaf and dumb; you’ve let that slip without intending it; you can’t cover that up now.
paragraphs.cn: 这个西班牙人不是又聋又哑；你刚才不小心说漏嘴了；现在你藏不住了。

paragraphs.en: You know something about that Spaniard that you want to keep dark.
paragraphs.cn: 你知道一些关于那个西班牙人的事，你想藏着不说。

paragraphs.en: Now trust me—tell me what it is, and trust me—I won’t betray you.”
paragraphs.cn: 现在，相信我。告诉我那是什么，我不会出卖你。”

paragraphs.en: Huck looked into the old man’s honest eyes a moment, then bent over and whispered in his ear:
paragraphs.cn: 哈克看着老爷爷诚实的眼睛，过了一会儿，他凑过去，在老爷爷耳边小声说：

paragraphs.en: “’Tain’t a Spaniard—it’s Injun Joe!”
paragraphs.cn: “它不是西班牙人——它是印第安·乔！”

paragraphs.en: The Welshman almost jumped out of his chair.
paragraphs.cn: 那个威尔士人差点从椅子上跳起来。

paragraphs.en: In a moment he said:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，他说：

paragraphs.en: “It’s all plain enough, now.
paragraphs.cn: “现在，一切都清楚了。

paragraphs.en: When you talked about notching ears and slitting noses I judged that that was your own embellishment, because white men don’t take that sort of revenge.
paragraphs.cn: 你说到割耳朵、切鼻子，我以为是你自己编的，因为白人不会那样报复。

paragraphs.en: But an Injun!
paragraphs.cn: 但如果是印第安人！

paragraphs.en: That’s a different matter altogether.”
paragraphs.cn: 那就完全不一样了。”

paragraphs.en: During breakfast the talk went on, and in the course of it the old man said that the last thing which he and his sons had done, before going to bed, was to get a lantern and examine the stile and its vicinity for marks of blood.
paragraphs.cn: 吃早饭的时候，他们还在说话。老爷爷说，他和儿子们睡觉前做的最后一件事，就是拿个灯笼，去栅栏附近看看有没有血迹。

paragraphs.en: They found none, but captured a bulky bundle of—
paragraphs.cn: 他们没找到血迹，但抓到了一个大大的包裹——

paragraphs.en: “Of _what_?”
paragraphs.cn: “是什么？”

paragraphs.en: If the words had been lightning they could not have leaped with a more stunning suddenness from Huck’s blanched lips.
paragraphs.cn: 这些话从哈克发白的嘴唇里突然蹦出来，比闪电还快，让人吃惊。

paragraphs.en: His eyes were staring wide, now, and his breath suspended—waiting for the answer.
paragraphs.cn: 他现在眼睛睁得大大的，屏住呼吸——等着答案。

paragraphs.en: The Welshman started—stared in return—three seconds—five seconds—ten—then replied:
paragraphs.cn: 威尔士人愣住了——也回看他——三秒——五秒——十秒——然后回答说：

paragraphs.en: “Of burglar’s tools.
paragraphs.cn: “是小偷的工具。

paragraphs.en: Why, what’s the _matter_ with you?”
paragraphs.cn: 哎，你怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: Huck sank back, panting gently, but deeply, unutterably grateful.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克靠了回去，轻轻地、深深地喘着气，心里说不出的感激。

paragraphs.en: The Welshman eyed him gravely, curiously—and presently said:
paragraphs.cn: 威尔士人严肃又好奇地看着他——过了一会儿说：

paragraphs.en: “Yes, burglar’s tools.
paragraphs.cn: “是的，小偷的工具。

paragraphs.en: That appears to relieve you a good deal.
paragraphs.cn: 这好像让你放松了很多。

paragraphs.en: But what did give you that turn?
paragraphs.cn: 但什么让你那么吃惊呢？

paragraphs.en: What were _you_ expecting we’d found?”
paragraphs.cn: 你以为我们找到了什么？”

paragraphs.en: Huck was in a close place—the inquiring eye was upon him—he would have given anything for material for a plausible answer—nothing suggested itself—the inquiring eye was boring deeper and deeper—a senseless reply offered—there was no time to weigh it, so at a venture he uttered it—feebly:
paragraphs.cn: 哈克当时很为难——那好奇的目光一直看着他——他很想给一个说得过去的答案，但什么都没想到——那目光越看越深——一个没用的回答冒了出来——他没时间多想，就冒险说了出来——声音很微弱：

paragraphs.en: “Sunday-school books, maybe.”
paragraphs.cn: “主日学校的书，也许吧。”

paragraphs.en: Poor Huck was too distressed to smile, but the old man laughed loud and joyously, shook up the details of his anatomy from head to foot, and ended by saying that such a laugh was money in a man’s pocket, because it cut down the doctor’s bill like everything.
paragraphs.cn: 可怜的哈克难过得笑不出来，但老爷爷却大声开心地笑了，他从头到脚都笑得抖动起来，最后他说，这样一笑就像把钱放进了口袋，因为它能省下好多医药费。

paragraphs.en: Then he added:
paragraphs.cn: 然后他又说：

paragraphs.en: “Poor old chap, you’re white and jaded—you ain’t well a bit—no wonder you’re a little flighty and off your balance.
paragraphs.cn: “可怜的老伙计，你脸色发白，很累——一点都不舒服——怪不得你有点心神不宁，站不稳。

paragraphs.en: But you’ll come out of it.
paragraphs.cn: 但你会好起来的。

paragraphs.en: Rest and sleep will fetch you out all right, I hope.”
paragraphs.cn: 好好休息和睡觉，你就会没事的，我希望。”

paragraphs.en: Huck was irritated to think he had been such a goose and betrayed such a suspicious excitement, for he had dropped the idea that the parcel brought from the tavern was the treasure, as soon as he had heard the talk at the widow’s stile.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克想到自己那么笨，还那么高兴，就有点生气。因为他一听到寡妇家门口的谈话，就不觉得酒馆拿回来的包裹是宝贝了。

paragraphs.en: He had only thought it was not the treasure, however—he had not known that it wasn’t—and so the suggestion of a captured bundle was too much for his self-possession.
paragraphs.cn: 他只是觉得那不是宝贝，但并不知道它真的不是。所以，一听说包裹被抓住了，他一下子就紧张起来了。

paragraphs.en: But on the whole he felt glad the little episode had happened, for now he knew beyond all question that that bundle was not _the_ bundle, and so his mind was at rest and exceedingly comfortable.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，他总体上还是挺高兴这件事发生了。因为现在他完全确定那个包裹不是他们要找的宝贝，心里就放松多了。

paragraphs.en: In fact, everything seemed to be drifting just in the right direction, now; the treasure must be still in No. 2, the men would be captured and jailed that day, and he and Tom could seize the gold that night without any trouble or any fear of interruption.
paragraphs.cn: 看来一切都进展得很顺利。宝贝一定还在2号屋子里。那些坏人今天就会被抓起来。他和汤姆今晚就能轻松拿到金子，不用担心被别人打扰了。

paragraphs.en: Just as breakfast was completed there was a knock at the door.
paragraphs.cn: 早餐刚吃完，门就响了。

paragraphs.en: Huck jumped for a hiding-place, for he had no mind to be connected even remotely with the late event.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克赶紧藏起来，因为他一点也不想跟昨晚的事有任何关系。

paragraphs.en: The Welshman admitted several ladies and gentlemen, among them the Widow Douglas, and noticed that groups of citizens were climbing up the hill—to stare at the stile.
paragraphs.cn: 威尔士人请了几位先生女士进来，道格拉斯寡妇也在。他还看到好多人正爬上山去看那个台阶。

paragraphs.en: So the news had spread.
paragraphs.cn: 看来消息已经传开了。

paragraphs.en: The Welshman had to tell the story of the night to the visitors.
paragraphs.cn: 威尔士人只好把昨晚发生的事告诉客人们。

paragraphs.en: The widow’s gratitude for her preservation was outspoken.
paragraphs.cn: 寡妇很感谢自己得救了，一直说着谢谢。

paragraphs.en: “Don’t say a word about it, madam.
paragraphs.cn: “夫人，别再说了。

paragraphs.en: There’s another that you’re more beholden to than you are to me and my boys, maybe, but he don’t allow me to tell his name.
paragraphs.cn: 也许你更应该感谢另一个人，而不是我和我的孩子们。但他不让我说他的名字。

paragraphs.en: We wouldn’t have been there but for him.”
paragraphs.cn: 要不是他，我们也不会在那里的。”

paragraphs.en: Of course this excited a curiosity so vast that it almost belittled the main matter—but the Welshman allowed it to eat into the vitals of his visitors, and through them be transmitted to the whole town, for he refused to part with his secret.
paragraphs.cn: 这让大家非常好奇，都快忘了其他事了。但威尔士人不肯说出秘密，让客人们一直很想知道，还把这份好奇带到了镇上。

paragraphs.en: When all else had been learned, the widow said:
paragraphs.cn: 大家知道了所有其他事情后，寡妇说：

paragraphs.en: “I went to sleep reading in bed and slept straight through all that noise.
paragraphs.cn: “我在床上看书就睡着了，那些吵闹声我一点都没听到。

paragraphs.en: Why didn’t you come and wake me?”
paragraphs.cn: 你们怎么没来叫醒我呀？”

paragraphs.en: “We judged it warn’t worth while.
paragraphs.cn: “我们觉得没必要。

paragraphs.en: Those fellows warn’t likely to come again—they hadn’t any tools left to work with, and what was the use of waking you up and scaring you to death?
paragraphs.cn: 那些坏人应该不会再来了——他们也没工具了。叫醒你，把你吓坏了又有什么用呢？

paragraphs.en: My three negro men stood guard at your house all the rest of the night.
paragraphs.cn: 我的三个朋友在你的屋子外面守了剩下的半夜。

paragraphs.en: They’ve just come back.”
paragraphs.cn: 他们刚刚才回来。”

paragraphs.en: More visitors came, and the story had to be told and retold for a couple of hours more.
paragraphs.cn: 更多的客人来了，这个故事又被讲了好几个小时，一遍又一遍。

paragraphs.en: There was no Sabbath-school during day-school vacation, but everybody was early at church.
paragraphs.cn: 学校放假，所以没有主日学。但每个人都早早地去了教堂。

paragraphs.en: The stirring event was well canvassed.
paragraphs.cn: 这件激动人心的事，大家都在议论。

paragraphs.en: News came that not a sign of the two villains had been yet discovered.
paragraphs.cn: 有消息说，那两个坏人一点踪影都还没找到。

paragraphs.en: When the sermon was finished, Judge Thatcher’s wife dropped alongside of Mrs. Harper as she moved down the aisle with the crowd and said:
paragraphs.cn: 布道结束后，撒切尔法官的妻子跟着人群走下过道，走到哈珀太太旁边，然后说：

paragraphs.en: “Is my Becky going to sleep all day?
paragraphs.cn: “我的贝琪要睡一整天吗？

paragraphs.en: I just expected she would be tired to death.”
paragraphs.cn: 我还以为她会累坏了呢。”

paragraphs.en: “Your Becky?”
paragraphs.cn: “你的贝琪？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” with a startled look—“didn’t she stay with you last night?”
paragraphs.cn: “是的，”她吃惊地看着说：“她昨晚没跟你在一起吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, no.”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，没有啊。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Thatcher turned pale, and sank into a pew, just as Aunt Polly, talking briskly with a friend, passed by.
paragraphs.cn: 撒切尔夫人脸色发白，一屁股坐到椅子上。这时，波莉姨妈正和朋友大声说笑，从旁边走了过去。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly said:
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈说：

paragraphs.en: “Goodmorning, Mrs. Thatcher.
paragraphs.cn: “早上好，撒切尔夫人。

paragraphs.en: Goodmorning, Mrs. Harper.
paragraphs.cn: 早上好，哈珀夫人。

paragraphs.en: I’ve got a boy that’s turned up missing.
paragraphs.cn: 我的一个孩子不见了。

paragraphs.en: I reckon my Tom stayed at your house last night—one of you.
paragraphs.cn: 我想我的汤姆昨晚是住在你们其中一家的吧？

paragraphs.en: And now he’s afraid to come to church.
paragraphs.cn: 现在他不敢来教堂了。

paragraphs.en: I’ve got to settle with him.”
paragraphs.cn: 我得好好和他算账。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Thatcher shook her head feebly and turned paler than ever.
paragraphs.cn: 撒切尔夫人虚弱地摇了摇头，脸色比刚才更白了。

paragraphs.en: “He didn’t stay with us,” said Mrs. Harper, beginning to look uneasy.
paragraphs.cn: “他没和我们住在一起。”哈珀夫人说，她开始看起来有些不安了。
