paragraphs.en: A marked anxiety came into Aunt Polly’s face.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈的脸上露出明显的焦虑。

paragraphs.en: “Joe Harper, have you seen my Tom this morning?”
paragraphs.cn: “乔·哈珀，你今天早上看到我的汤姆了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No’m.”
paragraphs.cn: “没有。”

paragraphs.en: “When did you see him last?”
paragraphs.cn: “你最后一次见到他是什么时候？”

paragraphs.en: Joe tried to remember, but was not sure he could say.
paragraphs.cn: 乔努力想了想，但他不确定自己能说出来。

paragraphs.en: The people had stopped moving out of church.
paragraphs.cn: 人们不再走出教堂了。

paragraphs.en: Whispers passed along, and a boding uneasiness took possession of every countenance.
paragraphs.cn: 小声的议论传开了，大家的脸上都露出了不安的神色。

paragraphs.en: Children were anxiously questioned, and young teachers.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们和年轻的老师都被着急地问着。

paragraphs.en: They all said they had not noticed whether Tom and Becky were on board the ferryboat on the homeward trip; it was dark; no one thought of inquiring if any one was missing.
paragraphs.cn: 他们都说，回家的路上天太黑了，没人注意到汤姆和贝琪是不是在渡船上；也没人想到要问问有没有人不见了。

paragraphs.en: One young man finally blurted out his fear that they were still in the cave!
paragraphs.cn: 终于，一个年轻人脱口而出，他担心他们还在山洞里！

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Thatcher swooned away.
paragraphs.cn: 撒切尔夫人晕了过去。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly fell to crying and wringing her hands.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈哭了起来，急得直搓手。

paragraphs.en: The alarm swept from lip to lip, from group to group, from street to street, and within five minutes the bells were wildly clanging and the whole town was up!
paragraphs.cn: 警报声从一个人的嘴传到另一个人的嘴，从一群人传到另一群人，从一条街传到另一条街。不到五分钟，钟声就疯狂地响了起来，整个镇子都沸腾了！

paragraphs.en: The Cardiff Hill episode sank into instant insignificance, the burglars were forgotten, horses were saddled, skiffs were manned, the ferryboat ordered out, and before the horror was half an hour old, two hundred men were pouring down highroad and river toward the cave.
paragraphs.cn: 关于卡迪夫山的事立刻变得不重要了，大家也忘了那些小偷。人们给马套上鞍子，划着小船，渡船也被派了出去。恐怖的事情发生不到半小时，两百个男人就沿着大路和河流，向山洞跑去。

paragraphs.en: All the long afternoon the village seemed empty and dead.
paragraphs.cn: 整个漫长的下午，村子看起来空荡荡的，死气沉沉。

paragraphs.en: Many women visited Aunt Polly and Mrs. Thatcher and tried to comfort them.
paragraphs.cn: 许多女人去看望了波莉姨妈和撒切尔夫人，想安慰她们。

paragraphs.en: They cried with them, too, and that was still better than words.
paragraphs.cn: 她们也和她们一起哭了，这比任何言语都更能安慰人。

paragraphs.en: All the tedious night the town waited for news; but when the morning dawned at last, all the word that came was, “Send more candles—and send food.”
paragraphs.cn: 整个漫长的夜晚，小镇都在等着消息。但当清晨终于到来时，传回来的消息却是：“多送些蜡烛——还要送吃的！”

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Thatcher was almost crazed; and Aunt Polly, also.
paragraphs.cn: 撒切尔夫人几乎要疯了；波莉姨妈也是一样。

paragraphs.en: Judge Thatcher sent messages of hope and encouragement from the cave, but they conveyed no real cheer.
paragraphs.cn: 撒切尔法官 从山洞里传来一些充满希望的话，但是听起来一点也不让人高兴。

paragraphs.en: The old Welshman came home toward daylight, spattered with candle-grease, smeared with clay, and almost worn out.
paragraphs.cn: 那个老威尔士人天快亮时才回家，他身上沾满了蜡油和泥土，累得筋疲力尽。

paragraphs.en: He found Huck still in the bed that had been provided for him, and delirious with fever.
paragraphs.cn: 他发现哈克还在为他准备的床上，发着高烧，神志不清。

paragraphs.en: The physicians were all at the cave, so the Widow Douglas came and took charge of the patient.
paragraphs.cn: 医生们都去了山洞，所以道格拉斯寡妇来照顾病人。

paragraphs.en: She said she would do her best by him, because, whether he was good, bad, or indifferent, he was the Lord’s, and nothing that was the Lord’s was a thing to be neglected.
paragraphs.cn: 她说她会好好照顾他，因为不管他好不好，都是上帝的孩子，上帝的孩子都不能被忽视。

paragraphs.en: The Welshman said Huck had good spots in him, and the widow said:
paragraphs.cn: 那个威尔士人说哈克身上有好的地方，那个寡妇说：

paragraphs.en: “You can depend on it.
paragraphs.cn: “你相信我说的没错。

paragraphs.en: That’s the Lord’s mark.
paragraphs.cn: 那是上帝的印记。

paragraphs.en: He don’t leave it off.
paragraphs.cn: 他不会把它去掉。

paragraphs.en: He never does.
paragraphs.cn: 他从来不会。

paragraphs.en: Puts it somewhere on every creature that comes from his hands.”
paragraphs.cn: 他会在每一个由他创造的生灵身上留下印记。”

paragraphs.en: Early in the forenoon parties of jaded men began to straggle into the village, but the strongest of the citizens continued searching.
paragraphs.cn: 上午很早的时候，一群疲惫的人陆续回到了村子里，但是最强壮的村民们还在继续寻找。

paragraphs.en: All the news that could be gained was that remotenesses of the cavern were being ransacked that had never been visited before; that every corner and crevice was going to be thoroughly searched; that wherever one wandered through the maze of passages, lights were to be seen flitting hither and thither in the distance, and shoutings and pistol-shots sent their hollow reverberations to the ear down the sombre aisles.
paragraphs.cn: 得到的消息是：洞穴里从未去过的地方都被仔细搜查了；每一个角落和缝隙都会被彻底搜查；不管你走到迷宫般的通道哪里，都能看到远处有灯光闪烁；喊叫声和枪声在阴暗的过道里回荡着。

paragraphs.en: In one place, far from the section usually traversed by tourists, the names “BECKY & TOM” had been found traced upon the rocky wall with candle-smoke, and near at hand a grease-soiled bit of ribbon.
paragraphs.cn: 在一个游客通常不去的地方，人们发现岩石墙上用蜡烛烟熏出了“BECKY & TOM”的名字，旁边还有一小段沾着油污的缎带。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Thatcher recognized the ribbon and cried over it.
paragraphs.cn: 撒切尔夫人认出了那段缎带，伤心地哭了。

paragraphs.en: She said it was the last relic she should ever have of her child; and that no other memorial of her could ever be so precious, because this one parted latest from the living body before the awful death came.
paragraphs.cn: 她说这是她孩子留下的最后一样东西了；也没有任何纪念品比这个更珍贵，因为这是孩子可怕的死亡来临前，最后离开孩子身体的东西。

paragraphs.en: Some said that now and then, in the cave, a far-away speck of light would glimmer, and then a glorious shout would burst forth and a score of men go trooping down the echoing aisle—and then a sickening disappointment always followed; the children were not there; it was only a searcher’s light.
paragraphs.cn: 有人说，山洞里有时会闪烁着远处的一点亮光，接着就会爆发出一阵欢呼，二十来个人会冲向回荡着声音的通道——接着总是会传来让人难过的失望消息：孩子们不在那里，那只是一束搜寻者的灯光。

paragraphs.en: Three dreadful days and nights dragged their tedious hours along, and the village sank into a hopeless stupor.
paragraphs.cn: 可怕的三天三夜过去了，时间过得又慢又长，村子里的人都陷入了绝望的麻木中。

paragraphs.en: No one had heart for anything.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都没有心思做任何事情。

paragraphs.en: The accidental discovery, just made, that the proprietor of the Temperance Tavern kept liquor on his premises, scarcely fluttered the public pulse, tremendous as the fact was.
paragraphs.cn: 大家发现禁酒旅馆的老板在店里藏酒了，这件事虽然很惊人，但大家已经没什么感觉了。

paragraphs.en: In a lucid interval, Huck feebly led up to the subject of taverns, and finally asked—dimly dreading the worst—if anything had been discovered at the Temperance Tavern since he had been ill.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克头脑清醒了一些，他虚弱地提起了旅馆的事情，最终，他有点害怕地问，自从他生病以来，禁酒旅馆有没有发现什么？

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” said the widow.
paragraphs.cn: “是的。”寡妇说。

paragraphs.en: Huck started up in bed, wild-eyed:
paragraphs.cn: 哈克猛地从床上坐起来，眼睛睁得大大的：

paragraphs.en: “What?
paragraphs.cn: “什么？

paragraphs.en: What was it?”
paragraphs.cn: 那是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Liquor!
—and the place has been shut up.
paragraphs.cn: ——那个地方已经被关了。

paragraphs.en: Lie down, child—what a turn you did give me!”
paragraphs.cn: 躺下，孩子——你可把我吓了一跳！”

paragraphs.en: “Only tell me just one thing—only just one—please!
paragraphs.cn: “就告诉我一件事——就一件——拜托了！

paragraphs.en: Was it Tom Sawyer that found it?”
paragraphs.cn: 是汤姆·索亚发现的吗？”

paragraphs.en: The widow burst into tears.
paragraphs.cn: 寡妇突然哭了起来。

paragraphs.en: “Hush, hush, child, hush!
paragraphs.cn: “嘘，嘘，孩子，别哭！

paragraphs.en: I’ve told you before, you must _not_ talk.
paragraphs.cn: 我以前说过，你_不能_说话。

paragraphs.en: You are very, very sick!”
paragraphs.cn: 你病得很重，很重！”

paragraphs.en: Then nothing but liquor had been found; there would have been a great powwow if it had been the gold.
paragraphs.cn: 那时候只找到了酒，要是找到的是金子，那可就热闹了。

paragraphs.en: So the treasure was gone forever—gone forever!
paragraphs.cn: 宝藏就这样永远不见了——永远不见了！

paragraphs.en: But what could she be crying about?
paragraphs.cn: 可是，她为什么哭呢？

paragraphs.en: Curious that she should cry.
paragraphs.cn: 她哭，真奇怪。

paragraphs.en: These thoughts worked their dim way through Huck’s mind, and under the weariness they gave him he fell asleep.
paragraphs.cn: 这些念头模模糊糊地在哈克的脑海里转，他太累了，就睡着了。

paragraphs.en: The widow said to herself:
paragraphs.cn: 寡妇自言自语地说：

paragraphs.en: “There—he’s asleep, poor wreck.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀——他睡着了，真可怜。

paragraphs.en: Tom Sawyer find it!
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆·索亚快找到它！

paragraphs.en: Pity but somebody could find Tom Sawyer!
paragraphs.cn: 要是有人能找到汤姆·索亚就好了！

paragraphs.en: Ah, there ain’t many left, now, that’s got hope enough, or strength enough, either, to go on searching.”
paragraphs.cn: 哎，现在没多少人了，大家都没什么希望，也没力气继续找了。”

paragraphs.en: Now to return to Tom and Becky’s share in the picnic.
paragraphs.cn: 现在我们回到汤姆和贝琪参加野餐的事情。

paragraphs.en: They tripped along the murky aisles with the rest of the company, visiting the familiar wonders of the cave—wonders dubbed with rather over-descriptive names, such as “The Drawing-Room,” “The Cathedral,” “Aladdin’s Palace,” and so on.
paragraphs.cn: 他们跟着大家，在昏暗的过道里走啊走，参观洞穴里那些熟悉又奇妙的地方——那些地方都有很特别的名字，比如“客厅”、“大教堂”、“阿拉丁的宫殿”等等。

paragraphs.en: Presently the hide-and-seek frolicking began, and Tom and Becky engaged in it with zeal until the exertion began to grow a trifle wearisome; then they wandered down a sinuous avenue holding their candles aloft and reading the tangled webwork of names, dates, postoffice addresses, and mottoes with which the rocky walls had been frescoed (in candle-smoke).
paragraphs.cn: 很快，他们开始玩捉迷藏，汤姆和贝琪玩得很起劲，直到有点累了。然后，他们就拿着蜡烛，顺着一条弯弯曲曲的小路走下去，仔细看石头墙上用蜡烛烟熏出来的各种名字、日期、地址和标语。

paragraphs.en: Still drifting along and talking, they scarcely noticed that they were now in a part of the cave whose walls were not frescoed.
paragraphs.cn: 他们一边走一边说话，几乎没注意到，他们已经到了洞穴里墙壁上没有画画的地方了。

paragraphs.en: They smoked their own names under an overhanging shelf and moved on.
paragraphs.cn: 他们在一个突出的石架下面，用烟熏上自己的名字，然后继续往前走。

paragraphs.en: Presently they came to a place where a little stream of water, trickling over a ledge and carrying a limestone sediment with it, had, in the slow-dragging ages, formed a laced and ruffled Niagara in gleaming and imperishable stone.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，他们来到一个地方，那里有一股小水流，它从一个石架上滴下来，带着石灰石的泥沙，经过漫长的时间，形成了一片闪闪发光、像花边一样美丽的石头瀑布。

paragraphs.en: Tom squeezed his small body behind it in order to illuminate it for Becky’s gratification.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆把小小的身子挤到后面，好让贝琪看得更清楚、更开心。

paragraphs.en: He found that it curtained a sort of steep natural stairway which was enclosed between narrow walls, and at once the ambition to be a discoverer seized him.
paragraphs.cn: 他发现，那后面藏着一个很陡的天然石阶，两边是窄窄的石墙。他立刻就想成为一个探险家了。

paragraphs.en: Becky responded to his call, and they made a smoke-mark for future guidance, and started upon their quest.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪听到他的叫声，就过来和他们一起，他们做了个烟熏的记号，方便以后认路，然后就开始了他们的探险。

paragraphs.en: They wound this way and that, far down into the secret depths of the cave, made another mark, and branched off in search of novelties to tell the upper world about.
paragraphs.cn: 他们弯弯曲曲地往前走，一直走到洞穴深处，又做了个记号，然后就分开了，去寻找新奇的东西，好带回去讲给上面的人听。

paragraphs.en: In one place they found a spacious cavern, from whose ceiling depended a multitude of shining stalactites of the length and circumference of a man’s leg; they walked all about it, wondering and admiring, and presently left it by one of the numerous passages that opened into it.
paragraphs.cn: 在一个地方，他们发现了一个宽敞的大洞，洞顶上挂着许多闪闪发光的石钟乳，像人的腿一样粗长。他们绕着洞走了一圈，非常好奇和赞叹，过了一会儿，就从其中一个通向外面的小路离开了。

paragraphs.en: This shortly brought them to a bewitching spring, whose basin was incrusted with a frostwork of glittering crystals; it was in the midst of a cavern whose walls were supported by many fantastic pillars which had been formed by the joining of great stalactites and stalagmites together, the result of the ceaseless water-drip of centuries.
paragraphs.cn: 没过多久，他们来到一个迷人的泉水边，泉水池里结满了闪亮的晶体，像冰霜一样。这个泉水在一个大洞的中间，洞的墙壁上有很多奇特的石柱，这些石柱都是由大大的石钟乳和石笋经过几百年水滴不停地滴落，慢慢连接在一起形成的。

paragraphs.en: Under the roof vast knots of bats had packed themselves together, thousands in a bunch; the lights disturbed the creatures and they came flocking down by hundreds, squeaking and darting furiously at the candles.
paragraphs.cn: 洞顶下面，密密麻麻地挤满了蝙蝠，成千上万只聚在一起。光线惊动了这些小家伙，它们成群地飞下来，叽叽喳喳地叫着，凶猛地冲向蜡烛。

paragraphs.en: Tom knew their ways and the danger of this sort of conduct.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆知道这些蝙蝠的习性，也知道它们这样做的危险。

paragraphs.en: He seized Becky’s hand and hurried her into the first corridor that offered; and none too soon, for a bat struck Becky’s light out with its wing while she was passing out of the cavern.
paragraphs.cn: 他抓住贝琪的手，赶紧把她拉进最近的那个过道里。幸好走得快，因为当她刚走出大洞的时候，一只蝙蝠就用翅膀把贝琪的蜡烛打灭了。

paragraphs.en: The bats chased the children a good distance; but the fugitives plunged into every new passage that offered, and at last got rid of the perilous things.
paragraphs.cn: 蝙蝠追了孩子们很长一段路，但是孩子们不断地钻进新的过道里，终于摆脱了这些危险的家伙。

paragraphs.en: Tom found a subterranean lake, shortly, which stretched its dim length away until its shape was lost in the shadows.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆很快就发现了一个地下湖。湖水暗暗的，一眼望不到头，消失在黑影里了。

paragraphs.en: He wanted to explore its borders, but concluded that it would be best to sit down and rest awhile, first.
paragraphs.cn: 他想去湖边看看，但觉得还是先坐下来休息一下比较好。

paragraphs.en: Now, for the first time, the deep stillness of the place laid a clammy hand upon the spirits of the children.
paragraphs.cn: 现在，这里的寂静第一次让孩子们感到有点害怕。

paragraphs.en: Becky said:
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪说：

paragraphs.en: “Why, I didn’t notice, but it seems ever so long since I heard any of the others.”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，我都没注意到，好像好久没听到其他人的声音了。”

paragraphs.en: “Come to think, Becky, we are away down below them—and I don’t know how far away north, or south, or east, or whichever it is.
paragraphs.cn: “仔细想想，贝琪，我们现在比他们低好多，而且我也不知道我们往北、往南、往东，还是往哪个方向走了多远。我们在这里听不到他们的声音的。”

paragraphs.en: We couldn’t hear them here.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们在这里听不到他们的声音。

paragraphs.en: Becky grew apprehensive.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪开始担心起来。

paragraphs.en: “I wonder how long we’ve been down here, Tom?
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，我们在这里待了多久了呀？我们最好往回走了。”

paragraphs.en: We better start back.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们最好往回走吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, I reckon we better.
paragraphs.cn: “是啊，我想我们最好还是走吧。

paragraphs.en: P’raps we better.”
paragraphs.cn: 也许，我们还是走吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Can you find the way, Tom?
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，你还找得到路吗？这里对我来说，都是弯弯曲曲、乱七八糟的。”

paragraphs.en: It’s all a mixed-up crookedness to me.”
paragraphs.cn: 对我来说，这里弯弯曲曲的，太乱了。”

paragraphs.en: “I reckon I could find it—but then the bats.
paragraphs.cn: “我想我能找到路——但那些蝙蝠怎么办？要是它们把我们的蜡烛弄灭了，那就糟透了。我们还是走别的路吧，别去那里了。”

paragraphs.en: If they put our candles out it will be an awful fix.
paragraphs.cn: 如果它们把蜡烛弄灭了，那就太糟糕了。”

paragraphs.en: Let’s try some other way, so as not to go through there.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们走别的路吧，不要从那里过。”

paragraphs.en: “Well.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧。

paragraphs.en: But I hope we won’t get lost.
paragraphs.cn: 但我希望我们不会迷路。

paragraphs.en: It would be so awful!” and the girl shuddered at the thought of the dreadful possibilities.
paragraphs.cn: 那样就太可怕了！” 女孩想到那些可能发生的坏事，吓得打了个哆嗦。

paragraphs.en: They started through a corridor, and traversed it in silence a long way, glancing at each new opening, to see if there was anything familiar about the look of it; but they were all strange.
paragraphs.cn: 他们沿着一条走廊一直往前走，走了好远好远，一路上都没说话。他们会看看每个新的岔路口，想知道有没有熟悉的地方，但所有的路口都很陌生。

paragraphs.en: Every time Tom made an examination, Becky would watch his face for an encouraging sign, and he would say cheerily:
paragraphs.cn: 每次汤姆检查时，贝琪都会盯着他的脸，想看到一些让人高兴的信号。汤姆就会开心地说：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, it’s all right.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，没事的。

paragraphs.en: This ain’t the one, but we’ll come to it right away!”
paragraphs.cn: 这不是那条路，但我们马上就能找到的！”

paragraphs.en: But he felt less and less hopeful with each failure, and presently began to turn off into diverging avenues at sheer random, in desperate hope of finding the one that was wanted.
paragraphs.cn: 但每次找不到路，他就越来越不抱希望。后来，他开始随便走进一些岔路，希望能碰巧找到那条他们想走的路。

paragraphs.en: He still said it was “all right,” but there was such a leaden dread at his heart that the words had lost their ring and sounded just as if he had said, “All is lost!”
paragraphs.cn: 他嘴上还说着“没事的”，但他心里却充满了沉重的害怕，说出来的话一点力量都没有了，听起来就像在说“一切都完了！”

paragraphs.en: Becky clung to his side in an anguish of fear, and tried hard to keep back the tears, but they would come.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪害怕极了，紧紧地靠在他身边，努力忍住眼泪，可眼泪还是忍不住流了下来。

paragraphs.en: At last she said:
paragraphs.cn: 最后，她说：

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Tom, never mind the bats, let’s go back that way!
paragraphs.cn: “哦，汤姆，别管蝙蝠了，我们还是走那条路回去吧！我们好像一直走得越来越糟。”

paragraphs.en: We seem to get worse and worse off all the time.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们好像一直走得越来越不对劲了。”

paragraphs.en: “Listen!” said he.
paragraphs.cn: “听！”他说。

paragraphs.en: Profound silence; silence so deep that even their breathings were conspicuous in the hush.
paragraphs.cn: 四周很安静，安静得连他们自己的呼吸声都听得一清二楚。

paragraphs.en: Tom shouted.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆大声喊。

paragraphs.en: The call went echoing down the empty aisles and died out in the distance in a faint sound that resembled a ripple of mocking laughter.
paragraphs.cn: 他的声音在空荡荡的通道里回荡，渐渐消失在远处，听起来像是在嘲笑他们。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, don’t do it again, Tom, it is too horrid,” said Becky.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，别再这样了，汤姆，太吓人了，”贝琪说。

paragraphs.en: “It is horrid, but I better, Becky; they might hear us, you know,” and he shouted again.
paragraphs.cn: “是有点吓人，但我最好还是喊，贝琪；他们可能会听到我们，你知道的，”他又喊了一声。

paragraphs.en: The “might” was even a chillier horror than the ghostly laughter, it so confessed a perishing hope.
paragraphs.cn: “可能”这个词，比那幽灵般的笑声更让他们害怕，这说明他们的希望快要没了。

paragraphs.en: The children stood still and listened; but there was no result.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们一动不动地站着听；但什么也没发生。

paragraphs.en: Tom turned upon the back track at once, and hurried his steps.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆立刻往回走，加快了脚步。

paragraphs.en: It was but a little while before a certain indecision in his manner revealed another fearful fact to Becky—he could not find his way back!
paragraphs.cn: 没过多久，他有些犹豫的样子让贝琪发现了一个更可怕的事实——他找不到回去的路了！

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Tom, you didn’t make any marks!”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，汤姆，你没有做任何记号！”

paragraphs.en: “Becky, I was such a fool!
paragraphs.cn: “贝琪，我真是太笨了！

paragraphs.en: Such a fool!
paragraphs.cn: 真是太笨了！

paragraphs.en: I never thought we might want to come back!
paragraphs.cn: 我从没想过我们可能要回来！

paragraphs.en: No—I can’t find the way.
paragraphs.cn: 不——我找不到路了。

paragraphs.en: It’s all mixed up.”
paragraphs.cn: 全都乱了。”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, Tom, we’re lost! we’re lost!
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，汤姆，我们迷路了！我们迷路了！

paragraphs.en: We never can get out of this awful place!
paragraphs.cn: 我们永远也出不去这个可怕的地方了！

paragraphs.en: Oh, why _did_ we ever leave the others!”
paragraphs.cn: 哦，我们当初为什么要离开其他人！”

paragraphs.en: She sank to the ground and burst into such a frenzy of crying that Tom was appalled with the idea that she might die, or lose her reason.
paragraphs.cn: 她瘫坐在地上，大哭起来，哭得汤姆很害怕，他担心她会死掉，或者疯掉。

paragraphs.en: He sat down by her and put his arms around her; she buried her face in his bosom, she clung to him, she poured out her terrors, her unavailing regrets, and the far echoes turned them all to jeering laughter.
paragraphs.cn: 他坐在她旁边，抱住她；她把脸埋在他怀里，紧紧抓住他，把她的恐惧和后悔都说了出来，远处的回声却像是在嘲笑他们。

paragraphs.en: Tom begged her to pluck up hope again, and she said she could not.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆求她重新振作起来，她却说她做不到。

paragraphs.en: He fell to blaming and abusing himself for getting her into this miserable situation; this had a better effect.
paragraphs.cn: 他开始责怪自己，说他不该把她带到这个糟糕的境地；这样一来，效果反而好了一些。

paragraphs.en: She said she would try to hope again, she would get up and follow wherever he might lead if only he would not talk like that any more.
paragraphs.cn: 她说她会再试着抱有希望，她会起来跟着他走，只要他不再说那样的话。

paragraphs.en: For he was no more to blame than she, she said.
paragraphs.cn: 她说，他并不比她更该被责怪。

paragraphs.en: So they moved on again—aimlessly—simply at random—all they could do was to move, keep moving.
paragraphs.cn: 于是他们又继续往前走——漫无目的地——只是随便走——他们能做的就是不停地走，一直走。

paragraphs.en: For a little while, hope made a show of reviving—not with any reason to back it, but only because it is its nature to revive when the spring has not been taken out of it by age and familiarity with failure.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，希望好像又回来了——不是有什么特别的理由，只是因为希望本来就会这样，只要还没有完全消失。

paragraphs.en: By-and-by Tom took Becky’s candle and blew it out.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，汤姆拿过贝琪的蜡烛，把它吹灭了。

paragraphs.en: This economy meant so much!
paragraphs.cn: 这样节省很要紧！

paragraphs.en: Words were not needed.
paragraphs.cn: 什么都不用多说。

paragraphs.en: Becky understood, and her hope died again.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪明白了，她的希望又没了。

paragraphs.en: She knew that Tom had a whole candle and three or four pieces in his pockets—yet he must economize.
paragraphs.cn: 她知道汤姆口袋里还有一整根蜡烛和三四小块，但他还是要省着用。

paragraphs.en: By-and-by, fatigue began to assert its claims; the children tried to pay attention, for it was dreadful to think of sitting down when time was grown to be so precious, moving, in some direction, in any direction, was at least progress and might bear fruit; but to sit down was to invite death and shorten its pursuit.
paragraphs.cn: 慢慢地，他们都累了。孩子们努力打起精神，因为时间很宝贵，如果坐下来，就太可怕了。只要能走一步，就有点希望。但如果坐下，就好像在等死。

paragraphs.en: At last Becky’s frail limbs refused to carry her farther.
paragraphs.cn: 最后，贝琪瘦弱的腿再也走不动了。

paragraphs.en: She sat down.
paragraphs.cn: 她坐了下来。

paragraphs.en: Tom rested with her, and they talked of home, and the friends there, and the comfortable beds and, above all, the light!
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆也和她一起休息。他们聊起了家，聊起那里的朋友，舒服的床，还有最重要的——亮光！

paragraphs.en: Becky cried, and Tom tried to think of some way of comforting her, but all his encouragements were grown thread-bare with use, and sounded like sarcasms.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪哭了。汤姆想办法安慰她，但他那些鼓励的话都说得太多了，听起来像在嘲笑她。

paragraphs.en: Fatigue bore so heavily upon Becky that she drowsed off to sleep.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪太累了，迷迷糊糊地睡着了。

paragraphs.en: Tom was grateful.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆很感激。

paragraphs.en: He sat looking into her drawn face and saw it grow smooth and natural under the influence of pleasant dreams; and by-and-by a smile dawned and rested there.
paragraphs.cn: 他坐着，看着她疲惫的脸。在美梦中，她的脸慢慢变得平静又自然，不一会儿，脸上露出了微笑。

paragraphs.en: The peaceful face reflected somewhat of peace and healing into his own spirit, and his thoughts wandered away to bygone times and dreamy memories.
paragraphs.cn: 那张平静的脸让他心里也平静下来，感觉好多了。他的思绪飘回了以前，想起了很多美好的旧事。

paragraphs.en: While he was deep in his musings, Becky woke up with a breezy little laugh—but it was stricken dead upon her lips, and a groan followed it.
paragraphs.cn: 当他还在想着事情时，贝琪醒了，轻轻地笑了笑。但笑容立刻消失了，她发出了一声呻吟。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, how _could_ I sleep!
paragraphs.cn: “哦，我怎么能睡着呢！

paragraphs.en: I wish I never, never had waked!
paragraphs.cn: 我真希望我永远不要醒过来！

paragraphs.en: No!
paragraphs.cn: 不！

paragraphs.en: No, I don’t, Tom!
paragraphs.cn: 不，我不是那个意思，汤姆！

paragraphs.en: Don’t look so!
paragraphs.cn: 别那样看我！

paragraphs.en: I won’t say it again.”
paragraphs.cn: 我不会再说了。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m glad you’ve slept, Becky; you’ll feel rested, now, and we’ll find the way out.”
paragraphs.cn: “你睡了一会儿，真好，贝琪。现在你会觉得好多了，我们会找到出去的路的。”

paragraphs.en: “We can try, Tom; but I’ve seen such a beautiful country in my dream.
paragraphs.cn: “我们可以试试，汤姆。可是我在梦里看到了一个好漂亮的地方。

paragraphs.en: I reckon we are going there.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想我们就是要去那里。”

paragraphs.en: “Maybe not, maybe not.
paragraphs.cn: “也许不会，也许不会。

paragraphs.en: Cheer up, Becky, and let’s go on trying.”
paragraphs.cn: 振作起来，贝琪，我们继续努力吧。”

paragraphs.en: They rose up and wandered along, hand in hand and hopeless.
paragraphs.cn: 他们站起来，手牵手，漫无目的地走着，心里充满了绝望。

paragraphs.en: They tried to estimate how long they had been in the cave, but all they knew was that it seemed days and weeks, and yet it was plain that this could not be, for their candles were not gone yet.
paragraphs.cn: 他们试着算算在山洞里待了多久，但感觉好像好几天甚至好几个星期了。可他们知道不可能这么久，因为蜡烛还没用完呢。

paragraphs.en: A long time after this—they could not tell how long—Tom said they must go softly and listen for dripping water—they must find a spring.
paragraphs.cn: 过了好久好久——他们也说不清楚多久——汤姆说他们得轻轻地走，听听有没有水滴声，他们得找到水源。

paragraphs.en: They found one presently, and Tom said it was time to rest again.
paragraphs.cn: 很快他们就找到了一个，汤姆说该休息了。

paragraphs.en: Both were cruelly tired, yet Becky said she thought she could go a little farther.
paragraphs.cn: 他们两个都累坏了。但贝琪说她觉得还能再走一小段路。

paragraphs.en: She was surprised to hear Tom dissent.
paragraphs.cn: 她没想到汤姆不同意。

paragraphs.en: She could not understand it.
paragraphs.cn: 她不明白为什么。

paragraphs.en: They sat down, and Tom fastened his candle to the wall in front of them with some clay.
paragraphs.cn: 他们坐下了，汤姆 用泥巴把蜡烛粘在他们面前的墙上。

paragraphs.en: Thought was soon busy; nothing was said for some time.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都在想事情，一会儿没人说话。

paragraphs.en: Then Becky broke the silence:
paragraphs.cn: 然后，贝琪 开口了：

paragraphs.en: “Tom, I am so hungry!”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，我好饿啊！”

paragraphs.en: Tom took something out of his pocket.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 从口袋里拿出一个东西。

paragraphs.en: “Do you remember this?” said he.
paragraphs.cn: “你还记得这个吗？”他说。

paragraphs.en: Becky almost smiled.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪 差点笑了。

paragraphs.en: “It’s our wedding-cake, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “这是我们的结婚蛋糕，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes—I wish it was as big as a barrel, for it’s all we’ve got.”
paragraphs.cn: “是啊——我真希望它能像桶一样大，因为我们就只有这么多了。”

paragraphs.en: “I saved it from the picnic for us to dream on, Tom, the way grownup people do with wedding-cake—but it’ll be our—”
paragraphs.cn: “我把它从野餐中留了下来，好让我们做梦用，汤姆。就像大人会用结婚蛋糕做的那样——但它会是我们的——”

paragraphs.en: She dropped the sentence where it was.
paragraphs.cn: 她没有说完这句话。

paragraphs.en: Tom divided the cake and Becky ate with good appetite, while Tom nibbled at his moiety.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 分了蛋糕，贝琪 吃得津津有味，而 汤姆 小口小口地吃着他的那份。

paragraphs.en: There was abundance of cold water to finish the feast with.
paragraphs.cn: 还有很多冷水可以喝。

paragraphs.en: By-and-by Becky suggested that they move on again.
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，贝琪 建议他们再往前走。

paragraphs.en: Tom was silent a moment.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 沉默了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: Then he said:
paragraphs.cn: 然后他说：

paragraphs.en: “Becky, can you bear it if I tell you something?”
paragraphs.cn: “贝琪，如果我告诉你一件事，你能挺住吗？”

paragraphs.en: Becky’s face paled, but she thought she could.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪 的脸变白了，但她觉得她能挺住。

paragraphs.en: “Well, then, Becky, we must stay here, where there’s water to drink.
paragraphs.cn: “那么，贝琪，我们必须留在这里，这里有水可以喝。

paragraphs.en: That little piece is our last candle!”
paragraphs.cn: 那一小截是我们的最后一根蜡烛了！”

paragraphs.en: Becky gave loose to tears and wailings.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪 大哭起来。

paragraphs.en: Tom did what he could to comfort her, but with little effect.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 尽力安慰她，但没什么用。

paragraphs.en: At length Becky said:
paragraphs.cn: 最后，贝琪 说：

paragraphs.en: “Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆！”

paragraphs.en: “Well, Becky?”
paragraphs.cn: “怎么了，贝琪？”

paragraphs.en: “They’ll miss us and hunt for us!”
paragraphs.cn: “他们会想念我们，然后来找我们的！”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, they will!
paragraphs.cn: “是的，他们会的！

paragraphs.en: Certainly they will!”
paragraphs.cn: 他们一定会来的！”

paragraphs.en: “Maybe they’re hunting for us now, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “也许他们现在就在找我们，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, I reckon maybe they are.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，我想他们可能正在找呢。

paragraphs.en: I hope they are.”
paragraphs.cn: 希望他们会。”

paragraphs.en: “When would they miss us, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，他们什么时候会想我们呢？”

paragraphs.en: “When they get back to the boat, I reckon.”
paragraphs.cn: “他们回到船上时，我想。”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, it might be dark then—would they notice we hadn’t come?”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，那时候天可能黑了——他们会发现我们没来吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道。

paragraphs.en: But anyway, your mother would miss you as soon as they got home.”
paragraphs.cn: 不过啊，他们一到家，你妈妈就会想你的。”

paragraphs.en: A frightened look in Becky’s face brought Tom to his senses and he saw that he had made a blunder.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪的脸上露出害怕的表情，让汤姆回过神来，他发现自己说错了话。

paragraphs.en: Becky was not to have gone home that night!
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪那天晚上不应该回家！

paragraphs.en: The children became silent and thoughtful.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们安静下来，开始思考。

paragraphs.en: In a moment a new burst of grief from Becky showed Tom that the thing in his mind had struck hers also—that the Sabbath morning might be half spent before Mrs. Thatcher discovered that Becky was not at Mrs. Harper’s.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，贝琪又伤心地哭起来，这让汤姆明白，他心里想的事，她也想到了——可能等到安息日早上过了一半，撒切尔太太才会发现贝琪不在哈珀太太家。

paragraphs.en: The children fastened their eyes upon their bit of candle and watched it melt slowly and pitilessly away; saw the half inch of wick stand alone at last; saw the feeble flame rise and fall, climb the thin column of smoke, linger at its top a moment, and then—the horror of utter darkness reigned!
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们盯着那点蜡烛，看着它慢慢地、无情地融化；看到只剩下半英寸的烛芯；看到微弱的火焰忽高忽低，爬上细细的烟柱，在顶端停留片刻，然后——可怕的黑暗彻底降临了！

paragraphs.en: How long afterward it was that Becky came to a slow consciousness that she was crying in Tom’s arms, neither could tell.
paragraphs.cn: 过了多久，贝琪才慢慢意识到自己在汤姆怀里哭，他们俩都说不清楚。

paragraphs.en: All that they knew was, that after what seemed a mighty stretch of time, both awoke out of a dead stupor of sleep and resumed their miseries once more.
paragraphs.cn: 他们只知道，好像过了很长很长时间，两人都从昏睡中醒来，又开始感到痛苦了。

paragraphs.en: Tom said it might be Sunday, now—maybe Monday.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆说，现在可能已经是星期天了——也许是星期一。

paragraphs.en: He tried to get Becky to talk, but her sorrows were too oppressive, all her hopes were gone.
paragraphs.cn: 他想让贝琪说话，但她太伤心了，所有的希望都没了。

paragraphs.en: Tom said that they must have been missed long ago, and no doubt the search was going on.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆说他们肯定早就被发现了，现在一定有人在找他们。

paragraphs.en: He would shout and maybe some one would come.
paragraphs.cn: 他大喊一声，也许会有人来。

paragraphs.en: He tried it; but in the darkness the distant echoes sounded so hideously that he tried it no more.
paragraphs.cn: 他试了试；但在黑暗中，远处的回声听起来太可怕了，他就不再喊了。

paragraphs.en: The hours wasted away, and hunger came to torment the captives again.
paragraphs.cn: 时间一点点过去，饥饿又来折磨这两个被困的孩子了。

paragraphs.en: A portion of Tom’s half of the cake was left; they divided and ate it.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆那半块蛋糕还剩一点；他们分着吃了。

paragraphs.en: But they seemed hungrier than before.
paragraphs.cn: 但他们感觉比以前更饿了。

paragraphs.en: The poor morsel of food only whetted desire.
paragraphs.cn: 那一小块食物反而让他们更想吃东西了。

paragraphs.en: By-and-by Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “SH!
Did you hear that?”
paragraphs.cn: 你听到了吗？”

paragraphs.en: Both held their breath and listened.
paragraphs.cn: 两人都屏住呼吸，仔细听。

paragraphs.en: There was a sound like the faintest, far-off shout.
paragraphs.cn: 有一种声音，像是很远很远的微弱喊声。

paragraphs.en: Instantly Tom answered it, and leading Becky by the hand, started groping down the corridor in its direction.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆立刻回应，然后牵着贝琪的手，摸索着朝那个方向走廊深处走去。

paragraphs.en: Presently he listened again; again the sound was heard, and apparently a little nearer.
paragraphs.cn: 接着他又听了听；声音又出现了，而且好像近了一点。

paragraphs.en: “It’s them!” said Tom; “they’re coming!
paragraphs.cn: “是他们！”汤姆说；“他们来了！”

paragraphs.en: Come along, Becky—we’re all right now!”
paragraphs.cn: 快来，贝琪——我们现在没事了！

paragraphs.en: The joy of the prisoners was almost overwhelming.
paragraphs.cn: 这些被困住的孩子们高兴坏了。

paragraphs.en: Their speed was slow, however, because pitfalls were somewhat common, and had to be guarded against.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，他们走得很慢，因为路上有很多陷阱，要小心。

paragraphs.en: They shortly came to one and had to stop.
paragraphs.cn: 没多久，他们就走到一个陷阱前，只好停下来。

paragraphs.en: It might be three feet deep, it might be a hundred—there was no passing it at any rate.
paragraphs.cn: 这个陷阱可能三英尺深，也可能一百英尺深——反正过不去。

paragraphs.en: Tom got down on his breast and reached as far down as he could.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆趴下来，尽力往下探。

paragraphs.en: No bottom.
paragraphs.cn: 摸不到底。

paragraphs.en: They must stay there and wait until the searchers came.
paragraphs.cn: 他们只能待在那儿，等找他们的人来。

paragraphs.en: They listened; evidently the distant shoutings were growing more distant! a moment or two more and they had gone altogether.
paragraphs.cn: 他们听了听；那些远处的叫声好像越来越远了！过了一会儿，就完全听不到了。

paragraphs.en: The heart-sinking misery of it!
paragraphs.cn: 真是太让人伤心了！

paragraphs.en: Tom whooped until he was hoarse, but it was of no use.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆喊得嗓子都哑了，可是一点用也没有。

paragraphs.en: He talked hopefully to Becky; but an age of anxious waiting passed and no sounds came again.
paragraphs.cn: 他对着贝琪说着有希望的话；可是等了好久，一点声音都没有再传来。

paragraphs.en: The children groped their way back to the spring.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们摸索着回到了泉水边。

paragraphs.en: The weary time dragged on; they slept again, and awoke famished and woe-stricken.
paragraphs.cn: 疲惫的时间慢慢过去；他们又睡了一觉，醒来时又饿又难过。

paragraphs.en: Tom believed it must be Tuesday by this time.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆觉得现在一定是星期二了。

paragraphs.en: Now an idea struck him.
paragraphs.cn: 这时，他想到了一个办法。

paragraphs.en: There were some side passages near at hand.
paragraphs.cn: 旁边有一些小岔路。

paragraphs.en: It would be better to explore some of these than bear the weight of the heavy time in idleness.
paragraphs.cn: 与其什么都不做，不如去这些小路看看。

paragraphs.en: He took a kite-line from his pocket, tied it to a projection, and he and Becky started, Tom in the lead, unwinding the line as he groped along.
paragraphs.cn: 他从口袋里拿出一根放风筝的线，把它系在一个突起的地方，然后他和贝琪就出发了。汤姆走在前面，一边摸索着走，一边把线放开。

paragraphs.en: At the end of twenty steps the corridor ended in a “jumping-off place.”
paragraphs.cn: 走了二十步，这条小路就到了尽头，是个“跳下去的地方”。

paragraphs.en: Tom got down on his knees and felt below, and then as far around the corner as he could reach with his hands conveniently; he made an effort to stretch yet a little farther to the right, and at that moment, not twenty yards away, a human hand, holding a candle, appeared from behind a rock!
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆跪下来往下摸，然后又方便地把手伸到角落能摸到的最远的地方；他努力再往右边伸了一点，就在那时，离他不远的地方，一块岩石后面出现了一只拿着蜡烛的手！

paragraphs.en: Tom lifted up a glorious shout, and instantly that hand was followed by the body it belonged to—Injun Joe’s!
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆高兴地大叫起来，那只手的主人马上就出现了——是印第安·乔！

paragraphs.en: Tom was paralyzed; he could not move.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆吓呆了；他一动也不能动。

paragraphs.en: He was vastly gratified the next moment, to see the “Spaniard” take to his heels and get himself out of sight.
paragraphs.cn: 下一秒，他看到那个“西班牙人”拔腿就跑，消失不见了，心里非常高兴。

paragraphs.en: Tom wondered that Joe had not recognized his voice and come over and killed him for testifying in court.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆很奇怪，乔为什么没有认出他的声音，过来对付他，因为他曾在法庭上作证过。

paragraphs.en: But the echoes must have disguised the voice.
paragraphs.cn: 但回声一定让声音变样了。

paragraphs.en: Without doubt, that was it, he reasoned.
paragraphs.cn: 他想，肯定是这样。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s fright weakened every muscle in his body.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆吓得全身都没力气了。

paragraphs.en: He said to himself that if he had strength enough to get back to the spring he would stay there, and nothing should tempt him to run the risk of meeting Injun Joe again.
paragraphs.cn: 他对自己说，如果他有足够的力气回到泉水边，他就会待在那里，什么都不能再让他去冒遇到印第安·乔的危险了。

paragraphs.en: He was careful to keep from Becky what it was he had seen.
paragraphs.cn: 他小心地不让贝琪知道他看到了什么。

paragraphs.en: He told her he had only shouted “for luck.”
paragraphs.cn: 他告诉她，他只是为了“有好运”才大叫的。

paragraphs.en: But hunger and wretchedness rise superior to fears in the long run.
paragraphs.cn: 但饿肚子和难受久了，就什么也不怕了。

paragraphs.en: Another tedious wait at the spring and another long sleep brought changes.
paragraphs.cn: 又在泉水边等了好久，又睡了一大觉，事情变了。

paragraphs.en: The children awoke tortured with a raging hunger.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们醒来时，饿得肚子好痛好痛。

paragraphs.en: Tom believed that it must be Wednesday or Thursday or even Friday or Saturday, now, and that the search had been given over.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆想，现在一定是星期三、星期四，甚至星期五或星期六了，大家肯定已经不找他们了。

paragraphs.en: He proposed to explore another passage.
paragraphs.cn: 他说要去探探别的路。

paragraphs.en: He felt willing to risk Injun Joe and all other terrors.
paragraphs.cn: 他觉得就算有印第安·乔和其他吓人的事，他也要去。

paragraphs.en: But Becky was very weak.
paragraphs.cn: 但是贝琪已经很没力气了。

paragraphs.en: She had sunk into a dreary apathy and would not be roused.
paragraphs.cn: 她变得很没精神，怎么也叫不醒。

paragraphs.en: She said she would wait, now, where she was, and die—it would not be long.
paragraphs.cn: 她说她就呆在这儿等死吧，很快就好了。

paragraphs.en: She told Tom to go with the kite-line and explore if he chose; but she implored him to come back every little while and speak to her; and she made him promise that when the awful time came, he would stay by her and hold her hand until all was over.
paragraphs.cn: 她让汤姆拿着风筝线去探险，如果他想去的话。但她求他，每隔一会儿就回来跟她说话。她还让他保证，等最可怕的时候到了，他会一直陪着她，牵着她的手，直到一切都过去。

paragraphs.en: Tom kissed her, with a choking sensation in his throat, and made a show of being confident of finding the searchers or an escape from the cave; then he took the kite-line in his hand and went groping down one of the passages on his hands and knees, distressed with hunger and sick with bodings of coming doom.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆亲了她一下，喉咙里很难受，但他还是装作很有信心地说能找到大人或者能逃出山洞。然后他拿着风筝线，手脚并用，摸着黑走进了一条路。他又饿又难受，心里还很担心会发生可怕的事情。

paragraphs.en: Tuesday afternoon came, and waned to the twilight.
paragraphs.cn: 星期二下午到了，天色慢慢变暗，成了傍晚。

paragraphs.en: The village of St. Petersburg still mourned.
paragraphs.cn: 圣彼得斯堡小村庄还在难过。

paragraphs.en: The lost children had not been found.
paragraphs.cn: 那些不见了的孩子，还没找到。

paragraphs.en: Public prayers had been offered up for them, and many and many a private prayer that had the petitioner’s whole heart in it; but still no good news came from the cave.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都在为孩子们祈祷，很多人也自己偷偷地真心祈祷；但山洞里还是没有传来好消息。

paragraphs.en: The majority of the searchers had given up the quest and gone back to their daily avocations, saying that it was plain the children could never be found.
paragraphs.cn: 大部分找孩子的大人，都放弃了，回家忙自己的事去了。他们说，孩子们肯定找不到了。

paragraphs.en: Mrs. Thatcher was very ill, and a great part of the time delirious.
paragraphs.cn: 撒切尔阿姨病得很重，大部分时间都迷迷糊糊的。

paragraphs.en: People said it was heartbreaking to hear her call her child, and raise her head and listen a whole minute at a time, then lay it wearily down again with a moan.
paragraphs.cn: 大家说，听到她叫自己的孩子，然后抬起头听一整分钟，接着又累得放下头，还轻轻地叹气，真是太让人难过了。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly had drooped into a settled melancholy, and her gray hair had grown almost white.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈变得很忧伤，她的灰头发都快变成白头发了。

paragraphs.en: The village went to its rest on Tuesday night, sad and forlorn.
paragraphs.cn: 星期二晚上，村子里的人都睡了，心里很难过。

paragraphs.en: Away in the middle of the night a wild peal burst from the village bells, and in a moment the streets were swarming with frantic half-clad people, who shouted, “Turn out! turn out! they’re found! they’re found!”
paragraphs.cn: 半夜里，村子的钟声突然响起来，街上一下子挤满了好多还没穿好衣服的大人，他们又跑又叫：“快出来！快出来！孩子们找到了！找到了！”

paragraphs.en: Tin pans and horns were added to the din, the population massed itself and moved toward the river, met the children coming in an open carriage drawn by shouting citizens, thronged around it, joined its homeward march, and swept magnificently up the main street roaring huzzah after huzzah!
paragraphs.cn: 大家又敲盆子又吹号角，所有人都挤在一起，朝着河边走。他们看到孩子们坐着马车回来了，马车是好多大人拉着的，他们一边拉一边喊。大家把马车围起来，跟着它一起回家，然后浩浩荡荡地走过大马路，不停地大声欢呼！

paragraphs.en: The village was illuminated; nobody went to bed again; it was the greatest night the little town had ever seen.
paragraphs.cn: 村子里灯都亮着，没有人再去睡觉了。这是这个小镇从来没有过的最开心的夜晚。

paragraphs.en: During the first half-hour a procession of villagers filed through Judge Thatcher’s house, seized the saved ones and kissed them, squeezed Mrs. Thatcher’s hand, tried to speak but couldn’t—and drifted out raining tears all over the place.
paragraphs.cn: 最开始的半个小时里，好多村民排着队走进撒切尔法官的家，抱住那些被救回来的孩子亲亲，紧紧握住撒切尔阿姨的手，想说话却说不出来——然后流着眼泪走开了。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly’s happiness was complete, and Mrs. Thatcher’s nearly so.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈很高兴，撒切尔阿姨也差不多。

paragraphs.en: It would be complete, however, as soon as the messenger dispatched with the great news to the cave should get the word to her husband.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，等把好消息告诉她丈夫的人跑到山洞，她的幸福就更完整了。

paragraphs.en: Tom lay upon a sofa with an eager auditory about him and told the history of the wonderful adventure, putting in many striking additions to adorn it withal; and closed with a description of how he left Becky and went on an exploring expedition; how he followed two avenues as far as his kite-line would reach; how he followed a third to the fullest stretch of the kite-line, and was about to turn back when he glimpsed a far-off speck that looked like daylight; dropped the line and groped toward it, pushed his head and shoulders through a small hole, and saw the broad Mississippi rolling by!
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆躺在沙发上，好多人围着他，都想听故事。他讲起了这次奇妙的冒险，还加了很多有意思的细节，让故事更好听。最后，他说他是怎么离开贝琪去探险的：他沿着两条路走，走到风筝线够不到的地方；又沿着第三条路一直走到风筝线最长的地方。他正要回头，突然看到远处有一个小亮点，好像是外面天亮了！他放下线，摸着黑朝亮点走过去，把头和肩膀挤过一个小洞，结果看到了宽阔的密西西比大河！

paragraphs.en: And if it had only happened to be night he would not have seen that speck of daylight and would not have explored that passage any more!
paragraphs.cn: 而且如果当时正好是晚上，他就看不到那个亮光，也就不会再往前探索那条路了！

paragraphs.en: He told how he went back for Becky and broke the good news and she told him not to fret her with such stuff, for she was tired, and knew she was going to die, and wanted to.
paragraphs.cn: 他说他是怎么回去找贝琪的，还把好消息告诉她。可是贝琪却说不要用这些事来烦她，因为她太累了，知道自己快要死了，也想死掉。

paragraphs.en: He described how he labored with her and convinced her; and how she almost died for joy when she had groped to where she actually saw the blue speck of daylight; how he pushed his way out at the hole and then helped her out; how they sat there and cried for gladness; how some men came along in a skiff and Tom hailed them and told them their situation and their famished condition; how the men didn’t believe the wild tale at first, “because,” said they, “you are five miles down the river below the valley the cave is in”—then took them aboard, rowed to a house, gave them supper, made them rest till two or three hours after dark and then brought them home.
paragraphs.cn: 他说了他是怎么和她一起努力，最后说服了她。当她摸到真正能看到一点点蓝色亮光的地方时，她高兴得差点晕过去。他是怎么从洞口挤出去，又把她拉出来的。他们坐在那里，高兴地哭了。一些人划着小船来了，汤姆叫住了他们，问了他们的情况，知道他们很饿。那些人一开始不相信这个离奇的故事，因为他们说：“你们在离山谷五英里远的地方，那里根本没有山洞。”然后，他们把他们带上了船，划到一个房子，给他们吃了晚饭，让他们一直休息到天黑两三个小时以后，才把他们送回家。

paragraphs.en: Before day-dawn, Judge Thatcher and the handful of searchers with him were tracked out, in the cave, by the twine clews they had strung behind them, and informed of the great news.
paragraphs.cn: 天亮之前，撒切尔法官和他带着的几个找他们的人，顺着他们之前系在身后的绳子，在山洞里找到了出去的路。他们也知道了这个好消息。

paragraphs.en: Three days and nights of toil and hunger in the cave were not to be shaken off at once, as Tom and Becky soon discovered.
paragraphs.cn: 在山洞里累了三天三夜，又饿了三天三夜，这种辛苦不是一下子就能恢复的，汤姆和贝琪很快就发现了这一点。

paragraphs.en: They were bedridden all of Wednesday and Thursday, and seemed to grow more and more tired and worn, all the time.
paragraphs.cn: 他们星期三和星期四都躺在床上，感觉越来越累，越来越没精神。

paragraphs.en: Tom got about, a little, on Thursday, was downtown Friday, and nearly as whole as ever Saturday; but Becky did not leave her room until Sunday, and then she looked as if she had passed through a wasting illness.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆星期四能稍微动一动了，星期五去了市中心，星期六就差不多完全好了；但是贝琪一直到星期天都没出门，她看起来就像大病了一场。

paragraphs.en: Tom learned of Huck’s sickness and went to see him on Friday, but could not be admitted to the bedroom; neither could he on Saturday or Sunday.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆知道了哈克生病了，星期五去看了他，但没能进卧室；星期六和星期天也没能进去。

paragraphs.en: He was admitted daily after that, but was warned to keep still about his adventure and introduce no exciting topic.
paragraphs.cn: 从那以后，他每天都能进去看他了，但是他被提醒，不能说他冒险的事情，也不能说任何让人兴奋的话题。

paragraphs.en: The Widow Douglas stayed by to see that he obeyed.
paragraphs.cn: 道格拉斯寡妇一直在旁边看着，确保他听话。

paragraphs.en: At home Tom learned of the Cardiff Hill event; also that the “ragged man’s” body had eventually been found in the river near the ferry-landing; he had been drowned while trying to escape, perhaps.
paragraphs.cn: 在家的时候，汤姆知道了卡迪夫山的事情；也知道了那个“衣衫褴褛的男人”的尸体，最后在渡口附近被人在河里找到了；他可能是在逃跑的时候淹死的。

paragraphs.en: About a fortnight after Tom’s rescue from the cave, he started off to visit Huck, who had grown plenty strong enough, now, to hear exciting talk, and Tom had some that would interest him, he thought.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆从山洞里被救出来大约两周后，他去看哈克。哈克现在已经很强壮了，可以听一些刺激的事情了，汤姆觉得他有一些有趣的事情可以告诉他。

paragraphs.en: Judge Thatcher’s house was on Tom’s way, and he stopped to see Becky.
paragraphs.cn: 撒切尔法官的家在汤姆回家的路上，他就停下来去看了贝琪。

paragraphs.en: The Judge and some friends set Tom to talking, and some one asked him ironically if he wouldn’t like to go to the cave again.
paragraphs.cn: 法官和一些朋友让汤姆说话，有人开玩笑地问他，是不是还想再去山洞。

paragraphs.en: Tom said he thought he wouldn’t mind it.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆说他觉得他不会介意的。

paragraphs.en: The Judge said:
paragraphs.cn: 法官说：

paragraphs.en: “Well, there are others just like you, Tom, I’ve not the least doubt.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，还有别人也和你一样，汤姆，我一点都不怀疑。

paragraphs.en: But we have taken care of that.
paragraphs.cn: 不过我们已经处理好了这件事。

paragraphs.en: Nobody will get lost in that cave any more.”
paragraphs.cn: 以后再也没有人会在那个山洞里迷路了。”

paragraphs.en: “Why?”
paragraphs.cn: “为什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Because I had its big door sheathed with boiler iron two weeks ago, and triple-locked—and I’ve got the keys.”
paragraphs.cn: “因为两周前，我让人把山洞的大门用厚厚的铁板包了起来，还上了三把锁——钥匙在我这里。”

paragraphs.en: Tom turned as white as a sheet.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆的脸一下子变得像纸一样白。

paragraphs.en: “What’s the matter, boy!
paragraphs.cn: “怎么了，孩子！

paragraphs.en: Here, run, somebody!
paragraphs.cn: 快，谁去！

paragraphs.en: Fetch a glass of water!”
paragraphs.cn: 拿杯水来！”

paragraphs.en: The water was brought and thrown into Tom’s face.
paragraphs.cn: 水被拿来了，泼到了汤姆的脸上。

paragraphs.en: “Ah, now you’re all right.
paragraphs.cn: “啊，你现在没事了。

paragraphs.en: What was the matter with you, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，你刚才怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Judge, Injun Joe’s in the cave!”
paragraphs.cn: “哦，法官，印第安·乔在山洞里！”

paragraphs.en: Within a few minutes the news had spread, and a dozen skiff-loads of men were on their way to McDougal’s cave, and the ferryboat, well filled with passengers, soon followed.
paragraphs.cn: 几分钟之内，这个消息就传开了，几十艘小船上载着男人，正赶往麦克杜格尔山洞，一艘满载乘客的渡船也很快跟了上去。

paragraphs.en: Tom Sawyer was in the skiff that bore Judge Thatcher.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆·索亚就在载着撒切尔法官的那艘小船上。

paragraphs.en: When the cave door was unlocked, a sorrowful sight presented itself in the dim twilight of the place.
paragraphs.cn: 山洞的门打开后，在昏暗的光线中，里面出现了一个让人伤心的景象。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe lay stretched upon the ground, dead, with his face close to the crack of the door, as if his longing eyes had been fixed, to the latest moment, upon the light and the cheer of the free world outside.
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔 躺在地上，他死了。他的脸贴着门缝，眼睛好像一直看着门外，想看看外面多亮、多开心。

paragraphs.en: Tom was touched, for he knew by his own experience how this wretch had suffered.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 觉得很难过。因为他知道这个可怜人受了多少苦，他自己也尝过那种滋味。

paragraphs.en: His pity was moved, but nevertheless he felt an abounding sense of relief and security, now, which revealed to him in a degree which he had not fully appreciated before how vast a weight of dread had been lying upon him since the day he lifted his voice against this bloody-minded outcast.
paragraphs.cn: 他很同情这个人。但同时，他又觉得轻松和安全了很多。他这才明白，自从他大声反对那个坏人以来，心里一直很害怕。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe’s bowie-knife lay close by, its blade broken in two.
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔 的大刀就在旁边，刀片断成了两半。

paragraphs.en: The great foundation-beam of the door had been chipped and hacked through, with tedious labor; useless labor, too, it was, for the native rock formed a sill outside it, and upon that stubborn material the knife had wrought no effect; the only damage done was to the knife itself.
paragraphs.cn: 门下面的大木头被一点点凿开、砍开。他费了好大劲，可是没用。因为门外面有块大石头，刀子根本弄不动。结果，刀子反而弄坏了。

paragraphs.en: But if there had been no stony obstruction there the labor would have been useless still, for if the beam had been wholly cut away Injun Joe could not have squeezed his body under the door, and he knew it.
paragraphs.cn: 就算没有那块石头，他这样做也没用。因为就算木头完全被砍掉了，印第安·乔 也挤不过门下面，他自己知道的。

paragraphs.en: So he had only hacked that place in order to be doing something—in order to pass the weary time—in order to employ his tortured faculties.
paragraphs.cn: 所以他只是砍那里，就为了找点事做——为了打发无聊的时间——为了让痛苦的心情好受一点。

paragraphs.en: Ordinarily one could find half a dozen bits of candle stuck around in the crevices of this vestibule, left there by tourists; but there were none now.
paragraphs.cn: 平时，这里（这个门口）的缝隙里能找到好几截蜡烛头，是游客们留下的。但现在，一截都没有了。

paragraphs.en: The prisoner had searched them out and eaten them.
paragraphs.cn: 那个被关起来的人把它们都找出来吃掉了。

paragraphs.en: He had also contrived to catch a few bats, and these, also, he had eaten, leaving only their claws.
paragraphs.cn: 他还想办法抓了几只蝙蝠，也把它们吃掉了，只剩下了爪子。

paragraphs.en: The poor unfortunate had starved to death.
paragraphs.cn: 这个可怜的人饿死了。

paragraphs.en: In one place, near at hand, a stalagmite had been slowly growing up from the ground for ages, builded by the water-drip from a stalactite overhead.
paragraphs.cn: 附近有个地方，一根石笋已经从地上慢慢长了几千年。它是上面滴下来的水一点点长成的。

paragraphs.en: The captive had broken off the stalagmite, and upon the stump had placed a stone, wherein he had scooped a shallow hollow to catch the precious drop that fell once in every three minutes with the dreary regularity of a clock-tick—a dessertspoonful once in four and twenty hours.
paragraphs.cn: 那个被关起来的人把石笋弄断了。他在剩下的地方放了一块石头，还在石头上挖了个小坑，用来接水。每三分钟才滴一滴水，就像钟表一样准时。二十四个小时，才能接到一小勺水。

paragraphs.en: That drop was falling when the Pyramids were new; when Troy fell; when the foundations of Rome were laid; when Christ was crucified; when the Conqueror created the British empire; when Columbus sailed; when the massacre at Lexington was “news.”
paragraphs.cn: 金字塔刚建好时，这滴水就在滴了；特洛伊城塌了时，它还在滴；罗马城刚开始建时，它还在滴；耶稣被钉住时，它还在滴；那个征服者建立了英国时，它还在滴；哥伦布航海时，它还在滴；莱克星顿发生大事时，它还在滴。

paragraphs.en: It is falling now; it will still be falling when all these things shall have sunk down the afternoon of history, and the twilight of tradition, and been swallowed up in the thick night of oblivion.
paragraphs.cn: 现在它还在滴。等到所有这些事情都过去了，人们都忘了的时候，它还会一直滴。

paragraphs.en: Has everything a purpose and a mission?
paragraphs.cn: 是不是每一样东西都有它要做的事呢？

paragraphs.en: Did this drop fall patiently during five thousand years to be ready for this flitting human insect’s need? and has it another important object to accomplish ten thousand years to come?
paragraphs.cn: 这滴水滴了五千年，就是为了等这个人来接吗？它以后一万年，还有别的重要事要做吗？

paragraphs.en: No matter.
paragraphs.cn: 算了，别管它了。

paragraphs.en: It is many and many a year since the hapless half-breed scooped out the stone to catch the priceless drops, but to this day the tourist stares longest at that pathetic stone and that slow-dropping water when he comes to see the wonders of McDougal’s cave.
paragraphs.cn: 那个可怜的混血儿挖空石头来接这些水滴，已经过去好多年了。但是到现在，游客们来看麦克杜格尔洞穴时，还是会盯着那块石头和那些水滴看最久。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe’s cup stands first in the list of the cavern’s marvels; even “Aladdin’s Palace” cannot rival it.
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔 的杯子是洞里最棒的奇观，连“阿拉丁宫殿”都比不上它。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe was buried near the mouth of the cave; and people flocked there in boats and wagons from the towns and from all the farms and hamlets for seven miles around; they brought their children, and all sorts of provisions, and confessed that they had had almost as satisfactory a time at the funeral as they could have had at the hanging.
paragraphs.cn: 印第安·乔 被埋在洞口旁边。城里和附近村子里的人们都坐着船和马车来看。他们带着孩子，还带了好多吃的。他们说，来看这个葬礼，就和去看别的好玩的事情一样开心。

paragraphs.en: This funeral stopped the further growth of one thing—the petition to the governor for Injun Joe’s pardon.
paragraphs.cn: 这场葬礼让一件事停了下来——人们不再给州长写信，求他放过印第安·乔 了。

paragraphs.en: The petition had been largely signed; many tearful and eloquent meetings had been held, and a committee of sappy women been appointed to go in deep mourning and wail around the governor, and implore him to be a merciful ass and trample his duty under foot.
paragraphs.cn: 很多人在请愿书上签了名。大家还开了好几次会，很多人都哭了，说了好多话。还有一些爱哭的阿姨们被选出来，让她们穿着丧服去州长那里哭着求他，让他心软，不要按规矩办事。

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe was believed to have killed five citizens of the village, but what of that?
paragraphs.cn: 大家觉得印第安·乔 杀了村里五个人，可是这又有什么关系呢？

paragraphs.en: If he had been Satan himself there would have been plenty of weaklings ready to scribble their names to a pardon-petition, and drip a tear on it from their permanently impaired and leaky water-works.
paragraphs.cn: 就算他真是大魔鬼，也会有好多人愿意在求情信上写上自己的名字，还假装哭几滴眼泪在上面。

paragraphs.en: The morning after the funeral Tom took Huck to a private place to have an important talk.
paragraphs.cn: 葬礼结束的第二天早上，汤姆 把哈克 带到一个没人的地方，想好好说说话。

paragraphs.en: Huck had learned all about Tom’s adventure from the Welshman and the Widow Douglas, by this time, but Tom said he reckoned there was one thing they had not told him; that thing was what he wanted to talk about now.
paragraphs.cn: 这时候，哈克 已经从那个威尔士人和道格拉斯寡妇 那里，知道了汤姆 的所有冒险故事。但是汤姆 说，他觉得还有一件事他们没告诉他。他现在就想说说这件事。

paragraphs.en: Huck’s face saddened.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克 的脸变得有点伤心。

paragraphs.en: He said:
paragraphs.cn: 他说：

paragraphs.en: “I know what it is.
paragraphs.cn: “我知道是什么事。”

paragraphs.en: You got into No. 2 and never found anything but whiskey.
paragraphs.cn: 你去了2号，但只找到了酒。

paragraphs.en: Nobody told me it was you; but I just knowed it must ’a’ ben you, soon as I heard ’bout that whiskey business; and I knowed you hadn’t got the money becuz you’d ’a’ got at me some way or other and told me even if you was mum to everybody else.
paragraphs.cn: 没人告诉我那是你，但我一听说是酒的事，就知道肯定是你了。我也知道你没拿到钱，要是你拿到了，你肯定会告诉我，哪怕对别人保密。

paragraphs.en: Tom, something’s always told me we’d never get holt of that swag.”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，我总觉得我们永远也找不到那笔钱。

paragraphs.en: “Why, Huck, I never told on that tavern-keeper.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，哈克，我可没告发那个开酒馆的。

paragraphs.en: _You_ know his tavern was all right the Saturday I went to the picnic.
paragraphs.cn: 你知道的，我那天去野餐，他那个酒馆好好的。

paragraphs.en: Don’t you remember you was to watch there that night?”
paragraphs.cn: 你不记得那天晚上你要在那儿守着吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh yes!
paragraphs.cn: “哦，是啊！

paragraphs.en: Why, it seems ’bout a year ago.
paragraphs.cn: 哎，好像是一年前的事了。

paragraphs.en: It was that very night that I follered Injun Joe to the widder’s.”
paragraphs.cn: 就是那天晚上，我跟着印第安·乔去了寡妇家。”

paragraphs.en: “_You_ followed him?”
paragraphs.cn: “你跟着他？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes—but you keep mum.
paragraphs.cn: “是的——但你要保密。

paragraphs.en: I reckon Injun Joe’s left friends behind him, and I don’t want ’em souring on me and doing me mean tricks.
paragraphs.cn: 我猜印第安·乔还有朋友，我可不想他们生我的气，欺负我。

paragraphs.en: If it hadn’t ben for me he’d be down in Texas now, all right.”
paragraphs.cn: 要不是我，他现在肯定还在德克萨斯州呢。”

paragraphs.en: Then Huck told his entire adventure in confidence to Tom, who had only heard of the Welshman’s part of it before.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，哈克偷偷地把他的全部经历告诉了汤姆，之前汤姆只知道那个威尔士人的那部分。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” said Huck, presently, coming back to the main question, “whoever nipped the whiskey in No. 2, nipped the money, too, I reckon—anyways it’s a goner for us, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，”哈克接着说，回到了主要的问题上，“我猜，谁拿走了2号房间的酒，谁就也拿走了钱——反正对我们来说，钱是没了，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: “Huck, that money wasn’t ever in No. 2!”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，那笔钱根本就没在2号房间！”

paragraphs.en: “What!”
paragraphs.cn: “什么！”

paragraphs.en: Huck searched his comrade’s face keenly.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克仔细地看着他朋友的脸。

paragraphs.en: “Tom, have you got on the track of that money again?”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，你是不是又找到那笔钱的线索了？”

paragraphs.en: “Huck, it’s in the cave!”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，钱在山洞里！”

paragraphs.en: Huck’s eyes blazed.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克的眼睛亮了起来。

paragraphs.en: “Say it again, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “再告诉我一遍，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: “The money’s in the cave!”
paragraphs.cn: “钱在山洞里！”

paragraphs.en: “Tom—honest injun, now—is it fun, or earnest?”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆——说真的，你是开玩笑，还是认真的？”

paragraphs.en: “Earnest, Huck—just as earnest as ever I was in my life.
paragraphs.cn: “认真的，哈克——我这辈子从没这么认真过。

paragraphs.en: Will you go in there with me and help get it out?”
paragraphs.cn: 你愿意跟我一起进去把钱拿出来吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I bet I will!
paragraphs.cn: “我当然愿意！

paragraphs.en: I will if it’s where we can blaze our way to it and not get lost.”
paragraphs.cn: 只要我们能做好记号，不迷路，我就去。”

paragraphs.en: “Huck, we can do that without the least little bit of trouble in the world.”
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，我们能做到，一点儿麻烦都没有。”

paragraphs.en: “Good as wheat!
paragraphs.cn: “太好了！”

paragraphs.en: What makes you think the money’s—”
paragraphs.cn: 你为什么觉得钱会——

paragraphs.en: “Huck, you just wait till we get in there.
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，你等我们进去就知道了。

paragraphs.en: If we don’t find it I’ll agree to give you my drum and every thing I’ve got in the world.
paragraphs.cn: 要是我们找不到，我把我的鼓和所有东西都给你。

paragraphs.en: I will, by jings.”
paragraphs.cn: 我真的会给你，真的！

paragraphs.en: “All right—it’s a whiz.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，这太棒了。

paragraphs.en: When do you say?”
paragraphs.cn: 你说什么时候去？

paragraphs.en: “Right now, if you say it.
paragraphs.cn: “就现在，如果你说去的话。

paragraphs.en: Are you strong enough?”
paragraphs.cn: 你够强壮吗？

paragraphs.en: “Is it far in the cave?
paragraphs.cn: “洞里面远吗？

paragraphs.en: I ben on my pins a little, three or four days, now, but I can’t walk more’n a mile, Tom—least I don’t think I could.”
paragraphs.cn: 我走了三四天了，有点累，现在走不了超过一英里，汤姆——至少我觉得不行。

paragraphs.en: “It’s about five mile into there the way anybody but me would go, Huck, but there’s a mighty short cut that they don’t anybody but me know about.
paragraphs.cn: “别人进去大概要走五英里，哈克，但我知道一条很近的近路，只有我知道。

paragraphs.en: Huck, I’ll take you right to it in a skiff.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克，我会用小船直接带你去。

paragraphs.en: I’ll float the skiff down there, and I’ll pull it back again all by myself.
paragraphs.cn: 我会把小船划过去，然后我自己再把它拉回来。

paragraphs.en: You needn’t ever turn your hand over.”
paragraphs.cn: 你什么都不用做。

paragraphs.en: “Less start right off, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “我们现在就出发吧，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: “All right.
paragraphs.cn: “好的。

paragraphs.en: We want some bread and meat, and our pipes, and a little bag or two, and two or three kite-strings, and some of these new-fangled things they call lucifer matches.
paragraphs.cn: 我们要带些面包和肉，还有我们的烟斗，一两个小包，两三根风筝线，和一些他们叫火柴的新奇东西。

paragraphs.en: I tell you, many’s the time I wished I had some when I was in there before.”
paragraphs.cn: 我告诉你，我以前在里面的时候，好多次都希望有这些东西。

paragraphs.en: A trifle after noon the boys borrowed a small skiff from a citizen who was absent, and got under way at once.
paragraphs.cn: 刚过中午，孩子们从一个不在家的人那里借了一艘小船，马上就出发了。

paragraphs.en: When they were several miles below “Cave Hollow,” Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 当他们离“山洞谷”几英里远的时候，汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “Now you see this bluff here looks all alike all the way down from the cave hollow—no houses, no wood-yards, bushes all alike.
paragraphs.cn: “你看，从山洞谷下来，这边的峭壁都长得一样——没有房子，没有堆木头的地方，灌木丛也一样。

paragraphs.en: But do you see that white place up yonder where there’s been a landslide?
paragraphs.cn: 但你看到那边有个白色的地方吗？那里发生过山体滑坡。

paragraphs.en: Well, that’s one of my marks.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，那就是我的一个标记。

paragraphs.en: We’ll get ashore, now.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们现在靠岸吧。

paragraphs.en: They landed.
paragraphs.cn: 他们上岸了。

paragraphs.en: “Now, Huck, where we’re a-standing you could touch that hole I got out of with a fishing-pole.
paragraphs.cn: “现在，哈克，我们站的地方，用鱼竿就能碰到我爬出来的那个洞。

paragraphs.en: See if you can find it.”
paragraphs.cn: 你看看能不能找到它。

paragraphs.en: Huck searched all the place about, and found nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克在周围找了找，什么也没找到。

paragraphs.en: Tom proudly marched into a thick clump of sumach bushes and said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆得意地走进一片浓密的漆树丛，说：

paragraphs.en: “Here you are!
paragraphs.cn: “就在这儿！

paragraphs.en: Look at it, Huck; it’s the snuggest hole in this country.
paragraphs.cn: 看看，哈克，这是这个地方最舒服的洞了。

paragraphs.en: You just keep mum about it.
paragraphs.cn: 你要保密哦。

paragraphs.en: All along I’ve been wanting to be a robber, but I knew I’d got to have a thing like this, and where to run across it was the bother.
paragraphs.cn: 我一直想当强盗，可我知道得有这么个地方，找到它可不容易。

paragraphs.en: We’ve got it now, and we’ll keep it quiet, only we’ll let Joe Harper and Ben Rogers in—because of course there’s got to be a Gang, or else there wouldn’t be any style about it.
paragraphs.cn: 我们现在有了，要保密。不过我们可以叫上乔·哈珀和本·罗杰斯，因为得有个“团伙”才行，不然就没意思了。

paragraphs.en: Tom Sawyer’s Gang—it sounds splendid, don’t it, Huck?”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆·索亚的团伙”——听起来真棒，是不是啊，哈克？”

paragraphs.en: “Well, it just does, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，是啊，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: And who’ll we rob?”
paragraphs.cn: 我们去抢谁呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, most anybody.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，随便什么人。

paragraphs.en: Waylay people—that’s mostly the way.”
paragraphs.cn: 埋伏他们——大多是这样。”

paragraphs.en: “And kill them?”
paragraphs.cn: “那要杀了他们吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No, not always.
paragraphs.cn: “不，不总是。

paragraphs.en: Hive them in the cave till they raise a ransom.”
paragraphs.cn: 把他们藏在山洞里，直到他们交赎金。”

paragraphs.en: “What’s a ransom?”
paragraphs.cn: “什么是赎金？”

paragraphs.en: “Money.
You make them raise all they can, off’n their friends; and after you’ve kept them a year, if it ain’t raised then you kill them.
paragraphs.cn: 你让他们从朋友那儿弄到所有能弄到的钱；如果你把他们关了一年，还没弄到，那就杀了他们。

paragraphs.en: That’s the general way.
paragraphs.cn: 一般都这样。

paragraphs.en: Only you don’t kill the women.
paragraphs.cn: 不过女人不能杀。

paragraphs.en: You shut up the women, but you don’t kill them.
paragraphs.cn: 你把女人关起来，但不能杀她们。

paragraphs.en: They’re always beautiful and rich, and awfully scared.
paragraphs.cn: 她们总是又漂亮又有钱，而且特别害怕。

paragraphs.en: You take their watches and things, but you always take your hat off and talk polite.
paragraphs.cn: 你拿走她们的手表和东西，但你总是要脱帽，说话要客气。

paragraphs.en: They ain’t anybody as polite as robbers—you’ll see that in any book.
paragraphs.cn: 没有人比强盗更客气了——你会在任何书里看到。

paragraphs.en: Well, the women get to loving you, and after they’ve been in the cave a week or two weeks they stop crying and after that you couldn’t get them to leave.
paragraphs.cn: 呃，女人们会爱上你，在山洞里待了一两周后，她们就不哭了，然后你再也赶不走她们了。

paragraphs.en: If you drove them out they’d turn right around and come back.
paragraphs.cn: 如果你把她们赶出去，她们会立刻回来。

paragraphs.en: It’s so in all the books.”
paragraphs.cn: 所有的书里都是这么写的。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, it’s real bully, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “哇，这真是太棒了，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: I believe it’s better’n to be a pirate.”
paragraphs.cn: 我觉得这比当海盗还好玩。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, it’s better in some ways, because it’s close to home and circuses and all that.”
paragraphs.cn: “是啊，在某些方面是更好，因为它离家近，能看马戏团什么的。”

paragraphs.en: By this time everything was ready and the boys entered the hole, Tom in the lead.
paragraphs.cn: 这时一切都准备好了，孩子们进了洞，汤姆走在最前面。

paragraphs.en: They toiled their way to the farther end of the tunnel, then made their spliced kite-strings fast and moved on.
paragraphs.cn: 他们费力地走到隧道的尽头，然后系好接好的风筝线，继续往前走。

paragraphs.en: A few steps brought them to the spring, and Tom felt a shudder quiver all through him.
paragraphs.cn: 走了几步，他们来到了泉水边，汤姆全身都颤抖起来。

paragraphs.en: He showed Huck the fragment of candle-wick perched on a lump of clay against the wall, and described how he and Becky had watched the flame struggle and expire.
paragraphs.cn: 他给哈克看了一小截蜡烛芯，它粘在墙边一块泥土上。他还讲了自己和贝琪怎么看着火苗挣扎，然后灭了。

paragraphs.en: The boys began to quiet down to whispers, now, for the stillness and gloom of the place oppressed their spirits.
paragraphs.cn: 男孩们现在小声说话了，因为这里又安静又黑，让他们心里不舒服。

paragraphs.en: They went on, and presently entered and followed Tom’s other corridor until they reached the “jumping-off place.”
paragraphs.cn: 他们继续往前走，很快就进了汤姆的另一条走廊，一直走到那个“跳崖的地方”。

paragraphs.en: The candles revealed the fact that it was not really a precipice, but only a steep clay hill twenty or thirty feet high.
paragraphs.cn: 蜡烛照亮后，他们发现那不是真的悬崖，只是一座二十或三十英尺高的陡峭泥土山。

paragraphs.en: Tom whispered:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆小声说：

paragraphs.en: “Now I’ll show you something, Huck.”
paragraphs.cn: “现在我给哈克看个东西。”

paragraphs.en: He held his candle aloft and said:
paragraphs.cn: 他把蜡烛举高，说：

paragraphs.en: “Look as far around the corner as you can.
paragraphs.cn: “你往拐角那边，能看多远就看多远。”

paragraphs.en: Do you see that?
paragraphs.cn: “你看到那个了吗？”

paragraphs.en: There—on the big rock over yonder—done with candle-smoke.”
paragraphs.cn: “在那里——那边的大石头上——是用蜡烛烟熏出来的。”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, it’s a _cross_!”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，那是个_十字架_！”

paragraphs.en: “_Now_ where’s your Number Two?
paragraphs.cn: “_现在_你的二号在哪儿？”

paragraphs.en: ‘_under the cross_,’ hey?
paragraphs.cn: “‘_在十字架下面_’，是吗？”

paragraphs.en: Right yonder’s where I saw Injun Joe poke up his candle, Huck!”
paragraphs.cn: “就在那里，我看到印第安·乔把他的蜡烛举起来了，哈克！”

paragraphs.en: Huck stared at the mystic sign awhile, and then said with a shaky voice:
paragraphs.cn: 哈克盯着那个神秘的记号看了一会儿，然后用颤抖的声音说：

paragraphs.en: “Tom, less git out of here!”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，我们快离开这里吧！”

paragraphs.en: “What! and leave the treasure?”
paragraphs.cn: “什么！把宝藏留下？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes—leave it.
paragraphs.cn: “是的——留下它。”

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe’s ghost is round about there, certain.”
paragraphs.cn: “印第安·乔的鬼魂肯定就在那附近。”

paragraphs.en: “No it ain’t, Huck, no it ain’t.
paragraphs.cn: “不，不是的，哈克，不是的。”

paragraphs.en: It would ha’nt the place where he died—away out at the mouth of the cave—five mile from here.”
paragraphs.cn: “它会缠着他死去的地方——在洞口外面——离这里五英里呢。”

paragraphs.en: “No, Tom, it wouldn’t.
paragraphs.cn: “不，汤姆，它不会的。”

paragraphs.en: It would hang round the money.
paragraphs.cn: “它会围着钱转的。”

paragraphs.en: I know the ways of ghosts, and so do you.”
paragraphs.cn: “我知道鬼魂是怎么样的，你也知道的。”

paragraphs.en: Tom began to fear that Huck was right.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆开始害怕哈克说得对。

paragraphs.en: Misgivings gathered in his mind.
paragraphs.cn: 他心里充满了疑虑。

paragraphs.en: But presently an idea occurred to him—
paragraphs.cn: 但很快他想到了一个主意——

paragraphs.en: “Lookyhere, Huck, what fools we’re making of ourselves!
paragraphs.cn: “看这里，哈克，我们真是太傻了！”

paragraphs.en: Injun Joe’s ghost ain’t a going to come around where there’s a cross!”
paragraphs.cn: “印第安·乔的鬼魂才不会来有十字架的地方呢！”

paragraphs.en: The point was well taken.
paragraphs.cn: 这个理由很有道理。

paragraphs.en: It had its effect.
paragraphs.cn: 它果然有用了。

paragraphs.en: “Tom, I didn’t think of that.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，我没想到这个。

paragraphs.en: But that’s so.
paragraphs.cn: 但就是这样！

paragraphs.en: It’s luck for us, that cross is.
paragraphs.cn: 那个十字架真是我们的运气。

paragraphs.en: I reckon we’ll climb down there and have a hunt for that box.”
paragraphs.cn: 我想我们下去那里找找那个箱子吧。”

paragraphs.en: Tom went first, cutting rude steps in the clay hill as he descended.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆先下去，他在泥土坡上踩出粗糙的台阶。

paragraphs.en: Huck followed.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克跟着他。

paragraphs.en: Four avenues opened out of the small cavern which the great rock stood in.
paragraphs.cn: 大石头旁边的小洞里，有四条路通向外面。

paragraphs.en: The boys examined three of them with no result.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们查了三条路，什么也没找到。

paragraphs.en: They found a small recess in the one nearest the base of the rock, with a pallet of blankets spread down in it; also an old suspender, some bacon rind, and the well-gnawed bones of two or three fowls.
paragraphs.cn: 在离石头底部最近的那条路，他们发现了一个小凹进去的地方。里面铺着毯子，还有一条旧背带，一些培根皮，和两三只鸡被啃光了的骨头。

paragraphs.en: But there was no moneybox.
paragraphs.cn: 但没有钱箱。

paragraphs.en: The lads searched and researched this place, but in vain.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们反复找了这个地方，但没用。

paragraphs.en: Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “He said _under_ the cross.
paragraphs.cn: “他说在十字架下面。

paragraphs.en: Well, this comes nearest to being under the cross.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，这里离十字架下面最近了。

paragraphs.en: It can’t be under the rock itself, because that sets solid on the ground.”
paragraphs.cn: 不可能在石头下面，因为它紧紧地贴着地面。”

paragraphs.en: They searched everywhere once more, and then sat down discouraged.
paragraphs.cn: 他们又到处找了一遍，然后失望地坐了下来。

paragraphs.en: Huck could suggest nothing.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克想不出任何办法。

paragraphs.en: By-and-by Tom said:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，汤姆说：

paragraphs.en: “Lookyhere, Huck, there’s footprints and some candle-grease on the clay about one side of this rock, but not on the other sides.
paragraphs.cn: “你看，哈克，这块石头的一边泥土上有脚印和一些蜡烛油，但其他几边没有。

paragraphs.en: Now, what’s that for?
paragraphs.cn: 这是为什么呢？

paragraphs.en: I bet you the money _is_ under the rock.
paragraphs.cn: 我敢打赌钱就在石头下面。

paragraphs.en: I’m going to dig in the clay.”
paragraphs.cn: 我要挖一下泥土。”

paragraphs.en: “That ain’t no bad notion, Tom!” said Huck with animation.
paragraphs.cn: “这个主意不错，汤姆！”哈克兴奋地说。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s “real Barlow” was out at once, and he had not dug four inches before he struck wood.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆立刻拿出他的“真巴洛小刀”，他还没挖四英寸就碰到了木头。

paragraphs.en: “Hey, Huck!
paragraphs.cn: “嘿，哈克！

paragraphs.en: —you hear that?”
paragraphs.cn: —你听到了吗？”

paragraphs.en: Huck began to dig and scratch now.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克也开始挖和扒。

paragraphs.en: Some boards were soon uncovered and removed.
paragraphs.cn: 很快，几块木板被挖开，拿走了。

paragraphs.en: They had concealed a natural chasm which led under the rock.
paragraphs.cn: 它们藏着一条天然的裂缝，裂缝通向石头下面。

paragraphs.en: Tom got into this and held his candle as far under the rock as he could, but said he could not see to the end of the rift.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 钻了进去，他把蜡烛伸到石头下面，尽量往深处照。他说：“我看不到这条缝的尽头。”

paragraphs.en: He proposed to explore.
paragraphs.cn: 他想进去看看。

paragraphs.en: He stooped and passed under; the narrow way descended gradually.
paragraphs.cn: 他弯腰钻了进去。这条窄窄的路，慢慢地往下走。

paragraphs.en: He followed its winding course, first to the right, then to the left, Huck at his heels.
paragraphs.cn: 他跟着弯弯的路走，一会儿往右，一会儿往左。哈克 紧紧跟在他身后。

paragraphs.en: Tom turned a short curve, by-and-by, and exclaimed:
paragraphs.cn: 过了一会儿，汤姆 转过了一个弯，大叫起来：

paragraphs.en: “My goodness, Huck, lookyhere!”
paragraphs.cn: “天哪，哈克，快看！”

paragraphs.en: It was the treasure-box, sure enough, occupying a snug little cavern, along with an empty powder-keg, a couple of guns in leather cases, two or three pairs of old moccasins, a leather belt, and some other rubbish well soaked with the water-drip.
paragraphs.cn: 果然是宝箱！它在一个舒服的小洞里，旁边还有个空火药桶、两把装在皮套里的枪、几双旧鞋子、一条皮带，还有一些被水滴弄湿的旧东西。

paragraphs.en: “Got it at last!” said Huck, ploughing among the tarnished coins with his hand. “My, but we’re rich, Tom!”
paragraphs.cn: “我们终于找到了！”哈克 用手拨弄着那些旧旧的硬币。他大声说：“哇，汤姆，我们发大财了！”

paragraphs.en: “Huck, I always reckoned we’d get it.
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，我一直都觉得我们能找到它。

paragraphs.en: It’s just too good to believe, but we _have_ got it, sure!
paragraphs.cn: 这太好了，好得我都不敢相信了，但我们真的找到了！

paragraphs.en: Say—let’s not fool around here.
paragraphs.cn: 喂——我们别在这里玩了。

paragraphs.en: Let’s snake it out.
paragraphs.cn: 我们把它弄出去吧。

paragraphs.en: Lemme see if I can lift the box.”
paragraphs.cn: 我来试试能不能把箱子抬起来。”

paragraphs.en: It weighed about fifty pounds.
paragraphs.cn: 它大约有五十磅重。

paragraphs.en: Tom could lift it, after an awkward fashion, but could not carry it conveniently.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆 可以笨手笨脚地把它抬起来，但不太好搬走。

paragraphs.en: “I thought so,” he said; “_They_ carried it like it was heavy, that day at the ha’nted house.
paragraphs.cn: “我就知道是这样。”他说：“那天在鬼屋里，_他们_搬的时候，这个箱子就很重。”

paragraphs.en: I noticed that.
paragraphs.cn: 我注意到了。

paragraphs.en: I reckon I was right to think of fetching the little bags along.”
paragraphs.cn: 看来我带着这些小袋子是对的。”

paragraphs.en: The money was soon in the bags and the boys took it up to the cross rock.
paragraphs.cn: 钱很快就装进了袋子，他们把钱带到了那块交叉的石头那里。

paragraphs.en: “Now less fetch the guns and things,” said Huck.
paragraphs.cn: “现在我们去把枪和那些东西拿过来吧。”哈克 说。

paragraphs.en: “No, Huck—leave them there.
paragraphs.cn: “不，哈克——把它们留在那里。

paragraphs.en: They’re just the tricks to have when we go to robbing.
paragraphs.cn: 我们去抢东西的时候，它们可正好派上用场。

paragraphs.en: We’ll keep them there all the time, and we’ll hold our orgies there, too.
paragraphs.cn: 我们一直把它们放在那儿，我们也要在那儿开派对。

paragraphs.en: It’s an awful snug place for orgies.”
paragraphs.cn: 那是个开派对的好地方。”

paragraphs.en: “What orgies?”
paragraphs.cn: “什么派对？”

paragraphs.en: “I dono.
paragraphs.cn: “我不知道呀。

paragraphs.en: But robbers always have orgies, and of course we’ve got to have them, too.
paragraphs.cn: 但是坏蛋们总会开派对的，我们当然也要开呀。

paragraphs.en: Come along, Huck, we’ve been in here a long time.
paragraphs.cn: 快走吧，哈克，我们在这里待了好久了。

paragraphs.en: It’s getting late, I reckon.
paragraphs.cn: 我想，天快黑了。

paragraphs.en: I’m hungry, too.
paragraphs.cn: 我也饿了。

paragraphs.en: We’ll eat and smoke when we get to the skiff.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们到了小船那儿，就可以吃东西了。

paragraphs.en: They presently emerged into the clump of sumach bushes, looked warily out, found the coast clear, and were soon lunching and smoking in the skiff.
paragraphs.cn: 他们很快从漆树丛里出来，小心地往外瞧了瞧，没人！他们就赶紧跑到小船上，吃午饭，还抽了烟。

paragraphs.en: As the sun dipped toward the horizon they pushed out and got under way.
paragraphs.cn: 太阳快要下山了，他们就划着小船走了。

paragraphs.en: Tom skimmed up the shore through the long twilight, chatting cheerily with Huck, and landed shortly after dark.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆和哈克在傍晚时分沿着岸边走，开心地聊天。天一黑，他们就上岸了。

paragraphs.en: “Now, Huck,” said Tom, “we’ll hide the money in the loft of the widow’s woodshed, and I’ll come up in the morning and we’ll count it and divide, and then we’ll hunt up a place out in the woods for it where it will be safe.
paragraphs.cn: “好了，哈克，”汤姆说，“我们把钱藏在寡妇家柴棚的楼上。明天早上我过来，我们把钱数清楚，然后分好。再到树林里找个安全的地方藏起来。

paragraphs.en: Just you lay quiet here and watch the stuff till I run and hook Benny Taylor’s little wagon; I won’t be gone a minute.”
paragraphs.cn: 你就安静地在这儿，看着这些东西，我去借一下本尼·泰勒的小推车。我很快就回来，一分钟都不耽误！”

paragraphs.en: He disappeared, and presently returned with the wagon, put the two small sacks into it, threw some old rags on top of them, and started off, dragging his cargo behind him.
paragraphs.cn: 他走了，一会儿就推着小推车回来了。他把两个小袋子放进车里，上面盖了些旧布，然后拉着小推车走了。

paragraphs.en: When the boys reached the Welshman’s house, they stopped to rest.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们走到威尔士叔叔家时，停下来歇了歇。

paragraphs.en: Just as they were about to move on, the Welshman stepped out and said:
paragraphs.cn: 他们刚要继续走，威尔士叔叔就走了出来，说：

paragraphs.en: “Hallo, who’s that?”
paragraphs.cn: “喂，是谁啊？”

paragraphs.en: “Huck and Tom Sawyer.”
paragraphs.cn: “是哈克和汤姆·索亚。”

paragraphs.en: “Good!
paragraphs.cn: “好啊！

paragraphs.en: Come along with me, boys, you are keeping everybody waiting.
paragraphs.cn: 跟我来吧，孩子们，大家都在等你们呢。

paragraphs.en: Here—hurry up, trot ahead—I’ll haul the wagon for you.
paragraphs.cn: 快点——跑前面去——我帮你拉车。

paragraphs.en: Why, it’s not as light as it might be.
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，这车可不轻呀。

paragraphs.en: Got bricks in it?
paragraphs.cn: 里面装的是砖头吗？

paragraphs.en: —or old metal?”
paragraphs.cn: 还是旧金属？”

paragraphs.en: “Old metal,” said Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “旧金属，”汤姆说。

paragraphs.en: “I judged so; the boys in this town will take more trouble and fool away more time hunting up six bits’ worth of old iron to sell to the foundry than they would to make twice the money at regular work.
paragraphs.cn: “我就猜是这样！这镇上的男孩子们啊，宁愿花很多力气和时间去找一点点旧铁去卖钱，也不愿好好工作去挣更多的钱。

paragraphs.en: But that’s human nature—hurry along, hurry along!”
paragraphs.cn: 但人就是这样嘛——快走吧，快走吧！”

paragraphs.en: The boys wanted to know what the hurry was about.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们想知道为什么这么着急。

paragraphs.en: “Never mind; you’ll see, when we get to the Widow Douglas’.”
paragraphs.cn: “没关系，到了道格拉斯寡妇’那里你们就知道了。”

paragraphs.en: Huck said with some apprehension—for he was long used to being falsely accused:
paragraphs.cn: 哈克有点担心地说，因为他老是被冤枉：

paragraphs.en: “Mr. Jones, we haven’t been doing nothing.”
paragraphs.cn: “琼斯先生，我们什么都没做。”

paragraphs.en: The Welshman laughed.
paragraphs.cn: 威尔士叔叔笑了。

paragraphs.en: “Well, I don’t know, Huck, my boy.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，哈克，我的孩子，我不知道。

paragraphs.en: I don’t know about that.
paragraphs.cn: 这事儿我可不知道。

paragraphs.en: Ain’t you and the widow good friends?”
paragraphs.cn: 你不是和那位寡妇阿姨是好朋友吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes.
paragraphs.cn: “是的。

paragraphs.en: Well, she’s ben good friends to me, anyway.”
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，反正她一直对我都很好。”

paragraphs.en: “All right, then.
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，那。

paragraphs.en: What do you want to be afraid for?”
paragraphs.cn: 你为什么要害怕呢？”

paragraphs.en: This question was not entirely answered in Huck’s slow mind before he found himself pushed, along with Tom, into Mrs. Douglas’ drawing-room.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克还没完全想明白这个问题，他就和汤姆一起被推进了道格拉斯太太的客厅。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Jones left the wagon near the door and followed.
paragraphs.cn: 琼斯先生把车停在门口，也跟着进去了。

paragraphs.en: The place was grandly lighted, and everybody that was of any consequence in the village was there.
paragraphs.cn: 屋子里灯很亮，村里重要的人都来了。

paragraphs.en: The Thatchers were there, the Harpers, the Rogerses, Aunt Polly, Sid, Mary, the minister, the editor, and a great many more, and all dressed in their best.
paragraphs.cn: 撒切尔一家、哈珀一家、罗杰斯一家、波莉姨妈、希德、玛丽、牧师、编辑，还有好多好多人都在那里，大家都穿着最好的衣服。

paragraphs.en: The widow received the boys as heartily as any one could well receive two such looking beings.
paragraphs.cn: 寡妇非常热情地招待了两个男孩，就像她会招待所有客人一样。

paragraphs.en: They were covered with clay and candle-grease.
paragraphs.cn: 他们身上沾满了泥巴和蜡油。

paragraphs.en: Aunt Polly blushed crimson with humiliation, and frowned and shook her head at Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 波莉姨妈觉得很丢脸，脸都红了，还皱着眉冲汤姆摇头。

paragraphs.en: Nobody suffered half as much as the two boys did, however.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，没人比这两个男孩更难受了。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Jones said:
paragraphs.cn: 琼斯先生说：

paragraphs.en: “Tom wasn’t at home, yet, so I gave him up; but I stumbled on him and Huck right at my door, and so I just brought them along in a hurry.”
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆还没回家，我本来想放弃了；可我在我家门口碰到了他和哈克，所以我就赶紧把他们带来了。”

paragraphs.en: “And you did just right,” said the widow.
paragraphs.cn: “你做得太对了！”寡妇说。

paragraphs.en: “Come with me, boys.”
paragraphs.cn: “跟我来，孩子们。”

paragraphs.en: She took them to a bedchamber and said:
paragraphs.cn: 她把他们带到一个卧室，说：

paragraphs.en: “Now wash and dress yourselves.
paragraphs.cn: “现在，洗洗澡，穿上衣服吧。

paragraphs.en: Here are two new suits of clothes—shirts, socks, everything complete.
paragraphs.cn: 这里有两套新衣服——衬衫、袜子，什么都有，很齐全。

paragraphs.en: They’re Huck’s—no, no thanks, Huck—Mr. Jones bought one and I the other.
paragraphs.cn: 这些是哈克的——哦，不用谢，哈克——琼斯先生买了一套，我买了另一套。

paragraphs.en: But they’ll fit both of you.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，它们俩都适合你们。

paragraphs.en: Get into them.
paragraphs.cn: 快穿上吧。

paragraphs.en: We’ll wait—come down when you are slicked up enough.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们会在外面等——等你们收拾好了就下来吧。”

paragraphs.en: Then she left.
paragraphs.cn: 然后她就走了。

paragraphs.en: Huck said: “Tom, we can slope, if we can find a rope.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克说：“汤姆，要是我们能找到绳子，就能溜走了。窗户离地面不远。”

paragraphs.en: The window ain’t high from the ground.”
paragraphs.cn: 窗户离地面不高。

paragraphs.en: “Shucks! what do you want to slope for?”
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀！你为什么要溜走啊？”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I ain’t used to that kind of a crowd.
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，我不习惯那么多人。

paragraphs.en: I can’t stand it.
paragraphs.cn: 我受不了。

paragraphs.en: I ain’t going down there, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: 我不会去那里的，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, bother!
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，真麻烦！

paragraphs.en: It ain’t anything.
paragraphs.cn: 没什么大不了的。

paragraphs.en: I don’t mind it a bit.
paragraphs.cn: 我一点都不介意。

paragraphs.en: I’ll take care of you.”
paragraphs.cn: 我会照顾你的。”

paragraphs.en: Sid appeared.
paragraphs.cn: 希德 出现了。

paragraphs.en: “Tom,” said he, “auntie has been waiting for you all the afternoon.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，”他说，“阿姨下午一直在等你呢。

paragraphs.en: Mary got your Sunday clothes ready, and everybody’s been fretting about you.
paragraphs.cn: 玛丽 把你星期天穿的衣服都准备好了，大家都在为你着急呢。

paragraphs.en: Say—ain’t this grease and clay, on your clothes?”
paragraphs.cn: 喂——你衣服上是不是有油泥和黏土啊？”

paragraphs.en: “Now, Mr. Siddy, you jist ’tend to your own business.
paragraphs.cn: “哎，西迪先生，你管好你自己的事就行了。

paragraphs.en: What’s all this blowout about, anyway?”
paragraphs.cn: 这到底是怎么回事啊？”

paragraphs.en: “It’s one of the widow’s parties that she’s always having.
paragraphs.cn: “这是寡妇经常办的那种派对。

paragraphs.en: This time it’s for the Welshman and his sons, on account of that scrape they helped her out of the other night.
paragraphs.cn: 这次是为了感谢那个威尔士人和他的儿子们，因为他们前几天晚上帮了她一个大忙。

paragraphs.en: And say—I can tell you something, if you want to know.”
paragraphs.cn: 喂——如果你想知道，我可以告诉你一个秘密哦。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, what?”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，什么事？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, old Mr. Jones is going to try to spring something on the people here tonight, but I overheard him tell auntie today about it, as a secret, but I reckon it’s not much of a secret now.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，琼斯老先生今晚想给大家一个惊喜，但我今天偷听到他跟阿姨说，这是个秘密，可我觉得现在这已经不是什么秘密了。

paragraphs.en: Everybody knows—the widow, too, for all she tries to let on she don’t.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都知道了——连寡妇也知道了，虽然她假装不知道。

paragraphs.en: Mr. Jones was bound Huck should be here—couldn’t get along with his grand secret without Huck, you know!”
paragraphs.cn: 琼斯先生非要 哈克 在场——没有 哈克，他的大秘密就没法进行下去，你知道的！”
