paragraphs.en: “Secret about what, Sid?”
paragraphs.cn: “什么秘密啊，希德？”

paragraphs.en: “About Huck tracking the robbers to the widow’s.
paragraphs.cn: “就是 哈克 跟着那些强盗到了寡妇家这件事。

paragraphs.en: I reckon Mr. Jones was going to make a grand time over his surprise, but I bet you it will drop pretty flat.”
paragraphs.cn: 我猜琼斯先生本来想让他的惊喜很轰动，但我敢打赌，那肯定会变得一点也不好玩。”

paragraphs.en: Sid chuckled in a very contented and satisfied way.
paragraphs.cn: 希德 心满意足地笑了笑。

paragraphs.en: “Sid, was it you that told?”
paragraphs.cn: “希德，是你告诉的吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, never mind who it was.
paragraphs.cn: “哎呀，别管是谁说的了。

paragraphs.en: _Somebody_ told—that’s enough.”
paragraphs.cn: 有人 告诉了——这就够了。”

paragraphs.en: “Sid, there’s only one person in this town mean enough to do that, and that’s you.
paragraphs.cn: “希德，这个镇上只有一个人会做那么坏的事，那就是你。

paragraphs.en: If you had been in Huck’s place you’d ’a’ sneaked down the hill and never told anybody on the robbers.
paragraphs.cn: 如果你处在 哈克 的位置，你肯定会偷偷溜下山，然后一个字也不告诉别人关于那些强盗的事。

paragraphs.en: You can’t do any but mean things, and you can’t bear to see anybody praised for doing good ones.
paragraphs.cn: 你只会做坏事，而且你见不得别人因为做好事而受到表扬。

paragraphs.en: There—no thanks, as the widow says”—and Tom cuffed Sid’s ears and helped him to the door with several kicks.
paragraphs.cn: 好了——不用谢了，就像寡妇说的。”——然后 汤姆 掴了 希德 的耳朵几下，又踢了他几脚，把他赶到了门口。

paragraphs.en: “Now go and tell auntie if you dare—and tomorrow you’ll catch it!”
paragraphs.cn: “现在你敢去告诉阿姨，明天你就惨了！”

paragraphs.en: Some minutes later the widow’s guests were at the supper-table, and a dozen children were propped up at little side-tables in the same room, after the fashion of that country and that day.
paragraphs.cn: 几分钟后，寡妇家的客人们都坐在了餐桌旁，十几个孩子则像当时那个地方的习俗一样，在同一个房间里的小边桌旁坐着。

paragraphs.en: At the proper time Mr. Jones made his little speech, in which he thanked the widow for the honor she was doing himself and his sons, but said that there was another person whose modesty—
paragraphs.cn: 到了合适的时候，琼斯先生发表了一个简短的讲话，他感谢寡妇给他和他的儿子们带来的荣誉，但他说还有另一个人，他的谦虚——

paragraphs.en: And so forth and so on.
paragraphs.cn: 等等，等等。

paragraphs.en: He sprung his secret about Huck’s share in the adventure in the finest dramatic manner he was master of, but the surprise it occasioned was largely counterfeit and not as clamorous and effusive as it might have been under happier circumstances.
paragraphs.cn: 他用最棒的办法，告诉了大家一个秘密，说哈克也参与了那场冒险。大家假装很惊讶，但其实没那么高兴。

paragraphs.en: However, the widow made a pretty fair show of astonishment, and heaped so many compliments and so much gratitude upon Huck that he almost forgot the nearly intolerable discomfort of his new clothes in the entirely intolerable discomfort of being set up as a target for everybody’s gaze and everybody’s laudations.
paragraphs.cn: 不过，寡妇表现得很惊讶，还夸了哈克好多，非常感谢他。哈克觉得被大家盯着看、被夸奖比穿新衣服还不舒服。

paragraphs.en: The widow said she meant to give Huck a home under her roof and have him educated; and that when she could spare the money she would start him in business in a modest way.
paragraphs.cn: 寡妇说她想让哈克住在她家，送他去读书。等她有钱了，还会帮他开个小店。

paragraphs.en: Tom’s chance was come.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆的机会来了。

paragraphs.en: He said:
paragraphs.cn: 他说：

paragraphs.en: “Huck don’t need it.
paragraphs.cn: “哈克不需要。

paragraphs.en: Huck’s rich.”
paragraphs.cn: 哈克很有钱。”

paragraphs.en: Nothing but a heavy strain upon the good manners of the company kept back the due and proper complimentary laugh at this pleasant joke.
paragraphs.cn: 大家很想笑这个有趣的玩笑，但为了礼貌，都忍住了没笑。

paragraphs.en: But the silence was a little awkward.
paragraphs.cn: 但屋子里有点安静，怪怪的。

paragraphs.en: Tom broke it:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆打破了这份安静：

paragraphs.en: “Huck’s got money.
paragraphs.cn: “哈克有钱。

paragraphs.en: Maybe you don’t believe it, but he’s got lots of it.
paragraphs.cn: 也许你们不相信，但他真的有很多钱。

paragraphs.en: Oh, you needn’t smile—I reckon I can show you.
paragraphs.cn: 噢，你们别笑——我想我可以给你们看。

paragraphs.en: You just wait a minute.”
paragraphs.cn: 你们等等。”

paragraphs.en: Tom ran out of doors.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆跑出门去了。

paragraphs.en: The company looked at each other with a perplexed interest—and inquiringly at Huck, who was tongue-tied.
paragraphs.cn: 大家你看看我，我看看你，都很好奇，又都看着不知道说什么的哈克。

paragraphs.en: “Sid, what ails Tom?” said Aunt Polly.
paragraphs.cn: “希德，汤姆怎么了？”波莉姨妈问。

paragraphs.en: “He—well, there ain’t ever any making of that boy out.
paragraphs.cn: “他——哎，这个孩子真是让人摸不透。

paragraphs.en: I never—”
paragraphs.cn: 我从没——”

paragraphs.en: Tom entered, struggling with the weight of his sacks, and Aunt Polly did not finish her sentence.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆进来了，他吃力地背着几个袋子。波莉姨妈没有说完她的话。

paragraphs.en: Tom poured the mass of yellow coin upon the table and said:
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆把一大堆黄色的金币倒在桌子上，说：

paragraphs.en: “There—what did I tell you?
paragraphs.cn: “看——我说了什么？

paragraphs.en: Half of it’s Huck’s and half of it’s mine!”
paragraphs.cn: 一半是哈克的，一半是我的！”

paragraphs.en: The spectacle took the general breath away.
paragraphs.cn: 眼前这一幕让大家都很吃惊。

paragraphs.en: All gazed, nobody spoke for a moment.
paragraphs.cn: 大家盯着看，一时都没说话。

paragraphs.en: Then there was a unanimous call for an explanation.
paragraphs.cn: 接着，大家异口同声地要他解释。

paragraphs.en: Tom said he could furnish it, and he did.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆说他可以解释，然后他就解释了。

paragraphs.en: The tale was long, but brimful of interest.
paragraphs.cn: 故事很长，但特别有趣。

paragraphs.en: There was scarcely an interruption from any one to break the charm of its flow.
paragraphs.cn: 几乎没有人打断他，故事讲得太吸引人了。

paragraphs.en: When he had finished, Mr. Jones said:
paragraphs.cn: 他讲完后，琼斯先生说：

paragraphs.en: “I thought I had fixed up a little surprise for this occasion, but it don’t amount to anything now.
paragraphs.cn: “我本想给大家一个小惊喜，但现在看来，这算不上什么了。

paragraphs.en: This one makes it sing mighty small, I’m willing to allow.”
paragraphs.cn: “和这个比起来，我的惊喜简直微不足道，我承认。”

paragraphs.en: The money was counted.
paragraphs.cn: 钱被数完了。

paragraphs.en: The sum amounted to a little over twelve thousand dollars.
paragraphs.cn: 总共有超过一万两千美元。

paragraphs.en: It was more than any one present had ever seen at one time before, though several persons were there who were worth considerably more than that in property.
paragraphs.cn: 这是在场所有人一次性见过最多钱。虽然有些人财产更多，但他们也没见过这么多现金。

paragraphs.en: The reader may rest satisfied that Tom’s and Huck’s windfall made a mighty stir in the poor little village of St. Petersburg.
paragraphs.cn: 你们要知道，汤姆和哈克突然得了这么多钱，让圣彼得斯堡这个小村子热闹极了。

paragraphs.en: So vast a sum, all in actual cash, seemed next to incredible.
paragraphs.cn: 这么多现金，简直让人不敢相信。

paragraphs.en: It was talked about, gloated over, glorified, until the reason of many of the citizens tottered under the strain of the unhealthy excitement.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都在谈论它，炫耀它，把它说得神乎其神，很多人兴奋得都快失去理智了。

paragraphs.en: Every “haunted” house in St. Petersburg and the neighboring villages was dissected, plank by plank, and its foundations dug up and ransacked for hidden treasure—and not by boys, but men—pretty grave, unromantic men, too, some of them.
paragraphs.cn: 圣彼得斯堡和附近村子的所有“鬼屋”都被拆开，一块木板一块木板地检查。地基也被挖开，到处找藏起来的宝藏——不是小孩子做的，而是大人，有些还是很严肃、不爱幻想的大人。

paragraphs.en: Wherever Tom and Huck appeared they were courted, admired, stared at.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆和哈克走到哪里，大家就都想和他们亲近，羡慕他们，盯着他们看。

paragraphs.en: The boys were not able to remember that their remarks had possessed weight before; but now their sayings were treasured and repeated; everything they did seemed somehow to be regarded as remarkable; they had evidently lost the power of doing and saying commonplace things; moreover, their past history was raked up and discovered to bear marks of conspicuous originality.
paragraphs.cn: 孩子们都不记得以前说过的话有人听。但现在，他们说的话都被当成宝贝，反复传颂。他们做的每件事都变得很特别。他们好像都不会做或说普通的事了。甚至他们以前的事也被挖出来，发现他们从小就很不一般。

paragraphs.en: The village paper published biographical sketches of the boys.
paragraphs.cn: 村里的报纸还写了关于这些孩子的故事。

paragraphs.en: The Widow Douglas put Huck’s money out at six per cent.
paragraphs.cn: 道格拉斯寡妇把哈克的钱拿去投资，每年有百分之六的利息。

paragraphs.en: , and Judge Thatcher did the same with Tom’s at Aunt Polly’s request.
paragraphs.cn: 并且，应波莉姨妈的要求，撒切尔法官也把汤姆的钱照样投资了。

paragraphs.en: Each lad had an income, now, that was simply prodigious—a dollar for every weekday in the year and half of the Sundays.
paragraphs.cn: 两个孩子现在都有一大笔收入了——一年里每个工作日都有一美元，星期天也能拿到一半的钱。

paragraphs.en: It was just what the minister got—no, it was what he was promised—he generally couldn’t collect it.
paragraphs.cn: 这和牧师挣得一样多——不，是牧师被承诺的那么多——但他通常都收不到。

paragraphs.en: A dollar and a quarter a week would board, lodge, and school a boy in those old simple days—and clothe him and wash him, too, for that matter.
paragraphs.cn: 在过去那些简单的日子里，一周一美元零二十五美分，就够一个孩子吃住、上学了——甚至连衣服和洗澡的钱都够了。

paragraphs.en: Judge Thatcher had conceived a great opinion of Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 撒切尔法官对汤姆评价很高。

paragraphs.en: He said that no commonplace boy would ever have got his daughter out of the cave.
paragraphs.cn: 他说，一个普通的孩子是绝对不可能把他的女儿从山洞里救出来的。

paragraphs.en: When Becky told her father, in strict confidence, how Tom had taken her whipping at school, the Judge was visibly moved; and when she pleaded grace for the mighty lie which Tom had told in order to shift that whipping from her shoulders to his own, the Judge said with a fine outburst that it was a noble, a generous, a magnanimous lie—a lie that was worthy to hold up its head and march down through history breast to breast with George Washington’s lauded Truth about the hatchet!
paragraphs.cn: 当贝琪悄悄告诉爸爸，汤姆如何在学校替她挨打时，法官非常感动。当她请求爸爸原谅汤姆为了替她挨打而说的那个大谎话时，法官激动地大声说，那是一个多么高尚、多么大方、多么了不起的谎话啊——这个谎话值得昂首挺胸地载入史册，和乔治·华盛顿关于斧头的故事一样有名！

paragraphs.en: Becky thought her father had never looked so tall and so superb as when he walked the floor and stamped his foot and said that.
paragraphs.cn: 贝琪觉得爸爸从来没有像这样高大威武过，当他踱步、跺脚说出那些话的时候。

paragraphs.en: She went straight off and told Tom about it.
paragraphs.cn: 她立刻跑去告诉了汤姆。

paragraphs.en: Judge Thatcher hoped to see Tom a great lawyer or a great soldier some day.
paragraphs.cn: 撒切尔法官希望汤姆将来能成为一名大律师或一名大将军。

paragraphs.en: He said he meant to look to it that Tom should be admitted to the National Military Academy and afterward trained in the best law school in the country, in order that he might be ready for either career or both.
paragraphs.cn: 他说他会确保让汤姆进入国家军事学院，然后去全国最好的法学院学习，这样他就可以选择做军人、律师，或者两者都做。

paragraphs.en: Huck Finn’s wealth and the fact that he was now under the Widow Douglas’ protection introduced him into society—no, dragged him into it, hurled him into it—and his sufferings were almost more than he could bear.
paragraphs.cn: 芬恩哈克有钱了，而且现在又有道格拉斯寡妇的保护，这让他不得不进入“上流社会”——不，是被人硬拉进去，硬推进去——他痛苦得都快受不了了。

paragraphs.en: The widow’s servants kept him clean and neat, combed and brushed, and they bedded him nightly in unsympathetic sheets that had not one little spot or stain which he could press to his heart and know for a friend.
paragraphs.cn: 寡妇家的仆人把他洗得干干净净，头发梳得整整齐齐。晚上，他们让他睡在没有一点点污渍的干净床单上，他觉得这些床单一点也不亲切，没有一处能让他感到熟悉和安慰。

paragraphs.en: He had to eat with a knife and fork; he had to use napkin, cup, and plate; he had to learn his book, he had to go to church; he had to talk so properly that speech was become insipid in his mouth; whithersoever he turned, the bars and shackles of civilization shut him in and bound him hand and foot.
paragraphs.cn: 他必须用刀叉吃饭；必须用手帕、杯子和盘子；必须学习课本，必须去教堂；他说话必须非常得体，以至于在他嘴里，说话都变得索然无味了；无论他走到哪里，文明的规矩都像枷锁一样把他牢牢地困住，让他动弹不得。

paragraphs.en: He bravely bore his miseries three weeks, and then one day turned up missing.
paragraphs.cn: 他勇敢地忍受了三个星期的痛苦，然后有一天，他不见了。

paragraphs.en: For forty-eight hours the widow hunted for him everywhere in great distress.
paragraphs.cn: 整整四十八小时，寡妇到处找他，非常着急。

paragraphs.en: The public were profoundly concerned; they searched high and low, they dragged the river for his body.
paragraphs.cn: 大家都很担心；他们到处寻找，甚至还打捞了河里，想找到他的尸体。

paragraphs.en: Early the third morning Tom Sawyer wisely went poking among some old empty hogsheads down behind the abandoned slaughter-house, and in one of them he found the refugee.
paragraphs.cn: 第三天早上很早，汤姆·索亚很聪明，他去废弃屠宰场后面那些空木桶里找。在一个木桶里，他找到了那个躲起来的人。

paragraphs.en: Huck had slept there; he had just breakfasted upon some stolen odds and ends of food, and was lying off, now, in comfort, with his pipe.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克睡在那儿。他刚刚吃了些偷来的零碎食物当早餐。现在他舒服地躺着，抽着烟。

paragraphs.en: He was unkempt, uncombed, and clad in the same old ruin of rags that had made him picturesque in the days when he was free and happy.
paragraphs.cn: 他衣服脏乱，头发没梳。身上穿着和以前一样的破烂衣服。以前他自由开心的时候，这些衣服让他看起来很特别。

paragraphs.en: Tom routed him out, told him the trouble he had been causing, and urged him to go home.
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆把他叫起来，告诉他惹了什么麻烦，然后让他回家。

paragraphs.en: Huck’s face lost its tranquil content, and took a melancholy cast.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克的脸上没有了平静开心的表情，变得有些伤心。

paragraphs.en: He said:
paragraphs.cn: 他说：

paragraphs.en: “Don’t talk about it, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: “别说了，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: I’ve tried it, and it don’t work; it don’t work, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 我试过了，不行；不行啊，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: It ain’t for me; I ain’t used to it.
paragraphs.cn: 那不适合我；我不习惯。

paragraphs.en: The widder’s good to me, and friendly; but I can’t stand them ways.
paragraphs.cn: 寡妇对我很好，很友善；但我受不了那些规矩。

paragraphs.en: She makes me get up just at the same time every morning; she makes me wash, they comb me all to thunder; she won’t let me sleep in the woodshed; I got to wear them blamed clothes that just smothers me, Tom; they don’t seem to any air git through ’em, somehow; and they’re so rotten nice that I can’t set down, nor lay down, nor roll around anywher’s; I hain’t slid on a cellar-door for—well, it ’pears to be years; I got to go to church and sweat and sweat—I hate them ornery sermons!
paragraphs.cn: 她让我每天早上都准时起床；她让我洗漱，他们给我梳头梳得要命；她不让我睡在柴棚里；我得穿那些烦人的衣服，闷死我了，汤姆；它们好像一点都不透气；而且那些衣服太‘好’了，我不能坐着、躺着，也不能随便打滚；我好多年没在地下室门上滑下来玩了——好像好多年了；我必须去教堂，热得要命——我讨厌那些无聊的布道！

paragraphs.en: I can’t ketch a fly in there, I can’t chaw.
paragraphs.cn: 我在那里面不能抓苍蝇，也不能嚼东西。

paragraphs.en: I got to wear shoes all Sunday.
paragraphs.cn: 我整个星期天都得穿鞋。

paragraphs.en: The widder eats by a bell; she goes to bed by a bell; she gits up by a bell—everything’s so awful reg’lar a body can’t stand it.”
paragraphs.cn: 寡妇吃饭听铃声；睡觉听铃声；起床也听铃声——所有事情都太有规矩了，我受不了。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, everybody does that way, Huck.”
paragraphs.cn: “嗯，大家都是那样的，哈克。”

paragraphs.en: “Tom, it don’t make no difference.
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，那没用。

paragraphs.en: I ain’t everybody, and I can’t _stand_ it.
paragraphs.cn: 我不是大家，我受不了。

paragraphs.en: It’s awful to be tied up so.
paragraphs.cn: 这样被绑着太可怕了。

paragraphs.en: And grub comes too easy—I don’t take no interest in vittles, that way.
paragraphs.cn: 而且食物来得太容易了——那样一来，我对吃的就没兴趣了。

paragraphs.en: I got to ask to go a-fishing; I got to ask to go in a-swimming—dern’d if I hain’t got to ask to do everything.
paragraphs.cn: 我想去钓鱼得先问；我想去游泳也得问——天哪，我做什么都得问！

paragraphs.en: Well, I’d got to talk so nice it wasn’t no comfort—I’d got to go up in the attic and rip out awhile, every day, to git a taste in my mouth, or I’d a died, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 唉，我得说得那么礼貌，一点都不舒服——我每天都得去阁楼上，大声抱怨一会儿，才能让我心里好受点，不然我非死不可，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: The widder wouldn’t let me smoke; she wouldn’t let me yell, she wouldn’t let me gape, nor stretch, nor scratch, before folks—” [Then with a spasm of special irritation and injury]—“And dad fetch it, she prayed all the time!
paragraphs.cn: 寡妇不让我抽烟；不让我大叫；不让我在人前打哈欠、伸懒腰、挠痒痒——” “——而且她老是祷告！

paragraphs.en: I never see such a woman!
paragraphs.cn: 我从没见过这样的女人！

paragraphs.en: I _had_ to shove, Tom—I just had to.
paragraphs.cn: 我_必须_逃走，汤姆——我就是必须逃。

paragraphs.en: And besides, that school’s going to open, and I’d a had to go to it—well, I wouldn’t stand _that_, Tom.
paragraphs.cn: 而且，学校要开学了，我非得去上学——嗯，我才受不了_那个_呢，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: Looky-here, Tom, being rich ain’t what it’s cracked up to be.
paragraphs.cn: 听着，汤姆，有钱根本不像大家说得那么好。

paragraphs.en: It’s just worry and worry, and sweat and sweat, and a-wishing you was dead all the time.
paragraphs.cn: 只会一直担心，一直辛苦，一直希望自己死了算了。

paragraphs.en: Now these clothes suits me, and this bar’l suits me, and I ain’t ever going to shake ’em any more.
paragraphs.cn: 现在这些衣服适合我，这个木桶也适合我，我再也不想换了。

paragraphs.en: Tom, I wouldn’t ever got into all this trouble if it hadn’t ’a’ been for that money; now you just take my sheer of it along with your’n, and gimme a ten-center sometimes—not many times, becuz I don’t give a dern for a thing ’thout it’s tollable hard to git—and you go and beg off for me with the widder.”
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆，要不是因为那些钱，我根本不会惹上这么多麻烦；现在你把我的那份钱和你的一起拿走吧，偶尔给我一毛钱就行——别太多次，因为太容易得到的东西我才不在乎——然后你去跟寡妇说说，让她别再管我了。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Huck, you know I can’t do that.
paragraphs.cn: “哦，哈克，你知道我不能那么做。”

paragraphs.en: ’Tain’t fair; and besides if you’ll try this thing just a while longer you’ll come to like it.”
paragraphs.cn: “这不公平！你再玩一会儿这个，就会喜欢的。”

paragraphs.en: “Like it!
paragraphs.cn: “喜欢它？！

paragraphs.en: Yes—the way I’d like a hot stove if I was to set on it long enough.
paragraphs.cn: 是啊——如果我一直坐在一个热炉子上，我也会‘喜欢’它的。

paragraphs.en: No, Tom, I won’t be rich, and I won’t live in them cussed smothery houses.
paragraphs.cn: 不，汤姆，我才不要变有钱呢，我也不要住那些闷闷的房子。

paragraphs.en: I like the woods, and the river, and hogsheads, and I’ll stick to ’em, too.
paragraphs.cn: 我喜欢树林、小河和那些大木桶，我还要一直待在它们身边。

paragraphs.en: Blame it all! just as we’d got guns, and a cave, and all just fixed to rob, here this dern foolishness has got to come up and spile it all!”
paragraphs.cn: 真是的！我们刚弄好枪，找到一个山洞，准备去‘打劫’了，结果这件傻事就来了，把一切都搞砸了！”

paragraphs.en: Tom saw his opportunity—
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆看到了机会——

paragraphs.en: “Lookyhere, Huck, being rich ain’t going to keep me back from turning robber.”
paragraphs.cn: “看这里，哈克，有钱可不会让我不做‘强盗’的。”

paragraphs.en: “No!
paragraphs.cn: “真的吗？！

paragraphs.en: Oh, good-licks; are you in real dead-wood earnest, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: 哦，太棒了！汤姆，你真是认真的吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Just as dead earnest as I’m sitting here.
paragraphs.cn: “我像坐在这里一样认真。

paragraphs.en: But Huck, we can’t let you into the gang if you ain’t respectable, you know.”
paragraphs.cn: 但是哈克，如果你不是个‘好孩子’，我们就不能让你加入我们的队伍哦。”

paragraphs.en: Huck’s joy was quenched.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克的开心劲儿一下就没了。

paragraphs.en: “Can’t let me in, Tom?
paragraphs.cn: “不让我加入吗，汤姆？

paragraphs.en: Didn’t you let me go for a pirate?”
paragraphs.cn: 你不是让我去做海盗了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, but that’s different.
paragraphs.cn: “是啊，但是那不一样。

paragraphs.en: A robber is more high-toned than what a pirate is—as a general thing.
paragraphs.cn: ‘强盗’一般比‘海盗’更厉害一些。

paragraphs.en: In most countries they’re awful high up in the nobility—dukes and such.”
paragraphs.cn: 在很多国家，他们都是很高的贵族——比如公爵什么的。”

paragraphs.en: “Now, Tom, hain’t you always ben friendly to me?
paragraphs.cn: “汤姆，你不是一直都是我的好朋友吗？

paragraphs.en: You wouldn’t shet me out, would you, Tom?
paragraphs.cn: 你不会把我赶出去的，对不对，汤姆？

paragraphs.en: You wouldn’t do that, now, _would_ you, Tom?”
paragraphs.cn: 你现在不会那么做的，是吗，汤姆？”

paragraphs.en: “Huck, I wouldn’t want to, and I _don’t_ want to—but what would people say?
paragraphs.cn: “哈克，我也不想那样做，我真的不想——但是别人会怎么说呢？

paragraphs.en: Why, they’d say, ‘Mph!
paragraphs.cn: 他们会说，‘哼！

paragraphs.en: Tom Sawyer’s Gang! pretty low characters in it!’
paragraphs.cn: 汤姆·索亚的队伍里都是些不好的家伙！’

paragraphs.en: They’d mean you, Huck.
paragraphs.cn: 他们说的就是你，哈克。

paragraphs.en: You wouldn’t like that, and I wouldn’t.”
paragraphs.cn: 你不会喜欢那样，我也不会。”

paragraphs.en: Huck was silent for some time, engaged in a mental struggle.
paragraphs.cn: 哈克安静了一会儿，心里在想事情。

paragraphs.en: Finally he said:
paragraphs.cn: 最后他说：

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’ll go back to the widder for a month and tackle it and see if I can come to stand it, if you’ll let me b’long to the gang, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: “好吧，我回寡妇那里住一个月，试着看看我能不能习惯。如果你让我加入你们的队伍，汤姆。”

paragraphs.en: “All right, Huck, it’s a whiz!
paragraphs.cn: “太好了，哈克，真是太棒了！”

paragraphs.en: Come along, old chap, and I’ll ask the widow to let up on you a little, Huck.”
paragraphs.cn: 来吧，老伙计，我会叫寡妇对你松一点的，哈克。

paragraphs.en: “Will you, Tom—now will you?
paragraphs.cn: 你会吗，汤姆——你真的会吗？

paragraphs.en: That’s good.
paragraphs.cn: 那太好了。

paragraphs.en: If she’ll let up on some of the roughest things, I’ll smoke private and cuss private, and crowd through or bust.
paragraphs.cn: 要是她能少管那些最烦人的事，我就偷偷抽烟，偷偷骂人，我一定要挺过去，不然就完蛋。

paragraphs.en: When you going to start the gang and turn robbers?”
paragraphs.cn: 你什么时候组个帮派，去当强盗啊？

paragraphs.en: “Oh, right off.
paragraphs.cn: 哦，马上就去。

paragraphs.en: We’ll get the boys together and have the initiation tonight, maybe.”
paragraphs.cn: 我们会把伙伴们召集起来，可能今晚就搞入伙仪式。

paragraphs.en: “Have the which?”
paragraphs.cn: 搞什么？

paragraphs.en: “Have the initiation.”
paragraphs.cn: 搞入伙仪式啊。

paragraphs.en: “What’s that?”
paragraphs.cn: 那是什么？

paragraphs.en: “It’s to swear to stand by one another, and never tell the gang’s secrets, even if you’re chopped all to flinders, and kill anybody and all his family that hurts one of the gang.”
paragraphs.cn: 就是要发誓大家互相帮助，绝不告诉帮派的秘密，就算被砍成碎片也不说，还要杀了所有伤害我们帮派的人和他们的家人。

paragraphs.en: “That’s gay—that’s mighty gay, Tom, I tell you.”
paragraphs.cn: 那太棒了——那真是超级棒啊，汤姆，我告诉你。

paragraphs.en: “Well, I bet it is.
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，那当然了。

paragraphs.en: And all that swearing’s got to be done at midnight, in the lonesomest, awfulest place you can find—a ha’nted house is the best, but they’re all ripped up now.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且所有的发誓都得在半夜，在你能找到的最孤独、最可怕的地方进行——鬼屋是最好的，但是现在都被拆掉了。

paragraphs.en: “Well, midnight’s good, anyway, Tom.”
paragraphs.cn: 嗯，半夜也挺好的，汤姆。

paragraphs.en: “Yes, so it is.
paragraphs.cn: 是啊，就是这样。

paragraphs.en: And you’ve got to swear on a coffin, and sign it with blood.”
paragraphs.cn: 而且你还得对着棺材发誓，用血来签名。

paragraphs.en: “Now, that’s something _like_!
paragraphs.cn: 这才有意思！

paragraphs.en: Why, it’s a million times bullier than pirating.
paragraphs.cn: 哎呀，这可比当海盗好玩一百万倍！

paragraphs.en: I’ll stick to the widder till I rot, Tom; and if I git to be a reg’lar ripper of a robber, and everybody talking ’bout it, I reckon she’ll be proud she snaked me in out of the wet.”
paragraphs.cn: 我会一直跟着寡妇，不会离开的，汤姆；如果我变成一个真正厉害的强盗，人人都谈论我，我想她会为收留我而骄傲的。

paragraphs.en: CONCLUSION
paragraphs.cn: 结局

paragraphs.en: So endeth this chronicle.
paragraphs.cn: 这个故事就到这里了。

paragraphs.en: It being strictly a history of a _boy_, it must stop here; the story could not go much further without becoming the history of a _man_.
paragraphs.cn: 它只是一个关于_男孩_的故事，所以必须在这里停下来；如果继续下去，就会变成一个关于_大人_的故事了。

paragraphs.en: When one writes a novel about grown people, he knows exactly where to stop—that is, with a marriage; but when he writes of juveniles, he must stop where he best can.
paragraphs.cn: 当一个人写关于大人的故事时，他知道在哪里停下——那就是结婚的时候；但是当他写关于小孩的故事时，就必须在能停下的地方停下来。

paragraphs.en: Most of the characters that perform in this book still live, and are prosperous and happy.
paragraphs.cn: 这本书里的大多数人物都还活着，过得很好，也很开心。

paragraphs.en: Some day it may seem worth while to take up the story of the younger ones again and see what sort of men and women they turned out to be; therefore it will be wisest not to reveal any of that part of their lives at present.
paragraphs.cn: 也许有一天，会觉得值得再写写那些小家伙们的故事，看看他们都变成了什么样的大人；所以现在最好不要透露他们生活中那一部分的事情。
